"So, while I appreciate your discovery of the Headless Ones," Eido continued, "I cannot support your conclusions regarding their origins."  

"Or their clearly inaccurate names," Eido added. 

"But, but I like—" Glint sputtered.

"I must reiterate that they do, in fact, have heads," Eido insisted in exasperation. "It's their defining feature."
3948917400.text_zh:
“你真的认为是人类创造了无头者吗？”格林特固执地倾着他的机壳盖。 

“是的。我推测它们是为着一种古老人类仪式而被创造出来的，”艾多回答道，丝毫未察觉到机灵的愤怒。“那个仪式…就叫做腕神节。”

格林特疑惑地斜了斜身子。“什么意思？” 

“它连接着生者和死者的域界，”艾多解释道。“古老的‘南瓜'便是其中的关键。” 

格林特的机壳盖困惑地松弛了下来。

“所以，虽然我很欣赏你对无头者的发现，”艾多继续说道，“但我不太赞同你关于它们起源的结论。”  

“这个名字显然也不够准确，”艾多补充道。 

“但是，但是我喜欢——”格林特气急败坏地说道。

“我必须重申，它们确实有头，”艾多恼怒地坚持道。“这是它们的明确特征。”

3948917401.name: Findings of Eido – 27
3948917401.text:
The Findings of Eido, Scribe of House Light, Regarding the Beings Known as the Headless Ones (Cont'd)

"It seems that the overarching theme of The Hall Between was 'transgression.' It was a time when social strictures were lifted, and Humans were permitted to cross the boundaries of nature and society. 

It appears that most Humans used this license to contact their ancestors, similar to the Vanguard's severance rituals aboard the Leviathan. However, it is entirely possible that more adventurous practitioners used the power of the pumpkins to create entirely new beings: the Headless Ones.

I'm grateful to Glint for conclusively proving the existence of these reclusive creatures. However, my subsequent research with the Guardian leads me to challenge his conclusions regarding their origins. This debate is likely to continue as long as Lightbearers retain their ghoulish taste for the Headless Ones' loot, and their visceral 'candy' innards."
3948917401.text_zh:
光能氏族文士艾多关于被称作无头者的生物的发现（续）

“腕神节的首要主题似乎是‘越界'。那是个社会结构消失的时刻，让人类可以跨越自然和社会的界限。 

大多数人类似乎都会借此来联系他们的祖先，类似于先锋在利维坦上的断舍仪式。不过，更有冒险精神的人完全有可能利用南瓜的力量创造出全新的生物：无头者。

我很感激格林特最终证明了这些隐秘生物的存在。然而，我随后与守护者进行的研究让我对他关于其起源的结论产生了质疑。只要负光者对无头者的战利品，以及糖果'内脏还保留着病态的口味，这场争论就可能会继续下去。”

3918040698.name: Chapter 1
3918040698.text:
The Tower Bazaar was beginning to wake with activity as Eido sighed and placed her datapad on the table in front of Crow's Ghost.

"Glint, this research on the Hall Between has me thinking about… stories. The ones that evoke fear. The 'scary' ones, as you've said."

"Like the ones about the Drowned Captain?" Glint asked.

"Exactly," she said. "My father told me not so long ago that odes are for hatchlings. But throughout our research on the Hall Between and the Headless Ones, I've discovered that people of all ages and backgrounds enjoy these tales of dread, regardless of the academic merit or accuracy. So I'd like to make something similar for people to enjoy; I want to try writing my own!"

"That's a wonderful idea. What will you write first?"

"Well, I'm not exactly sure. I need some… inspiration."

"Oh! I'd love to help. Now, the first thing to know about scary stories is that sometimes, nothing is as scary as the truth!"
3918040698.text_zh:
艾多叹了口气，把她的数据板放在乌鸦机灵前的桌子上，高塔集市开始活跃起来。

“格林特，对腕神节的研究让我想到了…那些故事。那些唤起恐惧的故事。就是你说的那些‘可怕的'故事。”

“就像溺亡队长的那些故事？”格林特问道。

“没错，”她说道。我父亲不久前告诉我颂歌是给孩子们听的。但通过我们对腕神节和无头者的研究，我发现任何年龄和背景的人都喜欢这些恐怖故事，无论其学术价值或准确性如何。所以我想尝试一些类似的东西给大家看；我想试试自己来写！”

“那是个好主意。你打算先写什么呢？”

“我还没想好。我需要一些…灵感。”

“哦！我很乐意帮忙。其实，恐怖故事首先要知道的一件事就是，有时候，没有什么比真相更可怕！”

3918040697.name: Chapter 2
3918040697.text:
The room Eris had stuck Immaru in was minuscule. There were no windows to watch the hours and days pass by. No electronics to hack. Just containers of decommissioned armor stacked against the far wall, and one small, empty crate in the middle of the room, adorned with a handwritten sign that simply said "YOU" and an arrow pointing menacingly downward. It was placed there as a warning, after he was caught lurking around the more sensitive areas of the Tower. Ikora had confiscated his Shaded Shell disguise and placed a Hidden agent somewhere outside to report on his every move. She did, however, leave some blank crossword pages for him.

Immaru stared at the crate, emitting a low-pitched growl, as a lone sweeper bot entered, surprising the Ghost. He circled, then scanned his random and unexpected visitor. It was standard issue, nothing special. Immaru was disappointed.

"I still can't believe Savathûn would do this to me," Immaru said to the bot as he flew directly into its face. "The nerve of it all, leaving me here as collateral. And then to ask for information? Hmph."

He watched the bot shuffle away and broom the open crate. "Then again, who says I have to share everything?"

Immaru swooped around, quickly hacking into the sweeper bot's systems. "Grab an empty kit bag from over here. Should be just the right size if I remove a little weight." As the bot complied, Immaru chuckled, shedding his standard Hive shell. "Right… time for a jailbreak."
3918040697.text_zh:
埃里斯让伊马鲁住的房间很狭小。没有窗户来观察时光的流逝。没有电子设备可以侵入。只有一些装有废弃护甲的箱子靠在远处的墙上，房间中央有一个空的小板条箱，上面饰有一个手写的牌子，只写着一个“你”字，还有一个箭头气势汹汹地指向下方。在他被逮到窥视高塔的敏感区域后，那牌子就被当作警告放在那儿了。艾可拉没收了他的遮阳外壳伪装，还在外面安插了一名隐秘者特工，监视汇报他的一举一动。不过，她倒是给他留了一些空白的填字游戏页。

伊马鲁盯着板条箱，发出一声低沉的咆哮，这时正好有个扫地机器人进来，吓了这机灵一跳。他绕了一圈，然后扫描了一下这位不速之客。是个标准配发的机器人，没啥特别的。伊马鲁很失望。

“我仍不敢相信萨瓦图恩会这样对我，”伊马鲁朝那机器人说着，径直飞到了它的脸上。“最可气的是，居然把我留在这里作为抵押。然后还让我提供消息？哼。”

他看着那机器人慢慢走开去打扫开启的板条箱。“话说回来，谁说我什么都得分享出来？”

伊马鲁猛扑下来，迅速侵入扫地机器人的系统。“从这儿拿个空的工具包。要是我去掉一点重量，应该正好合适。”机器人照办了，伊马鲁轻声笑着，脱掉了他的标配邪魔族机壳。“好…该越狱了。”

3918040696.name: Chapter 3
3918040696.text:
After a few arduous attempts and one superbly acted sob story told to an incredibly gullible Ghost, Immaru eventually sauntered off in a new Constricting Shell. In his latest disguise, he skulked through halls and hangars and workshops, scanning everything and anything he could find on his way to the Courtyard. There, he hovered among the gnarled branches of a giant tree, nearly invisible among the colorful lanterns adorning it.

He watched Guardians meditate among candles, the flames flickering in the breeze. Others, dressed as insects and arachnids, gleefully danced or bobbed for apples, their revelry flanked by a pair of Guardians "galloping" by with coconut shells. 

Amid the flurry of costumes and masks, his gaze finally settled on people sharing small, wrapped objects. Immaru gingerly floated closer to the base of the tree to get a better look.

"Hey, move along, pal. I saw that candy first," a voice sneered from behind him.
3918040696.text_zh:
经过几次艰苦的尝试，以及向一个非常好骗的机灵讲述了一个精彩演绎的动人故事后，伊马鲁总算穿着一件新的收缩机壳漫步离开了。依靠最新的伪装，他偷偷穿过大厅、机库和车间，扫描他在去往庭院的路上找到的一切。到达庭院后，他在一棵巨树的多节枝杈之间盘旋着，多彩的装饰灯笼几乎隐去了他的身形。

他看着守护者们在烛光中冥想，烛焰在微风中摇曳。其他人则打扮成昆虫和蛛形动物，欢快地跳着舞，玩捞苹果游戏，还有一对拿着椰子壳“疾驰”的守护者为其狂欢助兴。 

在纷乱的扮装和面具当中，他的目光终于落在了那些分享小包裹物品的人们的身上。伊马鲁小心翼翼地飘近树根，想看得更清楚。

“嘿，走开，伙计。我先看到那糖果的，”一个声音从他身后讥讽地说道。

3918040703.name: Chapter 4
3918040703.text:
"I called dibs on that candy. Don't make me say it again."

Immaru turned to see another Ghost as she made a beeline for the candy on the ground beneath him. 

"You—what are you wearing? You dipped your shell in… Human food?!" Immaru spat.

The other Ghost sighed. "It's a Caramel Apple Shell, you dolt. If you knew anything, you'd recognize how special it is."

"Looks sticky."

"It's a del-i-cacy. Note the elegant ornamentation of crushed toffee bits," she said and spun around.

"If you haven't lost your self-respect yet, allow me to lose it on your behalf," he shot back.

Her iris narrowed as she fixated on Immaru's shell. "Pff. I'm surprised your Guardian didn't dress you up like a lemon," she scoffed.

"I ain't got no Guardian," Immaru sniffed.

The other Ghost bobbed toward him. "Wait, you're unpartnered too? I knew there were more of us out—"

"Happy Festival of the Lost, friends!"

"Oh no," Immaru and the other Ghost groaned in unison as they faced a cheerful Glint.
3918040703.text_zh:
“那糖果归我。别逼我再说一遍。”

伊马鲁转身看着另一个机灵径直向他下方地上的糖果飘去。 

“你——你穿的是什么？你把你的机壳浸在了…人类的食物里？！”伊马鲁厌恶地朝地上吐了口唾沫。

另一个机灵叹了口气。“这是焦糖苹果机壳，你这个笨蛋。你但凡有点见识，就会知道它有多特别。”

“看起来黏糊糊的。”

“这可是美-味-佳-肴。瞧瞧那些用太妃糖碎块做的优雅装饰，”她说着转了个身。

“你不嫌丢脸，我都替你害臊，”他回击道。

她眯眼盯着伊马鲁的机壳。“噗。我很惊讶你的守护者没把你打扮得像个柠檬，”她嘲笑道。

“我没有守护者，”伊马鲁嗤之以鼻。

另一个机灵朝他点着头。“等等，你也没有搭档？我就知道不只是我——”

“英灵日快乐，朋友们！”

“哦，不，”伊马鲁和另一个机灵瞅着愉快的格林特，齐声咕哝道。

3918040702.name: Chapter 5
3918040702.text:
The toffee-covered Ghost transmatted away the second she heard Glint's voice. Unfazed, Glint approached the snake-covered Ghost, determined to meet a new friend.

"Hello, stranger! Are you enjoying the festival?" Glint asked.

"Get lost," Immaru snarled, and Glint jumped back in surprise.

"Immaru! You—"

"Be quiet, will ya! I'm, uh, trying to… enjoy the festival… incognito," Immaru whispered.

Glint quietly stared back for a moment. "You broke out of Eris's crate, huh," he said.

"I was in a room. Not a crate," Immaru replied tersely. "I wasn't waiting to be let out again on good behavior. I'm my own Ghost!"

"Then you should join me and Eido—"

"No."

"But we're collecting inspiration for scary stories, starting with our research on the Headless Ones and the Hall Between—"

"Headless what?"

"Headless Ones," Glint chirped. "Giant pumpkin-headed enemies that the Guardians have been fighting. They're mysterious monsters filled with candy!"

"Fighting the Guardians, hmm? In that case, I'd love to hear what your little Fallen friend has to say about them."
3918040702.text_zh:
被太妃糖裹着的机灵一听到格林特的声音就传送离开了。格林特毫不在意地走近蛇身机壳的机灵，决心认识这位新朋友。

“你好，陌生人！节日过得还愉快吗？”格林特问道。

“滚开，”伊马鲁咆哮道，惊得格林特向后退。

“伊马鲁！你——”

“你能不能小点声！我，呃，想…低调地…享受节日，”伊马鲁低声说道。

格林特静静地盯了他一会儿。“你从埃里斯的板条箱里逃出来了，哈，”他说。

“我之前是在一个房间，不是从板条箱里，”伊马鲁简洁地答道。“我才不会等到表现良好再被放出来。我按照自己的意愿行事！”

“那你就应该跟我和艾多一起——”

“不。”

“可是我们正在收集恐怖故事的灵感，从我们对无头者和腕神节的研究开始——”

“无头什么？”

“无头者，”格林特啾鸣着。“跟守护者们战斗的巨大南瓜脑袋敌人。它们是装满糖果的神秘怪物！”

“跟守护者们战斗，嗯？这样的话，我倒很想听听你那个堕落者小朋友有什么要说的。”

3918040701.name: Chapter 6
3918040701.text:
Eido sat in the Tower's Bazaar beneath the afternoon sun, comfortably situated at a table with a full pot of tea. She gazed intently into her cup, her research and data spread out around her.

"Eido! Immaru is going to—Eido? Why are you… staring at your tea instead of writing?" Glint peered at her in confusion, Immaru in tow.

"I was going to write. But then I discovered the art of tasseomancy while following an old research lead," she said, her eyes never leaving her cup. "Apparently it's a method of discerning things yet to come by assessing patterns within the leaves and sediment. I… thought it might help."

"I was lookin' for monsters, not tea," Immaru growled. Glint peeked over Eido's shoulder, watching the leaves move in her drink. 

Eido squinted her four eyes. "This pattern looks like—" 

"Commander Zavala! Knitting with Empress Caiatl!" Glint exclaimed. 

Eido watched as the leaves swirled around in the tea in the shape of a ragged claw, and a sharp chill suddenly settled deep within her. "No, it's—"

"Fynch! With a Lucent Knight! No, a Hunter! No, wait—he's hugging Savathûn!" Glint called out again.

"Why did I think for one second this was gonna be worth my while," Immaru muttered and left.
3918040701.text_zh:
艾多沐浴在午后的阳光下，舒适地坐在高塔集市里的一张桌子旁，端着满满一壶茶。她目不转睛地盯着杯子，她的研究和数据在她的四周展开。

“艾多！伊马鲁打算——艾多？你为什么…盯着茶看不写故事？”格林特带着伊马鲁，困惑地看着她。

“我本来打算写的。但后来我循着一条古老的研究线索发现了茶叶占卜的艺术，”她说着，眼神未曾离开过杯子。“据说，这是一种通过评估茶叶和茶渣中的图案来辨明未来之事的方法。我…认为这可能会有所帮助。”

“我要找的是怪物，不是茶，”伊马鲁咆哮道。格林特越过艾多的肩膀，偷偷望着茶叶在她的茶水里移动。 

艾多眯起她的四只眼睛。“这个图案看起来像——” 

“指挥官萨瓦拉！跟女帝查厄托一起织毛衣！”格林特喊道。 

艾多看着茶叶在茶里打转，像一只粗糙的爪子，内心深处突然泛起一阵刺骨的寒意。“不，这是——”

“芬奇！跟一个光明骑士在一起！不，是个猎人！不，等等——他在拥抱萨瓦图恩！”格林特再次喊道。

“为什么我居然会对这个抱有一丝期望，”伊马鲁咕哝着离开了。

3918040700.name: Chapter 7
3918040700.text:
"Forget the tea," Glint said. "I've got something better!"

He transmatted a set of objects onto the table, and Eido gasped, her heartbeat quickening. "The Deck of Whispers? You stole Eris's cards?!"

"Borrowed," he corrected, twirling around the table to face her. 

"Glint!"

"What? I left a note."

Eido shivered as she conjured the image of a Hive-altered Eris in her mind. "It's too dangerous." She quickly pushed the cards away, but Glint nudged them back.

"I heard that Eris consulted the deck to gain information or make decisions. I thought we could use it to inspire your writing! Let's just try," Glint begged. "How hard can it be?"

Eido sighed and picked up the cards, shuffling them with her four hands in the flamboyant style the Drifter taught her. "How many cards?" she asked.

"Try three," Glint said. "And when I watched Eris, she had to ask the cards a question."

Eido thought for a moment. "What kind of danger would be threatening enough for a 'scary' story?" Eido cut the deck in half, and she felt a surge of energy as she selected the first card.

THE HARBINGER

"Wait I've got a better one! What kind of dangerous situation could be happening RIGHT NOW?" Glint exclaimed.

"Glint! I don't think we should—" 

"We need to write based on a true story, right? This is exactly how we do it!"

Eido closed her eyes, feeling energy surge again in her hands, and continued.

THE LIE 

THREE OF WORMS 

She opened her eyes and studied the cards. "Eris can be, well, intimidating," she admitted, pointing to The Harbinger card.

"No, no, the cards aren't literal. It's a metaphor!" Glint said. "The Harbinger and The Lie! That means… the spirits of the dead are lost like leaves on the wind… and wandering the Earth!" Glint gasped.

"But The Lie is upside down. That wouldn't make sense."

"It's right side up to me!"

"Because you're on the opposite side of the table. It's my reading, remember?"

"Oh yeah." He quickly changed position. "Then… they aren't lost. They have purpose. They seek… REVENGE! Against the living! By changing us into Headless Ones. With paracausal worm power! Aaaaahhhh!"

Eido pondered the cards. "Actually, I was thinking that solitude and being isolated can evoke terror in both Humans and Eliksni. Perhaps my scary story could include that?"

Glint shrugged his shell. "Hm, not bad. I still like mine better. Maybe try it again?" 

Eido nodded and swept up the cards to shuffle once more.
3918040700.text_zh:
“别管茶了，”格林特说道。“我有更棒的东西！”

他把一组东西传送到桌子上，艾多倒抽了一口气，心跳加快。“低语卡组？你偷了埃里斯的卡牌？！”

“是借，”他纠正道，绕桌转了一圈来与她面对面。 

“格林特！”

“咋了？我留了一张纸条。”

艾多在脑海中浮现出邪魔族样貌的埃里斯的形象，不禁打了个寒颤。“这太危险了。”她赶紧把卡牌推开，但格林特又把它们推了回去。

“我听说埃里斯会占卜卡组来获取信息或做出决定。我想我们可以用它来激发你的写作灵感！我们来试试吧，”格林特恳求道。“能有多难呢？”

艾多叹了口气，拿起卡牌，用她的四只手按照浪客教她的华丽手法洗牌。“多少张牌？”她问。

“试试三张，”格林特说道。“我看埃里斯操作的时候，得问这些卡牌一个问题。”

艾多想了一会儿。“什么样的危险才配得上一个‘恐怖'故事？”艾多将牌组对半切牌，在选择第一张卡牌时感到了一阵能量的涌动。

先知

“等等，我有一个更好的问题！现在可能会发生什么样的危险情况？”格林特喊道。

“格林特！我觉得我们不应该——” 

“我们需要根据真实故事来写，对吧？我们就该这么做！”

艾多闭上眼睛，再次感受到手中的能量涌动，继续抽牌。

谎言 

蠕虫三 

她睁开眼睛，仔细研究着卡牌。“埃里斯有时候，嗯，有点吓人，”她指着先知卡牌坦言道。

“不，不，这些卡牌不是字面意思。这是个隐喻！”格林特说道。“先知和谎言！这意味着…死者的灵魂像风中的树叶一样消失了…在地球上游荡！”格林特倒抽了一口气。

“但是谎言牌是逆位。那说不通。”

“我看它是正位！”

“因为你站在桌子的对面。这是我的占卜，记得吗？”

“也对。”他迅速更换了位置。“那…他们没有迷失。他们拥有使命。他们寻求…复仇！对抗生者！要把我们也变成无头者。利用超因果蠕虫的力量！呃啊！”

艾多琢磨着这些牌。“实际上，我想到了孤独和被孤立会引起人类和埃里克斯尼族的恐惧。也许我的恐怖故事可以加进这一点？”

格林特耸了耸机壳。“嗯，还不错。我还是更喜欢我的想法。要不再试试？” 

艾多点点头，把卡牌扫起，重新洗牌。

3918040691.name: Chapter 8
3918040691.text:
The colors of dusk were already painted in the sky beyond the Last City by the time Glint approached Crow, stationed on the outskirts of the Tower.

"Crow! You'll never believe what happened today! Eido and I were talking. I mean, we talk a lot. But today about the Headless Ones, and then she got the idea to write a scary story! And then Eido was going to write. But then she didn't. I mean, she did but first tea! It didn't help. So then we—er, I—borrowed Eris's Deck of Whispers. The cards are incredible! No wonder Eris…"

Glint stopped and saw Crow's gaze following a squadron's contrails in the far-off distance. The Ghost floated up and nudged Crow's cheek; the Hunter jumped in startled surprise.

"Glint! I, uh, didn't see you there. Did—did you say something?" Crow asked.

"Just that… I'm here. If you want to talk."

Glint leaned against his Guardian's shoulder, and Crow reached up to touch the little Ghost's shell.
3918040691.text_zh:
格林特走近驻守在高塔外围的乌鸦时，圣城远处的天空已经晕染上了黄昏的色彩。

“乌鸦！你绝对不敢相信今天发生了什么！我和艾多在聊天。我的意思是，我们经常聊天。但是今天聊的是有关无头者的话题，然后她有了写个恐怖故事的想法！于是艾多就准备写。但后来她没有做。我是说，她做了，但首先是茶占卜！可是没有用。所以我们，呃，我，借了埃里斯的低语卡组。这些卡牌太不可思议了！难怪埃里斯…”

格林特停了下来，看到乌鸦的目光跟随着远处一支飞行中队的尾迹。机灵飘浮上去，轻轻碰了碰乌鸦的脸颊；猎人吓得跳了起来。

“格林特！我，呃，没看到你在那儿。你——你说什么了吗？”乌鸦问。

“只是说…如果你想谈，我随时奉陪。”

格林特靠在守护者的肩膀上，而乌鸦则伸手去摸了摸小机灵的机壳。

3918040690.name: Chapter 9
3918040690.text:
Immaru materialized again in the corner of the Courtyard, not far from the bust of Cayde-6.

He continued his studies, watching Guardians obediently crowd around a Human with… more candy. Lots of candy, in fact. Her laughter pealed like mesmerizing bells as she bestowed her confections, the Guardians seeming to respond to her every command.

"Subjugation by sucrose…" Immaru thought to himself, "Much less messy than the Hive way. Heh, what I wouldn't give to try it out myself." He chuckled out loud at the thought.

An oblivious Titan stopped directly in front of him, adjusting his giant chicken mask with one hand while cradling a mound of confections in the other.

"Bawk-aaaawk!"

A chicken charged the Titan. He gasped and quickly dropped his bounty of candy in front of the Ironwood Tree, hands outstretched in a semblance of surrender. The chicken feverishly flapped her wings and mercilessly pecked his fingers.

"Colonel! It's me, it's me!" The Titan cried out in agony, trying to yank his mask loose. "I'm not a chicken!"

Mask wedged askew, the Titan ran and frantically barreled straight through Immaru. The Ghost slammed into Colonel with a solid thud.

"Bawk-aaaawk!"

The chicken focused her rage on Immaru and snapped at his shell. She found purchase on the silver snake decoration and clamped down.

"Let! Go!" Immaru yelled, wishing he had his Hive shell to swat the bird away. He sped through the Courtyard toward the Hangar. But Colonel had the strength of a Titan, the finesse of a Hunter, the cunning of a Warlock, and held on the whole way.
3918040690.text_zh:
伊马鲁在庭院角落距离凯德6号半身像不远的地方再次显现。

他继续他的研究，看着守护者们乖乖地围着一个拿着…更多糖果的人类。事实上，是超多的糖果。她分发糖果时，笑声像迷人的铃铛一样响起，守护者们似乎对她百依百顺。

“用糖实现征服…”伊马鲁心想，“比邪魔族的方法干净利落。呵，我想亲自体验一下。”想到这，他咯咯地笑出声来。

一名没察觉到他的泰坦直接在他面前停下，一只手调整着他的巨型小鸡面具，另一只手捧着一堆糖果。

“咕…咕咕咕咕！”

一只鸡冲向了那名泰坦。他倒抽了一口气，迅速地把他的那份糖果丢在铁木树前，伸手摆出投降的姿态。那只鸡兴奋地拍打着翅膀，无情地啄着他的手指。

“上校！是我，是我！”那名泰坦痛苦地喊道，试图解开他的面具。“我不是小鸡！”

戴着歪斜面具的泰坦从伊马鲁身边狂奔而过。机灵砰的一声撞到了上校身上。

“咕…咕咕咕咕！”

小鸡把怒火聚集在伊马鲁身上，猛咬他的机壳。她牢牢钳住银蛇装饰，向下夹紧。

“放！开！”伊马鲁喊道，他现在多希望自己能有邪魔族机壳来赶走小鸡。他飞快地穿过庭院，奔向机库。但是上校有着泰坦的力量、猎人的技巧和术士的狡诈，一路都没被甩下。

3901262984.name: Chapter 10
3901262984.text:
Ana Bray passed through the Courtyard, her mechanical dog at her heels. "Happy Festival of the Lost, Eva!"

"Oh, Ana dear!" Eva called back and held out a small package. "I thought Archie deserved to celebrate the festival in style with his own costume this year."

Ana gasped softly with delight as she unfurled a tiny cloak. "Look at you, Archie! I always knew you were a Hunter at heart."

She bent to secure the cloak just as a Ghost came zipping in from the direction of the Hangar, a rage-filled chicken hanging off his shell.

Archie's cloak flapped over the Ghost's eye. Unable to see, the Ghost skipped and skidded along the floor of the Courtyard, landing in the abandoned pile of candy beneath the Ironwood Tree.

Colonel's beak shook loose on impact. She expertly bobbed and weaved around the candy, her pecking focused on the Ghost's eye.

*****

Mechanical barks sounded, and among the candy wrappers, Immaru saw a flurry of feathers fly past. Eventually, the squawking faded into the distance, Immaru sat motionless until he felt the dog's nose nuzzle softly against him. Only then did the flustered Ghost emerge from hiding.

"Aww, look at that! Archie saved that little Ghost from Colonel's wrath! What a good little Hunter!" a Guardian cooed. Immaru watched in awe as every Guardian in the Courtyard simultaneously forgot about the candy, their attention devoted exclusively to the dog.

"Incredible," he mused with fascination.
3901262984.text_zh:
阿娜·布瑞穿过院子，她的机械狗跟在后面。“英灵日快乐，伊娃！”

“哦，亲爱的阿娜！”伊娃回应道，递出一个小包裹。“我觉得阿奇今年该有自己的服装来庆祝节日了。”

阿娜轻轻地喘着气，高兴地展开一件小披风。“快看呐，阿奇！我一向知道你骨子里是个猎人。”

她弯下腰去系披风，就在这时一个机灵从机库方向猛冲而来，有只怒气冲冲的鸡则挂在他的机壳上。

阿奇的披风盖住了机灵的眼睛。由于看不清，机灵在庭院的地上一路踉跄，落到铁木树下那堆被丢弃了的糖果上。

上校的喙被撞得松开了。她熟练地在糖果周围来回跳动着，一心去啄机灵的眼睛。

*****

机械的狗吠声响起，在一堆糖果包装纸当中，伊马鲁看到许多羽毛飞过。最终，鸡叫声消失在远处，伊马鲁一动不动地坐着，然后感觉到狗的鼻子在轻轻地蹭他。直到这时，这个慌乱的机灵才从藏身处出来。

“噢，看啊！阿奇从发火的上校那里救下了小机灵！多棒的一个小猎人啊！”一个守护者柔声说道。伊马鲁惊讶地看到，庭院里的守护者同时忘记了糖果，把注意力都集中到了小狗身上。

“难以置信，”他入迷地思忖道。

3901262985.name: Chapter 11
3901262985.text:
Immaru eventually found Archie again, sleeping and curled on a blanket in the Annex. The Ghost approximated the guttural sound of clearing one's throat, and the dog opened one eye.

"You know, after the whole… chicken… thing, I saw what you did up there. To those Guardians in the Courtyard, the way you had them wrapped around your little, uh, paws. You've got a gift," Immaru said. "And I could really use your help."

Archie tilted his head, listening.

"Right now, those Guardians don't care about anything else besides candy—it's controlling them, and they'll do anything for it. So we gotta get control of 'it' instead."

Archie growled.

"Not to hurt the Guardians," Immaru said, feigned sincerity dripping in his voice. "Just to help 'em. You wanna… help Ana, don't you? Keep her safe?" 

Archie processed for a moment and then barked in agreement, sealing their pact.
3901262985.text_zh:
伊马鲁终于又找到了阿奇，它蜷缩在附属建筑的毯子上睡着。机灵发出近似清喉咙的声音，小狗睁开了一只眼睛。

“知道吗，在…小鸡…那件事之后，我看到了你做的事。你用小，呃，爪子捏住那些庭院里的守护者们。你很有天赋，”伊马鲁说。“而我很需要你的帮助。”

阿奇歪着头听着。

“当前，那些守护者除了糖果什么都不关心——他们受其所控，可以为了糖果做任何事。所以我们要掌控糖果。”

阿奇低声咆哮起来。

“不是为了伤害守护者，”伊马鲁假装真诚地说道。“只是为了帮助他们。你想要…帮助阿娜，不是吗？保护她？” 

阿奇想了一会儿，然后发出吠叫表示同意，于是他们达成了协定。

3901262986.name: Chapter 12
3901262986.text:
How nervous—how terrified—had I been when they told me he was here—fragmented remains, nothing more. Even still, I nearly thought the knowledge—telling no one, no where—would drive me completely mad. But I could be trusted, they said. I could handle it, they said. So too I said, and observed in silence, emplaced.

For many nights, I kept my watch, my distance. He would not see me, sense me, know me. I was determined. But then again, so was he.

Thump, tha-thump, tha-thump. 

I heard it then, the steady, softly beating. An unwavering drum, calling out, bidding me to follow. The pests, the wind, I told myself, cocooned in lackless supposition. 

I wished to be gone from here. 

But they trusted me, they said. I could handle it, I said. So too were they convinced, and left me to my watch. 

The sound returned for me, over and over and over, until it lost all patience and began to swell. Loud and round it filled my head, roaring and resounding—

The pulsing of a heart. 

I must see him, sense him, know him. How this thought entered my mind, I cannot say, but there it stayed, eternally.

Tha-thump, tha-thump, tha-thump.

I placed my hand along his cask.

Tha-thump, tha-thump, tha-thump.

I held him there, inside my hands, and screamed into the thick, deep dark.

—An excerpt from "The Forlorn Heart"
3901262986.text_zh:
当他们告诉我他在这里的时候，我是多么紧张，多么害怕啊——虽然只是支离破碎的遗体。这个消息不会透露给任何地方的任何人，尽管如此，我还是觉得它会让我彻底发疯。但他们说，可以信任我。他们说，我应付得来。所以我也这么说，默默地观察着。

很多个夜晚，我一直守望，也保持着距离。他看不见我，感知不到我，也不了解我。我很坚定。但话说回来，他也是如此。

怦怦，怦怦，怦怦。 

于是我听到了，那阵稳定而轻柔的敲击声。一种坚定的鼓声，呼唤着，命令着我跟随。我告诉自己，那是害虫，风声，蛰伏在茫茫的无端猜想之中。 

我希望离开这里。 

但他们说过他们信任我。我说过我应付得来。所以他们也被说服了，留下我来守望。 

那声音一次又一次地向我袭来，直到它失去了所有的耐心，开始响亮起来。它洪亮而圆润地充斥我的脑海，呼啸轰鸣着——

心脏的跳动声。 

我必须看见他，感知他，了解他。这种想法是如何进入我的脑海的，我说不出来，但它却永远留在了那里。

怦怦，怦怦，怦怦。

我把手放在装他的桶上。

怦怦，怦怦，怦怦。

我把他抱在手里，对着深不见底的黑暗尖叫起来。

——摘自《遗弃之心》

3901262987.name: Chapter 13
3901262987.text:
It wasn't hard for Immaru to find candy to steal, and it was even easier for Archie to find marks willing to hand it over, for him to transmat it into his stomach cavity. The complicated part, they quickly discovered, was what to do with it after. 

Immaru's room was too conspicuous, too close to his minder. Instead, he searched for hidden niches throughout the Tower. But the longer it took to find the next one, the longer Archie remained filled with candy. The extra weight slowed him significantly, and the effort to keep the candy from melting resulted in higher-function latency.

"We gotta think smarter, not harder," Immaru finally admitted to Archie. "We need to broaden this operation." 

Archie responded by rolling on the floor, his belly in the air, the candy wrappers crinkling inside him.
3901262987.text_zh:
对伊马鲁来说，找到糖果来偷并不难，而对阿奇而言，找到愿意交出糖果的目标，把糖果传送到他的胃腔里就更容易了。他们很快发现，最复杂的环节是之后该怎么处理糖果。 

伊马鲁的房间太过显眼，离他的看守人太近。于是，他转而在整座高塔里寻找隐藏的壁龛。可是，找下一个壁龛花的时间越长，阿奇胃里装满糖果的时间就越长。额外的体重极大地降低了他的速度，他为了努力防止糖果融化，运行速度越来越慢。

“我们必须聪明地思考，而不是靠蛮力，”伊马鲁终于向阿奇承认道。“我们需要扩大这项业务。” 

阿奇在地板上打滚以作回应，肚子翘在空中，糖果包装纸在他的体内发出了沙沙声。

3901262988.name: Chapter 14
3901262988.text:
I was a scholar once. Of vast renown among those beyond influence of the Great Machine. Here, I told my House. See the truth and speak it with me. They refused, and so I left, unable to consume the bile of their belief.

The wind was bitter, no hollowhot to warm me. The terrain full of danger, no scattercape to shield me. 

I was alone, wasting beneath a blanket of snow.

But then, in deepened slumber, they came to me. Larger than life, a shadow of stars that rose up around me and whispered my name in a crescendo that threatened to boil my brain. A roar of imperious inquiry surged in my veins, and when it finally subsided, only one question remained:

What did I want?

Knowledge. Percipience. Enlightenment.

How simple. 
Quaint and predictable. 

The words rang in my ears like a gong. 

Then we will REMAKE you, 
to guide your path toward all knowledge, 
and you will be bound to a 
T H O U S A N D D E A T H S. 

On that last breath, you will submit, 
claimed forever, 
made and unmade among the specter of the stars, 
until the end of time.

I did not have to think. Did not have to see or speak. All I needed… was to know.

—An excerpt from "The Tragical Scribe"
3901262988.text_zh:
我曾经是个学者。在那些大机器影响之外的人群中享有巨大声誉。在这里，我告诉我的氏族。看到真相，和我一起说出来。他们拒绝了，所以我离开了，在他们乖戾的信仰面前我无能为力。

寒风萧瑟刺骨，没有空热材料能来温暖我。地形危机四伏，没有散射披肩能来保护我。 

我孤身一人，在厚厚的积雪下日渐消瘦。

但后来，正当我沉睡之时，他们来找我。群星之影十分显眼地在我四周冉冉升起，低声呼唤我的名字，声音越来越强，我的脑袋都快炸了。我的血管里涌动着强烈的质问，而当它最终平息下来时，只剩下一个问题：

我想要什么？

学识。洞察。启迪。

多简单啊。 
古怪又老套。 

这些话语如同铜锣一般在我耳边回响。 

那我们就重塑你， 
指引你通往所有知识的道路， 
而你将会成为一名 
千亡者。 

咽下最后一口气时，你将屈服， 
永世为奴， 
在星辰幻影之中被创造和毁灭， 
直至时间的尽头。

我不需要思考。不需要看见也不需要言语。我只需要…知晓。

——摘自《悲惨文士》

3901262989.name: Chapter 15
3901262989.text:
The bar of The Ether Tank was packed with the City's patrons, Eliksni or otherwise. The forlorn drinkers. The karaoke enthusiasts. The social gamblers. Spider casually listened to the fervor as he scrolled through figures on his datapad, calculating his fortunes. 

Neon light reflected along the silver snake design of the Constricting Shell disguise that Immaru wore. Archie trotted beside him as he approached.

"I have a proposition for you," Immaru said, but Spider simply continued to read. "If I have to repeat myself, I'll—"

"Do it, and you'll be next in my collection," Spider replied and turned suddenly to face him, an empty Ghost shell held tight in his claws. 

"You have no idea who you're messing with," Immaru sneered.

Spider bent down to look directly at the Ghost, eyes to eye. "Oh. I absolutely… do. Now get out!"

"Candy is the driving currency around here right now. For everything," Immaru said quickly. "I got the means to extract it. Adjust the economics for the City, if you will. But I need someone with access to storage. Lots of it."

Spider paused for a moment. "What's the cut?"

"Fifteen percent. I'll also need tech for Archie here to quickly transmat the goods over long distances to a big facility," Immaru promised sweetly.

"Fifty percent," Spider responded.

"Fifty percent for storage?"

"The tech, the storage, and everything that goes with it."

"You're outta your mind. Fifteen."

"Sixty percent. Take it or leave it."

Immaru narrowed his iris. "Fifty."

"Sixty," Spider said again, and then turned to Archie. "And what about you—you agree with this?"

Archie barked excitedly, and Spider steepled his fingers. "Looks like we have a deal."
3901262989.text_zh:
乙太罐酒吧里挤满了圣城的顾客，埃里克斯尼族或其他人。孤独的酒客。K歌爱好者。社交赌徒。蛛王在数据板上滚动数字，计算着自己的财富，漫不经心地听着这热烈的氛围。 

霓虹灯沿着伊马鲁身上收缩机壳伪装的银蛇设计反射着。他靠近时，阿奇小跑跟在他身边。

“我有个提议给你，”伊马鲁说，但蛛王只是继续看着数字。“要我再说一遍的话，我会——”

“你会成为我下一个收藏品，”蛛王回答道，突然转过身来面对着他，爪子里紧紧攥着一个机灵空壳。 

“你根本不知道你惹的是谁，”伊马鲁讥讽道。

蛛王弯下腰，直视着机灵。“哦。我当然…知道。滚出去！”

“糖果现在是这里的主导货币。可以买一切东西，”伊马鲁脱口而出。“我有办法弄到它。你可以认为我是在调节圣城的经济。但我需要有仓库的人。非常大的仓库。”

蛛王停顿了一会儿。“怎么分成？”

“百分之十五。我还需要技术，让这位阿奇快速地将货物远距离传送到一个大设施里，”伊马鲁温和地承诺道。

“百分之五十，”蛛王答道。

“仓储值百分之五十？”

“技术、仓储，以及相关的一切。”

“你疯了。十五。”

“六十五。要么接受，要么滚蛋。”

伊马鲁眯起了他的眼睛。“五十。”

“六十，”蛛王再次发话，然后转向了阿奇。“你呢——你同意吗？”

阿奇兴奋地叫着，蛛王做出一个塔尖式手势。“看来我们成交了。”

3901262990.name: Chapter 16
3901262990.text:
"It's the cutest cloak, Elsie. You have to see it," Ana gushed over her earpiece as she tinkered in her workshop. Her computer suddenly flashed with a notification, and she frowned.

"You could dress that dog in a paper bag, and he'd still be inconceivably adorable," Elsie said.

The line was silent.

"…Ana? Are you still there?" Elsie asked.

"Hm?" Ana responded, focused on the computer screen.

Elsie laughed. "I'll call back later."

"No, wait," Ana exclaimed, her brow knitted with worry. "Sorry, I just… something's wrong with Archie."

"Is he hurt?" Elsie asked anxiously.

"No. But I just got a diagnostics report from him. The second one today. I thought the first one was a fluke." She sighed. "He must have a bad subroutine running. I'm just going to have to do a full workup on him."

"What do the reports say?"

"Lots of stuff. But the one constant is the chemical equations… formulas and compounds… carbon 12, hydrogen 22, oxygen 11. Carbon 6, hydrogen 8, oxygen 7. Ratios of crystalline carbohydrates. Amorphous ones. Carrageenan. Invertase. Theobromine. Individually, these make no sense. But synthesized in certain sequences, it's—"

"Candy?"
3901262990.text_zh:
“这披风再可爱不过了，艾尔西。你一定得看看，”阿娜一边在作坊里焊补，一边对着耳机滔滔不绝。她的电脑突然闪过一条通知，她皱起了眉头。

“你可以给那只狗穿上纸袋，他依然会可爱得不得了，”艾尔西说道。

通讯的另一头没有人搭话。

“…阿娜？你还在吗？”艾尔西问道。

“嗯？”阿娜回答道，专心地盯着电脑屏幕。

艾尔西笑了。“我一会儿再打过来。”

“不，等等，”阿娜喊道，她的眉头担忧地皱了起来。“对不起，我只是…阿奇有点不太对劲。”

“他受伤了吗？”艾尔西焦急地问。

“没有。但我刚收到他的诊断报告。今天的第二份。我以为第一份是意外。”她叹了口气。“他肯定是有个子程序运行不正常。我得给他做个全面检查。”

“报告怎么说？”

“很多东西。但共通的一点就是化学方程式…分子式和化合物…碳12，氢22，氧11。碳6，氢8，氧7。晶体碳水化合物的比例。非晶体的。卡拉胶。转化酶。可可碱。这些东西单独来看都没有意义。但按照一定的顺序合成，那就是——”

“糖果？”

3901262991.name: Chapter 17
3901262991.text:
Immaru was analyzing their take for the day when Spider called.

"You think I'm stupid?" Spider grumbled. 

"I don't know what you're talking about," Immaru said cooly.

"The numbers don't add up. The load assessed from your canine is not what my lackeys are… calculating in the warehouse."

"I ain't skimming from you. Maybe check your lackeys."

"These numbers keep coming in skewed and the deal's off, understand? Then you can kiss your 40% goodbye. Oh, and another thing. I keep seeing Guardians going to the Tower for their candy. Fix it," Spider demanded and hung up.

"Hmm. Maybe this isn't enough," Immaru said to Archie. The dog looked at him quizzically.

"We're going to have to go bigger. And Headless."
3901262991.text_zh:
蛛王来电时，伊马鲁正在分析他们当天的收入。

“你以为我是傻子吗？”蛛王抱怨道。 

“我不知道你在说些什么，”伊马鲁冷冷地说。

“这些数字不对。你的小狗评估的负荷和我的手下在仓库里…计算的不一样。”

“我没撇你的利润。也许你该检查一下你的手下。”

“这些数字要是继续不准确，交易可就泡汤了，懂吗？然后你就可以和你的40%说再见了。哦，还有一件事。我总看到守护者去高塔拿糖果。搞定这件事，”蛛王提出要求，挂了电话。

“嗯。也许这还不够，”伊马鲁对阿奇说道。机械狗疑惑地看着他。

“我们必须做得更大。从无头者下手。”

3901262976.name: Chapter 18
3901262976.text:
"Hey!" Immaru called out. The walls inside the Derelict creaked and groaned in response, shuttering as if the cobbled halls would suddenly rip apart. 

He was alone.

Immaru wandered through the ship until he stumbled on shelves of containment glass that lined the walls. A jar held eyeballs that roiled slowly in a viscous liquid, their stare following Immaru. There were hundreds of odd samples and organisms. Some could have still been alive, but he wasn't willing to find out.

Up ahead, he heard an impossibly low utterance. The infrasonic vibrations melded into a droning moan and swelled into something indescribable. The sound traveled toward him, closer and closer. 

And then… it stopped. 

Everything stopped.

Immaru turned, face-to-face with the blood-red eye of another Ghost.

"Get back!" Immaru shrieked. 

The red-eyed Ghost complied. Its eye seemed to bug outward from the grotesque and malformed patchwork shell that twisted and hunched to one side. The Ghost hung lopsided in the air, as if it was dragging the weight of the world.

"Is… is Drifter here?"

The Ghost's iris rapidly flickered from red to blue in a hypnotic pattern.

"Guess I'll take that as a no. You, uh, got a name there, pal?"

The other Ghost's eye immediately went solid red, its gaze still steady on Immaru. 

"Right. Uh, Drifter—Drifter has some goods on the Headless Ones. Mind if I borrow them? Anything you got."

The other Ghost floated over to a container marked "Cabal brains" and stroked the lid lovingly with its shell.

"No!" Immaru yelped. "No, uh, I don't need those brains… no, don't need those either. No, no—you can keep the eyes too."

The silent Ghost bobbed around Immaru and slid its flap down his shell. It pulled him close, until it grazed Immaru's iris.

"You're busy, I'll come back—never," Immaru whispered as he hurriedly released himself and transmatted away.
3901262976.text_zh:
“嘿！”伊马鲁叫道。遗落飞船里的墙壁吱吱作响，发出低沉的声音以示回应，震颤得仿佛那些鹅卵石大厅会突然崩裂。 

这里只有他。

伊马鲁在飞船里漫游，直到他偶然发现了排列在墙上放着玻璃容器的架子。一个罐子里装着眼球，它们在某种粘稠的液体中慢慢翻滚着，目光跟随着伊马鲁。那里头有上百个奇怪的样本和有机体。有些可能还活着，但他不想找出答案。

前方传来一个低得难以置信的声音。次声波的振动混合进嗡嗡的呻吟声，逐渐增大成某种难以形容的声响。那声音向他传来，越来越近。 

然后…它停了下来。 

一切都停了下来。

伊马鲁转过身，碰上了另一个有着血红色眼睛的机灵。

“退后！”伊马鲁尖叫道。 

红眼机灵照办了。它的眼睛似乎从扭曲弯缩到一侧的怪诞畸形的缝合机壳中向外突出着。那机灵失衡地悬在空中，仿佛在拖拽着世界的重量。

“浪客…在吗？”

那机灵的虹膜迅速从红色变为蓝色，以催眠的模式闪烁着。

“我就当是不在了。你，呃，有名字吗，伙计？”

那机灵的眼睛立刻变红，目光依然坚定地盯着伊马鲁。 

“好吧。呃，浪客——浪客有一些无头者的东西。我能借一下吗？什么都行。”

那机灵飘到一个标有“卡巴尔大脑”的容器旁，用它的机壳怜爱地触碰着盖子。

“不！”伊马鲁大叫起来。“不，呃，我不需要那些大脑…不，也不需要那些。不，不——那些眼睛你也可以留着。”

默不作声的机灵在伊马鲁周围盘旋，朝他的机壳垂下襟翼。它把他拉近，直到擦过伊马鲁的眼睛。

“你很忙，我会回来——才怪，”伊马鲁低声说道，匆忙地挣脱，传送离开了。

3901262977.name: Chapter 19
3901262977.text:
Back in the Last City, Immaru and Archie reviewed their data of the Headless Ones from a computer terminal.

"I think this is everything. Drifter was a no go," Immaru said. Archie whined in response.

"I don't wanna talk about it. He—he didn't have anything we could use. Look, we got ourselves Glint and Eido's research. And the goods I snagged from the Guardian while in the field. There's plenty here to work from."

Archie gave him a doubtful look.

Immaru donned his Hive shell and sighed. "You'll see. Now go find me some supplies. We got work to do."
3901262977.text_zh:
回到圣城中后，伊马鲁和阿奇从电脑终端检查了他们的无头者数据。

“我想就是这些了。浪客这条路行不通，”伊马鲁说道。阿奇哀鸣着回应着。

“我不想提这事。他——他手里没有任何我们能用的东西。听着，我们拿到了格林特和艾多的研究成果。还有我实地从守护者那里拿来的货物。这里有很多可以入手的线索。”

阿奇怀疑地看了他一眼。

伊马鲁穿上邪魔族机壳，叹了口气。“等着瞧吧。先去给我找些补给来。我们还有活儿要干。”

3951595841.name: Chapter 20
3951595841.text:
"What do you think?" Eido asked hopefully as Mithrax placed her datapad on the table in front of him.

"They are… good," he finally admitted.

"Really?" she exclaimed.

He nodded. "Especially the 'Tragical Scribe.' To sacrifice one's freedom for boundless knowledge—it is a sorrowful yet troubling tale. I believe everyone will enjoy these stories. Including the hatchlings. But Eido, I must caution you."

"The descriptions can be long sometimes, I know, but I think I can—"

"No, you misunderstand. My… apprehension is for you. You are a keeper of history and a seeker of truth. By publishing these stories, you conflate your name, your honor-trust as Scribe, with untruths."

Eido frowned and considered for a moment. "…Why can't I do both?"

Mithrax sighed. "Because history may not be able to tell the difference."
3951595841.text_zh:
“你觉得怎么样？”当米瑟拉克斯把她的数据板放到面前的桌上时，艾多满怀希望地问道。

“挺…好的，”他终于承认道。

“真的？”她惊呼道。

他点了点头。“尤其是《悲惨文士》。为了无限的知识牺牲自己的自由——这是个悲伤又令人不安的故事。我相信大家都会喜欢这些故事。包括孩子们。但艾多，我必须提醒你。”

“描写有时比较冗长，这我知道，但我想我可以——”

“不，你误会了。我…担心的是你。你是历史的守护者，也是真理的追寻者。而发表这些故事，会把你的名字、你作为文士的信誉和那些虚假混在一起。”

艾多皱起眉头，思忖了一会儿。“…为什么我不能两者兼顾呢？”

米瑟拉克斯叹了口气。“因为历史可能无法分辨其中的区别。”

3951595840.name: Chapter 21
3951595840.text:
Nightfall was never quite as dark when the Last City celebrated the Festival of the Lost. Lanterns cast a pastel mosaic over the people; glowing candles illuminated their offerings for the dead.

A lone Hunter wandered among the memorials and stopped to look at each one. Sometimes flowers, sometimes food. Sometimes well-loved trinkets or handwritten notes of remembrance and love. Photos, children's drawings.

He watched an Eliksni mother place a delicate scrap of eggcloth, then suddenly knelt beside her. He felt the wax of the lavender-hued candle already in his hand, the wick clean and bright. He moved to light it, to place it among the offerings. And then—

He stopped.

The Hunter's expression was gentle and warm as he held the candle out to the Eliksni mother.

"For your little one," he simply said. She hesitated, then thanked him in her language.

He abruptly left and continued on through the Tower, wandering past the Bazaar, into the Courtyard. Until, finally, he looked up and realized… he was standing in the one place he hated to be.
3951595840.text_zh:
以往圣城庆祝英灵日时，日落从未如此黑暗过。灯笼在人们身上投下了一幅淡雅的镶嵌图案；烛光照亮了他们为逝者献上的祭品。

有一名孤独的猎人在纪念碑群之间徘徊着，每一座都停下来看一看。有时是鲜花，有时是食物。有时是心爱的小饰品或留念与爱的手写便条。还有照片、孩子们的画。

他看着一位埃里克斯尼族母亲放上一块精致的卵布，然后突然跪在她身边。他感到淡紫色蜡烛的蜡已经滴落在他手里了，烛芯干净而明亮。他上前点燃，准备把它放到祭品之中。然后——

他停了下来。

猎人把蜡烛递给埃里克斯尼族母亲，表情温和而热情。

“给你的小宝贝，”他简单地说。她犹豫了一下，然后用她的语言向他道谢。

他突然离开，继续穿过高塔，走过集市，进入庭院。直到最后他抬头发现…自己正站在一个他不想待的地方。

3951595843.name: Chapter 22
3951595843.text:
The memorials left at Amanda's workshop were many. Too many for Zavala to count. He moved them aside, assessing the damage left by Colonel's rampage through the Tower from earlier that day.

"So many feathers," he mused. He pulled back a canvas covering Amanda's belongings to clean up the broken candles scattered beneath. A container of nuts and bolts fell from a workbench. Zavala gasped as they rained down, and he rushed to collect them before they could roll away. He opted to place them in a drawer for safe keeping, and as he did, his fingers brushed against a folded piece of paper. He opened it.

A colorful drawing. Not of ships. Not of adventure. But of a large, blue Titan and a smiling little girl.

Tears welled in his eyes, and he held the drawing close.

"Can't sleep?" a quiet voice asked.

Zavala looked up to find Crow standing in front of him. "I suppose I could ask the same of you," Zavala replied instead.

"Want some company?"

Zavala nodded and gently pocketed the drawing. He looked around at the uncovered workspace. At the half-full mug of coffee. The single welder's glove. The datapads and blueprints, shop rags and tools.

"I always knew I'd have to… face this task eventually. Tonight feels, well, right," Zavala said. He lovingly picked up a spanner. "I need to find a good home for her tools. Someone who will really appreciate them."

Crow gave him a slight smile. "I think I might know someone."
3951595843.text_zh:
阿曼达的作坊留下了许多纪念物。太多了，多到萨瓦拉数不过来。他把它们移到一边，评估着那天早些时候上校在高塔里横冲直撞造成的损失。

“太多羽毛了，”他若有所思地说。他拉开一块帆布，盖住阿曼达的东西，清理着底下散落的碎蜡烛。一个装螺母和螺栓的容器从工作台上掉了下来。它们如雨点般落下，萨瓦拉倒抽一口气，赶在它们滚走之前收起来。他选择把它们放在抽屉里妥善保管，在那样做时，他的手指触碰到一张折叠的纸。他打开了它。

一幅彩色的画。画的不是飞船。不是探险。而是一个高大的蓝色泰坦和一个微笑的小女孩。

他的眼中噙满泪水，他紧紧地抓住那幅画。

“睡不着？”一个安静的声音问道。

萨瓦拉抬头发现乌鸦站在他的面前。“我想我也能问你同样的问题，”萨瓦拉回答道。

“想要个伴吗？”

萨瓦拉点点头，轻轻把画放进口袋。他看了看四周没有遮盖的工作区。喝了一半的咖啡。单个的焊工手套。数据板和蓝图，车间抹布和工具。

“我一直知道我终究得…面对这任务。今晚感觉，嗯，挺合适，”萨瓦拉说。他温情地拿起一个扳手。“我需要为她的工具找一个好归宿。一个会真正珍惜它们的主人。”

乌鸦微微一笑。“我想我也许认识某个合适的人选。”

3951595842.name: Chapter 23
3951595842.text:
In the depths of the Tower, Immaru cobbled together a prototype torso for his monster with patchwork remnants of deceased Headless Ones, fragments of pumpkin stolen while tagging along with the Guardian. Missing sections were filled in: the left arm of a deceased Ogre; the right, ripped from a freshly made Thrall. Immaru worked well into the night, wiring and welding and seaming and cutting.

Finally, it was ready. 

Immaru sent a current flowing through the wires and ran siphoned Ether into his creation. The chest began to swell and heave, as if it were breathing. The eyes glowed bright blue and Ether poured from its ragged mouth. The monster torso pulled itself upright and dragged itself, a trail of seeds and fibrous orange flesh left behind along the table. The Headless One set its gaze upon its maker.

And then, it grabbed him.

The monster's Ogre arm gripped Immaru's shell with all its strength and pulled him toward its mouth as Ether vapor rolled over the Ghost's eye. Without warning, the head cracked at the seams. It split apart, splattering across the floor, the torso slumped lifeless against the table.
3951595842.text_zh:
在高塔的深处，伊马鲁用死去无头者的残骸和跟随守护者时偷来的南瓜碎片拼凑出了他的怪物原型躯干。缺失的部分得补上：一个死去虫瘤的左臂；右臂则是从新做的怨魂身上扯下来的。伊马鲁一直工作到深夜，接线、焊接、缝合、切割。

终于准备完毕。 

伊马鲁让电流流过电线，将虹吸的乙太注入他的造物之中。胸腔开始膨胀和起伏，仿佛它在呼吸一样。它的眼睛闪烁着明亮的蓝色光芒，从它粗糙的嘴里吐出乙太。怪物的躯干挺直了身子，拖拽着自己，在桌子上留下了一串种子和纤维状的橙色血肉。无头者凝视着它的创造者。

然后，它抓住了他。

怪物的虫瘤手臂用尽力量抓住伊马鲁的机壳，把他拉向自己的嘴边，乙太蒸汽在机灵的眼睛上涌流。脑袋毫无征兆地在接缝处裂开。它分崩离析，溅洒在地板上，躯干则毫无生气地倒在桌子上。

3951595845.name: Chapter 24
3951595845.text:
When Eido found Ikora, she was meditating beneath a jacaranda tree, away from the noise of the Bazaar.

"Is there something you need?" Ikora asked, amusement apparent in her voice, her eyes still closed.

"I'm sorry to disturb you," Eido said.

"Not at all," Ikora replied. She patted the ground beside her. "Glint tells me you have aspirations of becoming an author of scary stories. How are you doing?"

"It was going well at first. I had so many ideas! But now, I think I'm 'blocked' as Glint put it. I thought that writing could help me handle my fears. I've been… very scared of a lot of things lately."

Ikora looked at her knowingly. "Eris," she simply said.

Eido nodded. "But my writing is not improving in spite of my fear; it is suffering from it. When we used the Deck of Whispers—"

Ikora quirked an eyebrow, and Eido raised one of her hands. "I know, I know, Glint said he left a note. The cards made me realize that there are so many different sources of fear in the universe. A multitude of threats. Of unknowns. Perhaps that has become my greatest source of dread."

"It's important to be honest with yourself and what you're feeling," Ikora replied kindly. "You are not alone in these thoughts, these fears. But don't let the cards distract you. They are not meant to tell your fortune or future. They are meant as a guide, a form of insight into yourself. You are the one who ascertains a course of action. Not the cards."
3951595845.text_zh:
艾多找到艾可拉时，她正在一棵蓝花楹树下冥想，远离集市的喧嚣。

“你需要些什么吗？”艾可拉问道，声音中透着愉悦，她的眼睛仍然闭着。

“很抱歉打扰你，”艾多说。

“没关系，”艾可拉回答道。她拍了拍身旁的地面。“格林特告诉我，你渴望成为一名恐怖故事作家。进展如何？”

“一开始很顺利。我有好多的想法！但现在，按格林特的话讲，我有点“哽住”了。我以为写作能帮我克服恐惧。我最近…对很多事情都感到害怕。”

艾可拉心神意会地看着她。“是埃里斯吧，”她一语道破。

艾多点点头。“尽管我很害怕，但我的写作并没有进步；而是很煎熬。当我们用低语卡组的时候——”

艾可拉皱了一下眉毛，艾多举起了一只手。“我知道，我知道，格林特说他留了张纸条。这些卡牌让我意识到宇宙中有如此多不同的恐惧来源。有太多威胁，太多未知。也许这已经成为了我害怕的最主要原因。”

“诚实面对自己和自己的感受是很重要的，”艾可拉和蔼地回答。“有这些想法和恐惧的不止你一个。但别让那些卡牌干扰你。它们不是用来预言你的命运或未来的。它们是一种指引，一种让你洞察自我的方式。你才是决定如何行动的人。而不是那些卡牌。”

3951595844.name: Chapter 25
3951595844.text:
Immaru and Archie nervously stared at their second assembled prototype on the table.

The tech knitted through the salvaged organic components had been upgraded: a Cabal sword replaced its right hand. Splicer wiring wove through its left arm. Vex milk coursed throughout its veins. The rest had been completely pieced together from carefully procured Headless One parts, reassembled into a patchwork of organic horror. It oozed a dark, gelatinous liquid from its seams and smelled of death.

Next to the body was the final piece: a perfectly intact pumpkin head. Archie sniffed and pawed at the dormant head, and the pumpkin rocked from side to side.

"Careful," Immaru snapped. "Those things don't sever easily without exploding." He shuddered. "One favor to Drifter is enough."

Immaru attached the head to the body. A perfect, mutilated fit. He opened the chest cavity, the flesh stretching and tearing as he inserted a discolored Hive crystal inside. Energy surged though the Headless monster, and a haunting red light flickered inside its head. It howled and snarled as it sat up.

"Ahahaha, it's perfect. Perfect!" Immaru mused with glee. "You want candy, huh? You crave it. Need it," Immaru said to the monster. It ambled forward and swiped its good arm at him in response.

"Then go out there and get it. All of it," Immaru said. The monster found its footing and began to hurry toward the door. Archie growled and raced after it as Immaru giggled with delight.

"Now the real fun begins."
3951595844.text_zh:
伊马鲁和阿奇紧张地盯着桌子上第二个组装好的原型。

通过回收的有机部件编织起来的技术已经升级：一把卡巴尔的刀剑取代了它的右手。它的左臂缠绕着熔岩军团电线。Vex奶白色液体在它的血管中流淌。其余部分都是用精心找来的无头者器官拼凑起来的，重新组装成了一个有机恐怖的缝合怪。它从接缝处渗出一种黑色的胶状液体，散发着死亡的气息。

身体旁边是最后一块组件：一个完好无损的南瓜头。阿奇嗅了嗅，用爪子抓了抓那个沉睡的头颅，南瓜左右晃动着。

“小心点，”伊马鲁厉声说。“这些东西不爆炸就不会轻易断裂。”他哆嗦了一下。“帮浪客一个忙就够了。”

伊马鲁将头部固定在身体上。完美而残缺的契合。他打开胸腔，将一块褪色的邪魔族水晶插进去，其血肉伸展撕裂开来。能量在无头怪物的体内涌动，一道挥之不去的红光在它的头里闪烁。它一边坐起来，一边嚎叫着。

“啊哈哈，太完美了。完美！”伊马鲁高兴地思忖道。“你想要糖果哈？你很渴望，很需要它，”伊马鲁对怪物说。它缓缓走上前，用那只完好的胳膊朝他一挥以示回应。

“那就出去抢。把糖果全抢走，”伊马鲁说道。那怪物站稳了脚跟，开始向门口跑去。阿奇咆哮着跟在它身后飞奔，伊马鲁高兴得咯咯直笑。

“真正有趣的事开始了。”

3951595847.name: Chapter 26
3951595847.text:
The Headless One quickly made its way to the Bazaar. Vendors scattered. People grabbed hatchlings and children, running in every which direction.

Glint and Eido watched in horror as the Headless One lashed out and shoved a rotisserie over, quickly catching nearby booths on fire. It ripped apart a display of candy, devouring every last piece in sight. And when it was gone, the monster continued its rampage. It tore through lanterns, pulling them apart as if searching for something. It smashed fruit from one booth, threw vegetables from another. Frustrated, it began to claw at a drawing of candy on the ground, a fistful of decorations in its good hand as it shrieked with a blood-curdling scream.
3951595847.text_zh:
无头者迅速地向集市走去。商人四散奔逃。人们抱起孩子，东逃西窜。

格林特和艾多惊恐地看着无头者猛地发威，把一个烤炉推翻，附近的摊位很快烧了起来。它撕毁了陈列出的糖果，把看到的每一块都吃掉。吃完之后，怪物继续肆虐。它撕破灯笼，把它们扯成碎片，就像是在寻找什么东西。它砸碎了某个摊位上的水果，扔了另一个摊位上的蔬菜。它十分沮丧，开始抓地上一幅画着糖果的画，完好的手上握着一把装饰物，发出了声嘶力竭的尖叫。

3951595846.name: Chapter 27
3951595846.text:
"A Headless One?!" Eido and Glint exclaimed in unison as Archie raced up beside them.

"We need help. I'll go find Crow!" Glint said.

"There's no time. The longer we wait, the more dangerous this monster becomes, and someone could be killed. We have to stop it now!" Eido replied. She hastily analyzed the composition of the monster. "It's not like the Headless Ones we've studied before. Look at its appendages… is that Vex milk?"

"I think so," Glint said. "Saccharomyces cerevisiae and sucrose react with Vex milk. If my calculations are correct, the chemical reaction creates a mass in what Humans categorize as a 'toothpaste.' If the excreted gas gets caught—"

"The point, Glint!"

"The Headless One would break apart without putting anyone in danger!" he quickly shouted.

"It would have to ingest the catalyst," Eido surmised.

"Exactly. But it's not like we can force feed it bread. It eats candy."

Archie barked repeatedly beside them.

"I—don't speak dog," Glint said, and Eido shrugged. Archie growled and then transmatted a pile of candy onto the ground.

Eido and Glint exchanged a look of surprise. "That'll work," she said.
3951595846.text_zh:
“无头者？！”阿奇跑到他们身边时，艾多和格林特异口同声地叫道。

“我们需要帮助。我去找乌鸦！”格林特说道。

“没时间了。我们等得越久，这个怪物就会变得越危险，甚至可能杀人。我们必须马上阻止它！”艾多答道。她急忙分析了怪物的构成。“它不像我们以前研究过的无头者。看看它那些附器…那是Vex奶白色液体吗？”

“我想是的，”格林特说道。“酿酒酵母菌和蔗糖与Vex奶白色液体发生反应。如果我计算无误的话，这种化学反应会产生一种被人类归类为“牙膏”的物质。如果分泌的气体被捕获——”

“说重点，格林特！”

“无头者就会在不危及任何人的情况下自行解体！”他迅速喊道。

“那它必须得摄入催化，”艾多推测说。

“没错。但们没法强行喂它面包。它吃的是糖果。”

阿奇在他们旁边不停地狂吠。

“我——没法和狗沟通，”格林特说，艾多耸耸肩。阿奇咆哮了一声，然后把一堆糖果传送到了地上。

艾多和格林特惊讶地看了彼此一眼。“这样应该就行了，”她说道。

3951595849.name: Chapter 28
3951595849.text:
Eido raced to a nearby vendor table of Eliksni baked goods and swiped the biggest loaf she could find. Her four hands worked furiously, tearing off chunks of bread and wrapping them in candy wrappers, and she suddenly realized she was very glad to be Eliksni. 

"Eido!" Glint yelled. 

She looked up and saw the Headless One barreling toward them and the assorted pile of "candy" at her feet. They scrambled out of the way just as the Headless One descended on the colorful wrappers. It devoured everything without a second glance.

But nothing happened.

"I don't understand," Glint said. "That should have worked!"

"Perhaps there is a chamber inside? Something to hold the Vex milk as it distributes around the body?" Eido asked.

"We're going to find out," Glint said. He zipped toward the Headless One, scanning it as it swiped furiously at him. "The chest!" he called out, just as the monster batted him away. Glint spun through the air, dizzy but unharmed.

Archie barked and immediately rushed to action, enticing the Headless One to chase him. The dog led it toward the kettle corn stand, weaving quickly through its legs. The monster stumbled and Archie leapt forward, giving it a solid shove. The monster caught the massive cast iron kettle, pulling it down as it fell to the ground. The kettle landed on its chest with a solid crunch, pouring popcorn and hot, liquid sugar into the Headless One's body. 

The monster howled in pain and pried itself free. It swayed as it stood, Vex milk bubbling from its chest wound. Crow, Zavala, and Ana rushed forward with Glint beside them, and Eido pushed them away. "Get back!" she yelled and took cover. 

The Headless One screamed again, its body expanding, the edges of the pumpkin head splitting and cracking. Suddenly—the monster exploded, erupting in a rainbow of foam that rose thick and high into the sky before cascading in a sticky sea, coating the entire Bazaar.
3951595849.text_zh:
艾多跑到附近一个卖埃里克斯尼族烘焙食品的摊贩桌前，拿走了她能找到的最大的一条面包。她用四只手狂乱地撕下面包块，用糖纸把它们包起来，她突然意识到她很庆幸自己是埃里克斯尼族。 

“艾多！”格林特喊道。 

她抬头看见无头者正朝他们，还有她脚下一堆各色各样的“糖果”飞奔而来。他们在无头者扑向五颜六色的糖纸时赶紧闪开。它毫不迟疑地吞掉了一切。

但是什么也没发生。

“我不明白，”格林特说。“那应该起作用才对！”

“也许里面有个腔体？Vex奶白色液体在身体各处流动时，用来容纳它的东西？”艾多问道。

“我们会找出答案的，”格林特说道。他飞快地奔向无头者，在它愤怒地向他扑来之际进行扫描。“胸腔！”他在怪物把他击飞时高喊道。格林特在空中旋转，头晕目眩，但没有受伤。

阿奇吠叫着，立即冲上前去，引诱无头者追赶他。机械狗把它引向了爆米花摊位，在它的两腿间快速穿梭。怪物踉跄了一下，阿奇向前一跃，猛地推了它一把。怪物抓着巨大的铸铁锅，倒在地上时把它拉了下来。铁锅落在它胸前，发出坚实的碎裂声，将爆米花和滚烫的液体糖浆灌入了无头者的身体。 

怪物痛苦地嚎叫着，挣脱开来。它站起时摇晃着，胸口的伤口汩汩地冒着Vex奶白色液体。乌鸦、萨瓦拉和阿娜向前冲去，格林特跟在他们旁边，而艾多则把他们推开。“退后！”她喊道，找了个地方躲起来。 

无头者再度尖叫，它的身体在膨胀，南瓜头的边缘裂开。突然之间——怪物爆炸了，喷出一道彩虹般的泡沫，又厚又高，直冲云霄，然后倾泻成粘稠的茫茫一片，涂满了整个集市。

3951595848.name: Chapter 29
3951595848.text:
The remains of the festival stands laid in a heap, everything and everyone covered in a layer of rancid, foamy pumpkin ooze.

Immaru drifted by, almost dancing through the air as he surveyed the destruction. "Did you see that? It was like a giant, foamy SCREEB!" he laughed. "Better than anything I could have imagined!"

"You did this?!" Crow exclaimed, and Immaru tipped his Hive shell toward him in response.

"I just set the events in motion. Your little friends there finished the job. This sticky substance, haha, is amazing, by the way. No notes! Definitely worth the look on your faces right now," he cackled and floated away. "Happy Festival of the Lost, meatbags!"
3951595848.text_zh:
节日摊位的残留物堆在一起，所有东西和每个人都沾上了一层腐臭、泡沫状的南瓜泥。

伊马鲁飘着巡视毁坏的场面，就差在空中跳起舞来。“你们看到了吗？就像一个巨大的、泡沫般的变异体！”他笑着说。“比我想象的还精彩！”

“这是你干的？！”乌鸦叫道，伊马鲁向前倾了一下他的邪魔族机壳以示回应。

“我只不过是设定了事件的发展方向。是你的那些小朋友们完成了任务。顺便说一句，这种粘稠的物质，哈哈，太神奇了。完美无缺！你们现在脸上的表情绝对值得一看，”他咯咯笑着飘走了。“英灵日快乐，肉包子们！”

3934818286.name: Chapter 30
3934818286.text:
"What a mess," Eido said. "The destruction of the Bazaar's festival space is disheartening. The substance created in the explosion is, well, much stickier than we calculated."

"Not to mention the smell," Zavala said, covering his nose. "This is… unbearable."

Ana swiped a sample of the material from her shoulder. "Hm. It's disgusting, but still just organic material. When I was performing some diagnostics on Archie the other day, I noticed a 'clean up' protocol buried in his subroutines, but I couldn't access the code. Maybe we could ask him to try it out here."

"What does he do with it? Put everything in a pile? …Eat it?" Crow asked.

Ana shrugged. "Only one way to find out. Archie? Would you be willing to run it?"

Archie barked and got to work.
3934818286.text_zh:
“真是一团糟，”艾多说。“集市节日场地被毁实在叫人沮丧。爆炸产生的物质，呃，比我们计算的要粘稠得多。”

“更别提那股气味了，”萨瓦拉捂着鼻子说。“这真是…让人受不了。”

阿娜从她的肩膀上取了一些样品。“嗯。很恶心，但依然是有机材料。前几天我对阿奇进行诊断时，我注意到他的子程序中隐藏着一个‘清理'协议，但我无法访问代码。也许我们可以让他在这里试试。”

“他会拿它做什么？把所有东西都堆起来？…吃掉？”乌鸦问道。

阿娜耸耸肩。“试试就知道了。阿奇？你愿意运行它吗？”

阿奇吠了一声就开始工作了。

3934818287.name: Chapter 31
3934818287.text:
Deep in the bowels of one of Spider's warehouses, he gripped the neck of a warehouse worker. "So tell me something. When the rule 'no stealing' was explained to you, which part did you not understand?"

The worker struggled against Spider's grip. "I—I didn't steal the candy!"

"You know what's worse than stealing from me? Lying to me about it!" Spider snarled. "I'll have you—"

He stopped suddenly, sniffing the air, and immediately dropped the worker as his gag reflex kicked in. "What's that smell?!"

He looked up, only to see a barrage of brightly colored foam and rancid pumpkin rain down on his head.
3934818287.text_zh:
在蛛王的某个仓库的深处，他掐住了一个仓库工人的脖子。“说吧。我跟你解释‘禁止偷窃'的规则时，你哪一条没听懂？”

工人挣扎着想挣脱蛛王的钳制。“我——我没有偷糖果！”

“你知道什么比偷我的东西更糟糕吗？对我撒谎！”蛛王咆哮道。“我要你——”

他突然停下来，嗅了嗅空气，感到一阵恶心，就放下了工人。“那是什么气味？！”

他抬起头，看见一连串五彩缤纷的泡沫和腐臭的南瓜像雨点一样落到了他的头上。

3934818284.name: Chapter 32
3934818284.text:
As Crow and Zavala made their way through the Eliksni Quarter, they passed a cluster of young Eliksni gathered around a mechanical dog. One hatchling ran forward and stopped short in front of Zavala, her four arms full of candy. She looked up at him and chittered with delight. A chuckle escaped Zavala's lips, and he was surprised by his own sudden smile. Crow waved him on, and they eventually found themselves in front of a small but impressive workshop. A Sparrow sat suspended on a lift, thrusters removed. An Eliksni tinkered beneath.

"It's coming along," Crow called out. The teenage mechanic jerked in surprise and hit her head on the Sparrow. She muttered an Eliksni phrase under her breath.

"Itzelas, who taught you such curse-talk?" Niik chided as she rounded the corner.

"You did," Itzelas replied with a grin.

"Hm, very likely. Come. Greet our guests."

"Niik and her sister, Itzelas. This is Commander Zavala," Crow said.

"Itzelas? That's a unique name," Zavala said.

Niik slung two arms around her younger sister. "Standard Eliksni would not do for this one." Itzelas pushed her arms away, earning a laugh from Niik.

Zavala nodded. "A pleasure to meet you both. We don't want to keep you, but… well, there's something I wanted to deliver personally to you today."

He held up a small, unsuspecting toolbox. Niik's eyes went wide, and she gasped.

"Amanda's instructions were to share them with someone who 'has machinery on the brain and oil in their veins.' We couldn't think of anyone more fitting, Niik, than you," Crow explained.

Niik accepted the gift, and Zavala held out an item wrapped in cloth toward Itzelas. "And from what Crow has told me about you, I am sure Amanda would want you to have this."

Itzelas unwrapped the cloth, revealing a well-loved spanner. She tenderly touched the initials engraved on the tool, then hugged it to her chest. "Commander… I would like to know her. As you knew her. Will you share her stories?"

"There are Servitor's holo-recordings. We could together-watch," Niik said and motioned for the two Guardians to come inside. "Would you like… some tea?"

Zavala looked down into the hopeful gaze of Itzelas and recognized something he had seen in a young Human girl… so many years ago.

"I would be honored to share her with you."
3934818284.text_zh:
乌鸦和萨瓦拉穿过埃里克斯尼居住区的时候，他们经过了一群围着一条机械狗的年轻埃里克斯尼族。一个孩子跑上前来，在萨瓦拉面前停下，她的四只胳膊上满是糖果。她抬头看着他，高兴得叽喳乱叫。萨瓦拉发出了咯咯的笑声，这让他自己颇感惊讶。乌鸦挥手让他继续前行，他们最终来到了一个不大但却令人惊叹的作坊前。一架快雀悬在升降机上，推进器被移走了。一名埃里克斯尼族正在底下修补着。

“进展不错啊，”乌鸦喊道。那名年轻的机修工吃惊地抽搐了一下，头撞在了快雀上。她低声嘀咕了一句埃里克斯尼族语。

“伊泽拉斯，这句诅咒是谁教你的？”妮可绕过转角责备道。

“是你教的，”伊泽拉斯笑着回答道。

“唔，很有可能。来。跟我们的客人打声招呼。”

“妮可和她的妹妹伊泽拉斯。这位是指挥官萨瓦拉，”乌鸦说道。

“伊泽拉斯？真是个独特的名字，”萨瓦拉说。

妮可用两只胳膊搂着她的妹妹。“普通的埃里克斯尼族不太适合这名字。”伊泽拉斯推开她的双臂，妮可笑了起来。

萨瓦拉点点头。“很高兴见到你们两位。我们不想耽误你们的时间，但是…嗯，今天我有东西想亲自交给你们。”

他举起一个小巧而毫不起眼的工具箱。妮可睁大眼睛，倒抽了一口气。

“阿曼达的指示是，把它们分享给那些‘脑子里装着机器，血管里流着机油'的人。妮可，我们想不出比你更合适的人选了，”乌鸦解释道。

妮可收下了礼物，而萨瓦拉也把一个包裹在布里的物品递给了伊泽拉斯。“乌鸦告诉了我关于你的事，我相信阿曼达会想把这个给你。”

伊泽拉斯打开布包，里面是一把备受喜爱的扳手。她温柔地抚摸着刻在工具上的首字母，然后把它抱在胸前。“指挥官…我想了解她。就像你了解她一样。你能跟我讲讲她的故事吗？”

“有魔眼的全息记录。我们可以一起看，”妮可说着，示意两名守护者进来。“你们想…喝点茶吗？”

萨瓦拉俯视着伊泽拉斯充满希望的目光，认出了多年前…他在一个年轻的人类女孩身上看到的东西。

“我很荣幸能与你分享她的故事。”

3934818285.name: Epilogue
3934818285.text:
The amazing stories you have just experienced are now a part of Eliksni record. You may not believe any of them to be true, but if you do, know that you are in good company with those who have lived to tell these tales. 

The universe is an enigma, wild and mysterious, full of horrors and terrors and temptation. But go where others are tremulous to tread, step beyond your senses, and embrace the unknown. For only then will you discover new truths and new adventures—but only if you dare.

—Ithaaks, House of Light
3934818285.text_zh:
你刚刚经历的那些神奇故事现在都被收录在了埃里克斯尼族记录里。你也许一个都不信，但如果你相信，希望你能知道，那些活下来讲述这些故事的人与你同在。 

宇宙是个谜团，狂野而神秘，充满了恐怖、惊惧和诱惑。但还是前往别人不敢涉足的地方，超越你的感官，拥抱未知吧。因为只有这样，你才会发现新的真理和新的冒险——如果你有那个胆量。

——伊萨克斯，光能氏族

1527171891.name: Chapter 1
1527171891.text:
Faint guitar music drifted through the streets of the Last City, barely audible over the buzz of citizens in the market. Glint's iris flicked between passing patrons and the pleasing festival decorations. His self-assigned patrol was barely a distraction from his racing thoughts, but it made him feel helpful to Crow and the Vanguard—even if they didn't know and were too preoccupied to care.

A nearby stand decorated with stained glass wind chimes caught his attention. He gave them a closer look, wondering how to get one back to Crow.

"Come on! Quick!" a voice shouted. Glint turned to see four teens rush by the stall, narrowly avoiding a cart full of vegetables. To Glint's surprise, one teen carried a large pumpkin.

"These kids and their Headless Ones nonsense, I swear," the stall owner said.

"It's that time of year. Silly pranks abound," responded a patron with a chuckle.

Glint quickly floated after them.
1527171891.text_zh:
微弱的吉他乐声轻轻拂过圣城的街道，几乎被市场上市民们熙熙攘攘的喧嚣声所掩盖。格林特的视线在往来的顾客与节日的喜庆装饰间游移。他自发的巡逻虽然未能完全驱散心中的纷扰思绪，但至少让他觉得自己能为乌鸦和先锋尽一份力——即使他们未曾察觉，因忙于其他事务而无暇顾及这份心意。

不远处，一个装饰着彩色玻璃风铃的摊位吸引了他的目光。他走近细看，琢磨着怎么才能给乌鸦弄一个回来。

“快！快点！”一个声音喊道。格林特转身望去，只见四个孩子匆匆跑过摊位，险些撞翻满载蔬菜的小车。令格林特惊讶的是，其中一个孩子怀里还抱着一个大南瓜。

“这些孩子和他们那些无头者的无稽之谈，真是让人头疼，”摊主抱怨道。

“又是一年中的这个时候了，尽是些无聊的恶作剧，”一位顾客笑着回应道。

格林特迅速跟了上去。

1527171888.name: Ghost Den – 1
1527171888.text:
[NEW RECORDING] Ghost Den–Session 1

LOCATION: Tower–Bazaar—Previously New Monarch Meeting Area

FACILITATORS: Eva Levante, Micah-10, and Mihaylova (Recordkeeper)

PARTICIPANTS: Ghost, Glint, Ophiuchus, Kugu, Lexicon, Bee, and Batt

—START OF RECORDING—

Eva: Welcome, little Lights. Thank you for joining us.

Micah: In the spirit of the season, and with recent events in mind, we wanted to hold this gathering to give you space to talk and share.

Eva: The Festival of the Lost is an opportunity to celebrate life and honor death. We often forget to do both and can feel much turmoil as a result.

Micah: Mihaylova is recording, but only so you can look back on your progress if you like. So please don't feel intimidated by her.

[CIRCLE NOTE: The participants glance at each other. Ghost shrinks under everyone's curiosity and floats closer to the open air of the balcony.]

Eva: Now, who would like to begin?
1527171888.text_zh:
[新记录] 机灵集会地–第1次会议

地点：高塔–集市–前新王派集会区

主持人：伊娃·莱万特、米迦-10以及米哈伊洛娃（记录员）

与会者：机灵、格林特、蛇夫座、库谷、莱克森、比和巴特

-记录开始-

伊娃：欢迎，小家伙。谢谢你们的参与。

米迦：为了节日精神，同时考虑到最近发生的事件，我们决定举行这次集会，让你们有机会来倾诉和分享。

伊娃：英灵日是一个庆祝生命并纪念死亡的时刻。我们时常忘记去做这两件事，因而内心感到纷扰。

米迦：米哈伊洛娃正在记录，但这只是为了方便你们日后回顾自己取得的进展。所以请不要被她吓到。

[圈注：与会者们相互对视，机灵在众人好奇的目光下蜷缩起来，飘得更靠近了阳台的开阔空间一些。]

伊娃：那么，由谁开始呢？

1527171889.name: Chapter 2
1527171889.text:
Glint saw the teens running into an abandoned building and floated in behind them. The rays from the setting sun trickled through the windows, allowing Glint to find his way without providing his own light. Keeping to the shadows, he bobbed his way through piles of debris, passing half-finished murals on the walls until he found the room the pranksters had decided to make their hideout.

As he entered, he noticed a collection of curiosities that he couldn't quite place, but it was an unfamiliar book in one of the teens' hands that claimed his attention first. It looked thrown together; pages of varying quality and color poked out haphazardly, like an art project gone wrong.

"No, no, the pumpkin has to be in the center, Cash," the young Awoken girl said, exasperated.

Glint spotted "Cash." The Human boy made a patronizing face but moved the pumpkin anyway. With its carved-out eyes and sharp teeth, the item in question fit with what Glint knew of Headless Ones. Nothing about it glowed, which was a good sign, so he dipped slyly behind a box to avoid detection and continued to examine the room while the teens argued over this "ritual."
1527171889.text_zh:
格林特看到孩子们跑进一栋废弃的建筑，便跟在他们后面飘了进去。夕阳的余晖透过窗户洒落，为格林特指引方向，让他无需点亮自己的光能。他尽量避开亮光，在废墟堆中跃动前行，经过墙上未完成的壁画，最终找到了那群捣蛋鬼选作藏身处的房间。

他进入其中，注意到了一些让他感到困惑的奇怪东西，但首先吸引他目光的是某个孩子手中紧握的一本陌生书册。它看起来像是随意拼凑而成的；书页材质与颜色各异，杂乱无章地突出在外，就像是一件失败的艺术作品。

“不，不，南瓜一定要在中间，凯什，”年轻的觉醒者女孩恼怒地说道。

格林特注意到了“凯什”的身影。这个人类男孩虽面露不屑，但还是把南瓜挪到了中间。那件物品上面雕刻着深邃的眼洞和锋利的獠牙，与格林特心中无头者的形象不谋而合。南瓜并未散发出丝毫光芒，这是个好兆头，于是他偷偷地躲到箱子后面，避免被发现，在那些孩子争论这场“仪式”的细节时，继续观察着房间。

1527171894.name: Ghost Den – 2
1527171894.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

[CIRCLE NOTE: A Ghost with a light blue shell, Kugu, beeps and floats toward the center of the circle made by the other Ghosts.]

Micah: Ah, Kugu! Go right ahead.

Kugu: The Witness is a spineless, weak jerk that made everyone's lives horrible. Who asked for its opinion on how the universe should be run? No one! I've never seen such an entitled being in my life. I wish I could have gone shell to smoke head with it. I would have ripped it in—

[CIRCLE NOTE: Other Ghosts looking between one another, a few giggling. Another Ghost with an all-black shell, Lexicon, quickly flies up and pushes gently against Kugu.]

Lexicon: Yes, the Witness is awful, but maybe we should try to move forward? It's dead. Holding onto anger will only poison us and our future.

Micah: That's an excellent perspective, Lexicon. Thank you.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Kugu grumbles in agreement and returns to their original spot, with Lexicon close behind.]
1527171894.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

[圈注：一个浅蓝色机壳的机灵，库谷，发出蜂鸣声，飘向其他机灵围成的圆圈中心。]

米迦：啊，库谷！请说吧。

库谷：见证者是个懦弱无能的混蛋，它让每个人的生活都变得一团糟。谁问过它对宇宙应该如何运行的意见？没人问过！我这辈子从没见过那么自以为是的家伙。真希望能和它来场单挑。我一定会把它撕成——

[圈注：其他机灵面面相觑，有几个在咯咯笑。另一个全黑机壳的机灵，莱克森，迅速飞了过来，轻轻地推着库谷。]

莱克森：没错，见证者的确是糟透了，但也许我们应该试着向前看？它已经死了。继续沉溺于愤怒只会对我们自己和我们的未来造成伤害。

米迦：这是个很好的观点，莱克森。谢谢你。

[圈注：库谷咕哝着表示同意，然后回到原来的位置，莱克森紧随其后。]

1527171895.name: Chapter 3
1527171895.text:
There were some unusual objects in the room. Glint scanned them when he was sure no one was looking: colorful fabrics draped over various things, a hundred or so melting candles, counterfeit Gambit coins, swords that were supposed to be Hive in origin, candy dumped in a variety of buckets, boxes, and vases. Everything was a forgery, some sort of fake.

Two young Eliksni had been standing off to one side. At the Awoken girl's behest, they approached her in the center of the makeshift ritual circle. That was when Glint's eye caught something interesting. An altar, covered in more candles and smaller baubles that reflected against something familiar, an item he hadn't expected to find here: a golden reliquary container.
1527171895.text_zh:
房间里摆放着一些不寻常的东西。格林特趁没人注意时扫描了它们：披在各种东西上的五颜六色的布料，一百来根快要融化的蜡烛，伪造的智谋硬币，标称来自邪魔族的刀剑，装在各种桶、盒子和花瓶里的糖果。所有东西都是赝品，都是某种假货。

两名年轻的埃里克斯尼族一直居于一侧。在觉醒者女孩的示意下，他们走到了临时仪式环的中央。就在这时，格林特注意到了一件有趣的东西。有个祭坛上摆放着更多的蜡烛和一些小饰品，映衬着某个熟悉的东西，一件他没想到会在这里看到的物品：一个金色的圣物匣。

1527171892.name: Ghost Den – 3
1527171892.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

Eva: Would anyone else like to go?

[CIRCLE NOTE: The Ghosts idle in place, irises nervously looking around.]

Micah: Anyone…? Ophiuchus?

[CIRCLE NOTE: Ophiuchus does not say anything. He stares back at Micah and slowly blinks. Lexicon floats toward a pillow and hides behind it. Another Ghost makes a noise akin to someone clearing their throat. Eva continues to smile from her place next to Micah on the couch.]

Micah: All right, moving on.
1527171892.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

伊娃：还有谁想发言吗？

[圈注：机灵们停留在原地，眼神紧张地环顾四周。]

米迦：有人愿意吗…？蛇夫座？

[圈注：蛇夫座没有说话。他回头盯着米迦，缓慢地眨了下眼睛。莱克森飘向一个枕头，躲在后面。另一个机灵发出类似清嗓子的声音。伊娃坐在沙发上，挨着米迦继续微笑着。]

米迦：好吧，继续。

1527171893.name: Chapter 4
1527171893.text:
A debate had started between the teens. While they were distracted, Glint could easily float unnoticed from one hiding spot to the next. They were arguing whether to use melted candy on their hands to bond them even further before the ritual, which resulted in huffs and objections. Cash sighed at the response to his suggestion.

Glint floated past some deactivated—or more likely broken—Cabal shields and some weird blue substance in a mason jar before stopping at a box a few feet from the altar. He wasn't close enough to scan it, but it certainly looked like a real reliquary. It sat beside a book holder that took up the center of the table. There were other items around it: a gold medallion with a symbol he didn't recognize, an orb that shimmered like starlight, an assortment of scarves, and rocks that gleamed in the candlelight. But nothing looked as potentially concerning as the reliquary. Anything could be in there…

He glanced over at the group for a moment. Having checked that their attention was elsewhere, he floated over to the altar for a closer inspection.
1527171893.text_zh:
孩子们之间开始了一场争论。趁着他们分心的时候，格林特轻易地从一个藏身处飘到另一处而未被察觉。他们争论是否要在仪式前用融化的糖果把他们的手粘合起来，结果引起了一阵抱怨和反对。凯什听着大家对自己提议的反响叹了口气。

格林特飘过一些关闭的——或者更可能是坏掉的——卡巴尔护盾和一些装在玻璃罐里的奇怪蓝色物质，在离祭坛几英尺远的一个盒子前停了下来。他离得不够近，没法进行扫描，但它看起来确实是个真正的圣物匣。它放在桌子中央的一个书架旁。周围还有其他物品：一枚带有他不认识的符号的黄金勋章，一个像星光一样闪烁的球体，各式各样的围巾，还有在烛光下闪闪发光的石头。但没有任何东西看起来能像圣物匣那样引人注目。里面可能藏有任何东西…

他瞥了那群孩子一眼，确认他们的注意力都在别处后，飘到祭坛前仔细检视。

1527171898.name: Ghost Den – 4
1527171898.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

[CIRCLE NOTE: A Ghost with an orange shell, Bee, floats forward. Another, Batt, dons a red shell. She hovers close to her.]

Bee: I can go. Ahem.

Batt: It's okay, you got this.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Batt gives Bee a comforting nudge. She takes a shaky breath.]

Bee: We almost died during the War. I—I know that "almost" isn't as bad as "did", but… I haven't felt the same since then.

Micah: What you experienced is just as important. No need to minimize it.

Bee: It was… terrifying. The way its limbs reached out to crush anyone in its path…

Batt: We got grabbed. It looked like that was it, but then it disappeared.

[CIRCLE NOTE: The two turn to Ghost, who can't meet their gaze. He floats a bit lower.]

Bee: We're alive because of you. Thank you.
1527171898.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

[圈注：一个橙色机壳的机灵，比，向前飘了出来。另一个叫巴特的红色机壳机灵紧挨着她盘旋。]

比：我来吧。呃哼。

巴特：没事，你能行的。

[圈注：巴特安慰地推了推比。她颤抖地喘了口气。]

比：战争期间我们都差点死掉。我、我知道“差点死掉”没有“死掉”那么糟糕，但是…从那以后，我的感觉就不一样了。

米迦：你所经历的一切同样重要。没必要轻视它。

比：真的…太可怕了。它伸展肢体，要把挡道的人统统捏碎…

巴特：我们被抓住了。似乎一切都完了，但它随即消失了。

[圈注：两人转头看向机灵，而他无法直视他们的目光。他飘得更低了一些。]

比：我们能活下来都是因为你。谢谢你。

1527171899.name: Chapter 5
1527171899.text:
The teens stood in a circle. At the center was a pumpkin, positioned in the middle of an intricate symbol, painted with unsure brushstrokes, smudged to fix mistakes.

"Stop fidgeting, Nirysk," the young Eliksni girl muttered, tightening her grip on the other Eliksni's hands. "You don't see Cash or Rhea fidgeting."

"I'm not fidgeting," said Nirysk as he grabbed Cash's hand.

"If you're scared, I'm sure we can do this alone—"

"Melii, I'm fine," Nirysk retorted, his tone short.

"Everyone ready?" Rhea asked. The teens nodded. In one hand, she held up the book she'd been leafing through when Glint initially arrived. The words they strung together seemed a bit nonsensical, despite recognizing a few. Glint approached the altar with the intention of scanning the reliquary… but he couldn't.

Confused, Glint tried again. Nothing happened. His sensors were jammed. He couldn't even send an SOS to the Vanguard.

A violet glow danced in his peripherals, demanding his attention. He spun around and, to his surprise, saw it was from the pumpkin head—eyes and mouth alight.
1527171899.text_zh:
孩子们站成一圈。中心是一个南瓜，它被放置在一个复杂的符号中央，那符号是用不确定的笔触绘制的，为了修正错误而涂抹得有些模糊。

“别动来动去的，尼瑞斯克，”年轻的埃里克斯尼族女孩低声抱怨道，紧紧握住另一名埃里克斯尼族的手。“你看凯什和瑞亚在乱动吗？”

“我没有动来动去，”尼瑞斯克边说边抓住凯什的手。

“如果你害怕的话，我相信我们可以单独做这件事——”

“梅莉伊，我没事，”尼瑞斯克反驳道，语气简短。

“大家都准备好了吗？”瑞亚问道。孩子们点了点头。她用一只手拿着格林特刚来时她就一直在翻阅的那本书。尽管他认得其中一些字，但它们连在一起似乎有点莫名其妙。格林特靠近祭坛，打算扫描一下圣物匣…但他做不到。

困惑之余，格林特又试了一次。什么也没发生。他的传感器被干扰了。他甚至无法向先锋发出求救信号。

一丝紫色的炫光在眼角边缘闪烁着，引起了他的注意。他转过身去，惊讶地发现这光芒来自于南瓜头——它的眼洞和嘴巴都亮了起来。

1543949477.name: Ghost Den – 5
1543949477.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

[CIRCLE NOTE: The focus has now shifted to Ghost. The rest of the participants, quiet and waiting, turn their attention toward him.]

Ghost: I don't know what to say… I-I'm glad I could help. I just…

[CIRCLE NOTE: He looks around and retracts.]

Ghost: I can't. Not yet.

Glint: Hey, it's okay.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Glint floats over to Ghost and huddles beside him, shells touching for comfort.]

Glint: I can go next.
1543949477.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

[圈注：焦点现在移到了机灵身上。其他与会者安静地等待着，把注意力转向了他。]

机灵：我不知道该说什么…我、我很高兴能帮上忙。我只是…

[圈注：他环顾四周，然后缩了回去。]

机灵：我做不到。还不行。

格林特：嘿，没事的。

[圈注：格林特飘到机灵身边，蜷缩在其一旁，机壳触碰，以示安慰。]

格林特：我来发言吧。

1543949476.name: Chapter 6
1543949476.text:
Panic surged through Glint.

No. No, no, no. According to all the research he and Eido had done on the Headless Ones over the years, this shouldn't have been possible. It shouldn't have been allowed to happen. Nothing in this room was real, or at least shouldn't have been able to power a ritual—the book! It had to have been the book.

The teens were lost in the trance of their spell, a palpable energy lifting them slowly from the ground.

This was only supposed to be a prank! Glint tried once more to reach out to the Vanguard, to Crow, but his radio was eating static. He did the next best thing.

"Hey!" he shouted. It worked instantly. The startled teens yelled in surprise and, with their concentration broken, tumbled to the ground with loud thuds.
1543949476.text_zh:
恐慌涌上了格林特的心头。

不。不，不，不。根据他和艾多这几年来对无头者的研究，这本是不可能的。这种事不该发生。这房间里没有任何东西是真的，至少没可能为仪式提供能量——那本书！一定是那本书。

孩子们陷入了咒语的恍惚之中，一种明显的能量正缓缓地将他们从地面上托起。

这本该只是个恶作剧！格林特再次试图联系先锋，联系乌鸦，但他的无线电一直在受到静电干扰。他选择退而求其次。

“嘿！”他喊道。这一招立刻奏效。吓了一跳的孩子们惊讶地大叫起来，由于注意力被分散，统统砰地一声摔倒在地。

1543949479.name: Ghost Den – 6
1543949479.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

Glint: The war with the Witness was never going to end without losses. I don't think any of us wanted that, but we all knew that if it meant saving lives, we'd pay whatever price was asked.

Glint: But I've never felt a Ghost's death before.

[CIRCLE NOTE: The circle falters for a moment. Many of the Ghosts shift uneasily. They don't look at Glint.]

Glint: I didn't know Targe for very long. The nature of our mission in the Pale Heart brought everyone's Ghosts together. I've talked with Ghost a lot in the past and consider us friends, but it was nice to be around Targe and Ophiuchus. To see things from a new perspective.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Glint sighs. Ghost looks to him. Ophiuchus does not react.]

Glint: I wish I could have gotten to know him better.

Ophiuchus: He didn't have to die.

[CIRCLE NOTE: All eyes snap to Ophiuchus, shells twisting with curiosity.]
1543949479.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

格林特：与见证者开战必将伴随着丧失。我想我们谁也不希望这样，但我们都知道，如果这意味着拯救生命，我们愿意付出任何代价。

格林特：但从未有过哪个机灵的死这般触动我。

[圈注：围圈的机灵动摇了片刻。许多机灵不安地挪动着。他们移开了视线不去看格林特。]

格林特：我和塔吉相处的时间并不长。我们在苍白之心内任务的性质让所有人的机灵都聚到了一起。我以前经常和机灵交谈，认为我们是朋友，但和塔格、蛇夫座在一起感觉也很好。能从新的角度看待事物。

[圈注：格林特叹了口气。机灵看向他。蛇夫座没有反应。]

格林特：我希望我能多了解他一些。

蛇夫座：他本来没必要死的。

[圈注：所有人的目光都投向了蛇夫座，好奇地扭动着机壳。]

1543949478.name: Chapter 7
1543949478.text:
"The hell is a Ghost doing here?!" Cash asked. Everyone had risen, hissing painfully, to their feet. They looked around as they brushed themselves off and checked for injuries.

"Wait," Melii said. Glint floated closer to them, and the Eliksni's eyes widened. "That's not just any Ghost, egghead! That's the Hunter Vanguard's Ghost!"

"Glint?" Nirysk asked. Melii nodded. Beside them, the flickering candlelight danced on Rhea's pale violet arms as she folded them protectively over the book.

"That doesn't answer the question," she said defensively.

"I could ask you the same," Glint said. He looked at each of them in turn, but found his gaze drawn invariably back to the book. Even from a distance it didn't look special. "What in the world were you trying to do, exactly? Summon a Headless One?"

"What? No! That'd be ridiculous," Rhea said. "Everyone knows there's no way to do that."

"Yeah, exactly," Cash said. "We were trying to speak to the dead."

Glint blinked.
1543949478.text_zh:
“真该死，这里怎么会有机灵？”凯什问道。所有人都站了起来，痛苦地嘟囔着。他们环顾四周，拍拍自己身上的尘土，检查有没有受伤。

“等等，”梅莉伊说道。格林特飘到他们身边时，这名埃里克斯尼族睁大了眼睛。“那不是普通的机灵，笨蛋！那是猎人先锋的机灵！”

“格林特？”尼瑞斯克问道。梅莉伊点了点头。在他们身边，闪烁的烛光在瑞亚浅紫色的手臂上跃动着，她抱紧了那本书。

“这并没有回答那个问题，”她回嘴道。

“我也可以问你们同样的问题，”格林特说道。他依次看了看他们每个人，却发现自己的目光总是被那本书吸引。即使走近了点看，这本书看上去也很普通。“你们到底想做什么？召唤无头者？”

“什么？当然不是！那太荒谬了，”瑞亚说道。“大家都知道那是不可能做到的。”

“对，没错，”凯什说道。“我们是想要跟死者对话。”

格林特愣了。

1543949473.name: Ghost Den – 7
1543949473.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

Ophiuchus: Targe was a pain, just like Zavala, sometimes… but he was a good Ghost.

[CIRCLE NOTE: A soft gust of wind passes through the circle. It sounds closer to a roar in the silence.]

Ophiuchus: You get used to someone's presence when you've been around them for so long. Even if you don't speak often.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Ophiuchus sighs.]

Ophiuchus: I knew he was going to do it. Something reckless… But I thought he would make it out. He and Zavala have been in many a bind, so I foolishly thought this would be no different.

Ophiuchus: I do think I miss him.

[CIRCLE NOTE: There is a long pause. The other Ghosts share glances.]

Ophiuchus: Ghost…

Ophiuchus: What was it like when you died?
1543949473.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

蛇夫座：塔格有时很讨厌，就像萨瓦拉一样…但他是个好机灵。

[圈注：一阵微风吹过机灵围成的圈子，它在寂静中听起来近似于咆哮。]

蛇夫座：跟某人相处这么久的时间后，你会习惯其存在。即使你们彼此不常说话。

[圈注：蛇夫座叹了口气。]

蛇夫座：我就知道他会去做鲁莽的事…但我以为他能成功脱险。他和萨瓦拉经历过许多困境，所以我愚蠢地认为这次也不会有什么不同。

蛇夫座：我想我确实想念他。

[圈注：一阵长久的停顿。其他机灵互相交换着眼神。]

蛇夫座：机灵…

蛇夫座：你死的时候是什么感觉？

1543949472.name: Chapter 8
1543949472.text:
"You were trying to… what?" Glint asked, taken aback.

"Well…" Melii started, then paused. She looked hesitantly at her peers. "We were talking about how many people fell during the war, and, uh, we just wanted to try to speak to them."

Glint noted the cautiousness in her voice. He floated higher to be level with their faces and saw how they all looked away from him, as if ashamed. Or… was it something more?

"We don't care about stupid pranks," Rhea explained quietly. "We had heard that this time of year was the best to try something like this…"

"The Hall Between," Glint muttered. They nodded.

Realization dawned on Glint.

They'd lost people to the Witness, and they were looking for solace. For answers. They wanted to feel close to their loved ones again after having had them taken away so suddenly and without warning. Glint could understand that.
1543949472.text_zh:
“你们想要…什么？”格林特震惊地问道。

“嗯…”梅莉伊开了个头，然后停顿了一下。她迟疑地看着同伴们。“我们聊到了有多少人在战争中倒下，呃，我们只是想试着和他们交谈。”

格林特注意到了她声音中的谨慎。他飘得更高，与他们的脸平齐，看到他们都把目光从他身上移开，好像感到了羞愧。或者…是有别的原因？

“我们对愚蠢的恶作剧不感兴趣，”瑞亚低声解释道。“我们听说每年的这个时候最适合尝试这样的事情…”

“腕神节，”格林特咕哝道。他们点了点头。

格林特恍然大悟。

他们因见证者而失去了亲人，正在寻找慰藉，寻找答案。他们想在亲人被如此毫无征兆、猝不及防地夺走后，再次感受到亲人的温暖。格林特能理解这一点。

1543949475.name: Ghost Den – 8
1543949475.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

Glint: You don't have to answer that…

Ghost: No, it's fine. I'm fine.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Ghost's shell flexes and shakes a little. Micah and Eva watch him carefully.]

Ghost: Final Deaths are always a possibility. We all know that.

Ghost: There's a complacency we feel, a comfortability, when it comes to our immortality… But, being in the Pale Heart, fighting alongside the Guardian, feeling the damage to me increasing with each moment…

Ghost: I don't know why I came back.

Ghost: I… I don't know why it was me and not Targe. He was just as important as any of us.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Ghost's shell droops. The rest of the group look away. Some float closer to one another.]

Ghost: He should have come back…
1543949475.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

格林特：你不必回答这个问题…

机灵：不，没事。我没事。

[圈注：机灵的机壳绷紧起来，微微颤抖。米迦和伊娃谨慎地观察着他。]

机灵：最终的死亡总是有可能发生的。我们都知道这一点。

机灵：每次谈到自己的不朽，我们都会感到一种自满，一种安逸…可是，在苍白之心里，与守护者并肩作战，感受到我身上的伤害每时每刻都在恶化…

机灵：我不知道我为什么能回来。

机灵：我…我不知道为什么是我而不是塔格。他和我们其他人一样重要。

[圈注：机灵的机壳耷拉下来。其余的人把目光移开。有些机灵相互靠得更近了。]

机灵：回来的应该是他…

1543949474.name: Chapter 9
1543949474.text:
"I put this book together with all the things we found during our research," Rhea said. She gently placed the book on its stand at the altar. "My mentor…" Her voice faltered. "She always said to keep your notes in one place, so they're easier to find… She never liked things to be messy."

"My sister was also like that," Cash said, eyes downcast.

Nirysk and Melii looked at each other. One of Melii's arms wrapped around Nirysk.

"Our brother went into the Great Machine as well…" Melii started.

"It should have been me," Nirysk whispered.

Glint felt their sorrow deeply. They were all so young.

"I was going to join him. I was supposed to be there," Nirysk said. "But I was a coward. I turned back. He… he didn't look at me with shame, only understanding, and that somehow makes it worse. I should have given my life to protect the Great Machine, too."

Nirysk kicked the pumpkin head just hard enough for it to tumble out of the circle they'd painted on the floor, its face dark and mocking.
1543949474.text_zh:
“我把我们在研究过程中发现的所有东西整理成了这本书，”瑞亚说道。她轻轻地把书放在祭坛的支架上。“我的导师…”她的声音有些颤抖。“她总是说要把笔记都放在同一个地方，这样才更容易找到…她从来不喜欢把东西弄得乱七八糟。”

“我姐姐也是那样，”凯什说道，目光低垂。

尼瑞斯克和梅莉伊互相看了一眼。梅莉伊用一只手臂环抱着尼瑞斯克。

“我们的哥哥也进入了大机器…”梅莉伊开口说道。

“本来应该是我的，”尼瑞斯克低声说。

格林特深深地感受到了他们的悲伤。他们都还那么年轻。

“我本来要和他一起去的。我本该在那里的，”尼瑞斯克说道。“但我是个懦夫。我退缩了。他…他没有用羞愧的眼神看我，而是充满了理解，这让我更难过了。我也应该献出自己的生命来保护大机器。”

尼瑞斯克踢了南瓜头一脚，力道刚好让它从他们在地板上画的圆圈里滚出来。它的脸上是一副阴沉而嘲弄的神情。

1543949485.name: Ghost Den – 9
1543949485.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

Micah: I'm proud of you for expressing how you're feeling about this, Ghost. I know it can't be easy.

Micah: Targe's death was a tragedy. And so was yours.

Micah: No one could possibly have known you'd get a second chance.

Micah: And it's okay that you don't feel okay. Any one of us would likely feel the same.

[CIRCLE NOTE: The participants nod in agreement, empathizing.]

Micah: You're not alone, Ghost. You are here and we're here for you… We'll get through it together. It'll just take a little bit of time.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Glint nudges Ghost for reassurance.]
1543949485.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

米迦：你能表达出自己的感受，我为你感到骄傲，机灵。我知道这不容易。

米迦：塔格的死是个悲剧。你的死也是。

米迦：没人能知道你还会有第二次机会。

米迦：你感觉不好也没关系。换做是我们任何人都会有同样的感受。

[圈注：与会者点头表示同意，感同身受。]

米迦：你并不孤单，机灵。你在这里，而我们支持你…我们会共同度过这个难关。只是需要一点时间。

[圈注：格林特推了推机灵，以示安慰。]

1543949484.name: Chapter 10
1543949484.text:
"You shouldn't think like that," Glint said, his tone soft and full of empathy. "I know that's easier said than done but trust me when I say, I understand. Someone I knew died, and I thought… 'Why not me?' It's so easy, isn't it? To blame ourselves and think we could have done something differently? 'If only I'd been there, maybe they'd still be here…'"

Emotion welled up within the Ghost, and he struggled to contain it.

"How do you get past that?" Nirysk asked. "It just feels like… Ether draining out of me constantly and I don't know how to stop it."

"Time," Glint said simply. "You give it time… and you lean on each other. You get through it together."

The teens were quiet. Glint knew it wasn't the answer they wanted. They were here in search of closure. Their hopes pinned on forged relics and fabricated rituals. All they wanted was closure.
1543949484.text_zh:
“你们不应该这么想，”格林特说，他的语气柔和，充满同情。“我知道这说起来容易做起来难，但相信我，我能理解你们。我认识的一个人去世了，我当时就想…‘为什么死的不是我？'这很容易，对不对？我们会责怪自己，认为自己本可以做得更好，‘要是我当时在场，也许他们就不会死…'”

机灵的内心涌动着情绪，他努力克制着。

“你是怎么熬过来的？”尼瑞斯克问道。“那感觉就像…乙太在不断地从我体内流走，我不知道该怎么阻止它。”

“时间，”格林特言简意赅。“给它一些时间…你们可以互相依靠。一起度过难关。”

孩子们都沉默了。格林特知道这不是他们想要的答案。他们是来寻找解脱的。他们把希望寄托在伪造的圣物和虚构的仪式上。他们想要的只是解脱。

1493616620.name: Ghost Den – 10
1493616620.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—
