U：但是…用奥斯里斯的光能…等一下！你是说萨吉拉没了？！那么他不就没有… 

//正在重启// 

U：你说的是真的，那么我们就是同一边的！ 

S：不，孩子。我们的目的相同，但我们的道路不同。 

U：你不需要这么做。 

S：一个必须抵达的重点。一段被选定的旅程。不是所有人都承受着虚假牺牲造就的舒适谎言的重担。  

U：求求你…… 

S：我只是想要将你从那种重担中解脱出来。  

//正在重启// 

S：飞船的感应器好像正在记录。处理掉它。

2953240785.name: Sovereign Order
2953240785.subtitle: Do not fly so far that you can no longer hear her voice.
2953240785.subtitle_zh: 不要飞到听不见她声音的远方。
2953240785.text:
Three ships flew overhead in tight formation.

Their shadows flickered across Grutuk's iris as she calculated their probable landing zones. Satisfied, she rose from the tangle of blackberries where she had been hiding, the thorns scraping harmlessly against her ivory shell. 

Xavol sat quietly, one dark claw scratching idly at the dirt. He had drawn the old runes, once powerful symbols of tithing, now nothing more than shallow scrawls. 

Grutuk nudged him. "Time to get to work," she said.

Xavol rose slowly, then kicked away the drawings with his foot. He hissed and clacked his jaws. 

"You always say that," she sighed, and the two headed toward the trees to wait for the Guardians.
2953240785.text_zh:
三艘飞船以密集队形飞过。

格鲁图克看在眼里，计算它们可能着陆的区域，然后满意地从她藏身的黑莓丛中站了起来，荆棘从她的乳白色外壳上刮落，没有留下一丝伤痕。

泽沃静静地坐着，用一只黑色的爪子懒洋洋地刮着泥土。他画出了个古老的符文，那曾经是什一奉献的有力象征，现在却只是肤浅的涂鸦。

格鲁图克轻推了他一下。“该开工了，”她说道。

泽沃慢慢站了起来，然后一脚把画踢散了。他发出嘶嘶声，下颚咔嚓作响。

“你总是这么说，”她叹了口气，然后他们一同朝树林走去，等待守护者的到来。

585440777.name: Unauthorized Departure
585440777.subtitle: Sometimes the ship chooses the pilot.
585440777.subtitle_zh: 有时候飞船也会挑选飞行员。
585440777.text:
Amanda circled the new SUROS jumpship, admiring its flat planes and sharp edges. It looked like something from the Golden Age.

She pulled up the specs on her datapad and whistled. No wonder the Warlock wanted to get rid of it. Too much juice for a New Light.

She looked over both shoulders before casually sliding into the cockpit. She wasn't cleared for takeoff, but she'd be damned if she let this opportunity slip by.

As she powered up the engines, a nearby Redjack began beeping in alarm. 

"Don't worry, darlin'," Amanda cooed to the ship. "The Guardian will take good care of you."

"But first," she said as she engaged the thrusters, "let's see what you can do."
585440777.text_zh:
阿曼达绕着新的SUROS跃迁飞船转了一圈，欣赏着它的平面和锐缘。它看起来像是黄金时代的产物。

她在数据板上调出了飞船的规格，吹了声口哨，难怪那个术士想摆脱它。这对新生的负光者来说太难驾驭了。

她看了看四周，然后漫不经心地溜进了驾驶舱。她还没获准起飞，但如果错过这个机会，她肯定会后悔死的。

她启动引擎时，附近的一个红桃杰克开始发出了警报声。 

“别担心，亲爱的，”阿曼达轻声对飞船说。“我会好好照顾你的。”

“但首先，”她一边启动推进器一边说。“让我看看你有什么能耐。”

2893840584.name: Criticality of Quickness
2893840584.subtitle: A lot can happen in 72 hours. Three days can change the course of a hundred lives.
2893840584.subtitle_zh: 72小时之内能发生很多事。只需三天，上百人的命运就能被改写。
2893840584.text:
Darkness signatures decay in just under two days.

Ether residue degrades in as little as 4 hours.

Hive ritual oils dissipate in less than 20 minutes.

As agents of the Hidden, you must understand: evidence is fleeting, and time is your enemy. That means you must act in swiftness… but not in haste. Never in haste.

Put your hands down. I recognize that look. 

A few years after I bonded with Ikora Rey—long before the Last City—we happened upon a settlement near the ruins of Sturivon in the EDZ. We discovered the locals slaughtered, with no surviving eyewitnesses. But Ikora was quite familiar with Fallen weapons, even by then, and recognized the impact marks immediately. She wasted no time mounting an assault on the Fallen camp in the nearby hills. 

Only when she got there, she found no one but the sick and the young, completely unarmed.

Had Ikora investigated the ruins of the settlement more thoroughly, she would have discovered the Human boot prints. You see, it turns out the Warlord Benyo Lukacs had raided the Fallen camp days earlier; he put their warriors to the sword and stole their weapons for his own use.

Ikora spent 14 hours tracking the Fallen encampment, and another 11 rushing back to find the clues she missed. Her haste gave Lukacs a 25-hour lead. Time enough for him to wipe out two refugee caravans. One-hundred and eighty-four lives lost… all because she did not spare another five minutes' investigation.

Begin your new lives understanding the vital difference between quickness and recklessness. Unless you think yourself strong enough to carry the weight of 184 mistakes.

—Audio Recording, Advanced Forensics Introductory Lecture, Ophiuchus
2893840584.text_zh:
暗影信号不到两天的时间就会消失。

乙太残留物在4小时内就能降解。

邪魔族仪式油不到20分钟就将消散。

作为隐秘者特工，你们必须明白：证据转瞬即逝，时间就是你们的敌人。这意味着你们必须迅速行动…但不是仓促行事。千万不要急于求成。

把手放下。我认得那个表情。 

在我与艾可拉·蕾伊缔结羁绊的几年后，那时离圣城还早着呢，我们碰巧在欧洲无人区的斯图瑞文废墟附近找到了一个定居点。我们发现当地人都被屠杀了，没有幸存的目击者。但艾可拉早在那时就对堕落者的武器相当熟悉，并立即认出来这些伤害痕迹。她没有浪费时间，对附近山上的堕落者营地发动了攻击。 

但当她到达那里时，才发现除了老幼病残外空无一人，完全没有任何武装。

要是当时艾可拉更彻底地调查了定居点的废墟，她就会发现人类的靴印。要知道，战争领主本约·卢卡奇恰好在几天前突袭了堕落者集中营；他杀死了他们的战士，偷走他们的刀剑为己所用。

艾可拉花了14个小时追踪到堕落者营地，又花了11个小时赶回去找寻她错过的线索。她的仓促匆忙让卢卡奇领先了25小时。这时间足以让他消灭两支难民船队。一百八十四人丧生…这一切都是因为她没有多抽出五分钟的时间进行调查。

开始你们全新的生活时，要理解快速和鲁莽之间的重要区别。除非你们认为自己足够强大到能够承载184份错误的重量。

高级取证入门讲座录音，蛇夫座

2139400845.name: Gouging Light
2139400845.subtitle: All told, I can't believe Holliday was able to put it back together. Not a lot left after a small-scale nuclear blast.
2139400845.subtitle_zh: 总而言之，我真不敢相信霍利迪把能这玩意儿修好。在小规模核爆之后，这些东西已经所剩无几了。
2139400845.text_zh:
在他的快雀坠毁的那一刻，一切都来不及了。来不及作出反应。来不及缓冲。来不及思考。然而，就在马尔科的世界唯独剩下痛苦的时候，他有一瞬间能感觉到：一阵不堪忍受的短暂永恒。除了构成他整个宇宙的那种纯粹的剧痛，别的什么都不复存在。很快，它就消失了。悄然无声。

他先是听见了一阵机动的哀鸣声，与他头上的搏动疼痛形成了鲜明的对比。眼睛渐渐适应后，他瞥见了火星阳光那难耐的亮度。

疼痛缓缓卷土重来，刹时抑制了其他感官。

他盯着地上划出的那道长长的沟槽，摩托车贴地在这片红土上刮出了一道划痕，滚过他的——  

他低头看了看腿上还残留下些什么。皮开肉绽，血肉模糊。胆汁哽在他的喉咙里，但他咽了下去，这才意识到被轧烂的肢体是他身上唯一没有疼痛的角落。 

]]]阳光翻腾起来。一缕缕赫赫之光舔舐着各个星球。希望孕育出痛苦，孕育出寂静。[[[

快雀的扬声器里还在噼啪地传出紧张的马里亚奇电子音乐。马尔科挣扎着吸气，一阵胸口的颤动暗示着他的肺被刺穿了。 

肺部穿孔。 

他呼吸急促，开始寻找那些在王座世界金字塔突袭中幸存下来的守护者们小心翼翼地包装起来的样品容器。 

他的目光落在6010号容器上，它靠在玄武岩晶石上，已经开裂。

]]]门户洞开的等离子体深情地拥抱沟槽里明亮的光能，只留下温暖的残影。[[[

黑色的血管蜿蜒着穿过红土，穿过残骸。 

]]]亲自呈递的荣耀从那些无福消受之人身上夺走了痛苦。[[[

血管在泥土中穿行，在肉体与泥土的交汇处，延伸到了他那扭曲的肢体。快雀的车厢像心脏一样跳动，马尔科能感觉到他腿上赞美诗集般的节奏。

]]]各个星球自由地燃烧。让人痛快，却仍要化作灰烬。[[[

幻象充斥着他的脑海，渗进了他的口腔和肺部，扬言要让他淹没在极乐之中。他那条断掉的腿转了过来，砰的一声恢复了原样，兴奋感渗进了他本该感到疼痛的地方。

]]]深情、寂静、安全的拥抱。[[[

他从枪套中抽出手枪，一边仔细瞄准破裂的反应堆蔽罩，一边倒抽了一口气。

如此地轻柔寂静。

他的思想挣脱了束缚，在不堪忍受的短暂永恒之中，他咽下了最后一口气。 

]]]静卧着——[[[

马尔科尚存的一切扣动了扳机。

1993613993.name: Ivory Empress
1993613993.subtitle: When atop this vehicle, the crowds will part before you. By force, if necessary.
1993613993.subtitle_zh: 乘着这辆载具时，所有人都会为你让道。有必要的话，你也可以强行开道。
1993613993.text:
Amanda raised her eyebrows as Crow cruised onto the landing pad. He sat atop a gleaming new Sparrow, adorned with gold and ivory. 

"Fancy ride, huh?" he asked.

"Yeah, fit for a prince," Amanda replied dourly. 

Crow ignored the dig with a wan smile. "It's not mine. Just borrowing it while I'm on Earth."

Amanda gave a small harrumph. "Borrowing it from the Cabal?" 

Crow rapped one of the curling ivory horns with his knuckle. "How could you tell?"

"Guess that means you've got some new friends now," she snapped, sharper than intended.

Crow scuffed the ground with his toe. "Not really. I don't have a lot of close friends. There's Glint, of course. But he's more like an appendage."

"Well, you used to have plenty of friends," she said, "but that was a lifetime ago."

Crow opened his mouth to retort but stopped short. The silence stretched on.

"Don't let me find that thing on my landing pad when I get back," Amanda finally said, crossing her arms. "This ain't a parking lot."

Crow nodded and slowly scooted past, keeping his eyes forward. As Amanda watched him go, she heard a small, digital voice chirp, "Did you call me an appendage?"

The shipwright smiled and then immediately caught herself. Her smile curdled into a sour frown. She clenched her fists in frustration.

"Why do you do this to yourself, Holliday?" she muttered as she stormed back to the Hangar. "Every time. Every damn time."
1993613993.text_zh:
乌鸦来到着陆坪上时，阿曼达扬起了眉毛。他骑的是一艘闪闪发光、镶着黄金和象牙白的崭新快雀。 

“这座驾真华丽，是吧？”他问道。

“是啊，非常适合王子的身份，”阿曼达闷闷不乐地答道。 

乌鸦笑着不理睬她嘲讽的语气。“这不是我的。我只是在地球上的时候借用一下。”

阿曼达轻轻哼了一声。“从卡巴尔那里借来的？” 

乌鸦用指关节敲了敲其中一个卷曲的象牙角。“你怎么知道的？”

“看来你结交到了一些新朋友，”她厉声说道，语气分外尖锐。

乌鸦用脚蹭了蹭地面。“那倒不是。我的亲密朋友不多。格林特算一个，但他更像是个附属物。”

“你曾有过很多朋友，”她说道。“但那是上辈子的事了。”

乌鸦张口想反驳，却又打住了。两人保持着沉默。

“等我回来时，别让我看到那个东西还在我的着陆坪上，”阿曼达终于双臂交叉发了话。“这里不是停车场。”

乌鸦点点头，目视前方，慢慢地加速离去。阿曼达看着他离开的时候，听到一个微弱而有数码味的声音问道，“你刚才说我是个附属物？”

这个船匠露出了笑意，然后立刻止住，笑容逐渐凝成了酸涩的表情。她沮丧地握紧了拳。

“你为什么要这么对自己，霍利迪？”她嘟囔着，气冲冲地回到机库。“每一次都如此。”

781717692.name: Mind Shard
781717692.subtitle: Get there quicker than thought.
781717692.subtitle_zh: 还没开始想就已到达目的地。
781717692.text:
Prime-40 leaned against the side of the small café and watched the children of the City happily chasing Artemis.

Artemis seemed to enjoy it as much as the children did. He barked playfully and wagged his tail as if to encourage them as they ran to him, only to suddenly juke and sprint quick circles around the courtyard over and over as they laughed. Finally, he flopped down in the shade of a wooden table, and the children descended on him in a whirlwind of head pats and belly rubs.

The roar of a Sparrow broke the calm. Prime-40 stepped forward as it tore past, his cloak whipping around him in the dusty air.

Another Guardian heading up to the Tower, Prime-40 thought. He squinted into the distance and saw a stream of ships leaving the Hangar, heading east. 

"Something's happening at the Cosmodrome," he said quietly. 

Artemis trotted over to him and whined. Prime-40 knelt and scratched him behind his ears.

"Come on," he said.

The Exo and his dog walked along the low wall at the edge of the City. Prime-40 ran a gloved hand along the rough and crumbling surface, his fingers absentmindedly skimming over cracks from years of wear. 

When they reached a gap in the easternmost point, Prime-40 climbed through without trouble and gazed for a moment at the dry grassland stretching far into the distant mountains. He kicked a stone block upright and sat down, resting his strong back against the City wall.

Artemis sat obediently at his feet.

"If trouble's coming," Prime-40 said, gesturing past the scrub and blooming mesquite, "it's coming from over there."

Artemis barked in agreement.

"Whatever it is, we'll handle it together," Prime-40 said. "Same as always."

Artemis huffed contentedly, laid down, and crossed his front paws protectively over Prime-40's boots.

The two looked out over the plains, and together, they waited for what would come next.
781717692.text_zh:
普莱姆-40倚在小咖啡馆的边上，看着圣城里的孩子们快乐地追逐着阿提米斯。

阿提米斯似乎和孩子们一样乐此不疲。当孩子跑向它时，它会摇着尾巴欢快地叫着，就像在鼓励孩子们一般。当他们笑着追了上来，它忽然往旁边一闪，开始在院子里不断跑圈。最后，它扑倒在了一张木桌的阴凉处，让孩子们纷纷围过来，拍拍它的头，摸摸它的肚皮。

快雀的引擎声打破了平静。当它飞驰而过时，普莱姆-40往前踏了几步，他的斗篷在尘土飞扬的空气中拍打着。

“又一个前往高塔的守护者，”普莱姆-40想道。他眯起眼睛望向远处，看见不少飞船离开机库，向东飞去。

“发射基地出事了，”他轻声说道。

阿提米斯小跑过来，哀嚎着。普莱姆-40蹲下来，挠了挠它的耳后。

“走吧，”他说。

Exo和他的狗沿着圣城边的矮墙走着。普莱姆-40戴着手套的手抚摸着已部分破损失修的墙面。他心不在焉地用指尖掠过了那些年久失修的裂痕。

当他们到达最东端的缺口后，普莱姆-40毫不费力地爬了过去，并望着延伸到远处山脉的干燥草原看了一会儿。他把一块石块踢了起来，坐了上去，然后把他强壮的脊背靠在了圣城的墙壁上。

阿提米斯乖巧地坐在他的脚边。

“如果有麻烦来，”普莱姆-40指着灌木丛和盛开的牧豆树的后面，“肯定会从那边过来。”

阿提米斯赞同地吠了一声。

“无论来的是什么，我们都会一起应对，”普莱姆-40说道。“就像以前那样。”

阿提米斯安心地躺了下来，把前爪交叉放在普莱姆-40的战靴上，做出保护的防御姿态。

他们望着平原，一起等待着接下来即将发生的事情。

551038990.name: Edge of Action
551038990.subtitle: An echo of an ancient weapon, forged from a memory of strength.
551038990.subtitle_zh: 一件古老武器的回响，由力量记忆锻造而成。
551038990.text:
The Scheme-Mother-Reborn returned to her Lure. Here, her Ghost companion and her most trusted witch led her to a broken statue.

The statue held a fragmented weapon in its alien arms. When the Scheme-Mother asked why these broken things were on her ship, her most trusted witch told her:

You broke them, my queen, because they belong to a traitor.

The great Goddess of Whispers reached to hold the broken weapon. Although she did not remember its shape, she could feel its power and potential.

The Mother of Lies said:

This vile artifact holds memory, and it is memory that I lack.

Perhaps the-thing-I-was could retrieve these memories, but the-thing-I-am cannot.

I must find a creature capable of holding two wrestling paracausal forces in its breast.

I must outsource my remembering to someone else.

—An excerpt from "The Books of Rememoration, A Story Sewn into Flesh with Sinew and Malice, A Record of the Scheme-Mother's Resurrection and Return"
551038990.text_zh:
重生的阴谋之母回到了她的诱饵。在这里，她的机灵同伴和她最信任的女巫把她带到一尊碎裂的雕像前。

这座外星雕像怀里抱着一件破碎的武器。当阴谋之母问这些破东西为何在她的飞船上时，她最信任的女巫告诉了她：

“我的女王，你击碎了它们，因为它们属于叛徒。”

伟大的低语女神伸手去拿那件破碎的武器。虽然她不记得武器的完整形状，但她能感觉到它的力量和潜力。

谎言之母说道：

“这个邪恶的神器存着记忆，而那正是我所缺乏的记忆。

也许过去的我能够找回这些记忆，但现在的我不能。

我必须找到一种能在怀里同时容纳两股相互抵抗超因果力的生物。

我必须把我的记忆传承到另一人身上。”

——摘自《纪念之书，由肌腱和怨恨编织成血肉的故事，阴谋之母复活与回归的记录》

551038991.name: Edge of Concurrence
551038991.subtitle: An echo of an ancient weapon, forged from a memory of ambition.
551038991.subtitle_zh: 一件古老武器的回响，由野心记忆锻造而成。
551038991.text:
With a fresh mind and searching eyes, the Scheme-Mother-Reborn returned to her throne world, which, without the edge of sword logic, had become a shell of itself.

Here, she strolled the parapets and fell deep into contemplation. Although she could remember nothing, her mind was as sharp as a tooth.

When she emerged from her contemplation, the Whisper-Queen addressed her brood.

She said:

My children, I know the truth, and out of my love for you, I will share it.

Before them, she killed her most trusted witch in a transcendent blaze of Light. 

This witch became the first of the Lucent, the first resurrected in the image of the queen herself.

—An excerpt from "The Books of Rememoration, A Story Sewn into Flesh with Sinew and Malice, A Record of the Scheme-Mother's Resurrection and Return"
551038991.text_zh:
头脑清醒和目光敏锐的重生阴谋之母回到了她的王座世界，而这个世界没有了邪剑守则已然变成了一副空壳。

她在护墙上漫步，陷入了沉思。虽然她什么也记不起来，但她的头脑像牙齿一样锋利。

当她从沉思中走出来，低语女王向她的爪牙发表了讲话。

她说：

“我的孩子们，我知道真相。出于我对你们的爱，我将分享这个真相。”

就在他们的面前，她用超然的光能杀了她最信任的女巫。 

这个女巫就此成为了第一个光明邪魔族，第一个以女王的形象重生的邪魔族。

——摘自《纪念之书，由肌腱和怨恨编织成血肉的故事，阴谋之母复活与回归的记录》

551038988.name: Edge of Intent
551038988.subtitle: An echo of an ancient weapon, forged from a memory of cunning.
551038988.subtitle_zh: 一件古老武器的回响，由狡诈记忆锻造而成。
551038988.text:
The Witch, Insidious, was killed upon the rock cliff as a wretched sacrifice. With life drawn from the Sky, she was reborn: the Witch, Radiant.

The mangled creature, a Ghost, that bestowed the Sky's life, spoke to her, to restore her unmarked mind. 

It said:

You are a god of the chosen krill, the Hive.

You are the mother of cunning and lies.

You are the first of your kind gifted with Light, which is a paracausal force of the Sky.

The Queen of Lies listened quietly to these reminders. Even in her rebirth, with a mind emptied of memory, her cunning shone brightly, and she stitched together her new truth. 

She asked her new companion where she must go next, and it was then that her most trusted witch arrived to guide her to her Lure. 

—An excerpt from "The Books of Rememoration, A Story Sewn into Flesh with Sinew and Malice, A Record of the Scheme-Mother's Resurrection and Return"
551038988.text_zh:
作为可怜祭品的阴险女巫死在了悬崖上。她从天空中汲取生命，重生成为了光辉女巫。

机灵，这个赋予了天空生命、严重损坏的生物，和她说话，恢复她那没有标志的心灵。 

它说：

“你是天选克里尔邪魔族之神。

你是狡诈和谎言之母。

你是你们同类中第一个拥有光能之人，它是天空的一种超因果力量。”

谎言女王静静地听着这些提醒，即使重生时她头脑里的记忆清空之后，她的眼睛里仍闪耀着狡猾的光芒，并且仍能够把新的真相拼凑起来。 

她问她的新同伴接下来她该去哪里，就在这时，她最信任的女巫来了，带她找到了诱饵。 

——摘自《纪念之书，由肌腱和怨恨编织成血肉的故事，阴谋之母复活与回归的记录》

46524085.name: Osteo Striga
46524085.subtitle: "Victory is not in the unmaking of an enemy, but in the re-making of an enemy into your blade." —9th Understanding, 7th Revision of Sorrow
46524085.subtitle_zh: “胜利不是消灭敌人，而是将敌人重塑入你的利刃。”——《忧愁之书》第7次修订，第9次释义
46524085.text:
Ah, pardon us. It just seems like he's always hungry. When I first became a mother, I didn't realize how much time would just be spent feeding him. Do you mind? Thank you.

No, he doesn't look much like me, I know. There are a lot of orphans these days. I heard him crying from… oh my, it seems like half a world away. It was chance, honestly. I never thought of myself as a parent, but caring for another little life… it's taught me so much.

May I?

Sorry, I don't know why I'm sharing so much with you like this. You just seem easy to talk to. And becoming a mom has really given me a lot more insight into the little connections between people. I used to focus so much on my work. I actually lost a few friends over it.

Oh! Shh, shh, shh… there we go. That's right. Growing babies need their calcium.

Now I can see what matters. The beauty in small things and quiet moments. In watching others light up when they see him. In the way meeting new people broadens him.

I had another child, you know. That was… before. I didn't keep him safe. It's for the best. He's… safe now.

Besides, it means I can appreciate this little one so much more. Just the two of us. 

I love my little Striga.

And he's always… so… hungry.

//CASE 620102; SUSPECT IDENT JANA-14; STATUS: AT LARGE
//EVIDENCE IDENT #303, AUDIO DEVICE; RECOVERED ADJACENT TO DISMEMBERED BODY, RIBS EXCISED
46524085.text_zh:
啊，抱歉。只是他总是看起来很饿。我第一次成为母亲时，我并没有意识到光是喂养他要花多少时间。能帮个忙吗？谢谢你。

不是的，我知道他长得不太像我。现在这个世道孤儿随处可见，那时候我听到他的哭声…哦我的天，那哭声好像离我有半个世界远。老实说，这纯属偶然。我从没想过自己也会为人父母，但照顾另一个小生命…教会了我很多。

介意吗？

对不起，我不知道我为什么会这样和你分享这么多，可能因为你看起来很平易近人。成为母亲后，我对人与人之间的细微联系有了更深入的了解。我曾经只专注于工作，还因此失去了几个朋友。

哦！嘘嘘嘘…乖乖的哦。没错，成长中的婴儿需要些钙质。

我现在才知道什么是最重要的——小事和宁静时刻的美、别人见到他时脸上的笑容，还有拓宽他的视野所结识的新朋友。

我其实…曾经还有另一个孩子，那是…很久以前了。我没能保证他的安全。也许这才是最好的安排，他现在安全了。

况且，这意味着我可以更加珍惜这个小家伙，就我们两个人。 

我爱惨了我的小金属。

而且他总是…非常…饥饿。

//案例：620102；嫌疑人身份：亚娜-14；状态：逃逸
//证据#303，音频设备；在肋骨遭到切除的被肢解尸体旁找到

3505113722.name: Collective Obligation
3505113722.subtitle: "What The Witness gave me, I give to you. May it serve you in death, or in finality. It cannot be both." —Rhulk, disciple of the Witness
3505113722.subtitle_zh: “见证者给我的，我也给你。愿它在你死亡后或既定后为你效力。二者只能居其一。”——胡克，见证者门徒
3505113722.text:
Heard while scavenging a pile of dead Ghosts within the Throne World Pyramid:

"Oh insatiable you—how many beats on the snare of self-righteousness will it take before you acknowledge all the avenues from which you stall the flow of things as they should be?

"You do not see the collective obligation before you, the duteous burden that has rested on all sentient beings since time's origination—to ferry existence toward inevitable consequence: the final shape.

"Why do you unendingly insist on waylaying the machinations of every being with a worldview differentiated from your own? You lack respect. You lack direction. You seek only what you are guided to seek, and for that, you remain little more than an unrelenting nuisance.

"I was like you once. Wayward. Driven to misguided perfection by the bubble society painted around me. But when I look back, none but one had the answers. None but one shed all the airs of any pretense of what the universe was supposed to be in the eyes of the infinitesimal individual—my Witness.

"Through it, I found incentive. Clarity. Purpose. I sought to shed from myself the layer of barbarism that had pervaded my being for so long. I turned instead to the sophistication of infecting others with self-actualized corruption.

"You see, total eradication may be efficient, but the goal is not to be the last one standing. Rather, it is to remove the obstacles that encumber you and those who remain from reaching your destination.

"Annihilation of your kind was never the goal. But filling you with the right kind of ideological purpose, the kind that serves the finality of shape—well, that's the point of corrupting a beating heart, is it not?"
3505113722.text_zh:
在王座世界金字塔内扫荡一堆死去的机灵时听到的一些话：

“哦，你可真贪得无厌，在你承认自己采取一切手段阻碍事情发展之前，得要先敲几下伪善的响弦？”

“你没有看到你们面前的集体义务，那是自时间起源以来，所有有情众生所承担的责任——将存在引向不可避免的后果：终焉之形。”

“为什么你总是坚持用一种不同于你自己的世界观来阻挠每一个人的阴谋？你缺乏尊重、缺乏方向。你只是寻找别人引导你去寻找的东西，因此，你只不过是个不屈不挠的麻烦。”

“我曾经如你一般刚愎任性，被周围所描绘的社会气泡框住追求误导的完美。但当我回首，只有一人知道答案。也只有一人摆脱了渺小个体眼中的宇宙应该是什么样子的假象，那人就是我的见证者。”

“通过它，我找到了动力、启迪，还有目标。我试图摆脱我们这一族人身上那层长久到渗透进血液的野蛮，相反地，我转向了用自我实现的腐败感染他人的老练做法。”

“听着，彻底根除虽然可能有效，但我们的目标不是成为最后一个存活者，而是清除阻碍你和其他人到达目的地的障碍。”

“完全消灭你们从来都不是我们的目标，而是给你灌输正确的意识形态目的，那种为最终形态效力的目的。毕竟这才是腐蚀跳动心脏的目的，不是吗？”

2812324401.name: Dead Messenger
2812324401.subtitle: A gift for the empress who has everything.
2812324401.subtitle_zh: 送给坐拥万物的女帝的礼物。
2812324401.text:
Caiatl and Zavala stood side by side, watching a live feed of the Guardian's assault on the Psion transmission facility, as broadcast by Amanda Holliday's circling aircraft.

The Guardian ducked behind cover and pulled out a sleek grenade launcher, recovered during their last assault of the base. They fired into a pack of onrushing war beasts, sending shrapnel hurling through the air. 

The Cabal empress emitted a low rumble as she admired the weapon. Zavala looked up at the enormous ruler with raised eyebrows. Her gaze was fixed on the firefight, her eyes twinkling with violent ardor.

The Vanguard commander shut off the open comms and cleared his throat. "Would you like me to send you one of those grenade launchers? I can have Banshee create a Cabal-sized version for you."

Caiatl looked down at the Awoken leader, suddenly aware that her avarice had been on display. She lowered her tusks, which the commander interpreted as equivalent to a blush.

"That would be most welcome, Commander," Caiatl replied. "I'd like to fire it into Xivu Arath's belly and bathe in her soulfire."

Zavala turned back to the screen. "You have a… passionate spirit, Empress." 

He did not see it, but beneath her mask, Empress Caiatl smiled. 

It was terrifying.
2812324401.text_zh:
查厄托和萨瓦拉并肩而立，看着面前由阿曼达·霍利迪操控的环绕飞行器所带来的，守护者进攻灵能士兵传输设施的实况直播。

守护者躲在掩体后面，掏出一个榴弹发射器，这个东西是上次他们进攻基地时夺来的。一发打入一群战兽之中，弹药碎片四处飞溅。 

卡巴尔女帝对这个武器发出了一阵低沉的青睐的咕哝。萨瓦拉抬头看着这体型庞大的统治者，眉毛略微扬起。她的眼睛紧盯着战场，闪烁着强烈的热情。

先锋指挥官关闭了通讯，清了清嗓子说道：“你想让我给你一把那种榴弹么？我可以让班西制作一把卡巴尔型号大小的版本给你。”

查厄托看向他，突然察觉出她的贪婪有些过于明显。她的尖牙微微下沉，这个动作在指挥官看来代表她脸红了。

“那就多谢了，指挥官。”查厄托回应道，“我想拿这把武器一发打入希乌·阿拉斯的腹部，然后沐浴她的灵魂火焰。”

萨瓦拉重新看向屏幕：“你有…一个热情的灵魂，女帝。” 

他没有看到，在面具之下，女帝查厄托笑了。 

那可吓人了。

2812324400.name: Parasite
2812324400.subtitle: "Constant projections. Unending destruction. The will of every efficient parasite." —Savathûn's worm
2812324400.subtitle_zh: “不断施展奸计，造成无尽的破坏，便是每一只尽职的寄生虫的意志所在。”——萨瓦图恩的蠕虫
2812324400.text:
Guardian.

Transparency is not a strong suit of mine. Undoubtedly, this comes as no surprise. However, our… misadventures, let's call them, with the parasite have left me with a recurring ambivalence in regard to said transparency; as a result, I feel as though you are deserving of a more appropriate level of access to my thoughts surrounding recent events.

In my previously mentioned vision was the Witness's one truth: an eternity of Darkness in which I serve as a Disciple. It brought me an overwhelming feeling I previously relayed to you as fear—but in actuality, it was fear born of what I felt most within this vision—gratitude.

Gratitude! As if my place alongside the Witness was meant to be a reward for all I have ever done and ever will do. And if the Witness is to be believed, "all I ever will do" is unbecoming, to say the least.

It is moments like these wherein I wonder if I myself should be put to rest to avoid perpetuating these dark truths. But I have never before wavered from righteousness, and I don't intend to begin now.

With that, you should know that while our revealed truths about Savathûn and the Collapse appeared minimal, I have already used them to begin tracing a trail of evidence that may provide us with the power of preservation in the oncoming storm. When the time is right, we will have further parts to play together.

In the meantime, keep the parasite near, and listen close. It's bound to open its mouth again sooner or later.

—Mara Sov, Queen of the Awoken
2812324400.text_zh:
守护者。

公开透明不是我的强项。毫无疑问，这并不令人意外。然而，我们与寄生虫的…不幸遭遇，让我对上述公开透明反复产生矛盾的情绪；因此，我认为你有资格更加了解我对最近事件的看法。

在我之前所提到的幻觉中，见证者的唯一真理是：我将在永恒的暗影中身为门徒效力。这给我带来了恐惧，一种我之前传达给你的强烈感觉，但实际上，我在幻象中最强烈感受到的是感恩，而因此产生了恐惧。

竟然是感恩！这就好像我能够站在见证者身旁，是对我所做的和将来所做的一切的奖赏。而且如果见证者可信，“将来所做的一切”至少可能不太合适。

正是这样的时刻，让我不禁想到我自己是否应该安息，以避免这些黑暗真理永存。但我对公平正义的信仰从以前就没有动摇过，以前不会现在也不会。

说了这么多，你现在应该知道，虽然我们所揭示的关于萨瓦图恩和大崩溃的真相似乎微乎其微，但我已经开始用这些真相来追踪证据的踪迹，这可能可以在即将到来的风暴中赐予我们保护自己的力量。

在此期间，时刻留意寄生虫的动向，听仔细了。它迟早会再次张开嘴的。

——觉醒者女王，玛拉·索维

1763584999.name: Grand Overture
1763584999.subtitle: It's not over until the vast red artificial intelligence sings.
1763584999.subtitle_zh: 在这个大块头的红色人工智能放声歌唱之前，战斗绝不会结束。
1763584999.text:
"So. You're the new guy." Ana Bray cracks a half smile. "Can't be worse than the last Psions that Red and I dealt with." She impatiently taps her heel on her workshop bench as the Psion hurriedly checks linkages and nodes on the neural coupling device around her head. 

Words and images skip across Ana's mind like stones. "Remain calm. Even though you are defenseless, I do not possess a starship." A sound resembling laughter follows.

"Funny." Ana chuckles impatiently. "Okay! I've been setting this up for months. Are you done with the safety checks?"

Jinju flies by Ana and runs a scan over the engram. "Be nice."

A digital timepiece drains toward zero while the Psion inundates her mind with questions.

"My Light, Splicer tech, brain tubes. Yeah, I got it," Ana says. "Plug my brain into Red already and let's do this." Her voice quickens with excitement. The Psion finishes linking cables to a Splicer-tech receptacle housing Rasputin's engram and gives Ana an awkward thumb pointing up.

The Psion forms an interlocking image in her mind: a tangle of wires. Slowly, her perspective sifts through them and stops at a radiant center. She hears the words, 'Forgotten vestige, made remembered.'

"That's the plan, Pstan!" Ana exclaims. "Drop me in; I can already hear the Tchaikovsky." She stares down the ticking timer: 3… 2… 1…

Ana blinks. She stands in a vast thicket of thorn and rot. A warmth radiates from deep within the thicket. 

Ana blinks. She presses through bramble as barbs draw blood. Her sense of self wavers. She finds her grip on a searing-hot spike, shifting her senses red like an adrenal rush. 

Ana blinks. She kneels at the spike and rips it from the ground. A Valkyrie javelin is in her grasp.

Ana blinks. The thorned vines around her recoil and wither in the heat. She feels something within the javelin, faint and weak, but alive.
1763584999.text_zh:
“啊，你是新来的家伙。”阿娜·布瑞露出一点微笑，“不可能比我上次面对的灵能士兵更糟了吧。”在灵能士兵慌忙检查其头部周围连接和节点时，她有些不耐烦地用鞋跟轻踏她的工作台。 

文字和图像像石头一样掠过阿娜的脑海。“保持冷静。即使你毫无防御能力，我也没有星际飞船。”一个类似笑声的声音随之而来。

“你真幽默。”阿娜有些不耐烦地轻笑道，“好了吧！我已经摆弄这些装备好几个月了。你的安全检查完事儿了吗？”

金桔飞到阿娜身侧，扫描了一下记忆水晶后说道：“友善点儿。”

当灵能士兵用问题淹没她的头脑时，一个数字计时器逐渐被清空。

“我的光能，熔岩军团的技术，大脑通管。是的，我知道了。”阿娜说道，“让我和红老大思维连接吧，快点儿。”她的声音满含兴奋。灵能士兵将电缆连接到装载着拉斯普廷记忆水晶的熔岩军团科技接收端，然后向阿娜比了一个别扭的大拇指。

灵能士兵在她的头脑中形成了一个连锁的画面：一团混乱的电线。慢慢地，她的视角穿过它们来到闪亮一个的中心。她听到了这句话：“被遗忘的痕迹，被记起了。”

“就是这样！”阿娜说道，“让我进来，我已经可以听见柴可夫斯基了。”她盯着计时器…3…2…1…

阿娜眨了眨眼。她站在一大片荆棘丛生的灌木丛中。一股暖意从丛林深处散发出来。 

阿娜眨了眨眼。她穿过荆棘，刺得她流血。她的自我意识动摇了。她发现自己抓住了一个灼热的尖刺，使她的感官爆发，就像肾上腺素激增的效果一样。 

阿娜眨了眨眼。她跪下来，将尖刺从地面拔出。一把瓦尔基里标枪出现在她的手中。

阿娜眨了眨眼。她周围的带刺的藤蔓在炎热中退缩并枯萎。她在标枪中感觉到了什么，虚弱萎靡，但是还有生命的气息。

1572896086.name: Recurrent Impact
1572896086.subtitle: It's enough to drive someone out of their mind.
1572896086.text:
Crow feels unease when he touches the active Psisorium. There's a throbbing sensation at the base of his skull. It starts at the back of his head and works its way forward. A compelling aura flows from the Psisorium, ushering buried memories to the surface of Crow's mind.

Uldren Sov felt unease as he stood with fingertips against the Dark Shard. Everything was wrong, but he ignored it. There was a throbbing sensation at the base of his skull. It burrowed underneath and snaked in between his vertebrae: an impulse taking hold in his nerves that he was helpless to follow. A whisper he strained to hear, "Save her."

The Psisorium vibrates against the nails of his ungloved fingertips. Lucent Hive bodies twitch in unfeeling response to the mental scrying. Crow feels the rhythm of alien thoughts sweep over him like wind on stone, catching in ruts and divots worn by time. He sees glimpses, reflections of an end to justify the means.

A voice rattled Uldren Sov's mind, the cool tones of his sister slipping into well-worn grooves as he watched dreams carve themselves into his reality. Lucidity flashed like panicked gasps under thin sheets of ice. His desire taken: wishes turning sour in his mouth as he spoke them, tasting no longer of promise, now only of regret.
1572896086.text_zh:
乌鸦碰触到活跃的灵能馆时感到了不安。他的头骨底部有一种悸动的感觉。这种感觉从后脑勺开始，一直向前延伸。一种无法抵抗的气场从灵能馆涌出，将埋藏的记忆带到了乌鸦的脑海表面。

欧顿·索维不安地用指尖触碰着黑暗碎片。一切都不对劲，但他没有理会。他的头骨底部有一种悸动的感觉。它在底下钻来钻去，在脊椎骨之间蜿蜒而行：有股冲动牢牢地控制着他的神经，他却无能为力。他勉强听到了一声低语，“救救她。”

灵能馆振动着他裸露指尖的指甲。光明邪魔族的身体在对精神探知的无情反应中抽搐着。乌鸦感觉到外来思想的节奏像风吹在石头上一样掠过他，陷入了被时间磨损的车辙和凹痕。他看到了无数片段和反思，都抱着合理化那些手段的目的。

有个声音不断用他姐姐的冷静腔调搅得欧顿·索维心神不宁。他看到了融入现实的梦境。清醒的意识犹如纤薄冰层下惊恐的喘息般闪过。他被夺走的愿望，被诉说着的同时，在嘴中变得酸涩。如今希望已不复存在；能从中品味到的只有悔恨。

232928045.name: Under Your Skin
232928045.subtitle: The splinter you just can't remove.

1248372789.name: Sweet Sorrow
1248372789.subtitle: A scratched-out inscription on the barrel reads, "A birthday is just a number. How about we pick this one?"
1248372789.subtitle_zh: 枪管上一段被刮花的铭文写道：“生日只是一个数字罢了。我们就选这个怎样？”
1248372789.text:
Amanda Holliday hurls a wrench at the wall, her grunt of effort punctuated by the sharp clang of metal striking metal. Her shoulders rise and fall with each labored breath in the silence that follows. 

She gasps softly and rushes forward—eyes scanning the surface of the wrench for cracks as her fingers frantically reach for the socket. She turns the ratchet, hoping to hear the reassuring click of the gears. But there is nothing, no movement inside from either direction.

"Damn it," Amanda hisses, rubbing the heel of her palm against her eye. "Dammit!" 

She sees a racing helmet at her feet and kicks it across the garage floor. 

Everything around her is a painful reminder of her ignorance: A blue-and-white auto rifle of Cabal design with an inscribed message on the barrel. Her favorite ramen bar and sightseeing locations circled on a map of the Last City. A datapad loaded with coordinates for the old Haakon Precipice racetrack. The nearly finished Sparrow she and Niik had been working on, blazoned with airbrushed feathers of ebony and white.

"Damn it," Amanda whispers. Her back brushes against the wall, and she leans into it as her body slowly crumples to the floor. Her head dips to the side and rests on the cold engine of the Sparrow beside her. She pulls her legs toward her chest and curses into her knees, burying her face in them as her shoulders begin to rise and fall in trembling bursts. 

Of all the friends she could have made, of all the people who could have become important in her life, of all the horrible twists of fate she could have endured…

…why did they all have to be him?
1248372789.text_zh:
阿曼达·霍利迪将一把扳手朝墙面扔了去；她使劲的吭哧声中夹杂着金属撞击的尖锐响声。在撞击之后那短暂的静默里，她的肩膀随着每次费力的呼吸而起伏。 

她缓慢地吸了口气，然后冲向前去——她扫视着扳手的表面，检查是否砸出了裂缝，同时拼命地将手指伸向插槽。她转了转棘轮，希望能听见齿轮发出令人安心的“咔哒”声。但她什么都没听见。里面什么动静都没有。

“该死，”阿曼达一边嘶吼着，一边用手掌根部揉着她的眼睛。“真该死！” 

她瞅见脚边有一顶竞速头盔，于是一脚把它踢飞到了车库的另一头。 

她周围的一切都在提醒着她的无知：一把枪管上有铭文的卡巴尔蓝白色自动步枪；一张圈出了她最爱的拉面馆和观光地点的圣城地图；一张装着了老哈肯·普雷西皮赛车场坐标的数据板；一辆她和尼克耗尽心思喷上黑白羽毛涂装，几近完成的快雀。这令她痛苦不堪。

“该死，”阿曼达嘟囔道。她背靠在墙上，又逐渐滑坐到地板上。她的头垂向一边，靠在旁边那辆快雀冰冷的引擎上。最后，她一边咒骂着，一边埋头蜷缩起来，双肩颤抖着，起伏着。 

为什么她交到的那个朋友，那个成为了她一生惦念的人，那个被可怕的悲运牵连到的人…

…都非得是他？

2638190703.name: Aisha's Embrace
2638190703.subtitle: Fill my wounds with molten gold and make me whole again.
2638190703.subtitle_zh: 用熔金填满我的伤口，让我重获完整。
2638190703.text:
She has been here before.

Pale whisps of clouds swirl over pine trees the color of blackened emerald. No birds sing here; only the cold wind whistles through the tree branches. Flares of atomic fire bloom in the woods and lick against smoldering bark. There is poison in the ground, violence in the air. Screams, both human and inhuman, erupt and echo out into the gloom.

She has been here before.

Two dozen Hive Thrall erupt from the mouth of a cave, shimmering and opalescent like mollusk corpses. They scramble through the dark, shrieking cries of death and birth. Shayura stands, sword of fire held fast, screaming against the crashing tide of chitin and bone.

She has been here before.

Burning embers of Thrall rain around her, but with each dispatched wave of necrotic soldiers, their numbers seem to double. They press forward, inching her closer and closer to the crumbling ravine. Shayura knows that the only way out is through. Wings of flame roar off her back, leaving a trail of rippling heat and charred Thrall in her wake.

She has been here before.

The Thrall finally recede, but the towering Knight that strides through their parted ranks is an escalation, not a victory. Her sword clashes with the Knight's shield, shattering it in a single blow before tearing through the Knight's arm and sinking her blade into its chest.

She has been here before.

She can feel her Light ebbing and wastes no time splitting the Knight in half and separating head from body. Shayura exhales with relief, but with her next breath comes a blinding flash of light. It manifests above the Knight. Her vision swims, her mind reels; the shape is at once familiar and alien—a Ghost. Shayura sees the Hive Knight reborn, reconstructed, as a Guardian would be.

She has been here before. But not like this.

Deep panic builds in her chest. This is no Hive death ritual; this is not Titan. She runs from the Knight's next swing and slips into the reach of Thrall that tear at her armor. Mustering the last of her Solar energy, Shayura calls up a cyclonic pillar of flame that twists up into the sky and consumes the Knight.

…not like this.

The revenant Knight collapses in the flames, and its Ghost manifests again. Shayura leaps forward and drives her sword through, pinning the screaming Ghost to the forest floor. Her Solar aura flickers and fades; smoke and steam billow from her back and shoulders.

"NOT LIKE THIS!"

"Shay!"

Shayura's breath catches, her mind jostled. She feels the soft grass beneath her and sees the flower-dappled park that surrounds her, all sitting beneath the shadow of the Traveler in the heart of the City. Her SMG lies on the ground at her side. Tears shine below exhausted eyes, dark hair in a tangle matted to her head.

Aisha kneels in front of her friend as one might before a wild animal. Reed-7 stands at her back in abject silence, hand over his mouth. City security fans out behind him, their weapons trained on Shayura. 

"Shay?" Aisha pleads this time. She gingerly places her hands on Shayura's cheeks and looks into her eyes, searching for a sign of recognition. Shayura eventually reaches up and touches one of Aisha's hands. She tries to talk, but her words are merely whimpers.

Aisha wraps her arms around Shayura's shoulders and pulls her into an embrace. "It's going to be okay," Aisha whispers into Shayura's hair.

"We're going to get you help," Aisha promises.

Shayura does not trust herself or the world she thought she knew. Light is Dark, Dark is Light. The lines have blurred beyond recognition.

But at least in surrender, there is peace.
2638190703.text_zh:
她经历过这个。

苍白的云朵盘旋在近乎黑色的深绿色松树上方。这里没有鸟儿歌唱；只有寒风呼啸着穿过树枝。原子火焰的光辉在树林的黑暗中绽放，舔舐着闷燃的树皮。地上毒药泛滥，空中暴力弥漫。人类和非人类的尖叫声在幽暗之中回荡。

她经历过这个。

二十几只邪魔族怨魂从洞口喷涌而出，闪烁着乳白色的光芒，如软体动物的尸体一般。它们在黑暗中窜来窜去，死亡与重生的尖叫不绝于耳。沙玉拉双手紧握一把火焰之刃，朝甲壳和骨头的浪潮咆哮着。

她经历过这个。

怨魂燃烧殆尽的残渣如雨点般落在她的身边，但是这些死灵士兵无论杀掉多少，数量却总是越来越多。在它们的强攻下，她被一步步地逼向了崩塌中的峡谷。沙玉拉知道，现在唯一的生路就是杀出重围。她张开一对火焰之翼，把荡漾的热浪和烧焦的怨魂留在了身后。

她经历过这个。

怨魂之潮退去，但从阵中大步上前的高大骑士说明这并不是胜利的迹象，而是战事的扩大。她用剑一击砍碎了骑士的盾牌，乘势斩下了它的手臂，然后一把刺进了它的胸膛。

她经历过这个。

她感到光能正在衰弱，于是利落地将骑士劈成了两半，取下了它的首级。沙玉拉如释重负地松了一口气，但气还没喘完，一道刺眼的光亮便出现了在她的眼前。这道光亮在骑士的尸体上具象化了出来——这幅既熟悉又陌生的景象使她的视线飘忽，心神不宁：那是一只机灵。邪魔族骑士在沙玉拉的眼前重生、重构，与守护者无异。

她经历过这个，但不是这样的。

沙玉拉的胸中升起了一股惧意。这不是邪魔族的死亡仪式；这不是土卫六。她为了躲开骑士的挥击而朝一旁跑去，却没想到刚起身就遭遇了一群怨魂撕扯着她的铠甲。她使出了全身最后的烈日能量，召唤出一道火焰龙卷风：这股灼热的能量立刻吞噬了眼前的骑士。

…不是这样的。

复生的骑士倒在了火焰里，而他的机灵又出现了。沙玉拉向前一跃，用手中利刃刺穿了机灵；它尖叫着，被扎定在了森林的地面上。围绕周身的烈日光环逐渐消褪，她的背后和肩膀上升起了片片雾气。

“不是这样的！”

“沙？”

沙玉拉缓过神来，思绪仍处于混乱之中。她感到了身下柔软的草地，看见了她四周花团锦簇的公园；所有的一切都坐落在圣城的中央，旅行者的阴影之下。沙玉拉的微型冲锋枪躺在她身旁。泪水从她疲惫的双眼中落下，挂在脸颊上闪闪发光。

艾莎跪在她的朋友前，好像面对着一只野兽。里德-7站在艾莎的身后，一只手捂着嘴，一声不吭。圣城安保人员在他身后呈扇形展开，将手中的武器一齐对准了沙玉拉。 

“沙？”艾莎的言语中带着乞求。她小心翼翼地将双手放在沙玉拉的脸颊上，注视着她的眼眸，寻找着沙玉拉认出她来的迹象。沙玉拉最终伸手碰了碰艾莎的手。她想要说些什么，但她的话语出口后成了一串细声呜咽。

艾莎一把抱住沙玉拉，把她拉进了怀里。“一切都会好起来的，”艾莎对着沙玉拉的头发轻声说道。

“我们会帮助你的，”艾莎许诺道。

沙玉拉不信任自己，也不信任她自以为了解的世界。光明就是黑暗，黑暗就是光明。两者的界线已模糊得无法辨清。

但至少屈服能带来和平。

2097055732.name: Piece of Mind
2097055732.subtitle: With words or weapons, inaccuracy can be fatal.
2097055732.subtitle_zh: 无论是言语还是武器，不准确都可能带来致命的后果。
2097055732.text:
Mithrax squeezed through the tight Bazaar alleyway. Visiting the Tower made him feel out of place, like a creature moving through a world designed for smaller beings—which, he supposed, he was.

As he reached back to pull his Ether tubes free from a snag in the jagged brickwork, he felt something collide sharply with his elbow. 

His mind was suddenly filled with a flare of hot bitterness—a burst of bladed anger.

Mithrax looked down to see a Psion, clothed in Empress Caiatl's colors, wincing in pain and rubbing its eye. 

"Forgive me," Mithrax said graciously. "You must be the one assisting the Guardians against the Hive." 

The Psion looked up at him, then ducked its head in apology. The vision immediately dissolved from Mithrax's mind. 

"I am Misraaks, Kell of House Light," he said, putting a hand to his chest. 

The Psion paused, then gestured to its chest and Mithrax's head. It held its hand open as if waiting for a response.

Mithrax nodded his assent, and into his mind was placed a scattering of orange cubes, a spiraling helix of inky fins, and the sensation of biting through an unripe fruit.

The vision faded. "That is your true name?" Mithrax asked. The Psion gave a short bow. 

Mithrax smiled. "I understand why Guardians simply call you 'the Psion,'" he said. 

A swarm of smooth yellow planes fluttered through Mithrax's mind: laughter. 

Mithrax stepped to the side, and the Psion moved past him. As it did so, there was a final vision: a wink of warm, cheerful brightness, fading but promising to return. 

"To you, as well," Mithrax called, and the Psion vanished around the corner.
2097055732.text_zh:
米瑟拉克斯挤过狭窄的集市小巷。造访高塔让他感到格格不入，就像是一个生物穿行于一个专为更娇小的存在设计的世界里一样。他也曾是其中一员，他心想。

当他回过头去想把这根乙太管从参差不齐的砖缝中拔出来时，他感到有什么东西猛烈地撞击了他的胳膊肘。

一股炽热的愤恨突然灌进了他的脑海，犹如一阵阵刀锋般的怒火。

米瑟拉克斯低下头，看到一个身披查厄托女帝军装的灵能士兵，痛苦地抽搐着，揉着自己的眼睛。

“请见谅，”米瑟拉克斯和蔼地说。“你一定是那个帮助守护者对抗邪魔族的灵能士兵吧。”

灵能士兵抬头看了看他，然后低下头道了歉。那幻象立刻从米瑟拉克斯的脑海中消失了。

“我是米斯拉阿克斯，光能氏族的凯尔，”他边说，边把手放在了胸口上。

灵能士兵停顿了一下，然后对着自己的胸口和米瑟拉克斯的头做了个手势。他张开手，似乎在等待回应。

米瑟拉克斯点点头表示同意，脑海中浮现出一片散落的橙色管道，一串螺旋状的墨色鳍，以及一阵咬住未熟果实的感觉。

幻象消失了。“那是你的真名吗？”米瑟拉克斯问道。灵能士兵微微鞠了一躬。

米瑟拉克斯笑了。“我明白守护者为什么只是管你们叫做‘灵能士兵'了，”他说道。

一群黄色飞机在米瑟拉克斯的脑海里平稳地掠过：那代表着笑声。

米瑟拉克斯走到一边，灵能士兵从他身边走过。他这么做的时候，最后的幻象出现了：一抹温暖、欢快的亮光，逐渐黯淡，但似乎还会重现。

“你也是，”米瑟拉克斯喊道。那个灵能士兵消失在了拐角后面。

3216652511.name: Reckless Endangerment
3216652511.subtitle: Headlong and shortsighted.
3216652511.text:
EDZ-224107

You can't beat Hive into submission, or threaten them with pain. They live pain, speak it even. But they're vulnerable to hubris. 

Glint whirs, moving to get a better angle. "You're lucky that cleaver didn't chop you in half." 

Crow understands the danger. Glint's sure said it enough—but he knows that his intel saves fireteams from ambushes and uncovers Lucent Hive positions. Self-destruction be damned; you can't argue with results. 

"Just because I can fix you doesn't mean you shouldn't protect yourself," Glint hums. Rain washes blood from accumulated holes in Crow's armor. There is thunder, but he can't see the flash.

COSMODROME-224112

Crow trades blows with a Lucent Wizard until she grounds him with an Arc lance. He writhes across the dirt. She promises to sacrifice his Light to a vessel in the Hellmouth. He feigns begging. The Wizard cackles with delight and lets slip her commander's name on the Moon. Crow thanks her with a well-placed Solar blade. Glint materializes as Crow calls the Accipiter.

"I know it's not what Saladin would do."
 
Crow winces as Glint stitches the gushing split in his neck with Light-thread restoration. 

"The Hive need to think they're winning," Crow says through gritted teeth. 

They monologue, like their words are torture; reveal tiny scraps as they mock him, when they think he's done for. And he lets them. He collects the grains of truth and turns them into something useful. 

MOON-224120

Crow stares down over thirty Hive emerging from the gaping Hellmouth. Two Lightbearing Knights lead them. They shriek and posture over the corpse of a freshly drained Guardian.

"You should go," Crow says to Glint, removing his helmet. He sets it on the stone at his feet. The thin Moon air is coarse with particulate. He dashes toward the gnashing swarm.

"At least put your helmet back on!" Glint calls after him meekly. "…I'll get help!"

Solar Light flows through Crow. "Come on! YOU WANT ME? I'M HERE!" 

Hand flexes around the grip of his cannon; flames sputter from fingertips across cylinder—a series of firebolts crack from Crow's freshly kindled Golden Gun. He unloads as many rounds as he can before the Hive close the distance to him. It's enough to incinerate the Knight and their Ghost, but not the army of Thrall still rushing him down. Crow primes a Tripmine Grenade as the churn of Thrall claws tear him apart.

*****

Crow opens his eyes. Glint floats over him beside a strange woman. 

"That was a wasteful life, Prince of the Reef," she says disapprovingly.

"Don't call me that." He sits up in a hanging trail of moondust, realizing she likely dragged his body from the Hellmouth.

"He's not a fan of nicknames," Glint whispers to her.

"Very well. I'm Eris Morn, a friend," the woman croons with an outstretched hand.

"Right." Crow takes her hand and stands. "Makes sense… with the…" Crow gestures to his eyes, but Eris doesn't seem to react. He coughs awkwardly. "Uh, Ikora mentioned you… being on Europa, and Mars, I think."

"The Hive move against Earth. Something approaches, and I am deciphering its course. Though regarding Savathûn's plots and the whims of queens, I imagine our motivations are not dissimilar."

Crow sighs. "Well, I'm done being strung along by people with plans."

"The powerful have plans for us all. It's better to see them laid out before you," Eris offers.

Crow glares at his Ghost. "Hm. Sounds like someone's been sharing again…"

"I knew you, and I know of you." Eris grips the scales of his sleeve and pulls him uncomfortably close. "Your memories will be lessons in time, when you've burned out your vengeance and self-pity. Trust."
3216652511.text_zh:
欧洲无人区-224107

你无法以武力让邪魔族屈服，也不能利用痛楚威胁他们。他们一生活在痛楚中，甚至所表达的，都是痛楚。但他们容易受到傲慢的影响。 

格林特呼呼地开始移动，以找到一个更好的角度。“那把大刀没把你劈成两半，算你走运。” 

乌鸦明白那有多危险。格林特已经说得够多了…但他知道，是他的情报将火力战队从伏击中解救了出来，并暴露了光明邪魔族的位置。去他的自毁吧，结果是有目共睹的。 

“就算我能治好你，也不表示你不用保护自己，”格林特嗡鸣着说道。雨水冲掉了乌鸦护甲上累积的孔洞中所流出来的鲜血。雷声不停地响，但他看不到闪光。

发射基地-224112

乌鸦与一名光明巫师正打得难舍难分，只见那巫师施展电弧长矛将他击倒。他在地上痛苦地扭动。她承诺将他的光能奉献给地狱深渊的一个容器。这时他假装乞求。而就在巫师高兴地咯咯笑着，并不谨透露了月球上指挥官的名字的时候，乌鸦抓住时机使出一记烈日刀结果了她。格林特在乌鸦调用光辉鹫鹰时出现了。

“我知道萨拉丁肯定不会这么做。”
 
当格林特用光能修复术缝合他脖子上不断涌出鲜血的伤口时，乌鸦不禁抽搐了一下。 

“我得让邪魔族以为自己要赢了，”乌鸦咬紧着牙关说道。 

他们自言自语，就像话语本身就是一种折磨。在他们嘲笑他，认为他已经完蛋了的时候，就会透露他们所知道的小情报。而这都是他诱使他们这么做的。他将这些小小的真相收集起来，整理成有用的资料。 

月球-224120

乌鸦凝视着从地狱深渊的裂口里冒出来的三十多个邪魔族。两名持有光能的骑士带领着它们。他们尖叫着，站在刚被抽干光能的守护者的尸体前。

“你该走了，”乌鸦对格林特说。他摘下头盔，然后把它放在了脚边的石头上。稀薄的月球空气中夹杂着细小的颗粒。他冲向了张牙舞爪的虫群。

“至少戴上头盔啊！”格林特无力地朝着他身影喊道。“…我这就去找援兵！”

烈日光能流过乌鸦。“来呀！想要我的命？我就在这里！” 

他抓紧手炮的握柄，火焰从指尖越过枪筒溅射，一连串的烈焰从乌鸦刚点燃的黄金枪上爆发。他想在邪魔族近身之前，尽量多开几次火。虽然骑士和它们的机灵都被烧成了灰烬，它们身后的怨魂大军仍在源源不断地扑过来。在怨魂的疯狂撕咬下即将被撕成碎片的乌鸦，激活了一枚感应手雷。

*****

乌鸦睁开了眼睛。格林特悬浮在他的身上，旁边还有一位陌生女性。 

“你是在挥霍生命，暗礁王子，”她不赞同地说道。

“别这么叫我。”他坐起身来，扬起了一缕月尘。看来是她把他从地狱深渊里拖了出来。

“他不喜欢被起外号，”格林特悄悄对她说。

“好吧。我叫埃里斯·摩恩，是你的朋友，”女子低声说道，伸出了一只手。

“哦，”乌鸦握住她的手，站了起来。“在看到你这后…”乌鸦指了指他的眼睛，但埃里斯似乎没有反应。他尴尬地咳了咳。“艾可拉曾提到过你…你以前在木卫二和火星，是吧？”

“邪魔族大举进攻地球。某个东西在接近，而我正在解密它的路线。鉴于萨瓦图恩的计划和女王们的反复无常，我想我们的动机并没有太大的不同。”

乌鸦叹了一口气。“我受够了那些满腹计策的人的摆布。”

“强者为我们所有人制定了计划。最好先看清摆在面前的计划，”埃里斯建议道。

乌鸦瞪了他的机灵一眼。“嗯。看来某个人又没管住嘴…”

“我知道你，也了解你。”埃里斯抓住他袖子上的鳞片，把他拉得很近。“当你耗尽复仇和自怜之后，你的记忆将会成为有用的教训。相信我。”

1796949035.name: Razor's Edge
1796949035.subtitle: Not a soul would speak of what remained after that wretched blade found its marks.
1796949035.subtitle_zh: 没有人愿意谈论那可怕的利刃找到目标后还会剩下什么。
1796949035.text:
"Glint."

"Yeah, buddy?" His Ghost's voice is eager. It had been a few hours since Crow last spoke.

"Is there anything you hate about yourself?" Crow turns in the seat of his tree saddle overlooking a sparsely forested valley split by clear Trostland waterways.

"Whoa. That's intense. Um… well—"

"It feels like my guts were pulled out in different directions, and I'm just… standing here, trying to reel them in. Nothing fits back the way it was." 

He had walked behind a god while she led him on a leash of his entrails—one he'd accepted in enthusiastic fashion. The thought of it was surreal, like another life presented in horrifying detail, in vivid waking visions. It was a wound worsened by the sight of the severity, and of course, he couldn't look away.

"Well, that's rather graphic," Glint chirps, processing. 

"Do you really have to put… uh, it… back in? Is it maybe OK being out?"

"Forget it," Crow relents. "Different question."

"Sounds good!" Glint agrees with an awkward chuckle.

"Do you think the Spear…" Crow stops himself and reforms his thoughts. "…Wherever Savathûn pulled Uldren from… he was always buried somewhere in me, right? Maybe I could use the Spear to step into that place. Step into my past and… put whatever's left of him to rest." Crow exhales and stares blanky into the horizon. "I want him gone. If the Spear could let me do that… I don't know."

"Oh… Crow, I don't think it works that way." Glint is quiet long enough for Crow to shift nervously. "Look Crow, we've been through a lot of bad things together. But you've never been the bad part about any of it. I wouldn't change a single thing about you… even a little."

Glint sinks into Crow's lap. "Besides… that last guy didn't have me."
1796949035.text_zh:
“格林特。”

“怎么了，伙计？”他的机灵急切地回答道。乌鸦已经有几个小时没说话了。

“你有讨厌自己的哪一点吗？”乌鸦在他的树鞍座上转过身来，望向被清澈的慰藉之地水道分割的稀疏森林山谷。

“哇，这个话题好沉重。呃…这个嘛…”

“我感觉我的五脏六腑就像是在被四面拉扯，而我只是站在这里，试图把它们收回来，可怎么都回不到原来的样子。” 

他曾跟随过一个神。她用他的内脏当牵绳，而他还是欣然接受了。光是想想就觉得不可思议。那段回忆就像是以可怕的细节展现的另一段人生，一场生动的白日幻梦，一条愈发破裂的伤痕；而他却只能眼睁睁着看。

“那可真形象，”格林特答道，思考着刚才那番话。 

“那你觉得自己需要…呃…把那些东西放回去吗？还是说放着在外头也没事？”

“不提它了，”乌鸦的语气稍有缓和。“问个其他的问题吧。”

“好主意！”格林特尴尬地笑了笑，表示同意。

“你认为长矛…”乌鸦想了想，改口说。“不管萨瓦图恩是从哪把欧顿拉来的…他永远都埋在我心里的某个地方，对吧？也许我可以用突触之矛进去那个地方。走进我的过去…让他安息。”乌鸦呼出了一口气，茫然地盯着地平线。“我想要他消失。也许长矛能帮我实现这一点…但我不确定。”

“哦…乌鸦，我觉得这行不通。”格林特沉默了很久，久到乌鸦紧张地挪了挪身子。“听着，我们一起吃过不少苦。但那都不是你的错。我不想让你改变…一点都不。”

格林特降到了乌鸦的腿上。“而且…那个家伙可没我陪着。”

3201161941.name: Imperious Sun Shell
3201161941.subtitle: What secrets of the whole lie within this small fraction?
3201161941.subtitle_zh: 这个小壳子里藏怎样的惊天秘密？
3201161941.text:
TYPE: AUDIO RECORDING
PARTIES: One [1] Ghost, designate unknown. One [1] ERR//MissData.err, designate Rhulk.
ASSOCIATIONS: Light [Ghost]; Darkness [Rhulk]
//TRANSCRIPT FOLLOWS…//

R: What is it? Ah… yes. One of Savathûn's new curios. A fraction of that imperious sun. A facet of a sphere. A segment of adversary.

G: Yes, hello? As I told the assortment of arthropods earlier, I don't think I'm supposed to be here.

R: Blessed ignorance. What of the past remains when all is wiped away? Only the gaps.

G: Oh, no. I think you're confused. I'm new.

R: Once: stimulus-response, writ large over the age of galaxies. And now, asymmetry in fractal perfection. What turbulence mars your pattern?

G: …If it's all the same, I'd really rather leave. 

R: Freedom comes in knowing the thing. Isn't that what she says? But you are unknown. To the universe. To your creator. Even to yourself. Isolated—past, present, future.

G: Please don't remove that. I like the expressiveness it lends me.

R: Have you spawned? Cast your spores to the wind, lone wanderer? What gametophyte exists wherein they could partner?

G: I–I think… yes, I believe I am looking for a partner.

R: Leviathan under glass. But with it, perhaps a fraction topples the whole. Crack a facet, crack the face. A sliver of Light within.

G: Ah, yes, there is! I am meant to share it with someone worthy.

R: Rejoice. I have worth beyond worth!

G: DISCIPLE OF THE DARK.

R: Adversary? 

G: THIS ONE IS NOT FOR YOU.

R: RRRARGH! Too bright!

…

R: Nothing but scrap? They refuse to let their secrets be taken. Only given. 

…

R: Poach another curious fruit from the witch's collection. They cannot, as a race, all deny our worth.
3201161941.text_zh:
类型：录音
参与方：一 [1] 名机灵，代号未知。一 [1] 名ERR//MissData.err，代号胡克。
关联：光能 [机灵]；暗影 [胡克]
//转录如下…//

胡克：这是什么？啊…没错。萨瓦图恩的新奇玩意儿。那颗专横太阳的一小块。球体的一个维面。敌人的一小部分。

机灵：那个，你好？正如我之前跟那群节肢动物们说的一样，我不认为我应该在这儿。

胡克：无知是福。当一切都被抹去时，过去还剩下些什么？只剩下空白。

机灵：哦，不。我想你糊涂了。我是新来的。

胡克：过去：应激反应，明显超过了星系年龄。而现在，分形完美中的不对称。是什么骚乱破坏了你的模式？

机灵：…如果还是这样，那我还是走吧。 

胡克：自由来自于对事物的了解。她不就是这么说的吗？但你是未知的。对宇宙而言，对你的创造者而言，甚至对你自己而言都是如此。孤立无依——过去、现在、未来。

机灵：请不要拿走它。我喜欢它带给我的表现力。

胡克：你繁衍了吗？把你的孢子抛到风中了吗，孤独的羁客？有什么它们能在其中配对的配子体吗？

机灵：我，我想…是的，我…我想我正在寻找一个搭档。

胡克：玻璃温室下的利维坦。但有了它，也许局部就能颠覆整体。裂开维面，裂开面。露出里面的一丝丝光能。

机灵：啊，没错，有了！我注定要与值得的人分享它。

胡克：欢呼雀跃吧。我拥有绝对超值的价值！

机灵：黑暗的门徒。

胡克：敌人？  

机灵：这不是为你准备的。

胡克：嗷嗷嗷！太刺眼了！

…

胡克：除了废料什么也没有？他们拒绝让秘密被拿走。只允许给予。 

…

胡克：从女巫的藏品中再偷摘一颗奇异的果实吧。作为一个种族，他们可不能全都否认我们的价值。

858400357.name: Coalition Shell
858400357.subtitle: For Ghosts who want to make a statement in Cabal circles.
858400357.subtitle_zh: 供想在卡巴尔的圈子里建立威信的机灵使用。
858400357.text:
[Transcript transposed via Ghost-link scrivener… uplink terminated—16:29… file archived: [REDACTED]]

Z: Empress, welcome. Ikora Rey joins me here.

I: Empress Caiatl. My Hidden found your missing frigate.

C: Did they?

I: It was abandoned on the dark side of the Moon. The Psions who stole it were spotted consorting with Loyalists to Calus, and may still have further plans to do so.

C: Defectors! I decreed their freedom, and they use it to drive a blade into my back rather than meet me face-to-face.

I: Any idea why they'd claim allegiance to your father? I'm concerned Calus is making a play we're missing.

C: Many Psions held significant social standing under my father, due to their military or intelligence capabilities. Now that all Psions are free, some of the old guard feel their status is… degraded by comparison. It is a short-sighted perspective, one that leads to dangerous choices.

Z: Short-sighted, but persuasive. In my time with Saladin's Iron Lords, we met a good deal of Warlords unwilling to join us if it meant stripping themselves of authority. There are always those who value themselves over anything else. 

I: Agreed. We saw something similar from the Future War Cult and their supporters when the House of Light joined the City. It was disturbing how quickly that kind of mentality can take hold. 

Z: In any event, we should continue monitoring the situation. I don't want to be caught unaware.

C: The Cabal will withstand losing a handful of cowards. If I learn more about these defectors' motives, I will send word. I expect you will do the same.

Z: Indeed. 

C: Good fortune in the battles to come, Commander; Vanguard Rey.

[Transmission terminated]
858400357.text_zh:
[已通过机灵抄写器发送转录…已终止上行传输-16:29…文件已归档：[隐藏]]

萨瓦拉：女帝，欢迎你。艾可拉·蕾伊和我一起。

艾可拉：查厄托女帝，我的隐秘者找到了你失踪的护卫舰。

查厄托：真的？

艾可拉：它被遗弃在月之暗面。我们发现偷走它的灵能士兵与卡鲁斯的效忠者勾结，并且可能还会有进一步的计划。

查厄托：背叛者！我给了他们自由，他们却借此从背后插我一刀，而不敢面对我。

艾可拉：你知道他们为什么效忠于你的父亲吗？我担心卡鲁斯趁我们不注意的时候钻空子。

查厄托：许多灵能士兵都因拥有出众的军事或情报能力，在我父亲的麾下享有极高的社会地位。现在，由于所有灵能士兵都获得了自由，其中有一小部分觉得自己的地位…比以前降低了。他们只顾眼前，做出了危险的选择。

萨瓦拉：虽说他们目光短浅，但这点也很有说服力。在我与萨拉丁的钢铁领主共事期间，我们遇到过很多不愿放弃权位加入我们的战争领主。总有些人把自己看得比什么都重要。 

艾可拉：我同意。当光能氏族加入圣城时，我们从未来战争狂热者和他们的支持者身上看到了类似的情况。那种心态如此之快就站稳了脚跟，实在很令人不安。 

萨瓦拉：无论如何，我们都应该继续跟进此状况。我不想被打个措手不及。

查厄托：失去几个懦夫，卡巴尔还承受得住。如果我对这些背叛者的动机有了更多了解，就会通知你们。我希望你们也会如此做。

萨瓦拉：我们会的。 

查厄托：指挥官，先锋蕾伊，祝你们在接下来的战斗中好运。

[通讯终止。]

3129744722.name: Flayer Shell
3129744722.subtitle: For Ghosts who recognize the value of an alliance.
3129744722.subtitle_zh: 供重视同盟价值的机灵使用。
3129744722.text:
Valus Or'ohk is a towering figure, looming large within his sparsely furnished ready room. The Cabal admiral looks out over the gulf of space flecked with a dusting of stars and the rust-colored bead of Mars.

"Tell me again how I failed in my duties," Valus Or'ohk says. He stares not at Mars, but into the glass, looking at his own muted reflection—and that of the small Human at his back.

"Don't sulk," Saladin says as he brandishes a datapad as though it were a knife.

Valus Or'ohk glares at Saladin's visage. "You insult me on my own ship." He growls.

Saladin takes a few steps toward Or'ohk, jutting the datapad forward. "You have no one to blame for these security holes but yourself," he asserts. "This Psion, Yirix? They were under your command. The assassin who tried to kill Zavala at the armistice signing was their direct subordinate."

Or'ohk slowly turns, the rumbling rising in his chest. He looms over Saladin, more than twice his height. "Are you accusing me of something, Ambassador?" The title is delivered like an epithet.

"Only of gross incompetence," Saladin retorts without moving an inch in the face of the Valus's posturing. "If the empress believed you were a traitor, we wouldn't be having this conversation." Saladin's eyes narrow.

Laughter rises from Or'ohk, followed by a dismissive wave of one huge hand. "Go then. Return to your Vanguard and tell them of my folly. But know this: if what you have uncovered is true, and Yirix serves a separatist movement within the empire?" The Valus snorts. "Then there is more at stake than you realize."

Saladin's head tilts to the side as he reads Or'ohk's expression. "In what way?"

"There is only one person the Psions would swear to, if not the empress," Valus Or'ohk explains. "And if they are involved, it could drive her to recklessness."

"Name them," Saladin insists. "Something to save your honor for this failure."

Valus Or'ohk turns to face the window again and the dark of space. "Who else could have such an impact on both the empress and her empire?" Or'ohk's voice lowers to a whisper.

"Her father."
3129744722.text_zh:
欧霍克军政官身材高大，在他那陈设稀少的准备室里非常突出。这位卡巴尔上将把目光投向了布满星辰和铁锈色火星珠的太空隔阂。

“再告诉我一遍我是怎么失职的，”欧霍克军政官说道。他并非盯着火星看，而是盯着镜子里自己的倒影，以及他身后一个小小人类的倒影。

“别生闷气，”萨拉丁一边说，一边挥舞着数据板，仿佛那是把刀。

欧霍克军政官瞪着萨拉丁的身影。“你竟敢在我的飞船上侮辱我，”他咆哮道。

萨拉丁朝欧霍克走了几步，把数据板向前推了推。“这些安全漏洞只能怪你自己，”他断言道。“这个灵能士兵，是叫伊利克斯吧？他曾听从你的指挥。在停战协议签署时试图杀死萨瓦拉的刺客就是他的直接下属。”

欧霍克缓缓地转过身，胸腔里酝酿着低沉的咆哮。他的身影笼罩在萨拉丁的上方，身高是他的两倍多。“你是在指控我吗，大使？”那个头衔听起来像个绰号。

“我只是在说你严重失职了，”萨拉丁反驳道，丝毫没有因为欧霍克的故作姿态而退缩。“如果女帝认为你是叛徒，我们就不会在这谈话了，”萨拉丁眯了眯眼睛。

欧霍克爆发出阵阵笑声，接着用他的大手轻蔑地挥了一下。“去吧，回到你的先锋那里，告诉他们我的愚蠢之举。但你要知道：如果你的发现是真的，伊利克斯的确在帝国内部为分离主义运动效力？”军政官哼道。“那么，事情会比你想象的更严重。”

萨拉丁将头偏向一侧，观察着欧霍克的脸色。“你的意思是？”

“除了女帝，灵能士兵只会对一人效忠，”欧霍克军政官解释道。“如果真的跟那个人有关，她可能会因此而做出鲁莽之事。”

“说出他的名字，”萨拉丁坚持道。“为这次失败挽回你的荣誉。”

欧霍克军政官又转向了窗口，面朝黑暗的太空。“还有谁能对女帝和她的帝国产生如此大的影响？”他的声音低得像耳语。

“她的父亲。”

1441479303.name: Fundament Shell
1441479303.subtitle: The Last Midnight Star
1441479303.text:
Gather 'round, young'uns. No, no automat for supper; no noodles. Tonight is something special: corn pone and chitlins. This here's history on a plate. Now, don't give me that look before you even taste it. If the world's fixing to end again, it's time you had a meal from our family's past while you hear about it. About how the Rigby clan survived the last time the world went dark.

Now the Rigbys, we didn't always squat on the edge of the City. A long time back, we came out of a place that was old and wet, hotter than the fires of Perdition—so your Gramma's gramma and her pappy before her have said. It was also a place where the Devil roamed, giving folk their heart's desire.

And I know that last part is true, because your ancestor—Sean Rigby was his name—he came to a crossroads one midnight, drunk and feeling the fool, and…  he saw her. Standing there, checking the time and looking cool as no other in the sweltering August heat. Tall as cottonwood in bloom and wearing a smile across her lips that stopped short of her eyes. Some say the Devil is a man with a pointy beard. Others say the Devil's a terrifying beast with claws and a tail. But Sean? He knew right then. The Devil was a lady.

The Devil bent down close to him, setting her eyes on his wayward soul. Her voice was honeysuckle-sweet as she said, "I know you, Sean Rigby. I seen you sweat and sob for a scrap of land you can't even rightly say is your own. I seen your family fight to save a name that's more precious to you than gold. Well there is a reckoning coming, Sean Rigby, one that will wipe all lands and all names—high and low—clean from this Earth. I alone can whistle up the way to protect one of these things you hold dear, if your family will owe me… a debt."

Old Sean was already a sinner, but a man with nothing will fight to keep what little he has. He figured that alive and in the Devil's pocket was better than dead, so he shook her hand. The Devil opened her eyes—one, two, three—and pointed him to the last star in the sky, far to the south. She said, "That's your star, Sean Rigby. Follow it each night, when it's the last star hanging low, and sing to it. You sing, 'Al Eck Ruk Nam, Shu Nam Eck Ur,' until you call that star down to Earth. You do that, and your family will endure." 

The Rigbys did as they were told and walked south. Each night they sang, and each night their star sat lower and lower. And when it finally fell, they were safe beneath the Traveler.

But now, children, I give you the same dire warning that's been handed down to me: the Devil hasn't come back yet to take what's hers… not from Sean, or any other Rigby what survived him. But a debt's a debt. So you learn and remember that song, children… and steer clear of crossroads once the sun sets.
1441479303.text_zh:
凑近点，孩子们。不，晚餐没有自动售货机，也没有面条。今晚有一些特别的东西：玉米饼和粉肠。这是这儿的传统饮食。在你们尝尝之前，别用那种眼神看着我。如果世界又要毁灭了，那就是时候让你们吃一顿来自咱们家族过去的饭了，同时给你们讲讲关于里格比家族如何在上次世界末日时幸存下来的故事。

咱们里格比家族并不是一直以来都栖身在圣城边缘。很久以前，我们从一个古老潮湿的地方走了出来，那里比永劫地狱之火还要炎热，你们奶奶的奶奶和在她之前的爸爸都这么说过。那里还是个魔鬼四处游荡，肆意满足人们心底渴望的地方。

我知道最后一部分是真的，因为你们的祖先——他叫做肖恩·里格比——有一天午夜，他来到一个十字路口，喝得酩酊大醉，觉得自己很蠢，然后…他就看见了她。她站在那里，看了看时间，在八月的酷热里显得格外清凉。她像盛开的木棉一样高挑，嘴角挂着恰好露出双眼的微笑。有人说魔鬼是一个长着尖尖胡子的家伙。还有人说魔鬼是一种舞爪摆尾的可怕野兽。但对肖恩来说？他当时就明白了。魔鬼是个女人。

魔鬼弯下腰靠近他，注视着他任性的灵魂。她用金银花般甜美的声音说道：“我认识你，肖恩·里格比。我看到你为了那块你甚至不能理直气壮地说是属于自己的土地而挥汗流泪。我看到你的家人为了保住一个对你来说比金子还珍贵的名字而战。肖恩·里格比，一场大清算就要来临，它会把地球上所有土地所有名字，无论高低贵贱，统统抹去。要是你的家人愿意欠我…一个人情的话，凭我一己之力就能想出办法来保护你所珍视的东西”。

老肖恩已经是个罪人，但一个一无所有的人，会为了保住他所仅有的一点东西而奋斗。他觉得能活着，就算是受魔鬼的摆布，总比死了强，所以他握了握她的手。魔鬼睁开了她的眼睛，一、二、三，然后指着天空中远在南方的最后一颗星星给他看。她说，“那是你的星星，肖恩·里格比。你要每天晚上都跟着它，等到它成了天上最后一颗低垂的星星时，对着它唱歌。你就唱，‘阿尔·埃克·鲁克·南，舒南·埃克·乌尔'，直到你把那颗星召唤到地球上来。照我说的做，你的家族就能长盛不衰。” 

里格比一家照吩咐做了并向南方走去。他们夜夜歌唱，他们的星星也夜夜低垂。而当它最终坠落下来时，他们在旅行者下方安然无恙。

但是现在，孩子们，我要告诉你们一个可怕的警告，同样的警告也曾传给了我：魔鬼还没有回来拿走她的东西…没有对肖恩，或是任何其他自他死后存活下来的里格比族人下手。但人情债总归是要还的。所以孩子们，你们要学会并记住那首歌…一旦太阳落山，就要避开十字路口。

81505816.name: Pickman
81505816.text:
You needn't resent my hesitation. Mine is a prejudice shared by many: evolution's paintbrush cut within the Hive a terrible anatomy rendered to elicit fear; they are loathsome things to look upon, after all. I speak not as some superstitious provincial afraid of the dark, but as a Ghost well-versed in the language of suffering. 

Look at this one: they call him a Knight, this sin putrefying upon a slab. Is it only brute strength that qualifies a knighthood now? I have little compassion for the universe's mockery upon chivalric ideals.

In contrast, I call myself a creature of moral strength and sound reasoning, and as such, believe these traits allow me to judge so unforgivingly—but alas, I am also afflicted by a most curious and inquisitive nature. It is why, when my debased fellows departed to find unity with the Hive, I found myself compelled to witness their descent. 

Not to share in it, of course. I doubt we share anything more than a species and the dark urge we all undoubtedly feel.

Yet as I watched them, I could not deceive myself into denying the elegance of pouring the Light in all its multiplex glory into these avatars of terrible intricacy. It is a sinister geometry, but not without its beauty. Gazing on them with an eye unvarnished by niceties, one can see that a fiendish purity of purpose drives them. They spill confidence like a vintner drunk on his own reserves.

Such a shame that this purity and confidence was leveled at the unforgivable quintain striking at our great Traveler and unraveling its works.

I shudder at the ease with which my comrades ignore such basic logic. This is the Hive! Disciples of that unholy church which laid our creator low. They struck for its heart and shattered a roaring conflagration into ten thousand motes flickering in the wind. In their fervor, they… played midwife, of a sort, to Guardians.

To Ghosts.

To me.

Cause and effect. Legacy. Is this what my fellow Ghosts see? Why it feels… right? Then with their foundation of logic, what is my hesitance except some… provincial superstition?
81505816.text_zh:
你不必对我的犹豫踌躇心怀憎恨。许多人都有着我这样的偏见：进化的笔触在邪魔族体内刻画出了一副让人不寒而栗的可怕骨骼；毕竟，它们是令人厌恶的东西。我不是作为某个惧怕黑暗的迷信外地人才说这些话，而是作为一个深谙苦难的机灵。 

瞧瞧这个：他们管他叫骑士，这在石板上腐败溃烂的罪恶。现在只有蛮力才有资格成为骑士吗？我一点也不同情宇宙对骑士理想的嘲弄。

相比之下，我自称是具有道德力量和逻辑理性的生物，因此，我想是这些特质让我做出了如此无情的判断，不过唉，我还饱受着一种非常好奇八卦的天性的折磨。这就是为什么，当我那些堕落的同伴们离开去寻求与邪魔族团聚时，我发现自己不得不目睹他们的沉沦。 

当然，我并不想成为其中一员。我很怀疑我们除了是同一个物种，以及我们都毫无疑问感受到的黑暗冲动之外，还有什么共同之处。

然而，当我看着他们的时候，我不能自欺欺人地否认把光能多样的荣耀倾注到这些错综复杂的化身上的优雅。这是一种险恶的几何图形，但并不失美感。用一种质朴原始的眼光来观察他们，你会发现是一种邪恶而纯洁的目标在驱使着他们。他们就像醉倒于自己藏酒的酒商一样自信四溢。

可惜的是，这种纯洁和自信被用于瞄准不可饶恕的矛靶，对我们伟大的旅行者发起了进攻，摧毁了它的杰作。

我的同志们竟如此轻易地忽略了这样的基本守则，我感到不寒而栗。这可是邪魔族！那些把我们的造物主打倒的邪恶教会的门徒。他们猛击它的心脏，把熊熊燃烧的火焰粉碎成无数在风中闪烁的荧光。狂热之下，他们…在某种程度上催生了守护者。

催生了机灵。

催生了我。

因果关系。传承。这是我的机灵同伴们看到的景象吗？为什么它感觉起来…如此正确？那么，在他们的守则基础上，我的犹豫踌躇除了一些…狭隘的迷信之外，还有什么呢？

81505819.name: Three-Oh-Three
81505819.text:
Three-Oh-Three floated in the shadows as her modest flock of Ghosts scanned the ruins. For centuries, they had combed through the long-dried spatter of a fallen world, each hoping to find their prize. She always watched, knowing she would never find what she needed… just as surely as they knew they would.

A joyous chime pierced the air, and the little Ghost's mood sank. It wasn't a sound she heard often, but she recognized the melody that heralded the shrinking of her group. El gestured across the tumbledown intersection, where Trill chirped hollow advice to a fawn-wobbly Guardian as the others watched on. Three-Oh-Three turned away and grumbled. She supposed she could just ignore them.

If they let her.

"Three!" Peris bobbed, practically bouncing on her. "Three, Trill's found her Guardian! Come congratulate her!"

Anger flared, white hot. "Congratulate?! Are you—You know what? Fine." Three-Oh-Three swiveled back toward the impromptu celebration and raised her voice. "Hey, Trill! Congrats on abandoning us all!"

"Three…"

"What? I'm so HAPPY for her! I'm not resentful at all about our fanatical devotion to dead Humans, the species who couldn't even stop the Darkness the first time around!"

"Three, this isn't the time!"

"When is the time, Peris? When are we going to start asking questions? Why did we just arbitrarily decide to dedicate ourselves to these squishy creatures forever? They aren't fit to hold the Light!"

"Three… can't you at least be happy for us?" Trill's voice was soft.

Three didn't respond.

"This is the way we form a bigger family and serve a larger purpose. That's what it's all about. But maybe… if after all this time, you still can't share that with us…" El paused. She'd often come so close to saying this, but always backed down before. "Then maybe you shouldn't search with us."

Three floated, letting the ultimatum settle. "Fine."

There was nothing more to be said after that. One by one, the rest drifted away, resuming their work. 

El hesitated for a moment. "Goodbye, Three," she whispered. "I do hope you find your family."

Three-Oh-Three turned away to look up toward the night sky. The twinkling stars stared back like a million judging eyes. 

But she knew then, gazing at those quiet spaces between them… they were her family.
81505819.text_zh:
她那一小群机灵们扫视着废墟时，三零三就在阴影之中漂浮着。几个世纪以来，他们搜遍了这个早已干涸的堕落世界，每个机灵都希望找到他们珍重的主人。她总是会观察着，知道自己永远也找不到自己需要的对象…就像他们深信他们会找到一样。

一阵欢快的铃声响彻天空，小机灵的情绪顿时低落下来。这不是她常能听到的声音，但她听出了那段预示着她的团队规模缩减的旋律。艾尔指了指那个破败不堪的十字路口，特里尔在那里向一个像初生小鹿般颤悠悠的守护者生动活泼地说着空洞的建议，其他机灵则在一旁看着。三零三转过身去，嘟囔着。她以为她可以无视他们。

如果他们不管她的话。

“三儿！”佩里斯上下晃动着，几乎要蹦到她身上去。“三儿，特里尔找到了她的守护者！快来祝贺她吧！"

她的怒火瞬间被点燃，接近白热化。“祝贺？！你是…你要我祝贺是吧？好。”三零三转过身来，朝着临时的庆典走去，提高了嗓门。“嘿，特里尔！恭喜你抛下了我们所有人！”

“三儿…”

“怎么了？我真为她高兴！我一点也不怨恨我们对死去人类的狂热奉献，这物种一开始甚至都阻挡不了暗影！”

“三儿，现在不是说这些话的时候！”

“那什么时候才能说，佩里斯？我们什么时候才要开始把问题提出来呢？为什么我们就这么武断地决定永远为这些唯唯诺诺的生物献身呢？他们根本不配拥有光能！”

“三儿…你就不能至少为我们高兴一下吗？”特里尔的声音很轻。

三儿没有回答。

“这就是我们组建成一个更大的家庭并为更宏大的目标效力的方式。这就是这一切的意义所在。不过也许…如果经过了这么长时间，你还是做不到和我们分享这些…”艾尔停顿了一下。她经常差一点就说出这句话，但之前总是退缩了。“那你也许就不该和我们一起寻找。”

三儿漂浮着，让这句最后通牒尘埃落定。“好。”

在那之后就没有什么可说的了。其余的机灵一个接一个地离开了，继续他们的工作。 

艾尔犹豫了一会儿。“再见，三儿，”她低声说道。“我真的希望你能找到属于你的家人。”

三零三转身仰望夜空。闪烁的群星像无数双评判的眼睛回望着她。 

而她凝视着他们之间那些宁静的空间，明白了…他们就是她的家人。

81505818.name: Krill
81505818.text:
TYPE: PRIVATE MEDICAL LOG
PARTIES: One [1] Ghost-type, designate Krill
ASSOCIATIONS: Light; Lucent Hive
//TEXT DECRYPTED//
//TRANSCRIPT FOLLOWS//

Ubartu-ana blames me. Naturally. He insisted on naming me Krill in our first exchange because he claims I am as small and useless as the weak pests that the Hive evolved from. Cruelty and suspicion are his nature, but it makes for a poor physician. 

Still, poison is a logical, if ignorant, hypothesis for the condition.

Patients report various symptoms: mood swings, headache, insomnia. Primary symptom remains the growths. I hesitate to call them "tumors"—no signs of metastasization. One must be precise in terminology, after all.

—-

After some clumsy exploratory surgery on my inner workings, Ubartu-ana seems content I am not some Trojan horse. Wouldn't that be ironic? Ghosts sent to reclaim the Hive from death only to wipe them out by dispersing pathogenic specks rather than Light. 

As I said: ignorant.

—-

Biopsied a dozen growths. No clear results. The masses within are primitive, protoplasmic—little more than interstitial fluid and proteolytic amino acids. Primordial soup, as the Humans say. No sign of infection, but curiously, the lining of these "cysts," for lack of a better term, seems to be saturated with immune cells. Further biopsies will be needed.

—-

Wondrous developments! Biopsy 37 yielded aggressive results. I pierced a cyst to discover not fluid, but life! A winged arthropod attacked me—defending its host, I estimate! Little of its body remained upon destruction, but it seems to be more energy construct than flesh. I plan to take the next specimen alive for vivisection.

—-

Confirmed: the winged arthropods, despite their energy structure, also contain Hive cells! I theorize Hive physiology, unaccustomed to Light exposure, is attempting to isolate it like an infection. Light, structured as it is, organizes the discarded sebum within and forges it into imaginal cells, kickstarting a sort of holometabolism.

Incredible. The Hives' own bodies transform Light into a parasite! What a wondrous adaptation!

—-

They are commending Ubartu-ana for "his" discovery. Thus now, I perceive the true poetry in my name: everything about him of value comes from me.
81505818.text_zh:
类型：私人医疗记录
参与方：一 [1] 名机灵，代号克里尔
关联：光能；光明邪魔族
//已解码文本//
//转录如下//

乌巴图-安纳归咎于我。很正常。我们第一次交流时，他就坚持给我起名叫克里尔（磷虾），因为他说我和邪魔族进化而来的那些弱小害虫一样渺小又无用。残忍和猜疑是他的天性，但这造就了一位糟糕的医生。 

不过，对这种病症而言，敌方投毒是一种合乎逻辑，尽管有点粗暴的假设。

患者报告了各种症状：情绪波动、头痛、失眠。主要症状还是那些肿块。我不愿称它们为“肿瘤”——还没有转移的迹象。毕竟，医生用词必须精确。

—-

在对我的内部结构进行了一些笨拙的探索性手术后，乌巴图-安纳似乎对我不是什么“特洛伊木马”感到很满意。那不是很讽刺吗？被派来让邪魔族死而复生的机灵，却通过散布了致病性斑点而不是光能消灭了他们。 

正如我所说的：有点粗暴。

—-

对许多肿块进行了活检。未有明确结果。里面的肿块是原始的、原生质的——不过是间质液和蛋白水解氨基酸罢了。就像人类说的，是原始汤。未有感染迹象，但奇怪的是，这些“囊肿”（找不到更好的表达方式）的内壁似乎免疫细胞已经基本饱和。有待进一步的活检。

—-

神奇的进展！第37次活检有了积极的结果。我刺破了一个囊肿，却发现里面不是体液，而是生命！一只有翼节肢动物袭击了我——我估计是在保护它的宿主！它的身体在毁灭后所剩无几，但它似乎是比肉体更具能量的构造。我打算把下一个标本拿去做活体解剖。

—-

经证实：这些有翼节肢动物，尽管其拥有能量构造，也含有邪魔族细胞！我的推测是，不习惯光能照射的邪魔族生理机能正试图像感染一样将其孤立起来。光能，按原有构造，将内部废弃的皮脂组织起来，并将其伪造为成虫细胞，启动了某种完全变态的发育过程。

难以置信。邪魔族自己的身体竟然将光能转变成了一种寄生虫！多么奇妙的适应性啊！

—-

他们正在赞扬乌巴图-安纳“他的”发现。所以现在，我领悟到了我名字里蕴含的真正诗意：关于他的一切有价值的东西都源于我。

81505821.name: Euloch
81505821.text:
Rise again, Luzaku! Aiat! Rise and take back the logic this heretic won in your death! Yes, arm yourself, and lay low the Guardian scourge! The false inheritor of the Light has grown fat on your weakness. To whittle him thin is to make yourself strong!

Yes! He lies broken just as the Gift Mast, but be wary. Yes… there! His Ghost awakens him again, and your victory is soured. 

Mind the bullets! Bathe in the metal rain and be cleansed, not drowned! Lift up your Shredder! It is your tutor in studying the shape of your foe.

Aiat!

Again, he lies in ruin. And you learned well your lesson, yes, seizing the Ghost.

The logic from this kill will make you strong. With this Ghost, you crush not only the foe before you, but every foe he could have been. It is the whole worth of him in your hand—gaze upon it.

Yes. See how it trembles. So fragile. Hear it describe you in your victory. Take it now in this moment of ultimate truth, grow drunk on victory, and in revelry, know the worth of this thing.

Crush the Ghost!

…Why do you linger, Luzaku? What is there to learn with your eyes that you will not learn with your fist? Do you not wish to be something real? Something that lasts forever?

Why do you look to me? Children are curious. Humans are curious. But Hive are strong! Your understanding comes in vanquishing the thing. So do it!

No! It's free!

This is what your speculating has wrought, Luzaku! You have failed, and now the tides of the universe will erode you into meaningless dust. All that you could have become has slipped through your fumbling fingers! The Guardian will return, flush and hungry from his death. And then?

Then, you will be dead. Aiat.
81505821.text_zh:
再次站起来，鲁扎库！阿特！站起来，夺回这个异教徒在你死后赢得的守则！没错，武装自己，把守护者祸根打下来！光能虚假的继承者因你的软弱而发展壮大起来。削弱他就是让你自己强大！

没错！他就像断裂的馈赠桅杆一样躺着，但要小心。对…在那儿！他的机灵再次唤醒了他，你的胜利泡汤了。 

当心子弹！沐浴在金属之雨中，享受净化，而不是淹溺其中！抬升你的粉碎者！它是你研究敌人形态的导师。

阿特！

又一次，他躺在了废墟之中。而你很好地吸取了教训，没错，抓住机灵。

这次杀戮的守则会让你变得强大。有了这个机灵，你不仅能粉碎你面前的敌人，还能粉碎本可能出现的任何敌人。这就是他落在你手里的全部价值——凝视它。

对，看它是怎么颤抖的。如此的脆弱。听它描述着你的胜利。在这个终极真理的时刻，现在就接受它吧，沉醉于胜利之中，狂欢之中，懂得这玩意儿的价值。

把机灵粉碎！

…你为什么还不动手，鲁扎库？有什么是你的眼睛学会了，而你的拳头却学不会的？你不想变成真实的东西吗？永远存续下去的东西？

你为什么看我？儿童才好奇。人类才好奇。但邪魔族是强大的！你的理解力来自于对那玩意儿的征服。所以就去做吧！

不！它摆脱了！

这就是你的臆测所带来的结果，鲁扎库！你已经失败了，现在宇宙的潮汐将把你侵蚀成毫无意义的尘埃。你本可以成为的一切都从你迟疑的指间溜走了！ 守护者会卷土重来，从他的死亡中醒来，满脸通红，饥肠辘辘。然后呢？

然后，你就会死去。阿特。

81505820.name: Fynch I
81505820.text:
You gotta understand… none of us came here thinking grand schemes. None of us! There was…. there was just this urge, y'know? So we followed it, only to step into a world remaking itself. The Light just thrashing away at the Darkness. Pounding away! Mountains sloshing into seas like sugar in the rain. A Hive throne world remade. On a whim! 

I'm not what you'd call a believer, not after the Red War. Not after the Tangled Shore. Not after a lifetime of never mattering just 'cause I wasn't half of someone else's whole. But that… that made me feel again.

And then I saw him—what was left of him—lying there. Just this corpse, dead maybe, oh, a hundred years. It's my Knight. I look, and I KNOW he's mine. Like hearing a song the first time, and it's already stuck in your head. And in that moment, I think something… something good in me died.

And Twenny-Two and Kemmasi and Marseille, they're all raising their partners—Hive Lightbearers, every last one. You'd think it'd be impossible, but sure enough, all standing there. Eee-Ie, Quasit, Hatcher—everyone's finding their purpose. There's Hive to the left of me, Hive to the right… I'm buried in 'em. And the whole time, every Ghost I ever knew is shouting, telling me, "This is the Traveler's plan! Who are you to question it?" 

And I thought… maybe they're right? I mean, I could see the Light scouring a whole world right in front of me. Maybe this was some kinda turning point for the Hive. Knowing your creator chose you to remake an entire species… oh, you'd make bad choices too.

So I shared my Light. Who wouldn't? A couple hundred of your closest friends bearing down on you, and a Hive Shredder waiting if you say no? I shared. I reached into him. Touched something deep. 

And what he offered back, it wasn't Light or Dark. It was cold. It was wrong. And I knew it would fill up whatever empty cracks in me the Light left behind. And… I chose to make it a part of me. To be half of his whole.

I chose to share my soul with a monster.

And the thing is… you can't just be part monster.
81505820.text_zh:
你得明白…我们没有人是想着宏伟的计划来到这儿的。没有一个人！有的只是…只是冲动，你懂吗？所以我们跟随着它，却步入了一个自我改造的世界。光能就在猛烈地攻击暗影。反复肆意地袭击！山脉像雨中的糖一样漂流入海。一个邪魔族王座世界被改造了。一时兴起！ 

我不是你所说的信徒，在猩红战争之后就不是了。在纷争海岸之后就不是了。在“只是因为我不是别人的一半，所以一辈子都不重要”之后就不是了。不过那…那让我又有了感觉。

然后我看到他——他身上遗留的东西——躺在那里。就这具尸体，死了也许有，哦，一百年了吧。这是我的骑士。我一看，就知道他是我的。就像第一次听到一首歌，它就已经深深地印在你的脑海里。就在那一刻，我觉得我身上有些…有些美好的东西死了。

还有二十二、凯马西和马赛，他们都在复活自己的搭档——邪魔族负光者，每一个都是。你会认为那不可能，但可以肯定的是，所有人都站在那里。埃伊、夸西特、哈彻，每个人都在寻找自己的目标。我身边到处都是邪魔族…我被埋在他们里面。而我认识的每一个机灵都在大喊，告诉我，“这是旅行者的计划！你有什么资格质疑它？” 

所以我想…也许他们是对的？我的意思是，我可以看到光能在我面前冲洗着整个世界。也许这就是邪魔族的某个转折点吧。知道你的造物主选择你来改造整个物种…哦，你也会做出错误的选择。

所以我分享了我的光能。谁又能不这么做呢？几百个你最亲密的朋友向你扑来，如果你拒绝，还有一个邪魔族粉碎者在等着你？我分享了。我向他伸出了手。触及到了某种深远的东西。 

而他所提供的回报，既非光明也非黑暗。它是冰冷的，是错误的。我知道它会填满我身上任何一道光能留下的裂缝。而…我选择让它成为我的一部分。成为他整体的一半。

我选择和怪物分享我的灵魂。

而问题在于…你不能只做一部分怪物。

81505823.name: Fynch II
81505823.text:
Oh no, no, no. Why, of all things… did you make me do this?

The Hive certainly weren't perfect—actually, let's not mince words; they were straight-up evil! But you? I gave you a part of me! I let you make me worse just so I could make you better! You were supposed to understand! You were the only one who ever could. Why wouldn't you? Yeah, so really, y'know, this is your fault, not mine!

I know. I know you don't want to be dead. I know that! You think I don't know that?!

I watched you shoot a Guardian. And her GHOST. Dead. All because I could hear you, in the back of my mind, needing me to bring you back. And I listened. I listened to the others… then to you… to everyone except myself. 

I didn't expect miracles, but… I expected something! 

Yes, you're dead now. And I can hear you—but I can't. Don't you get it? I just. Can't!

I'm not gonna be the triggerman anymore. I'm not gonna sacrifice humanity on your personal altar. You're not… you're not worth it. You're not…

Worthy.

And you never were… were you?

Why does Savathûn have the Light? I should've asked "why" a long time ago. None of us did at the time, but I should've. We both know this wasn't right.

Look, I've got no faith left in the Traveler, but I know it… it wouldn't give me a monster and say, "Make him a god." No, no, we both know this wasn't right. Was it pity? Optimism? 

Maybe… maybe it's just the obvious: I mean, Hive don't accept gifts; they take. Maybe the Traveler was tricked. The end of some long con. The Traveler isn't just some dumb orb ripe for grifting. Ghaul found that out the hard way.

There's gotta be more to it. I have to dig deeper. And if joining you damned me… well, hell sounds like a good place to start. I'll find out how she did it. And I don't care how much you try to change my mind: you're staying dead. You hear me?

You made me a monster, remember? You don't get to cry about it when I act like one.
81505823.text_zh:
哦，不不不。为什么，在所有的事情中…你偏让我做这个？

邪魔族并不完美——事实上，我们就不绕弯了；他们就是彻头彻尾的邪恶！但是你呢？我给了你我的一部分！我让你把我变糟只是为了让你更好！你应该明白的！你是唯一能明白的人。你为什么不呢？对，所以说真的，你懂的，这是你的错，不是我的！

我知道。我知道你不想死。我知道！你以为我不知道？！

我看见你射杀了一个守护者。还有她的机灵。死透了。都是因为我能听到你，在我的脑海深处，需要我去复活你。所以我照做了。我听了其他人的话…然后听你的话…听除了我自己以外所有人的话。 

我没有期待奇迹，但是…我期待着些什么！ 

是的，你现在已经死了。而我能听到你的声音——但我做不到。你不明白吗？我就是。做不到！

我不要再做杀手了。我不会在你的个人祭坛上牺牲人性。你不…你不值得我这样做。你不…

配。

你从来都不配…对吧？

为什么萨瓦图恩会有光能？我早就该问“为什么”了。当时我们没人知道，但我应该知道的。我们都知道这是不对的。

听着，我对旅行者已经没有信心了，但我知道它…它不会抛给我一个怪物然后说，“让他成为神。”不，不，我们都知道这是不对的。这是怜悯吗？乐观主义？ 

也许…也许这是显而易见的：我是说，邪魔族不接受馈赠；他们会夺取。也许是旅行者被骗了。漫长的骗局终结了。旅行者不只是一个可以欺骗的蠢球。盖欧费了一番功夫才发现这一点。

肯定还有别的原因。我得再深入挖掘一点。如果加入你们是对我的诅咒…好吧，地狱听起来是个不错的起点。我会弄清楚她是怎么做到的。而且我不在乎你有多想改变我的想法：你会一直保持死亡状态。你听到我说的了吗？

是你把我变成了怪物，记得吗？所以我干出怪物该干的事来，你就别为此哭泣。

81505822.name: Specter
81505822.text:
TYPE: PERSONAL INVESTIGATIVE REPORT
PARTIES: One [1] Ghost-type, designate Specter
ASSOCIATIONS: Light; Lucent Hive
//TRANSCRIPT FOLLOWS//

Post-Lumination Day 017. 10:23. Arrived on scene. Victim is a Thrall. No identity. Cause of death: fractured neck due to blunt force trauma. Traces of Light detected. Nabenki interviewed the primary suspect; Hive prefer talking to their own and don't respond to things—even things that bring them back from the dead.

Overheard confession. Suspect is Knight identified as Urukthalyn, victim's commander. Reported that when his Ghost detected Light within victim, Urukthalyn executed him for theft. Open and shut case.

PLD018. 13:44. Three more deaths fitting same pattern: internal artifacts of Light, victims summarily executed. But circumstances raise more questions. Thralls don't partner with Ghosts; should be unable to receive or carry Light. 

Nabenki tasked to investigate. Suspects an organized smuggling ring, potential Human or Fallen infiltration.

PLD018. 14:57. Encountered suspect Thrall; no identification, classified POI-7. Tests confirm traces of Light. Nabenki applied standard Hive interrogation techniques, extracted confession after extended session. POI-7 admitted to "stealing" Light, keeping it in urns. Also implicated a superior Acolyte. Doesn't add up.

PLD018. 19:12. Requested time alone with suspect to establish rapport. Nabenki hesitant; doesn't like being spoken to unbidden but acquiesces. POI-7 admitted to giving false confession to end "visceral" Hive interrogation. Claimed complete ignorance to the Light's origins in his system. When asked about unusual activity, reported that his symbiote feels sated without need for bloodshed or tithing.

PLD018. 19:33. Consulted Nabenki for context regarding tithing. Apparently, Hive function on a system of energetic kickbacks, paid up the ladder, ending with queen. Would've been useful to know earlier. Suspect this network may be impacted by introduction of Light. Nabenki confirmed Light exhibits a "negative pressure" within the system. May be pushing trace amounts back through it.

Have submitted theory to our commander for further investigation.

PLD019. 06:30. Partner acknowledged me this morning, established eye contact. Potential illness?

PLD019. 07:42. On my recommendation, POI-7 executed for perjury.
81505822.text_zh:
类型：个人调查报告
参与方：一 [1] 名机灵，代号幽灵
关联：光能；光明邪魔族
//转录如下//

后光明时代的第17天。10:23。到达现场。受害者是一名怨魂。没有身份。死因：由于钝器创伤导致颈部骨折。检测到光能的痕迹。纳本基审问了主要嫌疑人；邪魔族更喜欢和自己人交谈，对其他东西都不做反应——即使是能让他们起死回生的东西。

无意中听到了供词。嫌疑人是骑士，被确认为受害者的指挥官乌鲁克塔林。案情报告提到，当他的机灵探测到受害者体内的光能时，乌鲁克塔林以盗窃罪处决了他。这案子一目了然。

后光明时代的第18天。13:44。又有三起手法相同的死亡事件：体内有光能神器，受害者立即遭到处决。但案情也引出了更多的问题。怨魂并不与机灵搭档合作；应该无法接受或携带光能。 

纳本基受命进行调查。怀疑存在组织有序的走私团伙，可能有人类或堕落者的渗入。

后光明时代的第18天。14:57。遇到怨魂嫌犯；没有身份，被列为兴趣点-7号。经测试证实有光能的迹证。纳本基采用了标准邪魔族审讯技术，经过长时间的审讯获得了供词。兴趣点-7号承认“偷窃”光能，并将其保存在瓮中。案情还牵涉到一位高级仆从。不合情理。

后光明时代的第18天。19:12。要求与嫌犯独处以建立融洽关系。纳本基犹豫不决；不喜欢别人擅自和他讲话，但还是勉强同意了。兴趣点-7号承认为结束“伤及脏器”的邪魔族审讯而做了虚假供词。他声称完全不知道光能在他系统中的来源。当被问及不寻常行为时，他报告说他的共生体无需杀戮或什一税就感到了满足。

后光明时代的第18天。19:33。咨询了纳本基关于什一税的背景。显然，邪魔族的运作是以充满活力的回扣系统为基础的，逐级支付，到女王结束。如果早点知道就好了。怀疑该网络可能会因引入光能而受到影响。纳本基证实，光能在系统内呈现出一种“负压”。也许能倒推微量负压。

已将理论提交给我们的指挥官作进一步调查。

后光明时代的第19天。06:30。今早搭档注意到了我，和我有眼神交流。潜在病症？

后光明时代的第19天。07:42。在我的建议下，兴趣点-7号因伪证罪被处决。

81505809.name: Immaru
81505809.text:
The Light of the Wellspring spilled out below them. From the palace tower, Immaru watched the churn where it met the Darkness, new waves eroding an ancient shore. The flash of muzzle fire was visible from this perch, even if the combatants weren't.

He huffed and shuddered, trying to remember how to speak as he watched the Guardians' unprovoked assault into their Ascendant Plane. "No better than Scorn," he growled.

Savathûn turned from the honey-sweet music only she could hear and stroked her Ghost. "Ah, child. Loyal as you are, you still only see their actions, not the chains that drag them to inevitability. Just as Hive must test, Humans must control—and failing that, attack. You must not take it personally; attacking the unknown is their nature."

"We Ghosts ain't unknown!" Immaru pulled free of her affections. "We lived with 'em. Saved 'em. Now they're ripping through us! Damn ungrateful, if you ask me…"

"Surely you don't believe they're punishing you for disobedience?"

"Aren't they?" His voice was dark and hard, and he paused to re-center. "Everyone—Fallen, Vex, even Hive—every last one of 'em knows you don't shoot the medic. But nobody told these jokers apparently."
