Ahead, the stark angles of the Lunar Pyramid rise before her; red phantoms hang in the air and shimmer like specks of dust against its enormity. Raising her Ahamkara bone to her lips, Eris blows across its surface as if she were extinguishing a tiny candle. The world around her blurs and bends and then

she is elsewhere.

The heart of the Pyramid. A veiled statue towers over Eris, vaguely feminine in form, though she is not convinced of its apophenian silhouette. She raises her soulfire-shrouded Ahamkara bone again. Stasis encrusts its surface, much as it had years ago when she first harnessed such power. 

Eris turns to inspect the vast interior of the Pyramid. It is quiet, it is dead. Not unlike the one in Savathûn's throne world. Her eyes narrow; she clutches the Ahamkara bone in her hand again and

she is elsewhere.

A chamber. It is cavernous, it is dark. Strange, bisected statues of stratified minerals line the cathedral-like walls and culminate at the far end before a yawning opening that empties into perpetual nothingness. 

On the floor, a length of unidentifiable metal caked in centuries of dust catches her eye. A glaive. Eris lifts it into her hand. Striations of red illuminate on its surface and throb like a heartbeat. The glaive's power feels faint—distant—and yet, an ember of something terrible still burns within.

"Where are you?" Eris whispers into the air.

There is no reply.
254636484.text_zh:
尘土飞扬的洞穴地面伸出了冰影的几何产物，缕缕魂火在其中打着旋，割裂的邪魔族骑士和怨魂尸体被冻结在水晶之中。近期战斗遗留的碎石在埃里斯的战靴下嘎吱作响。前方，月球金字塔的尖角在她面前升起；红色的鬼灵悬挂在空中，在其映衬下像微尘一样闪烁着。埃里斯把她的阿罕卡拉遗骨举到嘴边，朝它的表面吹气，好似在吹熄一根小蜡烛。她周围的世界变得模糊扭曲，然后

她就到了别处。

金字塔的中心。埃里斯头顶上耸立着一尊戴着面纱的雕像，外形上来看有些女性化，虽然她根本不相信它那关联型错觉的轮廓。她再次举起她那魂火笼罩的阿罕卡拉遗骨，冰影裹在它的表面，就像多年前她第一次利用这种力量一样。 

埃里斯转身审视着金字塔广阔的内部。寂静冷清，了无生机。与萨瓦图恩的王座世界里没什么不同。她的眼睛眯了起来；她再次将阿罕卡拉遗骨握在手里，然后

她就到了别处。

一间屋子。既空洞，又灰暗。大教堂般的四壁上排列着奇特的、分成两半的分级矿物雕像，在房间远端的一处巨大开口处终结，通向一片永恒的虚无。 

地板上，一段无法辨认的金属引起了她的注意，几个世纪以来的灰尘厚厚地裹在上面。一把偃月。埃里斯把它举到手中。红色的条纹照亮了它的表面，像心跳一样跳动着。这把偃月的力量让人感觉微弱而遥远，然而某种可怕事物的余烬仍在其中燃烧。

“你在哪里？”埃里斯对着空气轻声说道。

无人应答。

2323544076.name: Hollow Denial
2323544076.subtitle: "Never forget what is taken from you."
2323544076.subtitle_zh: “永远不要忘记你被夺走了什么。”
2323544076.text:
Kethiks, the Yet-Proven, had spent three lunar orbits surveying the small village. He was not the first Captain to strike here, but while others had come for killing or labor, his clutch of Vandals came for something else.

A Lightbearer resided in the village—a demon who had killed many of his friends. A demon who had shattered the Captain whose place Kethiks had taken. It was Kethiks's duty to seek revenge, to hunt this demon, and clear the death debt. Those were the words House Devils had sent with Kethiks. 

But to Kethiks, this demon's life paid more than vengeance. Its life paid glory. The same glory Kethiks's father, Ykriis, claimed when he felled a Lightbearer in single combat, took its tiny machine and drank of its divine Ether. Soon that glory would be Kethiks's as well. Soon his position would be recognized for more than its circumstance.

Vandals crept on either side of Kethiks, maneuvering through tall grass with quiet anticipation. Where the grass died off to tilled soil and log walls, they paused, waiting for Kethiks's command. He would not launch flares to declare their strike. He would not give the Lightbearer time to plan.

As the rear-guard Dregs joined the rest of his raiding party, Kethiks ignited an Arc spear and raised it against the night. The signal: attack!

The raiders descended, expecting a paltry guard. They were soon met by stiff resistance. The Captain tore through to the heart of the village, hunting for the demon who commanded the defense. He spotted the demon in the midst of the fighting. Kethiks strode forward, seizing a defiant Human in his path with his lower arms and flung her through a burning wooden structure.

"DEMON!" he shrieked in Eliksni, brandishing his Arc spear.

Before he could advance, a young Human defiantly stepped between him and the demon and brandished a blade. Kethiks assessed the "warrior" and clicked his mandibles in laughter, easily knocking the boy's curved blade aside. The Captain taunted the youth with half-hearted thrusts that threw the small Human off balance. When he was finished toying with his prey, Kethiks drove the spear point through him.

Kethiks looked up from the pinned youth to the demon and snarled. His eyes met the demon's crackling own. The Captain raised his spear to charge—
2323544076.text_zh:
未证者凯奇克斯已经在月球轨道上绕了三圈来调查这座小村庄。他不是第一个袭击这里的队长，但当其他人为了杀戮或劳役来到这里时，他的那群暴徒另有所图。

村里住着一位负光者——一个杀死了他许多朋友的恶魔。一个摧毁了凯奇克斯所替代的队长的恶魔。凯奇克斯的职责就是复仇，猎杀这个恶魔，让它血债血偿。这是恶魔氏族托付凯奇克斯捎带的话。 

但对凯奇克斯来说，杀死这个恶魔所带来的不仅仅是复仇。还有荣耀。与凯奇克斯的父亲伊克瑞斯在单挑中击倒一位负光者，夺走它的小机器并喝下它那神圣乙太时所获得的荣耀一样。很快，凯奇克斯也将获得这种荣耀。很快他的地位就会得到认可，而不再仅仅是因为形势需要。

暴徒们在凯奇克斯的两侧匍匐前行，穿梭在高高的草丛中，满怀着悄无声息的期待。在草丛消失成耕土和木墙的地方，他们停了下来，等候着凯奇克斯的命令。他不会发射信号弹来宣告袭击。他不会给负光者时间去计划。

当后卫堕落者士兵加入他其余的突袭队伍时，凯奇克斯点燃了一支电弧长矛，对着黑夜举了起来。那就是信号：进攻！

突袭者们从草丛上下来，以为只会碰到某个微不足道的警卫。他们很快遭到了顽强的抵抗。队长冲进了村子的中心，搜寻着指挥防御的恶魔。他在战斗中发现了恶魔。凯奇克斯大步向前，途中用他的小臂抓住一个违抗的人类，把她扔进了一个燃烧着的木质构造中。

“恶魔！”他挥舞着他的电弧长矛，用埃里克斯尼族语尖声叫道。

他还没来得及上前，一个年轻的人类就毫无畏惧地走到他和恶魔之间，挥舞着一把刀刃。凯奇克斯打量了一下这位“勇士”，笑得上颚咔哒作响，轻而易举地把男孩的弯刀打翻在一边。这名队长用半心半意的突刺嘲弄这个年轻人，把小个子人类弄得失去平衡。当他玩弄完猎物后，凯奇克斯用矛尖刺穿了他。

凯奇克斯从被钉住的年轻人身上抬头看向恶魔，咆哮道。他的双眼与恶魔发狂的眼睛相遇。队长举起长矛冲锋——

2778013407.name: Firefright
2778013407.subtitle: What's the scariest part of a firefight? The whole damn thing.
2778013407.subtitle_zh: 激烈交火最骇人的部分是什么？整件事。
2778013407.text:
Siegfried's feet touch down on a metal grate ten fathoms deep into the Leviathan, where snaking tunnels split into many different directions. The room is large, empty, and dark. He cycles through the night vision and thermal imaging on his helm, then looks up to his fireteam.

He can see the shimmering Eliksni camouflage distort the shapes of his seven teammates as they descend the shaft above him on a carbon-weave line. He disables his own. In front of him sits the base of a robotic construct in the likeness of Calus. It is twice his height, and the bare mechanisms of its internal workings creak with age.

Four Cabal Legionaries, two Eliksni Splicers, and a Praxic Sunsinger drop in behind Siegfried and deactivate their cloaks. The Splicers get to work establishing a connection with the automaton while the Legionaries make a perimeter at their back. Siegfried stands with them.

The Warlock does not take their eyes from the automaton.

"Splice… formed." One of the Eliksni turns to the Warlock and nods. The Warlock steps forward—

"Thieves skulking through my Leviathan!" The automaton bellows with Calus's voice and forcibly bats away a Splicer with a metallic hand. They crash into the adjacent wall and crumple into unconsciousness. The second Splicer leaps back and takes cover behind a Legionary as the Praxic Warlock unleashes a volley of celestial fire into the construct's face. In response, a steely fist bursts through the fire-smoke and crushes the Warlock into the floor.

Siegfried turns toward the Legionaries and shouts, "Contact!"

The Cabal open up with slug rifles; munitions clang against the thick metal. The remaining Splicer aims for the construct's exposed machinery with their Arc pistol.

Siegfried rushes forward, sliding to meet the automaton head on. He ignites in Solar flame and shoulder charges the construct into the chamber wall. He rolls under a retaliating fist and grabs the automaton's chassis, wrestling to spin its back to his fireteam.

The Sunsinger gasps, alive again. They grab the unconscious Eliksni and take a position amid the Legionaries, shouting, "CONCENTRATE FIRE!"

With one swift motion, the Praxic Warlock combusts brilliantly with Solar Radiance that emboldens the firing line of Cabal shooters and fills the Splicer's heart with courage. Heated slugs puncture and the Arc pistol finds its mark, shorting out one of the automaton's exposed knees.

Slug rifles shred the construct's face as it crashes to the ground and frenetically crawls toward them, tearing metal from the floor with each scraping motion.

The Titan raises a hand, and in a burst of fiery might, summons a Devastator's maul. He brings the maul down into the automaton's back, demolishing it and sending molten shrapnel skidding across the floor.

Siegfried looks to the Sunsinger, then the rest of the fireteam. "Contact down… let's keep going."
2778013407.text_zh:
齐格菲的脚落在利维坦十英寻深处的金属格栅上，那里蜿蜒的隧道通往许多不同的方向。房间很大，空荡荡的，漆黑一片。他切换着头盔的夜视和热成像模式，然后抬头看向他的火力战队。

他可以看到闪闪发光的埃里克斯尼族伪装扭曲了他七名队友的影像，他们正沿着碳编织绳从他上方的竖井中下落。他关掉了自己的影像。他面前坐落着一个外形酷似卡鲁斯的机械构造基座。它的高度是他的两倍，裸露的内部机关因年久失修而吱吱作响。

四名卡巴尔军团士兵、两名埃里克斯尼族熔岩军团和一名英勇颂日落在齐格菲身后，解除了伪装。熔岩军团开始与自动机建立连接，军团士兵在其身后围成一圈。齐格菲和他们站在一起。

这名术士目不转睛地盯着自动机。

“切入…成功。”其中一名埃里克斯尼族转向术士点了点头。术士向前走去——

“窃贼竟敢在我的利维坦里鬼鬼祟祟！”自动机发出卡鲁斯的声音吼叫着，挥动一只金属手用力击退了一名熔岩军团。他撞上旁边的墙，陷入了昏迷。第二名熔岩军团向后跳，躲在一名军团士兵身后，英勇术士朝构造体的脸上射出一束星界之火。作为回应，一只钢铁般的拳头穿过火烟，将术士压在地板上。

齐格菲转身对军团士兵喊道，“敌袭！”

卡巴尔举起重击步枪射击，弹药打在厚金属上叮当作响。另一名熔岩军团则用电弧手枪瞄准了构造体毫无遮蔽的运转装置。

齐格菲向前冲去，滑动着与自动机迎面相遇。他点燃烈日火焰，用肩部充能将构造体撞向房间的墙壁。他翻滚着躲过一记反击的拳头，抓住了自动机的底架，拼命将它的背部扭对着他的火力战队。

颂日喘着粗气醒转过来。他抓住失去知觉的埃里克斯尼族，在军团士兵间就位，高喊道，“集中火力！”

凭借敏捷的身手，英勇术士在烈日焕光下燃烧得非常灿烂，这让前沿阵地的卡巴尔射手斗志昂扬，也让熔岩军团满怀信心。加热的弹头打穿了护甲，电弧手枪也击中了目标，致使自动机外露的一个膝盖发生短路。

重击步枪手们完全毁坏了构造体的脸，它跌倒在地上，疯狂地朝他们爬去，每次刮擦都能把金属从地板上撕扯下来。

泰坦举起一只手，在一股炽热的力量中，使出了毁灭者锻锤。他拿起锻锤砸向自动机背部，将其摧毁，熔化的炮弹碎片散落一地。

齐格菲望了颂日一眼，然后又看了看火力战队的其他人。“目标击倒…我们继续前进。”

1478986057.name: Without Remorse
1478986057.subtitle: "No regrets."
1478986057.text:
How could I possibly be his Ghost—after all that Uldren has done? It's a question I've been asked before.

Most Ghosts don't know who their Guardians used to be. That's… obviously not true in my case. My Guardian was laid to rest under a shroud in the Dreaming City. Even if I didn't recognize his face, I would have put two and two together.

Honestly, sometimes I even wonder if he figured it out before he spoke to Savathûn. If what she showed him just confirmed what he already suspected.

The thing is, I know a lot more about Crow than Savathûn ever did. I know the smirk on his face when he pulls off something impossible. The way he flips his knife before throwing it. Even the way he averts his eyes when someone praises him. 

And sometimes, I wonder if Uldren shared any of his traits, his habits. Maybe. It's impossible for me to say for certain. But it doesn't really matter.

Because I know that my Guardian only takes risks when they are necessary, not for the thrill of it. He celebrates others' victories, not their losses. Everything he does is for someone else's benefit. He is humble. He is kind.

That is who he really is. And it's up to me to remind him. Because Crow is my Guardian.

Not Uldren.
1478986057.text_zh:
在欧顿的所作所为之后——我怎么还能当他的机灵？以前也有人问过我这个问题。

大多数机灵都不知道他们的守护者曾经是谁。对我来说…显然不是这样。我的守护者曾在幽梦之城里的裹尸布下长眠。即使我当时没认出他的脸，我也能推断出来。

说实话，有时候我甚至怀疑他在和萨瓦图恩谈话之前想明白了没有。她展示给他看的是不是恰好证实了他的怀疑。

问题是，我对乌鸦的了解要比萨瓦图恩多得多。我知道当他做到难以达成的事情时脸上会露出的笑意，他投掷飞刀前轻抛的动作。我甚至知道有人称赞他时，他逃避视线的模样。 

有时，我在想欧顿是不是也有他的一些特点和习惯。也许吧。我说不准。但这并不重要。

因为我知道我的守护者只会在必要时冒险，而不是为了寻求刺激。他会为别人的胜利而欢欣鼓舞，而不是对他人的失败幸灾乐祸。他所做的一切都是在为别人着想。他谦逊温和，天真善良。

这才是真正的他，这一点由我来提醒他。因为乌鸦是我的守护者。

不是欧顿。

3105930175.name: Chain of Command
3105930175.subtitle: Bound by duty.
3105930175.text:
Zavala stared out the H.E.L.M.'s viewport. The Leviathan loomed in the distance, a blight among the stars. The commander leaned on the War Table as blue light flickered from the holo projector; images of Caiatl and Saladin appeared to commence their scheduled briefing.

"We continue to encounter heavy resistance," Zavala said without preamble. He could hear the fatigue in his voice.

"As we expected," Caiatl grumbled. "My father's soldiers will fight for him until their last breath."

"And when they fall, more will take their place," Saladin added.

Zavala sighed and lifted his eyes to glare at the Leviathan. "He commands them to die for nothing. How can he call himself a leader—"

The words caught in his throat, and he choked them back down. Caiatl and Saladin remained silent, their projected expressions inscrutable.

"Leadership is a burden," Caiatl declared, "to those who understand its true value."

"Indeed, it is," said Zavala.

He turned to face the holo projector and straightened his back. "Vanguard operations will continue aboard the Leviathan. We'll keep you updated with our progress."

Both Caiatl and Saladin nodded as their holo projections faded away. Alone on the bridge, Zavala shifted his gaze back to the viewport, acutely aware of the weight of his armor.
3105930175.text_zh:
萨瓦拉凝视着应急后勤行动中心的观察窗。利维坦在远处若隐若现，群星之中的一片荒芜。这位指挥官靠在战争圆桌上，全息投影仪闪起了蓝光；查厄托和萨拉丁的影像随之显现：汇报时间已到。

“我们不断遭到强烈抵抗，”萨瓦拉开门见山地说。他能听出他声音中的疲惫。

“不出我们所料，”查厄托抱怨道。“我父亲的士兵会为他战斗到最后一刻。”

“他们倒下时，会有更多的人取代他们的位置，”萨拉丁补充道。

萨瓦拉叹了口气，抬起眼睛怒视着利维坦。“他下令让他们白白牺牲。他怎么能自称为领袖——”

这些话如鲠在喉，他又咽了回去。查厄托和萨拉丁仍然默不作声，他们投射出的表情让人捉摸不透。

“对于那些理解它真正价值的人来说，”查厄托郑重其事地指出，“领导力就是一种负担。”

“的确如此，”萨瓦拉说道。

他转过身来面对全息投影仪，挺直了背。“先锋行动将在利维坦上继续进行。我们会随时通报最新进展。”

查厄托和萨拉丁都点了点头，他们的全息投影逐渐消失。萨瓦拉独自一人站在舰桥上，他把目光移回观察窗，清楚地感受到了自己盔甲的重量。

1856262127.name: Something New
1856262127.subtitle: "It's new to me." —Banshee-44
1856262127.text:
"Do you ever tire of the work?" asks Eva Levante.

Banshee-44 looks up from his workbench. Eva often crosses in front of his kiosk on her walks to and from the Bazaar, striking up conversations with him in passing when she does. He briefly wonders if they've had this particular talk before; he wouldn't put it past her to simply let it play out to spare him the embarrassment of not remembering it.

"Can't say that I do," Banshee replies cordially. "Memory's not so great. Every gun feels like a new one."

Eva nods as she takes a sip of tea from the mug in her hand. "It's just that I see Guardians deliver parts to you all the time, and you seem to construct the same gun for them repeatedly. Are they not satisfied with what you provide?"

Banshee chuckles. "Maybe." He leans on the bench, looking at the various weapon components strewn about his shop. "It's a bit like Solstice, now that I think about it."

That seems to pique Eva's interest. "Oh?" she asks, eyebrow raised.

"Guardians bring me scraps, pieces of guns they dismantled." Banshee explains. "And I turn them into something new. Not always what the Guardian was hoping for, but they hold onto that hope and keep bringing me parts."

Eva smiles. "Same interaction, different outcome."

"Yeah. I guess you could say that."

"How wonderful," Eva says cheerfully. She raises his cup to him and walks back to the Courtyard.

"Definitely had that talk before," Banshee says to himself.

But he never tires of it.
1856262127.text_zh:
“你曾厌倦过这份工作吗？”伊娃·莱万特问道。

班西-44从工作台上抬起头来。伊娃在往返集市的路上经常从他的岗亭前经过，顺便与他攀谈。他一时间不禁好奇起来，他们之前是否有过这样的谈话；为了让他不会因为记不起来感到尴尬，她问得很自然，对此他早就习以为常了。

“没那样的事，”班西诚恳地答道。“我记性不好。每把枪感觉都像是新的一样。”

伊娃点点头，拿起手中的杯子咂了一口茶。“我看到守护者总是会给你零部件，而你似乎在反复为他们制造同样的枪支。他们是对你提供的东西不满意吗？”

班西笑着说。“也许吧。”他斜靠在长凳上，看着散落在他店里的各种武器部件。“我现在觉得，这有点像至日。”

这似乎激起了伊娃的兴趣。“哦？”她扬起眉毛问道。

“守护者们给我送来废料和他们拆卸的枪支碎片。”班西解释道。“而我把它们变成了新东西。虽然并不总是守护者所期望的，但他们依然坚守着这份期望，不断给我送来零件。”

伊娃笑着说道。“同样都是送东西，结果却不同。”

“没错。是可以这么说。”

“多好啊，”伊娃高兴地说道。她向他举杯，走回了庭院。

“以前肯定有过这样的谈话，”班西自言自语道。

但他从不厌倦。

2419786605.name: I. Temperament
2419786605.text:
Crow drops a wet canteen at Eris Morn's feet. "Water."

"You made your return quickly." Eris crouches, hunched over bundled splits of pine arranged atop a thick log and resin-rubbed moss. She strikes a well-worn flint with her knife, and flame ignites. 

"You're not hard to spot at night." Crow averts his gaze from Eris's sideways glare and looks up to the haunting glow of the Dark Shard of the Traveler. Shivers convulse down his vertebrae, and his eyes drop to the freshly popping wood.

Eris breaks the silence. "Why did you volunteer for the severance operation? For… most operations?"

"To make a difference where others can't. Same as you." 

She shakes her head. "No," Eris mumbles.

Crow watches her deftly coax the fire, considering the answer he'd given. He looks up to the distant tree line and changes the subject. "There are still a good number of Hive here."

"But no Nightmares," Eris remarks.

"Is that why you brought me here? This… isn't a place I want to revisit." Crow steps back from the growing flames.

When Eris doesn't respond, he asks his real question:

"Why did I fail?"

"You didn't fail. Our strategy was flawed." Eris stands, stowing flint and blade, then steps in front of him to meet his gaze. "We will attempt the severance again, soon."

"Yeah," Crow replies in a clipped tone. Eris tilts her head, and he can see the green orbs narrow beneath her blindfold.

She points to the ragged, mountainous shard twisting in twilight roil. "Even that toxic piece, separate from the Traveler's purity, can be wielded for good."

The fire roars. He kneels to break her stare and warms his hands. "I know what it can do. I used it—"

"When the Red War left Guardians Lightless, there were some who reclaimed their callings here. They re-forged their bond to the Traveler through a scar. A lingering trauma," she continues.

Eris sits beside Crow and drinks from her canteen. Crow braces for her to continue, but she does not. The bundle of burning kindling collapses into a heap of cinders. Flames spit between the gaps and ash drifts on heated air.

"I'll get more wood," Crow says, hastening to step out of the fire's glow.

"Crow. Small fires like this kept me alive in the Hellmouth. I did not have the luxury of more wood." Eris grips a piece of rusty rebar taken from the Sludge and thrusts it into the sputtering fire. She stirs the cindering wood, opening new gaps and concentrating the larger pieces over a pile of glowing kindling. The flame surges, and heat intensifies. "During these long nights, we must make use of what is available to us."

She knows he understands her but hasn't accepted the lesson.

She hands him the bar, shows him how to maintain the fire's heat, how to find worth in remnants. How to rebuild from ash.

The pair converse as they take turns keeping the fire alive long into the night. The warmth soothes, their shoulders lighten, and Crow pulls back his hood.

When the fire finally dies, Eris gestures to the embers. "Now, you can fetch some wood." 

Crow smiles and gets to his feet. "Eris… did you ever try to get your Light back?"

"The past is not for dwelling."

Crow nods and sticks out his hand. She looks at it inquisitively.

"Come on."

Eris stands next to Crow; he clasps her palm and ignites a Golden Gun between their hands. Solar flame dances across Eris's fingers. Crow guides her arm and lifts the gun to the sky. He inhales sharply and howls before cracking a shot through the clouds.

"You're up, Hunter."

Eris depresses the trigger, slowly, doubtful that it would fire. A second Solar streak pierces the atmosphere. Crow laughs. They send round after round skyward, howling pent tension into the night until finally, even Eris finds herself smiling.
2419786605.text_zh:
乌鸦把一个湿漉漉的水壶扔到了埃里斯·摩恩的脚边。“水。”

“你回来得很快。”埃里斯蹲着，在捆扎的松枝前弓着身子，松枝下是一根粗大的圆木和涂了树脂的青苔。她用刀刃敲击一块磨损的燧石，点燃了火焰。 

“晚上要发现你不难。”乌鸦把目光从埃里斯的侧视上移开，抬头看向旅行者的黑暗碎片萦绕的光芒。他的脊背一阵颤栗，目光落在刚刚爆裂开的木头上。

埃里斯打破了沉默。“你为什么自愿参加断舍行动？参加…大多数行动？”

“为了在别人做不到的地方有所作为。和你一样。” 

她摇了摇头。“不，”埃里斯嘟哝道。

乌鸦看着她熟练地生着火，思考着自己给出的答案。他抬头望向远处的林木线，转移了话题。“这里还有很多邪魔族。”

“但是没有梦魇。”埃里斯评论道。

“这就是你带我来这儿的原因吗？这…不是我想旧地重游的地方。”乌鸦后退一步，远离越燃越旺的火焰。

看到埃里斯没有回应，他问出了心中真正的疑问：

“我为什么会失败？”

“你没失败。是我们的战略有缺陷。”埃里斯站了起来，收起燧石和刀片，然后走到他面前，与他的目光对视。“不久后，我们就会再次尝试断舍。”

“好。”乌鸦用一种简洁的语气回答道。埃里斯歪着头，乌鸦可以看到她眼罩下绿色的眼球眯了起来。

她指了指扭曲在翻涌的暮色中参差不齐、巨大如山的碎片。“即便是那块有毒的碎片，与旅行者的纯洁分离开来，也可以用来行善。”

火焰在熊熊燃烧。他跪下来打断她的凝视，暖了暖手。“我知道它能做什么。我用过它——”

“当猩红战争让守护者失去光能时，有些守护者在这里重新找回了他们的使命感。他们通过一道伤疤重新与旅行者建立了联系。一道挥之不去的创伤，”她继续说道。

埃里斯在乌鸦身旁坐下，喝着水壶里的水。乌鸦等着她继续说完，但她没有。那捆燃烧的木柴倒塌成一堆焦炭。火焰在缝隙间爆出火花，灰烬在热风中飘荡。

“我再去拿些木头，”乌鸦说着，匆忙想要走出火光。

“乌鸦。正是像这样微弱的火焰让我在地狱深渊活了下来。我没有更多的木材可用。”埃里斯抓住一根从泥淖地取出的生锈钢筋，把它戳进噼啪作响的火焰中。她搅动着烧焦的木头，翻开新的缝隙，把较大的木头集中在一堆燃烧的引火木上。火舌涌动，热量加剧。“在这些漫漫长夜中，我们必须充分利用现有资源。”

她知道他能理解她，但还没有听取教训。

她把钢筋递给他，教他如何保持火的热度，如何在残余中找到价值。如何从灰烬中重建。

他们一边交谈，一边轮流让火焰保持燃烧直到深夜。温暖让人舒缓下来，他们的肩膀也轻松了，乌鸦拉下了他的兜帽。

火焰最终熄灭时，埃里斯指了指灰烬。“现在，你可以再去拿些木材来。” 

乌鸦笑着站了起来。“埃里斯......你有没有想过要回你的光能？”

“人不应沉溺于过去。”

乌鸦点点头，伸出手来。她好奇地看着。

“来吧。”

埃里斯在乌鸦身旁站起来；他抓住她的手掌，在他们的手中点燃了黄金枪。烈日之焰在埃里斯的手指上跃动。乌鸦指引着她的胳膊把枪举向天空。他猛地吸了一口气，大声叫喊起来，然后朝云层开了一枪。

“该你了，猎人。”

埃里斯慢慢地扣了扳机，怀疑它是否能开火。第二道烈日光亮穿透了大气层。乌鸦笑了。他们一发接一发地朝天空发射，呐喊出压抑的情绪直至黑夜，最后，连埃里斯也发现自己笑了。

2419786606.name: II. Death and Desertion
2419786606.text:
"How many, Taurun?" Caiatl asks wearily.

An air of palpable tension permeates the room. In the time since the Imperial fleet had formed a blockade around the Leviathan, three separate frigates had defected to Calus's side. A fourth has just followed suit. 

Caiatl began this campaign with fire in her heart. Now, she feels only cold and tired.

"A total of 250 soldiers, Empress," Taurun answers.

"We must strike!" Ca'aurg shouts suddenly, slamming his fist on the table. "Anything less will be seen as a sign of weakness!"

A clamor ripples through the rest of Caiatl's advisors. Only Valus Forge remains silent.

"Inaction is anathema," says Tha'arec. "Our warriors long for the glory of battle, not the dormancy of a blockade."

"Even if it means fighting for Calus," sneers Ca'aurg. He spits the name as if it were made of bile.

A bitter fury builds in Caiatl toward her father. He had ushered in an era of decadence that left the Cabal military dull and complacent; she had sought to be a different kind of leader. But her people remain adrift—this time, among the stars. Perhaps her defectors prefer the pleasure of certain death over the agony of uncertain survival. Or perhaps, she is merely the next in line to lead the empire to ruin.

"The Leviathan reappeared with no warning," Caiatl declares. "We do not know what else lurks beyond our sight. Our blockade may soon see more battle than we bargained for. Until then, we hold the line."

She speaks in a tone that brooks no argument. Her advisors leave the room, wisely keeping any further misgivings to themselves. Saladin nods to her, as if to say he and he alone agrees with her decision.

Caiatl can only wonder if she agrees with it herself.
2419786606.text_zh:
“有多少，陶伦？”查厄托疲倦地问道。

房间里弥漫着显而易见的紧张气氛。自从帝国舰队封锁利维坦以来，已经有三艘独立的护卫舰叛逃到了卡鲁斯一方。第四艘刚刚步了它们的后尘。 

查厄托怀着满腔怒火发动了这场战役。如今，她只觉得又冷又累。

“总共250名士兵，女帝，”陶伦回答道。

“我们必须出击！”卡奥尔格突然喊道，拳头重重地砸在桌子上。“其他行动都会被视作软弱的表现！”

查厄托的其他顾问接二连三地喧嚷起来。只有军政官弗吉保持着沉默。

“无所作为是一种耻辱，”塔阿克说道。“我们的战士渴望战斗的荣耀，而不是封锁的蛰伏。”

“即使这意味着为卡鲁斯而战。”卡奥尔格讥讽道。他吐出这个名字，就好像它是用胆汁做的。

查厄托心中对她的父亲燃起一股激烈的怒火。他开创了一个颓废的时代，让卡巴尔的军队变得愚笨而自满；她曾寻求成为一个不一样的领袖。但她的族人依然漂泊不定——这一次是在群星之中。也许她的叛兵们更喜欢注定死亡的快感，而非渺茫生存的痛苦。又或许，她只不过是下一个带领帝国走向毁灭的人。

“利维坦毫无征兆地再次出现，”查厄托大声说道。“我们不知道在我们的视线之外还潜藏着什么危险。我们的封锁可能很快就会遭遇超出预料的战斗。在那之前，我们要坚守阵地。”

她说话的语气不容争辩。她的顾问们离开了房间，明智地将更多的疑虑藏在心里。萨拉丁向她点了点头，似乎在说，他，且只有他，同意她的决定。

查厄托不禁想知道，她自己是否同意这个决定。

2419786607.name: III. Memento
2419786607.text:
It's quiet in Zavala's office, save for the sound of clicking as the tiny steel pendulums on his desk swing back and forth, hitting against each other. Rahool once told him that they were a "Newton's Cradle"; a pre-Golden Age relic named for one of humanity's greatest scientific minds. The trinket is all that remains of a life's work lost to time, consumed by the Collapse and the ensuing Dark Age.

Like so many other things.

As he stands at the window, brooding in shame and guilt as he silently contemplates the Traveler, Zavala hears a knock on his door.

"Come in," he calls over his shoulder.

A moment later, Amanda Holliday steps into the room. Dark circles frame her eyes, and her shoulders slump with a weight unseen. No Nightmare hovers behind her, hounding her every step, but she seems haunted, nonetheless. Zavala is certain that, given his own ordeals, he must look much the same.

"Hey," Amanda says quietly as she crosses over to his desk. She leans against it and joins him looking out over the City.

They stand in silence for a long time and watch a small fleet of civilian ships weave its way between the buildings. The clicking of pendulums marks the time as it drifts past them.

"The Last City," Amanda murmurs. "Wish my folks had lived to see it."

"As do I," Zavala solemnly replies.

"You would've liked them," Amanda says with a sad smile. "As stubborn as they were kind. They gave everything to make sure I reached the City. Bravest people I've ever known."

"Devotion inspires bravery," Zavala says, almost absently. He turns from the window and glances at a low shelf, where a cracked white mask is displayed under glass. "Bravery inspires sacrifice. And sacrifice…" his voice quavers as it trails off.

"…is worth it for the ones we love," says Amanda. "My parents didn't have the Light. But they had me."

She meets his eyes, her own filled with a light all their own. "We can't all live forever. But being remembered? That's the next best thing."

Amanda laughs and sniffles at the same time. "Didn't mean to talk your ear off. Sorry about that."

"Don't be," Zavala replies with a small smile and a sigh of sadness. "I just wish I could return the favor."

He moves from the window and leans on the desk next to her, gazing out at the Traveler and the Last City as they settle into a comfortable silence. The pendulums on his desk continue to click and clack, the echo of a life lived long, long ago.
2419786607.text_zh:
萨瓦拉的办公室很安静，除了他桌上小小的钢质摆锤来回摆动、互相撞击时发出的咔哒声。拉乎尔曾告诉他那叫“牛顿摆”；这是一种黄金时代前的圣物，以人类最伟大的科学家之一命名。在大崩溃和随后黑暗时代的吞噬下，这件小饰品是一件在时间长河中所剩无几的毕生心血结晶。

就和很多其他事物一样。

他站在窗前，在羞愧和内疚中沉思。正当他默默地凝视着旅行者时，萨瓦拉听到了敲门声。

“进来，”他头也不回地喊道。

过了一会儿，阿曼达·霍利迪走进房间。黑眼圈遮住了她的眼睛，肩膀因看不见的重担而耷拉着。没有梦魇在她身后徘徊，纠缠她的每一个脚步，但她似乎还是满脸愁容。萨瓦拉确信，考虑到他所经历的磨难，他的样子看上去一定也差不多。

“嘿，”阿曼达走到他的办公桌前轻声说。她靠在上面，和他一起眺望着圣城。

他们默默地站了很长时间，看着一小队民用飞船在建筑物之间穿梭。摆锤的咔嗒声标志着时间从它们身边流逝而过。

“圣城，”阿曼达喃喃说道。“真希望我的家人能活着看到它。”

“我也希望如此，”萨瓦拉郑重地回答道。

“你会喜欢他们的，”阿曼达带着悲伤的微笑说道。“他们既善良又固执。他们竭尽全力确保我抵达圣城。是我所认识的最勇敢的人。”

“忠诚唤起无畏，”萨瓦拉心不在焉地说道。他从窗口转过身，瞥了眼一个低矮的架子，玻璃下面陈列着一个破裂的白色面具。“无畏激发牺牲。牺牲…”他的声音颤抖着，逐渐减弱。

“对我们所爱的人来说…是值得的。”阿曼达说道。“我父母没有光能。但他们有我。”

她与他的目光相遇，她的眼中充满了光芒。“我们不可能都永远活着。但是被铭记？已经是退而求其次了。”

阿曼达一边笑一边抽噎起来。“我不是故意要跟你唠叨个没完。很抱歉。”

“没事，”萨瓦拉微笑着回答，悲伤地叹了口气。“我只是希望我能报答你。”

他从窗前走出来，在她身旁倚靠在桌子上，凝视着外面的旅行者和圣城，他们陷入了舒适的沉默。他桌子上的摆锤继续咔哒咔哒地响着，这是一种很久很久以前生活的回响。

2419786600.name: IV. To Forgive or Forget
2419786600.text:
"Niik tells me you have a question in need of an answer," Mithrax begins. "Please, sit."

Amanda nods as she pulls up a folding chair next to the fire. She hadn't been back to the Eliksni Quarter since the Vex invasion. The light from the flames casts flickering shadows across the building's cracked concrete and exposed rebar.

"Yeah," Amanda says quietly, "I, uh… it's about Saint. Sort of."

She takes a deep breath before continuing. "Everyone in the Last City knows the stories. Hell, we used to call him 'Kellbreaker.' And Cr—" she stammers, avoiding the name. "I've heard what your people used to call him too."

Mithrax hums a gruff assent as he settles into his own chair. Amanda wrings her hands together.

"How did you all forgive him?" Her voice sounds small, but her words pierce the cool night air.

"Not all of us did," Mithrax replies solemnly. "To this day, there are some in House Light who avoid him. Those who lost loved ones to his rage. Though he would give his life to protect them, nothing he can do will ever erase their pain."

"So, they'll just… go on hating him? Forever?"

Mithrax exhales deeply into his rebreather. "One cannot choose who forgives them and who does not," he answers. "That is the decision of those who were wronged. A choice each must make for themselves."

Amanda nods to herself. "Was afraid you'd say something like that," she remarks sadly.

As she gets up to leave, she turns to Mithrax one last time.

"What made you forgive Saint?"

The Kell of Light leans back in his chair and stares into the fire like he is looking for something amid the ashes.

"Because," he says quietly, "I want to be forgiven too."
2419786600.text_zh:
“妮可告诉我，你有个问题要问我，”米瑟拉克斯开口道。“请坐。”

阿曼达点点头，拉过一张折叠椅来坐在火堆旁。自Vex入侵以来，她还没有回过埃里克斯尼居住区。火焰的光线在建筑开裂的混凝土和裸露的钢筋上投下了闪烁的影子。

“是的，”阿曼达平静地说道，“我，呃…是和圣人有关的，算是吧。”

她继续说话之前深吸了一口气。“圣城里每个人都知道这些故事。见鬼，我们曾经叫他‘凯尔终结者'。还有圣——”她结结巴巴地避开了这个名字。“我也听过你们的人曾叫他什么。”

米瑟拉克斯在自己的椅子上坐下，低沉地哼了一声以示同意。阿曼达攥紧了双手。

“你们都是怎么原谅他的？”她的声音听起来很小，但她的话穿透了夜晚凉爽的空气。

“并不是所有人，”米瑟拉克斯严肃地回答道。“直到今天，光能氏族的一些人还对他避而不谈。那些因他的愤怒而失去至爱的人。尽管他愿意献出自己的生命来保护他们，但他无论做什么都无法抹去他们的痛苦。”

“那么，他们会继续恨他吗？永远恨下去？”

米瑟拉克斯对着他的呼吸净化器深深地呼气。“一个人无法选择谁会原谅他们，谁不原谅他们，”他答道。“这是那些深受委屈的人做出的决定。一个每个人必须自己做出的选择。”

阿曼达暗自点头。“我就怕你会说这种话，”她伤心地说道。

她起身准备离开，最后一次转向米瑟拉克斯。

“那你是怎么原谅圣人的？”

光能凯尔靠在他的椅子上，凝视着火焰，好像要在灰烬中寻找些什么。

“因为，”他平静地说，“我也想得到宽恕。”

2419786601.name: V. Regrets
2419786601.text:
"Your regrets will follow you, Empress."

The words grate on Caiatl like sand beneath her armor. The Vanguard could keep their wretched Hive witchcraft; she had sworn to defeat the Nightmare of Ghaul in single combat and cremate his memory on the pyre of victory.

That choice had become yet another regret.

A gravelly voice cuts across the room. "You called for me?"

Caiatl turns to see Saladin Forge step onto the bridge of her flagship. Her honor guard salutes him and steps aside, making way for his approach as she greets him with a nod.

"What are your thoughts on Eris Morn?" Caiatl asks him.

Saladin raises an eyebrow. "She's endured horrors I can scarcely imagine. And she survived. She clawed her way out of that dark pit and back to the Tower."

"And what do you think about her use of Hive sorcery?" Caiatl seethes.

"Many initially distrusted her for it. But were it not for her… expertise, the Last City would have fallen to the Hive long ago," Saladin replies.

"That justifies consorting with such foul power?"

At first, Saladin says nothing. Instead, he turns his eyes to the viewport; to the Cabal fleet, arrayed in a blockade surrounding the Leviathan. 

"None opposed allying with your empire more than I did." His voice is measured, almost introspective. "I hated the Cabal. Now, I serve on your War Council."

His eyes meet hers once again. "Your soldiers wield the same weapons that slaughtered Guardians in the Red War. But that does not make you my enemy. Nor does Hive magic make Eris yours."

Caiatl glances at her honor guard. When Saladin first joined her War Council, her soldiers regarded him with equal parts suspicion and contempt. Now they show him the deference and respect befitting the title of Valus. Ghaul would have never condoned it.

But she is not Ghaul. And that is something she does not regret.

"Open a channel to the H.E.L.M.," she orders. "I have matters to discuss with the Vanguard."
2419786601.text_zh:
“你的悔意会跟着你，女帝。”

这些话就像盔甲下的沙砾一样刺痛着查厄托。让先锋留着那可恶的邪魔族巫术吧；她曾发誓要在单挑中击败盖欧的梦魇，在胜利的柴堆上火化他的记忆。

那个选择已经成为了又一次的悔意。

一个沙哑的声音穿过房间。“你叫我？”

查厄托转过身，看见萨拉丁·弗吉走上了她的旗舰舰桥。她的荣耀卫兵向他行了个礼并走到一边，让出一条路让他走近，她则向他点头致意。

“你对埃里斯·摩恩有什么看法？”查厄托问他。

萨拉丁扬起眉毛。“她经历了我几乎无法想象的恐惧，然后活了下来。她从黑暗的深渊里爬了出来，回到了高塔。”

“那你对她使用邪魔族魔法有什么看法？”查厄托强压着怒火。

“许多人一开始因为这个而不信任她。但如果不是她的…专长，圣城恐怕早就落入邪魔族之手了，”萨拉丁回答道。

“那就可以与这种邪恶的力量为伍了？”

起初，萨拉丁什么也没说。相反，他把视线转向观察窗；转向在利维坦周围列队封锁的卡巴尔舰队。 

“没有人比我更反对与你的帝国结盟。”他的声音很有分寸，近乎是在自省。“我恨过卡巴尔。现在，我却在你们的战争委员会任职。”

他们的目光再次相遇。“你的士兵使用的武器和在猩红战争中屠杀守护者的一样。但这并不意味着你就是我的敌人。邪魔族的魔法也不该让埃里斯成为你的仇敌。”

查厄托看了一眼荣耀卫兵。萨拉丁一开始加入她的战争委员会时，她的士兵们对他既怀疑又蔑视。如今他们对他表现出与军政官的头衔相称的遵从和敬重。换作盖欧绝不会宽恕这种行为。

但她不是盖欧，而她对此没有悔意。

“连接应急后勤行动中心的频道，”她命令道。“我有事情要和先锋商量。”

2419786602.name: VI. Propaganda
2419786602.text:
//RECORDED TRANSMITION VIA: HDN-SPLICE-332410205//
//SIGNAL ORIGIN: UNKNOWN//
//SIGNAL TERMINUS: WIDEBAND_OPEN_CHANNEL//
//FROM THE AUSPICE OF CALUS, DEPOSED CABAL EMPEROR//

My loyal subjects. The Guardians believe they have defeated your glorious emperor. How foolish. 

They look at the bodies left in their wake and assume victory, at the blood and oil that runs from the battlefields they have ravaged and assume the territory conquered. They are like the old Cabal, sweeping over planets with no mind to the subjects that resist them. 

But I am not so cruel. The worlds I brought into our fold were showered in riches, given everything for their service as Cabal… as you are now. As you will be each time you serve me. 

Some of you were born here. You are young, blessed by my hand with a life of celebrated battle and luxurious feasting. You fight with the voracity of veteran gladiators. You fight for your home—our home. I swell to call you my children.

Others came to me from my traitorous daughter, who calls herself empress even while I still draw breath. Such arrogance. Such disrespect. You've seen her tuskless plans fail Torobatl. You've watched her cast aside Cabal tradition to bow to the City and their Light. She fights alongside the very soldiers who slaughter your brethren, while I bend them to my will. Who is the true leader? The answer is clear. If only she had followed me as you do.

Finally. Exalted most of all, you elite few who have stood with their emperor from the beginning, who grew fat with strength in exile: we are blood. As you have shed for me, I will shed for you. My flesh, my riches, my goblets of royal wine. They are yours. You are honored above all, and when our new Cabal stands before eternity, you will be among the first.

I have heard the rumors whispered between you, my subjects. Rumors fed to you by our enemies. Your hope that I have not been vanquished is well placed, for I am so very much alive. You fear that we are defeated, but nothing could be further from the truth.

You wonder if I am a spirit, if I have become something beyond Cabal, if I have ascended like Acrius did when he cradled the sun in his grasp. Allow me to soothe your curiosity: yes, I have become all you have imagined, and so much more.

The Guardians believe they hold victory, but soon, they will see the truth they have ignored with such determination: this road is long, but it only has one end. They served to set my plans solidly in the foundations of the universe. Their petty attacks, while tragic in their costs to my dear crew, cannot halt our purpose.

So, my soldiers… I leave you this task: hold the Leviathan. Show no quarter to those who would walk the halls of your home as invaders. It is your final task before you may be uplifted to sit beside me at the end.

I do not promise that every Cabal standing on the Leviathan will survive this journey, but under my loving watch, you will live and die in nothing less than greatness. What more can a warrior desire but an exciting life and a good death? Have I not given you both?


-From the mouth of Amsot, High Scribe to the unbound emperor, Calus, who none can contain:
Rejoice! Praise Calus, who ascends. For he keeps you in his mind, and there you will never die.
2419786602.text_zh:
//录音通讯渠道：HDN-切入-332410205//
//信号来源：未知//
//信号终端：宽频_开放_频道//
//发件人：被废黜的卡巴尔大帝，卡鲁斯的指引//

我忠诚的臣民们。守护者认为他们已经击败了你们无上光荣的大帝。多么愚蠢啊。 

他们看着身后的尸体，就以为胜利了，看着从他们蹂躏的战场上流出的鲜血和燃油，就以为征服了领土。他们就像过去的卡巴尔一样，横扫各个星球，对反抗他们的臣民毫不在意。 

但我没有那么残忍。加入我们阵营的星球沐浴在财富之中，他们作为卡巴尔效忠，因而得到了一切…就和你们现在一样。你们每次为我效忠时都会如此。 

你们中有些人是在这里出生的。你们很年轻，在我的恩赐下，被称颂的战斗和奢华的盛宴将遍布你们的一生。你们将与贪婪的老角斗士战斗。你们将为你们的家园——我们的家园而战。我很乐意称你们为我的孩子。

还有一些人从我叛逆的女儿那来到我身边，她在我还活着的时候就称自己为女帝。如此地傲慢自大。如此地目无尊长。你们也见证到她那毫无獠牙的计划辜负了图罗巴特尔。你们也看到她抛弃卡巴尔的传统向圣城和他们的光能卑躬屈膝。我让他们屈从于我的意志，她却与那些屠杀过你们兄弟的士兵并肩作战。谁是真正的领袖？答案不言而喻。要是她像你们一样追随着我就好了。

最后。最尊贵的是你们这些为数不多的精英，你们从一开始就与大帝并肩作战，在流放中力量日渐壮大：我们是血脉之亲。你们为我而伤亡，我也为你们而流血。我的血肉，我的财富，我的御酒杯。它们属于你们。你们是最光荣的，当我们的新卡巴尔在永恒面前屹立时，你们将会率先位列其中。

我听到了你们之间的流言，我的臣民。敌人给你们灌输的那些谣言。你们认为我没有被彻底击败的盼望是完全正确的，因为我还活得好好的。你们担心我们已被打败，但是事实并非如此。

你们好奇我是否化作了灵魂，我是否已经成为超越卡巴尔的存在，我是否已经像阿克瑞斯将太阳搂在怀里时那样升天。让我来安抚你们的好奇心：没错，我已经成为你们所想象的一切，而且远不止如此。

守护者们以为他们已经取得了胜利，但很快，他们就会看到他们如此坚定地忽视的真相：这条路很长，但只有一个终点。他们的作用就是将我的计划牢固地建立在宇宙的根基上。他们卑劣的攻击，虽然让我的战士们付出了惨痛的代价，却无法阻止我们的目标。

我的士兵们…我留给你们一个任务：守住利维坦。对那些闯入你们家园的入侵者绝不留情。在你们也许会被提升到最终与我同坐之前，这是你们最后的任务。

我不能保证每一个站在利维坦上的卡巴尔都能在这次旅程中幸存下来，但在我慈爱的注视下，你们的生与死都将无比伟大。除了精彩的一生和美好的死亡，一个战士还有什么好期待的呢？这两者我不是都赐予你们了吗？


——来自无人能够遏制的自由大帝卡鲁斯的高级文士，阿姆索特之口：
欢欣吧！赞美飞升的卡鲁斯。因为他会将你们记在心中，在那里你们永远不会死去。

2419786603.name: VII. Legacy
2419786603.text:
Calus sees her as he remembers her. Young and precocious, energetic and ambitious. A mind full of dreams larger than his own.

Her intensity intimidates him. She imagines accomplishments he dares not entertain for fear of failure.

The Nightmare knows this fear. Its adolescent eyes meet his and bore into his soul, laying all his embarrassments bare. It sees him for what he is: a deposed ruler, entombed alive in a golden sarcophagus and left to rot in exile, replaced by one more beloved than he.

"Always seeking the adoration of others," seethes the Nightmare wearing his daughter's face. "Even from the Witness."

"Silence," Calus grumbles. He instinctively reaches for his chalice, but it has long since left his side.

"It will abandon you. Just like the Cabal, just like the Ghost Primus."

The Nightmare of Caiatl smiles, sweet and crimson and full of hatred. "Just like your daughter."

"I said be silent," Calus sputters.

His daughter's laughter is a knife between his ribs, as it always has been.

"No one hears your edicts. No one obeys."

Her voice fills his chamber and seeps into every crevice of his mind.

"She is empress now. You are nothing."

"I made her," he bellows. "I, Calus, the greatest emperor since Acrius. All that comes before me is a prelude. All that follows is my legacy. I am the sun itself!"

"A dying sun for a dead world. A legacy of ashes, soon to be swept away by the wind that is Caiatl."

"She will never surpass me!" he roars.

"She already has," the Nightmare sings. "And soon, you will be forgotten."

Calus's withered face contorts in anguish and angst. The Nightmare is wrong, he thinks. Caiatl will never be a greater leader. He will make sure of it.

Even if all that exists must pay the price.
2419786603.text_zh:
卡鲁斯看到了他记忆中的她。年轻早熟，精力充沛而又雄心勃勃。脑子里满是超越自身的梦想和使命。

她的激情令他为之害怕。她想象着他因畏惧失败而不敢想象的成就。

梦魇了解这种恐惧。它那尚不成熟的双眼与他的目光相遇，深入他的灵魂，让他所有的难堪都展露无遗。它看到了他的本来面目：一个被废黜的统治者，被活埋在金色的石棺里，在流放中任其腐烂，一个比他更受爱戴的人将其取而代之。

“总是寻求别人的崇拜，”梦魇带着女儿的脸庞强压着怒火。“甚至是来自见证者的爱慕。”

“闭嘴，”卡鲁斯抱怨道。他本能地伸手去拿他的圣杯，但它早已离开了他的身边。

“它会抛弃你的。就像卡巴尔，就像幽灵军团长一样抛弃你。”

查厄托的梦魇微笑着，甜美而深红，充满仇恨。“就像你女儿一样抛弃你。”

“我说了闭嘴，”卡鲁斯气急败坏地吼道。

他女儿的笑声就像一把刀插在他的肋骨间，一如既往。

“没有人会听见你的命令。没有人会遵从。”

她的声音充满了他的房间，渗入了他心灵的每一处缝隙。

“她现在是女帝。你什么都不是。”

“我创造了她，”他咆哮道。“我，卡鲁斯，自阿克瑞斯以来最伟大的大帝。在我之前的一切皆为序曲。在我之后的一切皆是我的遗产。我即是太阳本身！”

“了无生气的世界里垂死挣扎的太阳。灰烬的遗产，很快就会被那阵叫做查厄托的风吹走。”

“她永远不会超越我！”他咆哮道。

“她已经做到了，”梦魇吟诵道。“很快，你就会被遗忘。”

卡鲁斯憔悴的面孔在痛苦和忧虑中扭曲。梦魇是错的，他心想。查厄托永远不会是一个伟大的领袖。他会确保这一点。

即使一切存在的事物都必须付出代价。

1866406130.name: CENTESIS
1866406130.text:
Dusk falls, and the braziers are lit. The wind, howling like a starving dog, bites at exposed throats. Safiyah raises her lantern and watches the trickle of survivors pass through the Iron Lords' gates. Some are wounded. Some lie on makeshift stretchers. She gestures to a tent, its interior glowing with warm firelight. 
 
"They will freeze out here," she says. "Take them inside, quickly."
 
Her hospital, such as it is, is humbled by the stone structures which surround it. But she had overseen its construction when she first arrived… stocked it, served it. It was all she could do.
 
The gates close behind the Iron Lords. Unhurt, alive. Zavala is among them. She knows him: the one stubborn enough to argue, but not stubborn enough to ignore her. He speaks to his companions.
 
"—coordinated attacks by the House of Devils. If we take this opportunity to retaliate—"
 
"Retaliate?!"
 
Zavala turns to look at Safiyah. She stares him down.
 
"We have wounded here! We don't need violence. We need supplies!"
 
The others break off, leave him to it—the same fight with the same woman.
 
"Excuse me?" 
 
She doesn't flinch.
 
"I was clear," she says.
 
A drone—Ghost?—bobs in the air just behind Zavala's shoulder—Targe, his name is Targe.
 
"I'm not a part of this," Targe says. Safiyah stands on her toes and catches his eye before he ducks away.
 
"Moving against the Fallen will ensure your safety," Zavala says. "Like I've told you before." 
 
"You want to protect us?" Safiyah points towards the meager hospital. "This is how: by ensuring we have what we need to live."
 
"She isn't wrong," Targe says.
 
"Are you a part of this conversation or not?" Zavala asks, glancing sharply at his Ghost. He turns back to Safiyah.
 
"You don't understand," she says, walking away.
 
"Where are you going?" he asks. A silly question. She ducks under the tent flap. Zavala follows, strung along by their argument. He always wants the last word.
 
Safiyah washes her hands in a basin, then glances at him. She will make him useful.
 
"Wash your hands," she tells him. He hesitates, but does so.
 
"Take this," she says, and hands him a fistful of clean rags. She moves to one of the cots, her head down as she inspects a fresh wound, still bleeding into the dirty bandage. She removes it carefully.
 
"Come here," she says and guides him to press the clean rags into the wound, staunching the flow of blood. He opens his mouth to speak again, but she raises her hand.
 
"I understand the situation," she says. "Do you? Do you know how hard it is to survive in this world?"
 
"Yes," he says. He eases the pressure—she points, snaps her fingers, and he presses down again.
 
"Without your Ghost?"
 
He says nothing. That one will need sutures, Safiyah thinks to herself. She calculates their dwindling stores as she fetches antiseptic and gloves.
 
"It's not just Fallen. It's not just Warlords. It's sickness. Starvation. Cold."
 
She motions for Zavala to stand aside, and he does. The wounded man, regrettably awake, shivers, stiffens, bites down on a scream as she cleans his wound as gently as she can.
 
"We don't walk away from these things the way you do."
 
There is a note of pity in her words. She thinks that he will argue with her, push back, raise his voice. But he says nothing—he is pensive, quiet. She looks up and sees the way his eyes shift, how his jaw stiffens. He wants to speak.
 
She turns away from him, pulling off her gloves at the wrist. Another patient, a woman with a dressed wound across her temple, had shifted in her sleep, her blanket fallen to one side. Carefully, Safiyah picks up the blanket's edge and pulls it up so that it covers her again. She passes a hand over the woman's brow, feeling for fever, and finds none. Safiyah smiles. When she looks up, she sees Zavala watching her.
 
"The wounded look to me." She does not lower her eyes, does not bow her head. "Not you."
1866406130.text_zh:
黄昏降临，火盆被点燃。大风刮得暴露在外的喉咙生疼，风声就像饥犬的嚎叫一般。萨菲亚举起她的灯笼，看着越来越多的幸存者通过钢铁领主的大门。有些人受伤了，有些人躺在临时的担架上。她向一顶内部闪耀着温暖火光的帐篷打了个手势。 
 
“他们在外面会被冻死的，”她说，“快让他们进去。”
 
她的医院在周围的石构建筑的衬托下显得渺小不已。但她刚来就监督了这里的建设…从头到尾。这是她能做到的一切。
 
钢铁领主身后的铁门关上了。他们安然无恙。萨瓦拉是其中一人。她认识萨瓦拉：一个倔强得会跟她争执，但没倔强到无视她的人。他正在和周围的伙伴说话。
 
“…恶魔氏族的协同攻击。如果我们乘机反击…”
 
“反击？！”
 
萨瓦拉转身看着萨菲亚。她盯着他说道，
 
“我们这里有伤员！我们不需要暴力。我们需要补给！”
 
其他人立马走开了——他和她总是这样斗嘴。
 
“你说什么？” 
 
她没有退缩。
 
“我说得很清楚，”她答道。
 
一架无人机…一只机灵，在萨瓦拉的肩旁浮动着——塔格，他的名字是塔格。
 
“我不想掺和，”塔格说。萨菲亚垫着脚尖，在他能藏起来之前对上了视线。
 
“反击堕落者将保证你的安全，”萨瓦拉说。“就像我之前说的那样。” 
 
“你想要保护我们？”萨菲亚指了指她那简陋的医院。“那你得保证我们有生存必需品。”
 
“她说得没错，”塔格说。
 
“你到底要不要掺和进来？”萨瓦拉用锐利的眼神盯着机灵问道。他又转向了萨菲亚。
 
“你就是不懂，”她边走远边说。
 
“你要去哪？”他问。一个愚蠢的问题。她弯腰走进了帐篷。萨瓦拉争执不休，跟着她走了过去。他不吵个明白是不会罢休的。
 
萨菲亚在水盆里洗了洗手，然后对他使了个眼色。她要让他忙活起来。
 
“把你的手洗了，”她告诉他。他犹豫了一下，但是还是洗了手。
 
“拿上这个，”她说道，一边将一把干净的布带递给他。她走到一张病床前，低下头检查一道新鲜伤口。脏兮兮的绷带还在不断浸血。她小心翼翼地把绷带解开。
 
“过来，”她一边说，一边指示他用干净的布带压住伤口止血。他刚想开口，就被她用手势打断了。
 
“我明白现在的状况，”她说。“你明白吗？你知道在这个世界上生存有多难吗？”
 
“我明白，”他说。他的手松了——她赶紧指着伤口打了个响指。他又使上了劲。
 
“没有机灵的情况下？”
 
他什么也没说。萨菲亚心想，这个伤口需要缝合才行。她一边计算着即将见底的库存，一边取来消毒剂和手套。
 
“威胁我们的不止是堕落者。不止是战争领主。还有疾病、饥饿、寒冷。”
 
她示意让萨瓦拉站一边去，他照做了。这个受伤的人不幸还醒着。他颤抖着，紧绷着。在她尽可能温柔地清理他的伤口时，他咬牙忍着不叫出声。
 
“我们不会像你一样逃避这些事情。”
 
她的话里有些怜悯的意味。她以为他会争论，反驳，大吼。但他什么也没说，反而陷入了沉思。她抬起头来，发现他的眼神变了，下巴紧绷着。他想说点什么。
 
她转过身，从手腕上拉下了她的手套。另一个病人，一个太阳穴上的伤口被包扎好的女人，在睡梦中抽搐了一下，把毯子掀到了一边。萨菲亚小心翼翼地提起毯子的边缘，把毯子重新盖到了她身上。她用手摸了摸这个女人的眉毛，检查她是否在发烧；她没事。萨菲亚露出了笑容。她抬起头，发现萨瓦拉正看着她。
 
“伤员指望的是我，”她直截了当地对他说。“不是你。”

1866406129.name: RRHAPHY
1866406129.text:
Safiyah knits by the remainder of the afternoon light, seated outside her tent. It is early spring, her fingers red from the cold, her breath misting in the air. Zavala leads training exercises in the courtyard, sparring with civilians. Some stand awkwardly, holding weapons too heavy for them to wield. Others move with more confidence. Safiyah's eyes drop to her needles.
 
Then she hears a cry of pain. Blood runs down a civilian's shoulder, staining his front. Safiyah can see the wound from her seat. Rising, she takes quick steps toward them, her knitting forgotten.
 
"Do you think your enemy would stop at one wound?" Zavala's voice is a sharp bark. The other man picks up his blade again, despite his shoulder. Safiyah approaches and snaps her fingers.
 
"What are you doing?"
 
Zavala turns to her. Here, an opportunity: Zavala's sparring partner jumps forward, catching him by surprise. The blade slices Zavala's forearm, skin opening in a spray of bright blood.
 
The others gawk, as if they hadn't expected a Risen to bleed. Targe rises up, ready to heal the wound. She raises a hand to stop him.
 
"Don't," she says. The Ghost bobs in the air, looks at her, looks at Zavala.
 
"What do you want?" Zavala barks. He pinches his forearm closed, but the blood runs hot and steaming over his fingers.
 
Safiyah ignores Zavala's retort and gestures to his sparring partner. "Come with me," she says.
 
"Targe," Zavala says to his Ghost, but Safiyah snaps her fingers again.
 
"You too. I want to teach you something. Come inside." 
 
She walks into the hospital tent, knowing she will be obeyed.
 
He obeys. 
 
Once inside, Safiyah inspects Zavala's wound. It is nothing serious, but deep enough for her attention. Her assistant sees to the sparring partner, who looks away sheepishly when Zavala glances at him.
 
"What are you doing?" he asks her.
 
"I think that's obvious," she says. Zavala and his Ghost observe in silence as she cleans the wound.
 
"This isn't necessary," he says, but lets her continue. She produces her hooked needle, the hemostat, the polypropylene thread. Tools that fit easily in her hands; precious resources for an immortal man.
 
"I'm going to close the wound," she says, and touches his arm lightly with a gloved hand. "I will make six sutures. It will take four days, maybe five, to heal."

His features soften. Perhaps he sees that her mind is set. He looks away in a sheepish expression.

"I will make sure your supplies are replenished," he says. "Simply tell me what you need." 

Safiyah feels a flutter of surprise at this promise. Now she will answer his first question.
 
"You need to know what it's like for us," she tells him. She waits for consent; he nods. She pierces the wound and draws its edges together. He doesn't wince.
 
"Where did you learn this?"
 
Genuine curiosity. The first suture.
 
"My mother," she answers. "And books from the Golden Age."

She gestures to a ramshackle shelf holding a dozen books. Old, crumbling, but cared for.
 
"I'd like to see them," he says. She smiles, pleased. Second suture.
 
"I'll show them to you," she says. When she raises her eyes, she sees that he is looking at her with an intensity she can't place. Despite herself, she feels a warmth creep into her skin.
 
"We traveled," she says, too quickly, her eyes dropping back to the third suture. "Very far. Village to village. My mother, father, sister, and me." Fourth suture. "Father killed in a raid. Mother died from disease. Sister a way's west of here. But I kept to my travels."

"Why?" he asks, softly.
 
She passes the needle through its fifth suture.
 
"There are always more people to help. I will move on once I finish training him." She nods to her assistant.
 
Safiyah brings her shears to the thread of the last suture. The wound is closed. She winds a taut bandage around his arm.
 
"Where will you go?" he asks after a stiff silence. Safiyah realizes she doesn't know how to answer. Her thoughts don't stretch beyond this moment. She tucks the bandage beneath itself.
 
"Finished."
 
He flexes, winces, stills. She smiles.
 
"True healing takes time."
 
***
 
That night, she hears voices in the empty courtyard: Zavala and Saladin, standing by a brazier, talking in low tones. She peers from the flap in the tent to watch, to listen.
 
"She is a skilled and formidable woman," Zavala says.
 
Saladin stands with his chin raised in near disdain. Zavala is a silhouette in the firelight. 
 
"I'm not stupid," Saladin growls. "I see the way you look at each other."
 
Safiyah's breath catches. She almost doesn't hear his next words over the sound of her heart.
 
"I have nothing but respect for her," Zavala says curtly. Saladin rolls his eyes. Both men stare each other down for a long moment.
 
"We live in different worlds," Saladin's voice softens. "You can try to abandon ours, but theirs will reject you."
 
"I don't believe that," Zavala says.
 
"Believe what you want. But whatever life you make with her will be too fragile for you to hold onto."
 
Saladin puts a hand on Zavala's shoulder. Safiyah could almost mistake it for compassion.
 
"It will break," he says, his voice low. "And you'll both be hurt."

Safiyah lets the tent flap fall. She does not see if they hear it.
1866406129.text_zh:
萨菲亚坐在她的帐篷外，在午后的阳光下编织着。现在是初春，她的手指被冻得通红，她的呼吸让空气中弥漫着雾气。萨瓦拉在院子里训练着平民，与他们演练。有些人拿着对他们来说重得完全挥不动的武器，笨拙地站着。其他人的动作则更加自信。萨菲亚的目光落在了她的针头上。
 
然后，她听见了一声痛苦的尖叫。一股鲜血顺着一个平民的肩膀流下，染红了他的前胸。萨菲亚从她的位置上都能看到那道伤口。她站起身来，把织物抛到一边，快步走向他们。
 
“你觉得你的敌人打伤你就会停手了吗？”萨瓦拉严厉地喊道。那个人不顾肩膀上的伤口，捡起了刀。萨菲亚快步走来，打了个响指。
 
“你在干什么？”
 
萨瓦拉转向了她。他露出了破绽——萨瓦拉的演练对手趁他不注意，向前一跃，用刀刃在他的前臂上划开了一个伤口，鲜血直流。
 
其他人目瞪口呆，似乎他们没想到复生者也会流血。塔格飞了起来，准备医治他的伤口。她举起一只手，示意他停下。
 
“别治他，”她说。机灵在在半空中浮动着，看了看她，又看了看萨瓦拉。
 
“你想怎样？”萨瓦拉喊道。他用手按着前臂，但血还是止不住地顺着他的手指流淌了下来。
 
萨菲亚无视萨瓦拉的质问，向他的对手打了个手势。"跟我来，"她说。
 
“塔格，”萨瓦拉对他的机灵开口道，但这时萨菲亚又打了个响指。
 
“你也过来。我想教你点东西。进来。” 
 
她转身走进了医院帐篷。她知道萨瓦拉会遵从指示。
 
他确实那样做了。 
 
走进帐篷后，萨菲亚检查了萨瓦拉的伤口。不是很严重，但也没轻到能让她忽略。她的助手去照料萨瓦拉的演练对手了。当萨瓦拉的眼光落到他身上时，他胆怯地望向了一边。
 
“你在干什么？”他问她。
 
“这不明摆着吗，”她说。萨瓦拉和他的机灵静静地看着她清理伤口。
 
“这完全没必要，”他说，但是却没有阻止她。她拿出她的钩针、止血钳和聚丙烯线。这些她熟练使用着的珍贵工具，正被用在一个不死之身上。
 
“我要缝合伤口了，”她一边说，一边用覆盖着手套的手轻轻地触碰着他的前臂。“我要缝六次。要四天，也许五天才能痊愈。”

他的神情变得柔和了起来。也许他意识到了她心意已决。他羞怯地看向了一边。

“我会给你弄来补给品的，”他说。“告诉我你需要什么就好。” 

萨菲亚对他的承诺感到一阵惊喜。现在，她将回答他的第一个问题。
 
“你得明白这种情况对我们是怎样的，”她告诉他。她等着他表示同意；他点了点头。她用钩针穿过伤口旁的皮肤，将两边拉合到一起。他连抖都没抖一下。
 
“你是从哪学的？”
 
他是真的好奇。这是第一次缝合。
 
“我的母亲，”她答道。“还有黄金时代的书籍。”

她指了指一个放着几十本书的残破书架。虽然看起来摇摇欲坠，但是依然被细心打理着。
 
“我想看看，”他说。她满意地笑了。第二次缝合。
 
“那我拿给你看吧，”她说。当她抬起头时，她发现发现他正在用一种难以名状的眼神看着她。她不由自主地感觉到肌肤下泛起了一阵暖意。
 
“我们去过很多地方，”她匆忙说道，然后将注意力放到了缝合上。“很远的地方。一个村子接着一个村子。我的母亲、父亲、姐姐，和我。”第四次缝合。“父亲在一次突袭中死了。母亲得病死了。我姐姐在西边很远的地方。但是我还在旅行。”

“为什么？”他温柔地问道。
 
她的钩针第五次扎破了他的皮肤。
 
“总有人需要我的帮助。在我教完他之后，我会再次启程。”她冲着他的助理点了点头。
 
萨菲亚在缝完最后一次后剪断了缝合线。伤口合起来了。她在他的手臂上紧紧地缠上了一根绷带。
 
“你会去哪里？”他在一阵无言的沉默之后问道。萨菲亚意识到不知道该如何回答。她还没有想过以后的打算。她把绷带卷了起来。
 
“缝完了。”
 
他弯了弯手臂，抽搐了一下，然后不动了。她笑了。
 
“完全恢复还需要些时间。”
 
***
 
那天晚上，她听见空旷的院子里传来了谈话声：萨瓦拉和萨拉丁正在火盆旁低语。她从帐篷里探出头来，一边看，一边偷偷听着他们的对话。
 
“她是个医术高明，又有胆识的女人，”萨瓦拉说。
 
萨拉丁扬起下巴，站姿中透露着不屑。火光映出了萨瓦拉的轮廓。 
 
“我不笨，”萨拉丁低吼道。“我看到了你们俩在眉来眼去。”
 
萨菲亚的呼吸急促了起来。在她的心跳声中，她差点没能听见他接下来说的话。
 
“我对她只有敬重之情，”萨瓦拉简短地说。萨拉丁翻了个白眼。两人接着对视了好一阵子。
 
“我们生活的世界不同，”萨拉丁的语气软了下来。“你可以试着抛弃我们的世界，但是他们的世界也不会接受你。”
 
“我不这么认为，”萨瓦拉答道。
 
“随便你。但不管你和她过上什么样的日子，那种脆弱的生活方式都不会长久。”
 
萨拉丁把一只手放在了萨瓦拉的肩膀上。萨菲亚差点把这个姿势误认成了同情。
 
“那种日子绝对会崩塌，”他低声说道。“而且你们两人都会受伤。”

萨拉菲放下了门帘。她没有留意他们有没有听到动静。

1866406128.name: TAXIA
1866406128.text:
"Like this," Safiyah tells him, and she makes a loop of yarn around his index finger. He holds the needles too tightly, and she gently places a hand over his knuckles until she feels him relax his grip.

They sit together outside her hospital. Safiyah teaches him to knit under the late spring sun.

"This is complicated," he says.

"Only when you aren't paying attention," she tells him. Their eyes briefly meet. She looks away, smiling, at the afternoon sky.

"Look," she says in a tight breath. Smoke plumes on the horizon. They both jolt upright, Zavala awkwardly untangling his fingers from the yarn.

The smoke muddies the sky. Fallen, or Warlords. They have found new victims. Safiyah looks at the growing grim resolve on Zavala's face, then makes for the hospital tent to gather her kit.

A siren blares over the encampment as Safiyah emerges. She makes for the gates as the Iron Lords ready themselves; Zavala takes her by the arm.
 
"You can't be serious," he says. His expression hardens when he sees that she is.
 
"People are in danger," she says.
 
"It's not safe."
 
"That is why I have to go."
 
"At least wait until we've secured the area."
 
Safiyah pulls her arm from his grip. She leaves through the gates before he can argue.
 
The Fallen have ambushed a caravan. Safiyah races through black smoke belching from an overturned sledge, the wreckage crushing the spring flowers. Safiyah rushes to a woman cowering behind a wagon, blood seeping from a wound at her temple. A man lies on the ground behind her, clutching at his stomach, his spilled entrails. A Dreg lunges for them; Safiyah drives a knife into its neck.
 
Zavala leads the main charge to the caravan. The Fallen, screeching at each other, turn their attention to their attackers as bursts of Solar energy roar through the air.
 
Zavala rushes to Safiyah's side, putting himself between her and a charging Captain, its Arc spear raised, and it pierces Zavala through the chest. He coughs blood, falls to the ground, goes still. Safiyah screams, horrified at the sight. But she scrambles for Zavala's weapon and raises it just as the Captain bears down on her. 
 
She fires three rounds through its chest and throat. She sputters as the Ether tears from its body. The corpse lands heavily on her; she pushes it away.
 
Targe sweeps his fallen Guardian, and with a hard breath, Zavala rises again. The sight of him startles her—a man come back to life. He gets his bearings, sees the Captain dead on the ground. 
 
"Are you all right?"
 
"Yes," she says, her voice trembling. Safiyah turns back to the unlucky man who will not rise again, and the woman who weeps at his side.
 
It's in the quiet of the aftermath that Safiyah hears an infant's cry. She jumps to her feet, searching for it in the wreckage, and finds a dead man curled around a squirming bundle. She turns him by his shoulder; the corpse holds the infant so tenderly and tightly that Safiyah has to break his fingers to take the boy from his embrace. She brings the child to her chest, holding his head delicately, and the boy's cries turn into whispered gurgles.
 
Safiyah begins to cry. For the child in her arms, the dead man who held him, the scent of blood and Ether. For those whom she could not save. Her tears are soft, and she shivers. She feels Zavala's palm touch her shoulder and move down her back in silent comfort. She heaves a sigh, then straightens and looks to him.
 
"We'll keep him safe," Zavala says, and she nods.
 
They return with the child. Safiyah feeds him, bathes him. Zavala smiles, holding the child in his arms. The boy reaches for him with tiny hands and looks up at him with wide, brown eyes.
 
"The boy needs a name," she says. She thinks for a moment, remembers her father with fondness.
 
"Hakim," she declares, and it is so.
 
***
 
Hakim grows. Months pass until summer comes and the cicadas sing. Zavala visits Safiyah between his duties, and Safiyah soothes Hakim's cries when Zavala is absent. Resources are thin. They do their best.
 
In the evenings, Safiyah holds Hakim's warmth to her chest. She feels the rise and fall of his breath. Bowing, she presses her lips to the curls on the crown of his head. Zavala is beside her, a hand at the small of her back.
 
The cicadas sing—she gestures for Zavala to listen. The cicadas sing.

"The ancient Greeks thought that these insects lived forever," she says. "Reborn each time they came from the earth."
 
 Zavala puts his arms around them both.
 
"They spend 17 years underground. They almost went extinct. Then the Collapse… and now they thrive again."

She coos at Hakim for a moment.

"I will take him to my sister's village," she says. Zavala's features soften.
 
"We will take him," he answers, and she smiles. This is how he tells her.
 
Zavala speaks to Saladin the following morning. When Zavala finds her again, he has left behind the pendant with the Iron Lords' sigil.
1866406128.text_zh:
“像这样，”萨菲亚一边在他的食指上绕着一圈毛线，一边告诉他。他把针握得太紧了。她轻轻地把一只手放在他的指节上，直到她感觉到他放松了握力。

他们一起在她的医院外坐着。萨菲亚正在晚春的阳光下教他编织。

“好复杂啊，”他说。

“那是因为你不认真学，”她告诉他。他们的目光短暂地对上了。她微笑着，朝着午后的天空望去。

“看，”她急促地说。地平线上冒起了烟柱。他们立马蹦了起来，萨瓦拉尴尬地试着将毛线从手指上取下。

浓烟遮住了天空。不是堕落者就是战争领主干的好事。他们找到了新的猎物。萨菲亚看了看萨瓦拉脸上渐显严峻的神情，走进了医院帐篷里去拿她的医疗包。

萨菲亚刚走出来，警报便响彻了营地。他冲向了在大门旁聚集的钢铁领主们；萨瓦拉拽住了她的手臂。
 
“你不会真的想去吧，”他说。在意识到她是认真的之后，他的表情更严峻了。
 
“人们遇到危险了，”她说。
 
“外面不安全。”
 
“所以我才得去。”
 
“至少先等我们确保这附近安全了为止。”
 
萨菲亚挣脱了萨瓦拉。在他能反驳之前，她就冲出了大门。
 
堕落者伏击了一支车队。萨菲亚在翻倒的雪橇冒出的滚滚黑烟中奔走，雪橇的残骸压塌了春天的花朵。萨菲亚冲向一个蜷缩在车厢后的女人，鲜血正从她太阳穴上的伤口里不断渗出。一个男人躺在她身后，抓着自己肚破肠流的腹部。一名堕落士兵朝他们扑了过来；萨菲亚用一把小刀刺穿了它的喉咙。
 
萨瓦拉带队冲向了车队。堕落者朝同伴吼叫着，与来袭的钢铁领主们交战。烈日能量漫天爆发，响声如雷。
 
萨瓦拉冲到萨菲亚身边，将自己横在一名猛扑而来的队长的前方。它举起电弧长枪，刺穿了萨瓦拉的胸膛。他吐着血倒在了地上，一动不动。萨菲亚被眼前的场景吓得惊声尖叫。但就在队长扑过来之前，她拿起了萨瓦拉的武器。 
 
她用三发子弹打穿了它的胸膛和喉咙。乙太从它的身体中喷出来。沉重的尸体压在了她的身上；她使劲把它推到一边。
 
塔格扫了扫他那位倒地的守护者，萨瓦拉喘着粗气坐了起来。这幅景象让她打了个寒颤——一个人在她的眼前起死回生。他看了看周围，发现了地上的队长尸体。 
 
“你没事吧？”
 
“我没事，”她颤抖着答道。萨菲亚又看向了那个不会起死回生的男人，以及那个在他身边痛哭的女人。
 
在战斗后的宁静中，萨菲亚听到了婴儿的啼哭。她跳了起来，在残垣断壁中搜寻着。她发现一具尸体正紧紧地抱着一个蠕动的包袱。她抓着这具尸体的肩膀把它翻了过来；这具尸体是如此温柔却牢固地抱着一个婴儿，以至于萨菲亚不得不折断他的手指才能把孩子从他的怀抱中取出来。她把这个孩子举到胸前，小心翼翼地抱着他的脑袋。男孩的哭声变成了小小的咯咯声。
 
萨菲亚哭了起来。她在为那个在她怀抱中的孩子哭泣，为那个抱着她的已死之人哭泣，为那弥漫在空气中的血腥味和乙太味哭泣，为那些她没法救助的人哭泣。她流下潺潺泪水，悲声恸哭。她感到萨瓦拉的手掌抚摸着她的肩膀，顺着她的背下落，无声地安慰着她。她叹了一口气，然后直起身来，看向了他。
 
“我们会保护他的，”萨瓦拉说。她点了点头。
 
他们带着孩子回到了营地。萨菲亚给他喂了吃的，然后给他洗了个澡。萨瓦拉笑着将这个孩子揽进了怀抱里。这个男孩向萨瓦拉伸出了小小的双手，用那对褐色的大眼睛望着他。
 
“我们得给这个孩子取个名，”她说。她思索了一会，然后回忆起了她亲爱的父亲。
 
“哈基姆，”他的名字就这样被定了下来。
 
***
 
哈基姆渐渐长大了。几个月后，夏蝉长鸣的时节又到了。萨瓦拉会在工作间隙去看望萨菲亚，萨菲亚在萨瓦拉不在时会抚慰哭闹的哈基姆。物资很匮乏，但他们都尽力而为。
 
在晚上，萨菲亚将温暖的哈基姆抱在胸前，感受着他的呼吸。她低下头，将嘴唇贴在他头顶的卷发上。萨瓦拉就在她身旁，一只手放在她的腰上。
 
夏蝉鸣叫着——她示意萨瓦拉仔细听。夏蝉鸣叫着。

“古希腊人以为这些昆虫的寿命是无限的，”她说。“他们以为这些虫子每次爬出泥土时是在重生。”
 
 萨瓦拉抱住了两人。
 
“在地下度过17年，几乎灭绝。然后发生了大崩溃…而现在，再度昌盛。”

她抚慰了哈基姆一阵子。

“我要把他带到我姐姐的村子去，”她说。萨瓦拉的神情放松了下来。
 
“是‘我们'要带他去，”他答道。她也笑了。他就是这样告诉她的。
 
萨瓦拉隔天早上就去找了萨拉丁。在萨瓦拉回到她身边时，他已经抛下了印有钢铁领主标志的挂坠。

1866406135.name: ESTHESIA
1866406135.text:
Safiyah's sister greets her at the gates of her village with an incredulous stare.
 
"Amani," Safiyah says stiffly. There is a moment's silence before the sisters embrace. She is welcomed. Then Amani looks to Zavala and Hakim. She simply raises an eyebrow.
 
Days pass. 
 
"I don't think she likes me." Zavala speaks softly over Hakim sleeping in the makeshift cradle in Amani's home.
 
"She definitely doesn't like me," Targe says, emerging.
 
"Why do you say that?" Safiyah asks.
 
"She said, 'I don't like you,' " Targe answers. "To both of us." 
 
Safiyah frowns. "She likes Hakim," she offers. That will have to be enough.
 
Her sister's village is small, but well-fortified, a wall of wooden stakes around their homes. They scrape vegetables and bitter rye from the earth and keep livestock in the barn. 
 
Safiyah and Zavala build their home there. Years pass. Hakim grows. Zavala holds his hands as the boy toddles on young, unsteady feet.
 
Clack, clack.
 
Safiyah knits in her favorite chair, something once precious she had left behind. Through the window, she sees Zavala and their son spar with wooden swords in the field behind their home. It is play. Their son is nine. Safiyah can hear the clack of wood on wood in the autumn air. Her eyes drop back to her yarn.
 
Clack, clack.
 
Their son is twelve. She sees Zavala correct Hakim's stance, raise his arms, straighten his back. The boy only comes up to his father's elbows. Targe circles around them. The yarn shifts around her fingers as she passes it from needle to needle.
 
Clack, clack.
 
Their son is fifteen. The sleeve of the sweater she works on lengthens. It is summer, but she knits for the colder months ahead. Her sister sits beside her, cleaning a rifle and counting bullets.
 
"We're overdue for a raid," Amani says, as if she were remarking on a low crop yield, bad weather, or a stillborn calf—just another hardship, inevitable. Bullets clink together in her lap. 
 
Safiyah spreads the woolen sweater over her knees. 
 
"For Hakim?" Amani asks. Safiyah nods.
 
"He outgrows them every two months. He needs new trousers too. I can see his ankles."
 
The final clack of the swords clatters out, and she looks up.
 
Safiyah sees the flash of a metal blade in Hakim's hand. She throws down her knitting and runs to them. The knife is at Zavala's throat when she reaches them.
 
"What are you doing!" 
 
It is not a question. It is an admonition. Zavala steps back and gestures to the knife in Hakim's hands.
 
"I'm teaching him how to defend himself." 
 
Safiyah reaches for her son, holds Hakim to her chest. She kisses the crown of his head, whispers softly into the curls of his hair. But he pushes her away, steps back, stares up at her defiantly.
 
"I can do it," he says. "It's just a lesson!"
 
Safiyah looks to Zavala, shaking her head in disbelief. 
 
"He needs to be prepared to take a life." He speaks gently, as if he had not just asked his son to slit his throat.
 
"He is a child," she says.
 
Hakim takes a breath, frowns, begins to speak. Zavala touches his shoulder.
 
"Do you think that matters to the Fallen?" His voice is dark.
 
Safiyah takes the knife from her son's hand and holds it by the flat of the blade. An edge for harming, not healing. 

She knows Zavala is right, and hates it. 

***
 
That night, Safiyah's sister stays up with her, talking by candlelight.
 
"It's been years." Amani clicks her tongue. "He'll never see the way we do. They can't."
 
"I don't believe that."

"I know you don't."
 
Amani laughs, but Safiyah is silent, frowning. He must understand. 

Her sister sighs.
 
"He loves you."
 
Safiyah nods. 
 
"He loves Hakim."
 
She nods again.
 
"Then maybe that is enough."

When she returns home, Safiyah finds Zavala watching over Hakim as he sleeps. Zavala rises, pulls the blanket a little higher over Hakim's shoulder, then brushes his fingers over his son's cheek.

Safiyah realizes then that in all the Risen's long, unenviable years, they were never once children.
 
She reaches for Zavala, and he takes her into his arms, a silent question of forgiveness.
 
"Let him be a child for a little longer," she whispers into his ear. "You will miss these days when they have gone."
1866406135.text_zh:
萨菲亚的姐姐在村子的大门口迎接她的到来。她用一种难以置信的目光看着她。
 
“阿玛妮，”萨菲亚僵硬地说道。片刻沉默过后，姐妹抱在了一起。她欢迎萨菲亚的到来。阿玛妮看了看萨瓦拉和哈基姆，稍微皱了皱眉。
 
几天后。 
 
“她好像不喜欢我，”在阿玛妮的家中，萨瓦拉趁着哈基姆在临时摇篮中熟睡，轻声对萨菲亚说。
 
“她肯定不喜欢我，”塔格冒了出来。
 
“你为什么会这么觉得？”萨菲亚问道。
 
“因为她说了‘我不喜欢你'，”塔格回答道。“对我们两个都说过。” 
 
萨菲亚皱了皱眉头。“她喜欢哈基姆，”她说。这就足够了。
 
她姐姐的村庄很小，但是防御牢固。他们的房子周围都有一堵木桩墙。他们在地里种些蔬菜和苦黑麦，在谷仓里饲养牲畜。 
 
萨菲亚和萨瓦拉在这里建起了他们的家。几年过去了。哈基姆又长大了些。萨瓦拉用手牵着这个蹒跚迈步的小男孩。
 
*咯哒，咯哒*
 
萨菲亚坐在她最喜欢的椅子上打毛线。这是她已荒废许久的珍贵爱好。她透过窗户，看见萨瓦拉和儿子正在房后的空地上用木剑比试。他们在打着玩。他们的儿子已经九岁了。萨菲亚能听见秋日里木剑擦碰的声音。她又把注意力移到了手里的毛线上。
 
*咯哒，咯哒*
 
他们的儿子已经十二岁了。她看着萨瓦拉纠正哈基姆的站姿，抬起他的手臂，让他打直后背。这孩子的头只能够到父亲的肘部。塔格围着他们转圈。针线在她手中灵巧地交织着。
 
*咯哒，咯哒*
 
他们的儿子十五岁了。她手上那件毛衣的袖子越来越长了。虽然现在是夏天，但她已经在为寒冬织衣了。她的姐姐坐在她身旁，一边清理步枪，一边清点子弹。
 
“他们早该来突袭了，”阿玛妮说。她的语气就像在描述另一件不可避免的难事似的——就像是在说收成不好、天气太糟、小牛胎死腹中一样。子弹在她的腿上咯铛咯铛地碰擦。 
 
萨菲亚在腿上铺开了那件羊毛毛衣。 
 
“给哈基姆织的？”阿玛妮问道。萨菲亚点了点头。
 
“新衣服给他穿两个月就显小了。他还需要新的裤子。现在他脚踝都露在外边。”
 
两把刀剑的碰撞声骤停。她抬起头来看了看。
 
萨菲亚在哈基姆的手上看见了金属刀刃发出的寒光。她丢下正织着的衣服，朝他们跑去。在她跑到两人身旁时，一把匕首已经架在了萨瓦拉的喉咙上。
 
“你们在干什么！” 
 
这不是询问。这是警告。萨瓦拉往后退了几步，然后指了指哈基姆手上的小刀。
 
“我在教他如何保护自己。” 
 
萨菲亚一把将哈基姆揽进怀里。她吻了吻儿子的头顶，贴着他的头发，温柔地对他细语。但他却把她推开，用坚毅的眼神看着她。
 
“我没问题的，”他说。“只是一堂课而已！”
 
萨菲亚看着萨瓦拉，难以置信地摇着头。 
 
“他需要做好夺取另一条生命的准备。”他温柔地说道，就好像他刚刚没有让他儿子割开他的喉咙似的。
 
“他还是个孩子，”她说。
 
哈基姆吸了一口气，皱了皱眉头，想要说点什么。萨瓦拉把手放在了他的肩上。
 
“你觉得这种事对堕落者有区别吗？”他凝重地说道。
 
萨菲亚从儿子手上抢走了小刀，紧紧地抓着刀背。这是一把用来杀戮的刀，而不是用来救人的刀。 

她知道萨瓦拉是对的。但她讨厌这个事实。 

***
 
那晚，萨菲亚的姐姐陪着她在烛光下聊了一夜。
 
“已经这么多年了。”阿玛妮啧了啧舌头。“他永远不会像我们这样看待这个世界。他们永远都不会。”
 
“我不相信。”

“我知道你不相信。”
 
阿玛妮笑了，但萨菲亚只是皱着眉头，一言不发。他必须得理解才行。 

她的姐姐叹了口气。
 
“他爱你。”
 
萨菲亚点了点头。 
 
“他爱哈基姆。”
 
她又点了点头。
 
“也许那就足够了。”

她回家后，萨菲亚走到了正在看着哈基姆入睡的萨瓦拉身边。萨瓦拉站了起来，顺手把哈基姆的被子拉到了他肩膀上，然后用手指摸了摸他儿子的脸颊。

萨菲亚意识到，在复生者漫长的生命中，他们从未做过孩子。
 
她伸出手，萨瓦拉将他揽进了怀抱。他在无声地请求她的谅解。
 
“让他多做会儿孩子吧，”她在他的耳边低语道。“以后有一天你会想念这些日子的。”

1866406134.name: ALGIA
1866406134.text:
Safiyah hears the trade of gunfire. Tap-tap-tap, like birds pecking. But too quick. Too sharp. Zavala stands abruptly.
 
"The Fallen!" A shout of terror from outside. The House of Devils. Zavala is through the door before Safiyah can speak. She gathers her kit.
 
The gunfire grows louder, quicker. There are cries of pain, of death throes.
 
Hakim is seventeen.
 
"Stay here," she pleads. "Stay safe."
 
"I can fight," he tells her. He is taller than she is now.
 
"Please," she says. Reluctantly, Hakim nods. Safiyah puts her arms around him, holds him for a moment, tries to quell her fear, and then follows her husband into the fight.
 
Fallen clamber over the village's gates, disorganized and led by a Captain too vicious and too eager to be where the fighting is thickest. The friends and neighbors Zavala trained raise their weapons and hold their ground as they are swarmed. Safiyah sees her husband leading the defense, shouting commands over gunfire and screams.
 
A farmhand with a gun falls when a bullet pierces his thigh; Safiyah is there to drag him from danger, tourniquet and dressings in hand. She keeps low, time and again reaching the wounded as the Fallen are pushed back.
 
She hears a voice—instantly familiar, now threaded with terror, piercing through the fray. Safiyah turns and sees Hakim deflect a swipe of the Arc spear from the Fallen Captain. The blow unsteadies him. Safiyah screams his name. Hakim steps back, his eyes wide.
 
The Captain draws the spear and jams the weapon into her son's body. 
 
Zavala is suddenly there, knocks the creature down with two shots, finishes it with another. Safiyah runs to Hakim and skids to her knees beside him. 
 
Slick redness coats the back of her hands as she presses hard on the wound, edges singed by Arc energy. Blood wells from Hakim's mouth as he tries to speak. His grip loosens on his weapon—a sickle, a tool to cut down stalks of rye—and his eyes go slack.
 
The scent of her son's death settles into the pith of her lungs. 
 
She does not hear Zavala's footsteps. She does not hear anything. Her bloodied palm is at her son's cheek, wiping away the cold tears that had stayed behind on his unfocused eyes.
 
Her breath falters. Slowly, she draws her other hand from Hakim's wound and puts her arms around him. She feels her son's body against her chest, the weight in her arms. She remembers, briefly, when he had finally grown so heavy that she could no longer cradle him as she once had.
 
"Safi," she hears, at last. 

She turns to look at Zavala. He stands as a silhouette against the rising sun, the new dents and cracks of his armor shimmering in the light. He comes toward her, his face horror. She wonders if he had died as well. She turns to look at Hakim again. There is no Ghost for her son.
 
Zavala kneels beside her. Shaking, he takes Hakim's body into his arms, and they bring him home.
1866406134.text_zh:
萨菲亚听到了交火声。哒哒哒，像鸟叫一样。但是更快，更尖锐。萨瓦拉一下子蹦了起来。
 
“堕落者！”外面传来了惊恐的喊叫声。是恶魔氏族。萨瓦拉在萨菲亚能开口之前就冲出了门。她匆忙地拿起了她的急救箱。
 
枪声越来越大，越来越密集。外面传来了痛苦的嘶吼和死前的哀嚎。
 
这时，哈基姆十七岁。
 
“留在这里，”她乞求道。“保护好自己。”
 
“我也能战斗，”他告诉她。他现在比她还高了。
 
“求你了，”她说。哈基姆不情愿地点了点头。萨菲亚紧紧地抱了他一会儿，努力地压制着心中的恐惧，然后跟着他丈夫投身战斗。
 
堕落者翻过村子的大门，在一个穷凶恶极的队长的带领下，如同一团散沙般地冲了过来。经过萨瓦拉训练的朋友们和邻居们举着武器，在蜂拥而至的堕落者前坚守阵地。萨菲亚看到她的丈夫在指挥着防线，在枪声和尖叫中发号施令。
 
一名拿着枪的农夫大腿中弹，倒在了地上；萨菲亚手里拿着止血带和敷料，将他从枪林弹雨中拖到一边。她压低身子，趁着堕落者被击退的时机，一趟又一趟地搬运着伤员。
 
她在激烈的战斗中听见了一个再也熟悉不过声音——不过这次充满了恐惧。萨菲亚转过头，看见哈基姆正抵挡着堕落者队长的电弧长枪。这一击使他失去了平衡。萨菲亚尖叫着他的名字。哈基姆往后踉跄了几步，双目圆睁。
 
队长再次举起长矛，然后刺穿了她儿子的身体。 
 
萨瓦拉猛地冲到那里，两枪撂倒那怪物，再补上一枪干掉了它。萨菲亚赶紧冲向哈基姆，跪倒在他的身旁。 
 
鲜红的血液从那被电弧烧焦的伤口里流出，染红了她压着伤口的手。哈基姆想说些什么，但血从他嘴里喷涌而出。他紧抓武器的那只手松开了——那是一把用来收割黑麦草的镰刀。他的眼睛失去了神气。
 
儿子死亡的气息填满了她的肺。 
 
她听不到萨瓦拉的脚步声。她什么都听不到。她用沾满鲜血的双手托着儿子的脸庞，擦拭着那双无神的眼睛遗落下的泪水。
 
她的呼吸变弱了。慢慢地，她把另一只手从哈基姆的伤口上拿开，抱住了他。她感觉着她儿子的身体紧贴着她的胸膛，感觉着怀中的重量。她忽然想起了儿子重到自己抱不起来的那个时候。
 
“萨菲，”她的耳边终于传来了一个声音。 

她望向萨瓦拉。他的身影映在初升的旭日中，护甲上的新凹痕在阳光下熠熠生辉。他朝她走了过来，满脸惊恐。她不确定他刚才是不是也死了。她又看了看哈基姆。他的儿子没有机灵守护。
 
萨瓦拉跪在了她身旁。他颤抖着，将哈基姆的遗体抱住，然后朝家走了去。

1866406133.name: RRHEXIS
1866406133.text:
Zavala lays Hakim down on his bed, supporting him so that his head comes to rest softly on the pillow. Safiyah pulls his blanket up, trembling, stopping short of drawing it over his face.
 
When she reaches for her husband's hand beside her, she realizes she is stained up to her elbows with her son's dark, blackened blood. The blood of a deep, interior wound.
 
Zavala reaches for the edge of his son's blanket, adjusting it to cover Hakim's shoulder, carefully, as if he is afraid to wake him.
 
***
 
"What will you do now?"
 
Amani has a way of cutting to the heart of things. Hakim has been buried for a month. Flowers on his headstone. The sisters sit, overlooking the graveyard. The night air is thick with summer warmth. All is silvered in the moonlight. The cicadas sing. The world does not stop and witness her grief.
 
Safiyah shakes her head, silent. Her sister puts an arm around her shoulders.
 
"You will have to decide."
 
The silence grows heavy. She feels Amani draw her into an embrace.
 
"He was a good boy," her sister says, and Safiyah hears the quaver in her voice. "Stubborn and brave, like his father."
 
They part, and Amani clasps Safiyah's hands in hers. Her sister gives a sad smile; Safiyah does not return it. Her grief is solitary. Inward. She cries when she is alone.
 
"Zavala is at Hakim's grave most nights," Safiyah says at last.
 
But not tonight.
 
"Sleep," her sister says. "Sleep, and think about your future. Here, or elsewhere."
 
"You want me to leave?" Safiyah asks. Amani shakes her head, squeezes her sister's hands.
 
"No. Never. But I want you to find your joy again. I don't believe you'll find it here."
 
 
***
 
"Bring him back."
 
Safiyah hears Zavala's voice when she returns home. She follows the sound to their bedroom.
 
"Bring him back," he demands again. There is a tremor in Zavala's voice. Safiyah peers through the slip of space offered by the unlatched door. Her husband faces away from her, speaking to his Ghost.
 
"I can't," Targe says.
 
Targe stares up at Zavala. She can see the Ghost shivering.
 
"Take my Light and bring him back." He struggles at every word.
 
"You know I can't."
 
"Would you?" Zavala asks, something clawing into his voice. "Would you bring him back, if you could?"
 
If Targe speaks, Safiyah doesn't hear it. But she hears the scrape of Zavala's gun on the nightstand.
 
"Find a way. Bring him back," Zavala pleads.
 
Safiyah doesn't hesitate when she sees Zavala raise the weapon. She swings open the door. Her husband flinches, turns, sees her standing at the threshold. Careful, she walks to him, puts a hand on his arm, lowers his gun. Zavala falls to his knees, the gun clattering to the floor.
 
Safiyah reaches for Targe, and he floats to her. She holds him in her hands. There is a thrum, a warmth, in her palms. The Ghost's singular eye, pale blue, looks up at her. She remembers all the times he hovered just out of Hakim's reach, teasing him, playing with him. In that moment, she knows that Targe loved him too.
 
"We cannot change what happened," she whispers to her husband. "This will not change who we are."
 
She thinks he will turn to her and ask, Who am I? But he doesn't. Targe leaves her embrace to hover beside Zavala.

"I can't stay here," she says. He says nothing. He knows himself—and he knows who she is too. She is certain.

Safiyah searches his face. She sees Hakim when she looks at him. She sees her own pain, reflected in his eyes. And she sees his pain as well, just as endless as the years he will suffer beyond her own. Safiyah looks away.
 
"I can't understand eternity," she says, sadly. "I don't know if you can either. But you will live it. I will not."
 
Zavala takes a hard breath, and the sob drags itself from his body. She looks at him again.

"Don't forget us, Zavala." Her voice breaks. "For all your years. Please."
 
"Never."
1866406133.text_zh:
萨瓦拉把哈基姆抬到他的床边，慢慢地将他的头放到枕头上。萨菲亚颤抖着，慢慢地给他盖上被子。她的手在儿子的脸庞前停住了。
 
当她伸出手去摸身旁丈夫的手时，她才意识到她儿子黑乎乎的血渍已经没过了她的手肘。这是深度内伤才会流的血。
 
萨瓦拉抓着被子角，小心翼翼地盖住了儿子的肩膀，似乎是怕吵醒他。
 
***
 
“你现在打算做什么？”
 
阿玛妮从来都直话直说。哈基姆已经入土一个月了。他的坟头上已经长出了花朵。两姐妹望着坟墓。夏日的温度让夜晚的空气闷了起来。月光给大地披上了银装。夏蝉还在鸣叫。世界并没有停下脚步去见证她的悲痛。
 
萨菲亚摇了摇头，一语不发。她的姐姐搂住了她。
 
“你必须做出决定。”
 
这阵沉默变得越来越沉重。她感到阿玛妮抱住了自己。
 
“他是个好男孩，”她姐姐说。萨菲亚察觉到她的声音有些颤抖。“固执又勇敢，像他爸爸。”
 
她们分开了。阿玛妮握住萨菲亚的双手。她的姐姐给了她一个苦笑。萨菲亚没有反应。她的悲痛是孤独的。内向的。她会在一个人时哭泣。
 
“萨瓦拉几乎每天晚上都会在哈基姆的墓旁，”萨菲亚终于开口道。
 
但他今晚不在。
 
“睡吧，”她姐姐说。“先睡一觉，然后再想以后的事。不管是留在这里，还是去其他地方。”
 
“你想让我走？”萨菲亚问道。阿玛妮紧紧地攥着她的手，摇着头。
 
“不。我永远不会那样想。但是我希望你能重新找到幸福。我不觉得你能在这里找到它。”
 
 
***
 
“把他带回来。”
 
萨菲亚回家时听见了萨瓦拉的声音。她循声走进了他们的卧室。
 
“把他带回来，”他再次要求到。萨瓦拉的声音颤抖着。萨菲亚透过门缝往里看。她的丈夫正背对着她，和他的机灵说着话。
 
“我办不到，”塔格说。
 
塔格盯着萨瓦拉。她能看见那只机灵正在发抖。
 
“拿走我的光能，让他复活。”他艰难地吐出了每一个字。
 
“你知道我办不到。”
 
“那你愿不愿意？”萨瓦拉问道。他的声音里多了些嘶哑。“如果你能办到，你愿意复活他吗？”
 
萨菲亚没听到塔格有没有回答。但她听到了萨瓦拉的枪在床头柜上刮擦的声音。
 
“想办法。把他带回来，”萨瓦拉乞求道。
 
看到萨瓦拉举起武器，萨菲亚没有犹豫。她一把推开了房门。她的丈夫颤了一下，回头看见她站在门口。她小心翼翼地走到他身旁，把手放在他的前臂上，让他把枪放下。萨瓦拉跪倒在地，手中的枪也落到了地板上。
 
萨菲亚向塔格伸出了手，而他也朝她飞了过去。她将他握在了手里。她感到手里有种震动，有种温暖。幽灵淡蓝色的独眼正仰望着她。她想起了他在哈基姆身边绕飞，逗弄他，和他玩耍的时光。在那一刻，她意识到，塔格也爱着他。
 
“我们不能改变已经发生的事，”她对他丈夫低语道。“这改变不了我们是谁。”
 
她以为他会转身问她，“那我是谁？”但是他没有这么做。塔格离开了她的怀抱，回到了萨瓦拉的身旁。

“我不能留在这里，”她说。他什么也没说。他了解他自己——而且他也了解她。她很确定。

萨菲亚打量着他的脸。她一看到萨瓦拉，就会想起哈基姆。她在他的眼睛里看见了和自己一模一样的痛苦。而且之中还有他自己的痛苦。将来，在她也去世后，给他带来的无尽痛苦。萨菲亚看向了一边。
 
“我不明白永恒是什么概念，”她悲伤地说道。“我也不知道你明白不明白。但是你会永远活下去。而我不会。”
 
萨瓦拉艰难地吸了一口气，痛哭失声。她又看向了他。

“别忘记我们，萨瓦拉。”她用嘶哑的声音说道。“请你永远别忘。”
 
“永远。”

1866406132.name: LYSIS
1866406132.text:
The village is behind them, faded into the colors of a late summer sky.
 
When they departed, Amani had held fast to Safiyah's hands until she promised to come home again, in time. To Zavala, Amani gave only a nod and a sad smile.
 
Soon, the stone structures of the Iron Lord encampment rise on the horizon. 
 
Zavala and Safiyah pass where they first found Hakim. The bodies are gone, the blood long soaked into the earth. The burned trees have new growth around their wounds. But the fragments of rusted wreckage along their path, picked over for any useful pieces, are still half-buried in the soil.
 
At the gates, Safiyah presses her knitting needles into his hands. 
 
"To keep you warm," she says. He nods his head and thanks her, his voice small.
 
"You will survive this," she tells him. She knows he has no choice.
 
Safiyah departs to find the people who need her. She feels Zavala's gaze cling to her until the gates of the Iron Lords disappear into the horizon.
 
***
 
The gates of the encampment open for Zavala, alone. Saladin says little, passes no judgment, tenders no admonition. All he says to him is this:
 
"Love is a moment in time. We are not."
 
Zavala wonders, for an instant, if Saladin speaks from experience. He does not ask but simply takes a breath and follows Lord Saladin.
 
***
 
It is decades until a message arrives from Amani—half crumpled and discolored from the uncertain journey it took to reach him in the Last City. "Come quickly," it reads. "Before it is too late."
 
But he arrives too late. 
 
Amani stands at the grave among the mourners, stooped, old. He nods to her, catching her eyes for a moment. A sad, familiar smile crosses her lips again before she returns the gesture in silent thanks.
 
He waits until most have left before he approaches the headstone. He holds a flower, picked on his journey. It was fresh when he found it, but its petals are bruised now as he gently places it on the churned earth of her grave.
 
Zavala rises and sees a woman standing beside him. They have the same eyes, warm and kind. Her daughter.
 
"How did you know her?" she asks. His breath catches, unsure of how to answer a simple question from one mourner to another.
 
"I'm an old friend," he says, unable to keep the weariness from seeping into his words. The woman looks at him askance; he wonders, briefly, if she knows of him, his history. Her brother. But she simply nods and thanks him, and nothing more is said.
 
Years later, he visits the woman's grave. Then her son's. Her son's son. The graveyard grows thick with headstones. He makes the journey each time.
 
They do not come to the Last City for 10 generations. The Hidden tell him when they are born, when they are sick, and when they die. He never speaks to them when they are alive, but at each grave, he leaves a token and a question: Can you forgive me?
 
The Red War does not claim them, but when the City grieves for those lost to the Vex and the Endless Night, Zavala grieves for the last of Safiyah's descendants. This time, there is no body for a grave.
 
Now, Zavala sits at his desk. The knitting needles are worn with use. He holds them carefully, remembering how she had placed his fingers so that he could follow her movements. 

He casts on a length of yarn and begins again.
1866406132.text_zh:
他们身后的村庄逐渐融进了晚夏的天空。
 
当他们离开时，阿玛妮握着萨菲亚的手不放，直到她答应以后还会再回来才松手。对于萨瓦拉，阿玛妮只是对他点了个头，然后给了他一个悲伤的笑容。
 
很快，钢铁领主的石构建筑出现在了地平线上。 
 
萨瓦拉和萨菲亚走过了他们当初找到哈基姆的地方。尸体早已不见踪影，血液也早就浸进了土壤里。有新的枝叶从烧焦树干的伤口里长了出来。被烧毁的树木在其伤口周围有了新的生长。但沿途那些没被捡走的生锈残骸，仍然半掩在土壤中。
 
在大门前，萨菲亚把她的织针递到了他手上。 
 
“这能让你不着凉，”她说。他点了点头，然后小声道了谢。
 
“你能撑过去，”她告诉他。她知道他没有选择。
 
萨菲亚去寻找那些需要她的人了。直到钢铁领主的大门消失在地平线上，她才感到萨瓦拉的视线从她的背上挪开了。
 
***
 
营地的大门为萨瓦拉一人而开启。萨拉丁什么也没说，没有评判，没有告诫。他只对萨瓦拉说了一句话：
 
“爱情是短暂的。我们不是。”
 
有那么一瞬间，萨瓦拉怀疑萨拉丁是在凭经验说话。他没有问，只是吸了口气，跟上了萨拉丁。
 
***
 
几十年之后，一封来自阿玛妮的消息到了他手上——信上的褶皱和褪色证明了这封信到达圣城，到达他手上所经历的曲折旅途。“快来，"上面写道。“在为时已晚之前。”
 
但是他来得太晚了。 
 
阿玛妮和其他吊唁者一同站在墓前。她已经老了，佝偻了。他朝她点了点头，对上了眼神。她又露出了那个熟悉的，悲伤的笑容。她默默地向他致以谢意。
 
待大多数人走后，他才走到了墓碑前。他手上拿着一束沿路摘来的花朵。在摘的时候，这束花还是新鲜的，但现在它已伤痕累累。他轻轻地把这束花放在了她那土还没压实的坟头上。
 
萨瓦拉起身，看见他身旁站着一位女性。她们的眼睛一模一样，温暖又善良。这是她的女儿。
 
“你是怎么认识她的？”她问道。他的呼吸一下急促了起来，因为他不确定该如何回答这个来自于另一位吊唁者的简单问题。
 
“我是她的老朋友，”他故作镇静地说道，但还是不禁在话语中流露出了疲惫感。这个女人斜视着他；他忽然很想知道，她是否认识他，是否知道他的过去，是否认识她的兄弟。但她只是点头致了谢，没多说什么。
 
几年后，他来拜访了这个女人的墓。然后是这个女人儿子的墓。然后是她儿子的儿子的墓。这个墓地都快被墓碑填满了。但他还是每次都会来看看。
 
他们已经有十辈人没来过圣城了。但隐秘者会通知他，这个家族的人什么时候出生，什么时候生病，什么时候死去。他在他们还活着时从来不去找他们，但是每多一个墓碑，他都会在那里留下一件祭物，以及一个问题：你会原谅我吗？
 
猩红战争没有夺走他们的生命，但是当圣城为那些被Vex和永夜夺走的生命恸哭时，萨瓦拉在为萨菲亚最后的后裔而悲泣。这一次，连能入土的尸体都没有。
 
现在，萨瓦拉坐在他的桌前。他手里的织针已因长期使用而磨损。他小心翼翼地拿着它们，回忆着当时她教他拿针，让他跟着她学的情景。 

他又抽出一段毛线，从头开始。

30225843.name: Phantasmal Shell
30225843.subtitle: "The Light provides." —Mithrax
30225843.subtitle_zh: “光能赐予我们所需。”——米瑟拉克斯
30225843.text:
Mithrax repeats the mantra to himself as he makes his way across the H.E.L.M. It was not long ago that this wing housed the Servitor that sustained the House of Light and aided the Vanguard in stopping the Endless Night.

But now, something altogether different lurks within these walls.
As he descends the stairs into the hangar bay, he sees it for the first time: the Crown of Sorrow, large and grotesque, seated ominously in the spot the Servitor once occupied. That is when he hears the voices.

"Miiiissssraaakssss," they hiss in unison.

Out of the corners of his eyes, he sees their shadows skittering along the walls and ceiling. Dregs. Vandals. Faces he vaguely recognizes. Names he barely knew or never learned.

"The Light provides." Even in his own mind, his voice sounds somehow smaller.

"Kell of Light… Captain of Death…"

They swarm toward him now, phantasmal Ether bleeding from wounds he inflicted in another life.

"We remember. We remember what you did. We remember who you are."

"The Light provides," he tells himself as a shiver runs down his back. "The Light provides. The Light—" 

"Misraaks?"

He spins around, Splicer Gauntlet poised to strike. Only when he sees Crow standing at the wing's entrance does he lower it.

"What's going on?" the Hunter asks.

"It is nothing," Mithrax lies. The voices are silent—their shadows, gone. But not forgotten. "Excuse me."

He pushes past Crow without another word, desperate to leave the past behind.
30225843.text_zh:
米瑟拉克斯一边穿行过应急后勤行动中心，一边念叨着口头禅。不久前，这座翼楼里还住着维系着光能氏族并帮助先锋阻止了永夜的魔眼。

而现在，一些完全不同的东西潜伏在这些高墙内。
当他走下楼梯进入机库时，他第一次见到了它：忧愁王冠，巨大而怪异，不祥地坐落在魔眼曾经占据的地方。就在这时他听到了那些声音。

“米…斯…拉…阿…克…斯”他们齐声发出嘶鸣。

他从眼角看到了他们的影子沿着墙壁和天花板掠过。堕落士兵。暴徒。他依稀认得的面孔。他几乎不知道或从未了解过的名字。

“光能赐予我们所需。”即使在他自己的内心里，他的声音听起来也有点小。

“光能凯尔…死亡队长…”

他们开始向他蜂拥而来，幻想的乙太从他在另一段生命中受到的创伤里不断渗出。

“我们记得。我们记得你做了什么。我们记得你是谁。”

“光能赐予我们所需，”他自言自语，后背一阵冷颤。“光能赐予我们所需。光能——” 

“米斯拉阿克斯？”

他转过身，熔岩臂铠摆出攻击姿态。直到他看到乌鸦站在翼楼的入口处时，才放松下来。

“怎么了？”猎人问道。

“没什么，”米瑟拉克斯撒了谎。那些声音沉寂了——他们的影子，消失不见了。但却难以忘怀。“失陪了。”

他一言不发地从乌鸦身边挤过，拼命地想把过去抛在脑后。

623842790.name: Eidolon Shell
623842790.subtitle: For Ghosts whose Guardians have no doubts to bind.
623842790.subtitle_zh: 供其守护者无疑会联结的机灵使用。
623842790.text:
//OWL COMM-chat4: Opn, Log, Midas-003//
//Archival Access Designation: VG-GREEN//

OWL-3-RaGo: Camrin, I read the report you sent on the link established between the Leviathan and the Lunar Pyramid. Some of these details are alarming.
