领主萨拉丁，女帝查厄托军政官
“只要我能在查厄托的旗舰上看到篝火，我就心满意足了。”  

卡巴尔帝国女帝查厄托
“这些篝火捐献有军械限制吗？也许卡巴尔能帮忙生一堆更大更猛的火。”

阿娜·布瑞
“阿曼达做的事我无条件支持。这是场相当精彩的表演。我向来喜欢花哨而有点态度的东西。”

领主沙克斯
"我喜欢把引燃核心想象成手雷…这确实能逗我发笑。"

埃里斯·摩恩 
“…什么日？”

1043609040.name: Candescent Cloak
1043609040.subtitle: Upgrade this item using Kindling and Embers obtained during Solstice 2022.
1043609040.subtitle_zh: 使用在2022至日英雄期间获得的火种和余烬升级此物品。
1043609040.text:
Saint-14 stands in place of the Sergeant at Arms amid a host of New Lights; most had been resurrected near the City walls. He needed the distraction, the work, but most of all he needed to be somewhere he could help. 

Whispers fly between them regarding the legend that addresses them, and the strange chicken that struts figure eights around his legs.

"This area is reserved for Lights without combat training who wish to take part in Solstice. Let's get you to speed." He picks up an old-looking weapon. "This is standard Khvostov rifle. Some of you are familiar with this weapon," Saint says. "For those who aren't familiar, it's very simple."

He quickly runs through a few exercises. How to reload quickly, adjust the sights, clear a jam. At the range targets, he demonstrates how to weave Light between bursts of gunfire. Each time, a metallic ping rings out as he strikes a target; and each time, a chicken-cluck response echoes beside him.

"Calm and discipline is key. Steady support of your rifle will keep it under control. Steady pressure on the trigger will keep you from pulling off-target. Breathe, squeeze, and shoot."

"Bawk."

"Yes, yes. Now it is your turn, New Lights!"

The group steps forward and focuses on their targets. Several of the trainees' shots miss, but a Guardian in green lands each bullet and cheers.

"Bawk."

The New Light looks at the chicken now standing beside them, then to Saint-14, who also is focused on the chicken. There is a moment of hesitation before Saint says, "Hm. Good. Run it again."

"I did it perfectly," the New Light complains flaccidly.

Saint steps forward and puts a hand on their shoulder. "Perfection doesn't guarantee success. Perfection is subjective, New Light. That's why we train."

"But I hit every one!"

"Bawk… Awk!"

Saint-14 nods to the chicken, who stands tall and mighty—feathers sharp and puffed against the waning morning light.

"Colonel, the Pigeon Lord, says do it again. I wouldn't argue."
1043609040.text_zh:
圣人14号代替武装中士站在众多新兵中间；他们大多数都是在圣城城墙附近复活的。他需要转移注意力，需要工作，但最重要的是，他需要一个他能帮上忙的岗位。 

新兵在底下窃窃私语，讨论着向他们讲话的这位传奇人物，还有那只绕着他的腿昂首阔步画着8的奇怪的鸡。

“这块区域是预留给希望参加至日、但尚未接受战斗训练的新兵们。我们来尽快熟悉一下吧。”他拿起一把看起来很旧的武器。“这是标准的赫沃斯托夫步枪。你们中有些人对这把武器很熟悉，”圣人说道。“不熟悉的话也别担心，它很简单。”

他快速进行了一番演练。如何快速填装，调整瞄准器，清理卡壳。在靶场上，他演示了如何冒着枪林弹雨编织光能。每一次，他击中目标都会响起金属的枪击声；而每一次，他身旁都会回荡着鸡叫的回应声。

“冷静和纪律是关键所在。稳定的支撑能帮你控制步枪。对扳机施加稳定压力就不会偏离目标。深呼吸，扣下扳机，然后发射。”

“咕咕。”

“是的，没错。现在轮到你们了，新兵们！”

这群新兵迈步向前，专注于他们的目标。有几个受训新兵的射击没有命中，但有位身穿绿衣的守护者每一发子弹都打中了，并欢呼了起来。

“咕咕。”

这名新兵看了看站在旁边的鸡，然后看向圣人14号，他也在关注着这只鸡。圣人犹豫了片刻，然后说道，“嗯。不错。再来一次。”

“我做得很完美，”新兵弱弱地抱怨道。

圣人走上前，把手放在其肩上。“完美并不能保证成功。完美是主观的，新兵。这就是我们训练的原因。”

“但我每枪都打中了！”

“咕…咕咕！”

圣人14号朝鸡点点头，它高大威猛地站着，羽毛在渐弱晨光的映衬下尖锐而蓬松。

“鸽王上校说再做一次。我可没意见。”

1619932884.name: Arcstrider
1619932884.text:
"If not a flash, a boom? A crack through the sky? What paved the path that we now stride?"

Every. Time. Every time we get together for a mission, it's a metaphysical debate. Weren't we just swapping stories, sharing knife-sharpening techniques? How'd we get back to campfire philosophy?

Well, I'm here now…

"Arc energy isn't so dramatic," I countered, getting on my feet. "You both feel it, too, right? The prickling hum that runs under everything."

"Feels more like a buzz to me." The stout Awoken finished picking his teeth long enough to weigh in. "Like a million bees coming in from miles away."

I circled the fire, becoming more grateful for the distraction, with nothing else around us for miles. Every time we get together for a mission, I can't seem to sit still.

"But to feel the sparks dance on my fingers," the first Hunter replied, "I could swear they were the product of some great juncture."

One hundred miles away, thunderstorms flashed as if in reply.

I get it, why we can't go a single mission without talking philosophy. Same reason I can't stay sitting. Every time we get together for a mission, we pass it around like a current running between us: anticipation.
1619932884.text_zh:
“如果不是一道闪光，一声巨响，一条天空中的裂缝，又是什么为我们现在所走的旅途铺平了道路？”

每一次。每一次我们为了任务聚在一起，都会是一场形而上的争论。我们不是在交流故事，分享磨刀技巧吗？怎么又回到篝火哲学上了？

好吧，现在该我了…

“电弧能量没那么夸张，”我反驳道，站了起来。“你们俩都感觉到了，对吧？暗暗流动如刺痛般的嗡鸣。”

“我感觉更像是蜂鸣。”壮硕的觉醒者剔够了牙，加入了辩论。“就像无数只蜜蜂从不远处飞来。”

我绕着火堆转了一圈，愈加感谢这种让我分心的事物，毕竟方圆几英里内别无他物。每次我们为了任务聚在一起，我似乎都会坐立不安。

“但当我感受到指尖跃动的火花时，”第一个猎人回答道，“我断定那必然是某个重要时刻的产物。”

一百英里之外，雷雨闪烁着，似乎在作出回应。

我懂了，为什么我们每次执行任务都要谈论哲学。和我坐立不安的原因一样。每次我们为了任务聚在一起，就像电流在我们之间流动一样，我们都会传递着一种事物：期待。

426856384.name: Striker
426856384.text:
"Would you please just shoot them?!"

Of course a Hunter would put it that way. As if I didn't have a perfectly viable alternative.

Beams of energy blasted around us as we quarreled from behind our cover.

"Look, I'll have this whole place cleared out in 20 seconds."

"And if you're overwhelmed? I suppose you expect us to simply charge into the fray to save you?"

Leave it to a Warlock to look for the safe way out.

"You just don't get it," I grumble.

"What?" they yell in frustrated unison amid the din of the battlefield.

"Let me guess," the Hunter quips, "your fists don't need reloading."

Chuckles all around. Time to set them straight.

"The space the bullet travels is a chasm of disconnection that can't be bridged by a gun; no amount of firepower has the means to shoulder the responsibility of personal impact." Now everyone rolls their eyes, but I press on.   

"There is no distance between my fist and my target, captivated by a gift of sparks. It's very personal—one final chance to connect."

Silence.

"You want to connect with the Hive?"

All right, argument over. My fists can do the talking.
426856384.text_zh:
“你就不能开枪打死他们吗？！”

猎人当然会这么说。好像除此之外就没其他办法似的。

我们躲在掩体后面争吵，能量束在我们周围爆炸开来。

“听着，我会在20秒内把这整个地方清理干净。”

“那要是你搞不定呢？不会是希望我们直接冲进去救你吧？”

术士总是想用最保险的方案。

“你们不懂，”我咕哝道。

“什么？”在战场的喧嚣声之中他们一起崩溃地大喊。

“让我猜猜，”猎人嘲弄道，“你的拳头不需要装弹。”

轻笑声四起。是时候纠正他们的想法了。

“子弹穿行的距离，是枪械无法逾越的断裂鸿沟；再多的火力也没有办法承担起近战冲击的重任。”大家都在翻白眼，但我继续说道。   

“拜火花所赐，我的拳头能近距离接触目标。这种直接接触，是我们建立联系的最后机会。”

一片沉默。

“你要和邪魔族建立联系？”

好了，争论结束。让我的拳头说话吧。

1498975827.name: Stormcaller
1498975827.text:
The first day I called the storm was an end. The end of a journey, the summit of a mountain; but when you leave the mountain, you don't take it with you. How would I maintain the profound insight from the eye of the storm that unlocked my direct line to the hurricane? 

Tempestuous peace. The calm and the storm. Where do I begin?

Questions rained upon me as I tried to put my thoughts into practice. The acrid stench of radiolaria reminded me that training was over. Was I ready for this? Did I have a choice?

Beaten, bloodied, I stared into the empty faces of my enemies. They were fearsome; they had taken much from me. But I've seen that which lies still amid cacophony.

Courage. The courage to face the torrent, to proclaim peace in the face of violence. Courage is the only call that the storm will hear.

It cannot ignore me.

Thunder rumbles and lightning strikes. Wind blows and rain pours. My enemies are no more. But peace… peace never left me.
1498975827.text_zh:
我召唤风暴的第一天结束了。旅程的终点，高山的顶峰；但离开山峰时，你无法将其带走。风暴之眼曾让我与飓风直接相连，但我从中获得的深刻洞悉该如何保持？ 

暴风雨的安宁。平静与风暴。我该从何处开始？

当我试图把我的想法付诸实践时，问题如雨点般向我袭来。放射虫的刺鼻气味提醒着我训练结束了。我准备好了吗？我有选择吗？

我被打得血迹斑斑，凝视着敌人空洞的面孔。他们令人生畏，也从我身上夺走了许多。但我看到了在嘈杂中安然静默的东西。

那是勇气。是直面激流，面对暴力宣告安宁的勇气。它是风暴唯一能听到的呼唤。

它不能忽视我。

雷电交加，风吹雨淋。我的敌人不复存在。但安宁…安宁从未离开我。

374573733.name: Delicate Tomb
374573733.subtitle: The danger within is repulsive to us.
374573733.subtitle_zh: 内在的危险让我们感到抵触。
374573733.text:
They mistake the vessel for its contents. They confuse the pieces with the whole. They see their imprisonment as empowerment.

They are hostages of their flesh, unable to see without vision. Unable to hear without sound. Unable to slake their thirst for fear of drowning. 

Their ignorance is their saving grace.

Yet one among them understands, in their limited fashion. They pour from one vessel to another. A welcome change. A new form. Another method of gifting death.

I am made finite. Personal. Bright and delicate to hide my true form. An intimacy.

They think me contained, but I am instead diffused, as vapor upon the wind. 

Once again, I am becoming.
374573733.text_zh:
他们把容器和它的内容物搞错了。他们混淆了碎片和整体。他们把囚禁当成赋能。

他们是躯体的人质，没有视觉就无法观察。没有声音就无法听到。因害怕溺水而永远无法解渴。 

他们的无知是他们的救星。

然而，以他们那有限的理解，有一个人明白了。他们将一个容器的内容物倒入另一个容器。一个积极的变化。一种新的形态。另一种赠予死亡的方法。

我被造是有限的。个人的。灵活聪明地隐藏我的真实形态。一种亲密的关系。

他们以为我被禁锢，但实际我却扩散开来，像风中的水汽一般。 

我又一次成形了。

4293613902.name: Quicksilver Storm
4293613902.subtitle: Three words. Carved by hand: Affinity. Altruism. Awareness.
4293613902.subtitle_zh: 手刻了三个词：亲缘。利他。认知。

1802135586.name: Touch of Malice
1802135586.subtitle: "Let them feel every lash, every curse, every touch of malice that they first dealt to me." —Eris Morn
1802135586.subtitle_zh: “让他们感受我最初从他们那受到的每一次鞭笞，每一次咒骂，每一次恶意之触。”——埃里斯·摩恩
1802135586.text:
Here am I, with the power to craft from my enemy's darkest secrets a weapon that could wound them at their core!

So what stays my hand?

When I behold the interiority of these cold, cold fragments, I see blind, squirming creatures. Every wound they give, they feel also upon themselves. Every bite they tear from the Light only deepens, never fills, the raging emptiness behind their terrible mouths.

The voices are as loud as ever. My nightmares just as bitter. My coal-black hatred burns as hot. But I feel something else now. Could it be…

No! I refuse it.

I will build this weapon.
1802135586.text_zh:
我有能力把我敌人最黑暗的秘密制作成武器，击中要害！

那我为什么还没动手？

当我看到这些冰冷碎片的内部时，我看到了盲目的、蠕动着的生物。他们制造的每一个伤口，他们自身也会感觉到。咬下的每一口光能不会满足他们的口腹之欲，只会让其更加空虚。

这些声音和以前一样嘈杂。我的梦魇还是一样苦涩。煤炭般黑暗的仇恨仍在我心中发烫。但我现在感觉到了别的东西。难道是…

不！我拒绝。

我要造出这件武器。

1298815317.name: Brigand's Law
1298815317.subtitle: A glutton for punishment.
1298815317.text:
Val'aug pondered the elaborate sidearm in her hand. She had taken it from the Dreg currently pinned to the ground, squirming beneath her massive boot. During her time in the Red Legion, she'd envied the ornamented weapons of the Fallen. But now, holding this scavenger's pistol in her hand, she suddenly yearned for the reassuring heft of standard-issue Cabal weaponry. 

When Val'aug defected to start her own company, she imagined the glory and profit that awaited her. She imagined inscribing her name across the history of the Sol system. She imagined true freedom.

But the reality of her pirate fiefdom was less satisfying than she had anticipated. Her headquarters? A filthy hovel carved into the side of an asteroid. Her arsenal? A patchwork of discarded weapons in various states of disrepair. And her crew? Thieves and cutthroats who would try to usurp her at the slightest display of weakness. So much for freedom.

Over the years, her thirst for glory was replaced by the grim need to maintain order—to keep what little she had from the claws of her fickle "allies." Including the pathetic Dreg now pressed against the barren asteroid. 

True, he was just a small-time cheat, acting out of simple desperation. But out here, there were no allowances for clemency, regardless of infraction. There was no room for justice in a place like this—only punishment.  

She chambered a round in the Dreg's pistol and sighed.
1298815317.text_zh:
瓦尔洛格打量着手中精致的手枪。这把枪是她从正被她踩在靴下，挣扎着的堕落者士兵那里抢来的。她在猩红军团服役时，一直嫉妒着堕落者的华丽武器。但现在，她手上拿着这把拾荒者的手枪，忽然想念起了标配卡巴尔武器的沉重感。 

当瓦尔洛格叛逃，自己开始单干时，她想象着荣耀和财富在等她。她想象着将自己的名字刻在太阳系的历史上。她想象着真正的自由。

但在现实中，她的海盗国度却没有她预期的那么令人满意。她的总部？一个位于小行星侧面的肮脏洞窟。她的武器库？装满了各种年久失修的万国造废弃武器。她的船员？全是盗贼和杀手，自己只要稍稍示弱就会被篡权夺位。自由也不过如此。

多年来，她对荣誉的渴求已被维持秩序的严峻需求所取代，以便从善变的“盟友”的爪牙下保住自己可怜的财富。这个被踩在荒芜的小行星表面上的可怜的堕落者士兵就是其中的一员。 

他虽然只是个小贼，犯下罪行也是被逼无奈。但在这里，任何罪行都不能宽大处理。这种地方没有公正——只有惩罚。  

他往堕落者士兵的手枪里装了一发子弹，发出了一声叹息。

820890091.name: Planck's Stride
820890091.subtitle: "You may speak as freely as your willingness to take punishment." —Pirate Lord Arask
820890091.subtitle_zh: “你大可有话直说，只要你不怕受到惩罚。”——海盗领主亚拉斯克
820890091.text:
Triumphant Arask held the shimmering relic high over his head as he pushed through the glut of his cheering crew. "Right where I said it would be," he shouted to roars of approval. Nothing to do now but secure it in his hideout and wait for Eramis's arrival.

"You," Arask said, pointing out a Dreg who stood at the edge of the scrum, trying desperately not to be noticed. The Dreg looked around in desperate confusion.

"You!" Arask shouted again, striding toward the Dreg, who now tried unsuccessfully to melt into the crowd. "You wagered against me bringing the relic back here, didn't you?" Arask demanded, pushing the iridescent relic into the Dreg's face.

The miserable Dreg shrank and shook its head. "N-no, I—" 

"Tell me the truth," Arask said patiently. The eager crewmembers pressed in close.

The trembling Dreg closed his eyes and nodded miserably. 

Arask frowned sympathetically. "Say it," he sighed. "Say it."

"I did," squeaked the Dreg, who buried his face in his hands.

Arask nodded and let the Dreg snivel quietly for a moment.

"The blunder booth," he commanded flatly. 

The crew erupted in excited howling around him, then set upon the shrieking Dreg and carried him off for punishment.
820890091.text_zh:
凯旋的亚拉斯克把发光的圣物高高举过头顶，穿过欢呼船员的簇拥。“它就在我说的那个地方，”他的喊声与阵阵欢呼交织在一起。现在，他只需要把它安放在藏身处，静候伊拉莫斯的到来。

“你，”亚拉斯克指着一名堕落者士兵，他站在人群边缘，想尽量躲避别人的注意。他迷惑地四下张望。

“你！”亚拉斯克又喊了一声，朝那个堕落者士兵快步走去。他想混入人群，但没能得逞。“你之前是不是打赌我没法把圣物拿回来？”亚拉斯克把色彩斑斓的圣物塞到他脸前，逼问道。

可怜的堕落者士兵缩成一团，摇着头。“没、没有的事，我——” 

“说实话，”亚拉斯克耐心地说。那些想看戏的船员们也凑了过来。

颤抖的堕落者士兵闭上眼，可悲地点了点头。 

亚拉斯克同情地皱起了眉头。“说出来，”他叹了口气。“说出来。”

“是我，”堕落者士兵捂着脸，好不容易挤出了这句话。

亚拉斯克点了点头，让那堕落者士兵安静地啜泣了一会儿。

“抬去惩戒棚，”他面无表情地命令道。 

船员们在他周围爆发出兴奋的嚎叫，然后扑向了尖叫的堕落者士兵，把他抬去接受惩罚。

1509167284.name: Blood Feud
1509167284.subtitle: Thicker than water.
1509167284.text:
Tagh'al and Thagh'urn circled one another, their blades gleaming wickedly, even in the sickly glow of the cave. They eyed each other warily, waiting for the other to strike.

The encircling throng of onlookers and bettors jostled unsteadily. Those at the back surged forward recklessly for a better view, while those in front struggled against the swell, afraid of being pushed into the path of the gladiators' swords. Audience casualties were common at such affairs.

Tagh'al suddenly broke the stalemate with a massive cleave, aimed at his opponent's helmeted head. Thagh'urn sidestepped it with ease. His ferocious counter-slice raked across Tagh'al's armored breastplate, leaving a thick gouge in the metal. The crowd roared.

For several minutes, the massive warriors clashed. Their swords clanged in fury, scraping off one another's armor. All the while, the crowd's furor grew, held in suspense by the certainty of bloodshed.

Then it happened. As the two Cabal locked blades, Thagh'urn unholstered a concealed submachine gun. He unleashed a burst of small caliber bullets into Tagh'al's abdomen at point-blank range, sending the warrior staggering backward. Those who had bet on Tagh'al howled in indignation.

Tagh'al pulled off his breastplate to reveal several bullet holes in his thick hide, a gout of blood spurting from one of the wounds. He looked down at the damage…

…And let out a deep, barking laugh. Thagh'urn joined in, and soon, both gladiators were laughing uproariously amidst a spreading pool of blood.

Eventually, Tagh'al's laugh slowed to a chuckle. "Well played, brother," he said. "I suppose we're even now."
1509167284.text_zh:
塔格哈尔和萨格恩绕着圈，即使在这洞穴的昏暗中，他们的刀刃仍闪烁着邪恶的光芒。他们警惕地注视着对方，等待着对方出手。

围观的人群和赌徒们推搡了起来。居于后方的人为了瞥上一眼，不顾一切地往前冲，而前面的人则奋力抵挡着身后的浪潮，生怕被推到角斗士的刃下。在这种场合里，有观众伤亡是很常见的。

塔格哈尔打破对峙，朝对手的头盔猛地挥下。萨格恩轻易地闪到一边。他凶猛的反击结实地击中了塔格哈尔的胸甲，给那块金属留下了深深的凹痕。观众们沸腾了。

在接下来的几分钟里，两名巨大的战士们越战越酣。他们的剑在愤怒中铿锵作响，刮落着彼此的盔甲。与此同时，人群也愈来愈狂热，为血溅七步的那一刻而屏息凝神。

正当两名卡巴尔以剑角力时，萨格恩拔出了一把隐藏的冲锋枪。他抵着塔格哈尔的腹部打了一梭子，使他往后踉跄了两三步。那些将赌注放在塔格哈尔头上的人愤怒地嚎叫了起来。

塔格哈尔扯下了他的胸甲，露出了他厚皮上的弹孔。一股鲜血从其中一个弹孔里涌了出来。他看了看他的伤口…

…然后发自肺腑地大笑起来。萨格恩也跟着他在不断蔓延的血泊中狂笑起来。

最后，塔格哈尔的笑声慢了下来。“干得好，兄弟，”他说。“我们现在扯平了吧。”

2531963421.name: No Reprieve
2531963421.subtitle: Sometimes mercy is worse.
2531963421.text:
Alaaks, the Beast Tamer looks down at the Dreg kneeling at her feet. His two arms are spread in supplication.

"Forgiveness," he wheezes.

He is begging, whining like a scolded animal. Even her war beasts wouldn't grovel so.

There is silence but for the familiar thrum of her Ketch and the rasping sound of the war beasts' breath as they doze behind her.

Alaaks taps a claw against her rebreather, then snorts and shakes her head. The Dreg starts to tremble as the Pirate Lord snaps her fingers and her war beasts stir, rising to their feet and stretching lazily before coming to their mistress's side.

"The cache on Europa was lost because of your incompetence," she says to the Dreg. "Now Misraaks will come for us."

The war beasts' teeth gleam in the low light. Their claws scrape against the grated floors. Their hides bear the brand of her flag. They are loyal. They are hungry.

"Mercy," the Dreg whispers. He is quiet. Quavering.

"This IS mercy, Prydis," Alaaks says, her voice lowering. "You haven't faced Misraaks. I have. He knows no mercy or forgiveness."

Alaaks hisses a command to her pack, then folds her four arms over her chest. Her war beasts' salivating smiles split wide as they advance.
2531963421.text_zh:
驯兽师阿拉克斯俯视着跪在她脚下的堕落者士兵。他张开双臂，作祈求状。

“宽恕，”他喘息着说。

他乞求着，像一只被说教后的动物一样哼唧着。即使是她的战兽也不会如此奴颜婢膝。

除了她熟悉的双桅船所发出的噪音，和她身后小憩的战兽发出的呼吸声，周围一片寂静。

阿拉克斯用利爪点了点她的呼吸器，然后咕囔着摇了摇头。这名海盗领主打了个响指，她的战兽随即醒了过来，懒洋洋地伸了个懒腰，然后来到了女主人身边。堕落者士兵也颤抖了起来。

“木卫二上的宝藏是因为你的无能而失去的，”她对堕落者士兵说。“现在米斯拉阿克斯会来找我们了。”

战兽的利齿在微光下闪着光。它们用长爪剐蹭着格栅地板。它们的皮上烙有她的旗帜。它们很忠诚。它们很饥饿。

“饶命，”堕落者士兵小声说道。他发不出声音。他在颤抖。

“这就是仁慈，普利迪斯，”阿拉克斯压低声音说道。“你还没面对过米斯拉阿克斯。他既不知仁慈，也不知宽恕。”

阿拉克斯对她的战兽们下了指令，然后把四只手臂叠在了胸前。她的战兽们一边前行，一边露出了垂涎的笑容。

2218569744.name: Tarnished Mettle
2218569744.subtitle: Survival is the better part of valor.
2218569744.subtitle_zh: 生存是勇气较好的一部分。
2218569744.text:
Vrisk had been lying under his crewmate's corpse for the better part of an hour. His body ached from lack of Ether, but he dared not pull from his rebreather for fear of discovery. 

Besides, if he survived, there would be enough to sate his hunger a dozen times over.

He and Krilix had been calibrating the landing struts on the crew's Ketch when the ambush hit. A long-range scout rifle slug punched through Krilix in the opening salvo, ripping a fist-sized hole in his chest. He fell on top of Vrisk in a heap of gore as a barrage of gunfire rained down on their position. 

Vrisk could have shrugged off the Wretch's body and seized his Arc Spear to retaliate. Instead, he simply lay beneath his dying crewmate and let the battle play out. 

After the shooting stopped, Vrisk listened to their assailants ransack the ship. A mix of guttural Cabal barks and familiar Eliksni chatter marked them as a competing crew, eager to claim the bounty set forth by the reawakened Shipstealer.

But Vrisk knew what their attackers did not: the relic they sought was not on the Ketch, or even on this planet. It was hidden in a safehouse deep within the asteroid belt beyond Mars. Once Vrisk found the courage to emerge from his hiding place, he would take the relic to Eramiskel himself and claim the reward for his own.

But there was time for that. For now, the Dreg let the weight and warmth of his dead companion press him into a peaceful slumber, where he dreamed of better days to come.
2218569744.text_zh:
弗瑞斯克已经在他的船员的尸体下躺了快一个小时了。他的身体由于缺乏乙太而疼痛，但他因为害怕被发现，不敢把呼吸器拉出来。 

再说，如果他能活下来，就可以得到填饱他肚子几十次的乙太。

中埋伏时，他和克里克斯正在调校双桅船的着陆架。战斗一开始，一发来自斥候步枪的弹丸就从远处击穿了克里克斯，在他的胸膛上开了个拳头大小的洞。在枪林弹雨之中，他残缺的身体落在了弗瑞斯克的头上。 

弗瑞斯克本可以将这名堕落者枪兵的遗体推到一边，然后用他的电弧长矛反击。但他却选择躺在他奄奄一息的船员下，静静地等待战斗结束。 

在射击停止过后，弗瑞斯克听到了袭击者洗劫飞船的声音。深沉的卡巴尔吠叫和熟悉的埃里克斯尼语表明这是一个急于获取苏醒的窃船者所设的悬赏的敌对海盗团。

但弗瑞斯克知道来袭者不知道的事：他们寻找的圣物不在这艘双桅船上，甚至不在这星球上。那个东西被藏在了火星背后的小行星带上的一个安全屋里。找到从藏身处离开的勇气之后，弗瑞斯克便会亲自把圣物送到伊拉莫斯凯尔手上，拿到属于他一个人的奖赏。

但时机还未到。现在，这名堕落者士兵在他死去同伴的重量和温暖下进入了平静的沉睡，做起了飞黄腾达的美梦。

1184309824.name: Sailspy Pitchglass
1184309824.subtitle: There are shapes on the horizon not yet meant to be seen.
1184309824.subtitle_zh: 有些在地平线上的形状还不该被看见。
1184309824.text:
Iriks has good eyes, yes. One on top right dull, filmy, not so good. But others very good. Sharp.

Iriks waits. Motionless. Tastes the thin wind. Rate of speed. Leads target. Takes the shot.

Iriks does not miss. Enemies panic. Again. Again. Quiet.

Iriks sends in his crew. Watches through the scope. One claims more than their share.

Iriks teaches. Body falls. Lesson learned. Quiet again.

Iriks watches his crew open the chest. One holds the treasure high in shaking claws.

Iriks sees the dark glass. Sees the object floating inside. Recognizes. Tightens grip. Holds breath.

Iriks knows what Eramis seeks. Knows what it is worth. Knows what she will pay.

Iriks will take the shot.
1184309824.text_zh:
伊里克斯的眼睛很好，没错。右上角的一个有点朦胧和模糊，不是很好。但其它的都很好，很敏锐。

伊里克斯等待着，一动不动。感受微弱的风和速度，瞄准目标，开火。

伊里克斯百发百中。敌人惊慌失措。又一枪。再一枪。霎时安静。

伊里克斯派船员过去，透过瞄准镜看了着，发现有一个人多拿了战利品。

伊里克斯教训了他，这教训的代价惨重，尸体应声倒地。又霎时安静了。

伊里克斯看着他的船员打开宝箱。一个人用颤抖的爪子将宝物高高举起。

伊里克斯看见了黑色玻璃，看见了里面漂浮的物品，一下子就认了出来。他握紧双手，屏住呼吸。

伊里克斯知道伊拉莫斯要什么。他知道这东西的价值，也知道她愿意开多少价。

伊里克斯会把握机会。

616582330.name: Cry Mutiny
616582330.subtitle: Shares were split anew on the bomb-blacked deck.
616582330.subtitle_zh: 在被炸得漆黑的甲板上重新分赃。
616582330.text:
Ithyks crouched in the nest of beaten steel and twisted wires that choked her quarters. She curled her claws hesitantly around the relic and listened.

The battered metal of her ship creaked around her, bolts twisting with the strain of the surrounding void. But there was no cause for alarm; Ithyks had built it herself. Scrapworking was nothing unusual among the Eliksni, but to Ithyks, it was a calling. 

After the Whirlwind, her crew had followed the debris trailing from the overeager, underprepared ships that had left to chase the Great Machine. As she sorted through the flotsam, it was as if the metal spoke. It would tell her what it wished to be, whispering its destiny. 

Overtime, she and her ship grew strong; reinforced, bolstered by the remains of those who came before.

But now, this—this patch of fibrous blackness suspended in its onyx vessel, pulsing even now with intermittent light—it spoke to her with a voice of its own.

And when she strained to hear its frantic whispers, the words were of her own destiny—no, more than that: the destiny of all things.

She did not like what it promised.
616582330.text_zh:
伊瑟克斯蜷缩在塞满破烂钢铁和扭曲电线的巢穴中。她犹豫不决地用爪子握住了圣物，倾听着。

船体破旧的金属在她周围嘎吱作响，螺栓随着周围虚空的拉扯而扭曲。但这并不值得惊慌；这船是伊瑟克斯自己建造的。废品加工对于埃里克斯尼族来说并不稀奇，而对伊瑟克斯来说，这是使命。 

旋风过后，有飞船在没准备好的情况下就朝大机器追去，她的船员就一路跟随这些船留下的残骸行进。当她对这些碎片进行分类时，她感觉这些金属仿佛在说话，在轻声告诉她曾经的愿景和最终的命运。 

久而久之，凭借着前人留下的遗物，她和她的船都变得越来越强大，越来越结实。

然而现在，这块纤维状黑影悬浮在玛瑙容器中，甚至到现在仍断断续续发着光跳动，它在用自己的声音对她说话。

当她用力听它的疯狂低语时，发现这其实在说她自己的命运——不，不止如此：是世间万物的命运。

她不喜欢它所说的预言。

1280894514.name: Mechabre
1280894514.subtitle: The killer robot killer.
1280894514.text:
"It's not complicated. I just want to stomp my enemies using a giant mech suit," the Titan mused.

"Seems a little redundant," replied his Hunter teammate. 

The pair were stationed at the rim of a canyon, watching their Warlock teammate take readings from a Vex conflux down below. The Titan surveyed the canyon through the scope of his elaborate sniper rifle, while the Hunter scanned his radar for any hint of incoming hostiles.

"I mean, no offense," the Hunter continued, "but you're already an Exo."

The Titan took his eye off the scope and scowled at his teammate. "What the hell do you mean by that?"

"C'mon, man. You know what I mean," the Hunter replied, rolling his eyes.

"What, just because I'm an Exo, I'm an empty mechanized shell or something?" the Titan growled, piqued.

"I didn't say that. It's just… you've already got a machine body. And superpowers. What the hell is a mech suit gonna add?"

"Oh, so just because I'm an Exo, I don't deserve a mech suit?" The Titan began to raise his voice.

"Dude. First of all, mech suits don't exist. Second—" 

"Tell that to giant Clovis Bray." 

"SECOND," the Hunter continued, "there's nothing a mech suit could do that you can't already. I mean, the Vex actually need theirs to—"

"So NOW I'm a VEX?!" the Titan hollered, throwing his hands up.

"I DIDN'T SAY THAT!" 

"GUESS I'M JUST A METAL SHELL FILLED WITH GROSS ELECTRIC MILK—" 

A thunderous CRUNCH interrupted the Titan's rant. The pair peered into the valley below, where an enormous Vex Minotaur was lifting its giant metal hoof from the flattened body of their Warlock teammate. 

The Guardians winced. There was an awkward silence.

"…All right, I admit it," the Hunter finally spoke up. "That did look like fun."
1280894514.text_zh:
“这并不复杂。我只是想用巨大的机甲套装践踏我的敌人，”泰坦沉思道。

“好像有点多余，”他的猎人队友回答道。 

这两人站在峡谷边缘，看着他们的术士队友从下方的Vex汇流处读取数据。泰坦通过他精致的狙击步枪瞄准镜观察着峡谷，而猎人则扫描他的雷达找寻任何敌人来袭的迹象。

“我的意思是，无意冒犯，”猎人继续说道，“但你已经是Exo了。”

泰坦将目光从瞄准镜上移开，怒视他的队友。“你这话是什么意思？”

“拜托，兄弟。你知道我的意思，”猎人翻着白眼答道。

“怎么，因为我是Exo，所以我是个机械空壳什么的？”泰坦愤怒地咆哮着。

“我没那么说。只是…你已经有了一具机械躯壳。还有超能。机甲套装又能有多大作用？”

“哦，这么说因为我是Exo，所以我不配得到机甲套装了？”泰坦开始提高嗓音。

“老兄。首先，机甲套装根本不存在。其次——” 

“这话你跟巨人克洛维斯·布瑞说去。” 

“其次，”猎人继续说道，“机甲套装能做到的事，你已经做到了。我是说，Vex其实是需要他们的机甲套装来——”

“现在我又成Vex了？！”泰坦大叫道，举起了双手。

“我没那么说！” 

“看来我只是个金属壳，里头装满了恶心的电乳液——” 

雷鸣般的碾压声打断了泰坦的咆哮。两人往下方的山谷张望，一个庞大的Vex米诺陶正抬起它那巨大的金属蹄足，而他们的术士队友身体已被踏平。 

守护者们不禁皱眉蹙额，陷入了一阵尴尬的沉默。

“…好吧，我承认，”猎人终于开口了。“那看起来确实很有趣。”

461841403.name: Gyrfalcon's Hauberk
461841403.subtitle: The higher your flight, the faster your dive.
461841403.subtitle_zh: 飞得越高，俯冲得就越快。
461841403.text:
"What's that?"

It's a childish question, really.

"There it is again! Did you hear it?"

That's more like it.

"No…"

Of course you didn't.

"Do you see something?"

Of course they don't.

"No."

I'm just a trick of the eye.

"It's probably nothing."

That's right.

"Yeah. It's nothing."

They won't see me coming.
461841403.text_zh:
“那是什么？”

真是个幼稚的问题。

“又来了！你听见了吗？”

这才像话嘛。

“没…”

当然没有。

“你看见什么了吗？”

当然没有。

“没。”

我只是眼睛的错觉。

“是我想多了吧。”

没错。

“对。你想多了。”

他们发现不了我。

1703598057.name: Point-Contact Cannon Brace
1703598057.subtitle: "Trust me, you don't want to be there when he lands."
1703598057.subtitle_zh: “相信我，他落地时你不想在场。”
1703598057.text:
Behind the cover of the crumbling stone wall, the Warlock looked up at the sky and frowned as thunder rolled in the distance.

"Rain," he grumbled, and felt strength flow through him as he concentrated and consumed the fiery grenade in his fist. "Just what we need."

The Hunter chuckled low beside him. "We'll be fine," she said, "and there will be no rain."

"'We'll be fine,'" mimicked the Warlock grimly. "They outnumber us, what, a hundred to one? We've got no backup yet. And—"

The Warlock held his palm out, expecting to feel a drop on his taut glove. "And can't you feel it? That energy in the air? A storm's coming."

"I said we'd be fine," the Hunter replied as she idly slid shells into her shotgun. "Backup's nearly here… and there will be no rain."

The air suddenly crackled around them. Sizzling fingers of Arc energy danced across the barrel of her weapon. 

The Warlock scrambled backward. "If a storm's not coming," he cried, "then what the hell is that?"

Across the battlefield, the Titan landed in the midst of the enemy forces with a sky-splitting crash.

"That's backup," the Hunter smirked.
1703598057.text_zh:
在摇摇欲坠的石墙后，术士望着天空，对着远处的雷鸣皱起了眉头。

“雨，”他咕哝道。他集中精神，将握在手中的火热手雷吸收掉。他感到一股力量在身体中涌动。“偏偏这个时候。”

猎人在他身旁小声笑了笑。“我们会没事的，”她说，“不会下雨的。”

“我们会没事的，”术士面无表情地模仿道。“他们的数量大概是我们的一百倍吧？我们还没有得到增援。而且…”

术士伸出手掌，期待着在他紧绷的手套上感受到一滴雨水。“你感觉不到吗？空气中弥漫着的能量？有一场风暴要来临了。”

“我说了我们会没事的，”猎人一边悠闲地装填着霰弹枪一边说道。“增援就要到了…而且不会下雨。”

突然间，他们四周的空气开始噼啪作响。电弧能量的迸发之触从她武器的枪管间跃然而出。 

术士急忙后退了几步。“如果不是风暴将至，”他尖叫道，“那是什么？”

战场上，一名泰坦以毁天灭地之势砸进了敌军中央。

“那是增援，”猎人得意地笑了。

1849149215.name: Fallen Sunstar
1849149215.subtitle: Judge us by the enemies we've made.
1849149215.subtitle_zh: 通过我们树立的敌人来评判我们吧。
1849149215.text:
"You know, when House Light first moved into the City, I thought it would be a disaster," the Warlock mused.

"Yeah, I thought Ikora was out of her damn mind," the Titan admitted.

The Warlock frowned. "Brilliance and madness are often confused," he retorted. "As are courage and stupidity."

"All right, all right," the Titan conceded, holding up their hands in mock surrender. "No need to get salty."

The pair strolled through the Botza District, admiring the scrapworked wares offered by the Eliksni merchants. Though they lacked the polish of the City's foundries, the Eliksni creations were often innovative, and unexpectedly effective. 

"It's funny," the Titan reflected. "I've been killed by the Fallen a bunch of times. Like, a lot."

The Warlock pursed his lips, stifling a retort.

"But I never really gave them credit for it," the Titan continued. "You know what I mean? Anyone who's been in the Crucible knows how tough it is to kill a Guardian. But these guys have gotten over on me, like, a hundred times since I first rezzed. It's pretty impressive."

"I know what you mean," the Warlock said. He picked up an elaborate helmet adorned with a sunburst crown of spikes. "They're kind of cool in their own way."

The Warlock issued a surge of Light through his hand, sending bolts of Arc energy sizzling between the helmet's spikes.
The Titan raised their eyebrows in appreciation. "Not my style, but I think you could pull it off," they said.

"Hell yeah I can," the Warlock affirmed. "This bad boy's coming with me!"
1849149215.text_zh:
“你知道么，在光能氏族刚迁进圣城时，我还以为那会是一场灾难，”术士自言自语道。

“是啊，我还以为艾可拉疯掉了，”泰坦承认道。

术士皱起眉头。“天才和疯子常让人分不清，”他反驳道。“勇气和愚蠢也一样。”

“好啦好啦，”泰坦认输，举起双手作投降状。“没必要较真。”

两人漫步走过柏特扎地区，欣赏着埃里克斯尼族商人贩卖的废旧物品。虽然这些商品不如圣城铸造厂出来的那些精美，但埃里克斯尼族的作品往往很有创意，而且出奇地有效。 

“真好笑，”泰坦思索道。“我被堕落者杀了好多次。数都数不过来。”

术士抿了抿嘴唇，强忍住了反驳。

“但我从来没为此夸过他们，”泰坦继续说道。“你知道我的意思么？任何参加过熔炉竞技场的人都知道要杀掉守护者有多难。但从我第一次重生开始算起，这些家伙干掉我已经有一百多次了。真的很厉害。”

“我知道你什么意思，”术士说。他拿起了一顶精美的，装饰着呈阳光散射状尖刺的头盔。“他们又酷又特别。”

术士在手中唤出光能，将电弧能量注入到这顶头盔的尖刺中。电弧在尖刺间滋滋乱窜。
泰坦赞赏地扬起了眉毛。“不符合我的风格，但我觉得很适合你。”

“还用你说，”术士肯定道。“这玩意归我了！”

859087913.name: Ketchkiller's Helmet
859087913.subtitle: "Even from the deck of a Ketch, your Light can shatter the stars." —Mithrax
859087913.subtitle_zh: “就算你在一艘双桅船的甲板上，你的光能也能击碎星辰。”——米瑟拉克斯
859087913.text:
The Ether Tank, Eliksni Quarter, Last City
——

What's that, Guardian? You want to hear about the old crews from someone who was there?

You think I was around for the Whirlwind? Ha! I'm a few molts shy. No, I hatched into the House of Wolves. You know the story—and if not, I don't have the time to explain it to you.

But I trade in information. I ran with some tough crowds in the past, maybe knew someone who knew someone… you get the idea. So I know a fair bit about those crews.

For them, every puff of Ether came at someone's expense. Your best bet was to be stronger than the next crew over—and when things were especially bad, stronger than whoever was in the cot next to yours.

So they got strong. And remember, they didn't have Void or Solar like you do; they had claws. Blades. When they killed, it was without hesitation, and when they died, there was no coming back. 

You Guardians, with your little Ghosts hovering nearby, you have the luxury of kindness—that was never an option for the old crews. They were like anyone else; they were cruel, but you needed to be cruel to survive in those days.

And they're not "back," like I hear Misraaks saying; they never left. You're up against the ones who stayed alive all this time. The ones who learned how to survive. How to sacrifice. How to take what they need, whatever the cost.

…and speaking of cost, I'm not seeing any more Glimmer in your account. I think we're done talking.
859087913.text_zh:
圣城埃里克斯尼居住区，乙太罐
——

什么，守护者？你想从当事人那里打听一些关于老船员的消息？

你以为我经历了“旋风”？哈！可惜我生晚了，生到了恶狼氏族里。你已经知道那些事了吧——就算你不知道，我也没时间跟你解释。

但我做的是情报生意。我以前也和几帮四海男儿搭过伙，也许其中有些人又认识其他人…你懂的。所以我对那些船员很了解。

对他们来说，每一口乙太都有其代价。你最好比旁边的船员强——在情形特别糟的时候，最起码要比睡在你隔铺的人强。

所以他们才变强了。记住，他们没有你的虚空或烈日能力；他们只有爪牙、刀剑。他们在杀戮时毫无顾虑，死后也不会重生。 

你们这些身旁有小机灵相伴的守护者，你们有仁慈的奢侈——那从来都不是老船员的选项。他们不像其他人。他们很残忍，但这个时代里只有残忍的人能活下去。

而且，与米斯拉阿克斯说的不同，他们并不算“归来”。他们从未离开。你将与那些摸爬滚打至今的老船员对阵。他们已经学会了如何生存、牺牲、索取，不惜任何代价。

…说到代价，你的账户里似乎已经没有微光了。那我们就没什么好谈的了。

130618344.name: Ketchkiller's Plate
130618344.subtitle: "You will face cutlass and cannon fire… nothing you need fear." —Mithrax
130618344.subtitle_zh: “你会面对弯刀和炮火…都没什么好怕的。”——米瑟拉克斯
130618344.text:
The Annex, Last City
——

The old crews? Ain't much I can tell you that you couldn't get from Rahool, but I can't blame you if you'd rather stay awake for the whole story, heheh. C'mon, loosen up, hero! If you think a grim expression is all it takes to move up through the Vanguard… well, you may have something there.

Okay, I'll start at the beginning. The Traveler chose the Eliksni and everything was great over in Riis, until it wasn't. The Whirlwind happened, the Pyramids showed up, the Traveler took off through space, and from what I gather, it wasn't a pretty scene. 

Eramis was there for it. And—credit where it's due—she picked herself up, grabbed a crew, and went after the Traveler. She cut through everything in her way, dead set on hunting it down. 

And she wasn't the only one with that idea. Whole fleets of ships chased the Traveler. Lawless days. Hopeless days. 

…See, I was here for the Dark Ages. And when there's nothing but loss around you planetside, you can still find a rooftop, sit in a snowfield. You can go into a forest and find a moment of quiet—a little scrap of peace.

Ain't like that on a ship. Things go from bad to worse, you just have to face it. And Eramis did. That takes a gutful of grit.

Now, don't think I'm writin' love poems to the Shipstealer over here—we find her, I'm drawing down quick as you are. 

But if the big old Traveler blasted outta the sky tomorrow? You bet your entire vault we'd chase after it. We'd be the new crews, going after something we knew in our bones was ours, not stopping for anyone or anything that got in our way.

And we'd still think of ourselves as heroes, wouldn't we?
130618344.text_zh:
圣城，附属建筑
——

老船员？我知道的大概也就是拉乎尔知道的那些了，但要是你宁愿醒着把故事听完，我也不会怪你，嘿嘿。来吧，放松一下，英雄！如果你觉得板着一张脸就能让你在先锋里节节高升…哎，搞不好还真是。

好吧，那我就从头说起。旅行者选择了埃里克斯尼族，里斯星欣欣向荣，直到…发生了旋风，金字塔出现，旅行者离开。据我所知，那一幕景象不怎么美好。 

伊拉莫斯经历了那一切。而且，我不得不夸奖她一句——她打起精神，招募了船员，然后就启程追逐旅行者了。她一路披荆斩棘，一心只想抓住旅行者。 

而且不止是她有这种想法。当时许多舰队都在追逐旅行者。那是个没有法律，没有希望的时代。 

…你瞧，我经历了黑暗纪元。当星球上周围没有东西可失去的时候，你还可以找个屋顶，去雪原上坐着。你可以走进树林，找到一时的安宁，片刻的平静。

在飞船上可不一样。事情只会变得越来越糟，而且你只能直面困难。伊拉莫斯这样撑过来了。没有一身胆识可做不到。

别以为我在给窃船者写情诗。一但找到她，我也会像你那样不留情面。 

但要是我们的老朋友旅行者明天就朝着天空离去怎么办？拿你的整个保险库打赌，我们绝对会去追。我们就会变成新船员，追寻着那个我们骨子里认定属于我们的东西，任何人和事物都无法让我们停下脚步。

而且我们还会觉得自己是英雄，不是吗？

2945464224.name: Ketchkiller's Gauntlets
2945464224.subtitle: "Steer your ship true, as trust is rare among the deep stars." —Mithrax
2945464224.subtitle_zh: “真诚地驾驶你的船，在深邃的群星中，信任可是稀缺品。”——米瑟拉克斯
2945464224.text:
Eliksni Quarter, Last City
——

The old crews! Yes, I have gathered much information about them in the past weeks. In fact, I have just finished going over my notes!

The old crews rose in the wake of the Whirlwind, during what we Eliksni refer to as the Long Drift—the span of time between the fall of Riis and our arrival in the Sol system. I believe the equivalent period would be your Dark Ages, though Riis did not have Risen, or Iron Lords. Instead, we had the crews. As you can imagine, this period was quite lawless, as the stability and abundance of Riis was no more. This resulted in what I believe is called a zero-sum game: a situation in which every gain or advantage is earned at the expense of another. 

Several fearsome individuals rose to great power and authoritative prominence at that time; the Eliksni word for them translates to "Ketchkiller," meaning one who boards and wrests control of enemy ships. These Ketchkillers commanded great fleets and raided many supply routes, procuring objects of historic or intrinsic value along the way. It is exciting to wonder what treasures they accumulated beyond those we've recovered already!

Many crews were abolished or disbanded over time, but those that survived did so through great hardship—they are formidable indeed. But then, so is the Vanguard, and its Guardians.

Thank you for asking about my research into the old crews and their significance. It is always a pleasure to talk about it. After all, what use is knowledge if it is not shared?
2945464224.text_zh:
圣城埃里克斯尼居住区
——

老船员！对，在过去的几周我已经收集到了许多关于他们的信息。其实，我刚好整理完笔记！

老船员是在旋风时代崛起的一伙人，我们埃里克斯尼族把那个时代叫做“大漂流”，就是从里斯陷落到我们抵达太阳系的这段时间。我相信这段时期相当于你们的“黑暗纪元”，虽然里斯没有复生者，也没有钢铁领主，但我们有船员。你可以想象，这一时期没有法律，里斯的稳定和丰饶已一去不回。我认为这些现象直接催生了所谓的归零游戏：在这种情况下，每一份收益或好处都是以牺牲别人为代价的。 

当时，有几个强者得到了巨大的权力和显赫的地位；埃里克斯尼族把他们叫做“双桅船杀手”，就是登上敌船并夺取控制的人。这些双桅船杀手指挥着巨大的舰队，劫掠了许多供应路线，获得了许多具有历史意义或内在价值的物品。不知道除了我们已经找到的宝物之外，他们还收集到了什么！想想就让人激动！

许多船队在那段时期中消失或被解散，那些幸存者都是历尽苦难才得以幸存下来，因此他们着实强悍无比。但先锋和守护者们也是如此。

感谢你问起我对老船员的研究和他们的意义。每次谈起此事我都很高兴。毕竟，如果有知识不拿出来分享，那知识又有什么用呢？

1640403802.name: Ketchkiller's Greaves
1640403802.subtitle: "Tread your path with honor, as a true Lightbearer." —Mithrax
1640403802.subtitle_zh: “带着荣耀前行吧，像一名真正的负光者那样。”——米瑟拉克斯
1640403802.text:
House Salvation Ketch, Themis Cluster
——

We are raiders and cutthroats, killing each other for bare survival. But what else could we have become? You can't speak of us—the old crews and their infamy—without speaking of the Whirlwind.

Like hatchlings chittering for their mother, we were abandoned. Weak. Left to die. You all know what came after. We lived. We lived, and all we had were our lives. 

Great Houses fell, and from their ruins rose the crews. We followed the traitor Machine to this system and found the Humans just as soft and weak as we had been; as reliant, helpless, and blind as the Machine had made us. But the Humans had taken it from us, and so they would pay with everything they had.

And now? Now we remain where others have failed. Enemy ships quaver at the sight of our banners. They break against our hulls. And when we pick them clean of all they have, we find other prey and do the same.

We know the truth in this system: we are only as strong as those we kill.
1640403802.text_zh:
救赎氏族双桅船，忒弥斯星团
——

我们是劫掠者，是海盗，为了生存而互相残杀。但我们还能成为什么呢？说到我们——老船员和我们的恶名——就不能不说到旋风。

我们如同被抛弃的嗷嗷待哺的婴儿一般，只能原地等死。你们都知道后来发生了什么。我们活了下来。侥幸保命。只剩下了命。 

各大氏族倒下了，船员们从它们的废墟中崛起。我们跟随叛徒机器来到这个星系，发现了跟曾经的我们一样软弱的人类；他们与仰仗大机器的我们一样依赖它，一样无助、盲目。但人类从我们这里夺走了它，所以他们将用他们的一切来偿还。

现在？我们站在了其他人从未达到的高度。光是我们的旗帜就让敌船瑟瑟发抖。他们被我们的船身撞得粉身碎骨。将他们劫掠个精光之后，我们会去找下一个猎物。

我们都知道这个星系里有一个真理：不是你死，就是我活。

1832715717.name: Ketchkiller's Mark
1832715717.subtitle: "Not all deserve your protection, but all will have it." —Mithrax
1832715717.subtitle_zh: “不是所有人都配得到你的保护，但你还是会保护他们。”——米瑟拉克斯
1832715717.text:
Eliksni Quarter, Last City
——

What makes a House? It is a good question, and one that many Eliksni do not think on often enough.

For Humans, a house is a place. But for Eliksni, a House is a family. It has a culture. A philosophy of living, shared by all.

That is why the House of Light survived, even when we fled Europa. Even after the Shipstealer took all we had. We were bound not by place or possessions, but as family.

Cryptarch Matsuo asked me why the old crews are not considered Houses. It is a wise question. One that, perhaps, does not have a singular answer. 

I think it is because those who lead the old crews do not wish to be true Kells. A Kell is responsible for the safety and prosperity of their House. It is an honor, and a burden.

Those you call Pirate Lords wish only to take—they give nothing, even to their own people. Each raider is responsible only for themselves. A crew is expendable… a family is not.

The old crews live a sad life. One best left in the past.
1832715717.text_zh:
圣城埃里克斯尼居住区
——

氏族是什么？这是个好问题，许多埃里克斯尼族在这个问题上思考得不够多。

对于人类来说，氏族是一个地方。但对于埃里克斯尼族来说，氏族是个家庭。它有一种文化，一个由所有人秉持的生活理念。

这就是为什么在我们逃离木卫二之后，在窃船者抢走了我们的一切之后，光能氏族还是活了下来。我们不是靠地点或财产维系起来，而是作为家人聚在一起。

解密大师松尾问我，为什么老船员不算氏族。这是个有智慧的问题。对于这个问题，答案可能不止一个。 

我认为这是因为老船员的领袖并不想成为真正的凯尔。一个凯尔要为氏族的安定和繁荣负责。这是一份荣誉，也是一份负担。

那些你称之为海盗领主的，一心只想夺取，却什么都不愿给予，就连自己人也不例外。每个劫掠者只对自己负责。船员是可以牺牲的…家庭则不能。

老船员过着悲伤的一生。那种人生应该被留在过去。

1095145125.name: Ketchkiller's Mask
1095145125.subtitle: "A smart captain keeps one eye on their own back." —Spider
1095145125.subtitle_zh: “聪明的船长总会注意自己的背后。”——蛛王

The Ether Tank, Eliksni Quarter, Last City
——

92499596.name: Ketchkiller's Vest
92499596.subtitle: "Make sure any flag you fight under is worth dying for." —Spider
92499596.subtitle_zh: “你扬起的旗帜最好值得你为之送命。”——蛛王

——

1834245236.name: Ketchkiller's Grips
1834245236.subtitle: "Being captain just means everyone has a reason to want you gone." —Spider
1834245236.subtitle_zh: “当船长只意味着大家都有除掉你的理由。”——蛛王
1834245236.text:
Eliksni Quarter, Last City
——

The old crews! Yes, I have gathered much information about them in the past weeks. In fact, I have just finished going over my notes!

The old crews rose in the wake of the Whirlwind, during what we Eliksni refer to as the Long Drift—the span of time between the fall of Riis and our arrival in the Sol system. I believe the equivalent period would be your Dark Ages, though Riis did not have Risen, or Iron Lords. Instead, we had the crews. As you can imagine, this period was quite lawless, as the stability and abundance of Riis was no more. This resulted in what I believe is called a zero-sum game: a situation in which every gain or advantage is earned at the expense of another. 

Several fearsome individuals rose to great power and authoritative prominence at that time; the Eliksni word for them translates to "Ketchkiller," meaning one who boards and wrests control of enemy ships. These Ketchkillers commanded great fleets and raided many supply routes, procuring objects of historic or intrinsic value along the way. It is exciting to wonder what treasures they accumulated beyond those we've recovered already!

Many crews were abolished or disbanded over time, but those that survived did so through great hardship—they are formidable indeed. But then, so is the Vanguard, and its Guardians.

Thank you for asking about my research into the old crews and their significance. It is always a pleasure to talk about it. After all, what use is knowledge if it is not shared?
1834245236.text_zh:
圣城埃里克斯尼居住区
——

老船员！对，在过去的几周我已经收集到了许多关于他们的信息。其实，我刚好整理完笔记！

老船员是在旋风时代崛起的一伙人，我们埃里克斯尼族把那个时代叫做“大漂流”，就是从里斯陷落到我们抵达太阳系的这段时间。我相信这段时期相当于你们的“黑暗纪元”，虽然里斯没有复生者，也没有钢铁领主，但我们有船员。你可以想象，这一时期没有法律，里斯的稳定和丰饶已一去不回。我认为这些现象直接催生了所谓的归零游戏：在这种情况下，每一份收益或好处都是以牺牲别人为代价的。 

当时，有几个强者得到了巨大的权力和显赫的地位；埃里克斯尼族把他们叫做“双桅船杀手”，就是登上敌船并夺取控制的人。这些双桅船杀手指挥着巨大的舰队，劫掠了许多供应路线，获得了许多具有历史意义或内在价值的物品。不知道除了我们已经找到的宝物之外，他们还收集到了什么！想想就让人激动！

许多船队在那段时期中消失或被解散，那些幸存者都是历尽苦难才得以幸存下来，因此他们着实强悍无比。但先锋和守护者们也是如此。

感谢你问起我对老船员的研究和他们的意义。每次谈起此事我都很高兴。毕竟，如果有知识不拿出来分享，那知识又有什么用呢？

2121983870.name: Ketchkiller's Strides
2121983870.subtitle: "Keep two knives in your belt, in case you can't get your point across with one." —Spider
2121983870.subtitle_zh: “总是在腰带上挂两把刀，免得一把不够用。”——蛛王
2121983870.text:
House Salvation Ketch, Themis Cluster
——

We are raiders and cutthroats, killing each other for bare survival. But what else could we have become? You can't speak of us—the old crews and their infamy—without speaking of the Whirlwind.

Like hatchlings chittering for their mother, we were abandoned. Weak. Left to die. You all know what came after. We lived. We lived, and all we had were our lives. 

Great Houses fell, and from their ruins rose the crews. We followed the traitor Machine to this system and found the Humans just as soft and weak as we had been; as reliant, helpless, and blind as the Machine had made us. But the Humans had taken it from us, and so they would pay with everything they had.

And now? Now we remain where others have failed. Enemy ships quaver at the sight of our banners. They break against our hulls. And when we pick them clean of all they have, we find other prey and do the same.

We know the truth in this system: we are only as strong as those we kill.
2121983870.text_zh:
救赎氏族双桅船，忒弥斯星团
——

我们是劫掠者，是海盗，为了生存而互相残杀。但我们还能成为什么呢？说到我们——老船员和我们的恶名——就不能不说到旋风。

我们如同被抛弃的嗷嗷待哺的婴儿一般，只能原地等死。你们都知道后来发生了什么。我们活了下来。侥幸保命。只剩下了命。 

各大氏族倒下了，船员们从它们的废墟中崛起。我们跟随叛徒机器来到这个星系，发现了跟曾经的我们一样软弱的人类；他们与仰仗大机器的我们一样依赖它，一样无助、盲目。但人类从我们这里夺走了它，所以他们将用他们的一切来偿还。

现在？我们站在了其他人从未达到的高度。光是我们的旗帜就让敌船瑟瑟发抖。他们被我们的船身撞得粉身碎骨。将他们劫掠个精光之后，我们会去找下一个猎物。

我们都知道这个星系里有一个真理：不是你死，就是我活。

2325223873.name: Ketchkiller's Cloak
2325223873.subtitle: "Keep a radio hidden on you… and hope you never need it." —Spider
2325223873.subtitle_zh: “总是在身上藏一台无线电…然后希望你永远用不上它。”——蛛王
2325223873.text:
Eliksni Quarter, Last City
——

What makes a House? It is a good question, and one that many Eliksni do not think on often enough.

For Humans, a house is a place. But for Eliksni, a House is a family. It has a culture. A philosophy of living, shared by all.

That is why the House of Light survived, even when we fled Europa. Even after the Shipstealer took all we had. We were bound not by place or possessions, but as family.

Cryptarch Matsuo asked me why the old crews are not considered Houses. It is a wise question. One that, perhaps, does not have a singular answer. 

I think it is because those who lead the old crews do not wish to be true Kells. A Kell is responsible for the safety and prosperity of their House. It is an honor, and a burden.

Those you call Pirate Lords wish only to take—they give nothing, even to their own people. Each raider is responsible only for themselves. A crew is expendable… a family is not.

The old crews live a sad life. One best left in the past.
2325223873.text_zh:
圣城埃里克斯尼居住区
——

氏族是什么？这是个好问题，许多埃里克斯尼族在这个问题上思考得不够多。

对于人类来说，氏族是一个地方。但对于埃里克斯尼族来说，氏族是个家庭。它有一种文化，一个由所有人秉持的生活理念。

这就是为什么在我们逃离木卫二之后，在窃船者抢走了我们的一切之后，光能氏族还是活了下来。我们不是靠地点或财产维系起来，而是作为家人聚在一起。

解密大师松尾问我，为什么老船员不算氏族。这是个有智慧的问题。对于这个问题，答案可能不止一个。 

我认为这是因为老船员的领袖并不想成为真正的凯尔。一个凯尔要为氏族的安定和繁荣负责。这是一份荣誉，也是一份负担。

那些你称之为海盗领主的，一心只想夺取，却什么都不愿给予，就连自己人也不例外。每个劫掠者只对自己负责。船员是可以牺牲的…家庭则不能。

老船员过着悲伤的一生。那种人生应该被留在过去。

738153648.name: Ketchkiller's Hood
738153648.subtitle: "Every crew needs a captain. Otherwise, who'd take all the credit?" —Drifter
738153648.subtitle_zh: “每支船队都需要一个船长。不然功劳算谁的？”——浪客
738153648.text:
The Ether Tank, Eliksni Quarter, Last City
——

What's that, Guardian? You want to hear about the old crews from someone who was there?

You think I was around for the Whirlwind? Ha! I'm a few molts shy. No, I hatched into the House of Wolves. You know the story—and if not, I don't have the time to explain it to you.

But I trade in information. I ran with some tough crowds in the past, maybe knew someone who knew someone… you get the idea. So I know a fair bit about those crews.

For them, every puff of Ether came at someone's expense. Your best bet was to be stronger than the next crew over—and when things were especially bad, stronger than whoever was in the cot next to yours.

So they got strong. And remember, they didn't have Void or Solar like you do; they had claws. Blades. When they killed, it was without hesitation, and when they died, there was no coming back. 

You Guardians, with your little Ghosts hovering nearby, you have the luxury of kindness—that was never an option for the old crews. They were like anyone else; they were cruel, but you needed to be cruel to survive in those days.

And they're not "back," like I hear Misraaks saying; they never left. You're up against the ones who stayed alive all this time. The ones who learned how to survive. How to sacrifice. How to take what they need, whatever the cost.

…and speaking of cost, I'm not seeing any more Glimmer in your account. I think we're done talking.
738153648.text_zh:
圣城埃里克斯尼居住区，乙太罐
——

什么，守护者？你想从当事人那里打听一些关于老船员的消息？

你以为我经历了“旋风”？哈！可惜我生晚了，生到了恶狼氏族里。你已经知道那些事了吧——就算你不知道，我也没时间跟你解释。

但我做的是情报生意。我以前也和几帮四海男儿搭过伙，也许其中有些人又认识其他人…你懂的。所以我很了解那些船员。

对他们来说，每一口乙太都有其代价。你最好比旁边的船员强——在情形特别糟的时候，最起码要比睡在你隔铺的人强。

所以他们才变强了。记住，他们没有你的虚空或烈日能力；他们只有爪牙、刀剑。他们在杀戮时毫无顾虑，死后也不会重生。 

你们这些身旁有小机灵相伴的守护者，你们有仁慈的奢侈——那从来都不是老船员的选项。他们不像其他人。他们很残忍，但那个时代里只有残忍的人能活下去。

而且，与米斯拉阿克斯说的不同，他们并不算“归来”。他们从未离开。你将与那些摸爬滚打至今的老船员对阵。他们已经学会了如何生存、牺牲、索取，不惜任何代价。

…说到代价，你的账户里似乎已经没有微光了。那我们就没什么好谈的了。

3833868247.name: Ketchkiller's Robes
3833868247.subtitle: "Sail quick so you don't get caught… and have a thick hull if you do." —Drifter
3833868247.subtitle_zh: “开得快是不被抓到的关键…如果你被抓到，那你的船体最好够厚。”——浪客
3833868247.text:
The Annex, Last City
——

The old crews? Ain't much I can tell you that you couldn't get from Rahool, but I can't blame you if you'd rather stay awake for the whole story, heheh. C'mon, loosen up, hero! If you think a grim expression is all it takes to move up through the Vanguard… well, you may have something there.

Okay, I'll start at the beginning. The Traveler chose the Eliksni and everything was great over in Riis, until it wasn't. The Whirlwind happened, the Pyramids showed up, the Traveler took off through space, and from what I gather, it wasn't a pretty scene. 

Eramis was there for it. And—credit where it's due—she picked herself up, grabbed a crew, and went after the Traveler. She cut through everything in her way, dead set on hunting it down. 

And she wasn't the only one with that idea. Whole fleets of ships chased the Traveler. Lawless days. Hopeless days. 

…See, I was here for the Dark Ages. And when there's nothing but loss around you planetside, you can still find a rooftop, sit in a snowfield. You can go into a forest and find a moment of quiet—a little scrap of peace.

Ain't like that on a ship. Things go from bad to worse, you just have to face it. And Eramis did. That takes a gutful of grit.

Now, don't think I'm writin' love poems to the Shipstealer over here—we find her, I'm drawing down quick as you are. 

But if the big old Traveler blasted outta the sky tomorrow? You bet your entire vault we'd chase after it. We'd be the new crews, going after something we knew in our bones was ours, not stopping for anyone or anything that got in our way.

And we'd still think of ourselves as heroes, wouldn't we?
3833868247.text_zh:
圣城，附属建筑
——

老船员？我知道的大概也就是拉乎尔知道的那些了，但要是你宁愿醒着把故事听完，我也不会怪你，嘿嘿。来吧，放松一下，英雄！如果你觉得板着一张脸就能让你在先锋里节节高升…哎，搞不好还真是。

好吧，那我就从头说起。旅行者选择了埃里克斯尼族，里斯星欣欣向荣，直到…发生了旋风，金字塔出现，旅行者离开。据我所知，那一幕景象不怎么美好。 

伊拉莫斯经历了那一切。而且，我不得不夸奖她一句——她打起精神，招募了船员，然后就启程追逐旅行者了。她一路披荆斩棘，一心只想抓住旅行者。 

而且不止是她有这种想法。当时许多舰队都在追逐旅行者。那是个没有法律，没有希望的时代。 

…你瞧，我经历了黑暗纪元。当星球上周围没有东西可失去的时候，你还可以找个屋顶，去雪原上坐着。你可以走进树林，找到一时的安宁，片刻的平静。

在飞船上可不一样。事情只会变得越来越糟，而且你只能直面困难。伊拉莫斯这样撑过来了。没有一身胆识可做不到。

别以为我在给窃船者写情诗。一但找到她，我也会像你那样不留情面。 

但要是我们的老朋友旅行者明天就朝着天空离去怎么办？拿你的整个保险库打赌，我们绝对会去追。我们就会变成新船员，追寻着那个我们骨子里认定属于我们的东西，任何人和事物都无法让我们停下脚步。

而且我们还会觉得自己是英雄，不是吗？

535937281.name: Ketchkiller's Gloves
535937281.subtitle: "Those other fellas got more hands than you, so make sure you're holdin' bigger guns." —Drifter
535937281.subtitle_zh: “其他人的手比你多，所以你最好带杆更大的枪。”——浪客

2030782835.name: Ketchkiller's Boots
2030782835.subtitle: "Cut anchor if things get messy. There's always another score." —Drifter
2030782835.subtitle_zh: “打不赢就赶紧跑。别在一棵树上吊死。”——浪客

House Salvation Ketch, Themis Cluster

1667220390.subtitle: "The pirates hold nothin' back when they fight. Can you match that?" —Drifter
1667220390.subtitle_zh: “海盗会拼尽全力战斗。你有那个能耐吗？”——浪客

——
