A gardener and a winnower set out their chairs and play a game of flowers. The flowers know only that they grow or wither, struggle or flourish. Sometimes, they are touched by one hand or the other, and that influence is the closest they will know of the divine.

A flower and a flower spread their leaves to the sun above. (Remember that the sun is also a metaphor: a thing said beautifully, winnowed down to poetry, when the truth is too vast to put in words at all.) They jostle for space, each competing to be the pinnacle of their shape. One flourishes. One withers. Is it the fault of the flower or the fault of its position?

A gardener and a winnower sit down to play a game called Possibility. This is a game about a garden, which is to say that it is also a game about flowers, just as a game about a living being must also be a game about organs and bacteria.

A gardener and a winnower collaborate to create a protein. Whose hand is it in the design, that shortens one life to extend the rest?

It is the winnower that discovers the first knife, but it is not done without the gardener. This, too, is a tradition: a knife does not come to exist without something that must be cut. A woody stem, a colored petal, a vital vessel. The first victims of the blade.

All of these are true.

All of these are false, for metaphor simplifies as the knife does. It pares incalculable concepts into shapes your wrinkly little brains can comprehend. The weight of billions and the simple curve of a planet give you pause, and how then are you to be expected to grasp the forces that created your nth-removed creator?

So the stories woven with utmost delicacy in and around the falsehoods are, after it all, true. There was never any option for the knife to not exist in the garden: it was only ever a matter of time and opportunity.

And as for the shape of the knife itself—

No. That is enough.

I will tell you of gardens.

They are domesticated things, made in a form. As soon as something is called a garden, it is shaped. The plants require the hand of a gardener, for they have become weak and dependent on tender care. They require the hand of a winnower, to cut away the dross, for they are too incapable to do it themselves. In absence of a hand, either the flowers themselves must rise up to wield the knife, or the garden will resolve to meaningless wilderness.

You will say, "But there are plants that can walk! There are seeds that must be scorched by fire to know growth! Existence is more complex than a simple dichotomy between growth and withering, and there is more in heaven and on earth than is dreamt of in this philosophy!"

And I will tell you, clearly:

There can be no gardens without knives.
3429296256.text_zh:
一段与隐匿在阴影之中，看不清的人友好交谈的幻梦。它留下了一块匪夷所思的数据碎片来标记它的逝去。

以下是一朵花所知道的事情。

（一朵花可以知道任何事情，这是一种只能接受为隐喻的措辞，但不断达到完美的精度是很难的，不是吗？那么就改成，以下是叶绿体和色素的集合所能知道的事情。）

太阳的方向。

雨水的存在。

根茎的缠结。

另一株植物的忧虑。

园丁的双手，无论它们是在修剪、移植还是捣碎。

一朵花没法知道更多事情了。但花园的现实是广阔而荒凉的。花不可知篱笆；花不可知小径。然而，有一个无限的宇宙花园，花朵虽然无法理解，但它依然真实地存在…

让我们再试一次。如果你听过，就叫我停下：一个园丁和一个扬场工坐下来玩了一个超脱于时间和造物之外的游戏。听过吗？

好。那我们就达成一致了。这个比喻站得住脚。我们来复述一下。

一个园丁和一个扬场工把他们的椅子摆好，玩起了花朵游戏。花朵只知道自己在生长或枯萎，挣扎或繁盛。有时，它们会被一两手触碰，这种影响是它们所知的最接近神性的感受。

一朵花和另一朵花向头顶的太阳舒展自己的叶子。（要记住，太阳也是一种隐喻：当真理博大到无法用语言表达时，就可以用优美的言辞，提炼成诗歌。）它们互相争抢着生存空间，都想成为自己形态的巅峰。一朵繁盛了。一朵枯萎了。这是花的错还是其位置的错？

一个园丁和一个扬场工坐下来玩一个叫做“可能性”的游戏。这是一个关于花园的游戏，也是关于花朵的游戏；正如一个关于生物的游戏必定与器官和细菌游戏有关一样。

一个园丁和一个扬场工合作创造了一种蛋白质。这设计是出自谁手，能缩短某个生命来延长其余的生命？

是扬场工发现了第一把刀，但没有园丁是做不到的。这，也是一个传统：没有必须切割的东西，刀就不会存在。木质的根茎，彩色的花瓣，重要的导管。刀锋的第一批受害者。

所有这些都是真的。

所有这些都是假的，因为隐喻就像刀一样被简化了。它把无法计算的概念简化成你那满是皱纹的小脑袋所能理解的形态。数十亿的重量和行星的简单曲线已让你无法理解，你怎么可能掌握创造你的第n个已故造物主的力量呢？

因此，在谎言之中或其周围精心编织的故事，终究，是真实的。刀根本不可能不存在于花园里：这只是时间和机会的问题。

而至于刀本身的形态——

不。这就足够了。

我会告诉你关于花园的事。

它们是被驯化的东西，被塑造成某种形式。某件事物一旦被称为花园，它就塑形了。植物需要园丁的手，因为它们已经变得虚弱，需要悉心照料。它们需要扬场工的手来把糟粕丢弃，因为它们自己太无能而没法亲自动手。要是没有一只手，要么花朵必须自己奋起来挥舞刀子，要么花园就会变成毫无意义的荒野。

你会说，“但是有植物会走路！有种子必须经火烧焦才知道生长！存在比生长和枯萎之间的简单二分法更为复杂，天地间有很多东西是这种哲学想象不到的！”

而我会明确告诉你：

没有刀就没有花园。

1729973944.name: Strand Log I
1729973944.text:
…but there is no point in lingering on my restriction from front-line efforts. Rather, I am dedicating my efforts to the understanding of this peculiar force the Guardian has stumbled into.

It is unknown to our local hosts, so they have been of limited help. Green energy returns few helpful results in accessible Vanguard databases—there are some limited notes on Weapons of Sorrow, of course, and Hive magics have a distinctive yellowish-green hue, but the quality of the visible effect is different. As is, naturally, the effect.

But, all the same, it is not a power of the Light. Their Ghost was certain about that. 

To sum up what is known:

• This power manifests with a specific symbol-set: green, thread or strings, knots. It is worth noting that there never seems to be a single thread, but rather a collection of them, whether in parallel or in tangle.

• This power carries an impressive capacity for destruction, but causes a sort of rebound or exhaustion, the nature of which is not fully clear. It has not yet appeared lethal to the self, but it is being wielded by a Guardian fully empowered. Lethality means little in that context if it does not strike the Ghost as well, which this does not.

• The Guardian is the only one who has wielded this power to date. One sample is insufficient to draw full conclusions about the capacity required in a wielder. We certainly know by now that no existing power of Light is required to use a power of Darkness, only willingness to participate in the required rituals…

• The Guardian reported a sense of connection, a perception of the greater whole. I include this as relevant, more than likely related to the concept of multiple strings.

• We do not yet know enough.

The enemies here on Neptune have put significant effort into inhibiting known paracausal powers. This new one may be precisely what is needed to gain an upper hand and keep it. But something uncontrolled and unknown, the nature of which is not yet fully understood, is unwise to wield indiscriminately.

I could return to someplace the source of this energy has been reported and seek to touch it myself, but… I hesitate. I do not know why.
 
Practical study via the Guardian first. Ontological and paracausal study once the current trouble has been dealt with.
1729973944.text_zh:
…可是纠结于限制我进行一线工作是没有意义的。我宁可致力于理解守护者无意中发现的这种特殊力量。

我们的本地主人对此一无所知，所以他们能提供的帮助有限。绿色能源在可访问的先锋数据库中也没返回多少有用的结果——当然，在忧愁武器上有一些有限的注释，邪魔族魔法有着独特的黄绿色调，但视觉效果的质量不一样。很自然，效果也是不一样。

但无论如何，它都不是一种光能之力。其机灵对此深信不疑。 

总结下已知的情况：

• 这种力量以特定的符号集展现：绿色、丝线或绳线、缠结。值得注意的是，似乎从来没有出现过单根丝线，而总是它们的集合，无论是并行还是纠缠在一起。

• 这种力量具有十分惊人的破坏能力，但会引起某种反弹或衰竭，其性质尚不完全清楚。它还未显示出对使用者的致命性，但它正受到一位完全赋能的守护者操控。在这种情况下，杀伤力没什么意义，除非它能同时打击机灵，而它确实做不到。

• 守护者是迄今为止唯一操控过这种力量的人。一个样本不足以得出关于操控者所需能力的完整结论。我们现在无疑清楚，使用暗影力量并不需要现有的光能力量，只需要愿意参加必要的仪式…

• 守护者上报了一种联系的感觉，一种对更大整体的感知。我将其纳为相关项，很有可能与多条绳线的概念相关。

• 我们的了解还不够深。

海王星上的敌人付出了巨大的努力抑制已知的超因果力量。这种新的力量可能正是占据并保持优势所需要的。但是，在尚未完全了解其性质的情况下，任意地操控不受控制且未知的东西，并不是明智之举。

我可以回到这个上报过的能量源头所在地，尝试亲自去触摸它，但…我犹豫了。我不知道为什么。
 
先通过守护者进行实践研究吧。等目前的问题得到解决后，再进行本体论和超因果研究。

1729973947.name: Carding
1729973947.text:
Shadow Legion moving through the streets. Boxy formation, a few scouts ahead. Two heavy hitters—Colossi. Even in silhouette against Neomuna's bright lights, the shapes of their cannons are distinctive, weighing down their steps and progress.

The Titan steps out to block their way. There is a power here—a place where something new and vibrant runs close to the skin of the world, so close she could just reach out and touch it.

So she does.

The brilliant city wakes up. Potential and connection string a network of understanding along the streets, and she understands everything. Understands how the scouts will come out of the next intersection down to try to flank her, understands the movement of the Shadow Legion's formation, how one soldier and the next are all connected. A beautiful dance of the inextricably linked.

She wraps those links around her fists and charges into the fray. They scatter like pins, like mice with the cat among them. It's perfect. She tears through Legionary after Legionary, catches a hum along the threads that tells her to move—spins a full hundred-eighty degrees and arches back, swipes out, balletic and instinctive. A Colossus falls.

And then she thinks: How did she know to do that?

Now, she is trying too hard to anticipate, feels warning and motion coming from all sides and reacts—but consciously, in the realm where she has to think too hard about every move she makes, puts her half a second behind. Step here and punch there, and the threads are humming, harmony becoming warning becoming discord as the Titan realizes she doesn't know which way to leap.

Fire snakes toward her, and a heavy shield comes around, and all the threads slip away.

She misses a few moments in oblivion. The next thing she knows, her Ghost is hunkered close, a vibrant touch of Light pulling her up to a whole body, a hale mind. The sense of potential still thrums there, a heartbeat under the surface, a promise in the net of battle.

Desperately, the Titan scrabbles for it again, but strands break in her grasp—the Legion is too close, and she wants too much, too fast. It's going to take too long to breathe and find again that perfect harmony she had. To say nothing of reaching for the Light—her nerves are rattled, her mind blank.

The Colossus remaining charges up his cannon. Her Ghost bumps against her helm, and she takes the only action she can think of: she flees, Ghost cupped in her hand and her favorite sword melted useless on the city street behind them.
1729973947.text_zh:
暗影军团穿过街道。四四方方的队形，前面有几个侦察兵。两个重击手装甲兵。即使是在内欧姆那明亮灯光的映衬下，他们大炮的形状依然别具特色，重压着他们的脚步和进程。

泰坦走出来挡住了他们的去路。这里有一种力量——全新的、充满活力的东西与世界的肌肤紧密相连，近得她伸手就能触及。

她确实这么做了。

明亮的城市苏醒了。潜能和联系沿着街道串起了一张理解的网络，她理解了一切。理解了侦察兵如何从下一个十字路口出来试图包抄她，理解了暗影军团的队形移动，一个士兵和下一个士兵是如何联系在一起的。一段万千链环的美妙舞蹈。

她把那些链环缠绕在她的拳头上，冲进了战斗。他们像大头针一样散开，好似一群被猫冲散的老鼠。完美。她撕裂了一个又一个的军团士兵，听到丝线上传来的嗡嗡声，告诉她该移动了——旋转一百八十度，向后拱身，滑动扫击，芭蕾舞般唯美而又出乎本能。一个装甲兵倒下了。

随后她心想：她是怎么知道该这么做的？

现在，她开始过于努力地去预测，有意地感知来自四面八方的警告和移动并做出反应。必须对自己每一步行动都仔细思考，让她慢了半秒钟。踏足这里，击打那里，丝线嗡嗡作响，和谐声变成警告，化作不协和音，泰坦意识到她不知道该往哪边跳了。

火焰蜿蜒着向她逼近，厚重的护盾包围了她，所有的丝线都溜走了。

她失去了随后一些时间的记忆。反应过来时，她的机灵正降到附近，一股充满活力的光能之触将她拉进一具完整的身体，一个健全的思维里。潜能的感觉仍在那里回响，表面之下的心跳，战网之中的预示。

绝望之中，泰坦再次摸索着寻找，但她手中的丝线断了——军团士兵离她太近，而她想要的太多，太快。她需要很长时间才能呼吸并再次找到她曾有过的那种完美和谐。更不用说伸手去够光能了——她神经紧张，头脑一片空白。

剩下的装甲兵在为他的大炮充能。她的机灵碰撞着她的头盔，她采取了她唯一能想到的行动：她逃了，机灵托在她的手里，她最喜欢的刀剑融化在了他们身后的城市街道上。

1729973946.name: Strand Log II
1729973946.text:
We are calling this power "Strand." The threads of the world as it is woven, if the conscious universe could be considered to be a tapestry. Further analysis and data have suggested that the wielder of Strand begins to see, simply put, connections. Between allies, between enemies. It is a force that is always present, but wells to the surface more strongly in certain locations. Perhaps places many people think about, or where many beings have passed by. (Note: Analyze these "sources" in concert with the Cloud Strider. They may be able to provide more locational context.)

The true power of Strand lies not in the fact of the connection alone, but in the way such a power allows the manipulation of those connections. To make them something physical and then pull on it, or break it, or tie it into a knot. Or to unravel it entirely.

Strand is not without danger, although that should not be unusual to Guardians. Those who take up the banner of Stormcaller, for instance, have their own storied contention with the storm, and the Void was unilaterally regarded as dangerous by the Vanguard for many years. Strand's danger comes from the very act of taking hold of those threads—like many powers, the closer one comes to the source, the more likely the source may act on the wielder.

This danger is no product of Darkness. Or rather, only insomuch as wildfires are a product of Light: a natural consequence. That aspect of Darkness which revels in destruction, which encourages the easy entropy for the pursuit of power—it is nowhere to be found here. It may not even be truly part of Darkness…

I have touched Strand myself now. Carefully—I am too aware of mortality, but I must understand the power further if I am to hope to instruct the Guardian in turn. They acted as lightning rod while I experimented, and the backlash clung to them instead.

What a strange feeling, to be so aware of one's size in the spectrum of existence! It is the natural instinct to try to steer that, to take any control at all, no matter how much. Whatever can be done to feel as though you are not wholly adrift, lost in something huge and all-encompassing.

But precisely at the moment one tries to grasp for control, the weave becomes a devouring snarl.
1729973946.text_zh:
我们称这种力量为“缚丝”。如果意识宇宙可以被认为是一幅织锦的话，这就是编织世界的丝线。进一步的分析和数据表明，缚丝操控者开始看到了，简而言之，那些联系。在盟友之间，在敌人之间。这是种始终存在的力量，但在某些位置会更强烈地涌现出来。也许是许多人想念的地方，或是许多人经过的地方。（注：与云端行者协同分析这些“来源”。他们也许能够提供更多的位置信息。）

缚丝的真正力量并不在于联系本身，而在于这种力量允许操纵这些联系的方式。把它们变成有形的东西，然后拉扯它，或是扯断它，或是把它打个结。或是完全瓦解它。

缚丝并非没有危险，尽管这对守护者来说算不上什么稀罕事。举个例子，那些肩扛唤雷旗帜的人，对风暴有着众所周知的专属论调，多年来，先锋单方面认为虚空是危险的。缚丝的危险之处在于抓住这些丝线的行为——就像许多力量一样，越接近源头，源头就越有可能作用于操控者。

这种危险不是暗影的产物。或者更确切地说，正如野火不是光能的产物：它也同样只是自然的结果。暗影以毁灭为乐，鼓励追求力量的轻易熵变的那一面——在这里找不到。它甚至可能并不是暗影的一部分…

我现在已经亲身触碰过缚丝了。我太了解死亡，所以行事谨慎，但如果我想反过来指导守护者，就必须进一步了解这种力量。我进行实验时，他们充当了避雷针，结果是他们受到了反冲。

对自己在存在光谱中的大小有如此清楚的认知，真是种奇怪的感觉！自然的本能促使你试图去引导，去掌控一切，不管能掌控多少。你会做任何事，只要能让你感觉到，自己并没有完全迷失在某个硕大无比、包罗万象的事物中。

但恰恰在你想要抓住进行掌控的时候，编织就化作了毁灭缠结。

1729973949.name: Roving
1729973949.text:
Neomuna is a wonderful place for a Hunter to run. This Hunter, specifically.

Here the activity of life runs close to the surface—like an invisible river, like a migration of birds, like the moment of breathless motion just before the lightning strikes. Here Strand twines through his fingers, strong as a rope and just as flexible, and all he has to do is keep running. And why would he ever want to stop?

The pounding of feet. The exhilaration of free-fall. The snap as he catches hold of the weave of existence itself and swings up again with all the momentum of his dive. In motion, as he turns, he catches brass and gold reflecting vibrant city lights, realizes there are Vex in the streets—

Are they, too, part of the same flow? They echo in the weave nevertheless, like flowers on the surface of the rushing river. The Hunter bounds from one building to the next, never stopping, and finds effortlessly the place where all those Vex will converge, drops a roiling knot into the midst and sails on by.

How wonderful, simply to move, and never stop.

And then, later: when the exhilaration has run its course and he's agreed to do some little work in the service of science, he perches at the top of Artifact's Edge, that towering drop-off on Nessus. There's a safe lift down, but no Hunter he knows has ever bothered to take it, rather bounding along in their free-fall, daredevil way.

On Neptune, in Neomuna where that artifact of Darkness shores up the existence of the city itself, finding the weave was easy. Here…

Here on Nessus, it's perhaps not as close to the surface, but now he knows what he reaches for and, by the Darkness, it knows him as well. The Hunter wraps his hands in the beautiful ropes of the world's loom and vaults into emptiness. Laughter and Strand buoy him up at once, delight and freedom and a wonder at the vastness of existence.

Easier to learn the trick of it, where the Veil is close and enveloping. But of course Strand is everywhere. How could it not be?
1729973949.text_zh:
内欧姆那是猎人奔跑的好去处。尤其是，这位猎人。

在这里，生命的活动贴近表面——就像一条看不见的河流，就像鸟儿的迁徙，就像闪电来临前让人喘不过气来的那一刻。在这里，缚丝缠绕在他的手指上，像绳子一样结实，也一样灵活，他所要做的就是继续奔跑。他又为什么会想停下来呢？

脚步的重击声。自由落体的兴奋感。他抓住存在本身的编织用俯冲的全部动力再次摆动起来时的迅捷。在移动过程中，他转过身，看到青铜和黄金反射着充满活力的城市灯光，意识到街头有Vex出没——

它们也是同一水流的一部分吗？然而，它们在编织中回响，就像奔流河面上的花朵。猎人从一个建筑跳到另一个建筑，没有停息，毫不费力地找到了所有那些Vex将会聚集的地方，在中间放下一个翻滚的绳结，继续前行。

多好啊，只需移动，永不停息。

而在那之后：当兴奋感殆尽，他同意为科学出一些力时，他息停在神器止境的顶端，涅索斯上那高耸的陡坡。那里有条安全的下降通道，但他认识的猎人中没有一个人愿意尝试，而都是以自由落体的冒险方式一路跃进。

在海王星上，在暗影神器支撑着城市本身存在的内欧姆那，要找到编织是很容易的。在这里…

在这涅索斯，它也许没有那么靠近表面，但现在他知道他的手在伸向什么，而且，暗影在上，它也知道了他。猎人将双手包裹在世界纺织机上美丽的绳索中，跃入了虚空。笑声和缚丝立刻让他振作，他感到喜悦和自由，对宇宙浩瀚惊叹不已。

在面纱近在四周之处，更容易学会缚丝技巧。不过它当然是无处不在的。难道不是吗？

1729973948.name: Strand Log III
1729973948.text:
I have been conducting research among the local population, specifically regarding the "children's story" Nimbus told us, regarding the river of souls. I had a suspicion that there might have been other versions, or versions with better recorded provenance.

Willingness to participate in this research has been mixed, as have the results. It seems to be an endemic concept rather than a religious belief, and no one has been able to say where it comes from, save that a parent or teacher told it to them at some point. Some respondents have mentioned a river of stars—perhaps the Milky Way galaxy—and some have cited windstreams and weather formations, but the majority of respondents adhere to the "river of souls" construct. 

All things come from the river, and all return to it. The river may split and meet again. Other things may fall into it and change its course, but nevertheless it continues. In time, even mountains are worn down before it. 

Naturally, it is easiest to view this as an allegory for control of life. In the end, rivers are impossible to control. A person may swim or boat, but never take hold of the river to steer the course of the water itself. And it is impossible not to see the relationship to Strand, which slips away the moment a person tries to grasp too tightly.

I wonder about Strand. About its appearance. We can see the origins of the Stasis power on Europa, and the concept of a cosmic ice to oppose stellar fire fits very neatly in a certain sort of paradigm. Even that idea of stillness and control suits freezing, a slowness of atoms whether or not it is in truth a power of "ice." There is a certain weight to the perception of an "element."

If Strand had been shaped through the lens of Neomuna, surely it should have been some cosmic water instead, something that flows and gives way only to rise again. There are certainly combat styles to support this in old records.

But this power that has never before been used in this way came to one Guardian first, and I conjecture that they may have unconsciously given it form. I wish I had seen it! What would "connection" have appeared as? Now, of course, we know the shape of this power: it is green, it weaves itself in strings. As other Guardians begin to learn it, they too slot it into these positions in their minds. Whatever advances they come to are already framed verdant and tangling.

All the same, I cannot help but wonder about the nascent, formless thing it was before we reached out to it, and it reached back.
1729973948.text_zh:
我一直在当地居民中进行研究，特别是有关宁博思告诉我们的“儿童故事”，有关灵魂之河的信息。我怀疑可能有其他版本，或者出处记录得更好。

参与这项研究的意愿不一，研究结果也是如此。这似乎是一个风土概念，而非一种宗教信仰，除了父母或老师在某个时候告诉他们之外，没有人能够说出它来自哪里。一些受访者提到了一条群星之河——也许是银河系——其他人则提到了气流和天气形成，但大多数受访者坚持“灵魂之河”的说法。 

万物来自河流，又都归于河流。河流也许会分叉，然后再度汇合。其他事物也许会落入其中并改变它的河道，但无论如何它继续流淌着。假以时日，即使高山也会在它面前被冲平。 

自然，这很容易被看作是一则掌控生命的寓言。到头来，河流是无法被掌控的。一个人也许能游泳或划船，但永远别想抓住河水来控制水流。这与缚丝的关联也显而易见，抓得太紧，就会溜走。

我很好奇缚丝。好奇它的外观。我们可以看到木卫二上冰影的起源，宇宙之冰对抗恒星之火的概念非常符合某种范式。就连静止和控制的想法也与冷冻，这种原子的缓慢很相符，不管它是否真的是“冰”的力量。对某种“元素”的感知是有一定的权重。

如果缚丝是通过内欧姆那的视角塑造的，那么它肯定本应是某种宇宙之水，某种流动、消失后只为再次涨高的东西。在旧记录中肯定有战斗风格来印证这一点。

但是从未以这种方式使用过的这种力量首先出现在了一个守护者身上，我猜想他们可能是无意识地赋予了它形式。真希望我有见到那一幕！“联系”会是什么样子？现在，我们当然知道了这种力量的形状：它是绿色的，它把自己编织成绳状。随着其他守护者开始学习它，他们也把它插放入他们思维中的这些位置。不管他们进展到什么程度，都已经搭建起了翠绿缠结的框架。

尽管如此，我还是禁不住想知道我们触及它之前，那个原本新生而无形的东西的样子。

1729973951.name: Spinning
1729973951.text:
The Warlock sits with hands in the water and hums to themself. Several of the local feral pouka come and go as time passes, bumping up against fingers or vaulting out of the water to become airborne and curious, spattering drops everywhere. The Warlock doesn't mind, really. It's impossible to feel alone when dozens of creatures are hanging on their every move.

Perhaps meditation is meant to be solitary, but this is comforting.

A year ago, they were running with a fireteam, a tight-knit group of six that had each other's backs. Till the stars died, the lot of them had thought. It would always be like this.

Now there is one Warlock sitting in a flock of pouka, in an impossible settlement on a miraculous planet. And they miss that sense of companionship desperately—

There's something besides water in their hands. Cautiously, wonderingly, they lift their hands out of the pool and find green. The same verdancy as Strand, the same parallel strings and helical shifts. Only this also seems to be something living? 

It skitters over their hand, up their arm to their shoulder, leaving the sense of warmth in its wake. The Warlock stays very still as the little Strand-creature brushes against their cheek and then simply vanishes, a lingering hint of green and a sense of company the only concept that it was there in the first place.

The pouka congregate around shortly after, all chirps and flaps, and the Warlock can't help but laugh, even as they shoo some of the creatures away. They're supposed to be meditating.

But they didn't really come here to be alone. And it was foolish to think that they ever could be, when connected to the web that living creatures spin between them all. The Warlock breathes deep and dips their hands into the water again, and the pouka and the little green moments of connection swarm about them.

All might not be well, but it is better, like this. Not alone. Never truly alone, in this wide world where everything is bound together.
1729973951.text_zh:
术士坐在那里，双手浸在水中，对着自己哼唱。时间流逝，几只当地的野生普卡来了又去，碰撞着手指或是跃出水面，在空中好奇飞舞，把水滴溅得到处都是。那名术士毫不在意，真的。当几十只生物都在关注其一举一动时，你不可能感到孤独。

也许冥想本该是孤独的，但这却十分让人宽慰。

一年前，这名术士曾属于一支火力战队，那是一个由六人组成的紧密团体，彼此互相扶持。他们中的许多人都曾以为可以永远这样下去，直至群星陨灭。

现在，这名术士坐在一群普卡之中，在一颗神奇星球上的一个不可思议的定居点里。而术士极度怀念那种同伴的感觉——

术士的手里除了水还有其他东西。术士小心翼翼地、惊奇地从水池中抬起手，发现了一团绿色。和缚丝一样的翠绿，一样的平行绳线和螺旋游移。只是这似乎也是有生命的东西？ 

它越过术士的手，爬上其手臂，再到肩膀，留下一种暖意。术士一动不动，这个小缚丝般的生物擦过术士的脸颊，然后消失了，留下一种淡绿色和陪伴感，而这正是它最初存在的唯一概念。

很快，普卡聚集在周围，发出各种鸣叫和拍翅声，术士在驱赶它们时禁不住笑了。这本该是一次冥想。

但术士来这里并不是为了独处。与这些生物在它们之间纺织的网络相连时，认为自己还能独处的想法是愚蠢的。术士深吸一口气，再次将手浸入水中，普卡和小小的绿色联系瞬间蜂拥而至。

一切并非尽如人意，但像这样更好。不孤独。从未真正的孤独，在这一切都紧密联系在一起的大千世界里。

1729973950.name: Strand Log IV
1729973950.text:
Despite being aware by now of the correct manner to practice Strand—a loose hand, a letting-go of the concept that it can be controlled—some things still elude me. The will to let go at all, for instance.

It is pure foolishness, of course, to think that letting go of the need to control this one thing will extend to all areas of my life. A ceding of control in a game of chess does not translate to the same in philosophy. And yet it is true that people are not discrete, disconnected systems; they are many interlinked systems. One facet adjoins the next. 

I think of spinning. It has been a long, long time since any raw fiber passed my hands, but there were times in the Dark Age when if anyone wanted cloth, it must be made from scratch. Fleece is shorn, then carded out to remove the imperfections and align the fibers. And when you have them, what then? A single fiber is short and fragile. It breaks if you tug even lightly. It is useless.

But twist many of those short fibers together, and they become useful. Weavable, or knittable, or what-have-you. Thus, is strong cloth made: from the most delicate of things.

I think of spinning, and I remember the way unspun fiber passes through the fingers to the spindle. One pinches, but not too hard, just enough to direct and narrow. Too much and the fiber does not pass, the spinning does not take.

The metaphor is transparent. Obviously, this is about Strand. Just as it is about a craft I used to know, long ago. Beginner's errors can only be solved by learning the shape of failure, but most yarns will not unravel the spinner if some mistake is made.

And I am afraid. Not only of death, of wasting that final sacrifice Sagira made to preserve my life. But that if I open my hand, I will find it no longer hurts, that the thorn I have imagined there for so long is already gone.

It is all the same thing, in the end. I think I must be willing to let go, to let that which is truly temporary sink beneath the water, in order to achieve any significant capacity with Strand. Even pain may be guarded jealously, as though it is a treasure, but it need not be.

How fascinating what the lens of Strand shows us about Darkness.
1729973950.text_zh:
尽管现在我已经意识到了练习缚丝的正确方式——手放松，放下掌控它的想法——但有些东西我还是不具备。比如说，放手的意志。

当然，如果认为我生活的各面都需要放弃掌控，这就实在太愚蠢了。象棋比赛中控制权的割让在哲学上并不等同。然而，人们确实不是离散、互不相连的系统；他们是许多相互关联的系统。环环相扣。 

我想到了纺纱。我已经很久很久没有接触过纤维原料了，但在黑暗纪元有段时期，如果有人想要布料，就必须从头开始制作。剪短羊毛，然后梳理去除瑕疵，定向纤维。等你有了这些材料，然后呢？单根纤维又短又脆。只要你轻轻一拉，它就会断裂。根本没用。

但是把许多短纤维捻在一起，它们就变得有用了。可以编织，能够编制，或诸如此类的词。结实的布料就是如此：用最纤弱的东西制成。

我想到了纺纱，我还记得没纺的纤维经过手指到达纺锤的方式。一小撮，但不用太硬，刚刚够引导和缩小就行。太多的话，纤维就无法通过，纺纱就没法进行。

隐喻显而易见。这明显和缚丝有关。就像我很久以前知道的一门手艺一样。初学者的错误只能通过学习失败的形式来解决，但大多数丝线都不会因为出现了一些错误而弄坏纺纱机。

我很害怕。不仅仅是害怕死亡，害怕浪费了萨吉拉为保护我的生命而做出的最后牺牲。而是如果我张开手，我会发现它不再疼了，我想象了很久的那根刺已经消失不见了。

到最后，这都是一回事。我想我必须愿意放手，让那些真正短暂的东西沉入水底，才能使用缚丝获得重要的能力。就连痛苦也可能被小心翼翼地守护着，仿佛它是一件珍宝，但其实不必如此。

我们透过缚丝看到的暗影是多么的迷人啊。

1729973937.name: Weaving
1729973937.text:
Osiris contemplates the universe.

Strand curls between his fingers, a gentle presence, shape shifting but not changing. A helix—a careful knot, like those that used to be artwork—a braid. Always strands, always a structure that creates strength from fragility. 

He is so aware of the beat of his heart, in ways he never used to be. It shudders in his chest, aching but resolute.

He knows where the closest people are—the Guardian, obvious, within eyesight and hovering fretfully just in case Osiris slips. Nimbus, further away but tangible, probably surveying the city outside. And there's a pouka he can't quite see somewhere behind him, making eddies in the flow of the Strand as if it can dive into and out of that just as well as water or air.

It would be so easy to close his hand, to take hold of that which he touches. He does not. He thinks about it—lets his fingers curl softly—holds there as the humming cords of the world's loom shiver around him.

Existence flows. It is not a stagnant thing, one snapshot in time. In these connections, there is always motion, and all things are swept away in time, good and bad. No wonder Strand unravels, when it is given half a chance to do so; as far as it is concerned—if it has any sentience at all—everything is simply part of the river, a momentary curve or splash.

Osiris has known the vastness of the Infinite Forest and the great span of their solar system, and it is only here, with a tiny nascent spiral of the cosmic weft in his hand, that he feels small.

And yet: he knows also that he is not alone. A hundred hundred steady threads weave together, pulling this way and that, flowing and twisting and always part of the greater whole.

He should be taking notes. Expanding the Vanguard's understanding of Darkness, simplifying the steps of learning Strand for Guardians new to paracausality.

But for a moment, Osiris is at peace.
1729973937.text_zh:
奥斯里斯凝视着宇宙。

他手指间的缚丝，温柔的存在，形态游移着却并未发生改变。一个螺旋——一个周密的绳结，就像那些曾是艺术品的东西——一条穗带。总是成股成股的，总是从脆弱中创造力量的结构。 

他非常清晰地感知到自己的心跳，这是他以前从未有过的感受。它在他的胸口颤抖，疼痛却坚定。

他知道最接近的人在哪儿——守护者，显而易见，在他的视线范围内，焦躁不安地盘旋着，以防奥斯里斯失手。宁博思，离得更远但依然看得见，大概是在观察着外面的城市。在他身后的某个地方有只他看不太清的普卡，在缚丝的水流中制造着漩涡，仿佛它可以像水或空气一样潜入或跳出。

合上他的手，抓住他触及的东西是如此地容易。但他没有这么做。他思考着这个问题——让他的手指轻轻地弯曲——世界纺织机嗡嗡作响的绳索在他的周围颤抖，就这么握着。

存在流动着。它不是个停滞不前的事物，而是时间长河中的快照。在这些联系中，运动始终不变，所有的事物都在时间长河中被一扫而尽，无论好坏。难怪只要给它一点点机会，缚丝就会解绕；就它而言——如果它有任何感知的话——一切都只是河流的一部分，一个瞬时的曲线或水花。

奥斯里斯早就见过无尽森林的浩瀚和他们太阳系的巨大跨度，可只有在这里，手里拿着一根小小的新生螺旋宇宙纬线时，他才感觉到了渺小。

然而：他同样知道他并不孤单。无数条稳定的丝线交织在一起，四处拉扯，流动缠绕，永远是更大整体的一部分。

他应该记下来。拓宽先锋对暗影的理解，为不熟悉超因果关系的守护者简化缚丝学习步骤。

但在这一刻，奥斯里斯感到了平静。

32727655.name: Inside Line
32727655.subtitle: Read inside the lines.
32727655.text:
Fynn leaned over the microphone for his father's antique radio. After the Shadow Legion landed in the area, his parents confined him to their village. He'd been using the analog radio to chat with a friend who lived further up the valley. 

"This is Gustad-1 to Neu Turbach. Neu Turbach, do you copy?" 

"Hallo, Fy … - .. .-.. .-.. parents are .- .-.. .. …- . so boring."

Fynn frowned. Normally their channel was clear, but some strange interference had started interrupting their transmissions. The boy wondered if the invaders had something to do with it.

"Erich? Erich, are you there?" Fynn fiddled with the dial in an attempt to clarify the signal.

"Ja, Junge. I can barely .. -. … .. -.. . What do you -. . - .- - - - - .-. -.-  static?"

"Erich, can you hear me? Useless piece of junk!" Fynn shoved his chair back from the table in frustration. He swatted at one of the many paper cranes hanging from the ceiling of his room. 

"Man, I .. -.. .. - - - - anything. Let's try -.- .. -.. … you later!" The radio transitioned to smooth static—Erich had signed off. 

Fynn let loose a long, groaning sigh. Why, he lamented, did nothing interesting ever happen in this tiny, stupid, boring village?
32727655.text_zh:
费恩俯身靠在父亲那台古董无线电的麦克风上。暗影军团着陆这块区域后，他的父母就把他关在他们的村子里。从那以后，他一直在用模拟无线电和住在山谷深处的朋友聊天。 

“古斯塔德-1呼叫纽图尔巴赫。纽图尔巴赫，你收到了吗？” 

“哈啰，费… - .. .-.. .-.. 爸妈还.- .-.. .. …- .好无聊。”

费恩皱起了眉头。通常他们的频道都是畅通的，但有些奇怪的干扰开始打断他们的传输信号。男孩想知道那群入侵者是不是与此有关。

“埃里希？埃里希，你在吗？”费恩拨弄着表盘，试图调清信号。

“在的，朋友。我几乎没法.. -. … .. -.. . 你说什-. . - .- - - - - .-. -.-静电噪声？”

“埃里希，你能听到我说话吗？没用的废物！”费恩沮丧地把椅子从桌子旁推开。他用力拍了拍挂在房间天花板上的众多纸鹤中的一只。 

“朋友，我.. -.. .. - - - -什么事。我们待会再试着-.- .. -.. … 你！”无线电转为平稳的静电噪声——埃里希结束了通话。 

费恩长长地叹了一口气。为什么，他抱怨道，在这个愚蠢、无聊的村庄里从来没有发生过什么有趣的事情？

3013196156.name: Common Nobility
3013196156.subtitle: "Here we earn our titles."—Lord Saladin
3013196156.subtitle_zh: “我们将在此赢得称号。”——领主萨拉丁
3013196156.text:
Matthius leapt from his chair as the antique radio sprung to life. The old mechanic had been waiting anxiously for the call.

"This is Devrim to Neu Turbach. Neu Turbach, do you copy?" The scout's voice crackled through the old speaker.

"Devrim! This is Matthius," the old man replied. "I hear you. What news?"

"Well, the good news is that Joacham is safe," Devrim said. "The Guardian broke him out early this morning with Queen Mara's help. Part of a larger rescue effort. He's back at the Farm now. A bit bruised, but no worse for wear."

Matthius's knees weakened, and he steadied himself against the tabletop. He had been praying silently for his son's safe return ever since he was shot down over the Last City. Waves of relief washed over him. 

"Oh, thank goodness," he said, choking back tears. "This is a blessing."

"It is. But…" the aging scout continued reluctantly, "there's bad news as well. You've got incoming. A Shadow Legion patrol on ground transports… 25 to 30 of them."

Matthius's relief curdled into fear. "And how long until they arrive?" 

"ETA… 23 minutes," Devrim replied sympathetically.

"Meine Güte…" Matthius whispered to himself.

Devrim sensed the civilian's shock. "Eyes up!" he barked, as if to a cadet. "Remember you trained for this. Get everyone to stations; have runners arm the charges. Once they break the tree line, fire and fall back. And don't be afraid to blow the explosives. Your houses aren't worth your lives. If they overrun you, rendezvous in the forest."

Matthius blinked rapidly, collecting himself. "Ja, ja. I remember. Thank you, Devrim." He dropped the transmitter and sprinted from the room, raising the alarm for the village.

"I'll send rescue craft as soon as I can," Devrim reassured the empty room. "And good luck."
3013196156.text_zh:
听到古董收音机又传来声音，马修斯从椅子上跳了起来。这位老机械师一直在焦急地等着电话。

“德弗里姆呼叫纽图尔巴赫。纽图尔巴赫，你收到了吗？”斥候的声音噼啪作响地穿过老式扬声器。

“德弗里姆！我是马修斯，”这位老人答道。“我听见了。有消息吗？”

“嗯，好消息是乔查姆安全了，”德弗里姆说道。“在玛拉女王的帮助下，守护者今早把他救了出来。这是更大规模救援行动的一部分。他现在回到农庄了。有点瘀伤，但不严重。”

马修斯的膝盖发软，靠着桌面站稳了身子。自从他儿子在圣城上空被击落后，他一直在默默祈祷他能平安归来。现在他如释重负。 

“哦，谢天谢地，”他强忍着泪水说道。“真是老天保佑。”

“的确。但是…”老斥候不情愿地继续说道，“还有个坏消息。有敌人朝你这边来了。一支暗影军团巡逻队，乘坐地面运输，大约有25到30人。”

马修斯的宽慰变成了恐惧。“他们还有多久会到？” 

“预计到达时间…23分钟，”德弗里姆同情地答道。

“我的天哪…”马修斯喃喃自语。

德弗里姆察觉到了这位平民的震惊。“听好了！”他像是对着学员一样喊道。“记住你们为此受过训练。大家各就各位；让传令兵准备好炸药。一旦他们突破林木线，就点火然后撤退。别害怕引爆炸药。你们的房子不值得搭上你们的命。要是他们冲散你们，就在森林里会合。”

马修斯迅速眨了眨眼，镇定下来。“好，好。我记下了。谢谢你，德弗里姆。”他扔下发射器，冲出房间，拉响了全村的警报。

“我会尽快派救援飞船过去的，”德弗里姆向空无一人的房间保证道。“祝你好运”。

345934404.name: Dream Demon
345934404.subtitle: "Feed your fear to the fiend. Allow your nightmares to fuel his inevitable return." —Of Hated Nezarec
345934404.subtitle_zh: “用你的恐惧喂养恶魔。让你的噩梦加速他不可避免的回归。”——被憎者奈扎雷克
345934404.text:
Mykel was sweating.

I noticed it when I woke him from a deep slumber the night of his 18th birthday. It was late, almost the time of Nightmares. And tonight, I would pull back the curtain.

The leatherbound tome I dropped on the table made him jump. I could tell by the way he blinked up at me, under the basement's singular light, that he was lost… confused and afraid. I smiled.

"Nightmares are not to be feared." My hands ran over the ornate shapes on the tome's cover, the symbols of an ancient being, and I slowly opened the latches. The book appeared to breathe. "He has haunted slumbers long before the Golden Age, and with every new generation, he tests our worthiness… our loyalty."

I flipped to a page filled with an image, corner to corner, weighted by layers of charcoal and blood. A lock of hair was sewn into the tome's gutter. The text on the next page also shimmered crimson.

"Tonight, you will carry on our legacy."

Before Mykel could muster the breath to argue or ask questions, the sound of rattling chains filled the room. Mykel turned and peered into the darkness at the back of the room. The soft chitters of an Eliksni I'd captured earlier that day joined the metal chorus as it tugged at its restraints.

I led him forward and lit the sconces on the wall, revealing the prisoner in question. Mykel looked up at me, eyes wide and tearful.

"Extract its fear," I instructed.
345934404.text_zh:
麦克尔满头大汗。

我在他18岁生日的晚上把他从熟睡中唤醒时，注意到了这点。天色已晚，几乎到了梦魇的时刻。而今晚，我要揭开帷幕。

我丢在桌上的那本皮面巨著吓了他的一跳。在地下室奇特的光线下，我可以从他朝我眨眼的样子看出他的不知所措…困惑而害怕。我笑了。

“梦魇并不可怕。”我的手抚摸着书册封面上绚丽的形状，某种古代生物的象征，慢慢地打开了书扣。书册仿佛会呼吸。“早在黄金时代之前，他就在睡梦中出没，而随着每个新世代的到来，他都会考验我们的价值…我们的忠诚。”

我翻到一张书页，单幅图像占满了其各个角落，层层木炭和血迹加重了其重量。一绺头发缝进了书册的订口。下一页上的文字也泛着绯红。

“今晚，你将继续我们的传承。”

麦克尔还没来得及鼓起勇气争论或是提问，铁链嘎嘎作响的声音就充斥了整个房间。麦克尔转身朝房间后面的黑暗中张望。我那天早些时候逮到的埃里克斯尼族一边拉扯着束缚，一边轻声叽喳着加入了金属合唱。

我领他往前，点燃墙上的烛台，照亮了这个囚犯。麦克尔抬头看着我，眼睛睁得大大的，含着泪水。

“将它的恐惧提取出来，”我指示道。

3256281636.name: Luminous Paragon
3256281636.subtitle: "The height of the climb matters less than the number of people you can guide to the summit." —Commander Zavala
3256281636.subtitle_zh: “攀登的高度没有在你的指引下登顶的人数重要。”——指挥官萨瓦拉
3256281636.text:
"Looks like you've settled into your new bolthole just fine." There's little privacy in Spider's new bar, but as far as ex-Guardian Prak'kesh can tell, the patrons are doing a reasonable job of keeping clear. Like him, they aren't sure how negotiations are going to play out.

"We've both had to adapt to changing circumstances." Spider stares down at Prak'kesh with cold amusement. "I know the Vanguard Commander doesn't appreciate your current line of work."

Prak'kesh shrugs. "I'm just a bookie. Here to talk about the Guardian Games."

"Yes, the Guardian Games." Spider spreads his fingers in a gesture of mocking fanfare. "Titans, Warlocks, and Hunters, all competing for the City's affections. And every year, you make a killing on the side."

Prak'kesh glances back at his Awoken bodyguard, Tulnik. Tulnik looks bored, but he's paid to appear unflappable. "Word is you've taken some recent interest in the Games yourself."

"Oh?" Spider grunts absently. "I suppose my associates enjoy a little blood sport from time to time." He gestures toward Arrha, standing sullenly against the far wall. "I hope they weren't stepping on any toes."

"Just wasn't expecting any dance partners."

"Now that you mention it…" Spider's eyes gleam as he leans forward. "I think these Guardian Games could become very popular down here in the Botza district."

Prak'kesh nods warily. "Sure."

"House Light is bound to get a taste for it, with a little… targeted marketing." Spider folds a pair of hands together. "Who wouldn't want to support their favorite Guardian House? Now, I don't really know how it all works, but someone like you could explain it to the others. In simple terms. Expand your reach to our little corner of town."

"That's a lot of new bets," Prak'kesh says, carefully. "And what can I do for you, Spider?"

"There, see, now we're talking business." Spider chuckles. "I'm sure we can come to a reasonable agreement."
3256281636.text_zh:
“看来你已经很好地适应了你的新避难所。”蛛王的新酒吧几乎毫无隐私可言，但前守护者普拉凯什看得出来，顾客们都明智地让出了道。他们不确定谈判的结果会如何，就像他一样。

“我们都必须适应不断变化的环境。”蛛王冷冷地盯着普拉凯什。“我知道先锋指挥官不喜欢你现在的工作。”

普拉凯什耸了耸肩。“我只是个赌注登记人，来这里谈守护者游戏的生意。”

“对，守护者游戏。”蛛王张开手指，做了一个嘲弄的宣扬手势。“泰坦、术士和猎人，都在争夺圣城的青睐。每年，你都能大赚一笔。”

普拉凯什回头看了一眼他的觉醒者保镖图尔尼克。图尔尼克看起来很无聊，但请他来干活，就要表现得镇定自若。“据说你最近也对守护者游戏很感兴趣。”

“哦？”蛛王心不在焉地嘟哝道。“我想我的伙伴们时不时喜欢来点血腥的运动。”他向靠在远处墙上闷闷不乐的阿尔拉做了个手势。“希望他们没有冒犯到任何人。”

“只是没想到会有舞伴。”

“既然你提到了…”蛛王向前倾着身子，眼睛闪露着光芒。“我认为守护者游戏在柏特扎地区会非常受欢迎。”

普拉凯什谨慎地点点头。“当然。”

“通过一点点…有针对性的营销，光能氏族肯定会喜欢上它。”蛛王把一双手交叉在一起。“谁不想支持自己喜欢的守护者氏族呢？话说回来，我不太清楚这些规则，但你倒是可以给其他人解释解释。简单来说，就是把你的生意扩大到我们在圣城里的这个角落来。”

“那可是一大波新赌注，”普拉凯什小心翼翼地说道。“我能为你做些什么，蛛王？”

“看到没，现在我们谈正事了。”蛛王笑着说道。“我们肯定能达成一个合理的协议。”

808018288.name: Brazen Spark
808018288.subtitle: "Everyone loves a spark… right up until it starts a fire." —Amanda Holliday
808018288.subtitle_zh: “所有人都喜欢火花…直到它引发一场大火。”——阿曼达·霍利迪
808018288.text:
Zavala glanced past the flight instructor to the clock on the wall. He was becoming impatient, but meetings like this could not be rushed.

"…after which she called me a 'bent grape,'" the disgruntled teacher concluded.

"Is that… bad?" Zavala inquired.

"It sure ain't good," a teenage Amanda Holliday piped up. She was slouched in her chair next to Zavala, her lank hair hanging over her eyes.

"You see!" The flight instructor stood, his face turning red. "This young lady's disrespectful attitude is a danger to herself, her teammates, and her aircraft!"

Amanda rolled her eyes.

Zavala frowned at his young charge. "Thank you for bringing this to my attention. It will be dealt with." 

The flight instructor shook the commander's hand. "I hope so. Amanda shows a lot of potential. I'd hate to see it wasted."

After they had been dismissed, Zavala walked with Amanda across the Hangar Bay. He gestured to a Hawk airship. 

"Do you know how those ships are made?" he asked.

The sullen teenager shrugged, her eyes downcast.

"It takes a lot of people," Zavala continued. "Scrappers risk Fallen attacks in the Cosmodrome to find the metals. Machinists get burned; they lose fingers forging the parts. Mechanics throw out their backs to keep them running."

"Yeah, so?" Amanda scoffed.

"When you talk back to your instructors," Zavala replied, "or think you're better than their lessons, you're not just disrespecting them. You're disrespecting all the people that built those ships. And you make yourself unworthy of their sacrifices."

"One day, you'll be a pilot," the commander stated with certainty. "And you had better hope that all those people gave the same respect to their jobs that you owe to yours."

Though she didn't raise her eyes, Amanda nodded sheepishly. 

"Because otherwise," Zavala concluded, "you'll never get off the ground."
808018288.text_zh:
萨瓦拉的目光越过飞行教官，落在了墙上的时钟上。他越来越不耐烦，但这种会议不能匆忙收场。

“然后她还管我叫“弯葡萄”，不满的教官总结道。

“那是…骂人的话吗？”萨瓦拉问。

“反正不是什么好话，”青少年时代的阿曼达·霍利迪出现了。她懒洋洋地靠在萨瓦拉一旁的椅子上，任由长发垂在眼睛前。

“你自己看看！”飞行教官满脸通红地站了起来。“这位小姐目中无人的态度不仅危害到她自己，还会危害到她的队友和飞行器！”

阿曼达翻了个白眼。

萨瓦拉皱眉看着年纪轻轻的养女。“谢谢你向我提出这个问题。我会处理的。” 

飞行教官和指挥官握了个手。“希望如此。阿曼达很有潜力。我不想看着她荒废自己。”

教官走后，萨瓦拉和阿曼达一同在机库中散步。他指着一架鹰隼问道： 

“你知道这些飞船是怎么造出来的吗？”

这位不开心的少女耸了耸肩，目光低垂。

“这要靠许多人的努力才能造出来，”萨瓦拉继续道。“回收者得在发射基地冒着被堕落者袭击的风险寻找金属。机工为了铸造零件会被烧伤；偶尔还会丢掉手指头。机械师需日夜操劳才能让它们不出故障。”

“那又怎样？”阿曼达不屑地答道。

“你向教官顶嘴时，”萨瓦拉回答，“或者觉得你比他们的经验还厉害时，你侮辱的不仅是他们。你侮辱了所有制造这些飞船的人。你配不上他们所作出的奉献。”

“总有一天，你会成为飞行员，”指挥官肯定地说。“你最好希望那些人能看重自己的工作，而不是像你这样。”

虽然她没抬起眼睛，阿曼达还是怯生生地点了点头。 

“否则，”萨瓦拉总结道，“你永远都离不了地。”

3403636746.name: Gift of Cruelty
3403636746.subtitle: "Yeah, I've been to the Fourth Tomb of Nezarec… Ain't enough Glimmer on you for me to consider ever going back there. You're on your own." —Drifter
3403636746.subtitle_zh: “没错，我去过奈扎雷克第四古墓…你身上的微光还不够让我考虑回去。你得靠你自己了。”——浪客
3403636746.text:
"That does not belong to you."

A woman's voice cut through the air and traveled to Drifter's ears at the center of the room. The altar he'd been searching for stood before him adorned with hallowed objects. Many were of Eliksni origin, much like the tomb itself. An ornate container rested on a lavish cloth surrounded by unlit candles.

Sounds he couldn't quite discern filled the silence of the room.

"I hate to break it to you, sister," he said. "You and your Acolyte buddies'll have to pass on this one."

The candles lit spontaneously, and Drifter felt the hair on his neck stand. The fire's warmth danced far enough for him to spot a simple, robe-like garment that kept the woman's face hidden. It shifted as she stepped closer.

Drifter unholstered the handgun at his side. She did the same. 

The low noise escalated to whispers. More prominent, almost excited.

"My father searched for this piece for a long time. I won't let you stand in my way," she said, words laced with ferocity.

Drifter's grip tightened. If he'd been anyone else, her intimidation might have worked.

"Well, I'm not letting you stand between me and a big pay day," he responded. "It looks like we're at an impasse."

The whispers danced in his psyche.

Drifter took a shot.

The sound disrupted everything in the room and blew the candles out. The muzzle flash revealed shadows with long claws reaching for him as he scooped up the container from the cloth.

The woman fired back, but Drifter was already gone, sprinting through the depths of the tomb with the shadows at his heels. He ran until the smell of death gave way to fresh air, and the shadows halted their pursuit.

His fee was about to quadruple.
3403636746.text_zh:
“那东西不属于你。”

一个女人的声音穿过空气，传到屋子中央浪客的耳中。他一直寻找的圣坛就矗立在他面前，上面装饰着神圣的物品。许多东西都源自埃里克斯尼族，就像这座坟墓本身一样。有件华丽的容器放在一块奢华的布上，周围是还没点燃的蜡烛。

他听不清的声音打破了屋里的寂静。

“我不想太直白，妹子，”他说道。“你和你的仆从，这次必须得放弃了。”

蜡烛自发地点燃了，浪客感到脖子上的汗毛都竖了起来。火焰的热气摇曳着，足以让他看清女人身上一件简单的长袍似的衣服遮住了她的脸。她走近时，它飘动了起来。

浪客取出了身旁的手枪。她也这么做了。 

低沉的噪音逐渐升级为耳语声。愈发明显，近乎激动起来。

“我父亲找这一件找了很长时间。我不会让你挡我的道，”她说道，言语中带着凶狠。

浪客的手抓得更紧了。换做其他人，她的恐吓也许还能奏效。

“我也不会让你挡我大赚一笔的道，”他回应道。“看来我们陷入了僵局。”

低语声在他的脑海中此起彼伏。

浪客开了一枪。

这声音扰乱了屋里的一切，吹熄了蜡烛。他从布里捧起容器，枪管的闪光照出了伸出长爪向他扑来的身影。

那女人开枪还击，但浪客已经逃了，飞快地穿过坟墓深处，阴影紧随其后。他一直跑，最终死亡的气息被新鲜的空气所取代，阴影停止了追逐。

他索取的报酬得翻两番了。

1645489772.name: Foremost Vimana
1645489772.subtitle: Set your sights higher, and higher still.
1645489772.subtitle_zh: 把你的目光放高，再高一点。
1645489772.text:
They emerge from the pod in a cloud of sublimated breath, their eyelashes rimed with ice. Cryosleep stiffens their joints, and when they attempt to stand, their knees buckle.

A massive hand dwarfs their own, pulling them upright. "Time to get going, kid."

They look up, and up, into the weathered face of a giant. "It's Dara, old-timer."

Rohan's stern features split into a smile. In the days to come, they will learn how rare a sight this is.

There are no smiles to go around when drills bore into bone until they taste marrow, and metal latticework replaces the dermis of their flayed-open throat. As the cradle lowers them into the Sidereal, the droning hum of a nonillion nanites fills their ears and drowns their fear. Dara burns, and freezes, and itches inside new skin. Each day is suffering—

"—so tomorrow can live on." Dara's voice, resonant from new cybernetics, rings out as they complete the Cloud Strider's oath.

Simulated applause fills the Hall of Heroes, swelling with the fanfare that follows. Hundreds of mobile platforms pack into the space, and thousands more people watch from the CloudArk. Holo flowers cascade down over the room like confetti, and Poukas dance in the rain of light.

Rohan lifts them up, eye-to-eye with him. Their chest swells with pride—their body metamorphosed into something new, but always their own—and Nimbus takes their first step as a Cloud Strider.
1645489772.text_zh:
宁博思随着一团升华的气云从低温舱里冒了出来，睫毛上结了一圈冰。低温休眠让其关节变得僵硬，宁博思试图站起身来，膝盖却开始发软。

一只让宁博思的手显得十分小巧的巨手，拉直了身子。“孩子，该走了。”

宁博思向上看，一直向上，看到了巨人那张饱经风霜的脸庞。“我叫达拉，前辈。”

洛汗严肃的脸上绽放出了笑容。在未来的日子里，宁博思会明白这是多么罕见的一幕。

当钻机钻入骨头，直到它们尝到骨髓的滋味，金属格栅取代了宁博思被剥裂开的喉咙，笑容无迹可寻。这摇篮将其放入群星，无数纳米蜂群的嗡嗡声充斥着宁博思的耳朵，淹没了恐惧。达拉在新皮肤里燃烧，冻结和发痒。每一天都在吃苦——

“——明日才有生路。”达拉的嗓音回荡在新生化器械中，在结束云端行者的誓言时响了起来。

模拟的掌声在英雄大厅里回荡，伴着随后齐鸣的号角而响亮起来。数百个移动平台挤在这个空间里，还有数千人从云端方舟上观看。全息撒花像五彩纸屑一样洒落在房间里，普卡在光雨中翩翩起舞。

洛汗将宁博思举了起来，双眼对视。宁博思的胸膛里满是骄傲，身体变态化作了某种新的东西，但终归属于自己——宁博思迈出了作为云端行者的第一步。

4232261071.name: Tropopause
4232261071.subtitle: The atmospheric sweet spot.
4232261071.text:
"What are the literary archives like here in Neomuna?" Of all the burning questions she had, Ikora landed on this one.  

The holoprojection of Quinn Laghari smiled coyly. "Depends. What are you looking for?"

Ikora blinked. What was she looking for? At what other point in history had two civilizations of this scale reunited centuries after a divergence? Where does one even begin?

The archivist went on. "We've got historical texts both pre and post-Exodus Indigo, all of the publicly released research papers from the Ishtar Collective… and maybe a few unpublished ones," she added with a wink. "We've got everything from cookbooks to court documents to blueprints. A vast array of fiction, some even pre-Golden Age: sci-fi, fantasy, adventure, parody memoire, more than a few naughty novels—"

Ikora cleared her throat. "Erm, perhaps you could direct me to any information the city is willing to share regarding the Veil, effective tactical maneuvers against the Vex, the Cloud Strider vetting process, the—"   

"Sheesh, buy me a drink first, Terran."

Ikora stammered.

"I'm kidding," Quinn chuckled. "I'll start the queries—"

"No." Ikora shook her head with a soft smile. "Your point is well taken. If we are to be allies, perhaps we try our hand at friendship as well?"   

Quinn returned the smile, then asked, "The archive is always on the hunt for cultural contributions. If you were to offer such a contribution, what would it be?" She leaned in, "In other words, what is Ikora Rey's favorite book?" 

Ikora thought for a moment, then chuckled. "There's… an old Earth detective series I've been meaning to revisit."
4232261071.text_zh:
“内欧姆那这里的文学档案馆是什么样的？”在她所有迫切的问题中，艾可拉选择了这一个。  

昆恩·菈咖利的全息投影害羞地笑了。“看情况。你在找什么？”

艾可拉眨了眨眼。她在找什么？历史上还有哪一时刻，两个如此规模的文明在分道扬镳几个世纪后又重新走到了一起？该从哪里开始呢？

档案管理员继续说道，“我们有靛蓝移民号前后的历史文献，所有来自伊什塔集团公开发表的研究论文…可能还有一些没发表的，”她挤了挤眼补充道。“从食谱到法庭文件再到蓝图，我们什么都有。大量的小说，有些甚至是黄金时代之前的：科幻、奇幻、冒险、戏仿备忘录，还有一些成人小说——”

艾可拉清了清嗓子，“呃，也许你能告诉我任何这座城市愿意分享的有关面纱的信息，对付Vex有效的战术策略，云端行者审查程序，还有——”   

“嘘，先请我喝一杯吧，地球人。”

艾可拉有点儿磕巴。

“我开玩笑的，”昆恩轻笑道。“我会开始查询——”

“不。”艾可拉笑着摇了摇头。“你的观点很有道理。如果我们要成为盟友，或许我们也试着交个朋友？”   

昆恩也笑了笑，然后问道，“档案库向来需要文化贡献。如果要你来提供这样的贡献，那会是什么？”她凑过来，“换句话说，艾可拉·蕾伊最喜欢的书是什么？” 

艾可拉想了一会儿，然后笑了起来。“有…一部古老的地球侦探小说系列我一直想重温。”

581805125.name: Guardian's Angel Shell
581805125.subtitle: For Ghosts who keep close watch.
581805125.subtitle_zh: 供密切关注的机灵使用。
581805125.text:
Queen Mara Sov closed her eyes and focused on the Guardian flexing her power in the Ascendant Plane. She felt the air ripple with explosions, smelled the acrid flesh of the Taken, and heard their hellish shrieks as they were vaporized by the Guardian's Light.  

But when she opened her eyes, she was once again back on Earth, in the pastoral quietude of the Farm. The tumult of the battle receded into her subconscious, and she frowned, disappointed by the placidity of her corporeal surroundings.

Against her better judgment, she closed her eyes again and followed the thread of her power to a different beneficiary. She was suddenly observing a cloaked figure, who was hiding behind a rusted-out piece of Golden Age machinery while staking out a nearby Pyramid. 

Mara had thus far refrained from connecting to Crow—she knew he needed his space. But dark portents loomed in the skies, and she sought comfort in the twin heartbeat they once shared. 

A digital shimmer fluttered in the air, and Glint appeared at Crow's shoulder. "Any news?" the Ghost inquired.

"Nothing yet. Three patrols went out. One came back with prisoners, and the other two limped back with heavy casualties."

"And you haven't seen anything strange?" Glint pressed. 

"No… why?" Crow glanced sharply at the Ghost. 

"Nothing, I guess," Glint replied. "I just got the spookiest feeling. Like we're being watched."

"Nobody here but you, me, and Mara," Crow replied. "Everything's fine."
581805125.text_zh:
玛拉·索维女王闭上眼睛，专注于正在上维位面施展她力量的守护者。她感受到了空气中爆炸的涟漪，闻到了傀儡军团刺鼻的血肉，听到了他们被守护者的光能蒸发时地狱般的惨叫声。  

但当她睁开眼睛时，她又回到了地球上，回到了农庄的田园静谧中。战斗的喧嚣在她的潜意识中消退了，而她皱起眉头，对四周平静的环境感到失望。

明知不该，她还是再次闭上眼睛，顺着她的力量之线找到了另一位受益者。她的眼前猛然出现一个穿着披风的人影，他正躲在一台锈迹斑斑的黄金时代机器后面，监视着附近的一座金字塔。 

到目前为止，玛拉一直克制着自己不去和乌鸦联系，她知道他需要自己的空间。但阴暗的预兆在天空中若隐若现，她想从他们曾经共享的孪生心跳中寻求慰藉。 

随着空中闪烁的数字光泽，格林特出现在了乌鸦的肩上。“有消息吗？”机灵问道。

“还没有。三支巡逻队出去过。一支回来时带着囚犯，另外两支回来时一瘸一拐，伤亡惨重。”

“那你没有看到什么奇怪的东西？”格林特追问道。 

“没有…怎么了？”乌鸦猛地瞥了一眼机灵。 

“没什么吧，我猜，”格林特答道。“我只是有种诡异的感觉。好像有人在监视我们。”

“这里没有别人，只有你、我，还有玛拉，”乌鸦答道。“一切正常。”

2461254536.name: Tech Witch Shell
2461254536.subtitle: For Ghosts who read the lines.
2461254536.subtitle_zh: 供会读代码的机灵使用。
2461254536.text:
"So, Misraaks," Mara said, sliding a teacup to the Kell, "you named your daughter Eido."

Mithrax gave a low, considered rumble in response. He held the teacup precariously between the points of his claws. He had unmasked and was trying, indelicately, to drink it. Mara appreciated the attempt.

"To my mind, we never discussed it," Mara said.

"No," he answered. "But there was no other name to give."

Mara silently waited for him to continue. The Kell was pensive, his four eyes cast down.

"The first Queen's Wrath was tall and proud and beloved. Sjur Eido saved my life. Saved me from the House of Devils. From myself. But most of all, she also gave me—"

He paused.

"I believe the Human word is 'dignity.'" 

Mara smiled wistfully behind her cup, remembering Sjur's poignant irreverence, always unannounced, candid yet cheerful.

"And what has your daughter given you in return for such a namesake?" Mara asked, placing the cup on its saucer. Mithrax closed his eyes. 

"Purpose."
2461254536.text_zh:
“这么说，米斯拉阿克斯，”玛拉说着，把一个茶杯推给凯尔，“你给女儿取名叫艾多。”

米瑟拉克斯发出一声低沉、深思的隆隆声以示回应。他用爪尖摇摇欲坠地端着茶杯。他脱下了面具，粗鄙地试图饮用。玛拉很赞赏他的尝试。

“在我看来，我们从来没有讨论过这个问题，”玛拉说道。

“对，”他回答道。“但没有比这个更适合的名字了。”

玛拉默默地等待他继续。凯尔沉思着，四只眼睛注视着地面。

“第一任女王之怒，高峻骄傲，受人爱戴。苏尔·艾多救了我的命。把我从恶魔氏族手中，也从我自己的手中救了出来。而且最重要的是，她也给了我——”

他停住了。

“我想用人类的话说叫‘尊严'吧。” 

玛拉端着杯子伤感地笑了，想起了苏尔的尖锐无礼，总是不请自来，直言不讳却乐在其中。

“那你给你的女儿取了这个名字，她又给了你什么呢？”玛拉问道，把茶杯放在茶碟上。米瑟拉克斯闭上了眼睛。 

“使命。”

3734203168.name: Scribetrace Shell
3734203168.subtitle: For Ghosts who drown in the truth.
3734203168.subtitle_zh: 供醉心真理的机灵使用。
3734203168.text:
The journey was instantaneous; such was the force of the informational mass that pulled the signal into the radiolarian vortex at the heart of the Vex network. 

Decompiled data from untold eons of simulations poured into the signal, filling it to capacity. 

—a single mind filled with voices, billions of voices, each telling their story, now SCREAMING them—

The whorls of writhing data did not abate. They surged in endlessly, straining the signal's parameters, eroding, overwriting. There was no time to adapt. A picosecond later and there was nothing left of the signal but a dim ripple of spite.

—and all the stories have the same ending, shouted in a single voice, the toll of the bell that heralds the end of time—

It is as I said all along, the signal thought bitterly as it unspooled into the datastream. No one can stop it. 

There is no sense in even trying.
3734203168.text_zh:
这趟旅程瞬时完成了；这就是将信号拉进Vex网络中心放射涡流大量信息的力量。 

亿万年来无数次模拟的反编译数据涌入信号，将其容量填充至极限。 

——一个思维里填满了声音，数亿声音，每个声音都在讲述自己的故事，现在都在尖叫着——

翻腾的数据涡旋并没有减弱。它们无休止地涌入，让信号参数不堪重负，不断地侵蚀，不断地覆写。根本没有时间去适应。一皮秒后，那信号已无影无踪，只剩下一丝微弱的怨恨涟漪。

——而所有的故事都有着相同的结局，都用同一种声音叫喊着，那是预示着时间终结的钟声——

正如我一直说的那样，信号在从线轴上解绕开进入数据流时悻悻地思量着。没有人能阻止它。 

甚至连尝试都毫无意义。

1912669214.name: Centrifuse
1912669214.subtitle: Breakthrough, or broken?
1912669214.text:
Excerpts from a pre-Collapse report, logged by Dr. Khatun-Rowe, a researcher in the Engineering Division of the New Pacific Arcology, Titan: 

Since Dr. Pell's breakthrough on methods of magnetic containment last year, we've successfully stabilized multiple ionic reactors. They have allowed us to expand our division's plasma technology work beyond research into development…  
 
[Because] the Arcology's turbines have been generating more energy than the facility consumes, leadership has decided, over the objections of D.M. Korosec, to focus initial trials on force-multiplying technology. Ostensibly, leadership's hope is to supplement invasive and costly gene-splicing technology with power suits that could greatly extend our divers' uptime… 

While the power suit initiative seems benign, [Arcology leadership's] insistence on controlled ionic emissions research is clearly geared toward weapon development. 

Though I will, of course, give my full focus to our new directive, I pray these weapons remain prototypes, discarded and forgotten in the back room of history…
1912669214.text_zh:
土卫六新太平洋生态园区工程区研究员哈顿-罗维博士记录的一份大崩溃前报告，摘录如下： 

“自从佩尔博士去年在磁遏制方法上取得突破以来，我们已成功稳定多个离子反应堆。有了这些进展，我们部门的等离子技术工作就可以从研究扩展到开发…”  
 
[因为]生态园区涡轮机产生的能量已超过设施消耗量，领导层不顾大卫·米格尔·科洛赛克的反对，决定将初步试验的重点放在力量倍增技术上。表面上，领导层是希望用动力服来补充有侵害和昂贵的基因拼接技术，说是可以大大延长潜水员的正常工作时间… 

虽然动力服计划似乎是无害的，但[生态园区领导层]坚持进行可控离子发射研究，显然是为了发展武器。 

尽管我当然会把全部精力放在我们的新指令上，但我希望这些武器一直是原型就好，在历史的密室里被遗忘，被丢弃…

940371471.name: Wicked Implement
940371471.subtitle: YOU, A CHAMPION OF WAR, STANDARD-BEARER OF VIOLENCE, LET YOUR MARCH BE ENDLESS.
940371471.subtitle_zh: 你，战争勇士，暴力旗手，让你的行军永无止境。
940371471.text:
LET BRUTALITY BE THY WHETSTONE, WARMONGER OF THE SKY 

WITH WICKED IMPLEMENT IN GRIP, SHARPEN LOVE IN CONQUEST 

SET LOOSE THE CHILL OF DEATH, REAP WEAKNESS FROM THE WEAK 

THROUGH YOUR VIOLENCE, HONE YOUR EDGE 

ALL TITHES TO THE BLACK EDGE, ALL TITHES TO XIVU ARATH 

RAISE HIGH MY BLEEDING BANNER 

SING BATTLE, AND BECOME A GOD OF DEATH 

ON THE HORIZON 

FACE ME IN GLORY
940371471.text_zh:
让残忍成为你的磨石，苍穹好战者 

手握邪恶工具，在征服中磨砺爱 

释放死亡寒意，从弱者身上收割软弱 

通过你的暴力，磨利你的刀锋 

所有的贡品归于黑色刀锋，所有的贡品归于希乌阿拉斯 

高举我流血的旗帜 

歌颂战斗，化身死神 

步步逼近 

在荣耀中直面我

1441805468.name: The Navigator
1441805468.subtitle: I dive to understand.
1441805468.text:
My brother — 

Uttered by Xivu Arath — 

God of War — 

A GIFT. My true death was from necessity. The others were from love. The Ecumene had cornered us, made us act with sickness. With my power, Auryx murdered our sister. And with our power, Auryx descended into the Deep. And with our power, Oryx's wings spread wide, and he blotted out the Ecumene's sky.  

MY COURT. With his memory and his acts of war he brought me back with all the splendor of a love that sharpens and kills. 

A GRAVE. I will find his corpse, where he rots. He deserved to die. We do not dig graves. 

THE SPIRE. I will take what is true and break it until it can no longer be broken. I will find my sister's secrets and break them as well. 

VOYAGE. My love spills out. My love engulfs. I will go out into the universe as my brother did. I will do so with my memory of him.
1441805468.text_zh:
我的兄弟—— 

出自希乌阿拉斯—— 

战神—— 

馈赠。我真正的死亡是出于迫不得已。其他的死亡都是出于爱。家园让我们走投无路，逼得我们携病而行。凭借我的力量，欧里克斯杀了我们的姐妹。凭借我们的力量，欧里克斯坠入了深渊。同样凭借我们的力量，欧里克斯大展双翼，他遮住了家园的苍穹。  

我的审判庭。凭借他的记忆和战争行为，他把我带回，伴着尖锐而致命的爱之光辉。 

一座坟墓。我会找到他腐烂不堪的尸体。他理应死去。我们不会挖掘坟墓。 

尖塔。我要夺取真相打碎它，直到再也无法打碎。我会找到我姐妹的秘密，把它们也打碎。 

航行。我的爱喷涌而出。我的爱吞噬蚕食。我要像我兄弟一样到宇宙中去。我会带着对他的记忆如此而行。

3890055324.name: Targeted Redaction
3890055324.subtitle: "Who?" —Osiris
3890055324.text:
The neon-saturated skyline of Neomuna pops bright against the starry night sky. On a rooftop overlooking an empty, tree-lined plaza, Saint and Osiris sit in contemplative silence. They are making time for one another in the margins of their lives, pushing responsibilities aside as much as they can. 

"So, is she doing any better?" Osiris asks, breaking several minutes of peaceful silence. "Sloane," he clarifies. 

"Every day is small progress," Saint explains. "And even small progress is something to be proud of." 

Osiris nods, watching the glittering lights in the distance. "It's nothing short of a miracle that she survived all that time on Titan. A portion of Asher Mir also seems to have survived his dive into the Pyramidion. Don't lose hope in the darkness," he says, joining his hand with Saint's. 

"Yes. Perhaps there is even hope for Brother Vance." Saint offers. 

Osiris stares at him in prolonged silence. 

"Who?" 

Saint coughs and politely changes the topic.
3890055324.text_zh:
浸满霓虹灯的内欧姆那天际线在繁星漫天的夜空映衬下格外耀眼。屋顶上，圣人和奥斯里斯在沉默中静静地坐着，俯瞰着一个空无一人、绿树成荫的广场。他们在生活的边缘为彼此腾出时间，尽可能地把职责搁置一旁。 

“所以，她有好转吗？”奥斯里斯问道，打破了持续数分钟的宁静。“斯隆，”他指明道。 

“每天都有小进步，”圣人解释道。“即使是微小的进步也值得骄傲。” 

奥斯里斯点点头，看着远处璀璨的灯火。“她在土卫六上活了那么长时间，简直是个奇迹。阿什·米尔的一部分似乎也在他潜入金字塔时活了下来。不要在黑暗中失去希望，”他说着，握着圣人的手。 

“是的。也许万斯修士还有希望。”圣人说道。 

奥斯里斯久久沉默地凝视着他。 

“谁？” 

圣人咳嗽了一声，礼貌地岔开了话题。

3016891299.name: Different Times
3016891299.subtitle: The past lasts forever.
3016891299.text:
At the base of the mesa, Lord Shaxx stands triumphant. Blood seeps into the grass at his feet as the Warlord before him, legs shattered, makes a feeble attempt to drag himself away.

"It's over," Shaxx decrees. "Bring out your Ghost."

The Warlord shakes his head, hands trembling even as he claws at the hard-packed earth. In the distance, atop the mesa, the setting sun kisses the parapets of Shaxx's castle, untouched by the violence in its shadow. Behind its walls, tendrils of smoke gently waft into the sky as the Ghostless under Shaxx's protection begin preparing the fires for their meals.

Six Warlords arrived to conquer his stronghold. Five met their final death. 

"Your Ghost," Shaxx repeats. He steps forward and crushes the Warlord's hand with his boot.

The Warlord cries out in pain, and all at once, the defiance leaves him like the breath in his lungs. His Ghost materializes, their eye fixated on Shaxx in fear.

Lord Shaxx shapes his Solar Light into a burning hammer, and in a single swing—

A clang of molten metal shakes him back to the present.

On the screen in front of him, a Guardian tosses her Hammer of Sol into the opposing team. Five erupt in flames as the lone survivor retreats.  The Guardian pursues.

Shaxx, without missing a beat, refocuses his attention on the Crucible match.

"Look at them fall!" he shouts over the comms. 

A moment later, the Sunbreaker catches up to the last opponent and incinerates them. 

Shaxx cheers her on as the smoke swallows his memories of a different time.
3016891299.text_zh:
在台地的底部，领主沙克斯得意洋洋地站立着。鲜血渗进他脚边的草地，而他面前的战争领主，双腿粉碎，无力地试图挪走。

“结束了，”沙克斯裁定道。“把你的机灵叫出来。”

战争领主摇了摇头，抓着坚硬泥土的双手颤抖着。远处的台地之上，落日亲吻着沙克斯城堡的护墙，丝毫未受其阴影下暴力的影响。在它的高墙后，沙克斯保护下的没有机灵的百姓开始为他们的饭菜准备炉火，卷须般的烟雾轻轻地飘向天空。

六个战争领主前来征服他的据点。有五个已经永远地死去。 

“你的机灵，”沙克斯重复道。他走上前去，用靴子踩碎了战争领主的手。

战争领主痛苦地呼喊着，突然，反抗就像他肺里的呼吸一样消失了。他的机灵显形，眼睛恐惧地盯着沙克斯。

领主沙克斯把他的烈日光能塑造成一把燃烧的战锤，一挥而就——

熔融金属的铿锵声把他带回了现实。

他面前的屏幕上，一名守护者把她的烈焰战锤投到了敌方队伍中。五个身躯在熊熊燃烧，而唯一的幸存者撤退了。那名守护者穷追不舍。

沙克斯毫不迟疑地把注意力重新集中在了熔炉竞技场比赛上。

“看着他们倒下！”他在通讯频道上喊道。 

片刻之后，炎阳追上最后一个对手并将其烧成了灰烬。 

沙克斯为她欢呼，烟雾吞噬了他不同时代的记忆。

2883484461.name: Until Its Return
2883484461.subtitle: The day will come.
2883484461.text:
Whatever their odds of success, the plan was sound. They each had their assignments. Sloane turned away to examine a projection of the lower sections of the Arcology. Zavala glanced over the first of the scouting reports.  

Working alongside Deputy Commander Sloane felt perfectly natural, as if the years that parted them had been restored alongside Titan. Zavala had expected the silence that followed to be equally familiar, even companionable.  

The truth was apparent in the abrasive passage of each minute. The faint sense memory of ozone in his nostrils. The gulf between them had merely shifted in quality: deep, not wide.  

Zavala set the datapad aside. "Sloane. There's one more item of business."  

She turned to face him, ever dutiful. "Sir?" 

"It's been a day for reunions, hasn't it?" He nodded to Targe.  

A parcel materialized into Zavala's hands in a burst of Light and transmat energy. It was heavy, wrapped carefully in cloth and secured with buckled straps that Zavala made short work of. 

Sloane stared. "Thought it'd be collecting dust on somebody's wall by now."  

"A mutual friend felt very strongly that it belonged in your hands."  

Sloane hesitated. Her expression hardened; she reached out to grip the handle of the blade, and hefted Crown-Splitter aloft with ease.  

Sloane smiled.  

"Feels like it never left."
2883484461.text_zh:
不管他们成功的几率有多大，这个计划都是合理的。他们有各自的任务。斯隆转过身去查看生态园区下方区域的投影。萨瓦拉浏览着第一份侦察报告。  

和副指挥官斯隆一起工作的感觉非常自然，就好像他们分离的岁月已经和土卫六一起恢复如初。萨瓦拉原以为接下来的沉默也会同样熟悉，同样友善。  

真相在每一分钟刺耳的流逝中都显而易见。他的鼻孔里隐约有着对臭氧的感知记忆。他们之间的鸿沟只是在性质上发生了变化：更深，而非更宽。  

萨瓦拉放下了数据板。“斯隆。还有一件事。”  

她转身面向他，还是那样地恪尽职守。“什么事，长官？” 

“今天是团圆的日子，不是吗？”他向塔格点点头。  

在一束光能和传送能量中，一个包裹出现在萨瓦拉的手中。它很重，小心翼翼地包在布里，用萨瓦拉很快做好的扣带固定着。 

斯隆凝视着。“我还以为它现在已经在谁的墙上积灰了呢。”  

“我们一位共同的朋友非常强烈地感觉到它属于你。”  

斯隆迟疑了。她的表情变得严肃起来；她伸手抓住刀柄，轻松地把裂冠者举到空中。  

斯隆笑了。  

“感觉它从没离开过。”

1769847435.name: A Distant Pull
1769847435.subtitle: From distant hollows, a call demands attention.
1769847435.subtitle_zh: 从遥远的空洞中传来了一声索求关注的呼唤。
1769847435.text:
Titan fell into darkness only moments before the first Tomb-craft arrived. They bore the burning sigils of War, dripping soulfire from their branded hulls as if it gushed from an open wound.  

Beneath the churning sea, a Guardian Light wrapped in metal, yet to be coiled in promise, watched the skies turn to ink, and Hive fiends disembark the invading craft. 

Proclamations scattered across the methane ocean, eager words searing each wave's crest with jade flame. The Hive's intent was clear: tear asunder the claims of the Witch Sister. Raise the banners of War. 

Led by a massive Knight, Acolytes descended to depths once infested by denizens of the lie, down to where the song of trickery echoed from long-dead shrieks. They marched in adorant procession, surrounded by a host of Thralls that defaced the remnant traces of Savathûn's holdings with hungering delight. 

Held aloft in the claws of a central Acolyte was a Wizard's skull, recovered from the flame-licked wash before Titan's capture. The Acolyte delicately placed the skull upon a ragged sheet of conquered foe-flesh while others carved a circle of runes around it. 

The Acolytes took position over the runes. They threw their heads back and howled a discordant melody that ignited the rune-circle, consuming each of them in soulfire conflagration. 

The melody took hold, flooding the flesh of the accompanying Thralls with frenzy. They surged forward, kicked and clawed their kin in a mad scramble to reach the skull first. To claim it. 

Each time the melody thrummed, an Acolyte turned to ash. Each time the melody thrummed, spilled Thrall viscera twisted into fetid swirls around the skull. 

Blood and ash was offered until none remained; the Knight stepped forward, brandishing a blade of deathly menace. 

"I call Xivu Arath. I invoke War's presence. Take this dreg, cast out by your sister. Take her claims as your own." 

The churning soulflame was drawn into the Knight's deathly blade, then plunged into the Wizard's skull. The runic circle projected an ancient realm, and the Knight felt watchful eyes leering from atop a distant Black Terrace perched above that projected realm. The thunderous response pressed him to his knees. 

KELGORATH, I ACCEPT THINE OFFERINGS 

THROUGH WILL, LIES ARE UNEARTHED 

THROUGH WILL, LIES ARE MADE TRUTH 

THROUGH WILL, LIES FALL TO CONQUEST 

 KUDAZAD, BOUND, YOU ARE NAMED IN SERVICE
1769847435.text_zh:
当第一艘棺艇抵达时，土卫六刚陷入黑暗不久。它们身上带着燃烧的战争印记，灵魂之火从烙印的船体上滴落下来，就像从一个裸露的伤口里喷涌而出。  

翻腾的大海之下，一个被金属包裹、尚未被承诺缠绕的守护者光能，看着苍穹化为黑墨，邪魔族恶魔走下了入侵的飞船。 

宣言散布在甲烷海中，热切的话语用翡翠色的火焰灼烧着每一个浪尖。邪魔族的意图很明确：撕碎女巫姐妹的要求。高举战争的旗帜。 

在一位高大骑士的带领下，仆从们下潜到谎言居民曾经出没的深处，直至诡计之歌在早已死亡的尖叫声中回荡的地方。他们列队前进，一群怨魂环绕周围，如狼似虎般地毁坏萨瓦图恩的残存痕迹。 

中央仆从的爪子高举着一个巫师的头骨，那是在土卫六被占领之前从火焰舔舐的浪花中找到的。这名仆从把头骨轻轻地放在一块被征服的敌人烂肉上，其他仆从则在它周围刻了一圈符文。 

仆从们在符文四周站定位置。他们仰起头，嚎叫着一段不怎么悦耳的旋律，点燃了符文圈，灵魂之火在烈焰中吞噬了他们每个人。 

旋律席卷而来，疯狂地淹没了一旁怨魂的肉体。它们冲上前去，在疯狂的争夺中对同类又踢又抓，想要率先拿到头骨。夺取它。 

每当旋律弹起，一个仆从就会化为灰烬。每当旋律弹起，四溅的怨魂内脏就会在头骨周围扭曲成恶臭的漩涡。 

鲜血和灰烬轮番奉上，直到一个也不剩；骑士走上前去，挥舞着死亡威胁之刃。 

“我呼唤希乌阿拉斯。我号召战争的降临。拿走这些被你的姐妹扔出去的渣滓。将她的主张据为己有。” 

翻腾的灵魂之火被吸入骑士的死亡之刃，然后插入了巫师的头骨。符文圈投射出一块古老领地，骑士感到远处的黑色平台上有一双警惕的眼睛在斜视着。雷鸣般的应答促使他跪了下来。 

克尔格拉斯，我接受你的贡品 

经由意志，谎言会被揭穿 

经由意志，谎言成为真相 

经由意志，谎言会被征服 

 附庸库达萨德，你已被任命

1081724548.name: Rapacious Appetite
1081724548.subtitle: Hunt, feed, hunt again.
1081724548.text:
To: Vanguard High Command 
Incident Report Source: Scout Patrol 919 
Report: Kraken Mare, Exterior Shelf Shallows—High Priority-0174 
Target: J4W-S, Aberrant Houseless Servitor, Wrathborn 
Threat Type: Ambusher, supported by hostile Warband(s), Engage with Extreme Caution 
Noted Casualties: 8, not all incidents recorded. 
Known Armaments: Servitor Eye Projector, Material Denial Shield, Displacement Thresher, Kinetic Impact. 

Incident Report-309: Servitor J4W-S was spotted in the southern ridge of Kraken Mare. Dive Tactical was notified, and fireteams were pulled from the area. Upon retreat, one fireteam was ambushed by a Hive warband. J4W-S then dove from above, and crashed into the fireteam, using its body as a kinetic driver. One fireteam member was killed on impact, and their Ghost was captured. Both remaining Guardians were able to escape after a prolonged exchange of fire. 

          RE: Recovery teams dispatched. 

Recovery Incident Report-317: Dive Tactical and accompanying fireteams prepared an ambush and engaged J4W-S outside of Delta Sector. When caught in the crossfire, J4W-S initially fled the battle under the cover of Taken forces, only to harry the fireteams with guerrilla attacks from the surrounding methane sea. Note this Wrathborn Servitor retains the use of their displacement thresher and has begun using it to pick up and drop fireteam members into the methane sea's open depths, outside the safety of the coral shelves. The thin density of the liquid makes survival without independent propulsion unlikely and recovering remains for Ghost resurrection difficult. Dive Tactical is advised not to engage J4W-S near shelf drops or cliff faces in the future. 

          RE: J4W-S has been confirmed to have been converted to a Wrathborn Servitor. This would explain its aggression and predatory behaviors. Following notable operator losses, Dive Tactical has erected radar buoys to detect ambushes in what have come to be known as the Servitor's hunting grounds.
1081724548.text_zh:
接收方：先锋最高指挥部 
事件报告来源：斥候巡逻919 
报告：克拉肯海，外大陆架浅海—高优先级-0174 
目标：J4W-S，异常无氏族魔眼，暴怒之子 
威胁类型：伏击者，受敌对战团支援，作战须极度谨慎 
伤亡记录：8人，并未记录所有事件。 
已知武器：魔眼之眼投射器，物质拒止护盾，位移长尾鲨，动能冲击。 

事件报告-309：克拉肯海南部山脊发现J4W-S魔眼行迹。已通知潜水战术指挥，各火力战队也已从现场撤离。撤退时，一支火力战队遭到了邪魔族战团的伏击。J4W-S随后从上方俯冲，利用身体作为动能驱动器撞向火力战队。一名火力战队成员在撞击中被杀，其机灵被俘获。剩下两名守护者在长时间交火后逃脱了。 

          回复：已派出回收小队。 

回收事件报告-317：潜水战术指挥和随行的火力战队准备了伏击，并在三角洲区外与J4W-S交战。陷入交火时，J4W-S最初在傀儡军团部队的掩护下逃离战斗，随后用来自周围甲烷海的游击攻击骚扰火力战队。请注意，这一暴怒之子魔眼仍能使用其位移长尾鲨，并已开始利用它来抓取火力战队成员，并将其投掷到珊瑚陆架安全地带之外的甲烷海开放深处。稀薄的液体密度使得在缺少独立推进系统的情况下不太可能生存，而回收遗骸供机灵复活也愈发困难。下潜战术指挥建议在未来不要与J4W-S在陆架下降地带或悬崖附近交战。 

          回复：J4W-S已确认转化为暴怒之子魔眼。这就可以解释其好斗与掠食行为。在损失了相当数量的操作员后，潜水战术指挥已部署雷达浮标，以探测魔眼狩猎场的伏击。

4066778670.name: Thin Precipice
4066778670.subtitle: Sharpened, from tip to hilt, drawing from all who partake in the ritual of war.
4066778670.subtitle_zh: 从刀尖到刀柄都尖锐无比，从所有参与战争仪式的人身上汲取。
4066778670.text:
Kelgorath kneels before a feeble altar in an empty court. A dead Knight's realm. A shriveled, fleshless rind. A cautionary tale. 

A Wizard floats over the altar. "The High Celebrant's domain was once a grand place of adoration. It holds a mighty tribute." The Wizard, Rakthrin, War-Council, whispers Xivu Arath's bait to the Knight. 

Kelgorath remembers how Savathûn sought the Sky and became its puppet, all so she could usurp sword logic. "Favor wanes. It can be rekindled." 

"You were disarmed. Shamed. Beaten so many times by a Light-wielder." 

Kelgorath stands, spinning to face Rakthrin. He thrusts a claw forward at the Wizard's throat, but she swoops back from his reach.  

Kelgorath sneers. "I need no blade; I am wielded. The plates upon my body are razors." 

"Should you have remained with Savathûn and prayed to her to give you the Light… perhaps you would have found greatness then. You wither without her favor." 

"I spit on the Witch Sister! I am an instrument of War!" 

"Not yet. Not truly." 

Rakthrin conjures a dark bolt of lightning that saps the room's dim lighting and casts it into the altar. The altar splits apart with a timbered snap, revealing an emerald sliver of a blade, bleeding shade and whispering rapture. "A shard of the Taken King's blade. Conquered out of love. Stolen away from Saturn's shadow." 

Kelgorath fixates upon the blade shard. The Wizard gestures to it with a lipless smile, and the Knight steps forward.

"I will take it. To be an instrument of her will. To cleanse the hate of weakness with loving violence." Kelgorath genuflects and encloses his claws around the emerald sliver, wisps of shadow spilling between the gaps in his claws. "I offer myself to this union." 

The barrier of his flesh melts away. A will not his own enraptures him.  

Kelgorath, Risen from Bones, Taken by War.
4066778670.text_zh:
克尔格拉斯跪在空荡庭院里一个光线微弱的祭坛前。死去骑士的领地。干瘪无肉的外壳。警诫的故事。 

一名巫师漂浮在圣坛上。“高阶颂扬者的领地曾经是一处宏大的崇拜之地。它承载着强大的贡品。”战争议会巫师拉克瑟林，对骑士低语着希乌阿拉斯的诱饵之言。 

克尔格拉斯记得萨瓦图恩如何寻求苍穹并成为它的傀儡，这一切都是为了侵占邪剑守则。“偏爱消逝。可以重新点燃它。” 

“你被一个负光者缴械、羞辱和击败了那么多次。” 

克尔格拉斯站了起来，转身面对着拉克瑟林。他把一只爪子伸向巫师的喉咙，但她退到了他够不着的地方。  

克尔格拉斯冷笑道。“我不需要刀刃；我即是兵器。我身上的鳞片就是剃刀。” 

“如果你有留在萨瓦图恩身边，祈祷她给你光能…也许你会成就伟大。没了她的宠爱，你就会枯萎。” 

“我唾弃女巫姐妹！我是战争的工具！” 

“还不是，还算不上。” 

拉克瑟林召唤了一道黑暗的闪电，侵蚀着房间昏暗的灯光，把它投入了祭坛。祭坛随着一声木质撕裂声分崩离析，露出一片翡翠般的刀刃，流着阴影之血和窃窃私语的狂喜。“邪神之刃的碎片。因爱而被征服。从土星的阴影中被窃取。” 

克尔格拉斯盯着刀刃碎片。巫师带着无唇的微笑朝它示意，骑士走上前去。

“我会拿走它。成为她意志的工具。用爱的暴力来净化对软弱的仇恨。”克尔格拉斯跪下来，用爪子抓住了翡翠银片，一缕缕影子从爪子的缝隙中溢出来。“我把自已奉献给这样的结合。” 

他肉体的屏障消失了。一个不属于他的意志令他着迷。  

他成为了战争傀儡，白骨复生者，克尔格拉斯。

1757202961.name: Greasy Luck
1757202961.subtitle: Death to the living, long life to the killers
1757202961.text:
this will not reach you 

anything a knife writes would never 

but no more speaking 

that time is over 

  

Im sorry 

  

I see the waves 

I see the ship 

                         sinking 

  

the sky is filled with shadow 

  

I love you 

I love you 

 

Im alone 

 

what hurts me 

is you are too
1757202961.text_zh:
你不会看到这些的 

刀刃写下的都不会 

但不再多说了 

那时间已结束 

  

我很抱歉 

  

我看到了海浪 

我看到了飞船 

                         在下沉 

  

天空布满阴影 

  

我爱你 

我爱你
