心痛的是 

你也如此

1125217994.name: New Pacific Epitaph
1125217994.subtitle: "This isn't happening. This isn't happening. This isn't happening."
1125217994.subtitle_zh: “这不可能发生。不可能。绝不可能。”
1125217994.text:
Beyond the dappled sea spray on the bedroom window, escape craft and their blue contrails sweep past the Arcology as beams of orange light punctuate the sky. They cut through contrails with certainty, and before long, each craft erupts in blossoms of fire and brilliant warmth.  

No one is leaving Titan. 

Nadia Jahandar is not leaving. She has a cup of tea cooling on the windowsill, a collection of her late brother's poetry on her tablet, and the recording of her last piano recital playing on her headphones. The roar of the apocalypse accompanies her. She looks away from the window. 

I stepped into the stars 
Because the seas were explored 
No dragons on our maps 
Islanded in a sea of night 
Though it could never be home 
No hearths in the gulf 

Nadia reaches for her tea, glancing out the window to watch the sea rise up in a kilometers-high wall. It casts a shadow so long, it throws the Arcology into darkness.  

She will tell her brother that this poem is her favorite.
1125217994.text_zh:
在卧室窗户上斑驳的浪沫外，逃生艇以及它们蓝色的尾迹扫过生态园区，橙色的光束点缀着天空。它们无一例外地穿过尾迹，不久后，每艘飞艇都迸发出花束般的火焰和绚烂的暖意。  

没人能离开土卫六。 

娜迪娅·贾汉达没打算离开。她把一杯茶放在窗台上冷却，平板电脑上是她已故兄弟的诗集，耳机里播放着她最后一次钢琴独奏会的录音。大灾难的轰鸣声伴随着她。她把目光从窗边移开。 

我踏入群星 
因为海洋已被探寻 
我们的地图上没有巨龙 
孤立在夜色的海洋中 
虽然它永远无法成为家园 
海湾里没有壁炉 

娜迪娅伸手去拿茶，瞥了眼窗外，看到海水涨成好几千米高的墙。它投下了长长的阴影，让生态园区笼罩进黑暗之中。  

她会告诉她兄弟，这首诗是她最喜欢的。

839786290.name: Cold Comfort
839786290.subtitle: "Do not be afraid."
839786290.text:
The submersible hits the water at an odd angle, throwing the passengers against the bulkhead. No one was buckled in before it dropped. Confusion erupts from the team of scientists as they begin their descent: the currents shouldn't be as strong as they are. Titan's atmosphere doesn't allow for that.  

But they are swept away. 

The pilot struggles to orient the craft, and for a moment, they are vertical, able to see blooms of fire expanding above the surface of the ocean. The submersible pitches in another direction, sinking rapidly.  

They have nowhere to go but down. Hide under the ice shelf, wait the chaos out. Hope for rescue. 

One of the scientists leans out of her seat, pressing her face up against the port window. A shape moves in the dark, too massive to be another craft, too sinuous to be mechanical. The scientist reaches back, blindly grasping for the hand of the person seated next to her. 

The shape in the sea doubles back, following the speed and telemetry of the current-swept submersible. Everyone sees it now, blocking out what little light is left as they sink past the ice shelf. It dives with them. Not after, but with. 

She will not let them die alone.
839786290.text_zh:
潜水器以某种奇怪的角度撞击水面，将乘客抛向舱壁。没人来得及在它落下前扣上安全带。当他们开始下降时，科学家团队突然感到困惑不解：洋流不可能像现在这么强。土卫六的大气提供不了这种条件。  

但他们被冲走了。 

领航员努力调整潜水器的航向，有一瞬间，他们是垂直的，能够看到花束般的火焰在海面上蔓延。潜水器转向另一个方向，迅速下沉。  

他们无处可去，只能往下。躲在冰架底，等待混乱过去。希望能够获救。 

其中一位科学家从座位上探出身子，把她的脸贴在左舷窗上。有个形状在黑暗中移动着，庞大异常，应该不是潜水器，又很蜿蜒，应该不是机械制品。科学家的手向后伸，盲目地抓住坐在她身旁的人的手。 

海水中的形状随着洋流裹卷潜水器的速度和遥测信号折回。现在每个人都能看到它，当他们沉到冰架下时，它挡住了仅存的一点光线。它和他们一起下潜。不是跟着他们，而是拽着他们。 

她不会让他们孤独地死去。

3262192268.name: No Survivors
3262192268.subtitle: "There's not enough seats."
3262192268.text:
Klaxons blare across the hangar. Seven terrified people huddle by the escape craft's open hatch, bracing against the wind cutting through the open hangar bay doors. 

"You're not leaving me behind!" an engineer shouts. He holds a young man hostage, arm like a vice around his neck. Pistol wavering. 

The last security officer looks down at his counterpart, long dead and bleeding out on the floor. He isn't sure how many rounds are left in his gun. His hands are shaking from the cold. From the reverberations of explosions shuddering through the superstructure. 

"Let me on! Make room for me! Move!" the engineer demands, motioning to the side with his gun. The security officer takes the opportunity and fires. He's not steady, hits the engineer and his hostage. Both crumple to the ground. The crowd behind him is screaming. 

The security officer curses, hurrying over to save the hostage. He hears a hatch door close behind him, turns to see the escape craft take off. He screams something, but it's cut short—the engineer was still alive. He doesn't even feel the bullet enter his spine before he hits the ground. 

From where he lies on the freezing cold floor, he can see the escape craft outside the hangar bay. Tears well up in his eyes. The last thing he sees is a beam of fire descending from the sky. 

His chest stills as the escape craft disintegrates, shot down by a Warsat.
3262192268.text_zh:
警笛声响彻机库。七名吓坏了的人挤在逃生艇敞开的舱口旁，顶着穿过敞开的机库大门的狂风。 

“你们不能丢下我！”一位工程师喊道。他挟持一名年轻人作为人质，胳膊像虎钳一样用手缠住他的脖子。手枪摇摆不定。 

最后一名安保人员低头看着他的同事，那人早就死了，倒在地上流血不止。他不确定枪里还有多少子弹。他的手冷得直发抖。上层构造因爆炸的回响而震动着。 

“让我上去！给我腾点地方！快！”工程师用枪指着侧边要求道。安保人员抓住机会开了枪。他没打准，子弹击中了工程师和人质。两人都瘫倒在地。他身后的人群在尖叫。 

安保人员咒骂着，急忙赶过去救人质。他听到身后舱门关闭的声音，转身看到逃生艇起飞。他喊了些什么，但被打断了——工程师还活着。他甚至没觉察到子弹进入自己的脊柱，就倒在了地上。 

躺在冰冷地板上，他可以看到机库外的那逃生艇。泪水在他的眼中涌动。他看到的最后一幕是一束火焰从天而降。 

逃生艇被战争卫星击落然后解体，他的胸膛也随之停止了起伏。

542573208.name: Last Rite
542573208.subtitle: How will you choose to die?
542573208.text:
Caiatl and Saladin sit alone in the council chamber. Two metal bowls bearing the inscription, Perun, sit between them. Each holds a pile of small smooth stones that rattle along with the hum of the Eligos Lex V's engine. 

Saladin rolls a stone in his fingers. He leans forward and places it on an intersection of lines seared into a thick leather mat. He taps the table beneath it. "These stones are like legions raising your banner. Each one placed is a claim." 

He leans back in his seat and gestures to her. "Turn." 

Caiatl's eyes remain on the spot where Saladin placed his stone. She flicks an azure stone from her bowl onto the mat, then nudges the stone adjacent to Saladin's last placement. 

"Aggressive. But the object isn't to kill. Establish borders. Hold territory." Saladin's words are measured as he places a counter-stone. 

Caiatl considers a flanking maneuver, then a defensive line, or— 

"Speaking of… borders…" Caiatl flanks. "You place too many between yourself and your Legionaries." 

Saladin looks up, then back to the board. 

Caiatl continues. "It is how Tarnth chooses to die. Rather than ossify into an immobile monument of bone, drawn on a cart that the young may hear their wisdom." 

Saladin shoots her a look, then connects a line of stones in defense. "I'm not an executioner." 

"You carry a large axe," she spars, placing another stone by his. 

He groans and places a stone away from the clash. 

"Tarnth respects your command, she bears your Iron Banner." Caiatl continues, "Death by your hand would be an honor." 

Saladin sighs. "That's not how I see it." 

"Because it is not YOUR custom. In the Age of Conquest, warriors nearing death were gathered into legions and deployed at the tip of the spear. A final, glorious death charge. Seen by all." 

Caiatl considers her next move. 

"Calus did away with the practice. Denied our greatest their glorious deaths. He surrounded himself with a host of petrified elders, soaking in their council. Those who resisted were shown the fighting pits, to reclaim lost honor. Most soldiers were called home to Torobatl to live out their lives in the empire, paid as citizens. But many still chose to die on distant battlefronts when the opportunity presented itself." 

"This is comfort for her." Caiatl captures her first of Saladin's stones. 

"Fine. But this is my last rite of proving." 

"Very well. She wishes you display her bleached skull in the barracks." 

Saladin glares up at her and moves to secure a corner of the board. "You're joking." 

"Yes," she snorts, "It goes to her family."
542573208.text_zh:
查厄托和萨拉丁单独坐在议事厅里。两个刻有“佩纶”字样的金属碗放在他们之间。每个碗里都放着一堆光滑的小石头，伴着伊犁苟斯·莱克斯五号引擎的嗡鸣而咯咯作响。 

萨拉丁用手指滚动着石头。他身体前倾，把石头放在一张厚皮垫子烧焦线条的交叉点上。他敲了敲垫子下的桌子。“这些石头就像是高举你旗帜的军团。放置的每一个，都是一次占领。” 

他向后靠在座位上，向她示意着。“到你了”。 

查厄托的眼睛依然停留在萨拉丁放置石头的地方。她把碗里的一块天蓝色石头弹到垫子上，然后把它推到了萨拉丁最后一次落子的相邻位置。 

“咄咄逼人。但目的并非杀戮。而是建立边界。守住领土。”萨拉丁放置了一块反制的石头，话语把握有度。 

查厄托思考进行侧攻，然后建立防线，或者—— 

“说到…边界…”查厄托选择了侧攻。“你在自己和你的军团士兵之间放置了太多。” 

萨拉丁抬头看了一眼，然后把视线转回到棋盘上。 

查厄托继续说道。“塔恩斯选择了那样的死法。宁可那样，而不是僵化成一座动弹不得的骨头纪念碑，被拉上一辆马车，让年轻人能听到其智慧。” 

萨拉丁看了她一眼，然后用一排石头进行防御。“我不是刽子手。” 

“可你拿着一把大斧头，”她反驳道，在他的石头旁放置了另一块。 

他咕哝着，把一块石头放在远离交锋的地方。 

“塔恩斯尊重你的命令，她肩抗着你的铁旗。”查厄托继续说道，“死在你手上是一种荣誉。” 

萨拉丁叹了口气。“我不这么看。” 

“因为这不是你的习俗。在征服时代，濒死的战士集结成军团，被部署成矛尖。最后一次光荣的死亡冲锋。让世人有目共睹。” 

查厄托思忖着下一着棋。 

“卡鲁斯废除了这种做法。否认了我们最伟大的光荣死亡。他身边围着一群僵化的长老，沉浸在他们的议会中。那些反抗的人被带到角斗场，以夺回失去的荣誉。大多数士兵都被召回图罗巴特尔，在帝国中度过余生，以公民的身份获得报酬。但一有机会，许多人还是会选择死在遥远的战场上。” 

“这对她来说是种慰藉。”查厄托拿下了她第一块萨拉丁的石头。 

“好吧。但这是我最后的证明仪式。” 

“很好。她希望你在军营里展示她漂白的头骨。” 

萨拉丁抬头瞪着她，下出守住棋盘一角的一步棋。“你在开玩笑吧。” 

“是的，”她哼了一声，“那个要给她的家人。”

4005780578.name: Unexpected Resurgence
4005780578.subtitle: "Stasis was the thesis. Strand is his dissertation." —Sister Faora
4005780578.subtitle_zh: “冰影曾是他的硕士论文。缚丝现在是他的博士论文。”——菲奥拉修女
4005780578.text:
Shayura kneels in front of a gilded copper pot and the young bonsai rising from inside it. Tucked away in the soil are the vertically sliced fragments of a Ghost. The tree grows up around them, and where root and dirt meet, Shayura places a stick of lit incense. 

The Bazaar is quiet as she lifts the freshly potted tree and places it on a low table, overlooking the City the Traveler once protected. "You are missed," Shayura whispers, brushing her fingertips against the soft branches.  

The remains of Reed-7's Ghost stare up at her.  

For a moment, she remembers seeing the cockpit of her jumpship littered with the Ghosts of her victims. Yet her Ghost was spared the Witness's wrath. Aisha's too, but this pain isn't about her. It is selfish. Shayura's heart lurches, and she tries to center herself. 

"I exalt my fireteam."  

"Is that a prayer?" A woman asks behind her. Shayura quickly turns and spots a stranger approaching between stalls. She carries a glaive like a walking staff. Its design matches the ornate pattern of her robes. Familiar. Osirian. 

"…Of sorts," Shayura answers belatedly.  

The robed woman bows, apologetic. "I ask for a moment of your time, Shayura."  

Hearing her name from the mouth of a stranger sets Shayura on edge. She glances at the memorial, then stands.  

"Please, leave me be." 

"My name is Sister Faora," the robed woman continues. "Devotee of Osiris, Seeker of Truth. Outcast." The last title earns a squint from Shayura. 

"What do you want, Outcast Faora?" 

Sister Faora gestures to herself with one hand. "Only to offer you something that few others would, given your history." 

Shayura raises a brow in challenge. Faora boldly meets it. 

"Friendship."
4005780578.text_zh:
沙玉拉跪在一个镀金的铜壶前，幼小的盆栽从壶内长出来。埋在土里的是被垂直切割的机灵碎片。树苗在它们周围生长着，而在树根和泥土相遇的位置，沙玉拉放上了一根点燃的香。 

集市寂静无声，她举起刚栽下的树，放在一张矮桌上，俯瞰着旅行者曾经保护过的圣城。“我们想念你，”沙玉拉低声说道，用指尖抚摸着柔软的树枝。  

里德-7机灵的残骸凝视着她。  

有那么一瞬间，她忆起了跃迁飞船的驾驶舱里到处都是受害者机灵的画面。但她的机灵躲过了见证者的怒火。艾莎的也是，但这痛苦与她无关。太自私了。沙玉拉的心猛地一跳，她试图集中注意力。 

“我赞美我的火力战队。”  

“是在祈祷吗？”一个女人在她身后问道。沙玉拉迅速转身，发现一名陌生人正在走近。她像拐杖一样拿着偃月。它的设计与她长袍的华丽图案相匹配。看起来很熟悉。奥斯里斯的风格。 

“…算是吧，”沙玉拉半晌才回答。  

穿长袍的女人带着歉意鞠了个躬。“我想占用你一点时间，沙玉拉。”  

从陌生人的口中听到她的名字让沙玉拉紧张不安。她望了一眼纪念碑，然后站了起来。  

“请不要打扰我。” 

“我是菲奥拉修女，”穿长袍的女人继续说。“奥斯里斯的信徒，真理追寻者。放逐者。”听到最后那个称号，沙玉拉瞥了她一眼。 

“你想做什么，放逐者菲奥拉？” 

菲奥拉修女用一只手对自己做了个手势。“鉴于你的过去，我只是想给你一样很少有人愿意提供的东西。” 

沙玉拉挑衅地扬起了眉毛。菲奥拉大方相迎。 

“友谊。”

1123421440.name: Epochal Integration
1123421440.subtitle: "It is a wonder that we are still here. Keep it that way." —Osiris
1123421440.subtitle_zh: “我们还在这真是个奇迹。继续保持下去。”——奥斯里斯
1123421440.text:
The Ishtar Collective's researchers knew no bounds: amidst a sea of their data, I found schematics for a weapon using the Veil's paracausal field as supplemental power. However, it appears the weapon project was abandoned early. I hoped I could finish what they started, and so I share the fruits of my labor with you, Guardian. 

Fusing Golden Age designs with modern necessity involved considerable guesswork, made worse by the lack of an extant prototype. I took liberties with the original schematic, choosing what to preserve, what to discard, and how to harmonize elements separated by centuries.  

The first fabricated pieces clicked into place, and abstraction became reality. But it was not what I envisioned. Too cold, impersonal, and utilitarian.  

I confess, I was sorely tempted to discard everything and start over. Yet I knew if I gave in to that familiar impulse, the hours would slip into days, and the days into months, while I strained for the vanishing limit of perfection in vain. 

In the end, I asked Saint if he could suggest the finishing touches. Engraving a pattern into the steel was his idea. I took his word for it; aesthetic flourishes are not a strength of mine. 

The result is this weapon: a synthesis of disparate elements into an unexpected shape. I am eager to see what you add to it, Guardian. 

—Osiris
1123421440.text_zh:
伊什塔集团的研究者们可谓旷古绝今：在他们几乎无尽的数据之中，我找到了一种使用面纱的超因果力场作为额外能源的武器图纸。然而，这种武器的研发似乎提前终止了。我希望我能实现他们的愿景，所以我将把自己的劳动成果与你分享，守护者。 

将黄金时代的设计与现代的需要融合在一起涉及到相当多的揣测，由于缺乏现存的原型，这个步骤会更加艰难。我对原始图纸进行了一些修改：我留了些东西，也丢了些东西。我还思考了如何协调相隔几个世纪的设计元素。  

第一批零件新鲜出炉，完美地嵌进了武器主体。梦想成为了现实，但它与我的期待不相符。它太过冷酷、没有人情味，而且过于功利。  

我承认，我很想抛弃一切，重新开始。但我知道，如果我屈服于这种熟悉的冲动，那么任凭时光流逝，岁月蹉跎，只会余我徒劳地追求完美的极限。 

到最后，我问圣人对完成这把枪有何建议。他的主意是在金属部分雕刻图案。我听从了：美学上的修饰并不是我的强项。 

这件武器便是成果：一把由不同的元素糅合而成的、形态瑰异的武器。我等不及想看看你会为它添上什么了，守护者。 

——奥斯里斯

3256453690.name: Crowning Duologue
3256453690.subtitle: The stage is yours.
3256453690.text:
It took a full seven minutes before Lord Shaxx stopped pretending that the screen in front of him was transmitting a live Crucible match and not a looped recording. He finally let out an aggrieved sigh and folded his arms across his chest.  

"Forge." 

"If you can spare a few moments," Lord Saladin said, with grim humor, "I wanted to talk."  

Shaxx leveled his helmet in Saladin's direction.  

Saladin returned his stare. "Fine. It isn't a matter of wanting. We need to talk." Saladin braced himself. "About Twilight Gap."  

Shaxx turned to face Saladin, arms sliding down to his sides. His chest expanded as he filled the great bellows of his lungs.  

"You made the right call," Saladin said, quickly.  

There was a muffled, choked sound from beneath Shaxx's helmet.  

"We've always known that much." Saladin's mouth twisted unhappily. He turned his gaze to the City's horizon, feigning interest in a flooded crater near the outskirts. "Even if I refused to admit it." 

"You saw hope where I couldn't. I told myself your defiance was grandstanding." Saladin laughed ruefully. "I'd given up. But you—you and your fireteam bought us time. Enough time for all of us to change." 

Shaxx stood unmoving. They both waited in protracted silence.  

At last, Saladin sighed. "After all these years, after everything… I trust your judgment. I just wanted you to know that."  

Shaxx's helmet shifted, just slightly. "Before the end?"  

"Before whatever comes next."  

Shaxx nodded slowly.  

"You know, I had a host of incredibly scathing comments prepared for this moment."  

Saladin smiled. "I bet you did."
3256453690.text_zh:
足足过了七分钟，领主沙克斯才终于承认，他面前屏幕上的循环录像并不是熔炉竞技场比赛直播。他终于愤愤不平地叹了一口气，双臂交叉在胸前。  

“弗吉。” 

“有时间的话，”领主萨拉丁带着冷酷的幽默说，“我想和你谈谈。”  

沙克斯把头盔移向了萨拉丁的方向。  

萨拉丁回瞪着他。“好吧。这不是想不想的问题。我们需要谈谈。”萨拉丁打起精神。“关于暮光峡谷。”  

沙克斯转身面对萨拉丁，双臂滑落到身体两侧。他深吸了一大口气，胸膛随之扩张起来。  

“你做了正确的决定，”萨拉丁赶紧说道。  

沙克斯的头盔下面传来了低沉的哽咽声。  

“我们一直都心知肚明。”萨拉丁不高兴地撇了撇嘴。他把目光转向圣城的地平线，假装对郊区附近被水淹没的一处坑穴感兴趣。“虽然我拒绝承认。” 

“你看到了我无法看到的希望。我告诉自己，你的反抗不过是哗众取宠。”萨拉丁苦笑起来。“我放弃了。但你——你和你的火力战队为我们争取了时间，足以让我们所有人去做出改变。” 

沙克斯一动不动地站着。他俩都在漫长的沉默中等待着。  

最后，萨拉丁叹了口气。“对不起，沙克斯。这么多年过去了，发生了那么多事…我相信你的判断。我只是想让你知道这一点。”  

沙克斯的头盔微微晃动了一下。“在结束之前？”  

“在接下来发生的事之前。”  

沙克斯缓缓点了下头。  

“你知道么，为这一刻，我准备了一大堆苛责的话。”  

萨拉丁笑了。“早料到了。”

3825487421.name: I. Debriefing
3825487421.text:
"Sloane?"

Commander Zavala's voice sounds distorted, as if he were underwater. The chill running down Sloane's spine only adds to the sensation.

She knows she had been gone for a while. For how long, she isn't sure— Síocháin's internal chronometer had glitched out shortly after Titan disappeared and took them with it. Sloane had been left to measure the passage of time by feeling it in her bones.

The universe moved on without her. That was to be expected. But Sloane still can't believe Zavala's debriefing… the words crash into her like one tidal wave after another, threatening to knock her off balance and fill her lungs with brine.

Stasis. Caiatl. The House of Light. Savathûn. The Lucent Brood. Neomuna.

…Amanda.

Sloane's thoughts drift back to the wake of the Red War. Call signs and banter as Holliday's Hawk flew overhead. Small talk between sorties. Quiet moments and shared laughter between the staccato of gunfire and roar of jet engines. A friendship chiseled into marble, one stroke at a time.

Amanda was always fearless. The first to stand up, the last to go home.

Why did she always have to be such a damn hero?

"Sloane," Zavala says again.

She realizes she's been clenching her fists. She might have been shaking. Sloane's eyes focus once more, meeting those of her commanding officer.

He looks different than she remembers. His eyes seem older, wiser, and filled with something that catches her off guard.

Is that… pity?

Can he see it? This pit growing in her stomach, this yawning chasm that yearns to swallow her whole. Is he questioning her resolve? Her ability to see this through, to do her duty back on the frontline so others don't have to?

DOES HE SEE YOUR WEAKNESS?

Sloane clenches her fists again.

"Sir," she replies. Her voice holds steady. "Understood, sir."

Zavala's brow furrows. "It's a lot to take in. If you need to—"

"I don't."

A moment of silence passes. Sloane does not let him see anything. Zavala nods.

"Very well," he says. "Dismissed."

Sloane salutes and returns to her station.

She would be the first to stand up.

And the last to go home.
3825487421.text_zh:
“斯隆？”

指挥官萨瓦拉的声音听起来有些失真，像是在水下一般。斯隆脊背上的寒意让这种感觉更强烈。

她知道自己已经消失一段时间了。但她不确定是多久——在土卫六带着他们消失后不久，西奥昌的内部计时器就出故障了。斯隆只能透过自己骨头里的感觉来测量时间。

没有她，宇宙依然继续前行。这是意料之中的事。但斯隆还是不敢相信萨瓦拉的简报…其中的字字句句就像汹涌的潮水一般，随时可能让她失去平衡，让她喘不过气来。

冰影。查厄托。光能氏族。萨瓦图恩。光明虫群。内欧姆那。

…阿曼达。

斯隆想起了猩红战争刚打响的那些日子。霍利迪的鹰隼飞过头顶，电台中传出呼号和玩笑。任务间隙的闲聊。夹杂在零星的枪声和怒吼的喷漆引擎之间的静谧与欢笑。那一段友谊历经枪林弹雨的洗礼，坚若磐石。

阿曼达一直都勇敢无畏。第一个站出来，最后一个回家。

她为什么非得逞英雄？

“斯隆，”萨瓦拉又开口了。

她意识到自己紧攥着拳头。可能还在发抖。斯隆茫然的眼神变得清醒，与指挥官四目相对。

他看起来和她印象中不一样了。他的眼睛似乎更老成，更睿智。而且充满了某种她未曾料到的东西。

那是…怜悯？

他能看见吗？她腹中的这个裂谷正在渴望将她整个吞下。他在质疑她的决心吗？她有这个能力完成任务，执行使命，替别人上前线吗？

他看见了你的弱点吗？

斯隆又攥紧了拳头。

“长官，”她回答道。她的嗓音很稳。“明白了，长官。”

萨瓦拉皱起了眉头。“确实有很多事需要消化。如果你需要——”

“不需要。”

一时间无人开口。斯隆不会让他看见任何东西。萨瓦拉点了点头。

“那好吧，”他说。“你可以走了。”

斯隆敬了礼，动身返回她的岗位。

她会第一个站出来。

最后一个回家。

3825487422.name: II. Theory
3825487422.text:
Ikora pinches a thick and vibrant Strand thread from the air and twists it between her fingers with ease. It plies to her influence, but smooths the motions of her hands, tapering her movements to flow in cleaner lines.  

The Veil tones in rhythm with the plucks of tension rolling across her knuckles. She focuses on the subtle irregularities in each pulse, the patterns they form. There are a small few plucked reverberations that resonate out beyond the walls of this chamber, beyond the detection of her intuition, and out into the cosmos. Those capture her interest most. 

Behind her, an animated avatar escorts Osiris into the Veil's containment chamber. They gesture him toward Ikora and bid farewell.  

Osiris watches the ripples play out before him and across the fabric of reality, as a wave, then particles, then a wave again. He feels it brush over him. He steps with the cadence of each pulse sent rippling from Ikora's plucking knuckles, basking in Strand's energizing rhythm. Feeling whole again. 

"It's stronger… the Veil's signature." Ikora's voice carries a hint of learned suspicion. "Ever since we recovered Titan." 

"That is to be expected," Osiris retorts, now within the weave of droning Strand surrounding the Veil. The room around them trembles. "When Titan was torn back, the Veil took notice. It seemed to recognize Titan's arrival." 

Ikora tightens her grip on the Strand thread. "We have the Veil, our Ghosts… what are we missing? If we decipher the connection between Titan and the Veil, that connection might be what we need to follow the Witness." 

"What of the worm?" Osiris asks skeptically. "Sloane believes she is our best chance." 

"You taught me the value of a backup plan." Ikora gives him a stern look. "Titan, Savathûn's throne world, every place we've found egregore… I haven't found the exact threads yet but pull one and they all seem to spin back to Neomuna. To the Veil." 

"You're getting ahead of yourself. Following some of my… less favorable tendencies. Nimbus says we must 'flow' to understand Strand; perhaps it is the same with the Veil." Osiris moves beside Ikora and reaches up, palm parallel to the threads drawn taut from Ikora's braid of Strand. "Sol remembered Titan, in a way. The Veil's signal spiked when Titan returned from memory to reality, when the rhythm of the solar system had been restored to order." Osiris drops his hand and looks to Ikora. "Perhaps we must simply find that rhythm before we are able to interpret the beats within it." 

"And once we do… then we should be able to reverse that process," she replies. Ikora releases the thread and tracks the rippling points of connection that travel outward, along the fabric-like Strands of existence, to the walls of the containment enclosure. "We're too late in the game for something to mean nothing. It has to connect." 

Ikora sighs, then turns to Osiris. "Your flare for educating others is returning. Though I bet some would say you never lost it." She smiles. 

Osiris smirks. "Come, walk with me. We will discuss this unifying theory of yours."
3825487422.text_zh:
艾可拉从空中拿出了一条充满能量的厚重缚丝丝线，在指间把玩。它在她的影响下弯曲，使她手上的动作更加顺滑，让身法渐渐干净流畅起来。  

面纱随着她指节的旋律翻滚着。她把注意力放在了每次脉冲中微妙的不规则性，以及它们形成的规律上。有一小部分拨动的余韵回荡在这间屋子的墙壁之外，脱离了她的感知，进入了宇宙的虚空。这些现象最能引起她的兴趣。 

在她身后，一个虚拟形象护送奥斯里斯走进了面纱密封舱。它指了指艾可拉，然后告辞了。  

奥斯里斯看见涟漪在他面前和现实的结构中呈现，先是从波纹变成粒子，然后又变成波纹。他感觉到它拂过身边。他踏着艾可拉的指关节发出的每次脉冲形成的韵律，沉浸在缚丝充满活力的节奏中。这让他感到满足和完整。 

“面纱的信号…越来越强了。”艾可拉的声音中带着一丝怀疑。“从我们找到土卫六起就这样了。” 

“这不足为奇，”奥斯里斯反驳道。他现在走进了包裹面纱的一层嗡嗡作响的缚丝之中。周围的空间颤抖起来。“面纱注意到土卫六回来了。它似乎能识别出土卫六的到来。” 

艾可拉攥紧了缚丝的丝线。“我们有面纱，有机灵…还少了什么？要是能破译土卫六和面纱之间的联系，也许就有机会追踪见证者了。” 

“那蠕虫呢？”奥斯里斯怀疑地问道。“斯隆认为她是我们最好的机会。” 

“是你教我凡事都要留有后路的。”艾可拉给了他一个坚定的眼神。“土卫六、萨瓦图恩的王座世界，还有每个我们发现守望者的地方。我还没有发现关键的线束，但随便拉扯哪根，都联系着内欧姆那和面纱。” 

“你想得太超前了。这点跟我有点像…但不太好。宁博思说我们必须‘流动'起来才能理解缚丝；也许对面纱来说也是这样。”奥斯里斯走到艾可拉身边，伸出手，手掌与艾可拉编织的缚丝上绷紧的丝线平行。“某种程度上，太阳系还记得土卫六。当土卫六从记忆中回到现实，以及太阳系的韵律回归秩序时，面纱的信号出现了激增。”奥斯里斯放下手，看着艾可拉。“也许我们必须先找到这种韵律，然后才能解读其中的节奏。” 

“等我们做到了…我们应该就能逆转那种过程。”她答道。艾可拉放开丝线，寻找向前散去的连接点涟漪，沿着像织物一样的存在缚丝，直至密闭罩的墙壁。“我们起步太晚，不能再做无谓的尝试。这一切必须串联起来。” 

艾可拉叹了口气，然后转身面对奥斯里斯。“你喜欢教训别人的老毛病又回来了。不过肯定有人会说你一直如此。”她笑了。 

奥斯里斯得意地笑了一下。“陪我走走。我们好好讨论一下你的想法。”

3825487423.name: III. Legacy
3825487423.text:
A soft, simulated whimper echoes through the workshop as Archie rests his head on Ana's shoulder. They sit together in front of the harness holding up Rasputin's erstwhile Exo frame, a lifeless effigy of cables and steel.

"I know, buddy," Ana says quietly. "I miss him too."

After Rasputin's sacrifice, Ana had arranged for the Exo frame to be transferred from the H.E.L.M. to her workspace in the Tower. At the time, she had told herself that keeping the frame in storage would have been a waste; that its technological advancements could prove useful to other Exos in the future. Honestly, though, she simply wasn't ready to let go.

Nevertheless, she signed herself up for a new task, and what better way to cope with grief than by staying busy? So she had made good on her word, tinkering with the frame to reverse-engineer its more convoluted components.

That was, until she heard that Titan, like Mars before it, had suddenly reappeared. And Sloane along with it. A warrior in need of a war; a weapon in search of a target. Not unlike the Warmind. The thought kept Ana from fully burying herself in her work.

For now, she wraps her arm around Archie as her thoughts drift to all the detritus left in Rasputin's wake. Rasputin had assembled an arsenal of unfathomable scale. Remnants from thousands of Warsats strewn across the solar system, prototype weaponry never to be completed, stratagems and simulations forever forgotten.

And yet, sitting here in the shadow of his sacrifice, Ana finds that she wants to remember him by the one thing not built for war. A canine AI, created for no other purpose than companionship. One that has made a home for himself in the Tower, greeting everyone he meets on his daily walks.

In the end, Rasputin's legacy was not the war he waged, but the lives he sought to protect. The notion brings a smile to Ana's lips. It's what distinguished him from Xivu Arath. And Ana hopes that Sloane can realize the same holds true for her.

Ana looks to the Exo frame one last time before rising to her feet and pats the dog on his head. He happily wags his tail in response.

"Come on, Archie," she says as she reaches for her comms unit. "Let's go for a walk."
3825487423.text_zh:
当阿奇把头靠在阿娜的肩膀上时，一声轻柔的、模拟的呜咽声在车间里回荡。他们的面前是曾经支撑拉斯普廷的Exo框架的线束，一个由电缆和钢铁组成的遗像。

“我知道，兄弟，”阿娜轻声说。“我也想他。”

在拉斯普廷牺牲后，阿娜安排把Exo框架从应急后勤行动中心转移到她在高塔的工作间内。当时，她告诉自己，把框架放在仓库里是一种浪费；它的科技可能会在未来造福其他EXO。但其实，她只是没有准备好放手。

尽管如此，她还是接受了一项新的任务。对于她来说，只有让自己保持忙碌才能让她暂时忘记悲伤。于是她说到做到，开始修补框架，对那些较复杂的组件进行逆向研究。

后来，她听说土卫六就像之前的火星一样，突然重新出现了。而斯隆也随之归来。她是渴望战争的战士；就像不断搜寻目标的武器。与战争思维很像。这想法让阿娜无法全身心地投入到工作当中。

此刻，她搂着阿奇，任由思绪飘向拉斯普廷留下的一切。拉斯普廷组建了一个规模难以估量的武器库。遗留在太阳系里的数千个战争卫星，永远无法完成的原型武器，还有被永久遗忘的战略和模拟。

然而，阿娜坐在他牺牲的阴影下，忽然意识到她想要记住的，是那件并非为战争而造的东西。一个犬类人工智能，除了陪伴人类之外没有其他用途。它在高塔中安了家，日常散步时会向遇到的每个人打招呼。

归根结底，拉斯普廷留于世间的遗产不是他所发动的战争，而是他努力保护过的生命。这个想法让阿娜的嘴角露出了一丝微笑。这就是他和希乌阿拉斯的区别。阿娜希望斯隆也能这么想。

阿娜最后望了一眼Exo框架，然后站起身来，拍了拍狗狗的头。他高兴地摇着尾巴。

“来吧，阿奇，”她一边将手伸向通讯设备一边说道。“我们去散散步。”

3825487416.name: IV. Tether
3825487416.text:
Eris let her eyes wander over the interior of the Derelict, wondering if Drifter had hastily tidied it before her arrival. Unprecedented, but he could still surprise her. They sat together as they always did when she came to speak to him face to face. 

Drifter sighed and shook his head, flicking his coin absently between his fingers 

"Sloane's in a bad way," he said. Eris nodded. 

"And you believe my speaking to her will be beneficial," she replied. Drifter shrugged. 

"Helped a few people already, didn't it?" 

Eris considered this. 

"It should be you," she finally answered. Drifter laughed at this but fell silent when her expression remained unchanged. 

"Me?" His confusion was genuine. "Why would she trust me?" 

"Trust is built, Drifter," Eris said, "and you have taken the first step." 

He was pensive. The movement of the coin over his knuckles stopped. She continued. 

"I have found," she said, her words measured, "that one is grounded by honesty. Not only in oneself, but with those around you." 

He heaved a slow, hard breath. 

"I don't know if I can," he said, his voice small. 

"Yes. Honesty is a supplication," Eris said. "We ask to be seen. We are made vulnerable… but it is necessary to be treated with care." 

Her explanation was met with one of his rasping chuckles. Drifter leaned back in his seat, arms crossed. He held his coin tightly between a thumb and forefinger. 

"You always make somethin' so easy sound so freaky, Moondust," he said. Eris ignored this. 

"Tell her what you told me," she said more simply. "The Deputy Commander's trust will not come without reciprocity." 

Drifter fell quiet, looking down. She could hear his breath and see the strained shiver of his fingers where he clutched the coin. Eris reached out and placed a hand on his arm. He was tense to trembling, but her touch was light. Quiet. Comforting.  

He placed his hand over her own. 

"Y'know, some days I still wake up scared," Drifter said softly. "Even when I can't remember my dreams." 

"That is what it is to survive." 

There was a gentleness to Eris's voice. He nodded, then looked up and met her gaze. 

"Hey," Drifter said. "You find that joy yet?" 

"Soon," Eris answered. "Joy is built… but I have taken the first step." 

Drifter withdrew his hand. After a moment, she did too. Eris stood, and Drifter's eyes followed her.  

"Consider my counsel, Germaine." 

She knew he would. Drifter let the silence linger. 

"That's not my name," he said at last.  

"That is what you let them call you." 

It was a small link to his past. A link to a life he had picked for himself. He nodded slowly, holding her gaze. He would let her call him that too.
3825487416.text_zh:
埃里斯在遗落飞船内四处张望，心想浪客在她来之前有没有匆忙清理过这里。虽然以前从来没有过，但他没准会给自己一个惊喜。他们坐在一起，就像每次他俩面对面交谈时那样。 

浪客叹了口气，摇了摇头，漫不经心地在手指间拨弄着他的硬币。 

“斯隆的状态不好，”他说。埃里斯点了点头。 

“你觉得我和她聊聊会有点帮助，”她答道。浪客耸了耸肩。 

“以前你也帮过几个人，不是吗？” 

埃里斯考虑了一下。 

“应该你去才对，”她最后答到。浪客笑了笑，见她的表情没有变化，他陷入了沉默。 

“我？”他很疑惑。“她凭什么相信我？” 

“信任是逐渐建立起来的，浪客，”埃里斯说道，“你已经迈出第一步了。” 

他陷入了沉思。硬币在他指关节上的移动停止了。她继续往下说。 

“我发现，”她斟酌着措辞说道，“诚实是为人的基础。不仅是对自己，也包括对你周围的人。” 

他缓慢而用力地叹了口气。 

“我不知道我能不能做到，”他说道，声音很小。 

“没错。诚实是种祈求，”埃里斯说。“我们主动袒露自己。我们会变得脆弱…但一定要谨慎对待。” 

他用一声刺耳的轻笑回应她的解释。浪客向后靠在座位上，双臂交叉着。他用拇指和食指紧紧夹住硬币。 

“你总是把简单的事说得很诡异，小月月，”他说道。埃里斯没有回应。 

“告诉她，你对我说过的话，”她简明地说道。“不对等，就得不到副指挥官的信任。” 

浪客沉默了，低着头。她能听到他的呼吸，看到他抓着硬币的手指紧张地颤抖。埃里斯将一只手放在他的手臂上。他紧绷得直发抖，但她的触摸轻柔、安静而抚慰。  

他把手放在她的手上。 

“你知道吗，我有时还会在恐惧中醒来，”浪客温柔地说道。“就算我已记不起我的梦境。” 

“生存就是这样。” 

埃里斯的声音中透着一种温柔。他点点头，然后抬起眼与她的目光相遇。 

“嘿，”浪客说，“你找到快乐了吗？” 

“快了，”埃里斯答道。“快乐也是逐渐建立起来的…但我已经迈出第一步了。” 

浪客收回了他的手。过了一会儿，她也这么做了。埃里斯站起身来，浪客的眼神跟着她的动作。  

“考虑一下我的提议，杰曼。” 

她知道他会的。浪客继续沉默着。 

“那不是我的名字，”他终于说道。  

“是你让他们这么称呼你的。” 

那是他和自己过去的小小联系。与他为自己选择的生活的联系。他缓缓地点了点头，迎着她的目光。他也会让她这样叫他。

3825487417.name: V. Expectation
3825487417.text:
"I don't know what I expected." 

Zavala sets down a datapad on his desk, watching Ikora pace back and forth across his office. "I don't know," he sighs. "Maybe we should have." 

Ikora stops pacing. She turns to look at Zavala with an accusatory stare. 

"Every single enemy we've fought was brought here by the Traveler," Zavala says, slouching back into his chair. "The Hive, the Fallen, the worst of the Cabal." His attention drifts down to the datapad, Sloane's report on the origins of the Witness. "What's one more group of people chasing it?" 

"This isn't the Traveler's fault," Ikora says, doubling back on Zavala's desk. "You read the same report I did. We are at war with an entire civilization condensed into an individual. Multitudes of resentment and hatred crushed into a singularity." 

"Resentment toward the Traveler." Zavala grumbles. "I'm not saying the Traveler is at fault. I'm saying… it's a harbinger of ill-omen. Everywhere it's gone, nothing but death has followed. Does it realize that? Does it care?" 

Ikora approaches Zavala's desk. "Does it matter?" She challenges him. "It is obviously outgunned and running. For all the Traveler's strength the Witness is the greater power. It never came to us to uplift us. It came to us for help." 

Zavala is silent. He looks up from the datapad to Ikora, then sighs and slowly rises from his seat. Ikora follows him with her eyes, watching him move to the window where he would gaze out at the Traveler in the past. Now a fleet of allied vessels struggle to fill that void. 

"Were they really that unified?" Zavala asks, looking at Ikora's faint reflection. 

"Who?" 

"The Witness's people." Zavala stares past Ikora's reflection to the City. "Were they truly of one mind, united in a desire to become this… thing? Or were they forced? Compelled into action by the guidance of a few." She can feel the doubt in his words. Not in his wonderings about the Witness's origins, but in the Vanguard, in what he sees as a parallel. 

Ikora steps to Zavala's side, briefly touching his elbow. "We'd never become that," she says softly. "Not in all of Elsie's journeys through time, not in any hypothetical future. We stand together because—" 

"Because we believe what we're doing is right." Zavala interjects, looking Ikora in the eye. She sighs, turning to face the window. Her shoulders sag, and she is lost in the details of the cityscape. 

"I don't know what I expected either," Zavala says. "But you're right. It wasn't this."
3825487417.text_zh:
“我不知道我在期盼什么。” 

萨瓦拉把数据板放在桌上，看着艾可拉在他的办公室里来回踱步。“我不知道，”他叹气道。“也许我们该料到的。” 

艾可拉停下了。她转身用指责的目光看向萨瓦拉。 

“每个我们交手过的敌人都是旅行者带来的，”萨瓦拉靠在椅背上说。“邪魔族，堕落者，还有麻烦的卡巴尔。”他把注意力转向了数据板，上面有斯隆关于见证者来源的报告。“再多一批人追赶它又算得了什么？” 

“这不是旅行者的错，”艾可拉在萨瓦拉的桌前说道。“你也读了我刚读到的报告。我们是在与浓缩为个体的整个文明作战。一个由怨恨和仇恨压缩成的奇点。” 

“对旅行者的憎恶。”萨瓦拉埋怨道。“我不是说旅行者有错。只是…它总是能带来厄运。它所到之处，除了死亡，什么都没有。它意识到这一点了吗？它在乎吗？” 

艾可拉靠近了萨瓦拉的桌子。“这有关系吗？”她驳斥着他的看法。“它明显是寡不敌众，所以才被迫逃离。旅行者的力量比不过见证者。它不是来这里提升我们的。它是来求助的。” 

萨瓦拉沉默了。他把视线从数据板转向艾可拉，然后叹了一口气，慢慢地从座位上站起来。艾可拉盯着他走到了窗前；他以前总是在那里望向旅行者。现在即使是千万兵马也填不满它留下的空虚。 

“他们真的团结一心吗？”萨瓦拉对着艾可拉淡淡的倒影问道。 

“谁？” 

“见证者的族人。”萨瓦拉看向艾可拉倒影后的圣城。“他们是真的是一心一意成为这个…东西？还是被迫加入的？比如在少数人的引导下被迫采取行动。”她能感到他这番话中的疑虑。他不是对见证者的起源感到疑虑，而是对先锋，他眼中的同类感到疑虑。 

艾可拉走到萨瓦拉的身旁，触碰到了他的手肘。“我们永远不会变成那样，”她轻柔地说。“在艾尔西穿越过的所有时空中都不会，在假想中的未来里也不会。我们团结在一起是因为——” 

“因为我们相信我们在做正确的事。”萨瓦拉看着艾可拉的眼睛，打断了她。她叹了口气，转向窗户。她垂下肩膀，沉醉在圣城的风景中。 

“我也不知道我在期待什么，”萨瓦拉说。“但你说得对。我期待的不是这个。”

3825487418.name: VI. Conviction
3825487418.text:
Xivu Arath's claw wraps around a hiltless, slender vantablack blade impaled into the spine of a prostrated Knight, whose own sword clatters to the ground, inches from its grip, defeated.  

She twists her blade, and the Knight's roars echo within the Dreadnaught. Xivu's will soars through the Ascendant Plane and crosses the barrier between this world and the next to find communion with the Witness. 

Within a distant hollow, they converse. 

"They resist." The Witness's many voices cascade over each other. 

LIKE WOUNDED PREY. ALL TIRE IN TIME. 

"If they do not?" 

Xivu Arath sees the hidden thrust of its question. She knows it doubts her but does not understand why. No matter the outcome, they stand at the precipice of the Final Shape. 

THE SWORD WILL DECIDE AND BE FORGED STRONGER FOR IT. 

"It is beyond that now." 

She does not want to fall before the end. She is so close now. She saw her past failures as blood-penance, paid for strength; notches where blades and Light met her carapace were legends given form. But it is not hers to decide, nor the Witness's. The logic is a perfect, deterministic sequence of causality, built into the experience of conscious existence. None can usurp it. 

Struggle within the finite is eternal. 

"To deny the blade is heresy"—her sister's words played in her thoughts like fingertips plucking dissonant chords.  

The Witness enters the solace of Xivu's mind. Her inner throne. A salt flat sliver extending eternally into darkness. Armaments of all fashion sleep, partially sheathed between the cracks of a battlefield, where there is no place to run.  

And from Its gaze, there is no place to run. 

"They hold the worm; they will pursue her knowledge." The words echo throughout the desolate realm. "The Final Shape remains to be hewn." 

THAT I MAY WIELD IT, GLORIOUS, AGAINST THE SKY. 

"Not as you are. Weakened by defeat." The echoes slither over her mind but find little purchase. 

[LAUGHTER LIKE SCREAMING FEAR] 

MEAGER VICTORIES OF NO CONSEQUENCE; BLURRED BATTLES LOST WITHIN MY GREATER WAR. 

"No victory is of no consequence. They scheme." 

WAR IS FED, REGARDLESS. THE SKY CAN GRANT NO PASSAGE. 

"That time will soon come to an end. Show her your love, Xi Ro." 

She is alone again. 

Her blade: buried in spent ash.
3825487418.text_zh:
希乌阿拉斯的利爪握着一把细长的无柄黑色大剑，刺进了一个倒地骑士的脊柱中，而它自己的刀剑落在触手可及的地上哐当作响，毫无还手之力。  

她扭动了刀刃，骑士的吼声响彻了无畏战舰。希乌的意志在上维位面中翱翔，跨过这个世界和下一个世界之间的屏障，以求与见证者进行交流。 

他们在遥远的虚空中交谈。 

“他们抵抗。”见证者的众多声音互相交织着。 

“像是受伤的猎物。迟早会疲惫。” 

“如果没疲惫呢？” 

希乌阿拉斯看见了这个问题中暗藏的刀锋。她知道它质疑自己，但不明白理由。无论结果如何，他们都处于终焉之形的边缘。 

“那就剑下见分晓，强者为王。” 

“现在已超出那一层了。” 

她不希望在终局前倒下。她已经那样接近终局。她把自己过去的失败看作是为力量而付出的血色忏悔；刀刃和光能与她的躯壳相接，铸就了一段传奇。但这不是她的决定，也不是见证者的决定。邪剑守则是一个完美的决定性的因果关系序列，建立在有意识的存在的经验中。没有人可以篡改它。 

局限中的斗争是永恒的。 

“拒绝刀刃便是异端”——她姐姐的话在她的思绪中回荡，就像指尖拨动着不和谐的琴弦。  

见证者进入了希乌心智的慰藉之所。她内心中的王座。一片银白的盐碱地，永远延伸到黑暗中。各种各样的武器沉睡着，一部分插在战场裂缝之间，无处可逃。  

在它的注视下，无处可逃。 

“他们拥有蠕虫；他们会追求她的知识。”这句话在这荒凉的世界中回响。“终焉之形尚未凿成。” 

“我可以挥舞它，光荣地对抗苍穹。” 

“现在的你不行。失败削弱了你。”回声在她的脑中来回涌动，没有触动任何东西。 

[如同发出恐惧的尖叫般的笑声] 

“毫无意义的小胜；那些战斗在我的宏大战争中不值一提。” 

“没有什么胜利是毫无意义的。他们在密谋。” 

“无论怎样，战争已被喂饲。天空不会提供通道。” 

“那段时光即将结束。向她展示你的爱，希罗。” 

她再度孤身一人。 

她的刀刃：掩埋在灰烬之中。

4017272394.name: Deepseeker Shell
4017272394.subtitle: For Ghosts who hold on tight.
4017272394.subtitle_zh: 供坚持不懈的机灵使用。
4017272394.text:
"It seems intact," a voice chirps in the dark. 

A Ghost and their Guardian sit in an idle jumpship orbiting Neptune. The swirling cerulean hemisphere dominates the cockpit's right field of view, the rest blanketed by the gulf of space, speckled with the remains of another jumpship. 

"Should… should we boot it up?" 

The Guardian holds a datapad, the battered case adorned with Vanguard designs. Their Ghost peers over their shoulder at the only surviving piece of hardware they could salvage from the wreckage. That, and the shards of another Guardian's Ghost, respectfully arranged on the console. 

"Whatever's in that device might be important," the Ghost urges in curiosity, more than anything else.  

The Guardian gives in and turns on the datapad. After a cursory review, they find no field reports, no mission briefings. Nothing but page after page of…  

Writing. Fiction, essays… poems. A huge collection of works, decades of material, all penned by the lost Guardian. 

"This Guardian… she'd invented her own fictional universe. It must have meant so much to her to keep as closely as she did. A personal space to share thoughts without fear of judgment." The Ghost's assessment is analytical but bordering on the emotional core of the discovery. With a soft, sad beep, the Ghost looks at their Guardian and sinks down to the datapad. 

"This is a piece of who she was. Personal truths." The Ghost muses, as if on the verge of a greater understanding. "Maybe… maybe through her stories, she lives on. Maybe… that's the same for all of us." 

The Guardian says nothing and begins to read.
4017272394.text_zh:
“好像完好无损，”一个声音在黑暗中响起。 

一艘闲置的跃迁飞船正在绕海王星飞行，上面坐着一个机灵及其守护者。旋转的天蓝色半球占据了驾驶舱的右侧视野，其余部分则被太空深渊所笼罩，零星散落着另一艘跃迁飞船的残骸。 

“我们…应该启动它吗？” 

守护者手里拿着一块数据板，磨损的外壳上装饰着先锋设计。其机灵同伴越过肩膀看着这个他们唯一能从残骸中回收的硬件。这东西，以及另一位守护者机灵的碎片，被恭敬地摆放在控制台上。 

“那个装置里的东西也许很重要，”机灵催促着，好奇心显然占了上风。  

守护者让步了，打开了数据板。粗略地看了一番，没有发现任何战地报告，也没有任务简报。除了一页又一页的…  

文字。小说、散文…诗歌。大量的作品，数十年的资料，都是这位失踪的守护者写的。 

“这位守护者…她创造了自己虚构的宇宙。对她来说一定意义重大，才会放在身边。这是一个私人空间，可以分享想法而不用担心受到评判。”机灵做了一个分析性评估，但就快接近这一发现的情感核心了。随着一声柔和而悲伤的哔哔声，机灵看向守护者，然后又下降到数据板的高度。 

“这是她自我的一部分。个人的真理。”机灵沉思着，仿佛马上就要有更宏观的理解。“也许…也许通过她的故事，她可以继续存在。也许…我们所有人都是这样。” 

守护者一言未发，开始读了起来。

1279846187.name: Síocháin's Scuba Shell
1279846187.subtitle: For Ghosts who are acclimated to the pressures of the job, and the depths.
1279846187.subtitle_zh: 供适应工作压力和水深的机灵使用。
1279846187.text:
Ahsa settled from a long journey within an undersea cavern, pocketed by air. Síocháin surveyed the mix of ancient rig foundations and natural stone. It seemed quiet enough, and Sloane needed rest. No Hive barnacles grew there. Ahsa had swam far from the largest concentrations of Hive and Taken and hid away in a cove tucked beneath Golden Age wreckage. 

Ahsa filled the yawning space. She slipped through gaps and wrapped herself around plunging stalactites, her serpent-worm segmentations gripping the stone, her face half-submerged in slick methane liquid.  

Síocháin floated down from Ahsa's back and turned to see Sloane slide and crumple to the cave floor as trails of steam seeped from the cracks in the ground beneath her. 

Sloane closed her eyes. "It's cold here, but the steam… it's warm," she said weakly. 

The worm coiled a section of her body around Sloane, trapping in the heat around her.  

Síocháin watched every exchange between the two and drifted out of Sloane's earshot to the worm's gargantuan face. Ahsa's attention snapped to the blades now protruding from the Ghost's shell.  

The Ghost got good and close. "I don't know why you helped us. You seem nice. I hope you stay that way. If you're using her, if you turn coat…" Síocháin sliced the air. "I'll gut you."  

Ahsa's massive eye dialed in on Síocháin's iris. The two stared unblinkingly until the worm's eyelid gently closed. She emitted a tone of contrite harmonic equilibrium:   

|I am not your enemy|  

The Ghost scanned the worm's face, and upon seeing its benign softness, retired to the coiled shelter Ahsa had woven them.  

Sloane sat in meditation within, radiating a sense of peace that Síocháin hadn't felt from her in months. The Ghost let herself pretend for a moment that even she felt almost safe.  

*** 

It was morning before Sloane woke. Ahsa met Sloane's eyes through her visor. The tilt of her enormous head signaled a sort of greeting or eagerness. Sloane removed her helmet. "Need something?" 

         |Aiat| 

Aiat |Ahsa| Aiat 

         |Aiat| 

Sloane stumbled backwards into the cavern wall. Síocháin perked up into the air. "Boss?" 

Sloane inhaled sharply and dropped to a knee as her Ghost swooped in front of her and turned to the creature. Before she could speak, Sloane's hand was on her shell, patting her. 

"It's fine. It's… Ahsa." 

"What's an Ahsa?" Síocháin questioned. 

"Some kind of… proto-worm?" 

"Like HIVE?!" Síocháin deployed her blades. 

"No… the Hive were something before they were Hive, right? The… worm gods were too. Ahsa is… her name, I think." 

The Ghost turned to Sloane, then to Ahsa. "What does she want?" 

"To not be alone," Sloane responded. "To be… known?" 

Síocháin retreated closer to Sloane and sheathed her blades. "Right then. We like big powerful allies… let's hear what they have to say." 

A joyful shiver trundled from Ahsa's head down through her coiled form, rippling the methane pooled around her, sending tremors through the stone, causing crumbled dust to rain from overhead. Ahsa turned and focused on the pair; her massive eye spanned well beyond Sloane's entire body. The worm's sympathetic iris flexed and shimmered in hypnotic fluctuations, drawing Sloane into a dissociative state. 

         |Aiat| 

Aiat |Ahsa| Aiat 

         |Aiat| 

Sloane tumbled through timeless alien remembrances. She was shown them; spoke of them, as if they are her own. Origins and sorrows she now shared. 

"Witness… offers… powerful curse… a lust… masquerading as love." Sloane exhaled hard. But Ahsa maintained her gaze, and Sloane was swept back into the current. 

"A blade… with ambition… I don't… I don't understand." 

Flashes of fratricidal frenzy ensue: a slither-mass carnage. Those once ever-bonded now drive fang and lash of tail; proclaim Deep magics once thought too cruel to utter. All in pursuit of a sacred, gifted logic.  

Vortexes that drink empty fathoms of encrimsoned Fundament sea churn above the fray. Ahsa cannot escape the writhe without unraveling from her captors with violence. She stains her fangs with the flesh of siblings turned rivals. 

"Blood… betrays blood. To prove strength. Survival… is pain…" 

Ahsa flees, familial aftertaste fresh in her mouth. She would never know love again. This gift sours theirs, makes it vicious and hungry. 

"Rejected logic… hunted as traitor… lost like you."  

Ahsa dives into an ascendant dream. Cosmic language bathes her as she ventures—radio-songs and magnetic roars that bellow across space. She slips between worlds across great distances, breaches back into space to glide along the curvature of galaxies, chasing a distant point of Light. A solar opposite to that which Takes love. 

Sloane gasped for air. "She came here for a chance to live." 

Ahsa crashes through Titan's thick skin and into its methane sea. The expansion of Humanity across Sol unfolds as she mourns. Within a Golden Age a bond is found. The Collapse found them; a bond is lost. She wages a battle of grief, fights against nightmares of despair. 

"The Disciple… of Fear… struck Ahsa. I…" 

Síocháin piqued at the title. 

"Lost, retreating… love wanes." 

 The ebb and flow of hope. 

"Bonded…  we live…"
1279846187.text_zh:
经过漫长的旅程，阿莎在一个被空气包裹的海底洞穴里歇了下来。西奥昌检视着这一古老的钻井地基和天然石材的结合体。周围似乎很安静，而斯隆需要休息。那里没有新生的邪魔族藤壶。阿莎远离最密集的邪魔族和傀儡军团，躲进了某个黄金时代残骸之下的岩洞。 

阿莎的身体填满了这休憩之地。她滑进岩缝，将半蛇半虫的身体缠绕在突兀的钟乳石周围，半边脸浸入浮油的甲烷液体中。 

西奥昌从阿莎的背上飘下来，转头看见斯隆滑下来，瘫倒在地，蒸汽从她身下的岩缝中不断冒出。 

斯隆闭上了眼。“这里真冷，但是蒸汽…真暖和，”她虚弱地说。 

蠕虫将躯体的一部分缠在斯隆周围，裹住了热气。 

西奥昌盯着她俩的一举一动，从斯隆的耳边飞过，飘到了蠕虫那张巨大的脸庞前。阿莎的注意力一下子被机灵外壳上突出的刀刃吸引了过去。 

机灵凑近了。“我不知道你为何要帮我们。你看起来挺可靠。我希望事实如此，若你想利用她、计划背叛她…”西奥昌划着空气。“我会宰了你。” 

阿莎的大眼注视着西奥昌的瞳孔。双方一眼未眨，直到蠕虫轻轻地合上眼皮。一股稍带悔悟，但平稳和谐的声音从她体内传出： 

|我不是你们的敌人| 

机灵扫视着蠕虫的脸庞，看到那和善的温柔后，飞回了阿莎用蜷曲的身体构成的小窝中。 

斯隆在里面打坐冥想，散发出平静的气场。西奥昌已经好几个月没有感受到她散发这种气息了。机灵也装出一副暂时感到安全的样子。 

*** 

斯隆醒来已是早晨。阿莎透过斯隆的面甲看着她的眼睛。她倾斜着的巨大头颅透着某种问候或渴望。斯隆摘下头盔，“怎么了？” 

         |阿特| 

阿特|阿莎|阿特 

         |阿特| 

斯隆踉跄着向后退了几步，撞到了洞壁上。西奥昌一下跳到了空中。“老大？” 

斯隆猛地吸了口气，瘫跪在地。她的机灵噌地一下冲到她面前，转向那巨大生物。她还没来得及开口，斯隆便把手放在她的机壳上，抚摸着她。 

“没事的。她是…阿莎。” 

“阿莎是什么？”西奥昌问。 

“某种…原生蠕虫？” 

“邪魔族那样的？”西奥昌亮出了利刃。 

“不…邪魔族变成现在这样之前完全不一样吧？虫神…也是如此。阿莎…应该是她的名字。” 

机灵转身看了看斯隆，然后又转向阿莎。“她想要什么？” 

“希望有个伴，”斯隆答道。“想要…有人理解？” 

西奥昌回到了斯隆身边，收起了刀刃。“好吧。我们喜欢个头大，力气也大的盟友…来听听她的想法吧。” 

一阵愉快的颤抖从阿莎的头部传遍了她蜷曲的身体，在她周围的沼气池上激起涟漪，让一旁的石壁也震了起来。连岩顶上碎裂的灰尘也被抖了下来。阿莎转头看向这对战士；她的巨眼比斯隆整个身子都大。蠕虫和蔼的眼眸像催眠一般缩张、闪耀着，使斯隆的神智恍惚了起来。 

         |阿特| 

阿特|阿莎|阿特 

         |阿特| 

斯隆在永恒的外来记忆中翻腾。她看到了记忆；讲述着记忆；就好象那是她自己的记忆。她们现在能一起分享出身和悲伤。 

“见证者…奉上了…强大的诅咒…一种欲望…伪装成爱。”斯隆长叹了一口气。但阿莎的眼神依然毫无变化，斯隆又被记忆的洪流冲走了。 

“一把刀剑…充满野心…我不…我不明白。” 

骨肉相残的狂乱紧接着在脑海中闪过：一场蠕虫的屠戮。那些曾经允诺永远结合在一起的生物舞动着獠牙，鞭挞着长尾；它们宣扬着曾被认为过于残酷的深渊魔法。全都是为了一个神圣的天赐法则。  

新星涡流吸干了猩红色的虫海，悬在战场上空。阿莎为了摆脱痛苦，只得暴力挣脱俘虏者。她的獠牙上挂着敌人的血肉；那些敌人曾经是她的兄弟姐妹。 

“血亲…背叛了血亲。为了证明力量。生存…是痛苦的…” 

阿莎逃走了，但口中还留有眷属的新鲜余味。她再也不会有爱。那法则改变了他们的“爱”。使之邪恶而饥渴。 

“被拒绝的法则…当作叛徒遭到追捕…像你一样迷失。”  

阿莎潜入了一个上维的梦境。她在宇宙之语的沐浴中冒险——广播歌曲和磁化吼声在太空中回荡。她穿行于遥远的世界之间，在太空中沿着银河边缘滑翔，追逐着一个遥远的光点。一个不会夺走爱的太阳。 

斯隆喘着气。“她为了活下去，来到了这里。” 

阿莎冲破土卫六厚重的表层，一头扎进了甲烷海。在她哀悼的同时，人类扩张到整个太阳系。联系在黄金时代期间被发现。他们遇上大崩溃；联系随之丧失。她进行着一场悲痛的战斗，对抗着绝望的梦魇。 

“恐惧的…门徒…攻击了阿莎。我…” 

这个称号激起了西奥昌的兴趣。 

“战败，撤退…爱在消逝。” 

 希望如潮水般起落。 

“彼此联系…我们才能活下去…”

3321971888.name: Hero's Wake
3321971888.subtitle: "He was like a father to us both." —Aisha
3321971888.subtitle_zh: “他就像我们俩的父亲一样。”——艾莎
3321971888.text:
"This above all else, I hold true." 

Shayura finishes her prayer but does not rise. Her kneeling position faces the sky where the Traveler once hung over the Last City. Morning sunlight fills the white space of her quarters with a warmth she does not feel. The light on her cheeks feels unwelcome. Undeserved. 

"Doctor Uzair will be expecting you," her Ghost urges softly, giving her a gentle nudge on the shoulder. Shayura nods, struggling to keep her expression firm.  

She fails. Her jaw trembles, and she scrapes tears from her eyes with the sides of her thumbs. Her Ghost emits a soft, sad chirp, before dematerializing to give her space. 

Her room is silent, but Shayura's thoughts buzz like a beehive. Too many to focus on. Just a riotous noise of doubts and insecurities, shames and regrets. She slouches backwards off her knees, draws them up to her chest, and makes herself small against the unwelcome light of the sun. She does not want the universe to see her; she does not want to be seen. She does not want to be. 

Doctor Uzair will remind her it is survivor's guilt. But it is so much more than that. 

It is not justice.
3321971888.text_zh:
“这是我最深信不疑的一点。” 

沙玉拉结束了她的祈祷，但没有起身。她跪向圣城上空，那是旅行者曾悬挂的位置。晨曦用一种她感受不到的温暖，洒满了她房间里的白色空间。照耀在她脸颊上的光感觉有些讨嫌，好像不配拥有似的。 

“乌泽尔医生在等着你，”她的机灵轻声催促着，轻轻推了一下她的肩膀。沙玉拉点了点头，想要维持坚毅的神情。  

她做不到。她的下颌颤抖着，她用拇指的两侧擦去眼角的眼泪。机灵发出一声柔和而悲伤的啾鸣，随后便消失，留给她独处的空间。 

她的房间寂静无声，但沙玉拉的思绪却像蜂箱一样嗡嗡作响。声音杂乱到无法专注。骚乱的噪音里满是疑虑和不安，羞耻和遗憾。她向后耷拉着，把膝盖抱到胸前，在讨嫌的阳光下让自己蜷缩起来。她不想让宇宙看到她；她不想被人看见。她不想存在下去。 

乌泽尔医生会提醒她这是幸存者的内疚。但事实远不止于此。 

这并不公正。

3135336191.name: Akashic Revelation
3135336191.subtitle: We end at the beginning.
3135336191.subtitle_zh: 我们在开始的地方终结。
3135336191.text:
Rosy light bathes the cockpit of a Hawk moving at cruising speed high above the Earth. Up ahead, the Traveler hangs motionless against the blackness of space, a triangular gateway of iridescent light bleeding from its shell. 

It was one thing volunteering for this mission, but sitting now on the precipice of the unknown, the Titan, Joxer, holds doubt close to his chest. "This isn't any different from the Ahamkara hunts," his Ghost reassures. "Reckless, hasty, and dangerous." Joxer glances over at his Ghost and smiles, already feeling better. 

Two Cabal escorts on either side of Joxer's Hawk stall their engines, letting the Hawk proceed forward toward the Traveler. They say something over the comms in Uluranth.  

"The translation roughly means 'Beyond the known is the terror of the universe,'" his Ghost offers. Joxer's not sure if it's a warning, a curse, or a pep talk. Knowing the Cabal, it's all three. 

Easing the flight stick forward, Joxer moves the Hawk ahead at a steady pace. His Ghost's eye widens as the rosy light from the portal brightens and the kaleidoscopic surface is all that can be seen in any direction. 

Joxer's grip on the controls tightens as he feels a bone-deep sense of vertigo. Echoes of piano notes tinkling in his periphery. He can feel hands on his chest beneath his armor, breath against his cheek inside his helmet. 

"Eric, come back to bed." A voice whispers inside his mind. He sees a city, a home. Family and children. He can't sleep. They aren't alone in the universe. The Ares project is going to— 

His Ghost is screaming, shell coming apart at the seams. Joxer pulls himself back to reality and jerks the controls as the nose of the Hawk touches the portal. He hears laughter, screams, feels lips on his cheek, hands on his shoulders as the ship begins to pass through.  

His Ghost's scream stretches from the moment of the big bang to the heat death of the universe.  

Joxer hears a scream he will make as his ship begins and ends. 

"Come back to bed." 

He catches up to the scream.
3135336191.text_zh:
一架鹰隼以巡航速度飞行在地球上空，它的驾驶舱沐浴在玫红色灯光下。前方，旅行者静静悬挂在黑暗的太空中，一条五彩斑斓的三角通道从它的外壳渗出。 

泰坦乔科斯虽说是自愿参加这次任务，但现在坐在未知的悬崖边上，他的心中满是疑虑。“这和阿罕卡拉狩猎没什么两样，”他的机灵安慰道。“鲁莽，草率，还很危险。”乔科斯瞥了一眼自己的机灵，笑了笑，感觉好多了。 

两艘卡巴尔护航舰在乔科斯鹰隼的两侧停下引擎，让鹰隼朝着旅行者继续前进。他们在通讯中用乌鲁兰思语说了些什么。  

“翻译大意为‘超脱已知之外的是宇宙的恐怖'，”他的机灵说道。乔科斯不确定这是警告、诅咒还是鼓励。据他对卡巴尔的了解，应该三者皆是。 

乔科斯让飞行杆缓缓向前，以稳定的速度向前驱动鹰隼。随着传送门发出的玫红色灯光变亮，从任何方向都只能看到万花筒般的表面，他的机灵睁大了眼睛。 

乔科斯紧抓着控制杆，感到一种深入骨髓的眩晕。钢琴音符的回声在他四周叮当作响。他能感觉到护甲下的双手放在了胸口，头盔里的呼吸贴着他的脸颊。 

“艾瑞克，回到床上来。”一个声音在他的脑海中低语。他看到一座城市，一个家。家人和孩子。他无法入睡。他们在宇宙中并不孤单。阿瑞斯项目马上就要—— 

他的机灵在尖叫，外壳在接缝处裂开。乔科斯让自己回到现实中，在鹰隼机首碰到传送门之际猛地拉起控制杆。他在飞船开始穿越时听到了笑声，尖叫声，感觉到嘴唇贴在他的脸颊上，双手放在他的肩膀上。  

他机灵的尖叫声从大爆炸的那一刻一直延伸至宇宙的热寂。  

乔科斯听到了一声尖叫，他会在飞船开始和结束时发出这样的声音。 

“回到床上来。” 

他追上了那声尖叫。

426260446.name: Valiant Memory
426260446.subtitle: "Of course, I'm wounded. That's what we do. We're Guardians. We die so that others might live." —Reed-7
426260446.subtitle_zh: “我当然会受伤，那是我们作为守护者的使命。我们拼死搏斗，其他人才能活下去。”——里德-7
426260446.text:
"Whatever that thing is, we've gotta take it down!" 

Amanda Holliday's voice crackles over the comms. Reed-7 glances at his Ghost, then pulls up alongside Holliday's Hawk and gives her a nod. He falls in behind her, with Shayura and Aisha following behind him in tight formation. 

Ahead, the beam of light extending from the Traveler is brighter than the sun. Instrumentation goes wild in its presence; astrogation systems don't know what to make of it and register the beam as a star. His ship tries to steer him away. Reed flips off autopilot. 

"Fly free, navs are down," he calls out to his fireteam.  

"Flying free," Aisha replies over comms. 

"We're right behind you, strike leader," Shayura affirms. 

Reed tightens his grip on the controls. "Holliday, take us in." 

"Block formation, let's give 'em the ol' Razzle Dazzle," Holliday radios to the strike team. Reed-7 boosts ahead under the Hawk and pulls up in front while Aisha and Shayura move to Holliday's flank. Reed activates manual targeting, reticle appearing on the windscreen. He tracks the shape held in the Traveler's beam—an impossible silhouette floating free in the void of space. 

The Witness is nothing more than a sliver of dark shearing through a field of white, but even at such a distance, Reed can feel its eyes on him. A chill jolts down his spine the moment the reticle locks on. His Exomind throbs with the sense-memory of a migraine.  

He immediately knows something is wrong. He turns to his Ghost. His Ghost looks at him, but it's already dead. The world separates into slices. 

And 

so is 

he.
426260446.text_zh:
“不管那玩意是啥，我们都得把它干掉！” 

阿曼达·霍利迪的声音在通讯中响起。里德-7瞥了他的机灵一眼，然后把飞船停在霍利迪的鹰隼旁边，向她点点头。他移到她身后，沙玉拉和艾莎紧紧地跟在他后面。 

前方，从旅行者身上发出的光束比太阳还要亮。仪器在它面前失控起来；导航系统搞不清是怎么一回事，把光束记录为一颗恒星。他的飞船试图引导他远离。里德关掉了自动驾驶仪。 

“自由飞行，导航已失效，”他对他的火力战队喊道。  

“正在自由飞行，”艾莎通过通讯回复。 

“我们跟着你，打击队长，”沙玉拉听命道。 

里德紧握着控制杆。“霍利迪，带我们进去。” 

“方块阵型，让他们好好欣赏一下我们的表演，”霍利迪向打击小队发送通讯。里德-7在鹰隼下方向前推进，然后在艾莎和沙玉拉移动到霍利迪侧翼时从底部往上来到前方。里德启动了手动瞄准，挡风玻璃上出现准星。他追踪到旅行者光束中的黑暗形状，一个不可能存在的轮廓漂浮在广袤太空中。 

见证者不过是白茫茫一片中断裂的一抹黑暗，但即使在这样的距离，里德也能感觉到它的眼睛在看着他。在准星锁定的那一刻，里德感觉到了脊背发凉。他的Exo脑袋随着偏头痛的感官记忆隐隐阵痛。  

他立刻意识到出问题了。他转向他的机灵。他的机灵看着他，但它已经死了。世界支离破碎。 

而他 

也是 

如此。

3110986887.name: Ephemeral Spark
3110986887.subtitle: The brightest thing in the sky.
3110986887.text:
"Wow, check out that power source. Retro." Even through the holoprojector's patchy connection and the rippling visage of Nimbus, there's no missing the excitement in their voice as it echoes off the walls of the Arcology. "You said this was New Pacific tech?" 

"Found it not too far from here," Sloane replies.  

"We've still got some of their old records. I always liked their jingle." 

Sloane smiles. "'The next frontier is you?'"  

"That's the one. Catchy, right?" Nimbus grins. "So hey, you're absolutely onto something—this exoskeleton of yours looks a whole lot like some of the early Cloud Strider prototypes I learned about. Before the Sidereal. Before the nanotech. Just a couple of neural links and some chrome. This biointerface—"  

Sloane snorts. "The part where the suit stabbed me full of wires?" 

"The frame alone must weigh a couple of tons. And you wore it into battle?"  

"Sure did."  

Nimbus's projection looks up at her with a serious expression. "You are so cool." They focus for a moment on the datapad in their hand. "I know some gearheads who'll flip. Quinn's gonna love this thing."  

"There are a few design flaws," Sloane says. "Once the suit was out of juice, it was impossible to maneuver. I basically had to rip myself out of it."  

Nimbus laughs. "Hey, there's downsides to the shiny new model too."  

Sloane wasn't sure what to expect from this exchange when Zavala first proposed it to her. A polite back and forth about Golden Age technology, as one might have with the Cryptarchs. Maybe a few resentful accusations, a little culture clash.  

Not this sense of recognition, like an old, familiar ache. 

Nimbus's smile is radiant. "Still, while you're along for the ride? What a rush."  

Sloane nods. "Best feeling in the world."
3110986887.text_zh:
“哇，快看那个电源。真复古。”就算是透过全息投影仪断断续续的连接和宁博思波动的面容，在生态园区的墙上回荡时，那声音里的兴奋可一点也不少。“你说这是新太平洋科技？” 

“在离这儿不远的地方找到的，”斯隆回答道。  

“我们还留着他们的一些旧唱片。我一直很喜欢他们的韵律。” 

斯隆绽开了笑容。“‘下一个前沿就是你？'”  

“就是它。很抓耳，对吧？”宁博思咧嘴一笑。“话说回来，你确实说的很对——你的这个外骨骼看起来很像是我知道的早期云端行者原型。早在群星之前。早在纳米科技之前。只是一些神经连接和铬合金。这个生物界面——“  

斯隆哼了一声。“动力服往我身上插电线的那部分？” 

“光是这个框架就有好几吨重。你居然穿着它上了战场？”  

“当然了。”  

宁博思的投影严肃地抬头看着她。“你太酷了。”宁博思把注意力集中在手中的数据板上。“我认识的一些设备迷会很感兴趣的。昆恩一定会喜欢这玩意儿。”  

“它有设计缺陷，”斯隆说道。“动力服没了电，就没法再移动。我基本上就得从里面把自己弄出来。”  

宁博思笑了。“嘿，我这个闪亮的新模型也有缺点啊。”  

萨瓦拉第一次向她提议时，斯隆并不确定这种交流会是怎样。一场关于黄金时代技术的礼貌对话问答，就像大家会对解密大师们做的那样。又或者是一些愤恨的指责，一点文化上的冲突。  

没想到会是这种认同感，像是某种陈旧、熟悉的疼痛。 

宁博思的笑容很灿烂。“不过，驾驭它的时候很棒吧？”  

斯隆点点头。“那感觉简直无与伦比。”

2274944459.name: Recalcitrant Host
2274944459.subtitle: Take what is not given.
2274944459.text:
The stormjoy rolls over the landscape, blanketing the coastline in the stinging fog of its exhalations. Its passing stirs crackling ribbons of lightning from Fundament's atmosphere. 

Xi Ro waits in hiding, folded up Krill-small, as the living cloud approaches. It lowers the dangling threads of its feeding tentacles. Each is tipped with light. The light fills Xi Ro's heart with a terrible, aching happiness. The sensation sits heavy inside her, bearable only because it is unwelcome.  

This will be the fourth bait star she collects. Xi Ro dreams that when the Helium Drinkers strike next, she will use the bait stars to blind them, then cut them up while they writhe.  

She must leap as high as she can to cleave the bait star loose. The tentacle detects a stirring in the air and whips around. If she is slow, it will tear the blade from her hands.  

She is not slow. Her sword cuts neatly through glistening, translucent muscle fibers, and with her free hand, she snatches the falling bait star from the air. The tentacle reels away, ascending into the sky like a withdrawn rope.  

Xi Ro exults. It is only when she turns around that she sees her elder sister.  

Aurash is standing with her limbs limp at her sides, her scrolls scattered at her feet. Xi Ro sees in her three eyes the euphoria that is the stormjoy's weapon.  

Xi Ro leaps and tackles her sister into the dirt.  

After, the two of them wait beneath shelter while the stormjoy advances down the coast. Aurash is sullen, but Xi Ro knows it can be fixed. 

"Look." Xi Ro holds out the bait star. "We can take joy for ourselves." 

Aurash lifts the star by its shriveled stalk, then cups the light in her claws, like a small fire.  

Xi Ro shoves her playfully, trying to knock the star loose.  

But Aurash holds fast.
2274944459.text_zh:
风暴之悦在大地上空掠过，将海岸线笼罩在其喷出的刺鼻烟雾之中。它的经过激起了虫群据点的大气中噼啪作响的带状闪电。 

希罗藏在暗处，像克里尔一样蜷缩起来，等待着这朵活云的到来。它放下了摄食触手上悬垂的线。每一条尖端都冒着光亮。那光让希罗的心里充满了可怕而痛苦的幸福。这种感觉在她心里沉甸甸的，只因不被接受而需要忍受。  

这将会是她收集的第四颗诱饵星。希罗梦想着当氦饮者下次袭击时，她会用诱饵星把它们致盲，然后在它们扭动时将其切碎。  

她必须跳得尽可能高，才能把诱饵星劈开。触须察觉到空气中有动静，开始四处挥舞。要是她动作缓慢，刀刃就会从她手上被扯下来。  

她动作不慢。她的刀剑整齐地划破闪闪发光、半透明的肌肉纤维。她用另一只手从空中抓住了落下的诱饵星。触须卷起，像一根抽回的绳子一样升向天空。  

希罗欣喜若狂。直到她转过身，才看到她的姐姐。  

奥拉什站在那里，肢体瘫软地垂在两侧，她的卷轴散落在她的脚边。希罗在她的三只眼睛里看到了风暴之悦的武器。  

希罗跳起来，把姐姐撞进了泥土里。  

之后，当风暴之悦沿着海岸前进时，她们俩在掩体下等待着。奥拉什在生闷气，但希罗知道这是可以弥补的。 

“看。”希罗拿出了诱饵星。“我们可以将喜悦据为己有。” 

奥拉什抓住枯萎的茎，把诱饵星捧在她的爪子里，就像是一小团火。  

希罗玩闹着推搡她，试图把诱饵星撞脱手。  

但奥拉什抓得很牢。

1853085236.name: Pale Reflection
1853085236.subtitle: The moon and mirrors have much in common.
1853085236.subtitle_zh: 月亮和镜子有很多共同点。
1853085236.text:
Eris Morn knows what she looks like. Her mirror holds nothing her memory cannot furnish for her—all that lives beneath the silvered surface of the glass is the uncanny. Still, she pulls away the cloth covering it and removes her bandage. 

Eris looks into her eyes and sees all the ghostly occupants of a haunted house. Her nightmares peer out through the green gleam into a world that will not meet her gaze.  

She reaches up and touches her face. Darkness coils around her fingertips and seeps back into her bare skin. Her hairline, her brow, the scars, the unctuous tears that slide eternally down her cheeks.  

But they are not tears. She does not weep for her condition. That condition had saved her life. It had granted her strength, access, and time. She'd torn it all from the Hive and turned it against them. 

Eris does not see pain. She sees triumph and survival. She sees a future. 

She sees power. 

Eris retreats from the mirror and covers it again.
1853085236.text_zh:
埃里斯·摩恩知道她看起来什么样。她的镜子里没什么是她的记忆没法带给她的——玻璃银色表面下存在的一切唯有神秘。尽管如此，她还是拉开了盖在它身上的布，拿掉了她的绷带。 

埃里斯看着她的眼睛，望见了鬼屋里所有幽灵般的居民。她的梦魇透过绿色的闪光窥视到一个不会与她的目光相遇的世界。  

她伸手摸了摸自己的脸。暗影缠绕着她的指尖，又渗回她裸露的皮肤。她的发际线，她的眉毛，她的伤疤，还有那顺着脸颊滑落、虚情假意的泪水。  

但那不是眼泪。她不会为自己的处境哭泣。这处境救了她的命。它给了她力量、途径和时间。她从邪魔族身上撕下一切，转而对付他们。 

埃里斯看不到痛苦。她看到了胜利和生存。她看到了未来。 

她看到了力量。 

埃里斯从镜子里退了出来，重新把它盖上。

2664281431.name: To Be Remembered
2664281431.subtitle: Never forget.
2664281431.text:
Each night, the clamor of the Tower Hangar gives way to silence as the engineers change shifts. Niik used to find the lull unnerving, preferring to bask in the sounds of arc welders and power tools. Together, she and Amanda would speak about nothing and everything over the cacophony.

Now, Niik prefers the silence.

Her Servitor shines a light on the Sparrow in front of her, as it has done for weeks. After making some final adjustments, Niik circles around to the front of the Sparrow and hits the ignition.

The engine sputters and burns out.

It's happened a hundred times before, on other nights, with other Sparrows. But this time, something is different. Niik snarls an Eliksni curse and hurls her spanner at the floor. Then she buries her face in her four hands and collapses into a heap, her eyes glistening with tears and her ether tank rattling with her ragged sobs.

"Well, there's your problem!" crackles a voice beside her.

She looks up to see her Servitor projecting a holo-recording. Miniature recreations of herself and Amanda crouch next to another Sparrow as Amanda gestures to its thrusters with a grease-stained arm. She imparts a lesson about its functionality with a smile that says she enjoys sharing the knowledge.

Watching now, Niik can't help but smile too. It was a lesson she had forgotten, but thanks to her Servitor, it would stay with her forever.

She wipes away her tears with a grease-stained arm and gets back to work.
2664281431.text_zh:
每天晚上，到了工程师们换班的时候，高塔机库里的喧闹声就会化为寂静。妮可曾经觉得这种间歇的平静令人不安，她更喜欢沉浸在电弧焊机和电动工具的声响之中。在喧闹声中，她和阿曼达在一起无话不谈。

现在，妮可更喜欢安静。

她的魔眼用灯照亮着她面前的快雀，就像几周以来一直做的那样。在做了一些最后的调整后，妮可绕到快雀前方，发动了点火装置。

发动机发出噼啪声，烧坏了。

在其他夜晚，这种情况在其它快雀身上发生过无数回。但这一次，情况有所不同。妮可咆哮着埃里克斯尼语的咒骂，把扳手扔在了地板上。然后她用四只手捂住脸，瘫倒在地，眼里闪着泪光，乙太罐里满是断断续续的抽泣声。

“这就是问题所在！”她身旁的一个声音噼啪作响。

她抬起头，看到她的魔眼正在播放着全息录音。她和阿曼达蹲在另一辆快雀旁边，阿曼达用沾满油脂的胳膊示意着它的推进器。她面带微笑地讲解了它的功能，似乎很乐于分享知识。

看到这时，妮可也忍不住笑了。这是一堂她已经忘了的课，但多亏了她的魔眼，它会永远陪着她。

她用沾满油脂的胳膊擦干眼泪，继续工作。

967777908.name: Survivor's Journey
967777908.subtitle: "When one life passes, another rises to take its place. That's balance. That's nature." —Reed-7
967777908.subtitle_zh: “一条生命逝去时，另一条会替代它的位置。这就是平衡。这就是自然。”——里德-7
967777908.text:
The engine of Aisha's Sparrow winds down to a steady thrum as she eases off the accelerator. The pine forest around her feels empty, still. The only noise is the creak and groan of the Arcology superstructure. Methane rain falls through the shattered dome overhead. Taking off her helmet, Aisha is mindful of her new threader earring, affixed with a thin strip of red metal, the edges hand-ground. 

"I didn't expect you to come in person," calls an old, familiar voice from the forest. Aisha turns to see Sloane, forced to grapple with the obvious shape of her transformation. The Taken energy rising off of her arm, the way her eyes catch light. 

Steeling herself, Aisha dismounts her Sparrow and closes the distance to Sloane in an instant, fearlessly embracing her. Sloane is stunned, arms stiff at her sides. It only lasts a moment, but the echo of sentiment fills her with painful nostalgia. 

Aisha takes a step back, struggling to maintain her composure. "I needed to see you," she says with a quaver in her voice. "Needed to—to tell you in person." 

It may have been years since she's seen Aisha, but Sloane knows only one thing could rattle her like this. 

"Reed's gone." 

The ache reminds Sloane she's still Human.
967777908.text_zh:
艾莎松开油门，她的快雀引擎渐渐平息为稳定的嗡鸣声。她周围的松林空无一物，悄无声息。唯一的声音是生态园区上部构造低沉的嘎吱作响。甲烷雨从头顶破碎的穹顶中落下。摘下头盔时，艾莎很留意她的新穿针器耳环，那上面有一串边缘经过了手工打磨的红色金属薄片。 

“没想到你会亲自过来，”森林里传来昔日熟悉的声音。艾莎转身看到斯隆，努力适应她明显变化了的形态，不管是她手臂上升起的傀儡能量，还是她眼睛捕捉光线的方式。 

艾莎鼓起勇气，从快雀上下来，快速来到斯隆身边，勇敢地拥抱了她。斯隆目瞪口呆，双臂僵硬地垂在身体两侧。这只持续了片刻，但情感的回响让她充满了痛苦的怀念之情。 

艾莎后退一步，竭力保持镇静。“我得见你，”她说，声音有些颤抖。“我得…亲自告诉你。” 

她已经很多年没有见过艾莎了，但斯隆知道只有一件事能让她如此慌乱不安。 

“里德走了。” 

那阵哀痛提醒着斯隆，她还是人类。

2007908580.name: NPA "Weir-Walker" Grips
2007908580.subtitle: [DAY 3] The Ghost of Titan walks on through sunless seas, having died long ago.
2007908580.subtitle_zh: [第3天]泰坦机灵继续行走在暗无天日的海洋中，早已死去。
2007908580.text:
REPULSION LATTICE INTEGRITY… NOMINAL 
OXYGEN SIEVE… NOMINAL 
DEPTH… 106m 

The lettering on Sloane's HUD clarified into vision. She dragged a hand through methane fluid to her faceplate, absentmindedly trying to rub the grogginess from her eyes.  

Motion in the dark surrounding her kicked up clouds of fine grit.  

Her headlights flared as her fingertips clinked against her helmet—a Thrall came screaming into the beam of light, bubbles spewing from its jaws. Sloane's eyes went wide before she reflexively flipped the Thrall over her shoulder and kicked its jaw through its skull. Her power suit spooled and pushed stimulants reactively. 

She pivoted and caught the sword of a Knight mid-swing, snapping the weapon in two between the fingers of her gauntlet and driving a shard of broken blade into its chest. Another Thrall crossed her headlights just before a silver streak whistled through its throat. Sloane eyed a selection in her visor, which hi-lighted over thirty dead Hive, slowly deteriorating in boils of tiny, rumbling ignitions that sent nerve-spasms through their husks. Her visor cleared the readings and snapped onto a friendly.  

Síocháin drifted forward, Hive viscera gently wafting into the sea from the slender razors protruding from her shell. "You were out for days." 

Sloane's face wrinkled in confusion. "I remember the Pyramid wave. Falling… dreams. Are you okay?" 

"Hive found us, like you said," Síocháin said, retracting her blades. 

Sloane grabbed the Ghost and hugged her to her power suit chassis for a moment. "Little killer. Really gave 'em the business." 

Síocháin chirped. "Pyramid wave swept over Titan, bounced around a bit and centralized where the Pyramid stopped. Gravity went crazy, then the ocean. I think we're a few miles from where we were when all this started." 

"The Pyramid stopped? Then that's where we're headed… after we grab some gear," Sloane said. 

Síocháin dipped forward. "One more thing. Something's out there circling us. Not Hive. Can't quite pin it down, but it's big." 

"Yeah?" Sloane said, thinking of what went through her mind before she lost consciousness. "Then let's not waste any time getting out of here." 

*** 

Sloane lifted herself from the ocean onto a half-submerged Arcology platform where she'd stowed a variety of rations and munitions since Titan's skies went dark. Her power suit clattered against the steel-mesh floor; she waited for the echoes to die down before taking a moment to exhale in silence. In that quiet moment, she made out a faint voice.  

Síocháin rose into view. "Do you hear that?" 

"Was about to ask you…" Sloane said, standing. She snatched First In, Last Out from a stow locker, racked the foregrip, then followed the voice down a barnacle-crusted causeway to an old research lab with Síocháin in tow. 

Fluid trickled down cracked walls surrounding rows of dead monitors. Glass reflected prismatic color from a gnarled tear in reality at the lab's center—as if it had been carved from another epoch and affixed to this one.  

A Human that didn't seem to notice them paced within the tear—standing in a fully functioning mirage of the Arcology. Once he turned toward them, the tear spasmed and lurched forward and backward in time at erratic durations and speed. He was ripped both ways into non-existence as the tear flittered through events like a fourth-dimensional montage. 

The tear held steady again, returning the man and his moment to existence. Síocháin took note of the badge on his coat that read "Gideon Tepin—NPA—Senior Marine Biologist." 

Tepin looked upset and turned away before speaking. "She's afraid. That's why we're all having them. Something's wrong. She's showing us what's coming in plain view!" The man angrily swiped his hand through the air in Sloane's direction. "It's like she's screaming it into my head. I know I'm not the only one hearing it."  

"It chose us." He stepped forward and placed his hand on the border between then and now. "I'm dreaming my own memories, but with little differences. Little omens. Black ships in the sky." 

Sloane leaned forward, hand nearly pressed to that of the living memory playing out before her on the other side of the tear. 

"She's trying to warn us. We should evacuate. We have to get her—" 

The tear lurched again, ripped away; lost to the rushing passage of time and blinked into non-existence. Gone. 

Sloane dropped her hand. Jaw clenched. "See if you can dig up any Arcology records on this." 

*** 

"That marine biologist… Tepin… was he in some sort of captured time fluctuation? Is that… even possible?" Sloane asked. 

"I've never seen anything like it," Síocháin said. "I'm not really sure." 

Síocháin skimmed archived reports. "It's under 'TLev-01.' Looks like a psychic space whale some biologists were studying out in the ocean. They never got accurate measurements, but this estimate can't be correct. Over 150 meters? Report says it wasn't from here though, and refers to a lot of visions that personnel were having… which is… odd? Not a lot of alien species in Sol until after the Golden Age." 

"I was having dreams while I was out, Síocháin. Of some other world, the Pyramid on Titan… the Tower. Like I remembered being there for each one." 

"Well, I guess it could be an ancient space whale… or sometimes the Traveler gives people dreams. But are we going to ignore the obvious 'you were rendered unconscious by a Pyramid wave' explanation?" 

"No… but we've seen enough weird not to knock it," Sloane sighed.  

"Sure. I'll log that away," Síocháin said. "You know… the readings coming from inside that field Tepin was in were consistent with atmospheric records on Titan during the Collapse." 

"What does that mean?" Sloane looked back to the spot of warped space-time. "Was he… real?" 

"I don't know. I just know it wasn't a simulation."
