They lived long, full lives. Reading about them makes me wish I had seen the City of their times. I was a boy when the Guardians won the battle of Twilight Gap. I've only ever known peace behind the walls, only watched the City grow and thrive. I barely know how to handle a rifle. I work textiles. I make clothes. I want to open a shop to tailor clothing for the Guardians. I don't want to die.

I've been hiding with the resistance for three weeks now, since they found me sleeping in a storm drain. I lost everything in the Cabal attack. All my family's writings. My sister. My son. The Guardians—even without their Light—are defending us. They're showing me how to shoot, how to survive. Every day someone leaves our hideout and never returns. Mas'ouda, Arzu, Brajko, Mitra, Kardelen, and Luca died this week. The Cabal are relentless, and sooner or later they're going to figure out where we're hiding. 

There's fifteen of us left, five combat frames, and two Guardians.

I have to survive. Humanity has to survive. It can't end like this.
2813298149.text_zh:
我母亲上周去世了。她把从建造城墙时就开始写的日记留给了我。她还留下了她父亲的父亲的日记，那时的圣城甚至还没有城墙。他们度过了漫长而充实的一生。读着他们的日记，我真希望能亲眼看到他们那个时代的圣城。守护者赢得暮光峡谷战役时，我还是个孩子。我只知道高墙之后的和平，只看到了圣城的成长和繁荣。我几乎不会用步枪。我从事纺织工作。我制作衣物。我想开家为守护者们定制服装的店。我不想死。

从我睡在暴雨排水沟里被反抗军发现后算起，我已经跟他们一起躲了三个星期。在卡巴尔的袭击中，我失去了一切。所有我家人的日志。我的妹妹。我的儿子。守护者们——即使没有了他们的光能——仍在保护着我们。他们教我如何射击，如何生存。每天都有人离开我们的藏身处，再没回来。马斯乌达、阿尔祖、布拉伊科、米特拉、卡德伦，还有卢卡，都死在了这周。卡巴尔步步紧逼，他们迟早会发现我们躲藏的地方。 

我们还剩下十五个人，五个战斗框架和两名守护者。

我必须生存下去。人类必须生存下去。不能就这样结束。

1469212984.name: Veteran Legend Bond
1469212984.subtitle: "All endings are beginnings."
1469212984.text:
Tonight, I watched a thousand lanterns fill the night sky. Tonight, I watched the hopes and dreams of humanity burn bright in the dark and challenge the uncertainty of the future. Tonight, I gave birth to a child that will shoulder the same burden of humanity's uncertain future that I have. Tonight a new person came into this world who will share in my family's stories, hear of their ancestors and their triumphs, their failures, and their legends. Tonight, humanity takes a step into a future so unknown we do not even have a word for it. Tonight is a moment that must live forever, no detail forgotten.

Tonight, the war is over. Tonight, a new age dawns. Tonight, I am so very tired. From my bedroom I hear congratulations and cheers. I hear excitement. Everyone I have spoken to is dreaming about the future now, rather than merely surviving the next day. Some of my friends want to venture into the stars, leave the safety of the City and explore. They want to reclaim everything we've lost; all these worlds. But I won't be joining them. My place is here in the City, where my family has lived and died for generations. My friends ask, "Why would you want to stay in the Last City?" But I don't think it's going to stay the Last City.

I think this is the First City of many to come.
1469212984.text_zh:
今夜，我看着万盏灯笼挂满夜空。今夜，我看着人类的希望和梦想在黑暗中熠熠生辉，挑战着未来的不确定性。今夜，我生下了一个孩子，他将和我一样肩负起人类不确定未来的重担。今夜，一个新成员来到这个世界，与我共享家族的故事，聆听祖先的事迹，以及他们的胜利、失败和传奇。今夜，人类踏出了迈向未来的一步，我们甚至找不到一个词来形容它的未知性。今夜是一个永恒的时刻，任何细节都不会被遗忘。

今夜，战争迎来终结。今夜，新的时代来临。今夜，我已疲惫不堪。我从卧室里听到了祝贺与欢呼，听到了兴奋与激昂。与我交谈过的每个人都在憧憬未来，而不仅仅是想着怎么熬过明天。我的一些朋友想去星际冒险，离开圣城的庇护向外探索。他们想重新夺回我们失去的一切；所有这些世界。但我不会与他们同行。我的归宿是圣城，这是我的家族世世代代生活和死去的地方。我的朋友们问我，“你为什么想留在最后的圣城里？”而我觉得，它将不再是最后的圣城。

我想对未来的众多城市来说，它会是第一座圣城。

672281666.name: Veteran Legend Hood
672281666.subtitle: "There's a last, safe city out there somewhere. We have to believe."
672281666.subtitle_zh: “一定还有最后的安全之城。我们必须相信。”
672281666.text:
"The Last Safe City" exists in name only. I came here expecting to find a lost metropolis from before the Collapse. Instead, it's a sea of tents and prefabricated shelters huddled around bonfires. Everyone here thinks that hiding in the shadow of the Traveler will keep them safe. Keep humanity's killers at arm's length. All I see are hundreds of miles of rough, snow-capped mountains. All I can feel is the memory of frostbite in my fingers. That's not going to stop anyone, just slow them down.

I came here in a caravan of settlers. The march up the mountains was worse than any battle I'd survived. Hundreds died along the way from injuries, starvation, exposure. All the greatest hits. We buried them along the roadside, with no time for markers or ceremony. I've heard some of the Risen here talking about forming guard patrols to escort people. I don't know. Sooner or later our enemies are going to follow the trail of ants back to the mound. We'd never survive a full-frontal assault.

More Risen arrive every day. They're starting to organize, make plans. They make me nervous. I can't shake the memories. Groups of them hitting settlements for ammunition and food, mass executions for those who dared speak out against them, entire towns turned to craters. These ones seem different from the Warlords, but I can't just let it go. The other settlers here are just like the ones outside the "City," consumed with their own ideas about how the world should run. I've heard plenty of people talking about organizing an exodus, just getting in whatever ships we have and abandoning Earth. As if anywhere else in this system is safe. Others want to form clear lines of succession and leadership. Then there's the people like me—trusting their guns—waiting for the other shoe to drop. We know war is a certainty.

Something is going to kill us all. It's just a matter of when, not if. There's nowhere safe. Not anywhere. Not anymore.
672281666.text_zh:
“最后的安全城市”有名无实。我来到这里，本以为会发现一座大崩溃前的失落大都市。但这里却是一片围着篝火的帐篷和预制房屋的海洋。这里的每个人都以为躲在旅行者的荫蔽之下，就能保证自己的安全，就能与残害人类的杀手保持距离。可我看到的只有数百英里的崎岖雪山，我能感受到的只有手指上冻疮的记忆。那阻止不了任何人，只会拖慢他们的脚步。

我是随着一队定居者来到这里的。上山的行进比我经历过的任何一场战役都要艰难。沿途数百人死于伤痛、饥饿、受冻。最糟糕的情况都发生了。我们把他们埋在路边，没时间立碑或是举行葬礼。我听说这里的一些复生者在谈论组建护卫巡逻队来护送人们。我不知道这是否明智。我们的敌人迟早会沿着痕迹追踪到我们的巢穴。到时候，我们绝对撑不过他们的全面进攻。

每天都有更多的复生者抵达。他们开始组织起来，制定计划。他们让我感到紧张。我无法摆脱那些记忆。他们那样的人曾抱团去定居点抢夺弹药和食物，大规模处决敢于出声反对他们的人，把各个城镇变成弹坑。这些人看起来与战争领主不同，但我的内心无法平静。这里的其他定居者跟“圣城”外面的那些人并无二致，认为世界就该像自己想的那样运作。我听到很多人都在谈论组织一次大逃亡，随便坐上什么飞船，抛弃地球。就好像这个星系里的其他地方都是安全的一样。另外一些人想制定明确的继任和领导体系。还有像我这样的人——相信自己的枪杆子——提心吊胆地等待着坏事发生。我们知道战争无可避免。

有东西会将我们所有人置于死地。这一定会发生，只不过是时间问题。没有地方是安全的。哪儿都不安全。也再也不会有安全的地方了。

1486564541.name: Veteran Legend Boots
1486564541.subtitle: "The Traveler didn't run, it rose up to meet the enemy."
1486564541.subtitle_zh: “旅行者没有逃跑，而是起身迎敌。”
1486564541.text:
The Traveler is gone.

I watched it as it left the City. The sky lit up like the world was ending. It's still up there, though. When the sun is at the right angle you can see it like a second moon. I remember, as a teenager, sitting on the roof of my apartment building, watching the pieces of the Traveler reform. I could feel the Light in the way they say Guardians and Ghosts can. I felt so confident that day, so sure that we were all going to be saved. Many are doubting, but when I look up into the sky and see that the Traveler is still there—defending not just the City, but all of Earth—my faith is as strong as ever.

In the days since the Traveler left, Coalition ships have filled the City's skies. I remember my uncle talking about the last time he saw Cabal ships in the sky—it was the day my mother died. It feels like we've been through so much in such a short time. My uncle would tell me our family's stories every night. We'd lost all the written copies after the invasion, but now they exist in me, and I will record what I remember. So we know where we came from and what was lost.

Everyone is saying this is the end. But I know enough history to be sure that it's not the first time we've felt this way. Every threat the City faces feels like it'll be the last. My uncle died during the Endless Night, saving Eliksni that once tried to lay siege to our home. Nothing lasts forever and everything changes. Buildings burn, people die, but we move on. 

I don't think this is the end. I think this is a new beginning.
1486564541.text_zh:
旅行者走了。

我看着它离开圣城。天空就像世界末日一样亮了起来。但它还在天上。太阳角度恰到好处时，你就可以看到它，像是第二个月亮一样。我还记得，十几岁的时候，我坐在公寓楼的屋顶上，看着旅行者的碎片重组。我能感受到光能，就像人们说的守护者和机灵能做到的那样。那天我很有信心，确信我们都会得救。尽管很多人表示怀疑，但是当我仰望天空，看到旅行者还在那里，不仅保护着圣城，还保护着整个地球时，我的信念一如既往地坚定。

旅行者离开后的日子里，联盟的飞船布满了圣城的天空。我记得舅舅说过他最后一次在天空中看到卡巴尔飞船是在我母亲去世的那天。感觉我们在这么短的时间内经历了太多。我舅舅每天晚上都会跟我讲我们家族的故事。入侵之后，我们失去了所有的书面文本，但现在它们存在于我的心中，我会记录下我所记得的一切。这样我们就知道我们从哪里来，失去了什么。

每个人都在说末日已到。但我对历史的了解足以让我确信，这不是我们第一次有这种感觉。圣城面临的每一次威胁都像是最后一次。我舅舅在永夜时牺牲了，为的是拯救曾经试图围攻我们家园的埃里克斯尼族。没有什么是永恒的，一切都会改变。建筑烧毁，人们死去，但我们会继续前进。 

我不认为这是末日。我相信这是一个新的开始。

1909305643.name: Hazardous Propulsion
1909305643.subtitle: WARNING: Sudden explosions may occur.
1909305643.subtitle_zh: 警告：可能会发生突然爆炸。
1909305643.text:
"This can't be right. They went inside the Traveler…?"

A message she had intercepted moments prior had to be read three times before it finally made it through her processes, and she could make sense of the information. She's been so disconnected.

Her cooling fans whir in a sigh. She hasn't seen the Captain since they stopped by to deliver Dawning cookies last year. They were still carefully stacked, untouched, a sugary cairn in the maintenance bay.

"They get to do all the cool stuff."

The fans hum louder in a sigh, though she is careful not to expend too much of her reserved energy. Sometimes a few stray messages found their way into her inbox, and she perused them when she remembered to check, but this one took the cake. All that fuss about the big mysterious ball in the sky, and now, there they were, running around inside of it like some sort of playground. She wishes she could see it too.

"I wouldn't take up much space. All my processes are highly efficient."

She considers the situation for a moment. Maybe there's a way for her to join them…

"I can be valuable…" she mutters.

A machine buzzes in a nearby room. The 3D printer that had been dormant for years springs to life. With a surge of energy, she flips on her 'politeness filter'—an uncomfortable feeling—as she pulls up old blueprints from her archives.

"What do Guardian's care about most? The Traveler? Cookies? The Last Cit—" Something catches her attention as it sweeps by. "No, wait…" She zooms in. Enhances. "ROCKETS!"

An excited buzz makes the ship's lights flicker as she processes a million disastrously fun ideas all at once. The arms of the printer move wildly.

"Rocket boots? Rocket arms? ROCKET HELMET?" She pauses, fingers scratching at a pretend chin as she contemplates. "Though a rocket helmet does seem hazardous to the Captain's health. The chance of head injuries is frequent and likely."

Failsafe spins through the records of her rocket-like blueprints while the printer's hands work overtime to keep up. Something gets bedazzled with old solar panel shards and is quickly discarded.

"Got it! ROCKET ARMOR! Surely the Captain won't harm themselves with this!"

It's the perfect solution. Just the right amount of danger and effectiveness. Surely the Captain will appreciate this and request her presence on their mission inside the Traveler.

The machine continues to print a variety of prototypes as she hums a tune she learned from Cayde-6.

She thinks about him sometimes…

Maybe she would have made something with rockets for him too.
1909305643.text_zh:
“这不对吧。他们进入了旅行者…？”

这条她不久前截获，不得不读取了三遍才通过处理程序的信息，终于可以被理解了。她真是孤陋寡闻啊。

她的冷却风扇呼呼作响，发出了一声叹息。自从去年船长顺道送来曙光节饼干，她就再也没有见过他们了。那些饼干还被小心翼翼地堆放在维修舱里，没有被碰过，就像一个含糖的石堆。

“他们得以去做所有这些酷炫的事。”

风扇的嗡鸣随着叹息而变得更响，但她有注意避免消耗过多库存能量。她的收件箱里不时会收到几条零星信息，她会在想起要查看的时候仔细品读，但这一条最惊人。大家曾对天空中那个神秘的巨球大惊小怪，现在他们却在里面跑来跑去，就好像那是个游乐场。她希望自己也能亲眼看到。

“我不会占用太多空间。我的所有程序都非常高效。”

她思忖了一下情况。也许有个办法可以让她加入他们…

“我可以派上用场…”她嘀咕道。

附近房间里的一台机器在嗡嗡作响。沉睡多年的3D打印机重新动了起来。她从档案里取出一堆旧蓝图，伴随着一股能量的涌动，打开了“礼貌筛选器”——那让她感到不舒服。

“守护者最在意什么？旅行者？饼干？圣城——”有什么东西掠过时引起了她的注意。“不，等等…”她变焦放大屏幕。强化了分辨率。“火箭！”

兴奋的嗡鸣声让飞船上的灯光闪烁个不停，她同时处理着无数个超有趣的想法。打印机的手臂疯狂地舞动着。

“火箭战靴？火箭护臂？火箭头盔？”她停顿了一下，用并不存在的手指抓着假想的下巴，沉思着。“但火箭头盔似乎的确对船长的健康有害。头部受伤的可能性很大。”

智能失效保险快速浏览着她那些火箭般蓝图的记录，而打印机的手臂则在拼命保持同步。有件东西伴随着旧太阳能电池板的碎片晃了下眼，然后很快就被丢弃了。

“就是它！火箭护甲！船长肯定不会被这个伤到！”

这是个完美的解决方案。危险和效率都恰到好处。船长肯定会对此心存感激，并请求她加入他们在旅行者内部的任务。

她哼着从凯德6号那里学来的曲调，守着机器打印出各种各样的原型。

她有时会想起他…

也许她本来也会用火箭给他做点什么。

3717431477.name: Wishful Ignorance
3717431477.subtitle: "My only wish is for this disrespect to end." — Ol-Amral
3717431477.subtitle_zh: “我唯一的愿望就是结束这种不敬。”——奥尔-阿姆拉尔
3717431477.text:
Complaint Tablet to Ganneth 

"Tell Ganneth: Ol-Amral sends the following message: 

When you came to the City, you said to me: "I will procure fine quality, pure Ahamkara bone for your armory." 

You then left, but you did not do what you promised. 

You put brittle bone chips before my Ghost and said: 

"If you want to take them, take them; if you do not want to take them, go away!" 

What do you take me for that you treat me with such contempt…?! 

…you who claim to be the mightiest of wish-dragon hunters? 

You have withheld my Glimmer from me in enemy territory; 

it is now up to you to restore it to me in full. 

Take notice that I will not accept any bone, fragment or otherwise, from you that is not of the promised quality or higher. 

Should you bring me this worthless dust again, 

I shall exercise against you my right of rejection because you have treated me with contempt."
3717431477.text_zh:
向甘内斯抱怨的平板 

“告诉甘内斯：奥尔-阿姆拉尔发来以下信息： 

当你来到圣城时，你对我说：“我会给你的军械库取来上等的纯正阿罕卡拉骸骨。” 

然后你就离开了，但你并没有履行你的承诺。 

你把脆骨碎块摆放在我的机灵面前说道： 

“愿意拿就拿去，不愿意拿就拉倒！” 

你当我是什么人，竟如此轻蔑对我…？！ 

…你还自称是最强大的神龙猎人？ 

你在敌占区让我无法拿到我的微光； 

而现在得由你来把它全部归还给我。 

注意，你提供的骸骨、碎片或是其他任何东西，只要低于承诺的质量，我一概不收。 

你要是再带给我这种没用的垃圾， 

我就会对你行使我的拒绝权，因为你待我轻蔑。”

266021826.name: Stoicism
266021826.subtitle: We are the final stand. The fortress in the storm.
266021826.subtitle_zh: 我们是最后的抵抗。风暴之中的堡垒。
266021826.text:
I'm not one to navel-gaze; that is better suited to the mystics and so-called philosophers who are ill at ease with the quiet absence of war. No offense to the late "Speaker" of our fair city, but I have come to view any person with big ideas with suspicion. Many think you're a big idea because they do not understand you.  

Not long ago, I fought alongside an Eliksni and a Cabal—both capable and proud warriors. We were on Neptune, and as I scanned the aftermath of battle, I thought of… home. Somehow, light-years and galaxies from where they'd been born, these two had become my comrades. They fought with an intensity warriors exert when defending their home. 

You aren't the meaning of the universe, or the meaning of life, are you? I don't pretend to know your intentions; not my business. But I feel it has to do with home. I just feel it, the way you stand guard over us—and that is what you're doing—that you know the importance of home. Hell, one day you might decide to leave for good, but I would still like to believe that, at least for a little while, this was your home. 

—Unknown Titan
266021826.text_zh:
我不是个钻牛角尖的人，那更适合神秘主义者和所谓的哲学家，他们对没有战争的平静感到不安。我无意冒犯我们美丽城市已故的先知，但我对任何自称有好主意的人都心存疑虑。许多人因为不理解你而认为你是个好主意。  

不久前，我与埃里克斯尼族和卡巴尔并肩作战——他们都是能干而骄傲的战士。我们当时在海王星上，当我扫视战后的景象时，我想到了…家。不知怎的，这两人在距离他们出生地无数光年和星系的地方成了我的战友。他们带着战士们保卫家园时的奋勇战斗。 

你不是宇宙的意义，也不是生命的意义，对吧？我不会假装我知道你的意图；那不关我的事。但我觉得这和家有关。我只是感觉到了，你守卫我们的方式——这就是你在做的事——你知道家的重要性。见鬼，也许有一天你会决定永远离开，但我还是愿意相信，至少有那么一小会儿，这里是你的家。 

——不知名的泰坦

1140861969.name: Promised Reunion Mark
1140861969.subtitle: "Together we would find peace."
1140861969.text:
—-Titan, O Titan. Your Traveler betrayed you just as it betrayed us. We do not pity you; we mourn with you. We wail alongside you at the graves of your beloved son and your treasured partner. We hold you in our arms and bear the weight of your sorrows, for they are our own.  

We will not lament the absence of fairness in this universe; indifference does not balk in the face of righteous anger. Nor does it bend to judicious retribution.  

No action should be reviled more than inaction in the face of great pain and agony. One may do evil, one may do good, but one must do something. This is where our Gardener failed you. It hung in the sky watching as your boy, your Hakim, was slain so mercilessly. It did nothing as his lifeblood drained in Safiyah's arms. He left this existence knowing not the breadth of its delights, nor the depths of its heartaches. Stolen. 

We give you justice, Commander Zavala. We give you the joy denied to you under the unfeeling god you once worshipped. We give him back to you whole and perfect, and we ask for nothing in return.—-
1140861969.text_zh:
——泰坦，啊，泰坦。你的旅行者背叛了你，就像它背叛了我们那样。我们不同情你；我们与你同悲。我们在你的爱子和挚友的墓前与你一起哭泣。我们将你拥入怀中，承受你的悲伤，因为它们也是我们自己的悲伤。  

我们不会哀叹这个宇宙的不公；冷漠不会在正义的愤怒面前退缩。它也不会屈服于明断的报复。  

在巨大的痛苦和折磨面前，没有什么行为比不作为更让人憎恶。人可以作恶，也可以行善，但必须有作为。这就是我们的园丁让你失望的地方。当你的孩子，你的哈基姆，被无情杀害时，它只是在空中注视着。当他的生命在萨菲亚的怀抱中流逝时，它什么也没做。他离开了这个世界，既不知道这个世界的快乐有多广阔，也不知道这个世界的痛苦有多深邃。他被窃取了。 

我们会为你伸张正义，指挥官萨瓦拉。我们会给予你，被你曾经崇拜的无情神明剥夺的快乐。我们会把他完整无缺地还给你，而我们不求任何回报。——

304385651.name: First Ascent Gauntlets
304385651.subtitle: Hold close your own.
304385651.text:
Light forgets, Darkness remembers. 

Caiatl wonders what waits inside the Traveler. She's heard the stories from Red Legion defectors about how it swallowed Ghaul like a warbeast choking down a bone. 

"He's still in its belly," a Valus on her War Council once told her, and Saladin Forge had made a breathy sound through his nose that Caiatl interpreted as laughter. 

That was days ago. Now she stands on the bridge of her ship, wondering what of Ghaul remains, the Traveler's glow reflected in the black of her eyes and the ornamental jewelry she wears on her tusks. She does not feel the pull of it, as she imagines Ghaul did, or even Saladin's quiet reverence. It is not a thing to be conquered or worshipped, but it is important to the people who are important to her—and that is all that matters. 

When she hears footsteps behind her, she does not turn. She already knows whom they belong to. 

"I did not request your counsel," she says without reprimand. "But if you have something to say, then speak." 

"Must I always have some wisdom for you?" Saladin asks. "Can't we simply await the end together in comfortable silence?" 

"Your worth is your wisdom. It's the only reason I let you live." 

Saladin makes that noise again. He knows that isn't true. 

And so does she.
304385651.text_zh:
光能遗忘，暗影铭记。 

查厄托想知道旅行者内部会有什么在等着他们。她从猩红军团叛逃者那里听说过旅行者是如何像战兽啃食骨头一样吞下了盖欧。 

“他还在它的肚子里，”战争议会上的一名军政官曾经这样告诉查厄托，而她将萨拉丁·弗吉用鼻子发出的哼哼声理解为了嗤笑。 

那是两天前的事了。她现在站在她飞船的舰桥上，琢磨着盖欧还剩下了什么。旅行者的光芒映在她的漆黑眼珠和装饰獠牙的珠宝上。她没有感受到在她的想象中盖欧对它的渴求，也没有感受到萨拉丁对它的崇敬。它不是一种该被征服或膜拜的东西，但它对那些对她很重要的人来说很重要——这才是重点。 

当她听到身后有脚步声时，她没有转身。她已经知道那是谁了。 

“我没有询问你的意见，”她说道，没有斥责的意思。“但如果你有话要讲，那就开口吧。” 

“难道我是位智慧导师？”萨拉丁问道。“我们就不能一起安静地等待终末吗？” 

“你的智慧是你的价值。那是我让你活着的唯一原因。” 

萨拉丁又发出了那种哼哼声。他知道那不是真的。 

而她也知道。

1725332125.name: First Ascent Plate
1725332125.subtitle: Oh, to read a pulpy golden age detective novel… just once more.
1725332125.subtitle_zh: 简陋通俗的黄金时代侦探小说…能再读一次就好了。
1725332125.text:
Light forgets, Darkness remembers. 

Ikora studied the strange approximation of the Tower, dust kicked up around her as the wind gusted through creaking halls. She felt the pull to explore… to find her old office. To see just how deep the recreation would go. 

But as she took a step up the stairs, her foot caught something—a small but familiar rectangular shape. She picked up the book and gently brushed dust from the cover. It was a copy of "The Spine-Tingling Adventures of Sedona Kane, P.I." The pulpy cover art told her it was the fourth installment of the series, with the subtitle "The Curious Case of Doctor Pennyworth." 

Light forgets, Darkness remembers. 

Darkness. In a place of such potent Light, would it be enough to manifest… everything? She flipped through the book; even the coffee stain still adorned page 95. 

Flashes of memory came back to Ikora as she studied the bold colors and heavy lines of the book's tattered jacket. She recalled kicking her feet up against the wall in her bunk one night after a particularly nasty Crucible loss… Ophiuchus's glow providing just enough visibility. Remembered cleaning the spilled drink off the pages in the mess hall and praying there was no lasting damage. And thought of other moments, of a warm hand covering her own as she read the text out loud for the thousandth time… 

The Warlock held the book to her nose. Just to take in the scent once more.  

Light forgets, Darkness remembers, and so would she.
1725332125.text_zh:
光能遗忘，暗影铭记。 

艾可拉审视着这座近似高塔的奇特建筑。她周围的尘土随着破败大堂中的狂风扬起。她感受到了探索的渴望…她想找到她以前的办公室。看看这个复制品到底有多像。 

但刚踏上楼梯，她的脚就碰到了一件物品——它的形状小而熟悉。她拿起那本书，轻轻拂去封面上的灰尘。这是一本《私家侦探塞多纳·凯恩的惊奇历险记》。从它俗气的封面上可以看出，这是该系列的第四部，副标题是“潘尼沃斯医生奇案”。 

光能遗忘，暗影铭记。 

暗影。在光能如此充足的地方，它是否能够显现…一切？她翻了翻书；甚至第95页上的咖啡渍都还在。 

当艾可拉打量着破旧书皮上大胆的色彩和厚重的线条时，她的记忆片段又闪现在了眼前。她回想起在熔炉竞技场中大败后，有一天夜里躺床上用脚蹬着墙…蛇夫座的光刚好够亮…在食堂里清理洒在书本上的饮料，祈祷没留下永久印记。她还想起，当她反复大声阅读时，一只温暖的手覆在自己的手上… 

这位术士把书抵到自己的鼻头，再一次感受它的气味。  

光能遗忘，暗影铭记，而她也会如此。

3187320016.name: First Ascent Mark
3187320016.subtitle: There is nothing as exquisite as the feeling of doing what no one has done.
3187320016.subtitle_zh: 做别人没做过的事，感觉最美妙了。
3187320016.text:
Light forgets, Darkness remembers. 

Mara Sov grit her teeth as she held the H.E.L.M. steady, straining all the while to keep the portal open with her power just long enough for the Guardian, Ikora, and Commander Zavala to slip through. 

Mara shifted her focus to watch the live feed in the viewscreen beside her as the Guardian took their first steps into the Pale Heart. 

And instantly… she remembered what it felt like to be first. 

She remembered unending emptiness, the spark of protons, cold rock against her back, and the sensation of spilling upwards eternally. She remembered glacial till veined with platinum, a forest that spread as mycelium, and alpine saddles cradling crystal clear lakes. She remembered a world so young and old, where all life was equal, meaningless and meaningful. She remembered making that memory, that place, calling it awake from the cauldron of her own imagination and raising it into matter, her lips curled on its name. The Distributary. 

Mara would never see that world again, and yet, on the grainy video stuttering before her, was its doppelganger. It was not home, but it was close. 

The video feed sputtered out. 

A roar of violet streaked past the H.E.L.M., and with a sudden silence, the ship burst from the portal into open space. The portal did not snap shut behind them—the Witness must have let go. 

Mara caught her breath. Her hands shook. There was no sign of Crow in there, or on comms, no sign he was alive other than the tug on her own heart. She glanced back to the Traveler and the Pale Heart within.  

Mara Sov thought once more of home.
3187320016.text_zh:
光能遗忘，暗影铭记。 

玛拉·索维咬紧牙关，拼尽全力让应急后勤行动中心保持稳定，同时用她的力量保持传送门开启，让守护者、艾可拉、指挥官萨瓦拉有机会顺利通过。 

玛拉把注意力转移到身旁的屏幕上，通过直播画面看到守护者在苍白之心中迈出了第一步。 

忽然…她记起了身为先行者的感受。 

她记起了无尽的空虚，质子的火花，抵着后背的冰冷岩石，永远向上的延伸感。她记起了被铂金缠绕的冰川，像菌丝一样蔓延的森林，还有被高山环抱的清澈湖泊。她记起了一个如此年轻而古老的世界。在那里，所有的生命都平等，没有意义，也充满意义。她记起自己创造那段记忆，那个地方，把它从自己想象的大锅里唤醒，将它升华为物质，嘴角微微翘起说出它的名字：两仪界。 

玛拉再也见不到那个世界了。然而，在她面前不断卡顿的模糊视频中，她看见了那个世界的复制品。那不是家，但已经很接近了。 

视频信号中断了。 

一道紫色的光芒席卷了应急后勤行动中心，飞船里忽然安静下来。他们通过传送门冲进了无垠的太空，身后的传送门并没有关闭——见证者肯定是松手了。 

玛拉喘过气来。她的手在颤抖。里面没有乌鸦的踪迹，也没有来自他的通讯。除了心中的牵挂，没有任何迹象表明他还活着。她回头瞥了一眼旅行者和其中的苍白之心。  

玛拉·索维再次想起了家园。

298824490.name: First Ascent Helm
298824490.subtitle: Choose what you will become next.
298824490.subtitle_zh: 选择你接下来要成为什么样的人。
298824490.text:
Light forgets, Darkness remembers. 

Once, a Ghost was heard to speak thusly. 

This one is Luzaku. Here, this one tells what is known of Sky. 

Sky is the breath taken between actions. It permits speculation. It invites doubt. It slips from sight and grasp, and yet persists. 

This one's Ghost would have us yield to certainty. He wishes us to walk the Bladed Path, to seek Hive-strength in the Witch Queen's abandoned logic, whereby all things prove themselves in slaughter. 

This one turns from simple inevitability. This one makes a choice: this one does not kill and does not die. Yet this one exists. Aiat. What follows? What other choices are to be made? 

This one must know. 

This one hides within a blade-ship of the Witch Queen's great foe. This one's Ghost is angry now, but he remains. In the hollows where a worm once coiled, this one senses our swift motion through the firmament, toward a center. 

This one seeks Sky. In the Sky, there are many paths. 

In the Sky, there is change.
298824490.text_zh:
光能遗忘，暗影铭记。 

很久以前，一个机灵说过这些话。 

鄙人是鲁扎库，在此讲述鄙人对苍穹的了解。 

苍穹是行动之间的喘息。它允许猜测。它引人怀疑。它难以追踪和把握，却始终留存。 

鄙人的机灵希望我们屈服于确定性。他希望我们走上刀锋之道，寻求邪魔族的力量，遵从巫妖女王遭抛弃的逻辑，即万物需在屠杀中证明自身。 

鄙人放弃了简单的必然性。鄙人做出了选择：鄙人不杀，也不死亡。然而，鄙人仍然存在。阿特。接下来呢？还要做出什么选择？ 

鄙人必须知晓。 

鄙人躲在巫妖女王宿敌的刀锋飞船里。鄙人的机灵很生气，但他没有离去。在蠕虫曾经盘踞的深渊里，鄙人感知到我们正迅速穿过苍穹，前往中心。 

鄙人探寻苍穹。苍穹内有许多道路。 

苍穹内有变化。

39339589.name: First Ascent Greaves
39339589.subtitle: To enter the body of a deity would be to unquestionably defile it.
39339589.subtitle_zh: 进入神灵的身体无疑是一种玷污。
39339589.text:
Light forgets, Darkness remembers. 

Mithrax stood at the bow of the H.E.L.M., watching as Zavala's ship vanished from view into the portal. That awful gateway pulsed and wavered, and though the H.E.L.M. was pointed straight at it, he was resolved in his decision. 

The notion of venturing inside the Great Machine was innately revolting. It reeked like a taboo as certain as cannibalism, as unthinkable as besmirching a house of worship; to enter the body of a deity would unquestionably be to defile it. He could find a way to support from afar. Surely that was plausible.  

"Father, the Queen is asking for you." 

Eido sidles up next to him, and the two look out over the Great Machine. It takes up the entirety of the window—the center of all Light punctured by the oscillating violet of the portal, and Mithrax realizes how small he feels alongside his daughter. 

"I'm not going down there without you," she says. 

Mithrax holds back his shiver and confesses, "To step inside feels like a transgression." 

"And who made that rule?" she says. Ever acute, ever wise. When Mithrax cannot answer, she continues, "The Traveler is in peril. So long as we can care, we are bound to enter and defend it. I have seen you still have fight in you, Father." 

"Would that not be worse? To wage war at the very center of Light?" 

"Only you can decide that. But I believe the Traveler would want you to enter the portal." 

"Why?" 

His daughter puts a loving hand on his own. "Because it knows you aren't there to hurt it."
39339589.text_zh:
光能遗忘，暗影铭记。 

米瑟拉克斯站在应急后勤行动中心的船首，注视着萨瓦拉的飞船从视野中消失，进入传送门。那道可怕的大门在脉动和摇摆，尽管应急后勤行动中心正对着它，但他已经下定了决心。 

进入大机器内部的想法令他反感。像同类相食一般让人厌恶，像糟蹋圣堂一般难以想象；进入神灵的身体无疑是一种玷污。他可以想办法从远处进行支援。他认为那是在理的。  

“父亲，女王在找你。” 

艾多走到他的身边。两人眺望着大机器。它填满了整个窗户——这位光能之神的中心，被传送门的震荡之紫刺穿了，米瑟拉克斯意识到自己和女儿在其身边是多么渺小。 

“没有你，我不会进去，”她说。 

米瑟拉克斯强忍着冷颤承认道，“进去像是一种亵渎。” 

“那种规则是谁定的？”她反问道。一如既往地机敏、睿智。米瑟拉克斯不知如何回答，而她还在继续，“旅行者正处于危险之中。只要我们还关爱它，我们就必须进去保护它。我知道你还有斗志，父亲。” 

“那样不是更糟糕吗？在光能的中心作战？” 

“那取决于你。但我相信旅行者会希望你进入传送门。” 

”为什么？“ 

他的女儿把一只充满爱意的手放在他的手背上。“因为它知道你不是去伤害它的。”

3306754793.name: Sublime Mark
3306754793.subtitle: We celebrate the future we will build together.
3306754793.subtitle_zh: 赞颂我们将会共同构建的未来。
3306754793.text:
The atmosphere inside Rehnpeir's hits Zavala differently today. Sounds are muted, the lights, harsh. He stops to stare sidelong at a piece of art on the wall. Bold colors streak across canvas, evoking the shape of a helm. How long has that been there, he wonders to himself. 

A hand on his shoulder startles him, shaking him free of his reverie. Zavala turns to see Sloane. She guides him to her table. He sits opposite her, his gaze fixed on the errant flower petals and strip of celebratory tinsel caught in the crook of her breastplate.  

"Got held up by the festivities?" she asks. Zavala grunts a noncommittal agreement.  

"Where's Síocháin?" he interjects. 

Sloane shrugs. "With Glint, last I saw. Catching up." Her nonchalance makes Zavala shift uneasily. 

They place their orders, Sloane never glancing at the menu she's already re-memorized; Zavala, taking too long to find his usual, tucked away on the menu's backside. Was it always there?  

He orders with extra spice. 

Sloane sips her tea for a moment, watching as Zavala forces his focus elsewhere. "Having any trouble?" she asks after a long while. 

"With what?" Zavala replies, pretending not to hear the depth of her question.  

Sloane adjusts her inquiry. "Stasis must be… an adjustment?" 

He recognizes the shift in her strategy, alters his own to match. "Opinions on Darkness have been changing," he says flatly. 

"I didn't ask what everyone else thinks. I asked you," Sloane reiterates. 

"My opinions… may be adjusting as well." 

She nods. "Change is hard. But if there's anyone I trust to handle that kind of thing, it's you," Sloane says frankly.  

Steaming bowls of noodles appear. Zavala is grateful for them suddenly, though the strength of his gratitude for such a distraction troubles even him. 

"How's the Vanguard holding up?" 

"Strangely," Zavala admits. He pokes at his noodles, watches the steam coil up into the air. "It was hard to believe we'd get this far. And now… we're adapting to this new way of living, I suppose." 

"It will get better. One day at a time," she reassures. 

It sounds like a platitude, save for the fact it's Sloane saying it. "It's hard to see it that way sometimes." Zavala says this to his noodles. 

"Even if things are different… we're doing this together," Sloane says. Her hand comes into his field of view, resting atop his; Zavala finally glances up. "Don't forget that."  

A look of understanding passes between them as Sloane gives Zavala's hand a reassuring squeeze. The physical contact grounds him. Despite it all, when he considers the future there is still a gentle warmth. Perhaps distant; perhaps small.  

It will grow.
3306754793.text_zh:
今日瑞恩佩尔餐厅内的氛围给萨瓦拉带来了不同的感受。声音没那么嘈杂，灯光则显得刺眼。他停下脚步，斜眼盯着墙上的一幅艺术品。大胆的色彩划过画布，让人联想到头盔的形状。他暗自疑惑，这幅画已经挂在这里多久了？ 

他被一只搭上他肩膀的手吓了一跳，从沉思中醒来。萨瓦拉转身看到斯隆。她领他走到自己的桌前。他坐在她对面，目光落在她胸甲夹着的花瓣和庆祝用的金丝上。  

“被庆典活动耽搁了？”她问道。萨瓦拉不置可否地哼了一声。  

“西奥昌在哪儿？”他插嘴问道。 

斯隆耸耸肩。“我上次看到时，是和格林特在一起，叙旧。”她的漫不经心引得萨瓦拉不安地挪动起来。 

他们点了餐，斯隆看都没看她已经熟记于心的菜单；萨瓦拉则花了很长时间才在菜单背面找到他常点的那道。它一直都在那个位置吗？  

他点了加料的口味。 

斯隆抿了一会儿茶，看着萨瓦拉努力把注意力转移到别处。“遇到什么麻烦了吗？”过了好一会儿，她才问道。 

“什么麻烦？”萨瓦拉假装没听出她问题的深意，回答道。  

斯隆改变了询问的方式。“冰影一定得有个…适应调整的过程吧？” 

他意识到她变化了策略，于是也改变了自己的回答方式。“大家对暗影的看法一直在变，”他平淡地说道。 

“我没问别人怎么想。我问的是你，”斯隆重申道。 

“我的观点…可能也在调整。” 

她点点头。“改变很难。但如果说我相信有谁能处理好这种事，那就是你了，”斯隆坦率地说。  

几碗热气腾腾的面条出现在了桌上。萨瓦拉突然间对它们心存感激，尽管他对这样一件小小的分心事产生的强烈感激，让他自己都感到有些困扰。 

“先锋的情况怎么样？” 

“有些怪，”萨瓦拉承认道。他戳了戳面条，看着蒸汽盘旋上升。“过去很难相信我们能走到这一步。而如今…我想我们正在适应这种新的生活方式吧。" 

“会好起来的。一天一天来，”她安慰道。 

这听起来像是一句陈词滥调，但出自斯隆之口就不一样了。“有时很难以这种方式看待问题。”萨瓦拉对着他的面条说道。 

“即使情况不同了…我们也会一起面对，”斯隆说道。她的手出现在他的视线中，放在他的手掌上；萨瓦拉终于抬起头看了一眼。“别忘了这一点。”  

斯隆握住萨瓦拉的手，两人交换了一个理解的眼神。肢体的接触让他感到安心。尽管发生了这一切，但当他想到未来时，心中仍然涌现出一股温柔的暖意，虽然有些遥远，也有些微弱。  

但它会慢慢增长的。

1800866764.name: Veteran Legend Gauntlets
1800866764.subtitle: "I'll tell my children I was there. Before the battle had a name. Before it became a symbol of victory for the Titan orders."
1800866764.subtitle_zh: “我会告诉我的孩子们，在那场战斗还没有名字之前，在它成为泰坦胜利的象征之前，我就在那里了。”
1800866764.text:
My grandfather came to the City when it was just tents and huts. He traveled the Pilgrim Road on foot, all the way across the Panama Ravine with his entire family and was the only survivor by the end. He never talked about the journey much, not until his last years. Honestly, it helped give me perspective. I never knew the City as he did. I've only ever known the walls as a project, and watching those last stones be put into place made it feel like we were invincible.

Now, I write this journal entry from a bunker hundreds of feet below the streets. There is a battle raging outside the City walls, but I can feel it reverberating through the stone. Every time the lights flicker, I wonder, "Is this it?" The feeds say the aliens are attacking from six directions at once. I don't know if the walls will hold, if the Risen protecting us will stand. I don't know if I will see tomorrow. I just know the Traveler is here, and we are safe in its shadow.

They promised that this was the Last Safe City. We've all sacrificed too much to give up on that dream. We must survive.
1800866764.text_zh:
我祖父来到圣城时，这里还只有帐篷和棚屋。他带着全家徒步走过朝圣者之路，穿过巴拿马峡谷，是最后唯一的幸存者。直到晚年，他都没怎么提起过这段旅程。说实话，这给了我很多启发。我从未像他那样了解圣城。我只知道城墙是一项工程，而看着那最后的几块石头砌放到位，让我们感到自己坚不可摧。

此刻，我正在街道下方数百英尺的地堡里写下这篇日志。圣城高墙外战火纷飞，但我能感觉到战争在石缝中回响。每当灯光闪烁，我都在想，“那一刻要来了吗？”消息称外星人同时从六个方向发动了进攻，我不知道城墙能否撑得住，也不知道保护我们的复生者能否屹立不倒。我不知道我能否活着看到明天。我只知道旅行者在这里，我们在它的荫蔽之下很安全。

他们承诺这里是“最后的安全城市”。我们都牺牲了太多，不能放弃这个梦想。我们必须活下去。

2183976852.name: Veteran Legend Plate
2183976852.subtitle: "I might not be a Guardian, but they've reminded us you don't need the Light to be a hero."
2183976852.subtitle_zh: “我也许不是守护者，但他们提醒我们，成为英雄不一定需要光能。”
2183976852.text:
My mother passed away last week. She left me the journals she'd been keeping since the days the walls were being built. She left her father's father's journals from before the City even had walls. They lived long, full lives. Reading about them makes me wish I had seen the City of their times. I was a boy when the Guardians won the battle of Twilight Gap. I've only ever known peace behind the walls, only watched the City grow and thrive. I barely know how to handle a rifle. I work textiles. I make clothes. I want to open a shop to tailor clothing for the Guardians. I don't want to die.

I've been hiding with the resistance for three weeks now, since they found me sleeping in a storm drain. I lost everything in the Cabal attack. All my family's writings. My sister. My son. The Guardians—even without their Light—are defending us. They're showing me how to shoot, how to survive. Every day someone leaves our hideout and never returns. Mas'ouda, Arzu, Brajko, Mitra, Kardelen, and Luca died this week. The Cabal are relentless, and sooner or later they're going to figure out where we're hiding. 

There's fifteen of us left, five combat frames, and two Guardians.

I have to survive. Humanity has to survive. It can't end like this.
2183976852.text_zh:
我母亲上周去世了。她把从建造城墙时就开始写的日记留给了我。她还留下了她父亲的父亲的日记，那时的圣城甚至还没有城墙。他们度过了漫长而充实的一生。读着他们的日记，我真希望能亲眼看到他们那个时代的圣城。守护者赢得暮光峡谷战役时，我还是个孩子。我只知道高墙之后的和平，只看到了圣城的成长和繁荣。我几乎不会用步枪。我从事纺织工作。我制作衣物。我想开家为守护者们定制服装的店。我不想死。

从我睡在暴雨排水沟里被反抗军发现后算起，我已经跟他们一起躲了三个星期。在卡巴尔的袭击中，我失去了一切。所有我家人的日志。我的妹妹。我的儿子。守护者们——即使没有了他们的光能——仍在保护着我们。他们教我如何射击，如何生存。每天都有人离开我们的藏身处，再没回来。马斯乌达、阿尔祖、布拉伊科、米特拉、卡德伦，还有卢卡，都死在了这周。卡巴尔步步紧逼，他们迟早会发现我们躲藏的地方。 

我们还剩下十五个人，五个战斗框架和两名守护者。

我必须生存下去。人类必须生存下去。不能就这样结束。

3352264425.name: Veteran Legend Mark
3352264425.subtitle: "All endings are beginnings."
3352264425.text:
Tonight, I watched a thousand lanterns fill the night sky. Tonight, I watched the hopes and dreams of humanity burn bright in the dark and challenge the uncertainty of the future. Tonight, I gave birth to a child that will shoulder the same burden of humanity's uncertain future that I have. Tonight a new person came into this world who will share in my family's stories, hear of their ancestors and their triumphs, their failures, and their legends. Tonight, humanity takes a step into a future so unknown we do not even have a word for it. Tonight is a moment that must live forever, no detail forgotten.

Tonight, the war is over. Tonight, a new age dawns. Tonight, I am so very tired. From my bedroom I hear congratulations and cheers. I hear excitement. Everyone I have spoken to is dreaming about the future now, rather than merely surviving the next day. Some of my friends want to venture into the stars, leave the safety of the City and explore. They want to reclaim everything we've lost; all these worlds. But I won't be joining them. My place is here in the City, where my family has lived and died for generations. My friends ask, "Why would you want to stay in the Last City?" But I don't think it's going to stay the Last City.

I think this is the First City of many to come.
3352264425.text_zh:
今夜，我看着万盏灯笼挂满夜空。今夜，我看着人类的希望和梦想在黑暗中熠熠生辉，挑战着未来的不确定性。今夜，我生下了一个孩子，他将和我一样肩负起人类不确定未来的重担。今夜，一个新成员来到这个世界，与我共享家族的故事，聆听祖先的事迹，以及他们的胜利、失败和传奇。今夜，人类踏出了迈向未来的一步，我们甚至找不到一个词来形容它的未知性。今夜是一个永恒的时刻，任何细节都不会被遗忘。

今夜，战争迎来终结。今夜，新的时代来临。今夜，我已疲惫不堪。我从卧室里听到了祝贺与欢呼，听到了兴奋与激昂。与我交谈过的每个人都在憧憬未来，而不仅仅是想着怎么熬过明天。我的一些朋友想去星际冒险，离开圣城的庇护向外探索。他们想重新夺回我们失去的一切；所有这些世界。但我不会与他们同行。我的归宿是圣城，这是我的家族世世代代生活和死去的地方。我的朋友们问我，“你为什么想留在最后的圣城里？”而我觉得，它将不再是最后的圣城。

我想对未来的众多城市来说，它会是第一座圣城。

2913980509.name: Veteran Legend Helm
2913980509.subtitle: "There's a last, safe city out there somewhere. We have to believe."
2913980509.subtitle_zh: “一定还有最后的安全之城。我们必须相信。”
2913980509.text:
"The Last Safe City" exists in name only. I came here expecting to find a lost metropolis from before the Collapse. Instead, it's a sea of tents and prefabricated shelters huddled around bonfires. Everyone here thinks that hiding in the shadow of the Traveler will keep them safe. Keep humanity's killers at arm's length. All I see are hundreds of miles of rough, snow-capped mountains. All I can feel is the memory of frostbite in my fingers. That's not going to stop anyone, just slow them down.

I came here in a caravan of settlers. The march up the mountains was worse than any battle I'd survived. Hundreds died along the way from injuries, starvation, exposure. All the greatest hits. We buried them along the roadside, with no time for markers or ceremony. I've heard some of the Risen here talking about forming guard patrols to escort people. I don't know. Sooner or later our enemies are going to follow the trail of ants back to the mound. We'd never survive a full-frontal assault.

More Risen arrive every day. They're starting to organize, make plans. They make me nervous. I can't shake the memories. Groups of them hitting settlements for ammunition and food, mass executions for those who dared speak out against them, entire towns turned to craters. These ones seem different from the Warlords, but I can't just let it go. The other settlers here are just like the ones outside the "City," consumed with their own ideas about how the world should run. I've heard plenty of people talking about organizing an exodus, just getting in whatever ships we have and abandoning Earth. As if anywhere else in this system is safe. Others want to form clear lines of succession and leadership. Then there's the people like me—trusting their guns—waiting for the other shoe to drop. We know war is a certainty.

Something is going to kill us all. It's just a matter of when, not if. There's nowhere safe. Not anywhere. Not anymore.
2913980509.text_zh:
“最后的安全城市”有名无实。我来到这里，本以为会发现一座大崩溃前的失落大都市。但这里却是一片围着篝火的帐篷和预制房屋的海洋。这里的每个人都以为躲在旅行者的荫蔽之下，就能保证自己的安全，就能与残害人类的杀手保持距离。可我看到的只有数百英里的崎岖雪山，我能感受到的只有手指上冻疮的记忆。那阻止不了任何人，只会拖慢他们的脚步。

我是随着一队定居者来到这里的。上山的行进比我经历过的任何一场战役都要艰难。沿途数百人死于伤痛、饥饿、受冻。最糟糕的情况都发生了。我们把他们埋在路边，没时间立碑或是举行葬礼。我听说这里的一些复生者在谈论组建护卫巡逻队来护送人们。我不知道这是否明智。我们的敌人迟早会沿着痕迹追踪到我们的巢穴。到时候，我们绝对撑不过他们的全面进攻。

每天都有更多的复生者抵达。他们开始组织起来，制定计划。他们让我感到紧张。我无法摆脱那些记忆。他们那样的人曾抱团去定居点抢夺弹药和食物，大规模处决敢于出声反对他们的人，把各个城镇变成弹坑。这些人看起来与战争领主不同，但我的内心无法平静。这里的其他定居者跟“圣城”外面的那些人并无二致，认为世界就该像自己想的那样运作。我听到很多人都在谈论组织一次大逃亡，随便坐上什么飞船，抛弃地球。就好像这个星系里的其他地方都是安全的一样。另外一些人想制定明确的继任和领导体系。还有像我这样的人——相信自己的枪杆子——提心吊胆地等待着坏事发生。我们知道战争无可避免。

有东西会将我们所有人置于死地。这一定会发生，只不过是时间问题。没有地方是安全的。哪儿都不安全。也再也不会有安全的地方了。

2446702198.name: Veteran Legend Greaves
2446702198.subtitle: "The Traveler didn't run, it rose up to meet the enemy."
2446702198.subtitle_zh: “旅行者没有逃跑，而是起身迎敌。”
2446702198.text:
The Traveler is gone.

I watched it as it left the City. The sky lit up like the world was ending. It's still up there, though. When the sun is at the right angle you can see it like a second moon. I remember, as a teenager, sitting on the roof of my apartment building, watching the pieces of the Traveler reform. I could feel the Light in the way they say Guardians and Ghosts can. I felt so confident that day, so sure that we were all going to be saved. Many are doubting, but when I look up into the sky and see that the Traveler is still there—defending not just the City, but all of Earth—my faith is as strong as ever.

In the days since the Traveler left, Coalition ships have filled the City's skies. I remember my uncle talking about the last time he saw Cabal ships in the sky—it was the day my mother died. It feels like we've been through so much in such a short time. My uncle would tell me our family's stories every night. We'd lost all the written copies after the invasion, but now they exist in me, and I will record what I remember. So we know where we came from and what was lost.

Everyone is saying this is the end. But I know enough history to be sure that it's not the first time we've felt this way. Every threat the City faces feels like it'll be the last. My uncle died during the Endless Night, saving Eliksni that once tried to lay siege to our home. Nothing lasts forever and everything changes. Buildings burn, people die, but we move on. 

I don't think this is the end. I think this is a new beginning.
2446702198.text_zh:
旅行者走了。

我看着它离开圣城。天空就像世界末日一样亮了起来。但它还在天上。太阳角度恰到好处时，你就可以看到它，像是第二个月亮一样。我还记得，十几岁的时候，我坐在公寓楼的屋顶上，看着旅行者的碎片重组。我能感受到光能，就像人们说的守护者和机灵能做到的那样。那天我很有信心，确信我们都会得救。尽管很多人表示怀疑，但是当我仰望天空，看到旅行者还在那里，不仅保护着圣城，还保护着整个地球时，我的信念一如既往地坚定。

旅行者离开后的日子里，联盟的飞船布满了圣城的天空。我记得舅舅说过他最后一次在天空中看到卡巴尔飞船是在我母亲去世的那天。感觉我们在这么短的时间内经历了太多。我舅舅每天晚上都会跟我讲我们家族的故事。入侵之后，我们失去了所有的书面文本，但现在它们存在于我的心中，我会记录下我所记得的一切。这样我们就知道我们从哪里来，失去了什么。

每个人都在说末日已到。但我对历史的了解足以让我确信，这不是我们第一次有这种感觉。圣城面临的每一次威胁都像是最后一次。我舅舅在永夜时牺牲了，为的是拯救曾经试图围攻我们家园的埃里克斯尼族。没有什么是永恒的，一切都会改变。建筑烧毁，人们死去，但我们会继续前进。 

我不认为这是末日。我相信这是一个新的开始。

1627691271.name: Gifted Conviction
1627691271.subtitle: "Perfection is overvalued." —Ikora Rey
1627691271.text:
The H.E.L.M. is quiet save for a few robotic sentries monitoring the systems close by. The tablet in Ikora's grasp beeps in response to her touch and a set of projections appears before her. She searches through the information on the Sol Divisive—models, weaknesses, radiolaria research, even Hidden-specific analyses of their habits and types.

She glides her index finger over the screen until she finds a recording of a troop of Goblins being felled by a Guardian. It's quick—a couple of shots at most before they crumble to the ground in a puddle of radiolaria and the recording stops. The dim eye of the broken Vex catches her attention and she becomes so lost in contemplation that she barely hears another enter the room. She turns her head.

"Mithrax," Ikora acknowledges with a small nod.

"Ikora," he says, returning the greeting. "Has your research proven fruitful?"

"Sadly, no," she answers. Her gaze returns to the screen, and she sighs. "I've spent hours investigating the factions most likely to support the Witness, but it all just feels like… a distraction. Like they're fodder for its end goal."

Mithrax hums in agreement, his attention on the Vex Goblin she'd previously been transfixed by.

"Why would the Sol Divisive consider throwing themselves into the line of fire for something like the Final Shape?" she asks.

"Maybe… they simply have faith."

"Faith?" Ikora huffs involuntarily, something akin to a faintly sardonic laugh. "We know the Sol Divisive are an anomaly among the Vex, but are they even capable of that?"

"What else would convince one to commit life and death to a cause, if not faith in said cause?" Mithrax's tone is one of self-recognition, of understanding. "The idea of a better future."

Ikora remains quiet. Her eyes find the single eye of the Goblin once more.

"They chose their path for a reason that gives them purpose. Not unlike ourselves," Mithrax elaborates, hand gesturing to the screen. "Perhaps that is how the Sol Divisive believe they can achieve perfection."

Ikora's head tilts up as she considers his words. His suggestion makes sense, and it is the sort of faith a Vex would embrace: the pursuit of total perfection. A natural feeling of defiance wells up in her at the thought. She's known the underlying gnawing of expectation in words like 'perfection' and 'faith.' The ideals that have driven her throughout most of her life, as she'd morphed into countless versions of herself in pursuit of them.

Ikora swipes her finger across the tablet and the recording disappears, replaced with a new set of combatants.

"It's never too late to re-evaluate your faith," she says.
1627691271.text_zh:
除了几个监视附近星系的机器人哨兵外，应急后勤行动中心内一片寂静。艾可拉手中的平板电脑在她的触摸下哔哔作响，一组投影出现在她面前。她搜索着有关太阳系分支的信息——模型、弱点、活性放射体液研究，甚至还有针对其习性和类型的隐秘者专题分析。

她的食指在屏幕上滑动，直到她找到了一段哥布林小队被一名守护者击倒的录像。过程很快——最多也就几枪，然后他们就倒在地上，变成了一滩活性放射体液，录像随之停止。破损Vex昏暗的眼睛引起了她的注意，她沉浸在自己的沉思中，几乎没有听到另一个人走进房间。她转过头。

“米瑟拉克斯，”艾可拉微微点头致意。

“艾可拉，”他说道，回以问候。“你的研究有什么成果吗？”

“很遗憾，没有，”她的目光回到屏幕上，叹了口气。“我花了好几个小时来调查最有可能支持见证者的派系，但这都像是…障眼法。就好像他们是它最终目标的炮灰。”

米瑟拉克斯哼呜着表示同意，注意力转到了刚才引起她注意的Vex哥布林身上。

“为什么太阳系分支会愿意为了终焉之形那样的东西而吃枪子？”她问道。

“也许…他们只是有信仰而已。”

“信仰？”艾可拉不由自主地咆哮了一声，像是一种略带讥讽的嘲笑。“我们知道太阳系分支是Vex中的异类，但他们真的能拥有信仰吗？”

“如果不是信仰，还有什么能说服一个人为一项事业献身？”米瑟拉克斯的语气是一种自我认可，一种理解。“对美好未来的憧憬。”

艾可拉保持着沉默。她再次望向了那哥布林的独眼。

“他们选择自己的道路是有原因的，这给了他们使命。和我们并无不同，”米瑟拉克斯解释道，用手对着屏幕比划。“也许这就是太阳系分支认为自己可以达到完美的方式。”

艾可拉侧头思忖他的话。他的意见不无道理，这也是Vex会乐于接受的那种信仰：追求尽善尽美。一想到这里，她心里自然涌起一股抵触的情绪。她深知“完美”和“信仰”等词背后的期望带来的痛苦。这些想法驱使她走过了大半生，而在追逐这些想法的过程中，把她化作了自己的无数个版本。

艾可拉用手指在平板电脑上轻轻扫了一下，录像随之消失，取而代之的是一组新的战斗人员。

“重新评估自己的信仰永远都不晚，”她说道。

3001449507.name: Balance of Power
3001449507.subtitle: "In my mind I heard it whisper: 'come and see.'"
3001449507.subtitle_zh: “我听见它在我心里低语道：‘过来看看。'”
3001449507.text:
Maya Sundaresh sits hunched over a display, the only source of light in her dark office. Brain wave scans of 16 Exos read flatline on the monitor. "How is Doctor Ardehi?" she asks into an open mic.

"Dead." Chioma Esi's voice is a hoarse whisper.

Maya switches to the security camera in Veil Containment and sees her wife kneeling on the catwalk over Doctor Ardehi's body. A procession of dead Exos are slumped over the railings to Chioma's left and right. Maya tabs away to study a bar graph.

"Neuropathy reports show a spike in activity in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus in the moments before brain death," Maya reports, eliciting a shaky sigh from Chioma over the comms before she continues her analysis. "The spikes plateaued for one fifth of a second, which may indicate a receptor error. We may need to utilize an intermediary rather than direct connections. Do the hard wires show any damage?"

Maya tabs back to the security feed, watching as Chioma wipes her eyes and then assesses one of the dead Exos, checking a thick cable plugged into the back of his head. "No sign of damage. Capacitance switches didn't trigger. It's…" She swallows down bile. "The problem isn't our hardware…"

'It's theirs,' is a whisper only Maya can hear.
 
"It's theirs," Maya agrees aloud.

"I think—I think we need to stop," Chioma finds the strength to admit. "Reassess our findings. Resume analysis of the initial electromagnetic anomaly before contact. We can't keep… we can't…"

"Keep shoveling coal into the furnace?" Maya suggests as she leans back into her chair. Chioma is too taken aback by the casual disregard to loss of life to reply. "You're right." Maya continues. "But we're not stopping. We're reorienting. The Veil is the future of humanity."

For a moment, neither woman says anything. There is only the soft hum of electronics in a darkened room to fill Maya's senses. That, and a static hiss at the back of her mind.
 
"The Veil is dangerous," Chioma asserts, her voice is tinged with a tremor of emotion.  Fear of losing the woman she loves keeps her from pushing harder as they stand on the edge of moral precipice together.

'It is.'
 
"It is," Maya agrees aloud. "We must treat it with caution, respect, and also… reverence." A thought crystallizes. "We must treat it like a knife."
3001449507.text_zh:
玛雅·桑戴尔什蜷缩着身子坐在显示器前，这是她黑暗的办公室里唯一的光源。显示器上是16名Exo呈平线的脑电波扫描结果。“阿尔代希博士怎么样了？”她对着开放式麦克风问道。

“死了。”希欧玛·艾西的声音嘶哑而低沉。

玛雅切换到面纱遏制舱的监控摄像头，看到她妻子跪在走道上阿尔代希博士尸体前。希欧玛左右两边的栏杆上耷拉着一群死去的Exo。玛雅切换出来，转而研究一张条形图。

“神经病变报告显示，在脑死亡的前一刻，前额叶皮层和海马体的活动出现了激增，”玛雅的报告引得希欧玛在通讯器中发出一声颤抖的叹息，然后她继续分析道。“激增在五分之一秒内趋于平稳，这可能表明出现了接收器错误。我们可能需要利用媒介而不是直接连接。硬导线有损坏吗？”

玛雅轻击回到安保影像，看着希欧玛擦了擦眼睛，然后对其中一名死亡的Exo进行评估，检查他后脑勺上插着的一根粗电缆。“没有损坏迹象。电容开关没有触发。这…”她咽了一口。“问题不在于我们的硬件…”

“是他们的问题，”只有玛雅才能听到这声低语。
 
“是他们的问题，”玛雅大声表示赞同。

“我想——我想我们得停下来，”希欧玛鼓起勇气承认道。“重新评估我们的发现。继续分析接触之前的初始电磁异常。我们不能继续…我们不能…”

“继续火上浇油？”玛雅边说边靠在椅子上。这种漠视生命损失的随意态度让希欧玛惊讶得无法回答。“你说得对。”玛雅继续道。“但我们不会停下来。我们会重新适应。面纱是人类的未来。”

一时间，两个女人都没有说话。玛雅只感觉到黑暗房间里电子设备发出的轻微嗡鸣声。此外，她的脑海中还回荡着静电的嘶嘶声。
 
“面纱很危险，”希欧玛断言道，她的声音因饱含情绪而有些颤抖。此刻她们正一起立于道德的悬崖边上，而她害怕失去自己所爱的女人，不敢再多使一点劲。

“的确。”
 
“的确，”玛雅大声赞同道。“我们对待它时必须带着谨慎、尊重，还有…敬畏。”一个想法逐渐清晰起来。“就像是在对待一把匕首。”

2809120022.name: Relativism
2809120022.subtitle: We watch, and we listen. We are the first to see the danger lurking in the abyss.
2809120022.subtitle_zh: 我们观察并聆听。我们率先看到了潜伏在深渊中的危险。
2809120022.text:
You were the first wanderer. Navigator. Searching for an answer to a question you've yet to ponder.  

I am the watcher. Invisible. The eyes of the Last City. The very nature of my duty necessitates solitude. 

We were both adrift. Along the brinks of space, under the black sky. You enter the lives of people that grow to resent your desertion. But we share the same heart, and I know you. You aren't disaffected.  

We are not walking away. We are looking to the horizon. 

—Unknown Hunter
2809120022.text_zh:
你曾是第一个漫游者。领航者。寻找着你尚未思考的问题的答案。  

我是守望者。不为人所注意。 圣城的眼睛。我职责的性质决定了我必将孤独。 

我们都在漂泊。沿着太空的边缘，在漆黑的天空下。你进入了人们的生活中，因你的遗弃而遭其怨恨。但我们共有一颗心，而我了解你。你并非想要背叛。  

我们没有走开。我们是在展望天边。 

——不知名的猎人

87946917.name: Promised Reign Cloak
87946917.subtitle: "I turn, and there she is. Radiant."
87946917.subtitle_zh: “我转过身，她就在那儿。容光焕发。”
87946917.text:
—-Inside you, the Kestrel and the Crow tangle in a bid for dominance. Hunter, you are ensnared, but you need not fear. We come to pry the trap open. We free you from your gilded prison; a cell bathed in light and glowing as if it would somehow fill the vast emptiness around it. Guilt follows you like a long shadow cast in the setting sun. In darkness, there is no shadow to fear. 

The children of Sol would force upon you the wretched title of "Vanguard," a title made famous by thieves and murderers. We do not offer you equality… we offer you sovereignty. We would make you king. 

Here, you are King Uldren, a Kestrel who slays the Crow and takes to the skies, triumphant. You are no longer a specter living in the shadow of an unfeeling sibling. The sun rises to greet you, the earth beneath your feet bends to your every whim.  

Would you not stay… and see your sunrise?—-
87946917.text_zh:
——在你的内心之中，快隼与乌鸦正为了主导权而搏斗。猎人，你被困住了，但你不必害怕。让我们来撬开陷阱。我们会把你从那个镀金牢笼里解救出来；那个沐浴在光芒中，仿佛那样就能填补周围巨大空虚的牢房。愧疚如夕阳投下的长影，跟随着你。黑暗中，没有令人恐惧的阴影。 

太阳系的孩子们把“先锋”这个卑鄙的称号强加给你。一个由小偷和杀人犯创造出来的头衔。我们要给你的不是平等…而是主权。我们会让你成为王。 

在这里，你是国王欧顿。一只杀死了乌鸦，得意洋洋地冲上云霄的快隼。你不再是一个活在无情姐姐阴影下的幽灵。太阳升起迎接你的到来，脚下的大地任由你的意愿重塑。  

你愿意留下来…看看你的日出吗？——

2252757719.name: First Ascent Grips
2252757719.subtitle: Hold close your own.
2252757719.text:
Light forgets, Darkness remembers. 

Caiatl wonders what waits inside the Traveler. She's heard the stories from Red Legion defectors about how it swallowed Ghaul like a warbeast choking down a bone. 

"He's still in its belly," a Valus on her War Council once told her, and Saladin Forge had made a breathy sound through his nose that Caiatl interpreted as laughter. 

That was days ago. Now she stands on the bridge of her ship, wondering what of Ghaul remains, the Traveler's glow reflected in the black of her eyes and the ornamental jewelry she wears on her tusks. She does not feel the pull of it, as she imagines Ghaul did, or even Saladin's quiet reverence. It is not a thing to be conquered or worshipped, but it is important to the people who are important to her—and that is all that matters. 

When she hears footsteps behind her, she does not turn. She already knows whom they belong to. 

"I did not request your counsel," she says without reprimand. "But if you have something to say, then speak." 

"Must I always have some wisdom for you?" Saladin asks. "Can't we simply await the end together in comfortable silence?" 

"Your worth is your wisdom. It's the only reason I let you live." 

Saladin makes that noise again. He knows that isn't true. 

And so does she.
2252757719.text_zh:
光能遗忘，暗影铭记。 

查厄托想知道旅行者内部会有什么在等着他们。她从猩红军团叛逃者那里听说过旅行者是如何像战兽啃食骨头一样吞下了盖欧。 

“他还在它的肚子里，”战争议会上的一名军政官曾经这样告诉查厄托，而她将萨拉丁·弗吉用鼻子发出的哼哼声理解为了嗤笑。 

那是两天前的事了。她现在站在她飞船的舰桥上，琢磨着盖欧还剩下了什么。旅行者的光芒映在她的漆黑眼珠和装饰獠牙的珠宝上。她没有感受到在她的想象中盖欧对它的渴求，也没有感受到萨拉丁对它的崇敬。它不是一种该被征服或膜拜的东西，但它对那些对她很重要的人来说很重要——这才是重点。 

当她听到身后有脚步声时，她没有转身。她已经知道那是谁了。 

“我没有询问你的意见，”她说道，没有斥责的意思。“但如果你有话要讲，那就开口吧。” 

“难道我是位智慧导师？”萨拉丁问道。“我们就不能一起安静地等待终末吗？” 

“你的智慧是你的价值。那是我让你活着的唯一原因。” 

萨拉丁又发出了那种哼哼声。他知道那不是真的。 

而她也知道。

1139897377.name: First Ascent Vest
1139897377.subtitle: Oh, to read a pulpy golden age detective novel… just once more.
1139897377.subtitle_zh: 简陋通俗的黄金时代侦探小说…能再读一次就好了。
1139897377.text:
Light forgets, Darkness remembers. 

Ikora studied the strange approximation of the Tower, dust kicked up around her as the wind gusted through creaking halls. She felt the pull to explore… to find her old office. To see just how deep the recreation would go. 

But as she took a step up the stairs, her foot caught something—a small but familiar rectangular shape. She picked up the book and gently brushed dust from the cover. It was a copy of "The Spine-Tingling Adventures of Sedona Kane, P.I." The pulpy cover art told her it was the fourth installment of the series, with the subtitle "The Curious Case of Doctor Pennyworth." 

Light forgets, Darkness remembers. 

Darkness. In a place of such potent Light, would it be enough to manifest… everything? She flipped through the book; even the coffee stain still adorned page 95. 

Flashes of memory came back to Ikora as she studied the bold colors and heavy lines of the book's tattered jacket. She recalled kicking her feet up against the wall in her bunk one night after a particularly nasty Crucible loss… Ophiuchus's glow providing just enough visibility. Remembered cleaning the spilled drink off the pages in the mess hall and praying there was no lasting damage. And thought of other moments, of a warm hand covering her own as she read the text out loud for the thousandth time… 

The Warlock held the book to her nose. Just to take in the scent once more.  

Light forgets, Darkness remembers, and so would she.
1139897377.text_zh:
光能遗忘，暗影铭记。 

艾可拉审视着这座近似高塔的奇特建筑。她周围的尘土随着破败大堂中的狂风扬起。她感受到了探索的渴望…她想找到她以前的办公室。看看这个复制品到底有多像。 

但刚踏上楼梯，她的脚就碰到了一件物品——它的形状小而熟悉。她拿起那本书，轻轻拂去封面上的灰尘。这是一本《私家侦探塞多纳·凯恩的惊奇历险记》。从它俗气的封面上可以看出，这是该系列的第四部，副标题是“潘尼沃斯医生奇案”。 

光能遗忘，暗影铭记。 

暗影。在光能如此充足的地方，它是否能够显现…一切？她翻了翻书；甚至第95页上的咖啡渍都还在。 

当艾可拉打量着破旧书皮上大胆的色彩和厚重的线条时，她的记忆片段又闪现在了眼前。她回想起在熔炉竞技场中大败后，有一天夜里躺床上用脚蹬着墙…蛇夫座的光刚好够亮…在食堂里清理洒在书本上的饮料，祈祷没留下永久印记。她还想起，当她反复大声阅读时，一只温暖的手覆在自己的手上… 

这位术士把书抵到自己的鼻头，再一次感受它的气味。  

光能遗忘，暗影铭记，而她也会如此。

1922402428.name: First Ascent Cloak
1922402428.subtitle: There is nothing as exquisite as the feeling of doing what no one has done.
1922402428.subtitle_zh: 做别人没做过的事，感觉最美妙了。
1922402428.text:
Light forgets, Darkness remembers. 

Mara Sov grit her teeth as she held the H.E.L.M. steady, straining all the while to keep the portal open with her power just long enough for the Guardian, Ikora, and Commander Zavala to slip through. 

Mara shifted her focus to watch the live feed in the viewscreen beside her as the Guardian took their first steps into the Pale Heart. 

And instantly… she remembered what it felt like to be first. 

She remembered unending emptiness, the spark of protons, cold rock against her back, and the sensation of spilling upwards eternally. She remembered glacial till veined with platinum, a forest that spread as mycelium, and alpine saddles cradling crystal clear lakes. She remembered a world so young and old, where all life was equal, meaningless and meaningful. She remembered making that memory, that place, calling it awake from the cauldron of her own imagination and raising it into matter, her lips curled on its name. The Distributary. 

Mara would never see that world again, and yet, on the grainy video stuttering before her, was its doppelganger. It was not home, but it was close. 

The video feed sputtered out. 

A roar of violet streaked past the H.E.L.M., and with a sudden silence, the ship burst from the portal into open space. The portal did not snap shut behind them—the Witness must have let go. 

Mara caught her breath. Her hands shook. There was no sign of Crow in there, or on comms, no sign he was alive other than the tug on her own heart. She glanced back to the Traveler and the Pale Heart within.  

Mara Sov thought once more of home.
1922402428.text_zh:
光能遗忘，暗影铭记。 

玛拉·索维咬紧牙关，拼尽全力让应急后勤行动中心保持稳定，同时用她的力量保持传送门开启，让守护者、艾可拉、指挥官萨瓦拉有机会顺利通过。 

玛拉把注意力转移到身旁的屏幕上，通过直播画面看到守护者在苍白之心中迈出了第一步。 

忽然…她记起了身为先行者的感受。 

她记起了无尽的空虚，质子的火花，抵着后背的冰冷岩石，永远向上的延伸感。她记起了被铂金缠绕的冰川，像菌丝一样蔓延的森林，还有被高山环抱的清澈湖泊。她记起了一个如此年轻而古老的世界。在那里，所有的生命都平等，没有意义，也充满意义。她记起自己创造那段记忆，那个地方，把它从自己想象的大锅里唤醒，将它升华为物质，嘴角微微翘起说出它的名字：两仪界。 

玛拉再也见不到那个世界了。然而，在她面前不断卡顿的模糊视频中，她看见了那个世界的复制品。那不是家，但已经很接近了。 

视频信号中断了。 

一道紫色的光芒席卷了应急后勤行动中心，飞船里忽然安静下来。他们通过传送门冲进了无垠的太空，身后的传送门并没有关闭——见证者肯定是松手了。 

玛拉喘过气来。她的手在颤抖。里面没有乌鸦的踪迹，也没有来自他的通讯。除了心中的牵挂，没有任何迹象表明他还活着。她回头瞥了一眼旅行者和其中的苍白之心。  

玛拉·索维再次想起了家园。

3238797830.name: First Ascent Casque
3238797830.subtitle: Choose what you will become next.
3238797830.subtitle_zh: 选择你接下来要成为什么样的人。
3238797830.text:
Light forgets, Darkness remembers. 

Once, a Ghost was heard to speak thusly. 

This one is Luzaku. Here, this one tells what is known of Sky. 

Sky is the breath taken between actions. It permits speculation. It invites doubt. It slips from sight and grasp, and yet persists. 

This one's Ghost would have us yield to certainty. He wishes us to walk the Bladed Path, to seek Hive-strength in the Witch Queen's abandoned logic, whereby all things prove themselves in slaughter. 

This one turns from simple inevitability. This one makes a choice: this one does not kill and does not die. Yet this one exists. Aiat. What follows? What other choices are to be made? 

This one must know. 

This one hides within a blade-ship of the Witch Queen's great foe. This one's Ghost is angry now, but he remains. In the hollows where a worm once coiled, this one senses our swift motion through the firmament, toward a center. 

This one seeks Sky. In the Sky, there are many paths. 

In the Sky, there is change.
3238797830.text_zh:
光能遗忘，暗影铭记。 

很久以前，一个机灵说过这些话。 

鄙人是鲁扎库，在此讲述鄙人对苍穹的了解。 

苍穹是行动之间的喘息。它允许猜测。它引人怀疑。它难以追踪和把握，却始终留存。 

鄙人的机灵希望我们屈服于确定性。他希望我们走上刀锋之道，寻求邪魔族的力量，遵从巫妖女王遭抛弃的逻辑，即万物需在屠杀中证明自身。 

鄙人放弃了简单的必然性。鄙人做出了选择：鄙人不杀，也不死亡。然而，鄙人仍然存在。阿特。接下来呢？还要做出什么选择？ 

鄙人必须知晓。 

鄙人躲在巫妖女王宿敌的刀锋飞船里。鄙人的机灵很生气，但他没有离去。在蠕虫曾经盘踞的深渊里，鄙人感知到我们正迅速穿过苍穹，前往中心。 

鄙人探寻苍穹。苍穹内有许多道路。 

苍穹内有变化。

4061292537.name: First Ascent Strides
4061292537.subtitle: To enter the body of a deity would be to unquestionably defile it.
4061292537.subtitle_zh: 进入神灵的身体无疑是一种玷污。
4061292537.text:
Light forgets, Darkness remembers. 

Mithrax stood at the bow of the H.E.L.M., watching as Zavala's ship vanished from view into the portal. That awful gateway pulsed and wavered, and though the H.E.L.M. was pointed straight at it, he was resolved in his decision. 

The notion of venturing inside the Great Machine was innately revolting. It reeked like a taboo as certain as cannibalism, as unthinkable as besmirching a house of worship; to enter the body of a deity would unquestionably be to defile it. He could find a way to support from afar. Surely that was plausible.  

"Father, the Queen is asking for you." 

Eido sidles up next to him, and the two look out over the Great Machine. It takes up the entirety of the window—the center of all Light punctured by the oscillating violet of the portal, and Mithrax realizes how small he feels alongside his daughter. 

"I'm not going down there without you," she says. 

Mithrax holds back his shiver and confesses, "To step inside feels like a transgression." 

"And who made that rule?" she says. Ever acute, ever wise. When Mithrax cannot answer, she continues, "The Traveler is in peril. So long as we can care, we are bound to enter and defend it. I have seen you still have fight in you, Father." 

"Would that not be worse? To wage war at the very center of Light?" 

"Only you can decide that. But I believe the Traveler would want you to enter the portal." 

"Why?" 

His daughter puts a loving hand on his own. "Because it knows you aren't there to hurt it."
4061292537.text_zh:
光能遗忘，暗影铭记。 

米瑟拉克斯站在应急后勤行动中心的船首，注视着萨瓦拉的飞船从视野中消失，进入传送门。那道可怕的大门在脉动和摇摆，尽管应急后勤行动中心正对着它，但他已经下定了决心。 

进入大机器内部的想法令他反感。像同类相食一般让人厌恶，像糟蹋圣堂一般难以想象；进入神灵的身体无疑是一种玷污。他可以想办法从远处进行支援。他认为那是在理的。  

“父亲，女王在找你。” 

艾多走到他的身边。两人眺望着大机器。它填满了整个窗户——这位光能之神的中心，被传送门的震荡之紫刺穿了，米瑟拉克斯意识到自己和女儿在其身边是多么渺小。 

“没有你，我不会进去，”她说。 

米瑟拉克斯强忍着冷颤承认道，“进去像是一种亵渎。” 

“那种规则是谁定的？”她反问道。一如既往地机敏、睿智。米瑟拉克斯不知如何回答，而她还在继续，“旅行者正处于危险之中。只要我们还关爱它，我们就必须进去保护它。我知道你还有斗志，父亲。” 

“那样不是更糟糕吗？在光能的中心作战？” 

“那取决于你。但我相信旅行者会希望你进入传送门。” 

”为什么？“ 

他的女儿把一只充满爱意的手放在他的手背上。“因为它知道你不是去伤害它的。”

1250597597.name: Sublime Cloak
1250597597.subtitle: We celebrate the future we will build together.
1250597597.subtitle_zh: 赞颂我们将会共同构建的未来。
1250597597.text:
The City has changed—at least for Crow. The memory of a mask still weighs against his face, but he walks tall now, and finds he's welcome at a Solstice bonfire whenever he sidles up to one. 

He knows it's the sort of festival not just for remembrance, but also for celebration of those you stand hand-in-hand with, of the future that may yet be built together. Today, Crow has friendship on his mind. 

Like the logs he watches crackle in the fire, so many of his connections are half-burnt for one reason or another. Cayde, more than others, lingers in his thoughts. Not only for his brief sojourn through Crow's new life, for the lost potential friendship that might have existed in another time and place, but also simply for the sort of person he was. In the moment, Crow wonders what Cayde would have to say about this navel-gazing. 

Keep moving forward, probably. So, what next? 

"I don't know how to meet people," Crow says aloud to Glint. "It sounds so stupid. I just think I… I forgot how when it comes to people who aren't Guardians." 

Glint buzzes gently, his iris bright against the dark evening sky like a floating spark. "We could take a class," he says, with all due thoughtfulness. "Not about meeting people, though. Maybe pottery?" 

Crow laughs, feeling that spark in his heart. Lighter than the burdens that weigh on him. He thinks how fortunate he is to build a future together. With Glint; with the Vanguard; with people he hasn't even met yet. "All right," he says. "Something new. And—" A hesitation, teetering on a precipice. "Maybe I'll wander down to the Tower Hangar. See if anyone there knows some tricks I don't." 

No standing still. Only moving forward.  

Cayde would approve.
1250597597.text_zh:
圣城已经变了——至少对乌鸦来说是这样。他的脸仍然忘不掉戴着面具的记忆，但现在他昂首阔步，发现每当自己溜达到至日篝火旁时，都会受到欢迎。 

他知道，这样的节日不仅是为了纪念，也是为了庆祝那些与你并肩作战的人，以及共同构建的未来。今天，乌鸦的心里满怀情谊。 

就像他看到的在火中噼啪作响的木头一样，他的许多人际关系都因为种种原因而几近消逝。和其他人相比，凯德更让他无法忘怀。不仅是因为他曾短暂地走进乌鸦的新生活，因为那段可能已经消逝的、本可能存在于另一个时空的友谊，更因为他的为人。在这一刻，乌鸦不禁想，凯德会如何看待自己这种过度自省的行为。 

他大概会说“继续前进”吧。那接下来要怎么办？ 

“我不知道怎么与人交往，”乌鸦大声对格林特说道。“听起来好蠢。我就是觉得…如果对方不是守护者，我都忘了该怎么打交道了。” 

格林特轻轻地发出嗡鸣，他的虹膜在漆黑的夜空中就像一缕漂浮的火花，显得格外明亮。“我们可以上一堂课，”他郑重其事地说。“但不是关于怎么与人交往。也许可以学下陶艺？” 

乌鸦笑了，体会着心中的那丝火花，这比压在他身上的重担要轻盈得多。他想，自己真是幸运，能和格林特，和先锋，和那些他尚未谋面的人一起创造未来。“好吧，”他说道。“学点新东西。然后——”他犹豫了片刻，仿佛立于悬崖边上摇摆不定。“也许我会去高塔机库转悠。看看那里有没有谁知道一些我不会的花招。” 

不能停滞不前。唯有不断前进。  

凯德肯定会赞同的。

2920433728.name: Veteran Legend Grasps
2920433728.subtitle: "I'll tell my children I was there. Before the battle had a name. Before it became a symbol of victory for the Titan orders."
2920433728.subtitle_zh: “我会告诉我的孩子们，在那场战斗还没有名字之前，在它成为泰坦胜利的象征之前，我就在那里了。”
2920433728.text:
My grandfather came to the City when it was just tents and huts. He traveled the Pilgrim Road on foot, all the way across the Panama Ravine with his entire family and was the only survivor by the end. He never talked about the journey much, not until his last years. Honestly, it helped give me perspective. I never knew the City as he did. I've only ever known the walls as a project, and watching those last stones be put into place made it feel like we were invincible.

Now, I write this journal entry from a bunker hundreds of feet below the streets. There is a battle raging outside the City walls, but I can feel it reverberating through the stone. Every time the lights flicker, I wonder, "Is this it?" The feeds say the aliens are attacking from six directions at once. I don't know if the walls will hold, if the Risen protecting us will stand. I don't know if I will see tomorrow. I just know the Traveler is here, and we are safe in its shadow.

They promised that this was the Last Safe City. We've all sacrificed too much to give up on that dream. We must survive.
2920433728.text_zh:
我祖父来到圣城时，这里还只有帐篷和棚屋。他带着全家徒步走过朝圣者之路，穿过巴拿马峡谷，是最后唯一的幸存者。直到晚年，他都没怎么提起过这段旅程。说实话，这给了我很多启发。我从未像他那样了解圣城。我只知道城墙是一项工程，而看着那最后的几块石头砌放到位，让我们感到自己坚不可摧。

此刻，我正在街道下方数百英尺的地堡里写下这篇日志。圣城高墙外战火纷飞，但我能感觉到战争在石缝中回响。每当灯光闪烁，我都在想，“那一刻要来了吗？”消息称外星人同时从六个方向发动了进攻，我不知道城墙能否撑得住，也不知道保护我们的复生者能否屹立不倒。我不知道我能否活着看到明天。我只知道旅行者在这里，我们在它的荫蔽之下很安全。

他们承诺这里是“最后的安全城市”。我们都牺牲了太多，不能放弃这个梦想。我们必须活下去。

3465152776.name: Veteran Legend vest
3465152776.subtitle: "I might not be a Guardian, but they've reminded us you don't need the Light to be a hero."
3465152776.subtitle_zh: “我也许不是守护者，但他们提醒我们，成为英雄不一定需要光能。”
3465152776.text:
My mother passed away last week. She left me the journals she'd been keeping since the days the walls were being built. She left her father's father's journals from before the City even had walls. They lived long, full lives. Reading about them makes me wish I had seen the City of their times. I was a boy when the Guardians won the battle of Twilight Gap. I've only ever known peace behind the walls, only watched the City grow and thrive. I barely know how to handle a rifle. I work textiles. I make clothes. I want to open a shop to tailor clothing for the Guardians. I don't want to die.

I've been hiding with the resistance for three weeks now, since they found me sleeping in a storm drain. I lost everything in the Cabal attack. All my family's writings. My sister. My son. The Guardians—even without their Light—are defending us. They're showing me how to shoot, how to survive. Every day someone leaves our hideout and never returns. Mas'ouda, Arzu, Brajko, Mitra, Kardelen, and Luca died this week. The Cabal are relentless, and sooner or later they're going to figure out where we're hiding. 

There's fifteen of us left, five combat frames, and two Guardians.

I have to survive. Humanity has to survive. It can't end like this.
3465152776.text_zh:
我母亲上周去世了。她把从建造城墙时就开始写的日记留给了我。她还留下了她父亲的父亲的日记，那时的圣城甚至还没有城墙。他们度过了漫长而充实的一生。读着他们的日记，我真希望能亲眼看到他们那个时代的圣城。守护者赢得暮光峡谷战役时，我还是个孩子。我只知道高墙之后的和平，只看到了圣城的成长和繁荣。我几乎不会用步枪。我从事纺织工作。我制作衣物。我想开家为守护者们定制服装的店。我不想死。

从我睡在暴雨排水沟里被反抗军发现后算起，我已经跟他们一起躲了三个星期。在卡巴尔的袭击中，我失去了一切。所有我家人的日志。我的妹妹。我的儿子。守护者们——即使没有了他们的光能——仍在保护着我们。他们教我如何射击，如何生存。每天都有人离开我们的藏身处，再没回来。马斯乌达、阿尔祖、布拉伊科、米特拉、卡德伦，还有卢卡，都死在了这周。卡巴尔步步紧逼，他们迟早会发现我们躲藏的地方。 

我们还剩下十五个人，五个战斗框架和两名守护者。

我必须生存下去。人类必须生存下去。不能就这样结束。

872282981.name: Veteran Legend Cloak
872282981.subtitle: "All endings are beginnings."
872282981.text:
Tonight, I watched a thousand lanterns fill the night sky. Tonight, I watched the hopes and dreams of humanity burn bright in the dark and challenge the uncertainty of the future. Tonight, I gave birth to a child that will shoulder the same burden of humanity's uncertain future that I have. Tonight a new person came into this world who will share in my family's stories, hear of their ancestors and their triumphs, their failures, and their legends. Tonight, humanity takes a step into a future so unknown we do not even have a word for it. Tonight is a moment that must live forever, no detail forgotten.

Tonight, the war is over. Tonight, a new age dawns. Tonight, I am so very tired. From my bedroom I hear congratulations and cheers. I hear excitement. Everyone I have spoken to is dreaming about the future now, rather than merely surviving the next day. Some of my friends want to venture into the stars, leave the safety of the City and explore. They want to reclaim everything we've lost; all these worlds. But I won't be joining them. My place is here in the City, where my family has lived and died for generations. My friends ask, "Why would you want to stay in the Last City?" But I don't think it's going to stay the Last City.

I think this is the First City of many to come.
872282981.text_zh:
今夜，我看着万盏灯笼挂满夜空。今夜，我看着人类的希望和梦想在黑暗中熠熠生辉，挑战着未来的不确定性。今夜，我生下了一个孩子，他将和我一样肩负起人类不确定未来的重担。今夜，一个新成员来到这个世界，与我共享家族的故事，聆听祖先的事迹，以及他们的胜利、失败和传奇。今夜，人类踏出了迈向未来的一步，我们甚至找不到一个词来形容它的未知性。今夜是一个永恒的时刻，任何细节都不会被遗忘。

今夜，战争迎来终结。今夜，新的时代来临。今夜，我已疲惫不堪。我从卧室里听到了祝贺与欢呼，听到了兴奋与激昂。与我交谈过的每个人都在憧憬未来，而不仅仅是想着怎么熬过明天。我的一些朋友想去星际冒险，离开圣城的庇护向外探索。他们想重新夺回我们失去的一切；所有这些世界。但我不会与他们同行。我的归宿是圣城，这是我的家族世世代代生活和死去的地方。我的朋友们问我，“你为什么想留在最后的圣城里？”而我觉得，它将不再是最后的圣城。

我想对未来的众多城市来说，它会是第一座圣城。

1216938185.name: Veteran Legend Casque
1216938185.subtitle: "There's a last, safe city out there somewhere. We have to believe."
1216938185.subtitle_zh: “一定还有最后的安全之城。我们必须相信。”
1216938185.text:
"The Last Safe City" exists in name only. I came here expecting to find a lost metropolis from before the Collapse. Instead, it's a sea of tents and prefabricated shelters huddled around bonfires. Everyone here thinks that hiding in the shadow of the Traveler will keep them safe. Keep humanity's killers at arm's length. All I see are hundreds of miles of rough, snow-capped mountains. All I can feel is the memory of frostbite in my fingers. That's not going to stop anyone, just slow them down.

I came here in a caravan of settlers. The march up the mountains was worse than any battle I'd survived. Hundreds died along the way from injuries, starvation, exposure. All the greatest hits. We buried them along the roadside, with no time for markers or ceremony. I've heard some of the Risen here talking about forming guard patrols to escort people. I don't know. Sooner or later our enemies are going to follow the trail of ants back to the mound. We'd never survive a full-frontal assault.

More Risen arrive every day. They're starting to organize, make plans. They make me nervous. I can't shake the memories. Groups of them hitting settlements for ammunition and food, mass executions for those who dared speak out against them, entire towns turned to craters. These ones seem different from the Warlords, but I can't just let it go. The other settlers here are just like the ones outside the "City," consumed with their own ideas about how the world should run. I've heard plenty of people talking about organizing an exodus, just getting in whatever ships we have and abandoning Earth. As if anywhere else in this system is safe. Others want to form clear lines of succession and leadership. Then there's the people like me—trusting their guns—waiting for the other shoe to drop. We know war is a certainty.

Something is going to kill us all. It's just a matter of when, not if. There's nowhere safe. Not anywhere. Not anymore.
1216938185.text_zh:
“最后的安全城市”有名无实。我来到这里，本以为会发现一座大崩溃前的失落大都市。但这里却是一片围着篝火的帐篷和预制房屋的海洋。这里的每个人都以为躲在旅行者的荫蔽之下，就能保证自己的安全，就能与残害人类的杀手保持距离。可我看到的只有数百英里的崎岖雪山，我能感受到的只有手指上冻疮的记忆。那阻止不了任何人，只会拖慢他们的脚步。

我是随着一队定居者来到这里的。上山的行进比我经历过的任何一场战役都要艰难。沿途数百人死于伤痛、饥饿、受冻。最糟糕的情况都发生了。我们把他们埋在路边，没时间立碑或是举行葬礼。我听说这里的一些复生者在谈论组建护卫巡逻队来护送人们。我不知道这是否明智。我们的敌人迟早会沿着痕迹追踪到我们的巢穴。到时候，我们绝对撑不过他们的全面进攻。

每天都有更多的复生者抵达。他们开始组织起来，制定计划。他们让我感到紧张。我无法摆脱那些记忆。他们那样的人曾抱团去定居点抢夺弹药和食物，大规模处决敢于出声反对他们的人，把各个城镇变成弹坑。这些人看起来与战争领主不同，但我的内心无法平静。这里的其他定居者跟“圣城”外面的那些人并无二致，认为世界就该像自己想的那样运作。我听到很多人都在谈论组织一次大逃亡，随便坐上什么飞船，抛弃地球。就好像这个星系里的其他地方都是安全的一样。另外一些人想制定明确的继任和领导体系。还有像我这样的人——相信自己的枪杆子——提心吊胆地等待着坏事发生。我们知道战争无可避免。

有东西会将我们所有人置于死地。这一定会发生，只不过是时间问题。没有地方是安全的。哪儿都不安全。也再也不会有安全的地方了。

1615373434.name: Veteran Legend Strides
1615373434.subtitle: "The Traveler didn't run, it rose up to meet the enemy."
1615373434.subtitle_zh: “旅行者没有逃跑，而是起身迎敌。”
1615373434.text:
The Traveler is gone.

I watched it as it left the City. The sky lit up like the world was ending. It's still up there, though. When the sun is at the right angle you can see it like a second moon. I remember, as a teenager, sitting on the roof of my apartment building, watching the pieces of the Traveler reform. I could feel the Light in the way they say Guardians and Ghosts can. I felt so confident that day, so sure that we were all going to be saved. Many are doubting, but when I look up into the sky and see that the Traveler is still there—defending not just the City, but all of Earth—my faith is as strong as ever.

In the days since the Traveler left, Coalition ships have filled the City's skies. I remember my uncle talking about the last time he saw Cabal ships in the sky—it was the day my mother died. It feels like we've been through so much in such a short time. My uncle would tell me our family's stories every night. We'd lost all the written copies after the invasion, but now they exist in me, and I will record what I remember. So we know where we came from and what was lost.

Everyone is saying this is the end. But I know enough history to be sure that it's not the first time we've felt this way. Every threat the City faces feels like it'll be the last. My uncle died during the Endless Night, saving Eliksni that once tried to lay siege to our home. Nothing lasts forever and everything changes. Buildings burn, people die, but we move on. 

I don't think this is the end. I think this is a new beginning.
1615373434.text_zh:
旅行者走了。

我看着它离开圣城。天空就像世界末日一样亮了起来。但它还在天上。太阳角度恰到好处时，你就可以看到它，像是第二个月亮一样。我还记得，十几岁的时候，我坐在公寓楼的屋顶上，看着旅行者的碎片重组。我能感受到光能，就像人们说的守护者和机灵能做到的那样。那天我很有信心，确信我们都会得救。尽管很多人表示怀疑，但是当我仰望天空，看到旅行者还在那里，不仅保护着圣城，还保护着整个地球时，我的信念一如既往地坚定。

旅行者离开后的日子里，联盟的飞船布满了圣城的天空。我记得舅舅说过他最后一次在天空中看到卡巴尔飞船是在我母亲去世的那天。感觉我们在这么短的时间内经历了太多。我舅舅每天晚上都会跟我讲我们家族的故事。入侵之后，我们失去了所有的书面文本，但现在它们存在于我的心中，我会记录下我所记得的一切。这样我们就知道我们从哪里来，失去了什么。

每个人都在说末日已到。但我对历史的了解足以让我确信，这不是我们第一次有这种感觉。圣城面临的每一次威胁都像是最后一次。我舅舅在永夜时牺牲了，为的是拯救曾经试图围攻我们家园的埃里克斯尼族。没有什么是永恒的，一切都会改变。建筑烧毁，人们死去，但我们会继续前进。 

我不认为这是末日。我相信这是一个新的开始。

810612804.name: Untethered Edge Gauntlets
810612804.subtitle: Tighten your grip.
810612804.text:
The metallic limbs of the Vex Goblin flailed wildly in the air as Saint-14 held it high above his head. The Titan dropped abruptly to one knee, bringing down the writhing Vex and cracking the radiolarian chamber at its center against his massive thigh.  

The red light in the Vex's eye flickered out as the cooling radiolaria trickled down Saint's boot. He stood, satisfied, and cast the dead frame aside. 

"Do you see?" he asked brightly. "I use the very weight of the creature against it!" 

"Whoa," came Failsafe's voice over the comms, low and impressed. Saint's visual feed held her full attention. She adjusted her filter, and her tone became cheery. "Please show me again!" 

"You cannot get this close to them all the time, but it is wise to save ammunition when you can," Saint said. He dusted off his hands and chuckled. "And it feels good to crush a Vex! It is very therapeutic!" 

"Ah, I believe I understand!" chirped Failsafe. "Is there a power transfer during this thanatotic expression that explains how you are able to maintain such high uptime on your socialization filters?" 

Saint slid his helmet off and the comms transferred seamlessly to his built-in Exo earpiece. "What is it you mean?"  

"I will rephrase," Failsafe replied. "What percentage of your processes are dedicated to positive outlook preservation?" 

Saint squinted at the stone outcroppings of Nessus and turned his helmet over in his hands. "Failsafe," he began kindly, but she interrupted. 

"Ugh, okay," she started, her tone somehow portraying an eyeroll. "I mean, you're in a good mood, like, all the time, so obviously you overclocked your joviality banks or something, yeah?" 

Saint broke into a wide smile. "Exos are not like AI. I am just who I am, Failsafe. It does not take anything extra to be me." 

"Oh!" Failsafe exclaimed after a moment. "How lovely that must be for you!" Her sunny voice did little to hide her envy. 

"Now for you, I understand it is different," Saint said, patting his helmet as if to soothe it. "But I think that maybe you should not have to spend extra power to talk to your friends." 

A heavy silence fell over the comms.  

Failsafe's voice was soft and reserved. "Saint-unit?" she said quietly. 

"Yes?" 

"Did you once headbutt a Kell?" 

Saint burst into laughter. "I have headbutted many things!" 

"I'm checking on your files, and uh, yeah, you really have," Failsafe said. She scrolled through a vast sea of Saint's accomplishments, all complete with uploads of his visual feed… except one.  

"Weird… Saint-unit, there's an unconfirmed VanNet report here about an unsanctioned solo operation in Savathûn's throne world sometime last year. According to this—"  

"Who made this report?" Saint asked. 

Failsafe accessed a VanNet profile and was met with a stream of account flags. "A heavily restricted user account, _MRU_, who claims firsthand knowledge of the event." 

"Pfah," Saint said dismissively. "You cannot believe every report in the system." He slid his helmet back on and walked purposefully toward a shimmering radiolarian stream where Vex were beginning to emerge. 

Failsafe recognized the subtle inflections in Saint's tone: the conversation had become suddenly troubling to him. 

Probably not enough juice in his cordiality partition, Failsafe thought, and dropped the subject.
810612804.text_zh:
圣人14号把Vex哥布林高举过头顶，它的金属四肢在空中疯狂地挥舞着。这名泰坦突然单膝跪地，把扭动的Vex猛地拉下，让其中央的活性放射体液腔室砸在他粗壮的大腿上。  

随着冷却的活性放射体液顺着圣人的靴子滴落下来，Vex眼中的红光一闪即逝。他满意地站了起来，把死去的框架扔到一边。 

“看到了吗？”他高兴地问道。“我用这生物的重量干掉了它！” 

“哇哦，”从通讯器里传来智能失效保险的声音，低沉而饶有兴致。圣人的视觉信号吸引了她的全部注意力。她调整了一下筛选器，语气变得愉快起来。“请再让我看一次！” 

“虽说并不总能和它们拉近到这个距离，但尽量节省弹药总归是明智的，”圣人说道。他掸掉手上的灰尘，轻声笑了起来。“而且碾碎Vex的感觉超好！很解压！” 

“啊，我想我明白了！”智能失效保险叫道。“这种死亡本能的表达过程中，是不是有某种能量转移，帮助你的社交筛选器保持长时间的激昂？” 

圣人把他的头盔摘下来，通信无缝地转移到了他内置的Exo耳机上。“你是什么意思？”  

“我换个说法，”智能失效保险回答。“你的进程中有多少是用来维持积极态度的？” 

圣人眯起眼睛看着涅索斯的露岩，把他的头盔在手里翻过来。“智能失效保险，”他温和地开口道，但她打断了他。 

“呃，好吧，”她开始说，语气里有种翻白眼的感觉。“我的意思是，你的心情一直都很好，所以很明显你超频了愉悦内存，对吧？” 

圣人突然绽出灿烂的笑容。“Exo不像人工智能。我就是我，智能失效保险。我不需要额外的东西。” 

“哦！”过了一会儿，智能失效保险叫道。“那对你来说肯定很棒！”她阳光的声音丝毫没有掩饰她的嫉妒。 

“我明白对你来说不太一样，”圣人说着，拍了拍他的头盔，好像要安抚它似的。“但我想也许你不必消耗额外的力量来跟你的朋友聊天。” 

通讯陷入了长时间的沉默。  

智能失效保险的声音轻柔而内敛。“圣人单位？”她平静地说。 

“什么？” 

“你曾经用头撞过凯尔吗？” 

圣人大笑起来。“我用头撞过很多东西！” 

“我正在查看你的文件，嗯，没错，你确实是，”智能失效保险说。她浏览了圣人的大量成就，都是通过他的视讯上传的…只有一个例外。  

“真奇怪…圣人单位，这里有一份未经证实的VanNet报告，是有关去年某个时候在萨瓦图恩的王座世界中的一次未经批准的单人行动。根据这份——”  

“这份报告是谁写的？”圣人问道。 

智能失效保险访问了一个VanNet配置文件，遇到了一连串的账户警告。“某个遭到严格限制的用户账号，_MRU_，声称掌握了事件的第一手资料。” 

“呸，”圣人轻蔑地说道。“你不能把系统里的每一份报告都当真。”他重新戴上头盔，坚定地朝着微微发亮的活性放射体液流走去，其中开始有Vex显现。 

智能失效保险听出了圣人语气中的微妙变化：这次谈话突然让他感到不安。 

可能是他的“友好”分区里电力不足，智能失效保险心想，搁置了这个话题。

2134769653.name: Untethered Edge Helm
2134769653.subtitle: Head to head.
2134769653.text:
Empress Caiatl looked out from the viewport of the H.E.L.M., watching the shimmer of the Traveler. It signaled change. It signaled danger. She shifted her weight from foot to foot, unsure of what might come. 

"Well," Failsafe chimed, off-key. "Look who finally decided to drop by." 

Empress Caiatl turned and stepped up to the terminal, surveying the apparatus that allowed the AI to interface with the command center. 

"The AI," Caiatl mused aloud. "From the Exodus Black. Failsafe. This is how you are communicating with the Vanguard." 

"Correct!" Failsafe chirped. "Welcome, Empress. What a delightful surprise!" 

Caiatl looked up in confusion at the greeting. Failsafe flashed and emitted a series of low beeps before she spoke again. 

"You're not going to land another tank on me here, are you? Or was one enough?" 

Caiatl lowered her tusks at the AI's sarcasm but did not respond. 

"Pretty sure you're not here to apologize, either." 

"No," the Empress answered without hesitation. "I will make no apologies. My presence on Nessus was a necessary step towards my eventual alliance with the Vanguard. It forced them to react." 

"Uh-huh," Failsafe said, unimpressed. 

"It was strategic," the Empress urged. Her tone was firm, but conciliatory. Failsafe's response was bright. 

"It was very rude!" 

Caiatl rumbled in thought. Failsafe imitated the noise in a crackle of modulator static. The Empress ignored this. 

"Yes," she said. "I will admit… it was rude." 

Failsafe was silent. Caiatl cleared her throat before she continued, her eyes wandering to the research specimens that littered the room. 

"Scans had detected a large wreck in the vicinity of the landing zone. Your presence was noted, but— " 

"Ignored?" 

"Yes," she said, looking back at the AI console. "Ignored. We did not view you as a threat."
