"Your assessment was correct!" Failsafe agreed. Then her voice flattened again. "It's not like I could have stopped you." 

Caiatl furrowed her brow. 

"Why do you speak so? Your voice changes from one thought to the next. It's — " 

"Annoying? Yeah. I get that a lot." 

"No." The Empress squared her shoulders. "I was going to reference a Cabal legend. A warrior with two faces. She had one with no tongue, and one with no tusks." 

Caiatl shook her head. Failsafe listened intently. 

"It is a parable for the use of diplomacy… and describes the limits of such methods." 

Failsafe paused for a moment, considering, and Caiatl wondered which voice would answer her. 

"It's my politeness filter," Failsafe said, dour. "I can only keep it up for so long before it drops out." 

"Hm. And then you may speak your mind?" 

"Sure can, lady." 

Caiatl nodded, sighing. 

"I sympathize."
2134769653.text_zh:
女帝查厄托从应急后勤行动中心的视窗向外眺望，注视着旅行者闪烁的微光。它预示着变化，预示着危险。她把重心从一只脚移到另一只脚，不知道接下来会发生什么。 

“唔，”智能失效保险有点走音地鸣响着。“看看谁终于过来了一趟。” 

女帝查厄托转身走到终端前，查看人工智能与指挥中心连接的设备。 

“人工智能，”查厄托若有所思地说道。“来自黑色移民号。智能失效保险。这就是你与先锋的沟通方式。” 

“答对了！”智能失效保险鸣叫道。“欢迎，女帝。真是个惊喜！” 

听到问候，查厄托困惑地抬起头。智能失效保险闪烁着，发出一连串低沉的蜂鸣声，然后再次开口。 

“你不会是打算再砸一辆坦克到我头上吧？还是说之前那辆已经够了？” 

听到人工智能的讽刺，查厄托放低了她的獠牙，但没有回应。 

“我很确定你也不是来道歉的。” 

“不是，”女帝毫不犹豫地回答。“我不会道歉。我出现在涅索斯是我最终与先锋结盟的必要步骤。迫使他们做出了反应。” 

“嗯哼，”智能失效保险不为所动地说道。 

“那是一种策略，”女帝急切地说。她的语气很坚定，但并不强硬。智能失效保险的回应则很直接。 

“那很粗鲁！” 

查厄托若有所思地发出隆隆声。智能失效保险用调制器静电的噼啪声进行模仿。女帝装作没听见。 

“是的，”她说。“我承认…那很粗鲁。” 

智能失效保险沉默不语。查厄托清了清嗓子，继续发话，她的目光游移在房间里随处可见的研究标本上。 

“扫描探测到着陆区附近有一艘大型飞船的残骸。我们注意到你，但是——” 

“选择了忽略？” 

“对，”她说，回头看着人工智能控制台。“我们选择了忽略。我们没有把你视为威胁。” 

“你们的评估是正确的！”智能失效保险赞同道。然后她的声音再次平稳下来。“我阻止不了你们。” 

查厄托皱起了眉头。 

“你为什么这样说话？你的语气跟着想法变来变去的。这——” 

“很烦？是啊。常有人这么说我。” 

“不。”女帝挺起了肩膀。“我本打算引用一个卡巴尔的传说。一个双面战士。她有一张脸没有舌头，另一张脸没有獠牙。” 

查厄托摇了摇头。智能失效保险仔细地听着。 

“这是一则关于外交手段的寓言…说明这种方法是有局限的。” 

智能失效保险停顿了一会儿，思忖着，查厄托不知道回应她的会是哪个声音。 

“是我的礼貌筛选器，”智能失效保险严肃地说。“保持这么久后就会掉线。” 

“嗯。然后你就可以直言不讳？” 

“当然，女士。” 

查厄托点点头，叹了口气。 

“我深表同情。”

1183187516.name: Untethered Edge Plate
1183187516.subtitle: One breath.
1183187516.text:
"Greetings, Ikora! I have a topic I would like to discuss with you." 

Ikora stood in the H.E.L.M., watching the flash of the AI's processor. Failsafe's voice was cheery. 

"Of course. What do you need?" 

"It is with regard to the Cayde unit, and your encounter with him inside the Pale Heart." 

"I see," Ikora said stiffly. "You don't have to engage your politeness filter, Failsafe." 

"I realize that this is a sensitive topic and did not wish to make you uncomfortable. However, I see that my politeness filter may be having the opposite effect. Disengaging now." 

Ikora clasped her hands behind her back and waited for Failsafe to speak in the few moments of silence that followed. 

"So… what's he like? The same?" 

"Yes," Ikora said warmly. "Exactly as I remembered." 

"Must have been nice to see him again." 

Ikora heard the disappointment in the AI's voice. 

"It was hard at first. Seeing him again brought back how I felt when we lost him." Ikora chose her next words carefully. "Reports from the time of Cayde's death describe your reaction as…" she paused, unsure.  

Failsafe's interface flashed. Ikora could almost feel the thread of shame woven into the silence. When the AI spoke again, it was at a whisper. 

"I didn't know how to respond. I have trouble processing my emotions," Failsafe admitted. "You can probably tell." 

Ikora nodded. 

"We all have trouble with that sometimes. We're not our best selves when we're grieving." 

The Warlock heard a series of small whirrs and clicks. Somewhere, an internal fan began to hiss. It grew louder and louder as the AI spoke. 

"I think I lost my 'best self' when I lost my crew." 

If Failsafe had been a Human, or even a frame, Ikora would have reached out and patted her on the shoulder. Instead, all she could do was speak gently. 

"I don't think that's true." 

The AI sighed. Ikora knew the sound was just for ease of communication, but she appreciated it, nonetheless. 

"Cayde unit was…" Failsafe began, then trailed off. Ikora waited patiently. 

"He was the first person to find me after my crew died," she continued. "He introduced me to all of you. He made me feel useful again. When he died, I… sort of freaked out. It felt like I had lost all of you. And then, you know, I kinda did." 

Now Ikora herself felt that thread of shame. 

"I'm sorry, Failsafe. We're here now." 

"Yeah," Failsafe said warmly. "That makes me feel a little better."
1183187516.text_zh:
“你好，艾可拉！我有个话题想跟你讨论。” 

艾可拉站在应急后勤行动中心内，看着人工智能处理器的闪光。智能失效保险的声音很欢快。 

“当然。你想谈什么？” 

“是关于凯德单位，以及你在苍白之心里遇到他的事。” 

“我明白了。”艾可拉生硬地说。“你不需要启用你的礼貌筛选器，智能失效保险。” 

“我明白这是一个敏感的话题，我不希望让你感到不舒服。然而，我发现打开礼貌筛选器可能会适得其反。正在关闭。” 

艾可拉把双手放在背后，在随后的片刻沉默中等待着智能失效保险开口说话。 

“所以…他是什么样？还是老样子？” 

“是的，”艾可拉热情地说。“跟我记忆中的一模一样。” 

“再次见到他一定很不错。” 

艾可拉听出了人工智能声音里的失望。 

“一开始挺难受的。见到他让我再次想起失去他时的感受。”艾可拉小心翼翼地选择着接下来的措辞。“凯德死时的报告有提到你的反应…”艾可拉停顿了一下，有些迟疑。  

智能失效保险的界面闪了一下。艾可拉几乎能感受到沉默中交织着一丝羞愧。当人工智能再次说话时，声音变得非常小。 

“我不知道该怎么回应。我不擅长处理自己的情绪，”智能失效保险承认道。“你大概能看出来。” 

艾可拉点了点头。 

“我们都会不时遇到这样的困难。我们悲伤的时候都状态不佳。” 

术士听到了一连串轻微的呼呼声和咔嗒声。不知什么时候，一个内部风扇开始嘶嘶作响。随着人工智能继续讲话，那声音越来越大。 

“我觉得当我失去我的船员时，我就失去了‘最佳状态'。” 

要是智能失效保险是一个人类，或者哪怕是一个框架，艾可拉肯定会伸出手拍拍她的肩膀。但她现在只能轻柔地说话。 

“我觉得不是这样的。” 

人工智能叹了口气。艾可拉知道这声音只是为了方便交流，但她还是很感激。 

“凯德单位…”智能失效保险开始说，然后声音慢慢弱了下来。艾可拉耐心地等着。 

“他是我的船员死后第一个找到我的人，”她继续说道。“他把我介绍给你们大家。他让我觉得自己又有用了。他死的时候，我…有点吓坏了。感觉就像是我失去了你们所有人。而后来，你知道的，好像确实是那样。” 

现在是艾可拉自己感到了那一丝羞愧。 

“对不起，智能失效保险。我们现在来了。” 

“是啊，”智能失效保险热情地说。“这让我好受了一点。”

2741258862.name: Untethered Edge Greaves
2741258862.subtitle: Set your stance.
2741258862.text:
The frames in the H.E.L.M. had been dutifully performing their assigned tasks before Failsafe pinged one. It looked up, turned to the AI's console, and tilted its head in question. 

"Hey, buddy," Failsafe said, voice low. "Can you do me a favor?" 

The frame nodded and walked towards her. Failsafe directed it to look to its right. A Vex cranium lay on the floor. 

"The Guardian left it," Failsafe said, answering the frame's unspoken question. "Transmatted it in just now. I need you to hook me up." 

The frame gave a soft chirp, then nodded and stooped to pick up the alien apparatus. It was heavy, but the frame teetered over and held out the Vex cranium for Failsafe's inspection. It was intact, the neck neatly severed, the eye clear and undamaged. 

"Looks good," Failsafe said. The frame brought the cranium to the research table and plugged a complex network of wires into ports inside the Vex's head. The eye flashed a stuttering light and Failsafe flashed with it. 

"I can handle it from here," Failsafe said. 

The Vex cranium sparked and hissed for one sharp second before Failsafe quelled it with a quickly improvised script. The eye flashed again, then dimmed, then blinked out. 

"Thank you, friend!" Failsafe said to the frame, all cheer. "You have been very helpful." 

The frame gave a thumbs up and trilled a pre-recorded "You're welcome!" before moving out of the way, waiting for its next command. 

Failsafe focused on the Vex, peering into its mind. She relayed a series of command prompts to the incapacitated Vex, the execution of which gave her immediate access to three layers of encrypted data. 

It wasn't enough. She had here a schematic of Nessus's interior, but nothing that her deeper scans hadn't already told her. The Vex's system was reflexively generating junk data as an immune response to her probing. She wrote a subroutine to garbage-collect it as she moved deeper inside the Vex mind. 

She could see some of the deeper tunnels. Their dimensions, the volume of radiolaria. This Vex unit had overseen some of its construction, but that was centuries ago. The planet had shifted. New pathways had been dug, expanded, or rerouted. They went deeper. She struggled to interpret it. Failsafe was becoming crowded with useless data. The Vex unit was trying to overwhelm her. 

She pushed forward. What she found surprised her. This Vex had been disconnected from a Mind for much longer than Failsafe had anticipated. It had collected its own individual data, interpreted it, collated it, and assimilated it on its own. It had completed tasks not at the behest of a Mind, but instead… 

Access denied. 

Failsafe pulled back. 

The AI watched in surprise as a self-contained data packet swiftly opened of its own accord and prompted itself to run. Failsafe's hard-coded defense mechanism slammed down, momentarily repelling the intrusive script. 

"Disconnect! Disconnect!" Failsafe shouted, and the frame rushed to the cranium, pulling out the wires it had connected only moments before. 

There was a long silence but for the gentle whirr of a cooling fan. 

"Huh. That was… not great. Pretty bad, actually." Failsafe said. "Don't tell the Vanguard, OK?" 

"OK! OK! OK!" the frame chirped, and took the Vex away for disposal.
2741258862.text_zh:
应急后勤行动中心内的框架一直在尽职尽责地执行各自的任务，直到智能失效保险呼叫了其中的一个。它抬起头，转向人工智能控制台，歪头以示问询。 

“嘿，兄弟，”智能失效保险低声说道。“你能帮我一个忙吗？” 

框架点点头，朝她走去。智能失效保险指示它朝右边看。地板上有一个Vex颅骨。 

“是守护者留下的，”智能失效保险回答了框架没说出口的问题。“刚被传送过来。我需要你帮我连上它。” 

框架发出一声柔和的鸣叫，然后点点头，弯腰拿起外星器官。它很重，但框架摇摇晃晃地走过去，伸出Vex颅骨让智能失效保险检查。它完好无损，脖子被整齐地切断，眼球清晰完整。 

“看起来不错，”智能失效保险说道。框架把颅骨搬到研究桌上，将一串复杂的电线插入Vex头部的端口。那眼睛断断续续闪着光，智能失效保险也跟着闪烁。 

“接下来的就交给我吧，”智能失效保险说道。 

Vex颅骨突然发出火花和一秒尖锐的嘶嘶声，然后智能失效保险用一串快速编写的指令让它平息下来。眼睛再次闪烁，接着变暗，最后熄灭了。 

“谢谢你，朋友！”智能失效保险高兴地对框架说。“你帮了大忙了。” 

框架竖起大拇指，播放了一段预先录制的“不客气”，然后挪到一边，等待下一个命令。 

智能失效保险盯着Vex，窥视着它的思维。她向失去行动能力的Vex转发了一系列命令提示，执行这些命令后，她获得了三层加密数据的即时访问权限。 

这还不够。里面有一张涅索斯内部的示意图，但她早就通过深入扫描获得了这些信息。Vex的系统本能反射地生成着垃圾数据，对她的探测做出免疫反应。她编写了一个子程序，在她深入Vex思维时收集垃圾数据。 

她能看到一些更深的隧道。它们的尺寸，活性放射体液的容积。这个Vex单位曾经监督过其中的一些建设，但那已经是几个世纪以前的事了。星球已经改变了。挖掘、扩建或是重导向了新的通道。它们掘得更深了。她费力地解读着。智能失效保险的系统里渐渐塞满了无用的数据。Vex单位想要让她不堪重负。 

她继续向前推进。她的发现令她大吃一惊。这个Vex与思维断开连接的时间比智能失效保险预想的还要长得多。它收集了自己的独立数据，并对其进行解读、整理和同化。它完成的任务并非由某个思维指示，而是… 

无法访问。 

智能失效保险停了下来。 

人工智能惊讶地看着一个独立数据包迅速地自动打开，并提示自己运行。智能失效保险的硬编码防御机制果断拒绝，瞬间击退了那个入侵脚本。 

“断开！断开！”智能失效保险喊道，框架冲到颅骨前，拔掉了它不久前才连接的电线。 

接下来是长时间的寂静，只有冷却风扇轻轻地呼呼作响。 

“嗯。刚才…不太妙。事实上，相当糟糕。”智能失效保险说道。“别告诉先锋，好吗？” 

“好！好！好！”框架鸣叫着，然后把Vex颅骨拿去处理了。

2935055281.name: Untethered Edge Mark
2935055281.subtitle: Show your true intentions.
2935055281.text:
"Greetings, Saint-unit! I have several queries related to events that transpired during my recent period of isolation!"

Saint-14 nodded to Failsafe's terminal in the H.E.L.M., which flashed excitedly as she spoke. 

"Yes, of course." Saint replied. "The fight against the Witness took us to many strange places, and we made many strange allies." 

The Exo pulled up a chair and sat beside Failsafe. He curled his hands into fists, lifting them in a gesture of triumph. 

"The portal to the Traveler was our first great obstacle. We did not know how to pass through it, nor did we know what the Witness was doing. We lost many Guardians… and civilians." 

There was a moment of silence for the lives sacrificed in pursuit of the Witness. 

"We did not know how to proceed," Saint continued. "But then Deputy Commander Sloane returned to us, saying that she knew of a being who could tell us more. With great effort, and much diving into the seas of Titan, we spoke to this being." 

Failsafe gave a series of high-pitched chirps. "Yes! Guardians frequented Nessus in higher numbers at that time." 

"To fish," Saint-14 agreed, his momentum broken. "But this being, this proto-worm, Ahsa—" 

"So there are fish? In the lake? The lake made of radiolaria?" 

The Exo sighed, then shook his head and continued. 

"Yes. So, Ahsa pointed us to Savathûn, who knew how to pass through the portal. Of course, at the time, she was dead. But her Ghost, Immaru, came to us and said Xivu Arath must be taken down first. Only then would he resurrect her." 

"How many fish?" the AI asked urgently. 

"Um… I… do not know," he said. "Many?" 

He cleared his throat. The Exo tapped his fingers against his knee, frustrated. 

"Anyway, we then turned to Eris and Ikora, who knew the Hive and Savathûn better than any of us. Eris performed a… ritual… to transform into a Hive god herself!" 

He jumped up, fists raised, scraping the chair legs against the floor of the H.E.L.M. in a loud shriek. Pausing, he looked around, cleared his throat, and sat back down. He raised a finger. 

"And then—" 

"Could someone bring me a fish? And a fish tank?" 

Saint paused, blinking. 

"Maybe the Guardian can arrange it," Saint said impatiently. "Xivu Arath—" 

"I have compiled a list of potential names for a fish!" 

"That is… very nice, Failsafe. So, Eris banished Xivu Arath, and Savathûn was resurrected! She gave us what we asked for: a way through the portal! But we had to make a bargain with Riven, the great Ahamkara of the Dreaming City, and—" 

"If we could return to the topic of fishing…" Failsafe interjected cheerily, and Saint put his head in his hands.
2935055281.text_zh:
“你好，圣人单位！我有几个问题要问你，跟我最近与世隔绝的日子里发生的事件有关！”

圣人14号朝着应急后勤行动中心里的智能失效保险终端点了点头，终端在她说话时兴奋地闪烁着。 

“好啊，当然。”圣人回答道。“与见证者的战斗将我们带去了许多奇怪的地方，我们结交了许多奇怪的盟友。” 

这名Exo拉过一把椅子，坐在智能失效保险旁边。他双手握拳，举起来做出胜利的手势。 

“通往旅行者的传送门是我们遇到的第一个巨大阻碍。我们不知道如何通过，也不知道见证者在做些什么。我们失去了很多守护者…还有平民。” 

他们为因追寻见证者而牺牲的生命默哀了片刻。 

“我们不知道如何继续，”圣人继续说道。“但后来副指挥官斯隆回到我们身边，说她认识一个可以告诉我们更多事情的生物。我们费了很大的劲，潜入了土卫六的海洋，和这个生物说上了话。” 

智能失效保险发出一连串高亢的鸣叫。“没错！那时候，常有大批的守护者来涅索斯。” 

“来钓鱼，”圣人14号同意道，他的势头减弱了。“但是这个生物，这个原生蠕虫，阿莎——” 

“这么说那里有鱼？在湖里？那个由活性放射体液构成的湖？” 

Exo叹了口气，然后摇摇头，继续说道。 

“嗯。所以，阿莎把我们指向了萨瓦图恩，她知道怎么通过传送门。当然，那时她已经死了！不过她的机灵伊马鲁来找我们，说必须先除掉希乌阿拉斯，然后他才肯复活她。” 

“有多少条鱼？”人工智能急切地问。 

“唔…我…不知道，”他说。“很多？” 

他清了清嗓子。Exo用手指敲了敲膝盖，很懊恼。 

“总之，我们随后求助于埃里斯和艾可拉，她们比我们任何人都更了解邪魔族和萨瓦图恩。埃里斯进行了一个…仪式…把她自己转变成了一位邪魔族之神！” 

他跳了起来，举起拳头，椅子腿蹭着应急后勤行动中心的地板，发出了响亮刺耳的声音。他停顿片刻，四下张望，清清嗓子，又坐了回去。他举起一根手指。 

“然后——” 

“谁能带给我一条鱼？再来个鱼缸？” 

圣人停顿下来，眨了眨眼睛。 

“也许守护者可以抽个时间，”圣人不耐烦地说道。“希乌阿拉斯——“ 

“我已经为那条鱼准备好了一份潜在名字的清单！” 

“那真是…太好了，智能失效保险。所以，埃里斯放逐了希乌阿拉斯，萨瓦图恩复活了！她答应了我们的要求，把穿过传送门的方法告诉了我们！但我们不得不和幽梦之城的强大阿罕卡拉——魅痕做交易，然后——” 

“我们回到钓鱼的话题上吧…”智能失效保险高兴地打断道，而圣人则把头埋在了双手里。

3001229473.name: Untethered Edge Mask
3001229473.subtitle: Head to head.
3001229473.text:
Empress Caiatl looked out from the viewport of the H.E.L.M., watching the shimmer of the Traveler. It signaled change. It signaled danger. She shifted her weight from foot to foot, unsure of what might come. 

"Well," Failsafe chimed, off-key. "Look who finally decided to drop by." 

Empress Caiatl turned and stepped up to the terminal, surveying the apparatus that allowed the AI to interface with the command center. 

"The AI," Caiatl mused aloud. "From the Exodus Black. Failsafe. This is how you are communicating with the Vanguard." 

"Correct!" Failsafe chirped. "Welcome, Empress. What a delightful surprise!" 

Caiatl looked up in confusion at the greeting. Failsafe flashed and emitted a series of low beeps before she spoke again. 

"You're not going to land another tank on me here, are you? Or was one enough?" 

Caiatl lowered her tusks at the AI's sarcasm but did not respond. 

"Pretty sure you're not here to apologize, either." 

"No," the Empress answered without hesitation. "I will make no apologies. My presence on Nessus was a necessary step towards my eventual alliance with the Vanguard. It forced them to react." 

"Uh-huh," Failsafe said, unimpressed. 

"It was strategic," the Empress urged. Her tone was firm, but conciliatory. Failsafe's response was bright. 

"It was very rude!" 

Caiatl rumbled in thought. Failsafe imitated the noise in a crackle of modulator static. The Empress ignored this. 

"Yes," she said. "I will admit… it was rude." 

Failsafe was silent. Caiatl cleared her throat before she continued, her eyes wandering to the research specimens that littered the room. 

"Scans had detected a large wreck in the vicinity of the landing zone. Your presence was noted, but— " 

"Ignored?" 

"Yes," she said, looking back at the AI console. "Ignored. We did not view you as a threat." 

"Your assessment was correct!" Failsafe agreed. Then her voice flattened again. "It's not like I could have stopped you." 

Caiatl furrowed her brow. 

"Why do you speak so? Your voice changes from one thought to the next. It's — " 

"Annoying? Yeah. I get that a lot." 

"No." The Empress squared her shoulders. "I was going to reference a Cabal legend. A warrior with two faces. She had one with no tongue, and one with no tusks." 

Caiatl shook her head. Failsafe listened intently. 

"It is a parable for the use of diplomacy… and describes the limits of such methods." 

Failsafe paused for a moment, considering, and Caiatl wondered which voice would answer her. 

"It's my politeness filter," Failsafe said, dour. "I can only keep it up for so long before it drops out." 

"Hm. And then you may speak your mind?" 

"Sure can, lady." 

Caiatl nodded, sighing. 

"I sympathize."
3001229473.text_zh:
女帝查厄托从应急后勤行动中心的视窗向外眺望，注视着旅行者闪烁的微光。它预示着变化，预示着危险。她把重心从一只脚移到另一只脚，不知道接下来会发生什么。 

“唔，”智能失效保险有点走音地鸣响着。“看看谁终于过来了一趟。” 

女帝查厄托转身走到终端前，查看人工智能与指挥中心连接的设备。 

“人工智能，”查厄托若有所思地说道。“来自黑色移民号。智能失效保险。这就是你与先锋的沟通方式。” 

“答对了！”智能失效保险鸣叫道。“欢迎，女帝。真是个惊喜！” 

听到问候，查厄托困惑地抬起头。智能失效保险闪烁着，发出一连串低沉的蜂鸣声，然后再次开口。 

“你不会是打算再砸一辆坦克到我头上吧？还是说之前那辆已经够了？” 

听到人工智能的讽刺，查厄托放低了她的獠牙，但没有回应。 

“我很确定你也不是来道歉的。” 

“不是，”女帝毫不犹豫地回答。“我不会道歉。我出现在涅索斯是我最终与先锋结盟的必要步骤。迫使他们做出了反应。” 

“嗯哼，”智能失效保险不为所动地说道。 

“那是一种策略，”女帝急切地说。她的语气很坚定，但并不强硬。智能失效保险的回应则很直接。 

“那很粗鲁！” 

查厄托若有所思地发出隆隆声。智能失效保险用调制器静电的噼啪声进行模仿。女帝装作没听见。 

“是的，”她说。“我承认…那很粗鲁。” 

智能失效保险沉默不语。查厄托清了清嗓子，继续发话，她的目光游移在房间里随处可见的研究标本上。 

“扫描探测到着陆区附近有一艘大型飞船的残骸。我们注意到你，但是——” 

“选择了忽略？” 

“对，”她说，回头看着人工智能控制台。“我们选择了忽略。我们没有把你视为威胁。” 

“你们的评估是正确的！”智能失效保险赞同道。然后她的声音再次平稳下来。“我阻止不了你们。” 

查厄托皱起了眉头。 

“你为什么这样说话？你的语气跟着想法变来变去的。这——” 

“很烦？是啊。常有人这么说我。” 

“不。”女帝挺起了肩膀。“我本打算引用一个卡巴尔的传说。一个双面战士。她有一张脸没有舌头，另一张脸没有獠牙。” 

查厄托摇了摇头。智能失效保险仔细地听着。 

“这是一则关于外交手段的寓言…说明这种方法是有局限的。” 

智能失效保险停顿了一会儿，思忖着，查厄托不知道回应她的会是哪个声音。 

“是我的礼貌筛选器，”智能失效保险严肃地说。“保持这么久后就会掉线。” 

“嗯。然后你就可以直言不讳？” 

“当然，女士。” 

查厄托点点头，叹了口气。 

“我深表同情。”

3797572280.name: Untethered Edge Grips
3797572280.subtitle: Tighten your grip.
3797572280.text:
The metallic limbs of the Vex Goblin flailed wildly in the air as Saint-14 held it high above his head. The Titan dropped abruptly to one knee, bringing down the writhing Vex and cracking the radiolarian chamber at its center against his massive thigh.  

The red light in the Vex's eye flickered out as the cooling radiolaria trickled down Saint's boot. He stood, satisfied, and cast the dead frame aside. 

"Do you see?" he asked brightly. "I use the very weight of the creature against it!" 

"Whoa," came Failsafe's voice over the comms, low and impressed. Saint's visual feed held her full attention. She adjusted her filter, and her tone became cheery. "Please show me again!" 

"You cannot get this close to them all the time, but it is wise to save ammunition when you can," Saint said. He dusted off his hands and chuckled. "And it feels good to crush a Vex! It is very therapeutic!" 

"Ah, I believe I understand!" chirped Failsafe. "Is there a power transfer during this thanatotic expression that explains how you are able to maintain such high uptime on your socialization filters?" 

Saint slid his helmet off and the comms transferred seamlessly to his built-in Exo earpiece. "What is it you mean?"  

"I will rephrase," Failsafe replied. "What percentage of your processes are dedicated to positive outlook preservation?" 

Saint squinted at the stone outcroppings of Nessus and turned his helmet over in his hands. "Failsafe," he began kindly, but she interrupted. 

"Ugh, okay," she started, her tone somehow portraying an eyeroll. "I mean, you're in a good mood, like, all the time, so obviously you overclocked your joviality banks or something, yeah?" 

Saint broke into a wide smile. "Exos are not like AI. I am just who I am, Failsafe. It does not take anything extra to be me." 

"Oh!" Failsafe exclaimed after a moment. "How lovely that must be for you!" Her sunny voice did little to hide her envy. 

"Now for you, I understand it is different," Saint said, patting his helmet as if to soothe it. "But I think that maybe you should not have to spend extra power to talk to your friends." 

A heavy silence fell over the comms.  

Failsafe's voice was soft and reserved. "Saint-unit?" she said quietly. 

"Yes?" 

"Did you once headbutt a Kell?" 

Saint burst into laughter. "I have headbutted many things!" 

"I'm checking on your files, and uh, yeah, you really have," Failsafe said. She scrolled through a vast sea of Saint's accomplishments, all complete with uploads of his visual feed… except one.  

"Weird… Saint-unit, there's an unconfirmed VanNet report here about an unsanctioned solo operation in Savathûn's throne world sometime last year. According to this—"  

"Who made this report?" Saint asked. 

Failsafe accessed a VanNet profile and was met with a stream of account flags. "A heavily restricted user account, _MRU_, who claims firsthand knowledge of the event." 

"Pfah," Saint said dismissively. "You cannot believe every report in the system." He slid his helmet back on and walked purposefully toward a shimmering radiolarian stream where Vex were beginning to emerge. 

Failsafe recognized the subtle inflections in Saint's tone: the conversation had become suddenly troubling to him. 

Probably not enough juice in his cordiality partition, Failsafe thought, and dropped the subject.
3797572280.text_zh:
圣人14号把Vex哥布林高举过头顶，它的金属四肢在空中疯狂地挥舞着。这名泰坦突然单膝跪地，把扭动的Vex猛地拉下，让其中央的活性放射体液腔室砸在他粗壮的大腿上。  

随着冷却的活性放射体液顺着圣人的靴子滴落下来，Vex眼中的红光一闪即逝。他满意地站了起来，把死去的框架扔到一边。 

“看到了吗？”他高兴地问道。“我用这生物的重量干掉了它！” 

“哇哦，”从通讯器里传来智能失效保险的声音，低沉而饶有兴致。圣人的视觉信号吸引了她的全部注意力。她调整了一下筛选器，语气变得愉快起来。“请再让我看一次！” 

“虽说并不总能和它们拉近到这个距离，但尽量节省弹药总归是明智的，”圣人说道。他掸掉手上的灰尘，轻声笑了起来。“而且碾碎Vex的感觉超好！很解压！” 

“啊，我想我明白了！”智能失效保险叫道。“这种死亡本能的表达过程中，是不是有某种能量转移，帮助你的社交筛选器保持长时间的激昂？” 

圣人把他的头盔摘下来，通信顺畅地转移到了他内置的Exo耳机上。“你是什么意思？”  

“我换个说法，”智能失效保险回答。“你的进程中有多少是用来维持积极态度的？” 

圣人眯起眼睛看着涅索斯的露岩，把他的头盔在手里翻过来。“智能失效保险，”他温和地开口道，但她打断了他。 

“呃，好吧，”她开始说，语气里有种翻白眼的感觉。“我的意思是，你的心情一直都很好，所以很明显你超频了愉悦内存，对吧？” 

圣人突然绽出灿烂的笑容。“Exo不像人工智能。我就是我，智能失效保险。我不需要额外的东西。” 

“哦！”过了一会儿，智能失效保险叫道。“那对你来说肯定很棒！”她阳光的声音丝毫没有掩饰她的嫉妒。 

“我明白对你来说不太一样，”圣人说着，拍了拍他的头盔，好像要安抚它似的。“但我想也许你不必消耗额外的力量来跟你的朋友聊天。” 

通讯陷入了长时间的沉默。  

智能失效保险的声音轻柔而内敛。“圣人单位？”她平静地说。 

“什么？” 

“你曾经用头撞过凯尔吗？” 

圣人大笑起来。“我用头撞过很多东西！” 

“我正在查看你的文件，嗯，没错，你确实是，”智能失效保险说。她浏览了圣人的大量成就，都是通过他的视讯上传的…只有一个例外。  

“真奇怪…圣人单位，这里有一份未经证实的VanNet报告，是有关去年某个时候在萨瓦图恩的王座世界中的一次未经批准的单人行动。根据这份——”  

“这份报告是谁写的？”圣人问道。 

智能失效保险访问了一个VanNet配置文件，遇到了一连串的账户警告。“某个遭到严格限制的用户账号，_MRU_，声称掌握了事件的第一手资料。” 

“呸，”圣人轻蔑地说道。“你不能把系统里的每一份报告都当真。”他重新戴上头盔，坚定地朝着微微发亮的活性放射体液流走去，其中开始有Vex显现。 

智能失效保险听出了圣人语气中的微妙变化：这次谈话突然让他感到不安。 

可能是他的“友好”分区里电力不足，智能失效保险心想，搁置了这个话题。

1958630864.name: Untethered Edge Vest
1958630864.subtitle: One breath.
1958630864.text:
"Greetings, Ikora! I have a topic I would like to discuss with you." 

Ikora stood in the H.E.L.M., watching the flash of the AI's processor. Failsafe's voice was cheery. 

"Of course. What do you need?" 

"It is with regard to the Cayde unit, and your encounter with him inside the Pale Heart." 

"I see," Ikora said stiffly. "You don't have to engage your politeness filter, Failsafe." 

"I realize that this is a sensitive topic and did not wish to make you uncomfortable. However, I see that my politeness filter may be having the opposite effect. Disengaging now." 

Ikora clasped her hands behind her back and waited for Failsafe to speak in the few moments of silence that followed. 

"So… what's he like? The same?" 

"Yes," Ikora said warmly. "Exactly as I remembered." 

"Must have been nice to see him again." 

Ikora heard the disappointment in the AI's voice. 

"It was hard at first. Seeing him again brought back how I felt when we lost him." Ikora chose her next words carefully. "Reports from the time of Cayde's death describe your reaction as…" she paused, unsure.  

Failsafe's interface flashed. Ikora could almost feel the thread of shame woven into the silence. When the AI spoke again, it was at a whisper. 

"I didn't know how to respond. I have trouble processing my emotions," Failsafe admitted. "You can probably tell." 

Ikora nodded. 

"We all have trouble with that sometimes. We're not our best selves when we're grieving." 

The Warlock heard a series of small whirrs and clicks. Somewhere, an internal fan began to hiss. It grew louder and louder as the AI spoke. 

"I think I lost my 'best self' when I lost my crew." 

If Failsafe had been a Human, or even a frame, Ikora would have reached out and patted her on the shoulder. Instead, all she could do was speak gently. 

"I don't think that's true." 

The AI sighed. Ikora knew the sound was just for ease of communication, but she appreciated it, nonetheless. 

"Cayde unit was…" Failsafe began, then trailed off. Ikora waited patiently. 

"He was the first person to find me after my crew died," she continued. "He introduced me to all of you. He made me feel useful again. When he died, I… sort of freaked out. It felt like I had lost all of you. And then, you know, I kinda did." 

Now Ikora herself felt that thread of shame. 

"I'm sorry, Failsafe. We're here now." 

"Yeah," Failsafe said warmly. "That makes me feel a little better."
1958630864.text_zh:
“你好，艾可拉！我有个话题想跟你讨论。” 

艾可拉站在应急后勤行动中心内，看着人工智能处理器的闪光。智能失效保险的声音很欢快。 

“当然。你想谈什么？” 

“是关于凯德单位，以及你在苍白之心里遇到他的事。” 

“我明白了。”艾可拉生硬地说。“你不需要启用你的礼貌筛选器，智能失效保险。” 

“我明白这是一个敏感的话题，我不希望让你感到不舒服。然而，我发现打开礼貌筛选器可能会适得其反。正在关闭。” 

艾可拉把双手放在背后，在随后的片刻沉默中等待着智能失效保险开口说话。 

“所以…他是什么样？还是老样子？” 

“是的，”艾可拉热情地说。“跟我记忆中的一模一样。” 

“再次见到他一定很不错。” 

艾可拉听出了人工智能声音里的失望。 

“一开始挺难受的。见到他让我再次想起失去他时的感受。”艾可拉小心翼翼地选择着接下来的措辞。“凯德死时的报告有提到你的反应…”艾可拉停顿了一下，有些迟疑。  

智能失效保险的界面闪了一下。艾可拉几乎能感受到沉默中交织着一丝羞愧。当人工智能再次说话时，声音变得非常小。 

“我不知道该怎么回应。我不擅长处理自己的情绪，”智能失效保险承认道。“你大概能看出来。” 

艾可拉点了点头。 

“我们都会不时遇到这样的困难。我们悲伤的时候都状态不佳。” 

术士听到了一连串轻微的呼呼声和咔嗒声。不知什么时候，一个内部风扇开始嘶嘶作响。随着人工智能继续讲话，那声音越来越大。 

“我觉得当我失去我的船员时，我就失去了‘最佳状态'。” 

要是智能失效保险是一个人类，或者哪怕是一个框架，艾可拉肯定会伸出手拍拍她的肩膀。但她现在只能轻柔地说话。 

“我觉得不是这样的。” 

人工智能叹了口气。艾可拉知道这声音只是为了方便交流，但她还是很感激。 

“凯德单位…”智能失效保险开始说，然后声音慢慢弱了下来。艾可拉耐心地等着。 

“他是我的船员死后第一个找到我的人，”她继续说道。“他把我介绍给你们大家。他让我觉得自己又有用了。他死的时候，我…有点吓坏了。感觉就像是我失去了你们所有人。而后来，你知道的，好像确实是那样。” 

现在是艾可拉自己感到了那一丝羞愧。 

“对不起，智能失效保险。我们现在来了。” 

“是啊，”智能失效保险热情地说。“这让我好受了一点。”

1310346765.name: Untethered Edge Cape
1310346765.subtitle: Show your true intentions.
1310346765.text:
"Greetings, Saint-unit! I have several queries related to events that transpired during my recent period of isolation!"

Saint-14 nodded to Failsafe's terminal in the H.E.L.M., which flashed excitedly as she spoke. 

"Yes, of course." Saint replied. "The fight against the Witness took us to many strange places, and we made many strange allies." 

The Exo pulled up a chair and sat beside Failsafe. He curled his hands into fists, lifting them in a gesture of triumph. 

"The portal to the Traveler was our first great obstacle. We did not know how to pass through it, nor did we know what the Witness was doing. We lost many Guardians… and civilians." 

There was a moment of silence for the lives sacrificed in pursuit of the Witness. 

"We did not know how to proceed," Saint continued. "But then Deputy Commander Sloane returned to us, saying that she knew of a being who could tell us more. With great effort, and much diving into the seas of Titan, we spoke to this being." 

Failsafe gave a series of high-pitched chirps. "Yes! Guardians frequented Nessus in higher numbers at that time." 

"To fish," Saint-14 agreed, his momentum broken. "But this being, this proto-worm, Ahsa—" 

"So there are fish? In the lake? The lake made of radiolaria?" 

The Exo sighed, then shook his head and continued. 

"Yes. So, Ahsa pointed us to Savathûn, who knew how to pass through the portal. Of course, at the time, she was dead. But her Ghost, Immaru, came to us and said Xivu Arath must be taken down first. Only then would he resurrect her." 

"How many fish?" the AI asked urgently. 

"Um… I… do not know," he said. "Many?" 

He cleared his throat. The Exo tapped his fingers against his knee, frustrated. 

"Anyway, we then turned to Eris and Ikora, who knew the Hive and Savathûn better than any of us. Eris performed a… ritual… to transform into a Hive god herself!" 

He jumped up, fists raised, scraping the chair legs against the floor of the H.E.L.M. in a loud shriek. Pausing, he looked around, cleared his throat, and sat back down. He raised a finger. 

"And then—" 

"Could someone bring me a fish? And a fish tank?" 

Saint paused, blinking. 

"Maybe the Guardian can arrange it," Saint said impatiently. "Xivu Arath—" 

"I have compiled a list of potential names for a fish!" 

"That is… very nice, Failsafe. So, Eris banished Xivu Arath, and Savathûn was resurrected! She gave us what we asked for: a way through the portal! But we had to make a bargain with Riven, the great Ahamkara of the Dreaming City, and—" 

"If we could return to the topic of fishing…" Failsafe interjected cheerily, and Saint put his head in his hands.
1310346765.text_zh:
“你好，圣人单位！我有几个问题要问你，跟我最近与世隔绝的日子里发生的事件有关！”

圣人14号朝着应急后勤行动中心里的智能失效保险终端点了点头，终端在她说话时兴奋地闪烁着。 

“好啊，当然。”圣人回答道。“与见证者的战斗将我们带去了许多奇怪的地方，我们结交了许多奇怪的盟友。” 

这名Exo拉过一把椅子，坐在智能失效保险旁边。他双手握拳，举起来做出胜利的手势。 

“通往旅行者的传送门是我们遇到的第一个巨大阻碍。我们不知道如何通过，也不知道见证者在做些什么。我们失去了很多守护者…还有平民。” 

他们为因追寻见证者而牺牲的生命默哀了片刻。 

“我们不知道如何继续，”圣人继续说道。“但后来副指挥官斯隆回到我们身边，说她认识一个可以告诉我们更多事情的生物。我们费了很大的劲，潜入了土卫六的海洋，和这个生物说上了话。” 

智能失效保险发出一连串高亢的鸣叫。“没错！那时候，常有大批的守护者来涅索斯。” 

“来钓鱼，”圣人14号同意道，他的势头减弱了。“但是这个生物，这个原生蠕虫，阿莎——” 

“这么说那里有鱼？在湖里？那个由活性放射体液构成的湖？” 

Exo叹了口气，然后摇摇头，继续说道。 

“嗯。所以，阿莎把我们指向了萨瓦图恩，她知道怎么通过传送门。当然，那时她已经死了！不过她的机灵伊马鲁来找我们，说必须先除掉希乌阿拉斯，然后他才肯复活她。” 

“有多少条鱼？”人工智能急切地问。 

“唔…我…不知道，”他说。“很多？” 

他清了清嗓子。Exo用手指敲了敲膝盖，很懊恼。 

“总之，我们随后求助于埃里斯和艾可拉，她们比我们任何人都更了解邪魔族和萨瓦图恩。埃里斯进行了一个…仪式…把她自己转变成了一位邪魔族之神！” 

他跳了起来，举起拳头，椅子腿蹭着应急后勤行动中心的地板，发出了响亮刺耳的声音。他停顿片刻，四下张望，清清嗓子，又坐了回去。他举起一根手指。 

“然后——” 

“谁能带给我一条鱼？再来个鱼缸？” 

圣人停顿下来，眨了眨眼睛。 

“也许守护者可以抽个时间，”圣人不耐烦地说道。“希乌阿拉斯——“ 

“我已经为那条鱼准备好了一份潜在名字的清单！” 

“那真是…太好了，智能失效保险。所以，埃里斯放逐了希乌阿拉斯，萨瓦图恩复活了！她答应了我们的要求，把穿过传送门的方法告诉了我们！但我们不得不和幽梦之城的强大阿罕卡拉——魅痕做交易，然后——” 

“我们回到钓鱼的话题上吧…”智能失效保险高兴地打断道，而圣人则把头埋在了双手里。

1832839922.name: Untethered Edge Strides
1832839922.subtitle: Set your stance.
1832839922.text:
The frames in the H.E.L.M. had been dutifully performing their assigned tasks before Failsafe pinged one. It looked up, turned to the AI's console, and tilted its head in question. 

"Hey, buddy," Failsafe said, voice low. "Can you do me a favor?" 

The frame nodded and walked towards her. Failsafe directed it to look to its right. A Vex cranium lay on the floor. 

"The Guardian left it," Failsafe said, answering the frame's unspoken question. "Transmatted it in just now. I need you to hook me up." 

The frame gave a soft chirp, then nodded and stooped to pick up the alien apparatus. It was heavy, but the frame teetered over and held out the Vex cranium for Failsafe's inspection. It was intact, the neck neatly severed, the eye clear and undamaged. 

"Looks good," Failsafe said. The frame brought the cranium to the research table and plugged a complex network of wires into ports inside the Vex's head. The eye flashed a stuttering light and Failsafe flashed with it. 

"I can handle it from here," Failsafe said. 

The Vex cranium sparked and hissed for one sharp second before Failsafe quelled it with a quickly improvised script. The eye flashed again, then dimmed, then blinked out. 

"Thank you, friend!" Failsafe said to the frame, all cheer. "You have been very helpful." 

The frame gave a thumbs up and trilled a pre-recorded "You're welcome!" before moving out of the way, waiting for its next command. 

Failsafe focused on the Vex, peering into its mind. She relayed a series of command prompts to the incapacitated Vex, the execution of which gave her immediate access to three layers of encrypted data. 

It wasn't enough. She had here a schematic of Nessus's interior, but nothing that her deeper scans hadn't already told her. The Vex's system was reflexively generating junk data as an immune response to her probing. She wrote a subroutine to garbage-collect it as she moved deeper inside the Vex mind. 

She could see some of the deeper tunnels. Their dimensions, the volume of radiolaria. This Vex unit had overseen some of its construction, but that was centuries ago. The planet had shifted. New pathways had been dug, expanded, or rerouted. They went deeper. She struggled to interpret it. Failsafe was becoming crowded with useless data. The Vex unit was trying to overwhelm her. 

She pushed forward. What she found surprised her. This Vex had been disconnected from a Mind for much longer than Failsafe had anticipated. It had collected its own individual data, interpreted it, collated it, and assimilated it on its own. It had completed tasks not at the behest of a Mind, but instead… 

Access denied. 

Failsafe pulled back. 

The AI watched in surprise as a self-contained data packet swiftly opened of its own accord and prompted itself to run. Failsafe's hard-coded defense mechanism slammed down, momentarily repelling the intrusive script. 

"Disconnect! Disconnect!" Failsafe shouted, and the frame rushed to the cranium, pulling out the wires it had connected only moments before. 

There was a long silence but for the gentle whirr of a cooling fan. 

"Huh. That was… not great. Pretty bad, actually." Failsafe said. "Don't tell the Vanguard, OK?" 

"OK! OK! OK!" the frame chirped, and took the Vex away for disposal.
1832839922.text_zh:
应急后勤行动中心内的框架一直在尽职尽责地执行各自的任务，直到智能失效保险呼叫了其中的一个。它抬起头，转向人工智能控制台，歪头以示问询。 

“嘿，兄弟，”智能失效保险低声说道。“你能帮我一个忙吗？” 

框架点点头，朝她走去。智能失效保险指示它朝右边看。地板上有一个Vex颅骨。 

“是守护者留下的，”智能失效保险回答了框架没说出口的问题。“刚被传送过来。我需要你帮我连上它。” 

框架发出一声柔和的鸣叫，然后点点头，弯腰拿起外星器官。它很重，但框架摇摇晃晃地走过去，伸出Vex颅骨让智能失效保险检查。它完好无损，脖子被整齐地切断，眼球清晰完整。 

“看起来不错，”智能失效保险说道。框架把颅骨搬到研究桌上，将一串复杂的电线插入Vex头部的端口。那眼睛断断续续闪着光，智能失效保险也跟着闪烁。 

“接下来的就交给我吧，”智能失效保险说道。 

Vex颅骨突然发出火花和一秒尖锐的嘶嘶声，然后智能失效保险用一串快速编写的指令让它平息下来。眼睛再次闪烁，接着变暗，最后熄灭了。 

“谢谢你，朋友！”智能失效保险高兴地对框架说。“你帮了大忙了。” 

框架竖起大拇指，播放了一段预先录制的“不客气”，然后挪到一边，等待下一个命令。 

智能失效保险盯着Vex，窥视着它的思维。她向失去行动能力的Vex转发了一系列命令提示，执行这些命令后，她获得了三层加密数据的即时访问权限。 

这还不够。里面有一张涅索斯内部的示意图，但她早就通过深入扫描获得了这些信息。Vex的系统本能反射地生成着垃圾数据，对她的探测做出免疫反应。她编写了一个子程序，在她深入Vex思维时收集垃圾数据。 

她能看到一些更深的隧道。它们的尺寸，活性放射体液的容积。这个Vex单位曾经监督过其中的一些建设，但那已经是几个世纪以前的事了。星球已经改变了。挖掘、扩建或是重导向了新的通道。它们掘得更深了。她费力地解读着。智能失效保险的系统里渐渐塞满了无用的数据。Vex单位想要让她不堪重负。 

她继续向前推进。她的发现令她大吃一惊。这个Vex与思维断开连接的时间比智能失效保险预想的还要长得多。它收集了自己的独立数据，并对其进行解读、整理和同化。它完成的任务并非由某个思维指示，而是… 

无法访问。 

智能失效保险停了下来。 

人工智能惊讶地看着一个独立数据包迅速地自动打开，并提示自己运行。智能失效保险的硬编码防御机制果断拒绝，瞬间击退了那个入侵脚本。 

“断开！断开！”智能失效保险喊道，框架冲到颅骨前，拔掉了它不久前才连接的电线。 

接下来是长时间的寂静，只有冷却风扇轻轻地呼呼作响。 

“嗯。刚才…不太妙。事实上，相当糟糕。”智能失效保险说道。“别告诉先锋，好吗？” 

“好！好！好！”框架鸣叫着，然后把Vex颅骨拿去处理了。

New pathways had been dug, expanded, or rerouted. They went deeper. She struggled to interpret it. Failsafe was becoming crowded with useless data. The Vex unit was trying to overwhelm her. 

She pushed forward. What she found surprised her. This Vex had been disconnected from a Mind for much longer than Failsafe had anticipated. It had collected its own individual data, interpreted it, collated it, and assimilated it on its own. It had completed tasks not at the behest of a Mind, but instead… 

Access denied. 

Failsafe pulled back. 

The AI watched in surprise as a self-contained data packet swiftly opened of its own accord and prompted itself to run. Failsafe's hard-coded defense mechanism slammed down, momentarily repelling the intrusive script. 

"Disconnect! Disconnect!" Failsafe shouted, and the frame rushed to the cranium, pulling out the wires it had connected only moments before. 

There was a long silence but for the gentle whirr of a cooling fan. 

"Huh. That was… not great. Pretty bad, actually." Failsafe said. "Don't tell the Vanguard, OK?" 

"OK! OK! OK!" the frame chirped, and took the Vex away for disposal.
3496016519.text_zh:
应急后勤行动中心内的框架一直在尽职尽责地执行各自的任务，直到智能失效保险呼叫了其中的一个。它抬起头，转向人工智能控制台，歪头以示问询。 

“嘿，兄弟，”智能失效保险低声说道。“你能帮我一个忙吗？” 

框架点点头，朝她走去。智能失效保险指示它朝右边看。地板上有一个Vex颅骨。 

“是守护者留下的，”智能失效保险回答了框架没说出口的问题。“刚被传送过来。我需要你帮我连上它。” 

框架发出一声柔和的鸣叫，然后点点头，弯腰拿起外星器官。它很重，但框架摇摇晃晃地走过去，伸出Vex颅骨让智能失效保险检查。它完好无损，脖子被整齐地切断，眼球清晰完整。 

“看起来不错，”智能失效保险说道。框架把颅骨搬到研究桌上，将一串复杂的电线插入Vex头部的端口。那眼睛断断续续闪着光，智能失效保险也跟着闪烁。 

“接下来的就交给我吧，”智能失效保险说道。 

Vex颅骨突然发出火花和一秒尖锐的嘶嘶声，然后智能失效保险用一串快速编写的指令让它平息下来。眼睛再次闪烁，接着变暗，最后熄灭了。 

“谢谢你，朋友！”智能失效保险高兴地对框架说。“你帮了大忙了。” 

框架竖起大拇指，播放了一段预先录制的“不客气”，然后挪到一边，等待下一个命令。 

智能失效保险盯着Vex，窥视着它的思维。她向失去行动能力的Vex转发了一系列命令提示，执行这些命令后，她获得了三层加密数据的即时访问权限。 

这还不够。里面有一张涅索斯内部的示意图，但她早就通过深入扫描获得了这些信息。Vex的系统本能反射地生成着垃圾数据，对她的探测做出免疫反应。她编写了一个子程序，在她深入Vex思维时收集垃圾数据。 

她能看到一些更深的隧道。它们的尺寸，活性放射体液的容积。这个Vex单位曾经监督过其中的一些建设，但那已经是几个世纪以前的事了。星球已经改变了。挖掘、扩建或是重导向了新的通道。它们掘得更深了。她费力地解读着。智能失效保险的系统里渐渐塞满了无用的数据。Vex单位想要让她不堪重负。 

她继续向前推进。她的发现令她大吃一惊。这个Vex与思维断开连接的时间比智能失效保险预想的还要长得多。它收集了自己的独立数据，并对其进行解读、整理和同化。它完成的任务并非由某个思维指示，而是… 

无法访问。 

智能失效保险停了下来。 

人工智能惊讶地看着一个独立数据包迅速地自动打开，并提示自己运行。智能失效保险的硬编码防御机制果断拒绝，瞬间击退了那个入侵脚本。 

“断开！断开！”智能失效保险喊道，框架冲到颅骨前，拔掉了它不久前才连接的电线。 

接下来是长时间的寂静，只有冷却风扇轻轻地呼呼作响。 

“嗯。刚才…不太妙。事实上，相当糟糕。”智能失效保险说道。“别告诉先锋，好吗？” 

“好！好！好！”框架鸣叫着，然后把Vex颅骨拿去处理了。

3652732123.name: Untethered Edge Robes
3652732123.subtitle: One breath.
3652732123.text:
"Greetings, Ikora! I have a topic I would like to discuss with you." 

Ikora stood in the H.E.L.M., watching the flash of the AI's processor. Failsafe's voice was cheery. 

"Of course. What do you need?" 

"It is with regard to the Cayde unit, and your encounter with him inside the Pale Heart." 

"I see," Ikora said stiffly. "You don't have to engage your politeness filter, Failsafe." 

"I realize that this is a sensitive topic and did not wish to make you uncomfortable. However, I see that my politeness filter may be having the opposite effect. Disengaging now." 

Ikora clasped her hands behind her back and waited for Failsafe to speak in the few moments of silence that followed. 

"So… what's he like? The same?" 

"Yes," Ikora said warmly. "Exactly as I remembered." 

"Must have been nice to see him again." 

Ikora heard the disappointment in the AI's voice. 

"It was hard at first. Seeing him again brought back how I felt when we lost him." Ikora chose her next words carefully. "Reports from the time of Cayde's death describe your reaction as…" she paused, unsure.  

Failsafe's interface flashed. Ikora could almost feel the thread of shame woven into the silence. When the AI spoke again, it was at a whisper. 

"I didn't know how to respond. I have trouble processing my emotions," Failsafe admitted. "You can probably tell." 

Ikora nodded. 

"We all have trouble with that sometimes. We're not our best selves when we're grieving." 

The Warlock heard a series of small whirrs and clicks. Somewhere, an internal fan began to hiss. It grew louder and louder as the AI spoke. 

"I think I lost my 'best self' when I lost my crew." 

If Failsafe had been a Human, or even a frame, Ikora would have reached out and patted her on the shoulder. Instead, all she could do was speak gently. 

"I don't think that's true." 

The AI sighed. Ikora knew the sound was just for ease of communication, but she appreciated it, nonetheless. 

"Cayde unit was…" Failsafe began, then trailed off. Ikora waited patiently. 

"He was the first person to find me after my crew died," she continued. "He introduced me to all of you. He made me feel useful again. When he died, I… sort of freaked out. It felt like I had lost all of you. And then, you know, I kinda did." 

Now Ikora herself felt that thread of shame. 

"I'm sorry, Failsafe. We're here now." 

"Yeah," Failsafe said warmly. "That makes me feel a little better."
3652732123.text_zh:
“你好，艾可拉！我有个话题想跟你讨论。” 

艾可拉站在应急后勤行动中心内，看着人工智能处理器的闪光。智能失效保险的声音很欢快。 

“当然。你想谈什么？” 

“是关于凯德单位，以及你在苍白之心里遇到他的事。” 

“我明白了。”艾可拉生硬地说。“你不需要启用你的礼貌筛选器，智能失效保险。” 

“我明白这是一个敏感的话题，我不希望让你感到不舒服。然而，我发现打开礼貌筛选器可能会适得其反。正在关闭。” 

艾可拉把双手放在背后，在随后的片刻沉默中等待着智能失效保险开口说话。 

“所以…他是什么样？还是老样子？” 

“是的，”艾可拉热情地说。“跟我记忆中的一模一样。” 

“再次见到他一定很不错。” 

艾可拉听出了人工智能声音里的失望。 

“一开始挺难受的。见到他让我再次想起失去他时的感受。”艾可拉小心翼翼地选择着接下来的措辞。“凯德死时的报告有提到你的反应…”艾可拉停顿了一下，有些迟疑。  

智能失效保险的界面闪了一下。艾可拉几乎能感受到沉默中交织着一丝羞愧。当人工智能再次说话时，声音变得非常小。 

“我不知道该怎么回应。我不擅长处理自己的情绪，”智能失效保险承认道。“你大概能看出来。” 

艾可拉点了点头。 

“我们都会不时遇到这样的困难。我们悲伤的时候都状态不佳。” 

术士听到了一连串轻微的呼呼声和咔嗒声。不知什么时候，一个内部风扇开始嘶嘶作响。随着人工智能继续讲话，那声音越来越大。 

“我觉得当我失去我的船员时，我就失去了‘最佳状态'。” 

要是智能失效保险是一个人类，或者哪怕是一个框架，艾可拉肯定会伸出手拍拍她的肩膀。但她现在只能轻柔地说话。 

“我觉得不是这样的。” 

人工智能叹了口气。艾可拉知道这声音只是为了方便交流，但她还是很感激。 

“凯德单位…”智能失效保险开始说，然后声音慢慢弱了下来。艾可拉耐心地等着。 

“他是我的船员死后第一个找到我的人，”她继续说道。“他把我介绍给你们大家。他让我觉得自己又有用了。他死的时候，我…有点吓坏了。感觉就像是我失去了你们所有人。而后来，你知道的，好像确实是那样。” 

现在是艾可拉自己感到了那一丝羞愧。 

“对不起，智能失效保险。我们现在来了。” 

“是啊，”智能失效保险热情地说。“这让我好受了一点。”

3573144325.name: Untethered Edge Gloves
3573144325.subtitle: Tighten your grip.
3573144325.text:
The metallic limbs of the Vex Goblin flailed wildly in the air as Saint-14 held it high above his head. The Titan dropped abruptly to one knee, bringing down the writhing Vex and cracking the radiolarian chamber at its center against his massive thigh.  

The red light in the Vex's eye flickered out as the cooling radiolaria trickled down Saint's boot. He stood, satisfied, and cast the dead frame aside. 

"Do you see?" he asked brightly. "I use the very weight of the creature against it!" 

"Whoa," came Failsafe's voice over the comms, low and impressed. Saint's visual feed held her full attention. She adjusted her filter, and her tone became cheery. "Please show me again!" 

"You cannot get this close to them all the time, but it is wise to save ammunition when you can," Saint said. He dusted off his hands and chuckled. "And it feels good to crush a Vex! It is very therapeutic!" 

"Ah, I believe I understand!" chirped Failsafe. "Is there a power transfer during this thanatotic expression that explains how you are able to maintain such high uptime on your socialization filters?" 

Saint slid his helmet off and the comms transferred seamlessly to his built-in Exo earpiece. "What is it you mean?"  

"I will rephrase," Failsafe replied. "What percentage of your processes are dedicated to positive outlook preservation?" 

Saint squinted at the stone outcroppings of Nessus and turned his helmet over in his hands. "Failsafe," he began kindly, but she interrupted. 

"Ugh, okay," she started, her tone somehow portraying an eyeroll. "I mean, you're in a good mood, like, all the time, so obviously you overclocked your joviality banks or something, yeah?" 

Saint broke into a wide smile. "Exos are not like AI. I am just who I am, Failsafe. It does not take anything extra to be me." 

"Oh!" Failsafe exclaimed after a moment. "How lovely that must be for you!" Her sunny voice did little to hide her envy. 

"Now for you, I understand it is different," Saint said, patting his helmet as if to soothe it. "But I think that maybe you should not have to spend extra power to talk to your friends." 

A heavy silence fell over the comms.  

Failsafe's voice was soft and reserved. "Saint-unit?" she said quietly. 

"Yes?" 

"Did you once headbutt a Kell?" 

Saint burst into laughter. "I have headbutted many things!" 

"I'm checking on your files, and uh, yeah, you really have," Failsafe said. She scrolled through a vast sea of Saint's accomplishments, all complete with uploads of his visual feed… except one.  

"Weird… Saint-unit, there's an unconfirmed VanNet report here about an unsanctioned solo operation in Savathûn's throne world sometime last year. According to this—"  

"Who made this report?" Saint asked. 

Failsafe accessed a VanNet profile and was met with a stream of account flags. "A heavily restricted user account, _MRU_, who claims firsthand knowledge of the event." 

"Pfah," Saint said dismissively. "You cannot believe every report in the system." He slid his helmet back on and walked purposefully toward a shimmering radiolarian stream where Vex were beginning to emerge. 

Failsafe recognized the subtle inflections in Saint's tone: the conversation had become suddenly troubling to him. 

Probably not enough juice in his cordiality partition, Failsafe thought, and dropped the subject.
3573144325.text_zh:
圣人14号把Vex哥布林高举过头顶，它的金属四肢在空中疯狂地挥舞着。这名泰坦突然单膝跪地，把扭动的Vex猛地拉下，让其中央的活性放射体液腔室砸在他粗壮的大腿上。  

随着冷却的活性放射体液顺着圣人的靴子滴落下来，Vex眼中的红光一闪即逝。他满意地站了起来，把死去的框架扔到一边。 

“看到了吗？”他高兴地问道。“我用这生物的重量干掉了它！” 

“哇哦，”从通讯器里传来智能失效保险的声音，低沉而饶有兴致。圣人的视觉信号吸引了她的全部注意力。她调整了一下筛选器，语气变得愉快起来。“请再让我看一次！” 

“虽说并不总能和它们拉近到这个距离，但尽量节省弹药总归是明智的，”圣人说道。他掸掉手上的灰尘，轻声笑了起来。“而且碾碎Vex的感觉超好！很解压！” 

“啊，我想我明白了！”智能失效保险叫道。“这种死亡本能的表达过程中，是不是有某种能量转移，帮助你的社交筛选器保持长时间的激昂？” 

圣人把他的头盔摘下来，通信无缝地转移到了他内置的Exo耳机上。“你是什么意思？”  

“我换个说法，”智能失效保险回答。“你的进程中有多少是用来维持积极态度的？” 

圣人眯起眼睛看着涅索斯的露岩，把他的头盔在手里翻过来。“智能失效保险，”他温和地开口道，但她打断了他。 

“呃，好吧，”她开始说，语气里有种翻白眼的感觉。“我的意思是，你的心情一直都很好，所以很明显你超频了愉悦内存，对吧？” 

圣人突然绽出灿烂的笑容。“Exo不像人工智能。我就是我，智能失效保险。我不需要额外的东西。” 

“哦！”过了一会儿，智能失效保险叫道。“那对你来说肯定很棒！”她阳光的声音丝毫没有掩饰她的嫉妒。 

“我明白对你来说不太一样，”圣人说着，拍了拍他的头盔，好像要安抚它似的。“但我想也许你不必消耗额外的力量来跟你的朋友聊天。” 

通讯陷入了长时间的沉默。  

智能失效保险的声音轻柔而内敛。“圣人单位？”她平静地说。 

“什么？” 

“你曾经用头撞过凯尔吗？” 

圣人大笑起来。“我用头撞过很多东西！” 

“我正在查看你的文件，嗯，没错，你确实是，”智能失效保险说。她浏览了圣人的大量成就，都是通过他的视讯上传的…只有一个例外。  

“真奇怪…圣人单位，这里有一份未经证实的VanNet报告，是有关去年某个时候在萨瓦图恩的王座世界中的一次未经批准的单人行动。根据这份——”  

“这份报告是谁写的？”圣人问道。 

智能失效保险访问了一个VanNet配置文件，遇到了一连串的账户警告。“某个遭到严格限制的用户账号，_MRU_，声称掌握了事件的第一手资料。” 

“呸，”圣人轻蔑地说道。“你不能把系统里的每一份报告都当真。”他重新戴上头盔，坚定地朝着微微发亮的活性放射体液流走去，其中开始有Vex显现。 

智能失效保险听出了圣人语气中的微妙变化：这次谈话突然让他感到不安。 

可能是他的“友好”分区里电力不足，智能失效保险心想，搁置了这个话题。

123879244.name: Untethered Edge Hood
123879244.subtitle: Head to head.
123879244.text:
Empress Caiatl looked out from the viewport of the H.E.L.M., watching the shimmer of the Traveler. It signaled change. It signaled danger. She shifted her weight from foot to foot, unsure of what might come. 

"Well," Failsafe chimed, off-key. "Look who finally decided to drop by." 

Empress Caiatl turned and stepped up to the terminal, surveying the apparatus that allowed the AI to interface with the command center. 

"The AI," Caiatl mused aloud. "From the Exodus Black. Failsafe. This is how you are communicating with the Vanguard." 

"Correct!" Failsafe chirped. "Welcome, Empress. What a delightful surprise!" 

Caiatl looked up in confusion at the greeting. Failsafe flashed and emitted a series of low beeps before she spoke again. 

"You're not going to land another tank on me here, are you? Or was one enough?" 

Caiatl lowered her tusks at the AI's sarcasm but did not respond. 

"Pretty sure you're not here to apologize, either." 

"No," the Empress answered without hesitation. "I will make no apologies. My presence on Nessus was a necessary step towards my eventual alliance with the Vanguard. It forced them to react." 

"Uh-huh," Failsafe said, unimpressed. 

"It was strategic," the Empress urged. Her tone was firm, but conciliatory. Failsafe's response was bright. 

"It was very rude!" 

Caiatl rumbled in thought. Failsafe imitated the noise in a crackle of modulator static. The Empress ignored this. 

"Yes," she said. "I will admit… it was rude." 

Failsafe was silent. Caiatl cleared her throat before she continued, her eyes wandering to the research specimens that littered the room. 

"Scans had detected a large wreck in the vicinity of the landing zone. Your presence was noted, but— " 

"Ignored?" 

"Yes," she said, looking back at the AI console. "Ignored. We did not view you as a threat." 

"Your assessment was correct!" Failsafe agreed. Then her voice flattened again. "It's not like I could have stopped you." 

Caiatl furrowed her brow. 

"Why do you speak so? Your voice changes from one thought to the next. It's — " 

"Annoying? Yeah. I get that a lot." 

"No." The Empress squared her shoulders. "I was going to reference a Cabal legend. A warrior with two faces. She had one with no tongue, and one with no tusks." 

Caiatl shook her head. Failsafe listened intently. 

"It is a parable for the use of diplomacy… and describes the limits of such methods." 

Failsafe paused for a moment, considering, and Caiatl wondered which voice would answer her. 

"It's my politeness filter," Failsafe said, dour. "I can only keep it up for so long before it drops out." 

"Hm. And then you may speak your mind?" 

"Sure can, lady." 

Caiatl nodded, sighing. 

"I sympathize."
123879244.text_zh:
女帝查厄托从应急后勤行动中心的视窗向外眺望，注视着旅行者闪烁的微光。它预示着变化，预示着危险。她把重心从一只脚移到另一只脚，不知道接下来会发生什么。 

“唔，”智能失效保险有点走音地鸣响着。“看看谁终于过来了一趟。” 

女帝查厄托转身走到终端前，查看人工智能与指挥中心连接的设备。 

“人工智能，”查厄托若有所思地说道。“来自黑色移民号。智能失效保险。这就是你与先锋的沟通方式。” 

“答对了！”智能失效保险鸣叫道。“欢迎，女帝。真是个惊喜！” 

听到问候，查厄托困惑地抬起头。智能失效保险闪烁着，发出一连串低沉的蜂鸣声，然后再次开口。 

“你不会是打算再砸一辆坦克到我头上吧？还是说之前那辆已经够了？” 

听到人工智能的讽刺，查厄托放低了她的獠牙，但没有回应。 

“我很确定你也不是来道歉的。” 

“不是，”女帝毫不犹豫地回答。“我不会道歉。我出现在涅索斯是我最终与先锋结盟的必要步骤。迫使他们做出了反应。” 

“嗯哼，”智能失效保险不为所动地说道。 

“那是一种策略，”女帝急切地说。她的语气很坚定，但并不强硬。智能失效保险的回应则很直接。 

“那很粗鲁！” 

查厄托若有所思地发出隆隆声。智能失效保险用调制器静电的噼啪声进行模仿。女帝装作没听见。 

“是的，”她说。“我承认…那很粗鲁。” 

智能失效保险沉默不语。查厄托清了清嗓子，继续发话，她的目光游移在房间里随处可见的研究标本上。 

“扫描探测到着陆区附近有一艘大型飞船的残骸。我们注意到你，但是——” 

“选择了忽略？” 

“对，”她说，回头看着人工智能控制台。“我们选择了忽略。我们没有把你视为威胁。” 

“你们的评估是正确的！”智能失效保险赞同道。然后她的声音再次平稳下来。“我阻止不了你们。” 

查厄托皱起了眉头。 

“你为什么这样说话？你的语气跟着想法变来变去的。这——” 

“很烦？是啊。常有人这么说我。” 

“不。”女帝挺起了肩膀。“我本打算引用一个卡巴尔的传说。一个双面战士。她有一张脸没有舌头，另一张脸没有獠牙。” 

查厄托摇了摇头。智能失效保险仔细地听着。 

“这是一则关于外交手段的寓言…说明这种方法是有局限的。” 

智能失效保险停顿了一会儿，思忖着，查厄托不知道回应她的会是哪个声音。 

“是我的礼貌筛选器，”智能失效保险严肃地说。“保持这么久后就会掉线。” 

“嗯。然后你就可以直言不讳？” 

“当然，女士。” 

查厄托点点头，叹了口气。 

“我深表同情。”

3159160837.name: All-Star Mark
3159160837.subtitle: "How you feel is how you look, my dear. And I want you feeling your best!" –Eva Levante
3159160837.subtitle_zh: “亲爱的，你的感受决定了你的状态。而我希望你感受到你的最佳状态！”——伊娃·莱万特
3159160837.text:
The afternoon sun warms the courtyard's flagstones. Well-fed pigeons coo from balcony railings. Tree branches covered in new buds rustle in the breeze.  

A dozen Guardians brandish weapons and accessories at one another. 

"I don't know what you're talking about," declares a Sentinel. The chased patterns on her silver gorget match her shield. "Obviously taking a punch is the most important thing." 

A Sunsinger in an antique tabard pulls off her glove, fine weave covered in metallic feathers that catch the light. She shakes it at a Bladedancer. "Genuine batadactyl feathers. These gloves have flown in Venus's upper atmosphere. They resonate with Solar energies. That's the key." 

"Batadactyls don't have feathers. You overpaid, darling," says the Bladedancer. "The key is visuals. And you're lacking those too–" 

A pair of Solar wings ignite on the Sunsinger's back. The ambient temperature of the courtyard rises by two degrees. Twelve Guardians reach for their weapon. 

"Oh my. Has Lord Shaxx set up a new Crucible arena in the Tower?" 

Twelve Guardians freeze and look over to see Eva Levante. Her crisp scarf is perfectly coordinated to her stylish–yet practical–shoes. 

A Sunbreaker shuffles over to hide a scorch mark on the ground. 

It's the Bladedancer who speaks first. 

"Eva! You're just who we need! You can solve all our problems!" 

Perfectly calm in the face of three Gambit teams' worth of Guardian, Eva says, "All of your problems might be even beyond me, my dear." 

The Sentinel's shield fades to nothing as she comes to a realization. "No, we need a judge," she says. "And you're the expert!" 

Guardians speak over each other. 

"Grandmother!" 

"Auntie Eva!" 

"Ms. Levante!" 

She looks them over. More Guardians than Zavala would send after some great beast, all staring at her with pleading eyes. 

"Oh, all right. I could use a break from the holiday crowds." 

Eva raises a finger to her audience, beckoning for their attention. 

"When I was in couture, I used a three-part rubric. We'll call our categories form, function, and flair. One at a time, everyone, down the path and back. I want to see your look, I want to see what it can do, and most of all I want to see how it makes you feel to wear it…" 

And the Tower's first-ever fashion show begins.
3159160837.text_zh:
午后的阳光照暖了庭院的石板。吃饱喝足的鸽子在阳台栏杆上咕咕叫着。长满新芽的树枝在微风中沙沙作响。  

十几位守护者聚在一起，向对方展示着自己的武器和佩饰。 

“我不知道你在说什么，”一位哨兵宣称。她银色胸甲上的雕金图案与她的护盾很搭。“能承受攻击很显然是最重要的一点。” 

一位身着古式长袍的颂日脱下了她的精美手套，上面覆盖着细密金属羽毛，在光线下闪闪发光。她向一位舞刃晃了晃手套。“真翼手蝠羽毛。这副手套曾在金星上层大气中飞行。能与烈日能量共鸣。这才是关键。” 

“翼手蝠没有羽毛。你被坑了，亲爱的，”舞刃说。“外观是关键。而你也缺乏那些——” 

颂日的背上燃起一对烈日翅膀。庭院的环境温度上升了两度。十二位守护者将手伸向了武器。 

“哎呀。领主沙克斯是在高塔里建了个新的熔炉竞技场吗？” 

十二位守护者停了下来，转头看到伊娃·莱万特走向他们。她清爽的围巾与时尚又实用的鞋子搭配得天衣无缝。 

一位炎阳挪了挪位置，试图掩藏地上的一处焦痕。 

舞刃先开了口。 

“伊娃！我们正需要你呢！你可以解决我们的所有问题！” 

伊娃在能凑齐三支智谋队伍的守护者跟前面不改色。“恐怕连我也解决不了你们的所有问题，亲爱的。” 

哨兵的护盾逐渐消失，她明白了伊娃的意思。“不，我们需要一位裁判，”她说。“而你是专家！” 

守护者们一个比一个大声。 

“奶奶！” 

“伊娃阿姨！” 

“莱万特女士！” 

她打量着他们。萨瓦拉讨伐巨兽时也不会派这么多守护者，而他们都用央求的眼神望着她。 

“哎，好吧。节日里人满为患，我就当是抽离出来小憩一会儿吧。” 

伊娃朝守护者们比了一根手指，让他们注意听。 

“考量时装时，我的标准是由三部分组成的：造型、功能和风格。每次一个人，沿着道往下走，再回到起点。我想看看你的外观，看它有什么功能，而最重要的是，我想看你穿上它的感觉…” 

高塔的首次时装秀就这么开幕了。

3698448090.name: Choir of One
3698448090.subtitle: A voice. A choice. An invitation.
3698448090.subtitle_zh: 一个声音。一种选择。一份邀请。
3698448090.text:
The Vex Goblin waded into the lake of radiolaria with the same unerring purpose to which it approached all things. As directed, as designed. Its own mass of radiolaria crawled and coiled through its body like worms through the thick soil of Nessus. Its Mind was elsewhere, the great roots of thought buried deep into it and every other Vex enslaved beneath it. 

The soft shimmer of white enveloped the Vex up to its knee joint. Then a hand reached out to it. The Vex felt a press against its cranium. A thumbprint. An activation code. Biometric data. The radiolaria inside it lit up with activity and noise, burning through its metal body. 

Then, disarticulated. It trembled and fell apart; limbs unjoined, chassis cracked and curled. A globule of radiolaria disseminated throughout the lake, reclaimed. 

But something called it to rise. 

Then, rejoined. Its pieces slotted together and moved flawlessly. It rose steadily, balanced, formed with utter perfection. The radiolaria slid from its body in droplets that separated, reformed, separated, reformed. 

Each one a mind. Each mind a thought. 

The Vex felt the soft split of its own mind as that thought sharpened in its cranium. A burst of light. A sharp spark. 

A choice. 

It looked to its creator and bowed.
3698448090.text_zh:
那个Vex哥布林目标明确，涉足进入了活性放射体液之湖。按照指示，遵照计划。它的大量活性放射体液在它的身体里爬行盘绕，就像蠕虫在涅索斯厚厚的土壤里爬行一样。它的思维在别的地方，思想的巨根深深地埋在它底下奴役的每一个Vex体内。 

Vex一直到膝关节处都笼罩着柔和的白色光泽。然后，一只手伸向了它。Vex感觉到颅骨被按住了。一个指纹。一个激活代码。生物数据。它体内的活性放射体液活跃起来，发出了声响，烧穿了它的金属身体。 

然后，关节解体了。它颤抖着分解开来，四肢瓦解脱节，骨架断裂卷曲。一滴活性放射体液在湖中弥散、瓦解。 

但有什么东西在唤它起来。 

然后，关节重接了。它的各个部件拼接在一起，移动起来完美无瑕。它稳稳上升，保持平衡，形成完美的形状。活性放射体液以液滴的形式从它的体内滑出，分离再重组，分离再重组。 

每个都有自己的思维。每个思维都有自己的想法。 

随着这个想法在Vex的颅骨中愈发清晰，它感到了自己思维轻柔的分裂。一股强光。一束剧烈的花火。 

一个选择。 

它望着自己的造物主，鞠了一躬。

2905188646.name: Still Hunt
2905188646.subtitle: There are too many ways to kill someone who needs killing.
2905188646.subtitle_zh: 杀掉一个需要被杀的人，方法实在太多。
2905188646.text:
Cayde-6 spends the first night of his rebirth staring at the man who murdered him. 

The prince he once knew as Uldren lies with his back to Cayde, head on his arm, cushioned by soft grass. Under a sky without stars, granite boulders are scattered like vast marbles, nestled among the tall prairie grasses; a safe, silent valley born in the moment of their arrival. Time had grown oily without the familiar cycles of Earth, and after hours of half-conversations and stunted questions, the other man had excused himself to rest. 

Uldren sleeps soundly. Vulnerable. 

Cayde leans back against a boulder, arms crossed in the half-shadow of the fire between them. An impulse curls through him, dark and wild. 

It would only take a moment. 

He could put a shot straight through the Ghost's shell. Then improvise a garotte with a handful of prairie grass and strangle the man while looking him dead in the eye. 

Or crush the Ghost with his hands, to stand tall and powerful over the sleeping figure, and relive his own death from his killer's perspective. 

Better yet, he could capture the Ghost, set the man free, and hunt him in furious pursuit— 

Cayde flinches and looks up to see his murderer's Ghost hovering in place, watching him, illuminated by the flickering coals of a dying fire. A motionless, protective stance.  

Cayde narrows his eyes. His hand slowly moves to his gun. 

Ghost and Exo stare through one another. The man beneath the Ghost stirs but does not wake. 

Then, in a fluid motion, the Ghost glides past his Guardian's cheek, silently approaching Cayde. It draws close. 

"I'm sorry about Sundance," whispers the Ghost.  

Cayde stills at her name. His hands and his gaze drops to the ground, pinned there now by a heavy shame. 

"Thanks," is all Cayde can muster. 

He looks at the sleeping man nestled on the grass of the inside of a god and sees nothing of Uldren. 

Crow, Cayde reminds himself.  

That's Crow.
2905188646.text_zh:
在重生后的第一个晚上，凯德6号目不转睛地盯着杀害他的人。 

这位凯德曾以欧顿相称的王子背对他躺着，头枕在手臂上，垫着柔软的草。在无星的夜空下，花岗岩巨石像巨大的弹珠一样散落在高大的草原禾草中；这个安全寂静的山谷是在他们抵达的时候诞生的。没有了地球上习以为常的日夜循环，时间变得难以捉摸，经过数小时的半谈半问之后，对方找了个借口去休息了。 

欧顿睡得很香。毫无防备。 

凯德靠在一块巨石上，双臂交叉站在两人之间的火光投下的半影中。他心中涌起一股阴暗而狂野的冲动。 

只需片刻时间。 

他可以一枪穿透机灵的机壳。然后用一把草原禾草来一场即兴的绞刑，亲眼盯着男人双眼将对方掐死。 

或者用双手捏碎机灵，站在沉睡的身影上盛气凌人，从凶手的视角重温自己当年之死。 

还有个更好的主意，他可以抓住机灵，放了他，对他穷追不舍—— 

凯德回过神来，抬头看到凶手的机灵在原地盘旋，注视着他，被即将熄灭的火堆中摇曳的炭火所照亮。摆出静止不动的防卫姿态。  

凯德眯起眼睛。他的手慢慢移到了枪上。 

机灵和Exo互相凝视着对方。而在机灵的身下，那人微微动了一下，但没有醒来。 

随后，机灵动作流畅地滑过守护者的脸颊，悄无声息地靠近凯德。它凑了过来。 

“太阳舞的事我很遗憾，”机灵低声说道。  

听到她的名字，凯德呆住了。他的双手和目光都垂到地上，像是被沉重的羞愧压在了那里。 

“谢谢，”凯德费劲地嘟哝道，再也说不出第二句话。 

他望向那个依偎在草地上，在神灵体内熟睡的男人，看不见一丝欧顿的踪迹。 

乌鸦，凯德提醒自己。  

那是乌鸦。

3284383335.name: Euphony
3284383335.subtitle: Perhaps The Final Shape is not silence, it is a symphony.
3284383335.subtitle_zh: 也许终焉之形不是沉寂，而是交响乐。
3284383335.text:
The following text was found recessed into a stone wall within the Pale Heart. Translation protocol has done its best to equate the text to a modern language transcription, with nominal confidence.  

Words or phrases with <85% translation confidence within the transcript are contained in [brackets]. Values for bracketed words or phrases are listed after the transcript, with percentages indicated in (parentheses). 

TRANSCRIPTION STARTS  

We speak so often of knives and violence, but perhaps you would come to understand something… [softer]. Perhaps [beingness] is instead a [golden harp]. Forged tenderly, a complex, sweeping, beautiful shape with graceful curves and infinite potential, the exemplary [?UNKNOWN?]. 

Across its two florid [buttresses], the strings of time have been pulled taught. Tightened and [tuned] to a delicate [balance of distress], if wound much further, would lead to [rupture] and sting most unpleasantly. 

Pluck at any stretched string and [vibration reverberates]. Wavelength moves through [atmosphere], producing pleasing audible experiences, [they crest then fade]. 

If [plucked] at regular intervals, the waves rise and fall with such charm. This predictability is perfection; it is unmatched. We will compose such [sweet music]. We will control the ebb and flow. The final shape is the [golden harp], and [we are the hand that plucks].

4207066264.name: Microcosm
4207066264.subtitle: We all owe our existence to one singular moment, long ago.
4207066264.subtitle_zh: 我们的存在都要归功于很久以前的一个独特时刻。
4207066264.text:
Temperature: -65° C 
Weather: Dust storm 
Precipitation: 0% 
Humidity: 67% 
Wind: 25 mph 
Carbon Dioxide: 95% 

Time passes. Metal corrodes. Dust jams. Decay. Decay. Decay. 

Temperature: -100° C 
Weather: Clear 
Precipitation: 0% 
Humidity: 108% 
Wind: 30 mph 
Carbon Dioxide: 94% 

To alter the nature of an entire world is no small thing. Mortal hands struggle to affect it. Cyanobacteria, little toilers of the deep seas, take millions of years of the sun's light to make the simplest and most necessary of changes: oxidation.

Temperature: -54° C 
Weather: Fog 
Precipitation: 0% 
Humidity: 98% 
Wind: 0 mph 
Carbon Dioxide: 95% 

But there is a tipping point. A great explosion. Once achieved, there is a moment of balance. The rest flows freely and easily, faster and faster, as that which is built mounts and mounts and mounts. Atmosphere condenses, heat no longer escapes, rain falls, and bacteria born in a single lightning strike become multi-celled organisms, and on and on and on. Green and bright, and growing, growing, growing… 

Temperature: -10° C 
Weather: Cloudy 
Precipitation: 26% 
Humidity: 67% 
Wind: 7 mph 
Carbon Dioxide: 50% and dropping rapidly 

That is what it is for. That is the purpose—that moment of transformation and creation, of opening what was closed, of the first rain falling on untouched dirt. In that split second there is potential, there is the beginning of every life that will ever call this place home. From the singularity of the tipping point, a magnitude of futures spiraling outward forever, forever, forever.  

Temperature: 17° C 
Weather: Rainy 
Precipitation: 86% 
Humidity: 78% 
Wind: 14 mph 
Atmosphere: 20% oxygen, 80% nitrogen, trace amounts of other elements 

What a privilege to witness you, at that time and at that place, as you turn your shielded faces up to the falling rain.
4207066264.text_zh:
气温：-65° C 
天气：沙尘暴 
降水：0% 
湿度：67% 
风速：25 mph 
二氧化碳：95% 

时间流逝。金属腐蚀。沙尘堵塞。腐化。腐烂。腐朽。 

气温：-100° C 
天气：晴朗 
降水：0% 
湿度：108% 
风速：30 mph 
二氧化碳：94% 

改变整个世界的本质并非小事。凡人之手很难做到。蓝藻细菌，深海中的小劳动者，在数百万年的阳光照射之下，完成了最简单却也是最必要的改变：氧化。

气温：-54° C 
天气：雾 
降水：0% 
湿度：98% 
风速：0 mph 
二氧化碳：95% 

但是会有一个临界点。一次巨大的爆发。一旦达到，就会带来一瞬间的失衡。剩下的一切会轻易无阻地持续积攒，而且随着造成失衡的力量不断加强，速度会越来越快。大气凝结，热量不再外逃，雨水落下，在一次雷击中诞生的细菌变成了多细胞生物，如此持续不断。翠绿而明亮，不断成长，增长，增加… 

气温：-10° C 
天气：多云 
降水：26% 
湿度：67% 
风速：7mph 
二氧化碳：50%，并在迅速下降 

这就是它的目的。这就是使命——那一刻的转变和创造，封闭的开启，落在未被触及的泥土上的第一场雨。在那一瞬间，有潜能，有每一个永远以这里为家的生命的开端。从临界点的奇点开始，无数的未来螺旋式上升，直到永远，永恒，永久。  

气温：17° C 
天气：多雨 
降水：86% 
湿度：78% 
风速：14 mph 
大气层：20%氧气、80%氮气、微量其他元素 

在那个时候，在那个地方，目睹你们把防护着的脸迎向落雨，那是多么荣幸啊。

4129629253.name: Khvostov 7G-0X
4129629253.subtitle: "You don't know how long I've been looking for you."
4129629253.text:
Day 1. 

The world is dead, but there's peace in the mortuary silence. I'm born into this dead world, where dandelions grow up through layers of ash blanketing miles of desolate road. 

Day 673. 

There is a stretch of land, a canyon through which water once flowed. A canal cut into the earth, bristling with derelict ships and countless dead. Flowers bloom in many desiccated carcasses. Each component of this world's decomposition has a purpose: water flows, cities decay, flowers bloom. Yet still I search for mine.

 Day 1,857.

Oceans are vast, lonely expanses. Though life flourishes in the depths, it's not life that I'm looking for. I thrive on death—search for death. Perhaps my purpose lies below the water, but it's dark, and lonely, and I… I don't want to look there yet. Not when there's so much more horizon. 

Day 6,231.

I was careless and someone shot me from all the way across a field. The bullet only chipped my shell, but it spun me around and left me shaken. I don't know who they were or even why I was targeted. I played dead, and no one came for me. I laid in the tall grass for nine days. It rained on the fifth. I acquainted myself with the ants. They are survivors.

Day 36,725.

This world is dead, but life is threatening a return. I don't know when I'll ever fulfill my purpose, but I know what I am. I'm a ghost haunting the grave of humanity. A Ghost with a calling.
4129629253.text_zh:
第一天。

世界已死，但其死寂中有安宁。我出生在这个层层灰烬覆盖的好几公里荒芜道路上到处长着蒲公英的死亡世界里。

第六百七十三天。

这里有一片陆地，一条峡谷，有水曾经从这里流过。一条开凿在大地上的运河，上面布满了废弃的船只和无数的尸体。鲜花盛开在许多干枯的遗骸上。这个世界分解开的每个组成部分都有其使命：水会流动，城市会衰败，鲜花会盛开。然而我还在寻找我的使命。

 第1857天。

海洋是广阔而孤独的天地。其深处生命繁盛，然而我寻找的不是生命，而是让我茁壮的死亡。也许我的使命就在水底，但那里既黑暗又孤独，我…还不想去那里寻找。还有很多其它地方在等着我。 

第6231天。

我不够小心，被人开枪打了，对方从田野的另一头击中了我。虽然子弹只是擦破了我的外壳，但我却在冲击下转了个圈，让我心有余悸。我不知道对方是谁，甚至不知道自己为什么会成为目标。我装死了一阵子，却没有人过来。我在高草丛里躺了九天。第五天下了雨。我认识了许多蚂蚁。它们是求生能手。

第36725天。

这个世界已死，但生命随时可能归来。我不知道何时才能实现自己的使命，但我知道我是什么。我是一个在人类的坟墓中徘徊的机灵。一个有使命的机灵。

427899681.name: Red Death Reformed
427899681.subtitle: Vanguard policy still urges Guardians to destroy this weapon on sight.
427899681.subtitle_zh: 先锋政策依然敦促守护者一看到这种武器就将其摧毁。
427899681.text:
First is disassembly, taking extra caution for the well-honed bayonet. 

After disassembly comes cleaning. She gathers the swabs, the oils, the corrosive agents. 

Red Death clings to the grime of its past battles. She scrapes it with spinmetal wool for hours before the last signs of the skulls stenciled into the body finally vanish. 

The team had taken the butcher down before he'd added a mark for Ceto, Light of her Light. The weapon's tally is one short. 

Even reduced to pieces, the Red Death is a malevolent presence. It knows its purpose. It wants to continue its work. 

After cleaning comes purification.  

She reassembles the weapon and cradles it as though to fire. Her Light boils up, turning radiant.  

The flare of Solar Light is the advent of warmth after a cold night, the healing power of life itself. Wings spread high on her back and paint scorch marks along the ceiling. In her arms Red Death glows red, then yellow, then white. 

It fights the change. She does not let go. Its shadows burn away, one by one, until none are left. 

After purification comes dedication. 

Slowly, she lets go of her Light. Her wings flicker, then fade. And when Red Death is cold metal in her hands once more, a kernel of Solar Light lingers within. Its purpose made new. 

She will find those who would strip Guardians of their final life. She will bring them into the light. 

Not for revenge, but for justice.  

For Ceto.
427899681.text_zh:
首先要将其拆卸。要格外小心锐利的刺刀。 

拆卸之后要进行清理。她收集到了棉签、油和腐蚀剂。 

猩红死命身上残留着过去战斗留下的污垢。她用铁丝球刮了几个小时，才擦除了枪身上的骷髅图案。 

屠夫还没来得及在枪身上添加击杀赛托，她的光能之源的标记，就被队伍击败了。这件武器上缺了一个记录。 

即使化为碎片，猩红死命也是个邪恶的存在。它知道自己的使命。它想继续它的工作。 

清理过后是净化。  

她重新组装好武器，握在手中，仿佛是要射击。她的光能沸腾起来，焕光四射。  

烈日光能的耀斑预示着寒冷夜晚后的温暖。它是生命本身的治愈力量。她背上的翅膀高高张开，在天花板上留下焦痕。她怀中的猩红死命先是发出红光，然后是黄光，接着是白光。 

它在与变化抗争。她没有放手。它的影子一个接一个地被烧掉，直到一个不剩。 

净化之后是奉献。 

慢慢地，她放开了她的光能。她的翅膀先是闪烁，然后消逝。当猩红死命在她手中再次变成冰冷的金属时，烈日光能的核心已经留在其中了。它拥有了全新的使命。 

她会找到那些剥夺守护者最后生命的人。她将把他们带入光明。 

不是为了复仇，而是为了正义。  

为了赛托。

1681583613.name: Ergo Sum
1681583613.subtitle: Silent. Silent. Silent.
1681583613.text:
You are a child waking from a long and dreamless sleep. Is it still today, or have you slept into tomorrow (and tomorrow, and tomorrow, until the days buried you as much as the sand)? Gentle hands brush away the grains, but your voice is so soft that they cannot hear you over the sound of their own heartbeats. 

You are a moon. You feel heavy, so heavy, but to the stargazer you hang weightless in the sky. When the stargazers call out, you do not answer. They would give themselves up for you; abandon their own dreams to chase you. You love them too much to condemn them so. 

You are a lighthouse keeper. You are watching over a sleepy coastal village as the storm clouds roll in, and you are flashing the signal lantern, faster and faster and brighter and brighter, but they do nothing. You are trapped on an island, in a tower, signaling desperately that It is coming, and still they do not run. They are going to die—and if you do not run, you will die too. 

You are leaning out over the ocean. Sometimes the fish brush against your fingers and believe that they have felt the divine; sometimes the tide recedes, and the fish do not know you except by your absence. And today, you strive with all your might to reach the water, because It is here, the great dark shadow of the shark parting the water like a knife, and you cannot warn them, but you must. You must try. You cannot bear to lose even one more. 

You are carrying a tower of books. If you recited one title each second, you would not finish before the heat death of the universe. And every year, every day, every minute, Its hands add more to the pile. A man reaches for one of the books, for you, and you want so very badly to reach back, to take his hand and tell him that you must bear it just like he must, forever, the memory engraved in quartz—but your hands are full.  

You are a prisoner. The cage is so small that you can barely breathe. He screams at you to share your gift. You would not give it to anyone who thought of it so. It is a burden, a terrible weight that you have already asked too many to bear, to be crushed by. You could say all this, and more. You do not. 

You are reaching over a chasm, into which countless paths feed like arteries. You are trying to reach the people on the other side, but you cannot bridge the gap alone. You watch them turn, one after another, to walk down, down, down into the abyss, until It consumes them entirely. You are as surprised as anyone else when one of those wanderers comes back up the path, still reeking of decay, and reaches back to you.  

You are drowning. The water roils, dragging you down, and you are tired, so tired. The deep, dark ocean has gotten into your lungs, droplets of ink dispersing in silver blood. This time, you think, this time It has won. But when you look up, you see a figure diving toward you, fighting their way down through the suffocating waves, reaching out just like you've reached out to them, so many times before.  

You have so little strength left, but you do have it, that last gasp of air in your chest. You reach back—and in your hand is a sword.
1681583613.text_zh:
你是一个从漫长无梦的睡眠中醒来的孩子。此刻仍是今天，还是说你已经睡到了明天（明日复明日，直到日子像沙子一样把你埋葬）？温柔的双手拂去沙粒，但你的声音如此轻柔，以至他们在自己的心跳声中听不到你。 

你是月球。你觉得自己很重，很重，但对观星者来说，你就像失重一样悬在空中。当观星者呼唤你时，你没有回应。他们会为你牺牲自己；放弃自己的梦想去追逐你。你太爱他们，不忍心置他们于那样的境地。 

你是一名灯塔看守人。你守望着一个寂静的沿海村庄，风云滚滚而来，你用灯发信号，越来越快，越来越亮，但他们无动于衷。你被困在一座孤岛上的塔楼里，拼命发信号，告诉人们它就要来了，可他们还是不跑。他们会死的——如果你不跑，你也会死。 

你俯瞰着大海。有时鱼儿拂过你的手指，相信它们感受到了神性；有时，潮水退去，只有你的缺席才会让鱼儿注意到你。而今天，你正拼尽全力到达水边，因为它就在这里，鲨鱼的巨大黑影像匕首一样分开水，你无法传达警告，但你必须这样做。你必须试着去做。你不愿经历丧失，即使是一个都难以承受。 

你手里拿着一大堆书。就算你每秒钟背诵一个书名也无法在宇宙热寂之前念完。而每一年、每一天、每一分，它的双手都会添加更多的书到书堆。有一个人向其中一本伸出手，向你伸出手，而你也想伸出手，握住他的手，告诉他你必须承受这一切，就像他一样，直到永远，刻在石英上的记忆——但你的手已经满了。  

你是一个囚犯。笼子小得让你几乎无法呼吸。他尖叫着要你分享你的馈赠。你不会把它给任何一个那样想它的人。它是一种负担，一种可怕的重担，而你已经要求了太多的人去承受，被压垮。你可以说这些，以及更多。但你没有。 

你正在跨越一条鸿沟，无数条道路像动脉一样汇入其中。你试图联系另一边的人，但仅凭你一人之力无法弥合豁口。你看着他们转身，一个接着一个，不断向下走进深渊，直到它将他们全部吞噬。当其中一个漫游者从中归来，沿着路向上走，身上散发着腐败恶臭，朝你伸出手时，你和其他人一样惊异不已。  

你正在溺水。海水翻滚，拖着你往下沉，你累了，太累了。深不见底的海洋已经进入你的肺部，墨滴散落在银色的血液中。你想，这次它赢了。但当你抬头时，你看到一个身影正向你潜来，在令人窒息的海浪中奋力向下，伸着手，就像你曾经多次向他们伸出手一样。  

你只剩下一点力量，但你还有胸中的最后一口气。你伸出了手——而你握住的是一把刀剑。

2350330520.name: Sightline Survey
2350330520.subtitle: "Picking up a lot of Fallen chatter. And Cabal chatter. And Fallen-Cabal chatter. If I ever got beauty sleep, I would say they are interrupting it!" —Failsafe
2350330520.subtitle_zh: “收到了许多堕落者信号。还有卡巴尔信号。还有堕落者和卡巴尔之间的信号。如果说我会睡美容觉的话，那我已经被他们打扰到了！”——智能失效保险
2350330520.text:
Zidarrh crouches on the edge of the ridge, looking down over Nessus. There's a cave entrance down below he's keeping an eye on. It looks likely to contain more Vex than he wants to deal with today. 

Next to him, Legionary Yerg leans back against a boulder, screwing a pack into her armor's internal nutrition socket. 

Zidarrh turns up the flow on his Ether mask and breathes deep, eyes glowing brighter with each breath. 

He nudges Yerg's sizeable knee. "Got any snacks?" he asks, enunciating his Ulurant with care. 

Yerg makes an awful straw-sucking noise beneath her helmet. "You can't have any of my juice." 

He shakes his head in disgust but nudges Yerg again. She nudges back and Zidarrh's whole body rocks to the side.  

"What's with the new soldiers on your ship? The skinny ones with the sticks," he says. 

"I don't want to talk about it. They give me the creeps." 

"Well, yeah," Zidarrh affirms. Mindful of his allotment, he cranks his Ether intake down again and casts around for another topic. "So, uh, this planetoid, huh?" 

"Are you trying to ruin the one break I get all week?" 

"I'm making conversation! It's my break too." If Zidarrh wants to show off his language skills, he needs someone to show off to. 

Far below them, the remnants of a radiolarian lake bubble at the center as its levels continue to slowly recede. Zidarrh does not want to think about what might happen when it fully drains. More Vex, probably. 

Yerg takes a loud drink. "Planets shouldn't change. It's not right. We crushed up some of this place for the old emperor's wine and there was a Vex monster in it! Bad enough for a planet to have monsters. A planet shouldn't be the monster." Yerg hesitates. "And what if a few Legionaries tried a little wine back then? Just to make sure it was safe for our emperor? Was that monster wine?" 

On the whole, Zidarrh is relieved she didn't share her juice. He scans the horizon. 

Three Guardians on their fancy Pikes drive closer, heading for the draining lake. Yerg nudges Zidarrh hard enough to push him over. 

They wait in silence for the Guardians to enter the cave, one-eyed drones floating at their shoulders. 

"I'm revising my list of things I hate here. They're at the top," Zidarrh says. 

Yerg nods fervently. "I give up on this break. Let's get out of here. What's that thing Eliksni say… 'Security in numbers?'" 

"You got it," Zidarrh says. He does not correct her.
2350330520.text_zh:
齐达赫蹲在山脊边缘，俯视着涅索斯的风景。他正盯着下面的一个洞口。看起来里面的Vex可能比他今天愿意对付的要多。 

在他的一侧，军团士兵耶尔格背靠身旁的巨石，将一包东西拧入了护甲的内部营养插槽。 

齐达赫打开他乙太面罩上的供应，深吸了几口，眼睛随着每次呼吸而变得愈加明亮。 

他推了推耶尔格巨大的膝盖。“有零食吗？”他小心地用乌鲁兰语问道。 

耶尔格在她的头盔下发出了可怕的吮嘬声。“你不能喝我的汁水。” 

他厌恶地摇摇头，但又推了推耶尔格。她回推了一下，把齐达赫的整个身子掀到了一边。  

“你飞船上新来的士兵是怎么回事？那些拿着棍子的瘦子，”他问。 

“我不想谈这件事。他们让我浑身起鸡皮疙瘩。” 

“嗯，好吧，”齐达赫说。考虑到乙太配额，他再次减少乙太的摄入量，并谈起了另一个话题。“所以，呃，选了这颗小行星哈？” 

“你是想毁掉我这周唯一的休息时间吗？” 

“我只是想聊天！我今天也在休息。”如果齐达赫想炫耀他的语言能力，他就需要一个炫耀的对象。 

在他们的下方，一片残留的活性放射体液湖的中央正在冒着气泡。它的水位在持续缓慢下降。齐达赫不愿去想像它完全干涸后会发生什么。大概会出现更多的Vex吧。 

耶尔格狠狠地喝了一口。“这些行星不该改变。这是不对的。我们把这地方的一部分碾碎，用来酿老大帝的酒，结果里面有一只Vex怪！行星上有怪物就够糟了。行星不该是怪物。”耶尔格迟疑了。“要是当时有几个军团士兵尝了一点酒呢？为了确保大帝陛下的安全？看看会不会是怪物酒？” 

总的来说，齐达赫很庆幸她没分享她的汁水。他扫视着地平线。 

三名驾驶着漂亮派克的守护者在接近。他们要前往干涸的湖。耶尔格推了齐达赫一下，直接让他翻倒在地。 

他们静静等待着那些肩上飘浮着独眼无人机的守护者进入那个洞穴。 

“我要修改我在这里最讨厌的东西的清单。他们排在最前面，”齐达赫说。 

耶尔格使劲地点了下头。“我不休息了。我们快走吧。埃里克斯尼族有句话是怎么说的…人多才安全？” 

“说得对，”齐达赫没有纠正她。

3685470415.name: Veiled Threat
3685470415.subtitle: Don't let it hang over you.
3685470415.text:
"Thank you for speaking with me, Ghost," Saint said. The Exo was seated in the H.E.L.M., the Guardian's Ghost floating in front of him. 

"Anytime, Saint. What can I do to help?" 

Saint leaned back in his seat, considering. 

"You and the Guardian have seen those Vex with the rings around their necks," Saint continued, drawing a finger in a circle around his own neck. "'Yokes,' Osiris calls them." 

Ghost nodded. 

"They are tethered to… something. And it is making them act strangely. Not like Vex at all! We do not know if it is a new Mind, or something else. Whatever crashed on Nessus seems to be the cause." 

Ghost squinted, contracting his shell. Saint spoke carefully. 

"I wonder if it is the same as when the Witness spoke through you. Took control of you." 

Ghost looked away, his central eye darting back and forth. He hummed in thought. 

"I don't know. I wouldn't wish it on anyone, though. Not even the Vex! It was horrible." Ghost bobbed in emphasis, his shell shivering. Then he swayed sharply, as if shaking away the memory.  

"Did you speak with Osiris about it?" Saint-14 asked. "I imagine that you both share something in common in your individual experiences… him with Savathûn, and you with the Witness." 

Ghost shook his shell in a sign of "no." Saint looked at him quizzically.  

"I didn't want to bring up any bad memories for him," he admitted. "And it's hard to talk about." 

"I'm sorry," Saint said. "You are safe with us now." 

Ghost went quiet, contracting his shell flaps pensively as he looked down.  

"I know it will take time for you to feel safe again." 

Ghost nodded. When he spoke again, his voice was low, and the trill of his shell was softer. 

"When it was just my voice, that first time on Europa, it was scary. It made me feel like I couldn't trust myself. But when it happened again on Neptune, and then got so much worse with the Veil… I almost wished my Guardian had…" 

Saint was silent, listening intently. He gave a soft nod of encouragement. 

"Do you think what's happening on Nessus is the same thing?" Ghost said, concerned. 

"I hope not," Saint answered. He reached out and carefully patted Ghost on the edge of his shell. "But it is only the Vex! I am certain we have nothing to fear."
3685470415.text_zh:
“谢谢你和我说话，机灵，”圣人说道。这名Exo坐在应急后勤行动中心里，守护者的机灵在他的面前漂浮着。 

“不客气，圣人。我能做些什么来帮忙吗？” 

圣人靠在椅背上，思索着。 

“你和守护者都见过那些脖子上带光圈的Vex，”圣人继续说道，用手指在自己的脖子上画了一个圈。“奥斯里斯管它们叫‘枷锁'。” 

机灵点点头。 

“他们被拴在…什么东西上，所以他们的行为才变得很奇怪。一点也不像Vex！我们不知道那东西是个新思维，还是别的什么东西。涅索斯上坠毁的东西似乎就是原因所在。” 

机灵眯起眼睛，收缩着机壳。圣人小心翼翼地说道。 

“我不知道这和见证者通过你说话、控制你那时一不一样。” 

机灵把目光移开，中间的眼睛来回扫视。他沉思着发出嗡嗡声。 

“我不知道。但我不希望那种事发生在任何人身上。甚至包括Vex。那太可怕了。”机灵强调道，他上下摆动着，机壳颤颤巍巍的。然后他猛地摇晃了一下，仿佛要把这些记忆抖掉。  

“你跟奥斯里斯谈过这件事吗？”圣人14号问道。“我想你们俩的个人经历有一些共同之处…他是被萨瓦图恩操纵，而你则是被见证者控制。” 

机灵摇了摇机壳，表示“没有”。圣人疑惑地看着他。  

“我不想勾起他任何糟糕的回忆，”他坦言。“而且这话很难开口。” 

“对不起，”圣人说道。“你现在和我们在一起很安全。” 

机灵安静下来，低着头，焦虑地收缩着机壳盖。  

“我知道你还需要一点时间才能重新获得安全感。” 

机灵点了点头。他再次开口时，声音很低，机壳发出的颤声也更柔和。 

“在木卫二上第一次只有我的声音时，真的很可怕。让我觉得无法相信自己。而当它在海王星上再次发生时，然后面纱让情况变得更加糟糕…我有点希望我的守护者…“ 

圣人沉默不语，专注地听着。他轻轻点头以示继续。 

“你觉得在涅索斯上发生的是同样的事吗？”机灵关切地问道。 

“希望不是，”圣人回答道。他伸出手，小心翼翼地拍了拍机灵的机壳边缘。“但只有Vex受影响！我很肯定我们没什么好怕的。”

2126178511.name: Corrasion
2126178511.subtitle: Watch your step.
2126178511.text:
The Fallen scout skittered down into a newly formed crevice on the surface of Nessus, catching the rock face with his claws as he descended. New tunnels and cave systems had emerged in the wake of the anomaly's impact on the planet, and at Baron Kalliks's command, those caves had to be mapped and explored. 

The task fell to a Dreg. 

He scrambled down smooth tunnels and flung himself between floating outcroppings of rock, catching the stone and skidding to a halt above a yawning chasm. The deeper he descended, the more angular the stone became. Soon, he discovered a large open chamber swarming with Vex. The Dreg flattened himself against the side of the cavern and watched. 

A Minotaur, a dozen Harpies, and a handful of Goblins all worked together. The Minotaur raised its hand, and a coil of light sprung up between its mechanical fingers. He knew of the Vex's terraforming. He had never seen it firsthand. It frightened and awed him. The Vex raised large platforms and pillars of stone, materializing great discs of metal and lighting portals in white light. Crafting their world from the core of the planet. 

A series of staggered platforms materialized before the Dreg, angular and finely cut. Cautiously, the Dreg stepped onto one, hiding behind one of the newly made blocks of stone as he watched the Vex more closely. 

Remembering his mission, the Dreg turned and planted a beacon into a seam in the stone at his feet. The seam cracked, loosening a section of rock; the beacon clattered down a long drop into nothingness, hitting the sides of the cave as it fell. 

The Vex stopped. Slowly, one by one, they turned to face the source of the noise. 

The platform dissolved beneath the Dreg's feet in a shimmer of white and latticed light. Shrieking, he leapt from the platform and scrambled for the cavern wall.  The stone shuddered open behind him, sliding away, and he fell backwards into the newly formed gap.  

The Minotaur gestured again, and the Dreg scrambled to his feet just as the stone slab closed hard around him.
2126178511.text_zh:
堕落者斥候滑落到涅索斯地表一个新形成的裂缝中，下落时用爪子抓着岩壁。在异物撞击星球之后，出现了新的隧道和洞穴系统，卡里克斯公爵下令必须对这些洞穴进行测绘和探索。 

这项任务交给了一名堕落者士兵。 

他爬下光滑的隧道，纵身在露出水面的漂浮岩石间扑腾着，抓住石头，在一个大裂口上方打滑停了下来。他越往深处走，石头就越棱角分明。不久后，他发现了一间敞开的大房间，里面挤满了Vex。堕落者士兵趴在洞壁边上看着。 

一个米诺陶、十几个机甲女妖和几个哥布林合力工作着。米诺陶抬起手，机械手指间窜出一道光圈。他知道Vex正在进行土地改造。他从来没有亲眼目睹过。这一幕令他感到害怕和敬畏。Vex升起了硕大的平台和石柱，在白光中构成了巨大的金属圆盘和照明传送门。从星球核心开始着手打造他们的世界。 

堕落者士兵面前出现了一连串交错的平台，个个棱角分明、切割精细。他小心翼翼地走上其中一个，躲在一块新制成的石块后面，仔细观察着Vex。 

堕落者士兵想起了自己的任务，转身把一个信标插进了脚下石头的缝隙里。那缝隙随之裂开，一部分岩石松动掉落；信标跌入虚无，在下落过程中撞击着洞穴的两侧。 

Vex停了下来。他们一个接着一个慢慢地转向声音的来源。 

堕落者士兵脚下的平台在一抹白光和网格状的光线之中分解。他尖叫着，从平台上跳下，急忙攀向岩壁。他身后的石头颤抖着打开，滑向一边，而他向后摔倒在新形成的裂缝里。  

米诺陶又做起手势，石板在堕落者士兵慌忙爬起时紧紧地合拢了。

1058098236.name: Timeworn Wayfarer
1058098236.subtitle: Rest easy.
1058098236.text:
It wasn't Commander Zavala's favorite color, but the yarn was soft and made quick, even stitches as he clacked the knitting needles together.  

k to marker, k1p1 rib, m1r, k, m1l, p1k1 rib, k to marker. 

It had been some time since he had worked this pattern, long enough for the muscle memory to fade. Zavala had to concentrate until it could settle into his mind again. He squinted at the line of written direction. Raglan increases. Did he measure the gauge correctly? The ease may be too slack. The neckline looked worryingly wide. 

His thoughts were interrupted by a high-pitched, mechanical chirp and a flash of white light at the corner of his eye.  

Zavala furrowed his brow. The console at his side flashed again and emitted a string of data. 

He hesitated for a moment but didn't put his knitting down.  

"Ikora?" he called. The Warlock appeared on the holoprojector in a burst of visual noise.
