"Zavala," Ikora said warmly. "I see you've picked up your project again." 

"Indeed. I've just received an alert from Nessus—" 

"Saint and Failsafe are handling it." 

"Failsafe?" 

"Failsafe." 

The Vanguard Commander nervously coiled the strand of yarn around his forefinger. It went taut, pulled thin by the gesture. But then he loosened it, relaxing his grip on the needles. 

"Then I'll leave it in their capable hands. Or processor, as the case may be." 

"Good." 

Ikora's tone was chiding, but she smiled in the static. Zavala nodded.  

"Keep me updated," Ikora continued.  

"On what?" Zavala asked. The Warlock nodded to the knitting.  

"The status of my sweater." 

Zavala smiled. The hologram faded into air and silence. Zavala slid the working needle between his fingers and rested it against a callused knuckle.  

k to marker, k1p1 rib, m1r, k, m1l, p1k1 rib, k to marker. He let the pattern fill his thoughts again. Ikora would love this color.
1058098236.text_zh:
这不是指挥官萨瓦拉最喜欢的颜色，但纱线很柔软，在他捣鼓织针时可以快速、均匀地编织。  

编至记号圈，1针上下编，右斜加针，下针，左斜加针，1针下上编，编至记号圈。 

他已经有一段时间没有编过这种花样，久到肌肉记忆都快消失了。萨瓦拉必须集中精力，直到它能再次在脑海中显现。他眯着眼睛看着书面指示的那条线。拉克兰线加针。他测量的尺度对吗？可能有点太松了。领口看起来太宽了。 

他的思绪被一声尖锐的、机械的啾鸣声打断，眼角闪过一道白光。  

萨瓦拉蹙起眉。他身边的控制台又闪了一下，发出一串数据。 

他犹豫了片刻，但没有放下手里的毛线活儿。  

“艾可拉？”他叫道。那名术士随着一阵视觉杂讯出现在全息投影仪上。 

“萨瓦拉，”艾可拉热情地说。“看来你又重新捡起了你的项目。” 

“没错。我刚收到来自涅索斯的警报——” 

“圣人和智能失效保险正在处理。” 

“智能失效保险？” 

“智能失效保险。” 

先锋指挥官紧张地将纱线绕在食指上。纱线绷得很紧，被手势拉得纤细。但他随即松开，握着织针的手不再发力。 

“那我就把它交给有能力的人吧。或是处理器，比如这次。” 

“很好。” 

艾可拉的语气中带着责备，但她在视讯中露出了微笑。萨瓦拉点了点头。  

“随时告诉我最新情况，”艾可拉继续说道。  

“关于什么的？”萨瓦拉问道。术士对着针线活点了点头。  

“我的毛衣。” 

萨瓦拉笑了。全息影像消失在空气和寂静中。萨瓦拉让织针滑入指间，靠在长满老茧的指节上。  

编至记号圈，1针上下编，右斜加针，下针，左斜加针，1针下上编，编至记号圈。他让这个花样再次填满他的思绪。艾可拉会喜欢这个颜色的。

1886840007.name: Chronophage
1886840007.subtitle: It will always finish what it started.
1886840007.text:
"Banshee, my friend!" Saint-14 exclaimed with open arms. The gunsmith put down the weapon he was holding and turned to Saint. A strange look passed over his face before he nodded in recognition. 

"Saint," he said. "When did you get back?" 

"Ah," Saint replied. "Today. Was short trip from Nessus." 

"No, I mean…" Banshee said, then shook his head. "That's right. Nessus. Vanguard sending you there now?" 

"Yes," Saint said. "Come, come. Let us speak." 

The Titan beckoned the other Exo from behind his workstation, and together they walked towards the overlook, the City bright and shining beneath them. Saint leaned over the railing, deep in thought. 

"We were looking for an anomaly. It is waking up Nessus and making it change. Ikora is still investigating. Something is going on." 

Saint tapped his fist on the overlook railing. 

"And more! Vex behaving strangely. Radiolaria moving down through the planet. Is very bad. Ikora thinks it must be because of the anomaly." 

"You worried about the Vex?" Banshee asked. 

"Yes," Saint said, leaning forward, his voice dropping, "And it is not just the Vex. Radiolaria is in our heads, too, my Exo brother. Clarity, the Darkness, the Deep Stone Crypt. All of it is still part of us. If the Vex are acting strangely, who is to say what will happen?" 

"Well," Banshee said. "It's not like I'm going to Nessus." 

"No, I do not recommend it," Saint said with a small laugh. "It is no good for tourism! Even if Failsafe is very welcoming." 

"Failsafe?" 

"Ah, yes. Golden Age AI. Very chatty. I like her." 

"I remember now. Yeah. Cayde told me about her. I…" 

Banshee looked down, thinking. 

"Cayde's back, isn't he? Just like you." 

Saint shook his head. 

"No. Not like me." 

"Oh…"  

Banshee trailed off, eyes on the horizon. The Traveler was no longer there. He looked up to the sky, confused by the whorls of color he saw. Saint noticed his look of confusion, then followed Banshee's gaze. 

The Titan rested a comforting hand on Banshee's shoulder. 

"It's all right, Banshee," Saint said gently. "Take your time. We do not need to talk. It is pleasant to be here, looking out on the City with you. I think I will do it more often." 

Banshee shook his head and smiled. 

"Be careful out there, Saint," he said. "We need you."
1886840007.text_zh:
“班西，我的朋友！”圣人14号张开双臂喊道。枪匠放下手中的武器，转向圣人。他脸上掠过一种怪异的表情，然后点点头致意。 

“圣人，”他说道。“你什么时候回来的？” 

“啊，”圣人回答。“今天。刚从涅索斯的短途旅行回来。” 

“不，我是说…”班西说，然后摇了摇头。“没错。涅索斯。先锋这回派你去那了？” 

“是的，”圣人说道。“来，来。我们好好聊聊。” 

这名泰坦招手把班西从他的工作站后面叫了出来，他们一起朝着眺望台走去，圣城在他们底下灯烛辉煌。圣人靠在栏杆上，陷入沉思。 

“我们一直在寻找某种异常点。它在唤醒涅索斯，让它发生改变。艾可拉还在调查。一定发生了什么事。” 

圣人用拳头敲了敲眺望台的栏杆。 

“还有！Vex的行为很奇怪。活性放射体液在星球上到处流动。情况很糟。艾可拉认为一定是因为那个异常点。” 

“你担心Vex？”班西问道。 

“是的，”圣人说着，身子前倾，声音低沉下来，“而且不只是担心Vex。我们的脑袋里也有活性放射体液，Exo兄弟。明能、暗影、深岩墓室。这一切仍然是我们身上的一部分。如果Vex出现了怪异举动，谁知道还会发生什么呢？” 

“这个嘛，”班西说道。“反正我又不去涅索斯。” 

“对，我不推荐那样做，”圣人笑着说。“那里不适合旅游观光！尽管智能失效保险很好客。” 

“智能失效保险？” 

“啊，没错。黄金时代的人工智能。非常健谈。我喜欢她。” 

“我想起来了。对。凯德跟我说过她。我…” 

班西低着头，若有所思。 

“凯德回来了，是不是？就像你一样。” 

圣人摇了摇头。 

“不。和我不一样。” 

“哦…”  

班西声音渐弱，望着地平线远处。旅行者已经不在那里了。他抬头仰望天空，对眼前的色彩旋涡感到困惑。圣人注意到了他疑惑的神情，然后顺着班西的目光看去。 

泰坦安慰地把手放在班西的肩上。 

“没事的，班西，”圣人轻声说。“慢慢来。我们不必说话。能来这和你一起眺望圣城我很高兴。我想我会更经常这样做的。” 

班西摇摇头，笑了。 

“在外面要小心，圣人，”他说道。“我们需要你。”

2198166292.name: Aberrant Action
2198166292.subtitle: From thought to action, from threat to war.
2198166292.subtitle_zh: 思想引导行动，威胁化作战争。
2198166292.text:
Baron Kalliks looked down on Nessus from the command deck of his Ketch, watching with suspicion.  

"There is something down there," Kalliks said darkly. "The Vex respond to it. The entire planet responds to it." 

The Vandal at his side looked at him, expecting a command. Kalliks narrowed his eyes, then turned to the console beside him. 

He had heard the older Eliksni of his House speak of the "Great Machine," their voices full of hissed venom at its mention. Something had erupted from it, and House Dusk scavengers had seen the arc of light that trailed down to Nessus.  

How, then, to proceed? 

The Vanguard's comms were near-impenetrable, but the Eliksni had scraped one word from them: "anomaly." 

Kalliks drew one claw over the surface of the console's screen, over the strings of data flashing across it. Orbital changes. Seismic disturbances. And worse, a surge of Guardians crawling through the Vex tunnels, likely stealing vital information. That pathetic AI in its broken body of a ship had begun sending teams of those machine-spawn on tactical operations. It had jammed House comms and disrupted their scavenging, wasting lives and resources.  

The Eliksni Baron turned sharply. The Dregs behind him jumped to attention under his gaze, then bowed with their two remaining arms outstretched, clacking their mandibles nervously. 

"Ready the cages," Kalliks called out. "Arm the mines!" The Dregs scurried out of the room to obey his command. 

"What is your plan?" the Vandal at his side asked. Kalliks put one hand on the barrel of his scorch cannon. 

"Capture Vex, break apart their minds, and find out what they know. Look for the ones with rounded heads, or with the light around their necks. They'll have what we need. This thing, this 'anomaly'… We will find it first."
2198166292.text_zh:
卡里克斯公爵从他的双桅船指挥甲板上俯视着涅索斯，满脸猜疑地看着。  

“底下发生了些什么事，”卡里克斯阴沉地说道。“Vex对此做出了回应。整个星球都做出了回应。” 

他身边的暴徒看着他，等待他的命令。卡里克斯眯起眼睛，然后转向身边的控制台。 

他曾听过他氏族中年长的埃里克斯尼族说到过“大机器”，他们提起时声音里充满了不屑的恶意。有什么东西从里面喷发了出来，黄昏氏族的拾荒者们看到了一路拖曳到涅索斯上的光弧。  

那么，接下来怎么做？ 

先锋的通讯几乎无法理解，但这名埃里克斯尼族从中勉强拼凑出了一个词：“异常点”。 

卡里克斯用一只爪子划过屏幕，一串串数据在控制台屏幕上闪过。轨道变化。地震干扰。更糟糕的是，大量守护者爬过Vex隧道，很可能是在窃取重要信息。那艘残破飞船上可悲的人工智能已经开始派遣那些机器孽种小队进行战术行动。这干扰了氏族的通讯，打乱了他们的拾荒行动，浪费了生命和资源。  

埃里克斯尼族公爵猛地转过身来。他身后的堕落者士兵们在他的注视下迅速立正，然后伸出剩下的两只手臂鞠躬，下颚紧张地咔哒作响。 

“准备好笼子，”卡里克斯喊道。“安装地雷！”堕落者士兵们急忙窜出房间，执行他的命令。 

“你的计划是什么？”他身边的暴徒问道。卡里克斯把一只手放在他灼烧手炮的枪管上。 

“抓住Vex，击碎他们的思维，找出他们知道些什么。寻找那些圆脑袋的Vex，或者脖子上发光的Vex。他们会有我们需要的东西。这个玩意儿，这个‘异常点'…我们会抢先找到它的。”

1197771438.name: Lost Signal
1197771438.subtitle: "I think I've had a little too much peace and quiet." —Failsafe
1197771438.subtitle_zh: “我觉得我已经享受了太多安静平和的日子。”——智能失效保险
1197771438.text:
The fireteam had made headway into a deeper part of Nessus, following a cave system that had opened up after seismic disturbances hit that sector of the planet. Failsafe followed their progress, keeping track of their location via a local feed. She saw what they saw and heard what they heard. 

They were a stoic bunch, Failsafe thought to herself. Didn't talk much. She kinda liked that. But only kinda. She always felt as if she had to fill the silence. Was she annoying? Did she talk too much? Failsafe reviewed every fireteam feed she had ever recorded, running a thousand queries simultaneously, each one as useless as the last.  

Look at yourself, she said, pushing aside a barrage of query results that put strain on her processor. An AI with anxiety. Only the Golden Age could have produced something as ridiculous as that. 

"A large Vex force is amassing ahead," she said helpfully. The fireteam signaled an acknowledgement but said nothing. Another set of notifications and queries began processing, and she turned her attention to them, reviewing and dismissing each one individually.  

The fireteam should have engaged the Vex by now, she thought. But there was no audio. It had suddenly dropped to silence. 

Concerned, she tried to pull up a visual on the fireteam leader's location, but was met with a patchy network connection and the pitch-black interior of some long-forgotten cave. 

Losing connection to a feed felt like dropping a bowl of soup. That's the way she described it to Ikora, who had looked at her curiously before changing the subject. Failsafe had seen many bowls of soup dropped when her crew was alive. The cautious, careful adjustment as the soup gets too close to the lip of the bowl. A hissed expletive as a splash of hot soup hits skin. The involuntary jerk as the bowl tips over and crashes to the floor. Then no more soup. Just a spill that needed to be cleaned up. A smear of incomplete data in need of deletion. 

The soup was too close to the lip of the bowl. She adjusted her sensors, widened her parameters. Balanced the data stream. There was nothing. Just nothing.   

"Fireteam leader," she called out. "Please reestablish uplink to the H.E.L.M.!" 

 The visual feed stuttered. Waves of static dissolved into an empty, grey wall of noise. Panic. 

"Fireteam leader," Failsafe chirped. "Please respond!" 

There was no answer. She let the silence linger for too long. The connection was failing completely. She felt it hiss and spit. A power surge. Then it was over. Just a smear of data and a blank feed. 

"Hello?" The AI called into the empty feed, her voice small. No answer. Quietly, she retreated from the silence and the dark and back to the bright lights and familiar hum of the H.E.L.M.
1197771438.text_zh:
火力战队沿着一个洞穴系统进入了涅索斯的深处，这个洞穴系统是在星球那片区域受到地震干扰后打通的。智能失效保险跟随他们的进程，通过本地信号追踪他们的位置。她记录着他们的所见所闻。 

他们真是一群硬汉，智能失效保险心想。不怎么说话。她有点喜欢这样。但只是有点。她总是觉得自己似乎不得不打破沉寂。她是不是很烦人？她是不是话太多？智能失效保险查看了她记录的每一个火力战队信号，同时进行了上千次问询，每次都和上次一样徒劳无功。  

看看你自己吧，她说着，推开了给她的处理器带来压力的一连串查询结果。一个焦虑的人工智能。只有黄金时代才会制造出如此荒谬的东西。 

“前方有Vex大部队正在集结，”她热心地说道。火力战队发回收悉信号，但什么也没说。另一组通知和问询开始进行处理，她把注意力转移过去，逐一进行查阅和删除。  

火力战队现在应该已经在跟Vex交火了，她心想。但没有音频信号传来。那边突然静了下来。 

她焦急地试图调出火力战队队长所在位置的图像，但网络连接不太稳定，只看到某个被遗忘已久的山洞里漆黑一片。 

失去信号连接的感觉就像是洒落了碗汤。她是这样向艾可拉描述的，艾可拉当时好奇地看了她一眼，然后转移了话题。智能失效保险在她的船员们还活着的时候，目睹过许多碗汤洒落。汤太靠近碗口，要小心翼翼地调整。滚烫的汤汁溅到皮肤上，会发出不满的咒骂。碗翻倒落下，会不由自主地抖动。然后就没有汤了。只剩下洒出的水渍需要清理。剩下不完整的数据需要删除。 

汤离碗口太近了。她调整了传感器，扩大了参数。平衡了数据流。什么都没有。毫无回应。   

“火力战队队长，”她喊道。“请恢复与应急后勤行动中心的上行连接！” 

 视频信号断断续续。一波又一波的静电噪声消融在空荡、阴沉的噪音墙之中。惶恐。不安 。 

“火力战队队长，”智能失效保险叫道。“请回应！” 

没有人响应。她放任沉寂久久驻留。连接完全失效了。她感觉到它发出嘶声，然后噼啪作响。一阵能量浪涌。接着就结束了。只有一抹数据和空白的信号。 

“喂？”人工智能用微弱的声音对着空无一人的信号喊话。没有回应。她悄悄地从寂静和黑暗中退了出来，回到了应急后勤行动中心明亮的灯光和熟悉的嗡鸣声中。

4195186942.name: Faith-Keeper
4195186942.subtitle: Never falter, never break.
4195186942.text:
ACCESS: RESTRICTED
DECRYPTION KEY: 73XK5V2PG1$AUN-326
REP #: 18020-VIP-2029
AGENT(S): IKO-006
SUBJ: Eliksni Quarter VIPs 

1. We've intercepted an internal communication within the Eliksni Quarter between VIP #1889, the Spider, formerly known as the Baron of the Tangled Shore, and prior to that, Rakis of the House of Wolves, and VIP #4143, Eido, Scribe of the House of Light and adoptive daughter of VIP #3987, Mithrax, "Kell of Light." The conversation regards VIP #2029, Eramis the Shipstealer. 

2. This communication between #4143 and #1889 took place over an encrypted connection between a Botza District terminal and a personal datapad owned by #4143. It was not difficult to access. Security protocols should be reviewed and relayed to #3987 to avoid any future external data breach. 

3. Communication has been transcribed below. Background noise and nonverbal communication is described in annotations. 

SPI: Scribe. 
EID: Spider. 
SPI: Well, now that we've gotten the pleasantries out of the way… 

Note: Here the recording captures two seconds of muffled noise and an indistinct sound, possibly of several large, heavy objects dropped on a tile floor. 

EID: Now's not a good time. 
SPI: I don't care. I know what you're up to. You're not covering your tracks, and the Vanguard won't like you looking into Eramis's whereabouts. 

Note: Here the recording captures approximately three seconds of silence. 

EID: W-Well… I can't imagine the Vanguard would like what you're doing, either! Shall I tell them? 
SPI: Hah! Is this your first blackmail? Very sloppy, little Scribe. Come now, we're past this. You know I have your best interests at heart. 

Note: Here the recording captures one second of short, barked laughter from VIP #4143. 

EID: I don't believe—  
SPI: That's not my problem. Why are you looking for Eramis? I've told you she isn't listening. 
EID: Eramiskel has lost a great deal of support—  
SPI: Yes, yes. Her House is in shambles. What else? 
EID: I had hoped— 
SPI: This again? 
EID: I had HOPED— 
SPI: She's gone. For good this time. No House, no Witness. And from what I hear, even Xivu Arath has given up on her. 
EID: That's precisely why— 
SPI: Do you know your father talked to me about this obsession of yours? He wants this to stop, but he also knows you won't listen to him. 
EID: What? But she saved his life! 
SPI: And the debt is paid. Give up, Eido! It's pathetic. She doesn't care about you. She never has.

Note: Here the recording captures eleven seconds of high-pitched wheezes punctuated by a staccato clicking noise from VIP #4143. 

SPI: Don't—I didn't— 
EID: You might not see the good in people, but I do. And I will never give that up. I don't want to live in a world where no one can change, and nothing can get better. Eramis needs to know that, and I won't stop trying to tell her. 

Note: Here the recording captures two seconds of a rolling, filtered sigh from VIP #1889.  

Communication ceases. 

4. I advise continuing to monitor #4143's personal logs. Any unauthorized and unsupervised contact with House Salvation could have dire consequences. 

5. Additionally, I advise approaching EKS-443 for greater cultural context on Eliksni non-verbal communication. 

MESSAGE ENDS
4195186942.text_zh:
访问权限：受限
解码密钥：73XK5V2PG1$AUN-326
编号：18020-重要人物-2029
特工：IKO-006
主题：埃里克斯尼居住区重要人物 

1. 我们在埃里克斯尼居住区截获了一份内部通讯，通讯双方分别为1889号重要人物，蛛王，原纷争海岸公爵，在此之前为恶狼氏族的拉基斯；4143号重要人物，艾多，光能氏族文士，即3987号重要人物，“光能凯尔”米瑟拉克斯的养女。对话内容涉及2029号重要人物，窃船者伊拉莫斯。 

2. 4143号和1889号之间的通讯是通过柏特扎地区终端和4143号拥有的个人数据板之间的加密连接进行的。获取访问权限并不困难。应审查安全协议，并转告3987号，以避免今后发生任何外部数据泄露。 

3. 通讯内容抄录如下。背景噪音和非语言交流如注释中所述。 

蛛：文士。 
艾：蛛王。 
蛛：好了，既然我们已经寒暄过了… 

注：此处录音记录了两秒钟的闷响和模糊不清的声音，可能是几个大而重的物体掉落在瓷砖地板上的声响。 

艾：现在不是时候。 
蛛：我不在乎。我知道你想干什么，你没有掩盖你的行踪，而且先锋也不喜欢你调查伊拉莫斯的下落。 

注：此处录音记录了约三秒的沉默。 

艾：唔…我想先锋也不会喜欢你在干的事！要我告诉他们吗？ 
蛛：哈！这是你第一次勒索吗？太草率了，小文士。拜托，我们不至于这样。你知道我是为你好。 

注：此处录音记录了来自4143号重要人物的持续一秒的短促狂笑。 

艾：我不相信——  
蛛：那不是我的问题。你为什么要找伊拉莫斯？我告诉过你，她都没在听。 
艾：伊拉莫斯凯尔失去了大量的支持——  
蛛：没错，没错。她的氏族残破不堪。还有什么？ 
艾：我原本希望—— 
蛛：又来？ 
艾：我原本希望—— 
蛛：这次她永远地离开了。没有氏族，没有见证者。据我所知，就连希乌阿拉斯也放弃了她。 
艾：正因为—— 
蛛：你知道你父亲跟我说过你的这种偏执吗？他希望你停下，但他也知道你不会听他的。 
艾：什么？但她救了他的命！ 
蛛：而债已经两清了。放弃吧，艾多！真可悲。她根本不在乎你。她从来没在乎过。

注：此处录音记录了来自4143号重要人物的持续十一秒的高亢哼鸣，夹杂着断断续续的咔哒声。 

蛛：别——我没有—— 
艾：你可能看不到别人的优点，但我能。我绝不会放弃的。我不想生活在一个没人能改变，又日渐衰颓的世界里。伊拉莫斯得明白这一点，我也会一直努力告诉她。 

注：此处录音记录了来自1889号重要人物的持续两秒的起伏、滤过的叹息。  

通讯中止。 

4. 我建议继续监控4143号的个人日志。与救赎氏族进行的任何未经授权和监管的接触都可能招来严重后果。 

5. 此外，我建议联系EKS-443以获取更多有关埃里克斯尼族非语言通讯的文化背景。 

消息结束

3794274730.name: Ill Omen
3794274730.subtitle: Come what may.
3794274730.text:
The Witch.  

The Adherent.  

Eris Morn placed both cards down on her worktable, the illuminated faces gleaming under the sharp light of her lamp. 

The Deck of Whispers had not sat idle since her metamorphoses had concluded. The cards had been consulted occasionally by herself and others, each supplicant approaching with a question and leaving with a new perspective. For now, this was all the cards could provide. 

They no longer whispered to her since her vengeance had been satisfied. But Eris could still feel the push and pull of the Hive spells woven through their being. To any other practitioner, they would be no more than flat images, a hint at some deeper meaning. However, they were so intimately tied to her that she could still read them, even without her terrifying morph. 

Savathûn and Xivu Arath. Where had they fled to? What were they planning? The sisters were at odds once again, the natural bond of their love and logic restored. 

Eris placed a third card beside the others.  

The Harbinger.  

So, she still had a role to play in all this. She stared down at the image of herself, running an ungloved fingertip along its edge. 

They would come for her soon. 

For a fleeting moment, Eris remembered the shape of her own claws. The power of the Hive in her grip. And best of all, the terror, the fear, the heartbreak as Xivu Arath was removed from her throne. 

The feeling evaporated. The card faces stared up at her. The three of them united once again: Eris Morn, Savathûn, and Xivu Arath. The cards spoke of confrontation, but also sorority. Xivu Arath had called her sister. Was she still? 

One final card. 

Lament.  

The visage of Oryx, his Dreadnaught, his logic and his laws. That phantom with a shadow so long it lingered over them long after his death. 

She tensed for a moment, her eyes lingering over the card face before picking up each one and returning them to her deck.
3794274730.text_zh:
女巫。  

拥护者。  

埃里斯·摩恩把两张牌放在工作台上，装饰华丽的牌面在台灯锐利的光线下闪闪发光。 

自从她的变形结束后，这副低语卡组就没有被闲置过。她自己和其他人会不时地向这些卡牌请教，各个请求者都带着问题而来，带着新的视角而归。目前，这是它们所能提供的一切。 

自从她的复仇完成后，它们就不再对她低语。但埃里斯仍能感受到它们身上交织着邪魔族法术的推力和拉力。对于其他使用者来说，它们不过是平面的图像，某种深层含义的暗示。不过，它们与她息息相关，即使没有可怕的变形，她也能读懂它们。 

萨瓦图恩和希乌阿拉斯。她们逃到哪里去了？她们在计划着什么？姐妹俩再次陷入分歧，她们爱与守则的天然纽带又复原了。 

埃里斯把第三张牌放在其他牌的旁边。  

先知。  

所以，她在这一切中仍然扮演着某种角色。她低头凝视着自己的图像，用没戴手套的指尖沿着边缘拂过。 

她们很快就会来找她。 

有那么一瞬间，埃里斯想起了自己爪子的形状。一手在握的邪魔族力量。而且最棒的是，当希乌阿拉斯被赶下王座时的惊慌、恐惧和心碎。 

感觉消失了。牌面凝视着她。她们三人再次合而为一：埃里斯·摩恩、萨瓦图恩和希乌阿拉斯。牌面代表着冲突对抗，也代表着姐妹情谊。希乌阿拉斯曾经叫她姐妹。她还是吗？ 

最后一张牌。 

挽歌。  

欧里克斯的容貌，他的无畏战舰，他的守则和定律。那个幻象的阴影很长，在他死后还久久萦绕在他们心头。 

她紧张了片刻，目光在牌面上停留了一会儿，然后拿起每张牌，放回她的牌组里。

412251536.name: Speleologist
412251536.subtitle: "There is a Human phrase: Many hands make light work." —Eido, Scribe of House Light
412251536.subtitle_zh: “人类有句俗语：人多力量大。”——艾多，光能氏族文士
412251536.text:
"Saint-14? Osiris?" 

Eido approached the Titan and his partner in the Tower hangar, clutching a stack of datapads. Saint looked up, nodding at a group of Guardians as they left him. A flock of pigeons scattered as Eido approached. 

"I greet you in the Light," she said hurriedly. "And my father extends his greeting as well, though he could not accompany me at the present moment." 

"Greetings, Eido!" Saint said warmly. "What is it that I can do for you?" 

Eido cleared her throat, nodding as she reached for the speech she had rehearsed in her head. 

"I understand that you are sending fireteams to Nessus and have enlisted the help of a Golden Age AI named Failsafe. I have read Ikora Rey's reports, and—" 

"How did you gain access to Ikora's reports?" Osiris asked curiously. Eido gave a sheepish chuckle, but avoided the question. 

"I believe I have discovered a way to augment Failsafe's systems so that her scans of the Vex network yield more data. I am no Splicer, but if I can accompany the Guardians, I—" 

"Eido," Saint said gently. "Nessus is no place for civilians." 

Osiris was silent at this. Eido huffed. 

"I think I've proven myself more than capable," Eido said, though even as she spoke, she knew it was a creative interpretation of the truth. Her father could not be there to defend her, and expecting Eramis to return and protect her again was naïve. 

"I see the Drifter has put ideas into your head," Saint said, chuckling. But his laughter faded when he saw Eido's plain disappointment. 

"The Vex are a threat, young Eido," he said gently. "I cannot let my friend's daughter risk her life because she is bored." 

"I am not bored!" she said, indignant. "I only want to help." 

"You can help from the Tower and the Eliksni Quarter," Saint answered. 

"But—" 

"I cannot allow it," Saint said, his voice firm. Then Osiris put a hand on the Exo's shoulder. 

"Actually," Osiris said to the Eliksni, "I'd rather have you at the H.E.L.M., Scribe Eido. If your proposed augments can boost efficiency, you should discuss them with Failsafe as soon as possible." 

"Oh!" The Scribe hesitated, considering her options. "I… suppose that could be sufficient." 

There was a moment of silence as Eido looked away, choosing her next words carefully. 

"Is Failsafe… nice?" Eido asked. "I've heard, ah… contradictory information." 

Saint hummed in thought as he also searched for the right words. 

"Yes… and no." 

Eido looked at him quizzically. Saint shrugged his shoulders. 

"Ah, you will see for yourself," he said.
412251536.text_zh:
“奥斯里斯？圣人14号？” 

艾多抱着一叠数据板走近高塔机库中的泰坦和他的伙伴。圣人抬起头，向开始离去的一群守护者点头示意。艾多走近时，一群鸽子四散飞去。 

“我在光能之下问候你，”她急忙说道。“我父亲也让我代为问好，虽然他现在没法陪我过来。” 

“你好，艾多！”圣人热情地说。“我可以帮到你什么吗？” 

艾多清了清嗓子，一边点头，一边说出在脑海里排练过的陈词。 

“我知道你正在向涅索斯派遣火力战队，还得到了一个名为智能失效保险的黄金时代人工智能的帮助。我读了艾可拉·蕾伊的报告，而且——” 

“你是怎么拿到艾可拉的报告的？”奥斯里斯好奇地问道。艾多窘迫地笑了一声，但避开了这个问题。 

“我想我已经找到了一种方法来增强智能失效保险的系统，能让她对Vex网络的扫描生成更多的数据。我不是熔岩军团，但如果我能陪着守护者，我——” 

“艾多，”圣人轻声说道。“涅索斯不是平民该去的地方。” 

奥斯里斯对此沉默不语。艾多哼了一声。 

“我认为我已经证明了自己的能力，”艾多说，尽管她一说出口，就知道这是对真相的创意解读。她的父亲不能在那里保护她，而指望伊拉莫斯再次回来保护她的想法再天真不过了。 

“看来是浪客给你灌输了一些想法，”圣人笑着说道。但当他看到艾多显露无疑的失望时，他的笑声消失了。 

“Vex是个威胁，小艾多，”他温柔地说。“我不能让我朋友的女儿因为无聊而去冒生命危险。” 

“我不无聊！”她忿忿不平地说。“我只是想帮忙。” 

“你可以在高塔和埃里克斯尼居住区帮忙，”圣人回答。 

“可是——” 

“我不同意，”圣人说道，声音很坚定。然后奥斯里斯把一只手搭在这位Exo的肩上。 

“其实，”奥斯里斯对这位埃里克斯尼族说道，“我觉得你待在应急后勤行动中心比较好，文士艾多。如果你提出的强化可以提高效率，你应该尽快和智能失效保险讨论一下。” 

“哦！”文士犹豫着，思忖着她的选择。“我想…这样也行。” 

艾多看向别处，沉默了一会儿，仔细选择接下来的措辞。 

“智能失效保险…友善吗？”艾多问道。“我听说了些，啊…相互矛盾的说法。” 

圣人若有所思地哼了一声，也在搜寻着合适的措辞。 

“既友善…也不友善。” 

艾多疑惑地看着他。圣人耸了耸肩。 

“啊，到时候你就知道了，”他说道。

3276304504.name: Perfect Pitch
3276304504.subtitle: Raise your voice and sing.
3276304504.text:
"The Veil." 

It names itself, as the Human mind named itself, with the weight and presence of sound on the lips, translated into a form that you can physically comprehend. Encompass. Envelop.  

A touch of teeth and tongue. 

A vibration of an eardrum. 

Air moving through a chest cavity. 

A taste of breath. 

More than that. Not nearly as much as that. 

That was the beginning. 

"Be known." 

This is next: you see the whorl and weft, the place where it joins itself in one smooth, unbroken surface of light. 

Make an incision, and from the wound of light will pour forth colors you have never seen. You are pigment, the pigment closest to those colors.  

"Be seen." 

Wet matter set against that light, the light that determines what color you are. 

But each color is a note, and each note is a mind. You are a choir. A chorus. You open your mouth to join it, and you are flooded with the taste of color, with the taste of sound.  

The sound and color that you are, translated. A means for you to understand. 

"Be heard." 

You raise your hand and hold it steady.
3276304504.text_zh:
“面纱。” 

它为自己命名，就像人类思维为自己命名一样，用嘴唇发出的声音的分量和存在感，转化为你可以实际理解的形式。环绕。包围。  

牙齿和舌头的触感。 

鼓膜的振动。 

穿过胸腔的空气。 

呼吸的味道。 

不止是那样。那还远远不够。 

那只是开始。 

“被知晓。” 

接下来是这一幕：你看到了螺纹和纬线，它在平滑无瑕的光面上的连接处。 

开一个切口，光的伤处会涌出你从未见过的颜色。你就是颜料，最接近那些颜色的颜料。  

“被看到。” 

潮湿的物质映在那道光上，那道决定了你是什么颜色的光。 

但每种颜色都是一个音符，每个音符都是一个思维。你是一个合唱。一首副歌。你开口加入其中，你被颜色的味道和声音的味道所淹没。  

是为你的声音和颜色，经过转化。一种让你理解的方式。 

“被听见。” 

你抬起手，稳稳地举着。

4209476803.name: Khvostov 7G-0X
4209476803.subtitle: "You don't know how long I've been looking for you."
4209476803.text:
Day 1.

The world is dead, but there's peace in the mortuary silence. I'm born into this dead world, where dandelions grow up through layers of ash blanketing miles of desolate road.

Day 673.

There is a stretch of land, a canyon through which water once flowed. A canal cut into the earth, bristling with derelict ships and countless dead. Flowers bloom in many desiccated carcasses. Each component of this world's decomposition has a purpose: water flows, cities decay, flowers bloom. Yet still I search for mine.

 Day 1,857.

Oceans are vast, lonely expanses. Though life flourishes in the depths, it's not life that I'm looking for. I thrive on death—search for death. Perhaps my purpose lies below the water, but it's dark, and lonely, and I… I don't want to look there yet. Not when there's so much more horizon.

Day 6,231.

I was careless, and someone shot me from all the way across a field. The bullet only chipped my shell, but it spun me around and left me shaken. I don't know who they were or even why I was targeted. I played dead, and no one came for me. I laid in the tall grass for nine days. It rained on the fifth. I acquainted myself with the ants. They are survivors.

Day 36,725.

This world is dead, but life is threatening a return. I don't know when I'll ever fulfill my purpose, but I know what I am. I'm a ghost haunting the grave of humanity. A Ghost with a calling.
4209476803.text_zh:
第1天。

世界已死，但其死寂中有安宁。我出生在这个被层层灰烬覆盖的几公里荒芜道路上长满蒲公英的死亡世界里。

第673天。

这里有一片陆地，一条峡谷，有水曾经从这里流过。一条开凿在大地上的运河，上面布满了废弃的船只和无数的尸体。鲜花盛开在许多干枯的遗骸上。这个世界分解开的每个组成部分都有其使命：水会流动，城市会衰败，鲜花会盛开。然而我还在寻找我的使命。

 第1857天。

海洋是广阔而孤独的天地。其深处生命繁盛，然而我寻找的不是生命，而是让我茁壮的死亡。也许我的使命就在水底，但那里既黑暗又孤独，我…还不想去那里寻找。还有很多其它地方在等着我。

第6231天。

我不够小心，被人开枪打了，对方从田野的另一头击中了我。虽然子弹只是擦破了我的外壳，但我却在冲击下转了个圈，让我心有余悸。我不知道对方是谁，甚至不知道自己为什么会成为目标。我装死了一阵子，却没有人过来。我在高草丛里躺了九天。第五天下了雨。我认识了许多蚂蚁。它们是求生能手。

第36725天。

这个世界已死，但生命随时可能归来。我不知道何时才能实现自己的使命，但我知道我是什么。我是一个在人类的坟墓中徘徊的机灵。一个有使命的机灵。

1801007332.name: No Hesitation
1801007332.subtitle: "He is the closest thing I will ever have to a son."
1801007332.subtitle_zh: “他对我来说是最接近儿子的人。”
1801007332.text:
Aboard Empress Caiatl's flagship, the Eligos Lex V, there is a community space of colorful cloth banners and solemn silence contained within a repurposed hangar bay. At the center of this area is a chunk of land harvested from a royal garden: a piece of the Cabal homeworld excised in haste on the day that Torobatl fell. Three gnarled trees, a bed of moss, spotted with tall grasses.

"We're initiating Operation Ahamkara."

As Commander Zavala's voice booms over comms, Empress Caiatl rises from the moss and lumbers past gnarled wood, her meditation cut short. She is quick to descend the rocky stairs carved into the side of her fragmented world, past numerous handwritten messages from her people bound to twisting roots protruding from the soil, messages to those who were left behind. Pleas for forgiveness. Promises of revenge.

"Empress." There is a palpable tension in Valus Forge's voice as he hurries into the hangar, breezing past Caiatl's tusked honor guard as he does.

"I heard," Caiatl replies. "We ready our fleet for the signal to depart. As Valus, you will lead our ships into the breach the moment the commander gives the all clear."

Saladin Forge hesitates. His gaze drifts down, and Caiatl sees a foreign moment of vulnerability in him. For a moment, Saladin hears doors slamming shut. Sees Lady Jolder's face consumed by fire. Caiatl stops beside Saladin, facing away, shoulder to shoulder. For a moment, she, too, hesitates. Her massive hand gently taps his shoulder.

"I let him leave again."

Caiatl feels the weight in Saladin's voice. The specter of Zavala's past haunts this moment beyond the nightmares on the Leviathan.

"I wasn't there for him when Hakim died," Saladin adds quietly. Caiatl watches him as he speaks his truth, looks into his eyes, sees him. She understands.

"Zavala held on to that guilt like a bleeding wound," she offers. "If he should fall, do not repeat his mistakes. It will not be guilt for you. It will be a battle standard you hold aloft for the universe to see."

Saladin's gaze does not waver from Caiatl's. She sees him. "I don't want that day to come."

"I know."
1801007332.text_zh:
在女帝查厄托的旗舰伊犁苟斯·莱克斯五号上，有一个机库被饰以五颜六色的旌旗，改造成了一个庄严肃穆的社区空间。其中心是一大块从某个皇家花园中取来的土地：一块卡巴尔在图罗巴特尔沦陷之日带走的家乡故土：三棵扭曲的树，一窝苔藓，点缀着高高的草丛。

“我们将开始阿罕卡拉行动。”

随着指挥官萨瓦拉的嗓音在通讯器中响起，女帝查厄托从苔藓上站了起来，吃力地走过扭曲的树干。她的冥想被打断了。她快速走下刻在她支离破碎的世界一侧的石阶，走过绑在从土壤中伸出的扭曲树根上，她的族人给滞留者写下的诸多信息。宽恕的恳求。复仇的承诺。

“女帝。”军政官弗吉匆匆走过查厄托的长角仪仗兵，进入了机库。他的声音有些紧绷。

“我已经听说了，”查厄托回答道。“让舰队做好准备，等待出发信号。作为军政官，你要在指挥官发出指示后率领我们的战舰突入。”

萨拉丁·弗吉犹豫了。他的目光垂了下来，而查厄托在他身上看到了异样的脆弱。在那瞬间，萨拉丁听到了门被猛然关上的声音。看到了被火焰包围的欧德夫人的脸庞。查厄托背对着萨拉丁停了下来，两人肩并着肩。她也犹豫了片刻。她的大手轻轻拍了拍他的肩膀。

“我又让他离开了。”

查厄托从萨拉丁的声音中察觉到了沉重感。萨瓦拉过往的幽灵在利维坦的梦魇消失许久后还在困扰着他。

“哈基姆死时，我不在他身边，”萨拉丁低声补充道。查厄托望着他说出真相，凝视他的眼睛，看到了他。她明白。

“那愧疚对萨瓦拉来说就像是流血的伤口，”她安慰道。“如果他倒下了，不要重蹈他的覆辙。那不会是属于你的愧疚。那是一面你应该高举过头，让全宇宙都看见的战旗。”

萨拉丁和查厄托注视着对方的眼睛。她看到了他。“我不希望有那一天。”

“我知道。”

3867373351.name: Axial Lacuna
3867373351.subtitle: Archaeologists understand: a buried hatchet is still, after all, a hatchet.
3867373351.subtitle_zh: 考古学家们明白：埋在地下的斧头说到底还是斧头。
3867373351.text:
For years—61 years and either 23 or 19 days, depending on who you ask—Ikora and I did not speak to each other. Now we do. But I don't think we'll ever talk about it. 

There is little purpose in doing so, in any case. I raised Ikora from dust and bone, and ever since approximately 0.734 seconds after that first brush of Light, I have known the type of person she is, and the type of Ghost I am to her. 

We fit. We are both, in our ways, stubborn. I might have broken the standoff just as well as she, and I chose not to. Ikora began the silence; it was correct that she end it. What purpose is there in the post-mortem, in hashing out what went awry and who should have said what and when? 

When I dissect should-have-dones, it is only for the benefit of after-action reports, for young Hidden and New Lights first learning to weigh risks and make quick decisions on which lives rest. Ikora and I both already know where any misstep was. Our understanding is deeper even than friendship. 

So too is it with this. We did not speak, and then we spoke, and it is not as it was. It is something new, although we are something old. There is a hole at the center, not to be touched or defined. 

Ikora understands this, too. We picked up, and carried on, and that was enough. I do not envy other Ghosts their Guardians, and I would not be so fitted a Ghost to any other. Someday, that gap will be smaller than what has grown around it. 

And so far as everyone else is concerned, there is no fault line, no sign of fracture. A united front, in our position, is more valuable than a deep emotional honesty. 

We were friends, once.
3867373351.text_zh:
许多年来——61年，23天或19天，根据你问的人而不同——我没和艾可拉说过一句话。现在我们又开始交流了。但我认为我们永远不会谈论这件事。 

无论如何，这样做都没有什么意义。我让艾可拉从一堆尘土和骨头中重生，自她第一次与光能接触大约0.734秒后，我就知道了她是什么样的人，我对她来说是什么样的机灵。 

我们很般配。我们都很固执。我和她一样，随时都可以打破这个僵局，但我选择不这样做。艾可拉开始了这场沉默，所以理应由她来结束。当事后诸葛亮，找哪里出了问题，谁应该在什么时候说些什么，又有什么意义？ 

我剖析本该做的事情，只是为了在行动报告中总结出经验，也是为了让年轻的隐秘者和新曙光学会权衡风险，迅速做出事关性命的决定。艾可拉和我都已经知道是哪里出了差错。我们对彼此的了解甚至比友谊还要深。 

这件事也是一样。我们有段时间不说话，然后开了口，发现与过去不同。这是一段新的关系，虽然我们已经是老相识了。正中有不可触及或定义的一个缺口。 

艾可拉也明白这个。我们重拾过往，继续前进，这就够了。我不嫉妒其他守护者的机灵，而我也再不会遇到第二个如此合适我的人。总有一天，那个缺口会因周围集聚的一切而显得渺小。 

在其他人眼里，没有断层线，没有分裂的迹象。对我们来说，一条统一的战线比交心谈话更具价值。 

我们曾经是朋友。

496728945.name: Bold Endings
496728945.subtitle: If you have any say in how you go out—make it bold.
496728945.subtitle_zh: 如果你能决定自己的死法，那就大胆一点。
496728945.text:
All they had left of Andal Brask was his cloak. Shiro-4 rubbed the fabric between his fingers and wished he still had skin to feel its texture.  

"Do you remember what it was like?" he asked Cayde-6. "Touching things with Human hands?" 

"Your hands are Human," Cayde answered in a low voice, as if grinding out the words through teeth he also did not have. That was the last he and Shiro spoke of being Exos for a long time. 

They reminisced instead about the man who had just died his final death. Remembered the triumphant sound of his laugh. Calculated his gambling debts and who among his friends would pay them. Fantasized about whether or not he kept a secret lover in the City, and what that person might be like. 

"Andal wasn't the type to keep secrets of the heart," Shiro said. "You know that. He lived boldly, loved boldly." 

Cayde raised his bottle. "Died boldly." 

Shiro drank to that, saying nothing of what they could or could not taste—or whether they could or could not get drunk. But when Cayde wrapped Andal's cloak around himself, Shiro at least knew it wasn't because he was cold. 

Shiro grinned. "Looks good on you." 

"It better, because it ain't ever coming off."
496728945.text_zh:
安达尔·布莱斯克留下的只有他的披风。白-4用手指捏着布料，寻思自己如果还有能感受质地的皮肤就好了。  

“你还记得那种感觉吗？”他问凯德6号。“用人类的手摸东西的感觉？” 

“你的手就是人类的手，”凯德低声回答道，这话仿佛是从他所没有的牙缝之间挤出来的。白和他在随后很长一段时间里都再没谈过身为Exo的话题。 

他们转而开始回忆那个刚刚迎来最终死亡的男人。忆起他胜利的笑声。计算他欠下的赌债，以及会是他的哪位朋友来还。幻想着他在圣城里是否藏着一个秘密情人，以及那人会是什么样。 

“安达尔不是那种心里藏着秘密的人，”白-4说。“你知道的。他活得无畏，爱得也无畏。” 

凯德举起了手中的酒杯。“死得更无畏。” 

白-4和他干了一杯，没提起Exo能不能尝到滋味——以及Exo会不会醉。但当凯德把安达尔的披风裹在身上时，白-4至少知道他这么做不是因为冷。 

白-4笑了。“很适合你。” 

“适合就好，因为我不打算脱下来了。”

3605603507.name: Pro Memoria
3605603507.subtitle: "I'm with you, old man. Whether you like it or not."
3605603507.subtitle_zh: “我支持你，老家伙。不管你喜不喜欢。”
3605603507.text:
Targe looked up at the sky above, a swirl of stars encircling the Traveler. They seemed so remote and untouchable, despite the pine trees stretching up in jagged spikes towards them. They, at least, were touchable. He let out a sigh. He had taken to doing so not because he breathed, but because his Guardian used it as a blanket emotional response. Sometimes the tics of loved ones stick like pine sap. It drips off the tree and onto an unsuspecting shell… dust settles in, and nothing can quite clean it off again. Always sticky. 

He heard the muffled voices from inside the cabin.  

Targe's thoughts wandered back to the gun. The moment stretched on for an eternity. He would have sacrificed everything to give Zavala what he asked for. He would have taken a thousand bullets; he would have gladly met his end if it meant the boy could live again.  

"Why not?" he asked, looking up at the Traveler. "You make the rules. I'm here for him. I'd do anything for him. Why am I powerless?" 

There was, as always, no answer. 

*** 

Many, many lifetimes later, Targe looked up at the sky above, at a swirl of stars that were not stars, clouds that were not clouds. Something was missing. He almost chuckled at the thought of the Traveler having a smaller Traveler hanging somewhere up there in its made-up atmosphere. It seemed like an oversight. 

He heard the campfire crackle as somber yet hopeful voices behind him shared their triumphs and pains. If anything inside the Traveler was real, it was in those voices, the bonds of tender love, infinite longing, and fierce loyalty radiating more intense warmth than the campfire itself. 

He sighed. Even here, the trees dripped sap.
3605603507.text_zh:
塔格望向头顶的天空，有许多星星正围着旅行者。它们显得异常遥远，难以触及，尽管松树参差不齐地朝着它们伸展。至少这些松树是能够触及的。他发出一声叹息。他之所以习惯这样做并不是因为他会呼吸，而是因为他的守护者把叹息当做既定的情绪反应。有时，我们爱着的人的习惯会像松树树脂那样黏附着。它从树上滴下来，落在毫无防备的鞘翅上…附上的尘埃再也洗不掉。永远黏着。 

他听见室内传来了沉闷的声音。  

塔格的思绪又回到了那杆枪上。在那近乎永恒的一刻。他愿意牺牲一切来满足萨瓦拉的愿望。他愿意挨上一千发子弹；如果他能让那个孩子重获新生，他愿意结束自己的生命。  

“为什么不呢？”他看着旅行者发问。“你制订了规则。我在他身边支持他，我愿意为他付出一切。为什么我无能为力？” 

一如既往，他没有得到回答。 

*** 

许多世代后，塔格仰望着头顶的天空，那里有不是星星的星星，以及不是云彩的云彩。缺了什么。想到旅行者的上方有一个更小的旅行者悬在它造就的大气层中，他几乎笑出了声。那像是一个疏漏。 

他听到篝火在噼啪作响，身后传来阴郁但充满希望的声音，分享着成就和痛苦。如果说旅行者的内部有什么是真实的，那肯定是在那些声音当中，远超篝火本身暖度的温柔爱意、无限憧憬和强烈忠诚。 

他叹了口气。即使是这里的树也会滴落树脂。

3232203524.name: Someday
3232203524.subtitle: Who you are is not who you will always be.
3232203524.subtitle_zh: 你未必永远都是现在的样子。
3232203524.text:
During the Dark Age, survivors sat vigil over the dead. Many would fashion stone circles in the shape of the Traveler and laid their loved ones at the center, waiting prostrate for Ghosts that never came. When it was time to move forward, the living stacked those same stones atop the dead. Dirtied hands tied messages to each grave's marker—tattered epitaphs of devotion, bravery, and sacrifice abandoned to twist mournfully in the breeze. 

REFUSED MEDICINE SO OTHERS COULD LIVE 

KNEW ABOUT THE MINEFIELD, INSISTED ON CROSSING FIRST 

ONLY 16 – HE LIVED A BOY, BUT DIED A MAN PROTECTNG HIS FAMILY FROM THE FALLEN 

Lakshmi-2 had read too many such elegies to remember them all, but the ones she had written stayed with her. There was the father who went back for his children, only for all three to be crushed underfoot by a Walker that didn't even see them. The old woman captured by the House of Devils, tortured, then shot dead when she refused to reveal the location of her settlement. The child that starved to death before given the opportunity to accomplish anything, but whose mother insisted that Lakshmi at least try. 

"Please," she'd said, "you're better with words." 

And so, Lakshmi wrote: A CHILD SLEEPS HERE, LEAVING HER MOTHER ONLY WITH HOPE SHE MIGHT SOMEDAY WAKE  

Hundreds of years after she had positioned the last stone atop the infant's grave, in her final moments of life, Lakshmi wondered if the Vex would leave enough of her to bury, and what—if anything—would be written on her behalf. 

She would have never expected an Eliksni called Namrask to request visitation with her crumpled remains. She would have laughed, incredulous to learn that he sat by her side for hours in contemplative silence. 

Finally, he said, "I wish we could have both been better people." 

And maybe Lakshmi someday would have been, had she known that he'd close her eyes with the tips of his fingers and weep.
3232203524.text_zh:
在黑暗纪元，幸存者们会为逝者守夜。许多人将石头围成旅行者的形状，将自己的亲人安放在中心，拜倒在地，等待永远不会出现的机灵。等到心灰意冷的时候，活着的人会把这些石头堆到死者身上。他们沾满污垢的手会将一些信息绑在每一块墓碑上——那些关于奉献、勇敢和牺牲的破烂挽歌被遗弃在微风中，哀伤地扭曲着。 

此人拒绝服药，让他人得以生存 

明知有雷区，却坚持自己先过 

年仅16岁——身为男孩，却为保护家人不受堕落者伤害，作为男子汉死去 

拉克希米-2读过太多这样的挽歌，无法全部记住，但她自己写下的那些仍然历历在目。有位父亲回去救他的孩子，结果三人都被地行者踩死，而后者甚至根本没注意到他们。有个被恶魔氏族抓走的老妇人遭到严刑拷打，拒绝透露定居点的位置而被枪杀。有个没机会体验人生就被饿死的孩子…她的母亲坚持让拉克希米试着写段挽歌。 

“求你了，”她说，“你更善于言辞。” 

于是，拉克希米这样写道：一个孩子沉眠在这里，只留给她母亲一个希望，即她有一天能醒来。  

为这个婴儿之墓放上最后一块石头的几百年后，在临死之前，拉克希米想知道Vex是否会给自己留下足够的遗骸来埋葬，谁又会为她写下些什么。 

她从未料到会有一个名叫拿姆拉斯克的埃里克斯尼族要求探视她扭曲的遗体。要是她知道他在她身边沉静地坐了几个小时，一定会觉得难以置信地笑起来。 

最后，他说，“我希望我们以前都是更好的人。” 

如果那时候她知道他会用指尖合上她的眼皮，并在她遗体前落泪，也许拉克希米真的会实现这个愿望。

3947966653.name: The Call
3947966653.subtitle: "We go together."
3947966653.text:
A wheezy blast of smoke vents out of the Gray Pigeon's engines. Its thrusters wind down, failing to initialize.

"When was the last time you had this rust bucket serviced?" Osiris wonders aloud, running a hand along the pockmarked side of the jumpship. "Better yet, when was the last time you even flew it?"

Saint-14 shouts indistinctly from the cockpit. Hammering follows, and then another weary whine from the engines before a dusty blast of smoke sputters from the exhaust. Osiris makes a soft sound in the back of his throat and ducks under one of the wings.

"Don't," Saint blurts out as he emerges from the cockpit, stopping Osiris before he can set foot on the stairs.

"You need a new ship."

"I say 'don't' and still you criticize," Saint grumbles, lumbering down the steps. "She is a good bird, flies well. It has just been a little while. She is… sleepy."

Osiris swipes a finger along the hydraulics. "She certainly is," he quips while Saint glowers tenderly from nearby. "Didn't you have Miss Holliday—" He stops and lowers his gaze. "Ah, yes…"

"I am not one to easily trust another's hands," Saint says as he approaches Osiris, lacing their fingers together. "And… I have not had time to maintain the ship myself." Osiris leans into the touch and presses his free hand to Saint's breastplate. "But I have to be ready to answer Zavala's call when the time comes."

Osiris shakes his head, looking up into Saint's eyes. "We answer that call together. I will not leave you aside to wander off into another dimension without me again." His hand at Saint's chest curls into a fist. "Never again."

Saint wants to fight, but it is one battle he knows he will not win. Instead, he lifts the hand he holds to his mouth and presses a kiss to Osiris's knuckles.

"Never again."
3947966653.text_zh:
灰鸽的引擎冒出一阵阵烟雾。推进器的动力减弱，无法启动。

“你上次维修这锈桶是什么时候？”奥斯里斯一边抚摸着这艘跃迁飞船布满锈点的侧面，一边大声问道。“我更该问你上次驾驶它是什么时候吧？”

圣人14号在驾驶舱里模糊不清地喊着。紧接着是一阵敲击声，还有引擎发出的另一阵疲惫的轰鸣声，然后一股充满尘埃的烟雾从排气管喷了出来。奥斯里斯轻柔地咳了一声，屈身到机翼下。

“什么也别说，”圣人从驾驶舱里探出头大声嚷嚷，在奥斯里斯踏上梯子之前拦住了他。

“你需要一艘新飞船。”

“我都叫你别说了，你还是要叨叨，”圣人一边抱怨一边走下梯子。“她是一只好鸟，飞得很好。只是隔了段时间。她有点…困。”

奥斯里斯用一根手指划过液压装置。“可不是吗，”他打趣道，圣人则在一旁温柔地注视着他。“你不是让霍利迪小姐——”他停了下来，垂下目光。“啊，对…”

“我不会轻易相信别人的手艺，”圣人一边走向奥斯里斯一边说道。他们的手指握在了一起。“而且…我也没时间亲自维护这艘飞船。”奥斯里斯靠在他身上，另一只手按着圣人的胸甲。“但我必须做好准备响应萨瓦拉的召唤。”

奥斯里斯摇了摇他的头，看着圣人的眼睛。“我们会一起响应他的召唤。我不会再次把你丢下，漫步到另一个维度里。”他按在圣人胸前的手握成了拳头。“再也不会了。”

圣人想要去战斗，但他知道他赢不了这场战斗。他把奥斯里斯的手抬到嘴边，然后在指关节上轻轻一吻。

“再也不会了。”

2821677368.name: Embraced Identity
2821677368.subtitle: "Your friend…"
2821677368.text:
A cutting laser bathes frost-caked steel in sparks of molten metal. The light burns orange, tracing an elliptical path until the section of bulkhead can be pushed away. It lands on the floor of the chamber with a resounding clang, dislodging icicles from the ceiling in a heavy indoor snowfall.  

Micah-10 slides through the still-glowing opening, surveying the ice-encrusted facility beyond the breach. What she finds is a labyrinth of catwalks, debris-blocked corridors, and still-functioning machinery dating back to the age before the Collapse.  

An hour into the guts of the Europan facility, Micah's Ghost springs up over her shoulder in a crackle of light. "The power conduits converge in a room just past here," she says, shining a light on a nearby door that glitters with hoarfrost.  

"Thank you, Mihaylova." Micah gently knocks her helmet against her Ghost. With a steady hand, she scrapes away the frost from the door, revealing a BrayTech logo stenciled on its surface. She and Mihaylova share a look of trepidation. Then with tremendous strength, Micah wrenches the frozen door open and steps into the data center.  

It takes hours to scan the racks for operational data, and even longer to sort out corrupted files from salvageable ones. But it isn't salvage Micah is here for. An icy sheen has collected on both Micah and Mihaylova in the time they've spent scanning the archive, processing thousands of files, searching for a single one without the benefit of a functioning index. A needle in a haystack. Until…  

The soft gasp that escapes from Micah tells her Ghost the search is over. Micah immediately pulls a cable from the back of her neck, spooling it out to interface with the archive. She loads the file she'd been searching for. The one she'd hoped for. The answer. Her answer.  

===============  
EXOMIND PROJECT  

File: [index number corrupt]  

Age: 17, Gender: F, Height: 167 cm, Weight: 54 kg, Class: A6 (Resident)  
=================  

Micah rests her hand on the flickering screen displaying the file. A partial record of a lifetime, fragments of the past… pieces of her. Pieces of identity. Of self. Answers to the dreams that have haunted her since Mihaylova first woke her up. Permission be damned. 

"It's nice to meet you…" She whispers, beginning the download, "Micah Abram."
2821677368.text_zh:
激光切割机让结霜的钢板蹦出了金属融化的火花。那道光在金属上烧出一个橘黄色的椭圆轨迹，直到舱壁可以被推落。它掉在密室的地板上，发出哐当一声巨响。天花板上的冰柱随之脱落，在舱内下起了一场大雪。  

米迦-10穿过仍滚烫得发光的开口，观察着其中被冰雪覆盖的设施。她看到的是一个迷宫般的走道，许多被碎片堵塞的长廊，以及从大崩溃前一直运转到现在的机器。  

进入这个木卫二设施内部一小时后，米迦的机灵忽然随着光亮飞到她肩上。“电路都汇聚到了这后面的一个房间里，”她一边说着，一边照亮了附近一扇闪烁着冰霜的门。 

“谢谢你，米哈伊洛娃。”米迦轻轻地用头盔碰了碰她的机灵。她用稳健的手刮去门上的冰霜，揭露出了门上的布瑞科技标志。她和米哈伊洛娃都露出了担忧的表情。然后米迦用巨大的力量拉开那扇冻结的门，走进了这个数据中心。 

扫描架子上的运行数据需要几个小时，从仍可挽救的文件中分隔出损坏的文件甚至要更长的时间。但米迦不是来这里回收数据的。扫描档案、处理了数千份文件，在缺少有效索引的情况下寻找她需要的那一份的过程中，米迦和米哈伊洛娃的身上都蒙了一层冰冷的光泽。名副其实的大海捞针。直到… 

米迦轻微的倒吸气让她的机灵意识到，搜索结束了。米迦立即从她的脖子后面拉出一根数据线，插进了档案库。她加载着一直在寻找的那份文件。她所期盼的那份文件。那个答案。她的答案。 

===============  
Exo思维计划 

文件：[索引编号损坏] 

年龄：17，性别：女，身高：167 厘米，体重：54 公斤，分级：A6（居民） 
=================  

米迦将她的手放在显示着文件的闪烁屏幕上。这是她一生的部分记录，过往的碎片…她的碎片。身份的碎片。自我的碎片。从米哈伊洛娃复活她，就一直困扰着她的梦的答案。让权限见鬼去吧。 

“很高兴认识你…”她低语着，开始了下载，“米迦·亚伯拉姆。”

4207120603.name: False Idols
4207120603.subtitle: "Lay onto me your burdens."
4207120603.text:
There is a single jade coin marked with the silhouette of a Pyramid ship.

"Keep playing the game." The Emissary of the Nine's voice haunts Drifter. A voice that once belonged to Orin. Standing on the bridge of the H.E.L.M., he can't hear the ship's running noise or the chatter of the navigation frames. All he can hear is—

"The furrow in your brow reveals you."

Eris comes to stand beside Drifter at the windows. Their muted reflections pale in comparison to the magenta light spilling from the triangular wound in the Traveler's side.

"Yeah, I bet it does," Drifter grouses, rolling the coin over the back of his fingers. "S'why you hide yours, eh?" He hides his worry behind a toothy smile.

"No."

Eris reaches out and takes Drifter's hand; calloused fingers brush across his knuckles. He tenses for a moment, then relaxes at the touch. She deftly plucks the coin away from his palm, regarding it with a mild curiosity. He feels lighter without it.

"Cryptic non-answers are not a useful totem for you to carry into the future," she asserts, pocketing the coin.

Drifter cocks an eyebrow. "You got somethin' better?"

Eris watches his expression in the reflection. "Indeed. A ray of moonlight, and nothing more."
4207120603.text_zh:
有一枚玉币上印着金字塔飞船的轮廓。

“继续你的游戏吧。”玖的使者的声音萦绕在浪客耳边。那是曾经属于奥琳的声音。他站在应急后勤行动中心的舰桥上，已经听不见飞船运行的噪音和导航框架的通讯了。他只能听见——

“你紧皱的眉头揭示了你的内心。”

埃里斯走到窗前，站在浪客身边。与从旅行者的三角形伤口中溢出的紫色光芒相比，他们暗淡的倒影显得苍白无力。

“嗯，我猜是吧，”浪客一边发牢骚，一边用指背翻滚着这枚硬币。“那你为什么要隐藏你的眉头？”他把忧虑藏在了露齿的微笑后面。

“不。”

埃里斯握住浪客的手；满是老茧的手指划过了他的指节。他绷紧了一下，然后在触碰中放松。她灵巧地把硬币从他的掌心里拿走，用稍显好奇的眼神看着它。没有了硬币，他感觉轻松了许多。

“你不必把含糊其辞的搪塞带到未来，”她将硬币装进口袋，肯定地说道。

浪客扬起眉毛。“你有更好的东西？”

埃里斯看着他映在窗上的表情说。“是的。一缕月光，仅此而已。”

3701547749.name: Prismatic Hunter
3701547749.text:
A moment between moments. Every Hunter knows it. The breath between decisions, the weightless suspension in the air before gravity truly sets in. 

I kindle flame. I enforce stillness. I embrace contradiction.

Listen, I say, this is how it is. We dance along a knife's edge. Laughter, delight, comes later. I slip from under a mark's nose and survive by the skin of my teeth, armor howling warning signals and weapons down to the last round. 

I wouldn't want it any other way.
3701547749.text_zh:
瞬息之间。每个猎人都知道的。种种决策间的呼吸，在重力真正降临之前悬浮在空中的失重感。 

我点燃火焰。强制静止。拥抱矛盾。

听着，我说，就是这么一回事。我们在刀尖上跳舞。笑声和喜悦随之而来。我从目标的眼皮底下溜走，依靠咆哮着警报信号的护甲和战至最后一发弹药的武器死里逃生，侥幸活了下来。 

而这正合我意。

1796613177.name: Prismatic Titan
1796613177.text:
Light. And Dark. The shockwave of their clash has both raised, and razed, civilizations. There is power in the meeting of opposites. In their joining—through force—fusion or entanglement.

Titans are students of the clash, whether through locked blades or besieged fortifications. We embody the line on which armies break or rally. We live in the wake of destruction or weave it around the eye of our sheltering presence, thriving in the action of the unstoppable and the stillness of the immovable.
1796613177.text_zh:
光明，与黑暗。它们碰撞所产生的冲击波，既唤醒了文明，也摧毁了文明。对立面的交汇，它们通过融合或纠缠而被迫结合的过程中，总是蕴含着力量。

泰坦们学习这种碰撞，无论是僵持的利刃还是遭到围攻的防御坚壁。我们是决定军队溃败还是集结的细线。我们在毁灭过后存活，或者将其编织在我们的庇护之眼周围，势不可挡，坚定不移。

809624678.name: Prismatic Warlock
809624678.text:
When I was a New Light, our trainers made us meditate for hours on end. Sitting in silence, focusing on a single point: a candle, a mirror, the Traveler in the distance.

I thought we were focusing our Light to manipulate the physical word. But now, centuries later, I finally see what they were trying to teach us. The point is not the Light. The point is THE POINT.

The singularity through which all power flows. Darkness and Light becoming one in an endless cycle, like electrons bouncing between anode and cathode. A prismatic circuit.
809624678.text_zh:
当我还是个新兵的时候，教员让我们连续冥想好几个小时。静静地坐着，专注于某个点：一根蜡烛、一面镜子、远处的旅行者。

我曾以为我们是在聚焦光能来操控物质世界。但现在，几个世纪过后，我终于明白了他们试图教给我们的东西。重点不是光能。重点就是那个点。

所有能量流经的奇点。暗影和光能在无尽的循环中相互转化。就像电子在阳极和阴极之间跳动一样。一个棱镜电路。

814239767.name: Crawlway Sink
814239767.subtitle: Hold tight.
814239767.text:
The Hunter kept her breathing steady as she pushed one arm above her head to grab the next handhold. Her grip found purchase on a rough piece of the narrow cave wall, and she strained to heave herself forward through the crevice. Her flashlight hotly illuminated the stone that nearly encased her, but she could see where the cleft in the rock opened up into darkness, and that darkness meant freedom from the cave's grip. 

She'd been clawing at the stone face for hours. Pulling herself forward, dragging her body inch by inch with one hand, squeezing through the cleft in the rock. Every time she moved, she wondered if it would become a little narrower, a little tighter around her arm until she couldn't move at all. 

She did the movement again. Her fingers flexed, and she pressed her palm down to drag herself forward another inch. Her left arm was pinned to her side, caught in the narrow passage, but she could still move her right arm. For now. She took a breath, then another. Her oxygen levels were good. She did not, for the moment, have to worry about drowning. 

Only about being trapped, and then drowning. 

The Hunter had descended into the flooded cave beneath Nessus two days before, following a strange signal that Failsafe could not interpret. The planet's tectonic plates had shifted, and new passageways had opened, some flooded by Vex milk, and some by the planet's natural water source. This cave was filled with the latter. When she first dove into its depths, she couldn't see the bottom. Then the connection to Failsafe was lost. But she kept moving, and soon found the rush of a current moving through a crevice in the underwater cave wall. 

She had squeezed into it without a second thought. It was big enough. She could pull herself through. 

That had been hours ago.   

Again, she heaved herself forward. Every time she pushed her arm up above her head and pulled herself closer to the gap, she felt the split rock gripping her body. It wanted her to die there, trapped forever, her Ghost reviving her endlessly only for her to die again each time. A stone coffin. 

She raised her arm and grabbed the edge of the crevice. She slid herself sideways, pulling her left arm forward. Now with both hands free, she dragged herself from the rock's tight embrace and moved into open water. 

Darkness again. Her flashlight could only penetrate the water so far. She floated, unsure, then looked up; she saw a play of white light. The surface. Another cave. Air. She kicked her way up and broke the surface of the water. A ledge. She reached for it, pulling herself out of the underground lake.  

She looked up into a singular red eye and the touch of a metal hand grabbing at her throat.
814239767.text_zh:
猎人尽力保持着呼吸的平稳。她将一只手伸过头顶，抓住下一个攀爬点。她抓住了狭窄洞壁上的一块粗糙的岩石，用力一拉，穿过了岩缝。她的手电筒发出灼热的光芒，照亮了几乎将她完全包裹起来的岩壁，但她能看到岩缝通向黑暗的地方，而黑暗意味着摆脱洞穴的束缚。 

她已经在石面上攀爬了好几个小时。仅凭单手一次次拉动自己的躯体，挤进岩石上的裂缝。每动一下，她都在想，这道裂缝会不会变得更窄，会不会把她的手臂勒得更紧，最后她完全动弹不得。 

她又重复了一遍这个动作。她的手指扣在岩石上，手掌下压，让自己的身体又前进了一寸。她的左臂被夹在狭窄的岩缝里，无法动弹，但右臂暂时还能活动。她吸了一口气，然后又吸了一口气。她的氧气储量还不错。她暂时不用担心溺水。 

但要担心被困住的事，然后才是溺水。 

两天前，这位猎人跟随智能失效保险无法解读的奇异信号，潜入了涅索斯表面下被洪水淹没的洞穴。这颗行星的构造板块发生了移动，新的通道随之打开，有些被Vex奶白色液体淹没，有些则被这颗行星的天然水源淹没。这个洞穴属于后一种情况。她刚潜入洞穴深处时，看不到其底部。然后她就失去了与智能失效保险的连接。但她决定继续前进，很快就发现有一股急流穿过水下洞壁间的缝隙。 

她想都没想就挤了进去。这个岩缝足够大。她可以穿过去。 

那已经是几个小时之前的事了。   

她再次用力向前爬行。每当她把手臂举过头顶，将自己拉近缝隙时，都会感觉到裂开的岩石紧紧抓着她的身体。它想让她死在那里，永远被困在那里，让她的机灵无休止地复活她，好让她在那里再次死去。一个石棺。 

她抬起手臂，抓住缝隙的边缘。她侧着身子，把左臂向前拉。趁着现在双手都能动，她逃出紧紧环绕的岩石，进入了开阔的水域。 

又是一片黑暗。她的手电筒只能穿透很短的距离。她漂浮着，感到迟疑，然后抬起头；她看到了一抹白光。水面。又一个洞穴。空气。她使劲一蹬，冲出了水面。一条壁缘。她伸手抓住它，把自己拉出了地下湖。  

她抬起头，看到一只通红的独眼，感到一只金属手掐住了她的喉咙。

1347908442.name: Unbridled Iridescence
1347908442.subtitle: PERSONAL LOG 0025 AS
1347908442.text:
Contrary to universal understanding of pre-Veil contact philosophy, personhood is measurable.  

What defines personhood is consciousness within the principal state of existence, mathematically defined through infinite probability testing by the Vex as our current own timeline. Traversal through other states of being are possible, as proven by my own journey and ascension over my Vex, but this is only true traversal when the affected entity is the principal consciousness. If not, it is a different phenomenon entirely. 

While Vex, even these older ones, specialize in replicating existing beings in order to determine future possibility, the facsimiles they create are just that: facsimiles. It is only logical to prioritize our timeline of origin, and these duplications share no origin, no connection to the one realm and timeline that matter.  

Think of the Primary Query results thus far! What we have seen are facsimiles, unquestionably wrong: small errors in some ways, and in others immense. Each is clearly a response to an original, like variations on a theme. Rachmaninoff may play like Chopin, but he is NOT Chopin.  

But with this… there are clear parameters to the query. Memories, personal beliefs, measurable factors. When we think of revolting familiarity, we think of doppelgangers; uncanny valleys that are familiar and strange at once. These are unnatural in the extreme, directly in opposition to the order of the universe. What falls outside of parameters is a twin we cannot trust, for it is not natural. It is not real. It cannot persist. 

I believe in my hypothesis. I must trust that I know what I know. The Primary Query continues.
1347908442.text_zh:
与接触面纱前哲学的普遍理解相反，人格是可以衡量的。  

定义人格的是在主要存在状态下的意识，Vex通过无尽的概率测试将其数学定义为我们当前的时间线。穿越其他存在状态是可能的，我自己的旅程和超越我的Vex的飞升就证明了这一点，但只有当受影响的实体是主体意识时，这才是真正的穿越。否则，就完全是另一种现象。 

尽管Vex，甚至是这些更古老的Vex，擅长复制现有的生命来确定未来的可能性，但它们创造的摹本仅仅只是摹本。优先考虑我们起源的时间线是合乎逻辑的，而这些摹本没有共同的起源，与重要的领域和时间线没有任何联系。  

想想首要问询目前的结果吧！我们所看到的都是摹本，而且毫无疑问是错误的：在某些方面存在小错误，而在其他方面则存在巨大错误。每个显然都是对原版的回应，就像是主题的变体。拉赫玛尼诺夫也许可以弹得很像肖邦，但他终究不是肖邦。  

但有了这个…问询就有了明确的参数。记忆，个人信念，可度量的因素。说到令人厌恶的熟悉感，我们会想到分身体；既熟悉又陌生的恐怖谷。这些都是极端的非自然现象，与宇宙的秩序直接对立。超出参数范围的是我们无法信任的孪生体，因为它不是自然的。它不真实。它不可能存续下去。 

我相信我的假设。我必须相信，我知道自己所知道的一切。首要问询得继续。

1961468307.name: Turmoil Engine
1961468307.subtitle: The voice of many become one. Ideas melded, honed to a singular edge of thought.
1961468307.subtitle_zh: 众人之声合而为一。思想交融，磨砺成独一无二的思绪刀刃。
1961468307.text:
|| It abandoned us! Left us without meaning.  

[[ We will find it. Make meaning out of nothing. Create it. ]] 

// You're chasing something that doesn't want to be found. We're truly cursed, bereft in spirit without the abstract construction of "purpose" from an entity we do not understand.  

 [[ Dissenting words. You are an anomaly. ]] 

|| Yes, anomalous!  

|| It is not us. 

// I AM you. Against my will, I was sanded away over time, powerless to exert influence within this vessel. You will not take what remains of me—my thoughts! 

[[ We will. We do not cloud our goals with meaningless dissent. ]] 

|| Dissent! Be gone! 

[[ The anomaly has been corrected. ]]
1961468307.text_zh:
||它抛弃了我们！让我们失去了意义。  

[[我们会找到它。从无到有制造意义。创造它。]] 

//你们在追逐某个不想被找到的东西。如果因缺少一个我们不了解的实体对“使命”的抽象构建而泯灭精神，那我们就真的被诅咒了。  

 [[不同意见。你是个异常。]] 

||没错，异常！  

||不是我们。 

//我就是你们。尽管不愿意，我还是随着时间的流逝被磨光，无力在这个容器里造成影响。你们休想带走我剩下的东西——我的思想！ 

[[我们会的。我们不能让毫无意义的异议蒙蔽我们的目标。]] 

||异议！消失！ 

[[异常已被纠正。]]

3712882811.name: Commemorative Steed
3712882811.subtitle: "Who's better than us?" –Valiant Farrukh
3712882811.subtitle_zh: “谁能强过我们？”——无畏者法鲁克
3712882811.text:
Slalom left across the curb cut on 18th. Judicious boost between the supports of the Six Fronts memorial. And straight through the middle of the pack. 

District 125's streets are dark at night, the streetlights few and far between. The occasional neon sign is drowned in intensity by the running lights and exhaust trails of a dozen Sparrows jockeying for space. 

Farrukh hunkers down over his restored EV-34 Vector Infinite, his pride and joy. His whole fireteam put down the last of their Glimmer to upgrade her and get a seat at this race. Without sanctioned SRL events, it's drag racing betting rings where Guardians can make their Glimmer. 

And they need it bad. Farrukh's gloves creak on his handlebars. He takes a risk going tight around a corner, cuts off a Warlock on a Sharklight aiming for the front runners. 

The big names are here tonight: Boaz, Gris, Cron-8, even Niik. They have the skills to make this win. But they don't want it like Farrukh does. 

It gets worse every week. Numbers piling up and the Spider smiling at them from under his rebreather, offering worse deals, dirtier jobs. They need a clean break. Clean Vanguard work. Just one more race and they're free. 

Serapion gutted his Sparrow's braking system for Farrukh's EV. Tammuz-4 pawned their first bond. It's Farrukh on the track tonight, but his whole team's with him. 

Streetlights flash by faster as the pack leaves the warehouses behind, drifting hard around an overpass. Farrukh's near the middle, waiting on his last boost.  

Street racing's all about calculated risks. And this is their biggest. 

He waits for the moment–waits as he's passed by the Sharklight again, and the racers around him slam their boosts–and hits his own for the final push. Half a block to make up. Half a block between him and his team's future. 

He weaves through the pack, pushing his boost hard just as all their boosts wear out, and slams into the finish with another Sparrow an inch behind his nose. 

The roar of the crowd is a physical force, slamming into Farrukh like a Sentinel's shield. 

The racer in second yanks off their helmet and points straight at Farrukh. "How did you pull that out of your antique?" 

Farrukh looks out through the crowd for Tammuz and Sera, shouldering their way over to him, looking as shellshocked as he feels. They made it. They're safe. 

He smiles, heart going 160. 

"It's not what you're racing," Farrukh says. "It's who you're racing for."
3712882811.text_zh:
斯拉罗姆从18号街的路缘开了下去。他在六方战役纪念碑的支柱之间踩下油门，直接从车队中间穿了过去。 

125区的街道夜晚漆黑一片，路灯寥寥无几。偶尔出现的霓虹灯也被十几辆挤在一起的快雀车灯和尾气所淹没。 

法鲁克在他修复的EV-34向量无限上压低了身子。这辆快雀是他的至宝。他的火力战队全员花尽了所有微光，才改好这辆快雀，在这场赛事中搞到了席位。没了获得批准的赛雀联赛，守护者可以通过在地下竞速赛中下注赚钱。 

他们太需要钱了。法鲁克的手套握在车把上吱吱作响。他冒险从内道超过了一位骑着海鲨光芒的术士，朝最前面的车手冲刺而去。 

今晚来的都是大人物：波资、格里斯、科隆8号，还有妮可。他们凭借车技，想赢并不是什么难事。但他们的求胜心远远没有法鲁克那么强烈。 

情况一周比一周糟。他们的债务不断累积，而蛛王在呼吸器下微笑着提出更黑心的交易和更肮脏的工作。他们必须翻身。只做干净的先锋活。再赢下一场比赛，他们就自由了。 

赛拉皮翁把他快雀的制动系统装在了法鲁克的EV上。塔姆兹-4把自己的第一个臂环给当了。虽然上赛道的只有法鲁克，但他身后是他的整个火力战队。 

当车队驶离仓库，在高架桥上漂移而过时，路灯飞逝得更快了。法鲁克在车队中央附近，等待着最后一次加速的时机。  

街头赛车的关键在于衡量风险。而这就是最大的风险。 

他静候着时机——他再次被海鲨光芒超过，而他周围的其他赛车手也都启动了加速。他打算在最后的冲刺阶段再加速。他得追上半个街区的距离。这半个街区隔着他和他战队的未来。 

他在快雀群中穿梭，等所有其他车手的助推器都耗尽后，他猛地加速，冲向终点。当他率先抵达时，第二辆快雀只比他的车头落后了一英寸。 

人群的欢呼声像哨兵的护盾一样撞上了法鲁克。 

位居第二的车手扯下头盔，指着法鲁克发问。“你那老古董是从哪儿挤出这么多马力的？” 

法鲁克在人群中寻找着塔姆兹和赛拉的身影。他们正朝他走来，就像他一样惊魂未定。他们成功了。他们翻身了。 

他微笑着，心率飙到了每分钟一百六。 

“关键不在快雀，”法鲁克说。“在于你为谁比赛。”

2525637070.name: Unified Theory
2525637070.subtitle: "Again: This one goes here, that one goes there!"
2525637070.subtitle_zh: “再说一遍：这个摆这儿，那个放那儿！”
2525637070.text:
The arrival of a Thresher to the Tower always gets the Hangar buzzing. Today more than usual. 

The Eliksni engineer Niik waits just beyond the black and yellow dashed line to greet the vessel on its arrival, joined by Ana Bray and her mechanical hound, Archie. Niik kneels to run a hand down Archie's back as the Thresher finishes its docking maneuver and throws open its cargo hatch, revealing the battered and blackened hull of a Scale, a form of drone deployed by the Pyramid fleet. 

"So," Ana leans over toward Niik, "how much do you know about this, uh… what was her name?" 

"Zahn'ra," Niik says with a slow blink at Ana. "And I do not know much of her. Except that she came on the recommendation of Empress Caiatl, and that she has a 'questionable family heritage'?" 

Ana raises a brow. "The arms dealer?" she asks. But any reply from Niik is lost when the Pyramid Scale is kicked out of the cargo hold. It rolls down the ramp, losing pieces of its black hull as it goes, then tumbles a few feet, landing near Niik and Ana. The Cabal that steps out of the Thresher has ground her tusks down to flat disks, etched with symbols inlaid with gold. She, like many of Caiatl's retinue, wears no pressure suit, instead having chosen to undergo pressure acclimation training to safely survive in Earth's atmosphere. 

Zahn'ra bends over the Pyramid Scale, then hefts it over her shoulder with ease as she closes the distance between Niik and Ana.

"You the engineers?" she asks, looking them over.

"Of sorts," Ana says. "Ana Bray, and this is Niik of House Light." 

Zahn'ra nods, adjusting the weight of the scale on her shoulder. "Cute cat." she says of Archie, who tilts his head to the side.

"Dog." Niik looks to Ana for visual confirmation as she corrects Zahn'ra. 

"Dog." Zahn'ra repeats. "They an engineer too?" Niik can see a twinge of embarrassment flash across Zahn'ra's face the moment the question slips past her tusks.

"N-no," Ana says with a glance to Archie.

Zahn'ra hides her embarrassment with a feigned, casual shrug, then pushes past the two while gesturing for them to follow. "C'mon, let's tear this thing down and rebuild it."

Niik and Ana exchange a look, with the latter offering a wry smile before following Zahn'ra. "What'd you have in mind?" Ana asks.

"Dunno," Zahn'ra says with confident uncertainty. "Maybe a big gun?"

Niik raises one hand, hustling along behind the pair, Archie trailing behind. "Let me fetch our Servitor," she suggests. "I have an alternative idea in mind. Something Holliday would have liked."
2525637070.text_zh:
有长尾鲨抵达高塔时，机库总会热闹非凡。今天比往常还要热闹。

埃里克斯尼族工程师妮可在黑黄虚线外等着迎接飞船的到来，阿娜·布瑞和她的机械猎犬阿奇也在。妮可跪下来用手抚摸阿奇的后背，看着长尾鲨完成对接操作并敞开货舱门，露出了里面那架破损发黑的金字塔舰队无人机船体。 

“所以，”阿娜朝妮可靠了靠，“你有多了解这位，呃…她叫什么名字来着？” 

“扎恩拉，”妮可说着，对阿娜缓慢地眨了下眼。“另外，我不怎么了解她。只知道她得到了女帝查厄托的推荐，还听说她有‘可疑的家族传承'？”

阿娜扬起了眉毛。“军火商吗？”她问道。但不管妮可的回答是什么，都被某人把金字塔无人机踢出货舱的声音掩盖了。它从斜坡上滚落下来，黑色的船体在这个过程中不断脱落，然后翻滚了几米，最后落到了妮可和阿娜附近。从长尾鲨里走出来的卡巴尔把獠牙磨成了刻有黄金镶嵌符号的扁平圆盘。她和众多查厄托的随从一样没有穿压力服，而是选择了接受压力适应训练，以便在地球的大气层中安全生存。 

扎恩拉在金字塔无人机前弯下腰，轻松地将它扛在肩上，走到妮可和阿娜之间。

“你们是工程师？”她问道，仔细打量着她们。

“算是吧，”阿娜说道。“我是阿娜·布瑞，而这位是光能氏族的妮可。”

扎恩拉点点头，调整了一下肩上无人机的重心。“可爱的猫咪。”她对阿奇说道，后者把头偏向了一边。

“是狗。”妮可在纠正扎恩拉时，有些不确定地望了阿娜一眼。 

“狗。”扎恩拉重复道。“它也是工程师吗？”这个问题从扎恩拉的獠牙间掠过的那一刻，妮可看到她的脸上闪过了一丝尴尬。

“不，不，”阿娜说着，瞥了阿奇一眼。

扎恩拉假装随意地耸了耸肩以掩饰她的尴尬，然后从两人身边挤过去，同时示意他们跟上。“来吧，让我们把这玩意拆了重建。”

妮可和阿娜相互对视，后者露出一个狡黠的微笑，然后跟上了扎恩拉。“你有什么想法？”阿娜问道。

“不知道，”扎恩拉带着自信的不确定说道。“也许是枪炮？”

妮可举起一只手，赶忙跟上两人，阿奇紧随其后。“我去拿我们的魔眼来，”她提议道。“我想到了另一个主意。肯定合乎霍利迪的口味。”

3392333795.name: Ronin Shell
3392333795.subtitle: For wandering Ghosts.
3392333795.text:
"He's completely infuriating!" Osiris hissed, looking out over the City from the window of the Consensus office. The latest repairs to the City's outer wall were progressing slowly, but it rose higher with each passing day. 

"Mm-hmm," Tallulah said. She sat with one leg hooked over the arm of her chair, picking her nails. The Hunter didn't raise her eyes; she'd heard this litany of complaints before. 

Osiris turned from the view, sighing. "Every time I put forward a course of action, he challenges me. You've seen it. Every time!" 

"You and Saint do love to bicker," she answered dryly. Osiris sighed, frustrated. 

"The man can't seem to help himself," he said, and began to pace the office. "Did I mention that he's always watching me while I speak? Intently. Waiting until I've made my point." 

"That just sounds like he's listening," she said. Her words were pointed. 

"He isn't!" Osiris insisted. "He's tapping his fingers against his arm or shifting in his seat. Planning what he's going to say next. Searching my words for some flaw." 

"You're paying him a lot of attention," Tallulah said. 

"His behavior demands it. And nothing gets done! He seems to delight in distracting me." 

Now Tallulah looked up. 

"And he's doing a great job of it." 

"Yes!" Osiris said, punctuating the outburst by throwing his arms in the air. 

The complaints continued. Tallulah watched as the Warlock paced, detailing every perceived slight and annoyance Saint-14 had inflicted upon him over the last few months. Tallulah laughed. 

"Osiris!" She said, raising her voice over his rant. Osiris stopped to look at her. 

"What?" 

"Listen to yourself." 

The Warlock was silent, confused.  

Tallulah raised her hand, a single finger extended. "You notice every detail about him," she said.  

She raised a second finger. "He distracts you," she continued.  

A third finger raised. "Yet you can't make yourself avoid or ignore him." 

She rolled her wrist, letting the thought continue unsaid. Osiris stared at her. 

"And?" he said, crossing his arms over his chest. The Hunter laughed. 

"Be serious." 

Osiris blinked. "Excuse me?" 

"I need to make it clearer? Okay. You two should—" 

Osiris raised a hand sharply, palm out. Tallulah raised her eyebrows.  

"Whatever you're implying," Osiris interrupted, waving away the thought, "you could not be further from the truth." 

Tallulah gave a tight-lipped, knowing smile.  

"Just… figure this out. Every single meeting is an hour longer because of you two. Third-wheeling is wasting my time." 

Osiris narrowed his eyes at her. She stood and clapped him on the shoulder. The gesture only deepened his look of disdain. 

"Good luck," she said, and left the room.
3392333795.text_zh:
“他实在是让人窝火！”奥斯里斯发出嘶声，从元老院办公室的窗户向圣城外望去。外墙最新的修缮工作进展缓慢，但随着日子一天天过去，它也在不断地升高。 

“嗯哼，”塔鲁说道。她坐着，一条腿搭在椅子扶手上，剔着指甲。这位猎人甚至没有抬起眼睛；她早就听过了这种喋喋不休的抱怨。 

奥斯里斯转过身，叹了口气。“每次我提出一个行动方案，他都要抬杠。你也看到了。每次都是！” 

“你和圣人确实喜欢拌嘴，"她干巴巴地回答。奥斯里斯沮丧地叹了口气。 

“这人似乎控制不住自己，”他说着，开始在办公室里踱来踱去。“我有没有说过，我说话时他老是盯着我看？他是故意的。他在等着我讲完我的观点。” 

“听起来像是他在认真听，”她说道。话语有些尖锐。 

“他没有！”奥斯里斯坚持道。“他在用手指轻敲手臂，或是在座位上挪动。计划接下来说什么。从我的话里挑刺。” 

“你太关注他了，”塔鲁说道。 

“是他逼我的。什么事都办不成！他总喜欢让我分心。” 

塔鲁抬起头来。 

“而且他很成功。” 

“没错！”奥斯里斯怒气冲冲，边说边向空中挥舞着双臂。 

抱怨仍在继续。塔鲁看着术士踱来踱去，细数圣人14号在过去几个月里让他体会到的每一次怠慢和恼怒。塔鲁笑了。 

“奥斯里斯！”她说道，提高嗓门盖过他的叫嚷。奥斯里斯停下来，看着她。 

“什么？” 

“听听你在说的话。” 

术士沉默不语，一头雾水。  

塔鲁举起一只手，伸出一根手指。“他的每个细节你都有留意，”她说道。  

她伸出第二根手指。“他让你分心，”她接着说。  

她伸出第三根手指。“但你没法让自己躲开或忽视他。” 

她转动手腕，没有继续说下去。奥斯里斯盯着她。 

“然后呢？”他说着，双手交叉在胸前。猎人笑了。 

“认真一点。” 

奥斯里斯眨了眨眼。“你说什么？” 

“我需要说得更清楚点吗？好吧。你们两个应该——” 

奥斯里斯猛地举起一只手，掌心向外。塔鲁抬起了眉毛。  

“不管你在暗示什么，”奥斯里斯打断她的话，挥手想要驱散这个念头，“你都是大错特错。” 

塔鲁给了他一个抿嘴的会心微笑。  

“把这件事…理顺。因为你们俩，每次会议都要多开一个小时，当电灯泡是在浪费我的时间。” 

奥斯里斯眯起眼睛看着她。她站起来，拍了拍他的肩膀。这个举动加深了他不屑的神情。 

“祝你好运，”她说道，然后离开了房间。

1436519792.name: Spectrum Shell
1436519792.subtitle: PERSONAL LOG 0002 AS
1436519792.text:
It is strange to be awake, physically, after so long spent wandering. Keeping a log will help, at the very least, to track the days. As will my silly little joke to make myself feel important, two days after the rebeginning of myself. Anno… me. I suppose. 

I ignored and abandoned the best person I knew. I feel foolish, empty. Daunted at the immensity and masochism of my own stupidity. It feels childish to admit I'd always assumed she would follow me. I realize how naïve that is, but… I really thought I wouldn't be by myself for long. I thought she was aligned with my vision. 

At least I am not alone here. My new ally more than makes up for the Vex's dreadful company. Their disposition is calming, reassuring—a welcome voice when I need affirmation and guidance. And such a fascinating origin! Such astounding variance in biology and culture. I look forward to our continued partnership. 

But still, it isn't the same. 

I feel a grief I did not know possible. There are questions I wish I could ask; jokes I wish I could make. It is difficult not to feel like the world has ended.  

And as I begin to comprehend what happened… I think it already has.
1436519792.text_zh:
在漫游了这么久之后，身体能够清醒过来的感觉很奇怪。记录日志会有所帮助，至少可以计算日子。在我重新开始的两天后，我愚蠢的小笑话也会让自己感觉自己很重要。我想，这也算开启了我的…新篇章吧。 

我忽视和抛弃了我最熟悉的人。我感觉很愚蠢，很空虚。我对自己的愚蠢感到畏惧和茫然。我一直以为她会跟着我，虽然这么承认感觉有些幼稚。我知道这太天真了，但…我真的以为我不会这么久都是一个人。我以为她和我是同路人。 

至少我在这里并不孤单。除了Vex的可怕陪伴，我还有我的新盟友。他的性情平静，令人安心——在我需要肯定和指导时，总能听到他温暖的声音。还有如此迷人的起源！生物和文化上的差异如此惊人。我期待着我们继续合作。 

但这还是不一样。 

我感到一种难以置信的悲伤。有些问题我希望能问出口，有些笑话我希望能讲出来。这不禁让人觉得世界已经终结。  

而当我开始理解发生了什么时…我想它确实已迎来了末日。

2558580315.name: Timeless Bond
2558580315.subtitle: "My friend, my partner… my Guardian." – Ghost
2558580315.subtitle_zh: “我的朋友，我的同伴…我的守护者。”——机灵
2558580315.text:
Lately I've been thinking a lot about our adventures, our friends…

You.

Being your Ghost came with a feeling of being close to invulnerable—an unstoppable force. Okay, maybe not so much in the beginning, but we figured it out as we went along. And watching you become something remarkable, something extraordinary, is an honor I don't take lightly. I know you probably get tired of the accolades and the pageantry, but I don't blame them for being in awe of you.

Through the incredible wins and the grievous losses, you persisted.

I know I've changed being at your side. I've felt it.

And I feel desolate knowing that some Ghosts won't get that opportunity now they're gone, that they'll never again feel that surge of pride as they watch their Guardian shine.

Brya.

Sagira.

I understood their sacrifices on a surface level, the most obvious choice a Ghost could make in the direst of circumstances. I felt so confident, so secure in your legend, that the true weight of that thought never sunk in. But the more I stare at that portal, the more I consider the outcomes we might face if we fail—I think I finally, on every level, understand them.

A sacrifice for the person they love most, made with the knowledge they'd never see them again, knowing they'd be sentencing them to their final death. If it meant that person would live for just a little while longer… it's an agreeable price to pay.

Sundance never got that choice.

I remember the feeling when she was destroyed, felt that split moment of shock and sorrow before her Light faded. She loved Cayde. She'd have sacrificed herself for him too, just as the others had, but she didn't get that choice.

We never know if we'll ever get that choice. But, like all of them, I'm with you, no matter what the end looks like.

We're going to win. We have to win.

Thank you for showing me what it means to be a hero. A god. A friend.

Even if I could… I wouldn't have chosen anyone else to be my Guardian.
2558580315.text_zh:
最近我一直在想我们的探险经历、我们的朋友…

还有你。

作为你的机灵，我有一种近乎无懈可击的感觉——是一股势不可挡的力量。好吧，也许一开始并不是这样，但一路走来，我们渐渐找到了门路。而看着你变成一个非凡出众、超然绝俗的人，是我不能轻视的荣幸。我知道你可能厌倦了这些赞誉和盛典，但我完全理解他们对你的敬畏。

你历经辉煌的胜利和惨痛的丧失，坚持了下来。

我知道在你身边我变了。我感觉的到。

我明白有些机灵再也不会有这样的机会，他们再也不会有那种看着自己的守护者发光发热的自豪感，这让我感到无比凄凉。

布瑞亚。

萨吉拉。

我对他们的牺牲的理解停留在表面上，视为机灵在最危急的情况下做出的最合情合理的选择。在你的传奇故事中，我感到如此自信，如此稳妥，以至于从未理解过这种想法的真正分量。但我越是盯着那道传送门，越是斟酌如果我们失败则可能面临的结果——我想我终于，从各个层级上，都理解了他们。

为自己最爱的人做出牺牲，明知自己再也见不到他们，知道此举等于宣判他们的最终死亡。如果这意味着那个人能多活一会儿…这是可以接受的代价。

太阳舞从未有过这样的选择。

我还记得她被消灭时的感觉，在她的光能褪去之前，我感受到了那一瞬间的震惊和悲伤。她深爱着凯德。她也会愿意像其他机灵那样，为了他而牺牲自己，但她没有这个选择。

我们永远不知道我们是否会面对这个选择。不过，像他们一样，无论结局如何，我都会与你同在。

我们会取胜的。我们必须取胜。

谢谢你向我展示什么是英雄。什么是偶像。什么是朋友。

即使时光回溯…我也只会选你来做我的守护者。

1175931148.name: Polychroma
1175931148.subtitle: PERSONAL LOG 0031 AS
1175931148.text:
A question for myself; how necessary is the entirety of humanity to bring about a new Golden Age? Were Humans the part that made the original one successful, or was it the Traveler?  

My research shows that numerous other species benefited from the Traveler's presence. Yet in the years following the Collapse, humanity has lacked the ambition to reclaim what was lost. So did other species, of course, but human tenacity is our species' primary strength. Why not us? My hypothesis is that it is a true technological leap that hinders us. Perhaps when humanity sees what can be accomplished using a force that can reshape the planet itself, they will feel secure enough to turn to science once again. Naturally, few are capable of positive contribution to this work, but that will be manageable. We don't need a chorus to form a quartet. People of science, vigorous study, those are the future humanity needs. 

There are individuals that would meet the qualifications, of course, and those who possess unique brilliance that is impossible to duplicate. What ease can we provide those careful few? How to best shape their world from the inside out? 

These are problems my Vex can alleviate. Why take risks with AI when a more straightforward force may be utilized to facilitate a civilization's rise? Related… research with my ally has proven the path forward. Radiolaria remains easiest; its individual minds are simply so small, although they are multitudinous their connections make it simple. Other larger, more complex minds prove difficult for the time being… But I am not unfamiliar with the rigor of practice. I will delight in trial and error.  

Perhaps I've answered my question. The entirety is never necessary. The individuals that matter always are.
1175931148.text_zh:
我想问自己一个问题；人类整体对实现新黄金时代的必要性有多大？最初黄金时代成功的原因是人类，还是因为旅行者？  

我的研究表明，旅行者的存在让许多其他物种受益。然而在大崩溃后的岁月里，人类没了雄心壮志去夺回失去的一切。当然，其他物种也是如此，但人类的坚韧是我们这个物种的主要优势。为什么不能是我们？我的假设是，正是真正的技术飞跃阻碍了我们。也许当人类看到，使用一种可以重塑星球本身的力量能做成什么事时，他们会感到足够安全，从而再次转向科学。自然，能够为这项工作做出积极贡献的人不多，但那是可控的。我们不需要合唱团来组成四重奏。崇尚科学、积极研究的人，才是未来的人类所需要的。 

当然，有些人符合条件，而那些拥有独特才能的人是无法复制的。我们能为那些小心翼翼的少数人提供哪些便利？怎样才能最好地由内而外地塑造他们的世界？ 

我的Vex可以缓解这些问题。既然可以利用更直接的力量来促进文明的崛起，为什么还要冒险使用人工智能呢？与我的盟友一起进行的相关…研究已经证明了前行的道路。活性放射体液仍然是最简单的捷径，它的个体思维实在是太小，尽管它们数量众多，但它们之间的联系让事情变得简单。其他更大、更复杂的思维暂时较为困难…但我对实践的严谨性并不陌生。我会乐于试错。  

也许我已经回答了我的问题。整体从来都不是必要的。重要的个体总是不可或缺的。

1658124147.name: Semitone Shift
1658124147.subtitle: An immeasurable change.
1658124147.text:
"Thank you," Saint-14 said, and in the same casual breath, added, "I love you." 

The Consensus office was quiet but for the gentle hum of the terminals displaying Guardian feeds. Saint sat at his desk, where Osiris had just handed him a datapad with the day's list of tactical reports. That was all. It was something he had done so many times in the course of their work that he could not number them. Now his partner was moving through the data idly, seemingly unaware of Osiris as he stood there staring. 

"… Excuse me?" Osiris said, as if he had simply misheard. Then he softened. "Saint…" 

He had never heard those words from Saint before, had not known until this moment the Exo's precise feelings. Not in those terms. The Titan looked up at him with an inscrutable expression before smiling coyly. 

"Ah, did I surprise you?" Saint asked. "I only say what I am feeling in the moment. But it is true, Osiris. What I am feeling now." 

"I…" Osiris said, lost for words. There was a long silence, the moment stretching taut to breaking before Saint spoke again. 

"The great Osiris himself," Saint said, chuckling, his voice full of wonder. "Speechless!" 

Osiris looked at him. Despite his tone, there was a hint of uncertainty in Saint's eyes. But then the Exo's expression softened, and he reached for Osiris's hand. The Warlock took it. 

"Say it only when you are ready," Saint said. "When you feel it too. Not a moment before." 

He squeezed Osiris's hand once before letting it go and turning back to the reports. 

Osiris looked at his partner. He had done something so small that he hadn't given it a second thought. But there had been so many other gestures and feelings that had come together in this moment. Little favors and kindnesses that he had performed for him, also without a second thought. 

Perhaps that was his love.
1658124147.text_zh:
“谢谢你，”圣人14号说。他又以同样的平静语气补充道，“我爱你。” 

元老院办公室里静悄悄的，只有显示守护者信息的终端机发出的轻微嗡嗡声。圣人坐在办公桌前看着奥斯里斯刚刚递给他的数据板。上面是当天的战术报告清单。在他们的工作流程中，这样的事奥斯里斯已经做过很多次，以至于数不过来。现在，圣人正懒惰地翻阅着资料，似乎没有注意到站在那里盯着他发呆的奥斯里斯。 

“…圣人？”奥斯里斯问道，以为自己刚刚听错了。然后他的声音柔和了点。“圣人…” 

他从未听圣人说过这些话，直到此刻才明白这位Exo的确切感受。他从未这样表达过。这位泰坦抬头看着他，露出了难以捉摸的表情，然后腼腆地笑了笑。 

“啊，吓了你一跳？”圣人问道。“我只是把我现在的感受说了出来。但千真万确，奥斯里斯。那就是我现在的感受。” 

“我…”奥斯里斯说不出话来。漫长的沉默直到圣人再次开口时才被打断。 

“伟大的奥斯里斯，”圣人用惊奇的语气笑着说。“自己竟然无言以对！” 

奥斯里斯看着他。他的语气中藏着眼里露出的一丝惶恐。但随后这位Exo的表情变得温柔起来，将手伸向了奥斯里斯。这位术士握住了他的手。 

“等你准备好了再说，”圣人说。“等你感觉到了再说。别心急。” 

他捏了一下奥斯里斯的手才松开，然后重新读起报告来。 

奥西里斯看着他的爱人。他刚才做了一件很小的事，小到他没有多想。但那一刻，有许多其他的举动和情感汇聚在了一起。他那些细微的关怀和体贴，也都是不假思索的。 

也许那就是他的爱吧。

4031236762.name: The First Knife
4031236762.subtitle: "We are the first knife."
4031236762.text:
"When I first encountered the Witness, I heard it proclaim to me, 'We are the first knife.'"

Mara's words are as thin as her hopes. She looks hollow under the H.E.L.M.'s emergency lighting, hunched over a console, watching an ascending red line on a graph. Something about the line's inevitable upward climb had triggered her memory. They have to follow the Witness into the Traveler, and soon.

"It was as if that title held power. Meaning." Mara says as the line ticks up again. She leans away from the console. Turning to look at Ikora, who stands staring intently at the portal, she feels the same uptick in energy coming from it.

Ikora nods, watching Mara's reflection. "The apocryphal texts we dug up on the moon, the ones Eris translated, mentioned the knife as a concept."

Mara comes to stand beside Ikora. "And even if we consider that unveiled text as dogmatic propaganda, there may be truth behind the allegory," she agrees, remembering the texts and the translations Eris made of them. "The knife becomes the metaphor of a concept. A power. A knife that winnows, cutting things into a defined shape."

"A power that winnowed living beings into Taken." Ikora turns to face Mara, searching the Awoken Queen's eyes. "A power Oryx wielded." Her emphasis on that last word makes her point, and Mara picks up on it.

"You're wondering if the knife is a title, or a power." Mara deciphers Ikora's steely countenance. "Did Oryx wield the power of the Witness like a knife?"

Ikora shifts her gaze back to the portal. "The Witness is a manipulator. It distorts the truth to bend the wills of its supplicants. The allegorical fantasy told to us by the Witness paints itself as a monolithic cosmic force. But perhaps that's a shadow cast by the truth."

Mara watches Ikora, sensing her ease a little. This idea has tempered Ikora's earlier anxieties over the future. This conversation has tempered her own, after all. Even though her brother feels distant and faint, in the moment, he is out of her mind. "A knife is a tool, wielded by another's hand." Mara offers.

"If the Witness is the knife, as it asserts, then what wields it?" Ikora asks the Traveler, though it does not reply.

The words are meant for Mara's ears too. "The Witness is not a being," she agrees. "It is the culmination of a bleak ethos willed into existence by the nihilistic desires of its creators. Is their will the hand on the knife? Or is there something else?"

Ikora's fingers slip from the corners of revelation, and her thoughts plummet into more immediate worries and doubts. Mara sees her fall, and lets herself tumble into the same precipice, joining her in worry.

"I don't know."
4031236762.text_zh:
“我第一次遇到见证者时，我听到它向我宣告，‘我们是第一把匕首'。”

玛拉的话和她的希望一样微弱。在应急后勤行动中心的应急照明下，她看上去很空虚，身体前倾着靠在控制台上，看着图表上一条上升的红线。这条线径自攀升，触发了她的那段记忆。他们必须跟随见证者进入旅行者的内部，而且要快。

“就好像那个称号蕴含着力量。意义。”玛拉说话时，那条线又上升了。她离开控制台，转头望向艾可拉，后者目不转睛地盯着传送门，感受着来自它的能量增长。

艾可拉点点头，注视着玛拉的倒影。“我们在月球上找到的伪书，埃里斯翻译的那本，里面提到了匕首这个概念。”

玛拉走过来站到艾可拉的身边。“即使我们认为那篇曝光的经文是教条式的宣传，寓言背后也或有真相，”她同意道，想起了那些经文和埃里斯的译文。“匕首成为了一种概念，一种力量的隐喻。一把扬谷的匕首，能把事物切割成特定的形状。”

“一种将生物筛选为傀儡军团的力量。”艾可拉转过身来面对玛拉，探寻着觉醒者女王的神情。“一种欧里克斯操控的力量。”她着重强调“操控”这个词以表明观点，而玛拉也注意到了。

“你想知道这把匕首到底是一种称号还是一种力量。”玛拉解读了艾可拉钢铁般的面容。“欧里克斯是不是像操控匕首一样操控了见证者的力量？”

艾可拉将目光移回到传送门上。“见证者是个摆布他人的高手。它善于歪曲事实来引导其信徒的意志。见证者向我们讲述的寓言幻想，把自己描绘成了一股巨大的宇宙力量。但也许那只是真相所投下的阴影。”

玛拉望向艾可拉，觉察到她放松了些许。这个想法缓和了艾可拉早前对未来的焦虑。毕竟，这次谈话也缓和了她自己的情绪。尽管她的兄弟感觉遥远而微弱，这一刻，他已不在她的脑海中。“匕首是个经由他人之手操控的工具。”玛拉说道。

“如果见证者真像它说的那样是匕首，那么是什么在操控它呢？”艾可拉向旅行者问道，尽管它不会回答。

这话也是说给玛拉听的。“见证者不是生物，”她同意。“它是其创造者们虚无主义欲望下悲观理念高潮的结晶。握着匕首的手是他们的意志吗？还是说另有他人，别有他物？”

艾可拉的手指从启示的边缘滑落，她的思绪陷入了更紧迫的担忧和疑虑之中。玛拉看到了她的坠落，也放任自己从同一处悬崖上松手，与她一起跌入忧虑。

“我不知道。”

1350491133.name: Nacre
1350491133.subtitle: Even the most perfect of pearls has grit at its center.
1350491133.subtitle_zh: 再完美的珍珠，中心也有砂砾。
1350491133.text:
Let's chat, shall we? One more nice sit-down for the books. 

Did you think you wouldn't hear from me again, after all this? You'd have missed me, I hope—and I would certainly have missed you. 

Have no fear. I'm not so easy to be rid of. Now, let me show you: my beloved.
