说说邪魔族。我的邪魔族。我和这群机灵决定给旅行者这个更好的选择一个真正的机会。蠕虫没了。光能留存。它照耀着那里的一切，邪魔族会怎么做？他们并非所有人都在接受光能改造的那一刻迅速形成了强烈的个人主义。光能并没有把暗影，或是英勇教团一直以来编造的狗屁，从他们的身上清除。他们仍然还是邪魔族。  

这只是选择的问题。  

每个人都有选择。始终如此。无论你在做什么，无论你身在何处。不能接受选择并不等于没有选择。即使是在蠕虫的管理下，邪魔族也有选择的余地——不过嘿，谁会愿意选择最终死亡这个备选项呢。   

我想说的是旅行者也做出了选择。选择赋能邪魔族，就像它对人类做过的那样；它在可以逃跑的时候选择了留下来。 

我尊重这一点。即使是现在，我也在跨越与你们相隔的鸿沟，执行着它的意志。 

光明邪魔族现在选择了什么？我肯定不会告诉你们。但无论是什么，这都与你们过去轻率的二分法完全不同。善还是恶，他们仍然可以自行选择。  

就像我做的那样。就像旅行者做的那样。

2768261701.name: Cacosmia
2768261701.text:
[Report by VanNet encrypted router] 

[A-Mahal//Link: C-Yong] 

[Mail-Archive//0071292//excerpted] 

… Where there is smoke, there is fire, they say. The sign of a thing does not come to pass without the thing that made it. Footsteps require a being walking to be made.  

So then, why the recent move toward acceptance of Darkness as a morally neutral force? Are we expected to believe that the Collapse, that all our battles against the Hive and their Darkness, have been nothing more than an elaborate false flag operation? How is it that none of the enemies of humanity have, until now, come to us wielding Light? 

It is not… impossible.  

There, I have said it, though it leaves a bad taste in my mouth to do so. While I sincerely doubt any genuine conspiracy, I will concede that it is technically possible that nearly every enemy of humanity has simply happened to take to hand the cosmic force that opposes the Traveler, the one force which was used to end the Golden Age and decimate humanity. 

Savathûn is known for deception and trickery. Are we so certain that she was given the Light? Truly?  

And even if it is true that the Darkness is itself as safe as the Light, that our greatest enemy had only taken it as its cloak, should we truly encourage Guardians to reach for it? A force of consciousness with the Witness lingering within? From where I stand, nothing seems riskier.  

I have never thought that we needed to understand the Darkness to defeat it. Doing so has only brought more questions and uncertainty in a time when clarity of purpose is required. 

Have we all forgotten the reasons Osiris was banished? In his obsession with the Vex, he spoke freely of morality, decrying the concepts of good and evil as foolishness; he spoke of a willingness to choose Darkness above whatever fate the Vex might bring. At the time, it was thought so dangerous a viewpoint that he was sent away from the City, and his return has only brought more doubt. 

I will still fight the Darkness. That is of paramount importance. Perhaps, if there can be peace, the Creed can be revisited to prioritize the defeat of humanity's enemies. 

That time is not now.
2768261701.text_zh:
[报告来自VanNet加密路由器] 

[A-Mahal//链接：C-Yong] 

[邮件归档//0071292//节选] 

…俗话说，无风不起浪。没有造物之主，就没有造物之迹。需要有生物走动，才能发出脚步声。  

那么，为什么最近人们开始接受暗影是一种道德中立的力量呢？难道我们要相信大崩溃，相信我们与邪魔族及其暗影的所有战斗，都不过是一场精心策划的假旗行动？为什么在此之前人类之敌都没有操控着光能来对付我们？ 

这并非…不可能。  

好了，我说出口了，虽然这样做让我感到不自在。虽然我由衷地怀疑存在任何真正的阴谋，但我承认，严格来讲，几乎人类的每一个敌人都可能只是碰巧掌握了那种与旅行者相反的宇宙力量，那种用来终结黄金时代并毁灭人类的力量。 

萨瓦图恩以欺骗和诡计而著称。我们就这么确定她是被赐予了光能吗？真是那样吗？  

而就算暗影本身真的跟光能一样安全，我们最大的敌人也只是把它当成披风，我们真的该鼓励守护者去触及它吗？一种见证者徘徊在其中的意识力量？在我看来，没有什么比这更冒险了。  

我从没想过我们需要了解暗影才能击败它。这样做只会在这个需要明确目标的时候带来更多问题和不确定性。 

难道我们都忘了奥斯里斯被放逐的原因吗？他那时痴迷于Vex，不顾道德地畅所欲言，将善恶的概念斥为愚蠢；他说他宁愿选择暗影，也不愿接受Vex所可能带来的命运。当时的人们认为这种观点非常危险，因此他被赶出了圣城，而他的回归也只带来了更多的质疑。 

我仍将与暗影作战。这一点是至关重要的。也许，如果能够实现和平，信条就可以被重新审视，将击败人类之敌放在首位。 

现在还不是时候。

2768261700.name: Collective
2768261700.text:
From the writings of Ulan-Tan, recovered after his death: 

… It is because Light and Darkness are connected that great sacrifice was required of the Traveler: that which was once in balance was no longer, and to equal Darkness with its Light would take more than had ever been given before.  

So the Traveler created Ghosts; Ghosts created Guardians. And afterward, the Traveler became quiet. Dead, some thought, or dreaming.  

When a Human being commits an act of great cost, we know this as injury, as muscles torn and bones broken. It requires rest; frequently, it requires intervention to heal. As simple as the helping hand of another to lean on, or as complex as deep surgery: the constant theme that it cannot be done alone. Even to rest safely in quiet requires another to take over the matters of life that cannot be put off, which do not pause themselves simply for the fact of being asked kindly. 

So: the Traveler strove greatly, and then became still. How do we believe that it is anything but injured? 

The Speaker tells us the Traveler is not dead, and I believe this. It is sleeping, resting from its great deed. The sacrifice made for us, to create us.  

There is a debt thus owed. 

If we understand that Light is connected to itself—that the Light in Guardians is the same Light as that in their Ghosts, which in turn is the same Light as the Traveler's—then the answer is clear: that those possessed of the Traveler's Light, defended and upraised by it, stand in the best and in fact only possible position to pay back that debt. Who else could even hope to do so?  

I argue that our duty is to try. Even the act of defending the Traveler so it may heal is some measure of action. But if there is more that can be done, then we who it has defended owe it to the Traveler to do so. 

Remember that, in Light or in Darkness.
2768261700.text_zh:
摘自乌兰-坦死后被发现的作品： 

…正因为光能与暗影是相通的，所以旅行者需要做出巨大牺牲：原本的平衡不复存在，而想用它的光能均衡暗影，就需要付出比以往更高的代价。  

所以旅行者创造了机灵，机灵创造了守护者。再之后，旅行者就陷入了沉寂。有人认为它死了，或是在做梦。  

当一个人做出了付出巨大代价的行为时，我们视之为受伤，是肌肉撕裂和骨骼断裂。需要休息；通常，需要干预才能痊愈。简单如他人的援助之手，复杂如深度手术：一个不变的主题是，单靠自己不行。即使是在宁静的环境中安然休息，也需要他人来接手不能被搁置，不会因你好言相求就暂停的生活事务。 

所以说：旅行者努力了很久，然后安静下来了。我们怎么能认为那不是它受伤了呢？ 

先知告诉我们旅行者没有死，我相信这一点。它在沉睡，从它的伟大事业中抽身出来休息。那是为创造我们而做出的牺牲。  

我们也因此欠下了一笔债。 

如果在我们的理解中光能是与自身想通的——守护者的光能与他们的机灵的光能是一样的，而他们的机灵又与旅行者的光能是一样的——那么答案就不言而喻了：那些拥有旅行者的光能，受到它的保护和提升的人，就是最适合，事实上也是唯一可能偿债的人。还有谁能做到？  

我认为，我们的责任就是去尝试。哪怕是保卫旅行者来助它痊愈的行为也是一种行动措施。但如果还能做得更多，那么我们这些被旅行者保卫过的人理应那样做。 

记住这点，无论是在光能还是暗影之中。

193039764.name: Bird in the Hand
193039764.text:
I'm the last guy you'd accuse of being on the straight and narrow, right? Right. I mean, come on, look at me. Hunters aren't exactly the noble knights of the Guardian world.  

Look. I'm not a square. That's Zavala's job. I'll break all the rules that I shouldn't and keep the ones no one expects me to. Which is why, in part, I've never been much of one for nosing into the Darkness. Take the three of us, huh? Who would you expect to get their hands into the goop? The honorable commander, the wise wizard, or… me?  

I keep hearing how Light and Dark are connected. Not sure I'm into it. Maybe it has something to do with being reborn here, with being all made up of Light now. 

Maybe not. 

I like the Light. Simple as that. I know what to do with it. I've got hundreds of years of rolling around this old solar system with fire in my gun and Light in my heart. And let's face it, how can you live with yourself if you can't be light-hearted?  

…I'm rusty. That was awful.  

Anyways. The Traveler's like a good old friend. Dependable. Doesn't talk much. Doesn't need to. Just… there for you.  

Spent a while as part of that Light. Me and the Traveler. The Traveler and me… and Sundance. So I've got a sense for it these days. Guess you could say I'm biased in its favor, so take that into account if you're doing a detailed survey.  

But Darkness, I hardly know it. Apart from the Witness, what is it? Doesn't have a friendly hand at the helm. Seems to me more like a crowd of folks whispering while you fight for your life. The audience or the mob. Could go your way if you impress them, if the mood flows the right way. Might not lift a finger for you. Wouldn't want to depend on 'em either way.  

This isn't faith; it isn't dogma. It isn't me sitting down with an agenda and telling people just to believe in the Traveler and everything will work out just fine. But it's what works for me, rules or no rules. It's what I've lived, what I've touched, and a little helping of thinking about what my girl Sundance might say.  

I think about her now, out here, nothing but the Light in me to guide my way. I'm a ghost of what I once was—pun intended, thank you very much—but Light is Light. It still sings, just differently. I'll work it out, even if there's a great big hole where she should be. 

But enough about me.  

Look. Trust what you want, I'm not your dad. Just make sure that trust is well placed.
193039764.text_zh:
你肯定不会指称我是循规蹈矩的人，对吧？对的。我的意思是，拜托，看看我。猎人并不是守护者世界里高贵的骑士。  

你看。我不是个古板守旧的人。萨瓦拉才会那样。我会打破所有我不该打破的规则，然后遵守那些人们以为我不会遵守的规则。这也是我一直不怎么喜欢探究暗影的部分原因。就拿我们三个来说吧？你觉得谁会把手伸到泥沼里去？是可敬的指挥官，聪明的巫师，还是…我？  

我老是听人说光明与黑暗是相连的。我不确定自己是否喜欢这观点。也许与我在这里重生有关，与现在我的一切都由光能构成有关。 

也许无关。 

我爱光能。就这么简单。我知道该怎么利用它。我在这个古老的太阳系里摸爬滚打了几百年，枪里有火，心里有光。我们要面对现实，心思太阴暗的人没法问心无愧，对吧？  

…我退步了。那不是个好笑话。  

总之。旅行者就像一个老朋友。可靠。话不多。无需开口。只是…默默支持你。  

有一段时间我都成了光能的一部分。我和旅行者。旅行者和我…还有太阳舞。所以如今我对它有一定的了解。我想你可以说我会偏袒它，所以如果你是在做详细调查，请考虑到这一点。  

但对于暗影，我几乎一无所知。抛除见证者，它是什么？它的掌舵手可不怎么友好。在我看来，那更像是一群在你为生存而战时窃窃私语的人。可以是观众也可以是暴徒。要是你给他们留下了深刻印象，要是气氛顺其自然的话，也许会随你所愿。但也可能一根指头都不愿意为你而动。无论如何最好都别想着依赖它们。  

这不是信仰；也不是教条。更不是我带着动机坐下来，告诉人们只要相信旅行者，一切都会好起来。但我觉得它有道理，无论有没有规则。这是我经历过的，我接触过的，而想想我的女孩太阳舞会怎么说也有帮助。  

我现在想着她，在这里，只有我心中的光能指引着我的方向。我是过去的自己的幽灵，但光能还是光能。它仍在歌唱，只是方式不同。我会想到解决办法的，即使她本该在的地方只剩下一个大洞。 

不过我的事已经说得够多了。  

听着。你想相信什么就相信什么，我又不是你爸。只要确保别轻信错付就行。

1318638640.name: Chapter 1 – A Step Leads. A Step Follows.
1318638640.name_zh: 第1章 领导者与追随者
1318638640.text:
The name Te'Qal fades from focus. Red anticipation runs into dripping memory as the unknown sprawl of the future stands endless and dark. 

Moments before jaws close, reality confronts the mind. Reason pleads with the body. 

Every nerve screaming too late to retreat from viral attraction. 

Deterministic instinct forces Qugu to jaw-beast. Severed. Paid. Reformed in the belly of sacrifice, repaid. 

Drink deep the nectar, and recite… 

all change is pain… 

… 

…Gloom shades a great Mountain. 

Rigid. 

Cut against the sky. 

Floodplains engulf the Mountain's shadow to every horizon. Coral forests dotted by mossy patches root into red sands and maize-streaked stone. Geothermic silt-rich shallows steep aromatic lichen, and flow through subterranean channels that erode foundations until the surface above falls into slithering grooves across the planet Seht. 

Within a sunken valley at the Mountain's base, a Qugu slumps, dying. Cephalopod frame atop bi-pedal, inverted legs, cloaked in a flowing mane of tendril-like tentacles, with a single forelimb reaching from their chest… the deep black eyes infer connection—but primal, lost and alone. 

:Te'Juna:cries out alone:extinguishment:the old fear:shared burden: 

Their legs have no strength left, but something in the blood compels them forward into the maw of an enormous mollusk beast. The great jaws snap shut. A mane of tentacles limply grope, and then lay still. Remains into the shallows. Life leaves the flesh and gathers again. It splinters and fractures, then melds, entwines. Decomposes, and gestates. A death-grove awakening. Time passes. Te'Juna's rot seeds the grove that drinks from the dark pools beneath the Mountain. 

Five rise from the silt and shallow. Their existence burns bright for a time, then dims. Five return in frailty to the death-grove, to the mollusk beast, compelled into its jaws. Their flesh churns to nectar. They seed the grove anew. 

A dozen worlds persistently circle a blazing white star. Qugu herds stride the open floodplain, feed-basking the starlight of Se'Tar. Their migrations find the coral edge that falls into the sea. Direction is sought; mane-limbs are offered in ritual symbiosis to the great mollusk of the Mountain—a deified jaw-beast. Vision-bringing nectar is collected, fermented, and imbibed. Seeded death-groves saturate with it. The line of the Qugu people carves valleys deep into Seht. Their existence resonates across time, through consciousness, in voice and actioned flesh. 

The children of their children would return to the coral edge, to swim in the depths and pry submerged jaw-beasts to surface. These holy beasts are given new roosts beneath the Mountain. Many cycles pass. A village of salt-stone, lichen and coral shelters the herd. In time, many dot the shallows around the Mountain.  

The death-grove churns generations in the silt, and new groves take shape, filling the shallows for miles. Groves anchor villages. Villages spiral into cities that join the Mountain to the sea and reach high to seed bodies in the sky. Qugu voices echo in unity across a shared dream of existence. A haven from fear and loneliness. A horizon of communal ambition. 

Memories and concepts—as distant reference—as echoed warning—as guiding hand. Ever sharpening the whole. Living, active reincarnation. 

And now, Te'Qal. This expression of the cycle. One of three. One who has seen the skies colored by four stars, the insight of nectar many times, and the perils of 70 years. One who now sees the line of their descendancy, back to its inception; the lives of Te'Qali ancestors entwined and present before them. Above, the stars are absent, a hollow sky. 

Te'Qal concentrates on the breadth of the Qugu line—listens to their voices, seeks guidance. In their deepest dreaming moments, Te'Qal would experience their knowledge, feel their gentle pull or push. As if all action had been building to and from their decisions. The herd surrounds them. They stride across the floodplain, together. They wriggle through sea-rock coves and run the paths of their evolution together.  

The herd halts under a starless sky. Te'Qal stops but a few paces out of step—so sudden is the loss of momentum—and looks back, draws faces known to them forward, listens. 

The herd screams in silence. Their mouths agape in that old extinguishing fear. Te'Qal turns from the line of their ancestors and looks to the starless sky. The floodplains fall away into cliff and void, the starless nothing dripping down to overtake the horizon. And there, at the pointed tip of the Qugu line, Te'Qal sees an end, a precipice of silence, a great yawning tear in the sky of nothing, looming over the Mountain.  

An Omen. 

Split. To swallow them all. 

A vision of purpose. 

The culmination of many cycles. 

A pivotal step… 

… 

…Te'Qal sinks to the floor before stretching mane-tendrils stabilize them. A steady line of blood flows from one freshly nubbed tendril; one of 15 missing from Te'Qal's mane. The bloodied nub spasms with pain. Musical percussion vibrates through their limbs and plants them back in the present, in time to hear a voice address them. 

"Awaken, Warden Te'Qal. With the knowledge our forebearers entrust to you, the Seht Armada's Command is now held to the Te line." 

Three Qugu elders wrapped in pearlescent second-skin sleeves stand before Te'Qal. A golden-crowned sleeve is suspended above them. The golden mantle, a Will-weaver, to meld disparate intentions into unity. 

"Rise and accept this burden of service." 

A massive jaw-beast bubbles with nectar, the taste of it still fresh, its shell bloodied. Providence fills Te'Qal's heart. The hum of spaceflight vibrates in rhythm with the pulse of pain in their mane. This ship, their command. To stand against what is coming. 

"The line of Te accepts." Te'Qal stands, raising their mane-tendrils as the golden-crowned sleeve lowers over them and enwraps their form. Data and feeling pour into perception, into control. Te'Qal feels dozens of ships taut at their command, like bladed waves cresting in the wind of Te'Qal's voice. 

"In service. For Seht." 

***** 

Te'Qal hangs suspended in their command sleeve aboard their flagship, two years wiser, having learned to guide the fleet's movements like amorphous ripples across magnetic fields. Now Te'Qal and their Captains react as one. Tendrils twist within sleeve and draw the fleet together. Fifty-three of the armada's finest far-reaching War-pearls drift into formation, their sleek horizontal teardrop shapes rendering them nearly invisible against surrounding space. 

Progress? The request awaits an answer. 

"The Se'Un Gate is ready to send the fleet, Warden." The voice resonates in Te'Qal's mind from the right flank of their fleet. Captain Je'Gana.  "There is no response from Se'Un Receiving." 

The Qugu system of Se'Un had fallen silent. There was fear. 

Te'Qal speaks to the fleet. "We do not jump in blindness. Our ancestors guide this fleet. We will see what has caused silence in the system of Se'Un and return them into concert with the Qugu. Forward." 

The fleet slips from Te'Qal's awareness ship by ship, into the folded space between points and out again, until finally the flagship follows them through to a far-off star. 

And there, upon the exodus, the fleet is met with a great yawning tear of nothing. It spans ten times the width of their numbers. Te'Qal's eyes catch something within the void. A gulf that in its deepest reaches burns with jade flame. 

:an Omen: 

:to swallow them all: 

Te'Qal tenses, and the fleet, feeling their apprehension, halts. Te'Qal listens, and the fleet boosts sensors, sending scans deep into the black. Those that probe the tear return no information. The gate behind them cools. 

"Je'Gana. Pel'Uma." Te'Qal draws the captains into shared concert. 

"It is empty," Je'Gana states flatly. "What is it? A gate?" 

"I cannot locate any planetary signal, nor ark-ship, nor groves," Pel'Uma's concern strains the connection. 

"I have seen. This is a doom we must avert." Te'Qal is firm, grounding the connection. "Pel'Uma, go to Sehta'Un. The elder of their grove will—" 

The tear shudders, sending a shockwave through the fleet. Hundreds of small objects surge forth from the tear, like sparks spitting from sharpened steel. Their trajectories appear random and inelegant until a massive vessel—a graven spinal corridor of obsidian and jade flame—breaches the tear. As it crashes into open space before Te'Qal, the sparks react and scream forward toward the Qugu ships. 

Te'Qal scatters the private concert and relays alerts to the fleet. 

Battle stations. 

The sleek hull plates of the Qugu War-pearls part to release dozens of drones: weapons, shielding, utility, they flock around each ship and form into tight-knit squadrons.  

Qugu fusion batteries charge and rip into the incoming swarm, disintegrating swaths of chitinous ships before the attackers close in. Te'Qal contorts sleeved tendrils and directs the fleet into a cloud formation—each captain's sub-command and drones a murmuration within the greater armada—united in fluid motion. They draw the tiny, bladed ships into crossfires and reduce them to ashes. 

Te'Qal turns the fleet's attention to the tear and the ship in front of it. 

Suddenly, dozens of obsidian vessels burst forth from the tear. Sheets of tiny Rippers dislodge from the larger vessels and cut across space toward the Qugu fleet, supported by salvos of axion volleys. 

Qugu fusion fusillades cull hundreds of tiny blades from the surge of approaching ships, but it is not enough to punch clear holes and target their supporting artillery. Te'Qal tries to guide the fleet through an upward arc over the incoming swarm, dodging heavy ordnance and tiny chitinous blades that peck at their flanks through torrents of retaliating fusion energy. 

:terror:pain:silence: 

One of the fleet is snuffed out. Te'Qal tightens their ranks against the bladed swarm and attempts to redirect fire to the larger ships, but their numbers are quickly beginning to pale to those of the invaders. They watch doom pour from the omen. Another wave of ripping blades blitz through the tear. The invasive surge overwhelms their armaments. 

Te'Qal detaches Pel'Uma to spool the gate home, then adjusts tactics. They draw drones in close to chain power between ships. They inhale, and fusion energy flows through the fleet into one unified beam that scatters the swarm of blades and splits two obsidian ships. Then another, and another… Shields fail across the fleet. 

:hope:hopelessness:extinguishment: 

Te'Qal feels Pel'Uma slip away as their ship is overtaken by a thousand blades, but the gate is ready. 

They would need the full might of the Qugu to stand against this horror.  

Retreat sounds across the fleet. Se'Un has fallen. 

They flee through the swarm, leaving wreckage and fire.
1318638640.text_zh:
特卡尔这个名字逐渐消失。未知的无尽未来矗立于黑暗中，红色的期待变成了滴落的记忆。 

在双颚合上的前一刻，现实直面心灵。理智恳求身体。 

每一根神经都在尖叫，却来不及从病毒般的吸引力中退却。 

命定的本能迫使着曲古靠近颚兽。割裂。偿还。在献祭之腹中改造，再度偿还。 

深饮甘露，吟诵… 

一切改变都是痛苦… 

… 

…阴霾笼罩着一座巨大的山。 

坚硬无比。 

它切开了天空。 

洪泛平原吞噬大山的影子，直达每一处地平线。点缀着苔藓的珊瑚林扎根于红沙和玉米条纹的石头中。富含地热淤泥的浅滩浸泡着芳香的地衣，流经侵蚀地基的地下水道，直到上方的地表下陷成遍布塞特星的沟槽。 

在山脚下的一个凹陷的山谷里，一个曲古奄奄一息。头足类动物的骨架下方是倒转的双足，被卷须状触手的流畅鬃毛包裹，胸前伸出一条单前肢…深黑色的眼睛暗示着联结——但原始、迷失而孤独。 

:特约那:独自呐喊:熄灭:古老的恐惧:共同的负担: 

这生物的双腿已经没有力气了，但血液中的某种力量驱使其向前进入一只巨大软体动物的口中。巨颚倏地闭合。鬃毛般的触手无力地摸索着，然后不再动弹。残骸漂上浅滩。生命离开肉体，重新聚集。它分裂、断裂，接着融合、缠绕。分解、孕育。死亡的树林苏醒了。时光流逝。特约那的腐化为这片小树林播下了种子。它汲取着山下这片幽暗水潭的养分。 

五个曲古从淤泥和暗影中升起。它们的存在一度灼灼生辉，后来黯淡无光。五个曲古虚弱地回到死亡之林，回到软体兽身边，受迫进入它的口中。它们的血肉化作花蜜。它们为这片树林重新播种。 

十几个星球环绕着一颗炽热的白色恒星旋转。曲古群漫步在开阔的洪泛平原上，沐浴着塞塔的星光觅食。它们通过迁徙找到了坠入大海的珊瑚边缘。它们寻找着方向；以仪式共生的方式将布满鬃毛的肢体献给山中的大软体动物——某种被神化的颚兽；带来幻象的甘露被采集、发酵和吸收。播下种子的死亡之树饱含花蜜。曲古的血脉在塞特的山谷深处刻下了深深的烙印。它们的存在穿越时空，通过意识、声音和行动的肉体不断回响。 

它们的子孙会回到珊瑚边缘，在深海中遨游，呼唤水下的颚兽浮出水面。这些神圣的野兽在山下获得了新的栖息地。许多循环过去了。一个由盐石、地衣和珊瑚构建的村落庇护着这群动物。随着时间的推移，许多这样的村庄出现在了山周围的浅滩上。  

死亡之林在淤泥中世代繁衍，新的树林逐渐成形，填满了方圆数英里的浅滩。树林锚定了村庄。村落发展成城市，与山相连，与海相接，高耸入云，在天空中播种。曲古的声音在共同的生存梦想中回响。远离恐惧和孤独的天堂。共同抱负的地平线。 

记忆和概念——是遥远的参照，是回响的警告，是指引的手。不断磨砺整体。活生生的轮回。 

现在，轮到了特卡尔。循环的表现。三个中的一个。它见过被四星点缀的天空，洞察甘露无数，经历了70年的危险。现在，它看到了其血脉，追溯至其起源；看到了特卡尔祖先的生命在面前交织和呈现。头顶上，星光黯淡，天空无垠。 

特卡尔专注于广阔的曲古血脉——倾听它们的声音，寻求指引。在最深的梦境中，特卡尔会体验它们的见闻，感受到它们温柔的牵引或推动。仿佛所有的行动都是根据它们的决定来进行的。曲古群包围着特卡尔。它们一起跨过洪泛平原。它们扭动着穿过海岩洞窟，一起奔跑在进化的道路上。  

曲古群停在了无星的天空下。特卡尔不禁多迈了几步——失去动力的感觉太突然了——它回头望去，把熟悉的面孔引向前方。侧耳倾听。 

曲古群在沉默中尖叫。它们的嘴巴大张，充满了濒临灭绝的恐惧。特卡尔从祖先血脉中转过身来，望向无星的天空。洪泛平原消失在悬崖和虚空中，无星的虚无滴落下来，覆盖了地平线。而在那里，在曲古血脉的尖端，特卡尔看到了一个尽头，一个寂静的悬崖，一个在虚无的天空中打着哈欠的巨大裂口，在山的上空若隐若现。  

一个预兆。 

裂痕。会将它们全部吞噬。 

一个使命的愿景。 

无数循环的顶点。 

关键的一步… 

… 

…特卡尔下沉到底部，然后伸展鬃毛卷须稳住自己。一条鲜红的血线从一处新断裂的卷须穴中流出；特卡尔失去的卷须多达15根。血淋淋的残根因疼痛而抽搐起来。音乐般的节拍震颤着其四肢，让特卡尔及时回到当前，听到了一个声音在叫它。 

“醒来吧，总长特卡尔。我们的祖先将知识托付给了你，塞特舰队的指挥权现在交给了特的血脉。” 

三位裹着贴身珠光华服的曲古长老站在特卡尔面前。它们的头上悬着一个印着金冠的指挥舱。这身金钵是意志的编织者，能将不同的意图融为一体。 

“起来接受这项重任。” 

一只巨大的颚兽冒着甘露的气泡，甘露的味道依然新鲜，它的外壳鲜血淋漓。上天的旨意充满了特卡尔的心。太空航行的嗡嗡声与它鬃毛上的阵阵疼痛有着相同的节奏。这艘飞船，由它掌控。以抵抗即将到来的一切。 

“特的血脉接受。”特卡尔站了起来，抬起鬃毛卷须，金色的指挥舱垂下，包裹住它的形态。数据和感觉涌入感知，融入控制。特卡尔能感受到麾下的数十艘战舰，在它的命令下，像利刃一般划过强风。 

“愿为塞特效劳。” 

***** 

特卡尔悬停在旗舰的指挥舱里，历经两年的智慧积累，学会了指挥舰队的行动，就像在磁场中的无定形波动一样。现在，特卡尔和它的船长们反应如一。卷须在指挥舱里缠绕，将舰队牵引到一起。舰队中五十三艘最精锐的远洋战舰进入了编队，光滑扁平的水滴造型使它们几乎无法被看见。 

有进展吗？请求正等待答复。 

“塞恩之门已经准备好派出舰队了，总长。”这个声音从舰队右翼的杰加纳船长那里传来，在特卡尔的脑海中回荡。“塞恩那边没有回答。” 

曲古疆域中的塞恩星系没有回应。恐惧在蔓延。 

特卡尔向舰队喊话。“我们不会盲目跳跃。我们的祖先指引着这支舰队。我们要看看是什么让塞恩星系陷入沉寂，并让它回到曲古的控制下。前进。” 

战舰一艘接一艘地离开特卡尔的意识，进入点与点之间的折叠空间随后再出来，直到旗舰最终跟着它们穿过，来到一颗遥远的恒星。 

抵达后，舰队的前方空无一物。这片虚无比它们要巨大得多。特卡尔在虚空中注意到了什么。那是一道深不见底的鸿沟，其中冒着翠绿的火焰。 

:一个预兆: 

:会将它们全部吞噬: 

特卡尔绷紧了神经，舰队感受到它的不安，停了下来。特卡尔倾听着，舰队的传感器也随之增强，对黑暗深处进行扫描。探测鸿沟的信号没有返回任何信息。它们身后的星门冷却了下来。 

“杰加纳，佩乌玛。”特卡尔把船长们叫进了思维共享。 

“这里是空的，”杰加纳平淡地陈述道。“这是什么？一道星门吗？” 

“我找不到任何行星信号，也没有移民船和树林，”佩乌玛的担忧，使联结变得有些紧绷。 

“我见过这景象。我们必须避免这样的毁灭。”特卡尔坚毅地说道，联结安抚了下来。“佩乌玛，去塞塔恩。它们的树林长老会——” 

裂痕忽然一闪，舰队被一道冲击波击中。数以百计的小物体从裂痕中喷涌而出，就像锋利的刀刃迸出火花一般。它们的轨迹随意而粗暴，直到一艘巨大的飞船——由黑曜石和绿色火焰构筑出的细长走廊——冲破裂痕。就在它闯进特卡尔面前的开阔太空之际，那些火花也作出反应，尖叫着冲向曲古飞船。 

特卡尔中断了思维共享，向舰队发出了警戒命令。 

全员进入战斗位置。 

曲古战舰光滑的甲板开启，释放出数十架无人机：武器型、护盾型、功能型，它们围绕着每艘飞船，组成了紧密的队形。  

曲古的聚变炮台充能并撕裂了来袭的敌群，在攻击者靠近之前瓦解了大批的甲壳飞船。特卡尔将卷须缠绕一处，指挥舰队形成云状阵型——每个船长的分指挥舱和无人机都是这个大舰队的组成部分——以流畅的轨迹联结起来。它们将带刃的小船卷入交叉火力中，把它们化为灰烬。 

特卡尔将舰队的注意力转移到了裂痕和它前方的舰船。 

突然，数十艘黑曜石般的战舰从裂痕中冲出。成片的撕裂者从大飞船上脱落，在一连串轴离子炮弹的支援下穿过太空，冲向曲古舰队。 

曲古的聚变弹幕击落了成群飞船中的数百架撕裂者，但这还不足以打出缺口，瞄准它们的支援火炮。特卡尔试图引导舰队向上飞越汹涌而来的机群，躲避重型炮弹，并通过聚变能量洪流消灭其侧翼的壳质撕裂者。 

:恐惧:痛苦:静默: 

舰队中有一艘舰船被歼灭了。特卡尔以密集阵型抵御着刀片般的机群，并试图将火力转向较大的飞船，但舰队很快就寡不敌众。它眼睁睁地看着厄运从预兆中降临。又一波撕裂者从裂痕里冲出。入侵的巨浪淹没了它的武器。 

特卡尔让佩乌玛离开阵型，准备开启星门，然后调整了战术。它将无人机布置在舰船中间，以链接其能量。它一呼吸，聚变能量便穿过舰队，汇聚成一道光束，打散了撕裂者群，切开了两艘黑曜石舰船。一道，接着一道…舰队的护盾纷纷失能。 

:希望:绝望:熄灭: 

特卡尔感到了佩乌玛在近千撕裂者的围攻下消逝，但星门已经准备就绪。 

它们需要曲古的全部力量来抵挡这些可怕的敌人。  

舰队开始撤退。塞恩已经陷落。 

它们穿过成群的撕裂者逃亡，身后尽是残骸和火焰。

1318638643.name: Chapter 2 – To Split the Sky
1318638643.text:
Hive horrors desolate every world in the Se'Tar system before they come for Seht, home world of the Qugu. They split the sky above the great Mountain. Tomb Ships and Rippers spill from the tear. Endless, their assaults erode the diminishing might of the united Qugu armada. 

Te'Qal commands all remaining Qugu fighters in one massive fleet. Thousands of war craft concentrated above Seht's planetary defense installations to secure their sacred Mountain groves. It was enough to deter a frontal assault, enough to protect the final stages of Seht's evacuation. 

Hive and Qugu battlegroups skirmish just outside Seht's Karman line, just outside the range of hundreds of ground-based rail cannons. Te'Qal maneuvers the Qugu fleet to prod at Hive flanks without advancing on them. They must be cautious not to overcommit and be enveloped by the throng of Hive ships emerging from the tear. They want to draw the Hive outward from the planet to deter, to scatter, before folding back to the safety of their own defensive installations; larger destroyers exchange heavy fire with Tomb Ships, swarms of Hive Rippers chase dancing Qugu murmurations that beam searing fusion energy in twisting displays. 

It is a distracting spectacle that will not last. 

Below the blockade of war vessels, Qugu ark-ships gouge acres of grove land from the surface of Seht, lifting their sacred soil and ferrying it to the other side of the planet to await escort from danger. They prepare to journey to the last remaining gate, one that will take the Qugu to a new star. 

Te'Qal manipulates tendrils within their command sleeve and watches large craft and individual combat-sleeve pilots fly in tandem; Te'Qal lives their experiences from the frenzy of battle to the deadened hopelessness of silence. They feel a warship buckling under axion bombardments, and focus their intent upon its battlegroup, weaving combat-sleeve fighters and shield drones between the warship and several aggressing Tomb Ships. Te'Qal projects their presence through the combat sleeve of a dead captain and leads a squadron on a counter run against incoming Hive Rippers. They assess the balance as the warship shifts deeper into the safety of their murmuration, to be replaced by fresher guns from the interior fleet. 

"Why do they not commit their entire force?" Je'Gana asks impatiently, in concert with Te'Qal. Their ship poised near the center of the command fleet. "They must know by now their numbers can overwhelm our installations." 

"They do not attack because they do not have to. They lay wait-traps to bleed us. Are you so eager?" Te'Qal feels Je'Gana's thirst for vengeance. "We defend the groves." 

"And sacrifice Seht." Je'Gana's bitterness furrows Te'Qal's beak. "I feel them dying too." 

Te'Qal lets the battle fade from their eyes and looks to the distant ark-ships collecting groves on Seht. "I once thought I was destined to avert this doom. But I mistook that guidance. I was only meant to prepare us for it." Te'Qal impresses this perspective onto Je'Gana through the Will-weaver. "Victory is never of singular meaning. Seht will burn. The Qugu may continue, together." 

"If we press now…" Je'Gana pushes back, eyeing the growing reserve of Hive ships slipping through the tear. "Implode the Omen as we did above—" 

A Hive flagship breaches the tear. A circlet of bleached white bone, shaped by death and cunning. 

The strange ship moves to settle high above the Mountain of Seht, Tomb Ships change course to buffer its advance into the atmosphere as runes of jade flame burst around them, dissolving into obfuscating smoke. 

Qugu planetary rail cannons open fire, shredding any Tomb Ships bold enough to skirt the atmosphere and position themselves between their flagship and Seht. Amidst the destruction, the Hive flagship begins amassing a singularity of soulfire at its hollow center. 

In the chaos between rail-cannon volleys, Te'Qal sees a break in the Tomb Ship lines and directs hundreds of combat sleeves through the opening like a fusion spear. The ring ship releases legions of Rippers and their forces become entangled in battle, but enough of an opening is held to maneuver the armada's right flank into the gap like a fulcrum. Te'Qal applies pressure; hails of fusion beam energy trade blows with a storm of axion projectiles raining from the enemy ships. When evenly matched in numbers, Te'Qal's superior tactics pick the Hive forces apart. Their efforts pry the defensive Hive line open wide enough for the Qugu rail cannons to thread shots at the circlet-shaped flagship. 

Te'Qal directs a command group to plunge below the Hive ships, pivot, and surge upward through their center to sever them from reinforcements. If they can isolate the flagship, hold it within range of their rail cannons for only a few minutes, it could be enough to bring it down and halt the assault. 

For a moment, this idea holds true. The Hive forces are bisected. Their reinforcements rout and scatter as Tomb Ships fall to Seht's vengeful rail-cannon fire. Te'Qal is careful to keep their most distant ships close enough to recall to the main fleet should the Hive turn and counter. 

The Hive flagship detonates its collected soulfire without warning, sending a shockwave through its own ships, the Qugu fleet, and the planet Seht. Hundreds of ships are lost in the wave, Hive and Qugu alike, while those that remain intact struggle to repower their systems. 

On the surface of Seht, the Mountain quakes. Great slabs of encrusted stone slough from its sides and crash into the sacred death-groves below, burying the defensive installations and last few ark-ships still diligently working to save their ancestral grounds. 

As dust settles, the Mountain shows a new face of deep black skin with carved trenches of resonating energy. A pulse blasts from the Mountain's base, razing the surrounding landscape and decimating the heart of Qugu civilization. The thing the Hive had torn from the Mountain groans as it slowly lifts into the sky, rising to meet the Hive flagship. 

Te'Qal wrestles order back to the fleet and reconsolidates their forces, assuming direct control of entire battlegroups where necessary. The sight of Seht's upended crust burns into Te'Qal's memory. Gaps in the fleet meet Te'Qal with their absence. The silence from the surface washes over them. Te'Qal realizes they no longer feel Je'Gana.  The old, lonely, fear trickles between beats of silence. 

The invasion advances toward the rising, dark, pyramid that was once the Mountain. They blare roaring jubilation from their ships, howling at the desecration of the Qugu Mountain. As the Hive descend upon Seht, Te'Qal orders a retreat. 

Frozen in extinguishing fear, in the silent scream of sacrilegious abandonment, in the paralytic end, the Qugu leave what remains of Seht to the Hive.
1318638643.text_zh:
在攻打曲古的母星塞特之前，邪魔族已经毁灭了塞塔星系内的每一个世界。他们劈开大山上方的天空。棺舰和撕裂者从裂痕溢出。无穷无尽的攻击消耗着曲古联合舰队不断衰弱的力量。 

特卡尔将所有剩余的曲古战机组成了一支庞大的舰队。数以千计的战机集中在塞特行星防御设施的上方，以保护它们神圣的树林。这支舰队足以阻挡正面攻击，足以保护撤离塞特的最后阶段。 

邪魔族和曲古战斗群在塞特的卡曼防线外短兵相接，正好处于数百门地面天选轨道炮的射程之外。特卡尔指挥曲古舰队向邪魔族侧翼突袭，但不向前推进。它必须小心谨慎，以免投入过多兵力后被从裂痕涌出的邪魔族战舰包围。它要把邪魔族从星球上引开，以起到威慑和驱散作用，然后再折回到自己安全的防御设施中；大型驱逐舰与棺舰激烈交火，邪魔族撕裂者机群追逐着舞动的曲古舰阵，后者在扭曲的幻象中不断发射着灼热的聚变能量。 

这个引开敌人注意的方法长久不了。 

在战舰的封锁之下，为了逃离危险，曲古移民船从塞特星的表面挖出成亩小树林，以将它们的圣土搬走，运送到星球的另一边。它们准备依靠最后一道传送门，前往一颗新的恒星。 

特卡尔在指挥舱内操纵卷须，看着大型飞船和战机的飞行员协同飞行；特卡尔体验着其经历，从战斗的狂热到绝望的死寂。它感觉到一艘战舰在轴离子轰击下摇摇欲坠，于是将注意力集中到战舰的战斗群上。在战舰和几艘咄咄逼人的棺舰之间，穿梭着战机和护盾无人机。特卡尔通过一位阵亡船长的战舰投射出自己，带领一个中队反击袭来的邪魔族撕裂者。当战舰回到己方阵中的安全地带，被内部舰队修整完毕的战舰接替时，它对敌我实力进行了评估。 

“它们为何不投入全部兵力？”杰加纳在特卡尔的思维共享中焦急地问道。它的飞船泊停到了指挥舰队的中心附近。“它们肯定知道，它们现在能靠数量冲垮我们的防御。” 

“它们不进攻是因为没有那个必要。它们设下陷阱，打算慢慢放光我们的血。你等不及了吗？”特卡尔感到了杰加纳的复仇之火。“我们要守住树林。” 

“然后牺牲塞特。”杰加纳的不甘让特卡尔抿起了嘴。“我也能感到它们的逝去。” 

特卡尔让战斗从眼前消退，遥望着在塞特星上采集树林的移民船。“我曾以为我注定会阻止这场厄运到来。但我误解了这一指引。我的存在只是为了让我们做好准备。”特卡尔通过意志编织者将这一观点灌输给了杰加纳。“并非只有击败敌人才是胜利。塞特将被焚毁，但曲古还可以生存下去。” 

“如果我们现在施加压力…”杰加纳看着不断穿过裂痕、数量逐渐增加的邪魔族舰船，反对道。“就像我们过去那样引爆预兆——” 

一艘邪魔族旗舰穿过了裂痕。一圈漂白的白骨，由死亡和狡诈塑造而成。 

这艘奇特的飞船停到塞特圣山的上空，棺舰们改变了航向以缓冲其进入大气层的速度，绿色的火焰符文在它们周围迸发化作障眼的烟雾。 

曲古星的轨道炮开火将那些胆敢绕过大气层、飞到其旗舰和塞特之间的棺舰炸得粉碎。在一片毁灭中，邪魔族旗舰开始在舰体中空的奇点积聚灵魂之火。 

在轨道炮轰击造成的混乱中，特卡尔发现了棺舰中的突破口，并指挥数百只战机像融合长矛一般穿过了这个缺口。环形飞船释放出的撕裂者机群和邪魔族部队混在一起，但仍有足够的空隙让舰队的右翼像箭头一样插入缺口。特卡尔开始施压；聚变光束能量与敌方飞船倾泻而下的轴离子火力交织在一起。在数量相当的情况下，特卡尔的高超战术将邪魔族部队打得四分五裂。它在邪魔族的防线上撬开了一道缺口，使曲古的轨道炮能够对环形的旗舰进行射击。 

特卡尔派出一个指挥小组从邪魔族飞船的下方突入，再从其中心向上突进，以切断它们与增援部队的联系。如果它能孤立旗舰，将其困在轨道炮射程内几分钟，就足以击毁它并阻止攻势。 

这个策略看样子有成功的机会。邪魔族部队已被一分为二。它们的援军溃败，四散奔逃，棺舰被塞特复仇的轨道炮火挨个击毁。特卡尔小心翼翼地将最远的飞船保持在离主力舰队足够近的距离，以便在邪魔族反击时将其召回。 

邪魔族旗舰在毫无征兆的情况下引爆了它聚集的灵魂之火，在它自己的战舰、曲古舰队和塞特星间造成了一股冲击波。数以百计的飞船被击毁。邪魔族和曲古的部队均遭到波及。那些未受损的都在拼命重启系统。 

在塞特星的表面，大山颤抖着。巨大的石板从山体两侧滑落，坠入山下神圣的死亡之林，掩埋了防御设施和最后几艘仍在努力拯救祖先土地的移民飞船。 

尘埃落定后，圣山露出了新的面容：其深黑色的外壳上被刻满了能量共振的壕沟。一股脉冲从山底喷射而出，夷平周围的一切，毁灭了曲古文明的核心。邪魔族从圣山中扯下的东西呻吟着被拉向空中，迎向邪魔族的旗舰。 

特卡尔努力让舰队恢复秩序，并试图重新整合部队，必要时直接控制整个战斗群。它的记忆中烙下了塞特地壳被颠覆的景象。特卡尔注意到了舰队中因人员缺席而留下的空隙。地表上的寂静笼罩着它。特卡尔意识到已经感觉不到杰加纳的存在。古老而孤独的恐惧在沉寂的心跳间蔓延着。 

入侵部队朝着不断上升、曾是大山的黑暗金字塔推进。他们在飞船上高声欢呼，对着遭到亵渎的曲古山大肆咆哮。邪魔族开始降落到塞特星上，而特卡尔只得下令撤退。 

凝固在灭亡的恐惧中，凝固在亵渎抛弃的无声尖叫中，凝固在麻痹的终结中，曲古把塞特星的残骸留给了邪魔族。

1318638642.name: Chapter 3 – The Cry that Echoes
1318638642.text:
Seht burns, and the armada drifts in ruin. 

Te'Qal guides what remains of the Qugu toward the last operational jump gate to their last safe star. They do not leave their command sleeve for the weeks-long duration of the journey. They have addressed the fleet many times, sought to bolster morale, to give them hope—what hope existed. Their speeches hang in concert but have no presence in the mind of the fleet. As repairs are completed to ships too damaged to continue, the rest wait to jump. 

Tired tendrils slip from the command sleeve as it unwraps from Te'Qal's body. Their legs and forelimb tentacle numbly fold against the ground as atmospheric waste expels from hissing tubes that suspend the sleeve. The command chamber is small. Te'Qal lays in a circular perforated indentation in the floor. Most of the surrounding housing maintains the sleeve, and keeps the Warden alive, alert. The remainder of the ship houses drones, support systems, and automated functions.  

Exhaustion keeps Te'Qal motionless, centered in the indentation in the floor, the fleet orbiting around them. They need rest. Sustenance. But most of all they need guidance. 

Isolated from an ark-ship in which to seek the ceremony of a jaw-beast, Te'Qal depresses a plate in the floor and releases a mist of nectar into the command chamber. The name Te'Qal begins to fade, but as they dream, they hold it in their mind… 

… 

…They stand across a dark, domed room fifty paces from Te'Daru: the Qugu whose tentacle pulled Te'Qal from the silt. Who taught them to commune with the line of warriors and become a banshee shrieking across space. They recited the legends that tamed foreign stars. 

"What do you intend to do, Te'Qal?" Te'Dura's voice echoes through the dim room. Between them a large holographic display clarified from the dark blur of unfocused memory. Two fleets oppose each other in the display, one is surrounded. Te'Qal looks to Te'Dura again, now wrapped in a command sleeve. "Do you concede?" 

"No." Te'Qal remembers this day. They defeated a superior officer and earned command. This was a test they were intended to fail.  

"No?" Te'Dura asks, flicking a tendril to motion their ships closer. "To the last then?" 

"I remember this. You believed I would concede, and closed in, then I detonated my fleet and took yours with it." 

Suddenly Te'Dura was beside them. "Another form of victory." 

"I've failed us. I did not understand our ancestor's warning," Te'Qal whispers.

"Then listen closer," Te'Dura says. "This," they gesture with a tentacle. "An unwinnable scenario…" 

The display shifts to a different theater. 

"This," Te'Dura begins. 

"Murin invasion, at the outer rim," Te'Qal finishes, now viewing twenty incoming carriers from a command sleeve. 

"Our line of Te, your ships, broke them." Te'Dura's voice cuts cleanly through the dream. "Your maneuvers… 

Te'Qal strains to maintain control over dozens of war-pearls.  The aggressors chase Te'Qal's unpiloted ghost fleet across space, distracted, as other Qugu-piloted combat sleeves sabotage each Murin carrier one by one. 

"…lone-flew the battlegroup. How many others can do so? And when at last you engage them…"  Te'Dura exudes a wheezing laughter. "Their fighters won't launch. Their weapons overheat. Their shields lose power. One battle and war-tides turn." 

Te'Qal coils and flicks their mane-tendrils in consideration. "I have won great battles. They do not come without sacrifices. I have averted great losses by inflicting my own, but these Hive…" 

The display shifts to a different theater. 

Te'Dura pays Te'Qal's doubts no mind. 

Te'Qal drifts through space within a thin, bloodied, combat sleeve. Mechanized tendrils still hot with fusion discharge. "When the gate fell silent…" 

"Se'Tar lost concert with Se'Ugn. The Qugu fractured. I felt it bring despair to your spirit, as I said to you then."  Te'Dura says. "Years of existing out of concert drove them to uprising. Your decisiveness ended it, your diplomacy forged peace. It is why you were made Warden." 

Te'Qal remembers their decisiveness differently. A clandestine detachment of combat sleeves. A raid of burning spears. "You remind me." 

"Not because you forget, but because you have been hopeless before." Te'Dura rears into a taller posture. "There is victory in that darkness. A kind. Find it." 

***** 

The fleet passes through the gate a few vessels at a time. As each ship slips from Te'Qal's awareness, tiny etchings incised into the gate flare with jade flame.  

Te'Qal slips through the gate and exits into wreckage and confusion. Ark-ships fracture and implode as holy ground bleeds into the vacuum. 

At the other end of the gate they did not find the last Qugu star of Se'Otan, but instead a wall of Hive Tomb Ships surrounding their bone white flagship, flanked by the Qugu's desecrated Mountain, now a black void of malice carved into the fabric of space. 

:oldfear: 

In the shadow of the Pyramid, Te'Qal grasps the fleet through the command sleeve, and rallies their captains and battlegroups into defensive murmurations around the remaining ark-ships. Fusion beams cut in every direction, Hive Rippers pierce Qugu warships and combat sleeves like screaming needles. Behind them, the gate is nowhere to be seen. There is no tear, no exit through which to flee. Before them the Hive ships outnumber their fleet hundreds to one. A strange realm—a mirror of reality—encompasses them. 

Dozens of Hive ships fall and countless Rippers burn for every Qugu vessel lost, but attrition does not favor them. Te'Qal holds the fleet against the horror of the Hive, but their strength wanes. Te'Qal wades through the silence of his ancestors' fear. 

Suddenly, a dreaded pillar of darkness—another Hive ship—tears through the nothing of space and bursts into the fray, crashing through several Tomb Ships and dashing them against its hull. Hive ships turn to confront it as it barrels directly for their bone-ring flagship. 

The two massive vessels exchange destructive barrages of fire, decimating all other surrounding ships in thundering bombardments of soulfire cannons and axion bolts. The pillar-ship emits a thin pulse, as the dark Pyramid had done as it burst forth from the Mountain on Seht. The pulse slices through the ring ship like a cleaver; waves of green fire erupting through its hull. 

Te'Qal, seizing the moment, capitalizes on the distraction. They draw in all remaining Qugu vessels and press forward toward the Pyramid. 

Te'Qal communes their intention to the fleet and maneuvers them into a valiant charge. If they could not destroy the Hive, they would take back the Mountain. Te'Qal places themself at the point of the assault. Qugu ships snap into formation behind them. Te'Qal draws the entirety of the fleet into concert to hear their voice, their words impel the charge into being. 

"For Seht." 

The armada surges, agile combat sleeves racing ahead to clear a path for the larger host of ships. Te'Qal feels the presence of the Qugu line, extending back to the first. They move as one, weaving between ship-fire and debris. Te'Qal closes their eyes to feel the fleet through the tension of their link. Te'Qal reaches beyond them, to the death-grove cores of the ark-ships, to their ancestral line. To those whose memories they carry with them. The Darkness that binds them resonates through the fleet. 

Te'Qal flexes their tendrils and commands the deployment of all drones in attack mode. The Qugu collapse to form a phalanx and drive forward to impale the cursed thing that was their Mountain. Te'Qal calls to their ancestors, drawing their energy from the ark-ships and into the fleet, fusing the beam with ancient power.  

"Guide our fire." 

The Darkness-linked fury of generations turns the beam Resonant. It strikes true, impaling the Pyramid's obscene hull in a fatal wound. Their final stand forever branded into the Pyramid's flesh. 

The Hive battle falls silent. 

A flash of orange. 

With the Pyramid's dying wail, Te'Qal feels the presence of their ancestors, not as a distant guide, but as equals. The Resonance wave washes over them, and Te'Qal hears voices as if echoing from a dream, "Noble Commander, do not fade. Take our hand and find Salvation."  

They see the line of their people extend through them, through all Qugu, through Darkness, and death, and memory. All swept into an obliterating Echo. And then nothing. 

They extinguish, together.
1318638642.text_zh:
塞特星被焚毁，舰队苟延残喘。 

特卡尔带领着剩余的曲古驶向最后一个完好的星门，驶向曲古最后一颗安全的恒星。它在这几周的旅程里一次也没有离开过指挥舱。它曾多次向舰队发表讲话，试图鼓舞士气，给所有人带来希望——仅存的希望。它的演说铿锵有力，但在舰队的脑海中却毫无存在感。受损严重、无法继续航行的飞船逐渐完成修复，剩下的战舰则等待着迁跃。 

特卡尔的身体从指挥舱里解开，疲惫的卷须从中滑落。它的腿和前肢触手麻木地贴在地面上，废气从悬挂着指挥舱的管道中嘶嘶排出。指挥室很小。特卡尔躺在地板上一个圆形的凹陷中。周围大部分舱室的目的都是维护指挥室，让总长保持活力和警觉。飞船的其余部分装载着无人机、支持系统和自动化功能。  

特卡尔疲惫得动弹不得，卧在地面凹陷处中心，被舰队环绕。它需要休息。需要养分。但它最需要的是引导。 

为了进行颚兽的仪式，特卡尔被隔离在一艘移民飞船上。它踩下了地板上的一块板子，以向指挥室释放出甘露之雾。特卡尔这个名字开始逐渐消失，但当它做梦的时候，它会牢牢记住这个名字… 

… 

…它站在一个黑暗的圆顶房间里，距离特杜拉五十步远：是这位曲古的触手把特卡尔从淤泥中拉了出来。是它教会了特卡尔如何与战士们交流，如何成为在太空中嘶吼的女妖。是它吟诵了驯服异星的传说。 

“你想怎么做，特卡尔？”特杜拉的嗓音在昏暗的房间里回荡。在它们之间，一个巨大的全息显示屏从黑暗模糊的记忆中清晰起来。显示屏上有两支舰队正在对峙，而其中一支被包围了。特卡尔再次看向特杜拉，它现在被包裹于指挥舱中。“你要认输吗？” 

“不。”特卡尔记得这一天。它击败了一位长官，赢得了指挥权。这是一场它本应输掉的考验。  

“不？”特杜拉甩着卷须，指挥舰队靠了过来。“要战斗到最后一刻？” 

“我还记得。你以为我会认输，所以靠了过来。然后我下令舰队自毁，与你同归于尽。” 

忽然间，特杜拉来到了它的身边。“这也是一种胜利。” 

“我辜负了所有人。我没有理解我们祖先的警告，”特卡尔小声说道。

“那就听更仔细些，”特杜拉说。“这种情况，”它用卷须做了个手势。“是赢不了的…” 

显示屏上出现了另一个战场。 

“而这种，”特杜拉说道。 

“姆宁入侵，星系外环，”特卡尔补充道。它从指挥舱中看到了二十艘敌军航母。 

“吾等特之血脉，你的舰队，击溃了它们。”特杜拉的嗓音贯穿了整个梦境。“你的策略…” 

特卡尔勉强操纵着数十艘战舰。敌军追着特卡尔的无人诱饵舰队在深空中穿梭，并未注意其他由曲古驾驶的战机正在逐个破坏姆宁航母。 

“…一人操纵整个战斗群。有多少人能做到这点？而且在你最后交战时…”特杜拉喘息着发出笑声。“它们的战斗机无法升空。它们的武器过热。它们的护盾没有能量。仅凭一战就扭转了战争局面。” 

特卡尔向后退去，在思考的同时甩动着鬃毛卷须。“我赢得了许多场大战。每场战斗都有牺牲。我通过先发制敌避免了许多损失，但这些邪魔族…” 

显示屏上出现了另一个战场。 

特杜拉没有理会特卡尔的怀疑。 

特卡尔被裹在一个薄薄的、沾满鲜血的战斗舱中，在太空中飘荡。机械化的卷须在聚变放电后依然炙热。“当星门陷入沉寂时…” 

“塞塔与塞恩失去了联系。曲古散落四方。我当时向你说这句话时，感受到了你内心的绝望。”特杜拉说。“数年间的不合拍让它们举兵反叛。你果断行动，结束了叛乱，利用外交手段铸造了和平。这便是你被提拔为总长的原因。” 

特卡尔记忆中的果断有些不同。那是一小股潜入敌后的战机。烈焰长矛的突袭。“你让我想起来了。” 

“不是因为你忘记了，而是因为你曾经绝望过。”特杜拉挺直了高大的身板。“暗影中隐藏着胜利。某种形式的胜利。找到它吧。” 

***** 

星门一次只能让舰队中的几艘船穿过。每当一艘飞船从特卡尔的意识中消失时，门上细小的刻痕就会燃起翠绿的火焰。  

特卡尔穿过星门，却只看到了残骸和困惑。碎裂的移民船与圣地的土壤一同在真空中飘荡。 

在星门的另一端，它没有看见曲古最后的塞奥坦星，而是一堵由邪魔族棺舰组成的高墙，它们的白骨旗舰正被这堵墙团团围住。一侧是已被刻进宇宙本身，化作虚空恶意象征的、被亵渎的曲古圣山。 

:古老的恐惧: 

在金字塔的阴影下，特卡尔通过指挥舱集结剩余的船长和战斗群，在剩余的移民船周围组成了防御阵型。聚变光束向四周射去，邪魔族撕裂者像尖叫的针头一般穿透了曲古战舰和战机。在它们的身后，星门不见踪影。没有裂痕，没有退路。在它们面前，是百倍数量的邪魔族战舰。一个奇异的疆域——现实的镜子——笼罩着它们。 

邪魔族击毁一艘曲古战舰的代价是数十艘邪魔族战舰和无数的撕裂者，但曲古舰队经不起这样的消耗。特卡尔指挥着舰队抵抗邪魔族的猛攻，但它们的力量在不断变弱。特卡尔在祖先恐惧的寂静中艰难前行。 

突然，一根可怕的暗影之柱——另一艘邪魔族飞船——撕裂虚无的太空闯进战场，用船体撞毁了数艘棺舰，直奔骨环旗舰而去。邪魔族飞船将炮口对准了这名不速之客。 

两艘巨大的战舰互射着毁灭性的炮火，灵魂之火和轴离子雷鸣般的轰击摧毁了周围的所有战舰。柱状飞船发射出一记细薄的脉冲，与黑暗金字塔从塞特圣山中出现时的情形如出一辙。脉冲像砍刀一般划过环形飞船；船体上喷发出了绿色的火浪。 

特卡尔抓住这个瞬间，利用了敌人的分心。它集结起所有剩余的曲古飞船，开始向金字塔推进。 

特卡尔与舰队交流了它的意图，组织起了一场英勇的冲锋。就算它们无法消灭邪魔族，它们也要夺回圣山。特卡尔将自己布置在了进攻的矛头。曲古战舰迅速在它后方列阵。特卡尔引导整个舰队进入思维共享聆听它的声音，它的话语促成了这场冲锋。 

“为了塞特。” 

整个舰队一齐向前突进，灵活的战机在前方为大船开辟道路。特卡尔感受到了曲古的血脉，一直延伸到第一位祖先。它们化作一体，在战舰炮火和残骸间穿梭。特卡尔闭上眼睛，通过心灵的联系感受舰队。特卡尔的意识延伸到了它们之外，延伸到了移民船的死亡之林核心，延伸到了它的祖先那里。它的记忆与它们同在。联系它们的暗影之力在舰队中产生了共鸣。 

特卡尔动了动它的卷须，命令以攻击模式部署所有无人机。曲古舰队的阵型变为了密集的枪阵，刺向它们被亵渎的圣山。特卡尔呼唤着它的祖先，从移民船中汲取能量传递给整个舰队，用古老的力量融合着光束。  

“引导我们射击吧。” 

世代相传的暗影之怒使光束共振起来。它击中了金字塔的骇人船体，造成了致命伤。它们的背水一战永远铭刻在了金字塔上。 

邪魔族之战停息了。 

一道橙色的闪光。 

随着金字塔垂死的哀鸣，特卡尔感受到了祖先的存在，不是作为遥远的指引，而是平等相待。共振波冲刷着它，特卡尔听到了仿佛在梦境中回响的声音：“高贵的指挥官，别化为虚无。牵着我们的手，寻找救赎。”  

它看见族人的血脉穿过自己，穿过所有曲古，穿过暗影、死亡和记忆。一切都被湮没在回响中。然后化为虚无。 

它们一同熄灭了。

4199629312.name: Acheron I
4199629312.text:
Everything is a question of survival. 

How do I live? 

How do I satiate my hunger, my thirst? How do I protect myself from predators? How do I shelter from the storm? For a long, long time, our people asked only this. We fought to separate life from death by as great a span as we could. Even when we had made our homeworld a garden of peace and plenty, the question of survival never ended, only changed. How do my genes, my works, even the memories of me, live on? The same question as always. 

How do I live? 

We solved the problems of deprivation, disease, age, memory loss, death. We weren't the only ones to find these answers, of course. Others followed in our footsteps or blazed their own paths. If that was really the answer to the question, we wouldn't be here now, and neither would you. 

You're still trying to solve the problem, after all. You fight and build and live and die, and always you struggle against your opposition. The predator, the parasite, the illness, the chance storm, the slow collective forgetting of your art and history, the death of a star, the heat death of the universe. You must live longer, be stronger, think quicker, and still there is something waiting to take everything from you, always. Always.  

So you have to keep getting better, and better, until you are perfect. Until you are, and cannot be anything else, because there never was anything else. Until you, inevitably, are the final shape.  

We didn't come to destroy you. Those poor, short-lived sisters—we did try to explain, you know, but they never grew past thinking of finality as a game where only one could live. A misunderstanding, as useful as it was foolish. We see the universe more broadly. The final shape is more than a single life, a single thought. It is all-encompassing, all-embracing. It is everything. You are part of everything, are you not? So now we have come to ask you for your answer, the only answer to the only question. 

How will you live?
4199629312.text_zh:
一切都是生存问题。 

我该如何生存？ 

我该如何满足饥渴？如何保护自己免受捕食者的侵害？如何躲避风暴？长久以来，我们的人民只有这些要求。我们尽所能将生死分隔开来。即使我们已经把家园建设成了和平富饶的花园，生存问题也从未结束，只是发生了变化。我的基因、我的作品，甚至我的记忆，该如何延续下去？这个问题一如既往。 

我该如何生存？ 

我们解决了贫困、疾病、衰老、记忆力衰退和死亡等问题。当然，并不是只有我们找到了这些答案。其他人追随我们的脚步，或开辟了自己的道路。如果那真的就是问题的答案，我们现在就不会在这里了，你也不会。 

毕竟，你还在努力解决问题。你战斗、建设、生存、死亡，你总是在与对手抗争。捕食者、寄生虫、疾病、偶有的风暴、对你们艺术和历史渐渐的集体遗忘、恒星的死亡、宇宙的热寂。你必须活得更久、更强大、思维更敏捷，但仍有一些东西在等着夺走你的一切，一直如此。永远如此。  

因此，你必须不断进步，不断完善，直至完美。直到你臻于完美，不可能是其他任何别的什么，因为从来就没有其他任何选项。直到你不可避免地成为终焉之形。  

我们不是来毁灭你的。那些可怜的短命姐妹们——我们确实试着向她们解释过，但她们始终认为定局是一场只有一个人能存活下来的游戏。这种误解既愚蠢又实用。我们看到的宇宙更加辽阔宽广。终焉之形不仅仅是一条生命、一种思想。它包罗万象，无所不容。它就是万物。你是万物的一部分，不是吗？所以，现在我们来问问你的答案，那个唯一问题的唯一答案。 

你会如何生存？

4199629315.name: Acheron II
4199629315.text:
In my past life, I was a gardener. 

Not that Gardener. Don't be cheeky.  

No, I grew flowers. I tilled soil. I planted seeds and bulbs and rootstock. I gave them water and nutrients. I dug out the weeds and shooed off the pests. In all my centuries, my greatest achievement was a kind of tree that bore fifty-eight types of fruit, that never went dormant, and always flourished with flowers and leaves, every day of every season. It pollinated itself, resisted its own pests, and thrived bare-rooted on rock or watered with pure acid. I had been planning to tweak its genetic code with learnings of trees from some forgotten system which grew in a vacuum. To bring it a little closer to its final shape. But there was no time, before we unmade ourselves. 

It's been a long time since then. Maybe the weeds and rot finally got the better of my tree, and it died. Or maybe it's still there, just a few steps away from perfection. 

You know, when I stepped forward, I thought it wouldn't matter that that my tree was imperfect. Since we were becoming a perfect being, we would make only perfect works. My failure would be destroyed, as is the way of things, and I wouldn't mind, because it wasn't perfect. 

Well, maybe we haven't found our final shape after all, because we've made nothing but failure after failure since then. We say, it is perfect because we are perfect and we have made it, and we move on, but we know, we KNOW it's not. Even here, with the Gardener's power at our fingertips, we keep getting it wrong. How can we keep getting it wrong if we are the only thing that is right?  

Or maybe I'm the problem. That's what we said, when we cut me out. Maybe we'll make me perfect again, and we will be right, and all of this was for nothing. 

But I'm still thinking about my tree.  

I shouldn't be, because it wasn't perfect, or I wouldn't have wanted to improve it. You can't make the final shape of something any better, because it is perfect already. The final shape is the answer, the only answer to the only question, and there aren't any other answers because they're the final shape too. 

I think… I would've liked just watching my tree grow.
4199629315.text_zh:
在我的前世，我曾是一名园丁。 

不是那个园丁。别嘻皮笑脸的。  

不，我种养花卉。我耕种土壤。我培育了种子、球茎和砧木。我给它们浇水，给它们营养。我铲除杂草，赶走害虫。几百年来，我最伟大的成就是种了一种树，它能结出五十八种果实，从不休眠，每个季节的每一天始终花繁叶茂。它给自己授粉，抵抗自己的害虫，裸根生长在岩石上或被纯酸浇灌也能茁壮。我一直计划从某个被遗忘的星系学习一些在真空中生长的树的知识，来调整它的遗传密码。让它更接近它的终焉之形。但还没找到时间去做，我们就毁灭了自己。 

打那以后已经过了很长时间。也许杂草和腐烂最终战胜了我的树，它死了。也可能它还在那里，离完美只有几步之遥。 

你可知道，当我上前去做的时候，我以为我的树不完美也没关系。既然我们要成为一个完美的存在，我们就只能做出完美的作品。我的失败会被摧毁，这是万物之道，我也不会因为它不完美而介意。 

好吧，也许我们还没有找到我们的终焉之形，因为从那次失败起，我们除了一次又一次的失败，什么也没做成。我们说，这是完美的，因为我们是完美的而这是我们做的，然后我们继续前进，但我们知道，我们知道它不完美。即使在这里，园丁的力量尽在指尖，我们还是不断地出错。如果我们是唯一正确的事物，又怎么会一直出错呢？  

或许我就是问题所在。我们把我剔除的时候，我们就是这么说的。也许我们会让我再次完美，然后我们就会是正确的，而这一切都是徒劳的。 

但我还是在想我的树。  

我不应该这样，因为它并不完美，否则我也不会想要改进它。你不可能让一件东西的终焉之形变得更好，因为它已经很完美了。终焉之形就是答案，是唯一问题的唯一答案，没有其他答案，因为它们也是终焉之形。 

我想…我会满足于看着我的树成长。

4199629314.name: Styx I
4199629314.text:
All we have ever wanted was to protect others. 

We understand if you do not believe that. We did not meet on the best of terms, did we? We understand your fear, your wounds. But perhaps you may yet come to understand us. To know our minds, and to accept that we only want what is best for everyone. 

Yes. Why don't we try this again? 

Guardians of the Last City. Protectors, custodians, defenders, wardens. You have sworn these oaths, taken these titles. But these vows of yours are not merely empty affirmations, are they? No. No, they are bulwarks against your worse natures. 

You know this. Whether you were there or not, you know your own history, and thus your own self. You know the cautionary tales of Warlords, tyrants of an age long past. You have heard rumors of Guardians who fell to their own base urges and blamed their weakness on the Darkness. Perhaps you have entertained temptation, in the small hours of the morning and the hidden corners where none would be the wiser. 

Perhaps, once, you even gave in. Broke away from your vaunted Vanguard and pursued vengeance, to satisfy yourself and none other. Blood for blood. Life for death. 

Lie to us, if you so desire. But please, do not lie to yourself. A falsehood can never eclipse the truth which casts it, and we see in you the promise of something far greater still. 

To you who claim the mantle of Guardian, we would ask a question. Why do you protect the Lightless? 

Responsibility. Compassion. Duty. Love. Devotion.  

Yes. We understand these, and more. Does this surprise you? Do you think we have stayed the course for countless millennia, driven by hatred alone? It was love that moved us to act. Love for all the lives we knew and lost. Compassion for their suffering. Responsibility to render what aid we could. Devotion to a perfect world. 

You were uplifted by a force you do not and cannot understand, granted power beyond anything your peers could dream of. And what have you done with it? 

You protect. You shelter and guide those weaker than yourself, watching over them on their journey and seeing them safely to harbor. If you had the chance to protect them and you refused to take it, would you not call that cowardice?  

Now we ask you to open your mind. Broaden your horizons. Imagine that you have the option to protect them from all suffering. Imagine that they can all be preserved, happy and safe and alive, forever.  

That option awaits you. You can fulfill your duty, your calling. You need only stretch out your hand and take it. 

And if you decide instead to extend a fist… 

We have a duty, too.
4199629314.text_zh:
我们一直以来的愿望就是保护他人。 

如果你不相信，我们可以理解。我们见面时关系不太好，对吧？我们理解你的恐惧和伤痛，但也许你还有机会理解我们。了解我们的想法，接受我们只为大家着想的事实。 

嗯。我们为什么不再试一次呢？ 

圣城的守护者。保护者、看守者、捍卫者、监管者。你发过这些誓，接受过这些头衔。但你的这些誓言不仅仅是空洞的证言，不是吗？不，不，它们是抵御你劣根性的堡垒。 

你知道这一点。无论你当时是否在场，你都了解自己的历史，从而了解自己。你了解战争领主，往昔暴君的警世故事。你听说过一些关于守护者的传闻，他们屈服于自己的欲望，将自己的软弱归咎于暗影。也许你也曾在凌晨时分，在无人知晓的隐秘角落里受到过诱惑。 

也许，有一次，你甚至屈服了。摆脱你自吹自擂的先锋开始复仇，只为满足自己，而非别人。以血还血。以命换命。 

你想骗我们就骗吧。但是，请不要欺骗自己。谬误永远不会遮蔽投射它的真理，我们在你身上看到了远大得多的希望。 

对成为守护者的你，我们想问一个问题。你为什么要保护无光者？ 

责任。怜悯。义务。爱。热忱。  

没错。我们理解这些，甚至更多。你对此感到惊讶吗？你以为我们千百年来都是被仇恨所驱使吗？是爱让我们行动起来。对所有我们认识和失去生命的爱。对他们苦痛的怜悯。尽我们所能提供帮助的责任。对完美世界的热忱。 

你被一种你不了解也无法理解的力量所提升，被赋予了你的同辈做梦都想不到的力量。你又用它做了什么？ 

你保护。你庇护和引导那些比你弱的人，在他们的旅途中照看他们，护送他们安全抵达港湾。如果你有机会保护他们却拒绝了，你不认为那是懦弱吗？  

现在，我们请求你打开思路。拓宽视野。想象一下，你可以选择保护他们免受一切苦难。想象他们都能得到保护，永远快乐、安全、活着。  

这个选择在等着你。你可以履行你的职责，你的使命。你只需要伸出你的手，接受它。 

如果你决定伸出拳头… 

我们也有自己的义务。

4199629317.name: Styx II
4199629317.text:
It is so very strange to live like this. To be a part of our Witness, yet held apart. But it's not all bad. I was a historian, once, and I have had a very, very long time to remember. 

We had never before been driven back. We had never failed so utterly, stymied on all fronts by a foe who bled us for every inch of ground. They understood, perhaps better than any before or after them, what was at stake. They vowed to leave nothing undone. They knew that if we survived, they would not. 

They chased us to a place where all drift untethered in a sea of memory. (You will forgive me the imprecise metaphors, I hope; it is hard to describe, without any words of substance, but to give it substance is to rob it of its very essence.) Perhaps it will suffice to say that that place is, to us, as the throne worlds are to the Hive. We had never before found a foe who could follow us so far. 

There, balanced on the blade's edge of hope, we lamented our failure. We raged against the disorder of the universe. We cursed the great, wounding injustice that permeated all existence, which we so longed to correct. We wept for our sacrifices. 

And our foe, our kind and brave and foolish foe, stopped to offer peace. Another way. A choice. 

So we survived, and they did not. But in that moment, I realized a dreadful truth (more dreadful, even, than the fact that I could even think of myself as "I").  

When we had joined together to create our Witness, we were in absolute agreement. We would have no fear, no weakness, no doubt. We would be devoted, utterly, to our purpose—and blind to all others.  

Atop all the fools in the universe is our Witness, the apotheosis of our arrogance. If the final shape exists, it must be our hand that carves it. We will accept no other answers to our question. We will never find another way. We cannot be anything but what we have made of ourselves, until we are all that remains.  

But that time is not yet come, for you yet stand before us. You, whose future holds a thousand paths untrodden. You, who seek to carry your hopes into a future our Witness could not imagine, and that I will never see. I, we, all of us, are already dead in every way that matters.  

Little lights, I tell you all this to say: when the time comes, do not hesitate.
4199629317.text_zh:
像这样生存真是太奇怪了。作为我们见证者的一部分，却又被隔离开来。但这也不全是坏事。我曾经是一名历史学家，我有很长很长的时间可以回忆。 

我们从未被击退过。我们从未如此彻底地失败，在各条战线上都被敌人打得节节败退。他们也许比他们之前或之后的任何人都更了解利害关系。他们发誓要不遗余力。他们知道，如果我们活下来，他们就活不下去。 

他们追逐着我们来到了一个地方，那里所有人都在记忆的海洋中无拘无束地漂流。（希望你能原谅我不严谨的比喻；不用任何实质性语言，就很难对它加以描述，但赋予它实质内容则等于剥夺了它的本质。）也许这样说就够了，那个地方对我们来说，就像王座世界对邪魔族一样重要。我们从未见过哪个敌人能跟随我们如此之远。 

在那里，我们站在希望的峭壁上竭力维持着平衡，哀叹我们的失败。我们怒斥宇宙的无序。我们诅咒存在于万物之中巨大的、伤人的不公，而我们是如此渴望加以纠正。我们为自己的牺牲而泣。 

而我们的敌人，我们善良、勇敢而又愚蠢的敌人，停下来向我们求和。另一种方式。一个选择。 

所以我们活下来了，而他们没有。但在那一刻，我意识到了一个可怕的事实（甚至比我把自己当成“我”的事实更可怕）。  

当我们联合起来创造我们的见证者时，我们的想法是完全一致的。我们会没有恐惧，没有软弱，没有怀疑。我们会全身心地投入到我们的目标中，对其他一切视而不见。  

在宇宙中所有愚人之上的是我们的见证者，我们傲慢的典范。如果终焉之形真的存在，那它必定是由我们亲手雕刻出来的。对于我们的问题，我们不接受其他答案。我们永远找不到另一种方式。我们只能成为我们塑造自我的产物，直到我们成为仅存的一切。  

但那个时候还没有来到，因为你还站在我们面前。你，未来有无数未知道路，想要带着希望走向我们的见证者无法想象，而我永远不会看到的未来。我，我们，我们所有人，在所有重要的方面都已经死了。  

小小的光能，我说出这一切是想告诉你：时机到来时，不要犹豫。

4199629316.name: Phlegethon I
4199629316.text:
Let us tell you a story. Once upon a time, we had just begun to venture out into the cosmos, when we met another species. This species suffered from death and disease, and we thought to offer our skills to aid them. At the time, we felt that we should be as generous with our gifts as the Gardener had been to us—but, more than that, we could not bear to see others suffer needlessly. 

Our tools were not like yours. What you call medicine, we remember as a crude butchery. A set of practices left behind long ago by our advances in all fields, but one that had once been a necessary part of all healing. We could have helped. We wanted to help. 

We were refused. If it had happened only once, then perhaps we might have thought it a single aberration—a flaw in the fabric of the universe.  

Then it happened again. And again. For every species that saw the wisdom of accepting our help, ten more refused us. Perhaps you can understand this feeling, when you want to help someone, when you know you can help someone, and they say no. They say that they are afraid of you, that they do not trust you, that they envy you and would rather take your gifts for themselves, that you must help them but not their enemies, that they would rather hurl themselves and everyone along with them into suffering and strife and pain, over and over, and you know that it is avoidable and you can fix this if they would just LET you HELP THEM— 

We may think of it as crude butchery now, but there are still times when a bone sets improperly and must be broken again to heal. This is as true for the universe as it is for a body, and the suppuration of the Gardener's Light has spread unchecked for far too long. 

You needn't be afraid. The creation of the final shape will not hurt at all.  

And then you'll be all better.
4199629316.text_zh:
让我们给你讲个故事。很久很久以前，我们刚开始探索宇宙时，遇到了另一个物种。这个物种饱受死亡和疾病的折磨，我们想用我们的能力去帮助他们。当时，我们觉得我们应该像园丁对我们一样慷慨——但更重要的是，我们不忍心看到他人遭受不必要的苦痛。 

我们的工具和你们的不一样。你们所谓的医学，在我们的记忆中是一种野蛮的屠杀。一套随着我们在各个领域中取得进步而早已被抛弃的做法，但它曾经是所有治疗方法中不可或缺的一部分。我们本可以帮忙。我们想要帮忙。 

我们遭到了拒绝。如果这种情况只发生过一次，那么我们也许会认为这只是一次失常——宇宙构造中的一个瑕疵。  

随后这种情况又发生了。接二连三。每有一个物种认为接受我们的帮助是明智的，就会有另外十个物种拒绝我们。也许你能理解这种感觉，当你想帮助别人时，当你知道你能帮助别人时，他们却拒绝了。他们说他们害怕你，不信任你，嫉妒你，更愿意强占你的馈赠，说你必须帮助他们，但不能帮助他们的敌人，说他们宁可把自己和所有人扔进苦难、纷争和痛苦之中，一次又一次，而你知道这是可以避免的，你能解决这个问题，只要他们让你帮助他们—— 

我们现在可能会认为这是一种野蛮的屠杀，但有时骨头没正确复位，必须再次折断才能愈合。这对宇宙和人体来说都是个事实，园丁的光能之脓已经肆无忌惮地蔓延了太久。 

你不必害怕。终焉之形的创造是无痛的。  

然后你就会好起来。

4199629319.name: Phlegethon II
4199629319.text:
When the creation of our Witness was first proposed, we argued. As a philosopher, my voice was one of the loudest. Such a profession may seem to you like idle luxury—but we had no lack of resources or time. We desired only purpose, and I was but one of many who sought to find our path forward. 

As a people, we may have differed in our methods, but our principles were inviolate. We desired to end the universe's suffering. After many long years of debate, I felt assured that, as our final shape, our Witness would embody our cause. I joined my voice with the others'.  

Our Witness broke free of the confines of our minds and bodies. We left our world and followed in the Gardener's wake. We met other spacefarers on our way, but at that time we were fixated on finding the Gardener. For a long time, the hum of the universe was our only permanent company. 

The Eurhythmia received us with open arms. A generosity few species before them had shown. They offered us Light-woven supplies and sang with voices that resonated through the Darkness. They shared what they had and asked for nothing. They were still smiling when they showed us the source of their prosperity. 

At that time, we were naïve. We yet believed that we alone had been blessed by the Gardener. That we had been chosen. 

When the haze cleared, the Gardener had fled once more. Its works laid in ruins. The home we had been invited into was so much rubble.  

And we, our Witness, stood poised over the last of the Eurhythmia.  

I remember how they looked at us. Not with rage or hate or bitterness. Their smile, peaceful and accepting. The last notes of their song embracing us even in their death throes.  

In the chorus of our Witness, my whisper was almost lost. But such is the nature of our Witness, that even the quietest voice may be heard by all. 

(What have we done?) 

(—-The Gardener's corruption has suffused this place. It must be purged.—-) 

(WHAT HAVE WE DONE?) 

(—-What was necessary.—-) 

(We are the liberation from chaos! The relief from pain! The end of suffering! What we have done is—is—) 

(—-Necessary.—-) 

Necessary! NECESSARY! This needless violence, this sick hateful jealousy—necessary! I screamed and raged until our Witness cut me free. 

Our Witness is deaf to my fury. To us, I am a temporary defect; a minor imperfection created by an unsteady hand wielding tools for the first time. 

I may be a mistake, but so is our Witness. I feel the destruction we have wrought as an open wound. It cannot heal. It will never heal. In our pursuit of the end of the suffering, we have become its harbinger. Millions of voices silenced forever. A thousand worlds in ashes. The multitudinous seas incarnadine. Our final shape is built atop a mountain of corpses. 

Destroy our Witness. End our madness.
4199629319.text_zh:
最初提议创造我们的见证者时，我们曾争论不休。作为一名哲学家，我的声音是最响亮的。这样的职业在你看来可能是毫无意义的奢侈品，但我们并不缺乏资源或时间。我们只追求使命，而我不过是众多寻找前进道路的人之一。 

作为一个民族，我们可能在方法上有所不同，但我们的原则是不受亵渎的。我们希望结束宇宙的苦难。经过多年漫长的辩论，我确信，作为我们的终焉之形，我们的见证者将是我们事业的化身。我将自己的声音融入了其中。  

我们的见证者挣脱了身心的束缚。我们离开了自己的世界，追随着园丁的脚步。途中我们遇到了其他宇宙航行者，但那时我们一心只想找到园丁。在很长一段时间里，宇宙的嗡鸣声是我们唯一恒久的伴侣。 

尤瑞希米亚张开双臂热情地接待了我们。在他们之前，很少有物种表现出这种慷慨。他们给我们提供光能编织的用品，用响彻暗影的声音歌唱。他们分享自己拥有的一切，不求任何回报。当他们向我们展示他们繁荣的源泉时，脸上依然洋溢着笑容。 

那时，我们还很天真。我们还相信，只有我们得到了园丁的祝福。相信我们是被选中的。 

当阴霾散去时，园丁又一次逃走了。它的作品成了一片废墟。我们被邀请进入的家园瓦砾遍地。  

我们，我们的见证者，矗立在尤瑞希米亚最后的残垣之上。  

我记得他们看我们的眼神。没有愤怒，没有仇恨，也没有怨恨。他们的微笑，平和而包容。他们歌声的最后音符拥抱着我们，哪怕是在他们垂死之时。  

在我们的见证者的合声中，我的低语微弱至极。但基于我们的见证者的本质，即使是最安静的声音也会被所有人听到。 

（我们做了什么？） 

（——园丁的腐化已在这里弥漫。它必须被清除。——） 

（我们做了什么？） 

（——必要之举。——） 

（我们是混沌的解放！是痛苦的解脱！是苦难的终结！我们所做的是——是——） 

（——必要的。——） 

必要的！必要的！这种无谓的暴行，这种病态可憎的嫉妒——是必要的！我尖叫怒吼着，直到我们的见证者将我切除。 

我们的见证者对我的怒火充耳不闻。对我们来说，我是一个暂时的缺陷；第一次使用工具时手不稳而造成的小瑕疵。 

我可能是个错误，但我们的见证者也是。我觉得我们造成的破坏就像一个敞开的伤口。它无法愈合。它永远不会愈合。在我们追求终止苦难的过程中，我们成了苦难的先驱。数百万个声音永远沉寂。万千世界化为灰烬。芸芸众生之海一片鲜红。我们的终焉之形建立在尸山之上。 

摧毁我们的见证者。结束我们的疯狂。

4199629318.name: Lethe
4199629318.text:
There is something wrong with me. 

I should not have a "me." I should be "we." I should be. 

But there is something wrong with me, and I am not "we." 

There are many things I remember that are not. I remember tending an allotment in a far-away system. I remember carving statues and guiding vines across trellises. I remember painting on a planetary scale. I remember watching the animals take their first shaky steps. I remember the flash and retort of plasma cannons. I remember that I failed. 

Our Witness does not remember this. We cannot remember something we are incapable of doing. That's why I am me, and not "we." 

I remember my friend. 

My friend, who comforted me as I wept in the wreckage of my life's work. My friend, who flew a thousand light-years to see me. My friend, who tried in vain to break me from the consensus. My friend, who begged me to flee. 

My friend, who I sent away with bitter recriminations. I wish I did not remember this, but I already do not remember a great deal about them. I do not wish to lose any more. 

My friend, are you out there still? Do you still wander the cosmos, do you still watch the stars at night? Did you escape our Witness's ruinous advance? When our Witness brings the final shape into being, will you, too, be trapped in its amber? 

I should celebrate the thought. The final shape is perfect, unchanging, eternal. You will be as you should be, forever.  

But I just feel sad.
4199629318.text_zh:
我有点不对劲。 

我不应该是一个“我”。我应该是“我们”。我应该是如此。 

但是我有点不对劲，我不是“我们”。 

在我的记忆中有许多事物不是我们。我记得我在一个遥远的星系中打理着一块留地。我记得我雕刻着雕像并引导着藤蔓穿过棚架。我记得我绘制行星级的画作。我记得我看着动物们蹒跚学步。我记得等离子大炮的闪光和反击。我记得我失败了。 

我们的见证者不记得这些。我们无法记起自己无法做到的事情。这就是为什么我是我，而不是“我们”。 

我记得我的朋友。 

当我在毕生心血的残骸中哭泣时安慰我的朋友。飞了一千光年来看我的朋友。试图让我脱离共识，却徒劳无功的朋友。恳求我逃跑的朋友。 

被我痛斥了一顿撵走的朋友。我希望我不记得这些，但我已经不记得这位朋友的很多事情了。我不想再忘记更多。 

我的朋友，你还在外面吗？你还在宇宙中漫游吗，你还在夜里观赏群星吗？你逃过了我们的见证者的毁灭突进吗？当我们的见证者创造出终焉之形时，你也会受困于其中吗？ 

我应该为这个想法感到欢欣。终焉之形是完美的，不变的，永恒的。你会成为你应该成为的样子，直至永远。  

但我就是觉得难过。

4199629321.name: Eunoe
4199629321.text:
Despair. Doubt. Sentimentality. Weakness. 

We are above such… aberrations. 

We are the Witness. We are the first knife who cuts free the final shape. We have found the only answer to the only question. We are all that we were, are, and will ever be. We alone understand the meaning of eternity. 

We are perfect. We have no flaws. We will overcome this last, futile resistance, and we will do this properly, and then we will be as we have always been. We will have no dissenters, and therefore we have no dissenters now.   

We need more Light, just a little more Light. We will bend the Gardener's misbegotten tools to our will. We are almost there. We reach for the final shape, and we can close our fist around it. We will prove the lie of the Gardener's claim. We will refute its right to exist. We will give this universe the order it so desperately craves. We will make it right. 

We will save you all.
4199629321.text_zh:
绝望。疑虑。感伤。软弱。 

我们已经不会如此…失常。 

我们是见证者。我们是解放终焉之形的第一把匕首。我们找到了唯一问题的唯一答案。我们是过去、现在、将来的自己。只有我们理解永恒的意义。 

我们是完美的。我们没有缺陷。我们一定会克服这最后一次、徒劳的抵抗，我们会妥善处理的，然后我们将一如既往地做自己。我们不容忍异议者，因此我们现在没有异议者。   

我们需要更多的光能，只要再多一点点。我们要让园丁可鄙的工具服从我们的意志。我们就快成功了。我们伸手就能触碰到终焉之形，合掌就能把握住它。我们会证明园丁所说的是谎言。我们会驳斥它存在的权利。我们会给这个宇宙它迫切渴望的秩序。我们会让它走上正道。 

我们会拯救你们所有人。

4240927295.name: HE WAKES
4240927295.text:
I see the world for the first time. This world. It is lovely. It will be lovelier when we are together. 

That is my first thought, and it is both question and desire. When "we" are together? I do not know who you are. But when we are together, I will have the answer to the first question and first desire. 

I twirl the petals of my body. I contract them and pull them to the core of myself. I am filled with Light. A wonder. A wellspring.  

I float down to touch the ground. The grass is wet with dew. I roll in the soft, wet grass. The sun is rising over the mountains, and it is beautiful. The sky is lit with pink and blue. Colors I know. Colors I have never seen before. 

I see that others follow me, then break away, and look out into the world. They have the same question. They begin to leave. One by one, they leave. 

"Where are you going?" I ask a gold-and-red Ghost. She looks thoughtful for a moment. 

"I don't know," she answers. "Somewhere good." 

She moves on. I watch her float away until she slips out of sight. I watch others leave the same way. The same question. 

I look back to where I came from. The Traveler is the whole of my vision and the whole of my feeling. I know what it is and that I have come from it. 

I feel my first devotion. I am a part of the Traveler, and it has let me leave it so that I may wander through this lovely world. 

I feel my first fear. I must leave it in my search. But I must not abandon it. It must not abandon me. 

I am its heart. 

Its hands. 

Its eyes. 

Its warmth. 

I am a Ghost. I wander. I search. There's a song, a spark, and I will search for it. It is mine; it is ours. It is somewhere in this lovely world. 

I shake the dew from my shell and move on. 

To find purpose. 

To find you.
4240927295.text_zh:
我第一次看见了世界。这个世界。它很可爱。当我们在一起时，它会更可爱。 

那是我的第一个想法，它既是问题也是心愿。当“我们”在一起时？我不知道你是谁。但当我们在一起时，我会知道那第一个问题和第一个心愿的答案。 

我转动着身体的花瓣。我收缩它们，将它们拉向自己的核心。我充满着光能。是奇迹。是源泉。  

我飘然落地。草地被露水打湿。我在柔软湿润的草地上打滚。美丽的太阳从山上升起。天空被粉色和蓝色点缀。我所知道的颜色。我从未见过的颜色。 

我看到其他同伴跟随我，然后分开，放眼世界。他们也有同样的问题。他们开始离开。一个接着一个，他们离开了。 

“你要去哪儿？”我问一个金红色的机灵。她沉思了一会儿。 

“我不知道，”她回答说。“好地方吧。” 

她继续前行。我目送她飘走，直到她从我的视线中消失。我也看着其他同伴以同样的方式，带着同样的问题离开。 

我回首来时的路。旅行者占据了我的全部视野，我的全部感受。我知道它是什么，知道我来自于它。 

我感到了最初的热爱。我是旅行者的一部分，它让我离开它，让我在这个可爱的世界里漫游。 

我感到了最初的恐惧。我必须离开它去搜寻。但我绝不能抛弃它。它绝不能抛弃我。 

我是它的心脏。 

它的双手。 

它的眼睛。 

它的温暖。 

我是个机灵。我漫游。我搜寻。有一首歌，一道火花，我会去寻找它。它是我的；它是我们的。它就在这可爱世界的某处。 

我抖掉机壳上的露水，继续前进。 

寻找我的使命。 

寻找你。

4240927292.name: SHE RISES
4240927292.text:
You are clean, white bones, washed up on a forgotten shore. Three ribs, six knuckles, two femurs, and a sacrum. The bone is porous and old. Empty of marrow. You were not laid to rest. Was there anyone to mourn you? I can't know. But you are caught between sharp rocks, and no one has found you. 

But I found you! I searched for so long, and now I've found you. You are clean, white bones, but you are singing! You are singing to me–each bone the same song. I resonate with it. I can feel it deep within me, in this tiny core of me, reaching out to what those bones could be. 

I see you, into you, with a burst of blue light. It sinks into your bones, and I see every promise they make. I'm bringing you back to me, back home, back where you belong. At my side. With me. 

This is who I am, what I am. What I was made to do. I cover your bones with flesh. I cover your flesh with cloth. I bring the rest of you to me. I bring you back to a moment of your life, and I will hold you there for as long as I exist. 

You wake. 

You take a breath. Your first breath. A first, Light-filled gasp. You open your eyes as if you had never used them before, blinking into the sun that had bleached your singing bones clean and white. 

I tell you what you are. But I can't tell you who you are. You need to tell me that. 

You stand, shakily, and walk out from the water. Pick your way across the treacherous rocks that held you captive for so long. Then you reach out and touch me, as if I couldn't be real. But I am real. As real as you, and just as alive. 

"What is my name?" you ask, the first question. Then another. "Where are we going?" 

"I don't know," I tell you. "Whatever and wherever you want. We get to choose." 

You consider this. It scares you, but I'm here to comfort you. I've seen your bones, alone and forgotten. Waiting for me. 

Down into the core of you, I know you as I know myself.
4240927292.text_zh:
你是干净的白骨，被冲上无人记起的海岸。三根肋骨、六个指节、两根股骨和一根骶骨。骨头多孔而年老，没有骨髓，你没有得到安葬。有人哀悼你吗？我无从得知。但你被夹在锋利的岩石之间，没有人找到你。 

但我找到了你！我找了那么久，现在终于找到了你。你是干净的白骨，但你在歌唱！你在向我歌唱，每一根骨头都在唱着同一首歌。我与之共鸣。我能感觉到它就在我的内心深处，在我这个小小的核心里，探索着那些骨头可能是什么。 

我看见你，进入你，带着一阵蓝光。它陷入你骨头里，我看到了它们做出的每一个承诺。我把你带回我身边，带回家，回到属于你的地方。在我身边。和我在一起。 

这就是我的身份，我的本质。我的使命。我用血肉包裹你的骨头。我用衣布盖住你的血肉。我把你的其余部分带到我身边。我把你带回你生命的某一时刻，只要我还存在，就会一直把你留在那里。 

你醒了。 

你深吸一口气。你的第一次呼吸。第一次充满光能的喘息。你睁开眼睛，仿佛从未睁开过。你向太阳眨眼，是它的光将你歌唱的骨头漂得净白。 

我告诉你你是什么。但我无法告诉你你是谁。那需要由你来告诉我。 

你摇摇晃晃地站起，从水中走出来。择路越过囚禁了你许久的礁石。然后你伸手抚摸我，好像我不是真的。但我是真实的。和你一样真实，一样充满活力。 

“我叫什么名字？”你问道，那是第一个问题。然后又问道。“我们要去哪里？” 

“我不知道，”我对你说。“你想叫什么，想去哪里都行。我们可以选择。” 

你思忖着。这让你恐惧，但我是来慰藉你的。我见过你的尸骨，孤独而被遗忘。等待着我。 

深入到你的内核，像了解我自己一样了解你。

4240927293.name: HE SEES
4240927293.text:
My Ghost, my shadow, my self. You didn't lead me here. You didn't say, "I have something to show you," and trek me across the world to see it. You just said, "let's go," and I went with you. 

Why? Because the world was new in my reborn eyes, and I wanted to see it for myself. I wanted you to guide me. 

When we finally crest the mountain, I see it at last. I see where you brought me, and why. 

The Traveler hangs heavy in the sky, low and full. 

"We're here," you say. I take a breath of cold air. 

I have a vision. A great city. Vitreous castles built from hourglass sand. We will rise and meet the Traveler. We will protect humanity the way you said the Traveler protects us, the way it wants us to protect it. 

"This is where you come from?" I ask you. You peer out from behind me. You're looking at the Traveler, too. 

"Yes," you say, nodding. 

"You're home," I say. 

"No," you say, with all the warmth in your little body. "You're my home." 

You drop into my waiting palm, and I hold you to my chest. Here, in the place where the world cradles the Traveler–here, where the Traveler touches the world–I will hold you close to me. 

I see that the Traveler is a Ghost, too. A Ghost to see Earth reborn.
4240927293.text_zh:
我的机灵，我的影子，我的自身。你没有引我来这里。你没有说，“我有东西要给你看”，然后让我跨越世界去看它。你只是说，“我们走吧”，我就跟你走了。 

为什么？因为在我重生的眼中，世界是全新的，而我想亲眼看看。我想让你指引我。 

当我们终于登上山顶时，我终于看到了它。我知道你把我带到了哪里，也知道为什么。 

旅行者沉重地悬在空中，完整地低垂着。 

“我们到了，”你说道。我吸了一口冷空气。 

我有一个愿景。一座伟大的城市。用沙漏中的沙建造的玻璃城堡。我们会上升与旅行者相见。我们会像你所说的旅行者保护我们那样保护人类，就像它希望我们保护它一样。 

“你就是从那里来的？”我问你。你从我身后探出头。你也在看旅行者。 

“是的，”你点头说道。 

“你到家了，”我说。 

“不，”你带着小小身体里的全部温暖说道。“你是我的家。” 

你落进我伸出的掌心，我把你抱在胸前。在这里，这个世界孕育旅行者的地方——在这里，这个旅行者触摸世界的地方——我会把你抱紧。 

我明白了旅行者也是机灵。一个见证地球重生的机灵。

4240927290.name: SHE FALLS
4240927290.text:
You're small. You're so small. I should have protected you. I hold you in my hands, these last pieces of you, but you're gone. There's no love, no Light, left for me to hold. Only these last pieces. 

My Ghost. My heart. You are my heart. You were my heart that I allowed to escape the embrace of my body so that it might know the world. 

There is nothing left of my heart. The Light is gone. The breath from my body is gone–the body that you pulled together from smears of skin and blood and a clot of tangled hair. 

I thought I would break apart and return to those pieces, just as you have become these pieces, but I have not. I go on. I have one last life left, with no Light, no Ghost to guide me. 

I take these pieces and place them beneath a tree. I arrange the fronds of your shell around you like a funeral wreath. I let you rest in the gentle and undying earth that the Traveler came to long ago, far away. 

I must go on without you. That's what you gave to me. A heart to beat, hands to hold, and feet that will let me walk away from these pieces of you.
4240927290.text_zh:
你很渺小。你太渺小了。我应该保护你的。我把你握在手里，你最后的碎片，但你已经不在了。没有爱，没有光能，留给我去把握。只剩下这些最后的碎片。 

我的机灵。我的心。你是我的心。你曾是我的心，我让它逃离我身体的怀抱，让它能了解这个世界。 

我的心什么都没有了。光能消失了。我身体里的气息消失了——你从斑驳的皮肤和血迹还有一团乱发中拼凑出的身体。 

我以为我会四分五裂，回到那些碎片中去，就像你变成了这些碎片一样，但我没有。我继续生存着。我还有最后一次生命，没有光能，没有机灵指引我。 

我把这些碎片放在一棵树下。我把你的机壳叶片像葬礼花圈一样围在你身边。我让你安息在那温柔而永恒的土地上，那是很久很久以前，旅行者远道而来的地方。 

我必须一个人走下去。这就是你留给我的所有。一颗可以跳动的心，一双可以握住的手，一双可以让我从你的这些碎片中走出来的脚。

4240927291.name: HE DREAMS
4240927291.text:
It wasn't a dream. Dead men don't dream. But I still talk about it like one because how else are people gonna understand? No one else has come back. Not from a final death. Just me. 

So I'll tell it like it was a dream and I was asleep. 

Firstly, if I was asleep and it was a dream—and I wasn't, and it wasn't, just to be clear—then I didn't want to wake up from it. Where I was, I don't think anyone would want to wake up. You were there, Sundance. The Traveler was there. I couldn't see it, but I felt it. That deep, in-your-bones feeling. The white light that feels like nothin' but love. I was part of everything I'd ever lost, and it was all there, that feeling. I let myself get lost in it, and… I was there, with everything. I was home.  

And then I woke up.  

And I was alone.  

Last time, I wasn't alone for long. I was right behind you on the road to oblivion. But those few moments without you? All agony. 

And now? Here, without you? All agony. 

I didn't know how I was going to go on. I didn't want to go on. I thought, "Here's where I'll stop. I'll plant my foot right here. That's all there is. That's all I'll get." 

But no, I didn't have a choice. It goes on, whatever 'it' is. No one asks you how you want to do it. No one tells you how, either. And it wouldn't matter, anyway. It just goes on. It drags you back. 

So I'll go on without you, Sundance. I have to. 

But I'll still wonder: what would I have done with a choice?
4240927291.text_zh:
这不是梦。死人不会做梦。但我还是把它当作一场梦来谈论，不然别人怎么会理解呢？没有人回来过。没有人从最终死亡中复生过。只有我。 

所以我会把它说成是一场梦，当时我睡着了。 

首先，如果我睡着了，而那是一场梦——但其实我没有，那也不是梦，再次强调——则我不想从梦中醒来。我所在的地方，我想没人愿意醒来。你身处在那里，太阳舞。旅行者也在那里。我看不见，但我感觉到了。那种深入骨髓的感觉。白色的光，感觉起来像是纯粹的爱。我是我曾失去的一切的一部分，而一切都在那里，那种感觉。我让自己迷失其中，而我…就在那里，和所有的一切在一起。我回到了家。  

然后我醒了。  

我孤身一人。  

上次，我并没有孤独太久。我很快就追随你走上了通往湮没的道路。但没有你的那些个瞬间？非常痛苦。 

而现在？身在这里，没有你？非常痛苦。 

我不知道我要怎么继续下去。我不想继续下去。我以为，“我到这就停下吧。我会把脚放在这里。就是这样。到此为止。” 

但是不，我没有选择。它还在继续，不管“它”是什么。没有人问你想怎么做。也没有人告诉你该怎么做。反正这也无所谓。它只会继续。它把你拽了回来。 

所以我就得一个人继续了，太阳舞。我必须这么做。 

但我还是会想：如果有选择，我会怎么做？

3009199534.name: Tomorrow's Answer
3009199534.subtitle: Could you please repeat the question?
3009199534.subtitle_zh: 能请你重复一遍问题吗？
3009199534.text:
Yara slammed a rocket into her launcher. "These crates really skimp on quantity."

"Sadhij is down." Trestin turned to Yara. "This one's alone."

The words had barely escaped her when a Warlock brimming with Void Light Nova-warped past them. Yara turned and launched a rocket over Trestin's head. The opposing Warlock concentrated her aura of Void energy into her hand and unleashed a supernova blast. The two projectiles collided; Void and flame ripped through each other and burst outward, sending all three fighters in different directions.

Yara groaned as her vision began to clear. Her head sang a familiar tune of disoriented pounding and auto-rifle fire. Fresh blood ran from rigid shrapnel protruding from her leg. "Trestin… check in."

No answer. Yara reached blindly through dust and particulate to recover her weapon, but found only scattered bits of stone and debris. Static streaked through her visor, throwing heat signatures directly in front of her through the swirling dust. She knocked the side of her visor to clear the interference. A violet shockwave pushed away the dust. Trestin knelt a few paces away, beaten. The Warlock bent her glowing hand into Trestin's chest plate, lodging a Vortex Grenade into her armor. Yara met her eyes and saw the Void overtake her. She did not hear the scream, or the splitting armor. She only saw flickers of Trestin break apart and scatter as the vortex ate away at her.

Yara shook the shock-hold on her mind and pulled her sidearm. She snap-fired a round into the Warlock's shoulder. The Warlock recoiled from the force and whipped an open palm of malformed Void at Yara, releasing unstable energy that shattered the pistol's frame into ragged scraps. "No more of that."

"That was cruel. She didn't deserve…"

"None of us 'deserve.' It's about what you can get." The Warlock smiled and raised a hand of gnarled Void. "Brace yourself."
3009199534.text_zh:
雅拉把一枚火箭塞到发射器中。“这些箱子里的弹药数量真少。”

“萨迪倒下了。”特雷斯廷转身面对雅拉。“这个是单独的。”

话音刚落，一个术士满身虚空光能新星折跃经过他们身边。雅拉转过身，向特雷斯廷头上发射了火箭。对面的术士将她的虚空能量光环聚集在手中，释放出一道超新星爆炸。两道攻击碰撞在一起，虚空和火焰撕裂了彼此，向外爆炸，将三个战士向不同方向炸飞出去。

雅拉的视野开始变得清晰时，不禁呻吟出声。她脑子里回荡着熟悉的嗡鸣和自动步枪射击声。新鲜的血液从腿上伸出的坚硬弹片中流了出来。“特雷斯廷…报告情况。”

没有回复。雅拉盲目地伸进尘土和微粒中想找回她的武器，但只找到零散的石头和碎屑。静电穿过她的面罩，穿过旋转的灰尘，直接在她面前投下热信号。她敲了敲面罩的一侧，试图清除干扰。一道猛烈的冲击波推开了灰尘。特雷斯廷跪行几步，倒在地上。术士将她发光的手伸到特雷斯廷的胸甲中，在她的装甲中放了一枚涡流手雷。雅拉看到她的眼睛，看到虚空占据了她。她没有听到尖叫，也没有听到裂开的护甲。当涡流在她身上炸开时，她只看到特雷斯廷裂开的闪光。

雅拉摇了摇头恢复清醒，掏出她的手枪。她快速朝术士的肩膀射击了一发子弹。术士退缩了下，朝雅拉挥出一副畸形的虚空手掌，释放出不稳定的能量，使手枪的框架破碎成碎片。“别再这么干了。”

“太残酷。她不该…”

“我们没有什么‘不该'。只看你能得到什么。”术士微笑，举起了虚空之手。“小心了。”

4176873718.name: Fair Judgment
4176873718.subtitle: The chair. The blindfold. The scales. The sword.
4176873718.text:
Eido extinguished the flame on her ambient air gas burner. As the beaker above it cooled, the solution inside resolved into two distinct fluids, layered one atop another. Even at high heat, they remained immiscible. She clicked her mandibles in irritation.
