[未知1: 02] “放轻松”的意思是停下。你支离破碎，只会让情况变得更糟。 

[未知2: 01] 前方仍有敌人推进，扫描未完成。 

[未知1: 03] 你的火力战队已经没了。如果我不能把你送回高塔建立连接，扫描也没有意义。 

[未知2: 02] 攻击来袭。 

[伴随着强效超因果放电，监控被嘶嘶的杂音覆盖，紧接着是三发硬弹的爆裂声。] 

[未知1: 04] 别动。你只会让情况变得更糟。 

[未知2: 03] 谢谢你，守护者。光谱分析已完成。 

[未知2: 04] 猎人先锋的推测是正确的。 

[未知1: 05] 乌鸦通常都是对的。什么推测？ 

[未知2: 05] 尽管是未知类型的嗤魅，但这些敌人是活的。此外，他们体内的黑暗乙太中检测到了旅行者的辐射。因此其起源可能是超因果的。 

[未知2: 06] 需要通过红桃杰克监控进行验证。 

[未知1: 06] 安静点。确保他们不会暗中接近我。 

[未知2: 07] 在费克鲁类型出现的地方，圣城的埃里克斯尼族都有危险。 

[未知1: 07] 我们知道。我们会找到他的。 

[未知2: 08] 守护者尚未发现终结那个单位类型的有效方法。 

[未知1: 08] 说点有用的话。 

[未知2: 09] 我鼓励你通过战斗寻求确证。 

[未知1: 09] 沙克斯，我知道你会听每一条记录。你的朋友要把我给吓坏了。

1427680276.name: Shadestalker Mark
1427680276.subtitle: In history's long shadow.
1427680276.text:
Undead screeches bounce off the ruined walls of Riis Reborn, carried by blizzard winds that obscure any path to safety. The small band of Eliksni got separated from the rest at the jetty and fled down this abandoned ally. A Salvation Ketch could barely defend itself from these pale monstrosities; what chance did they have? 

A second molt is unable to hold her composure; her antennal glands leak as her mother holds her close. Her clicking purr is hushed, just enough to voice comfort. 

"I can smell your fear." 

Above them, metal creaks under the Revenant's weight. One Dreg begins to scurry away, but his knee is pinned to the ground by a spear. 

"Do not weep," it sings, so close his mandibles rake the Dreg's respirator. "Rejoice. Today you will be made whole." The undead hulk salivates as the small band huddles together. 

A neon cord catches the aberration's carapace, pulling it up into the air by an unseen hand. 

The mother shields her brood's eyes as bitter ichor erupts from the undead's throat. Two more piercing rounds, in quick succession, see him sinking into the snow, now loosed from the ephemeral thread. 

The second molt breaks away to see a Slayer Baron, as if from an ancient epic, stepping through the gale. 

"Mother!" She chitters in relief. "A fate weaver from your stories!" 

The snowdrift clears, revealing the upright figure's alien anatomy. "Not my stories. A new one."
1427680276.text_zh:
不死者的尖啸声在重生的里斯的废墟墙壁间回荡，暴风雪将它传得更远，也遮蔽了任何通向安全的路径。一小群埃里克斯尼族在栈桥和大部队走散，逃进了这条废弃的小巷。救赎双桅船都几乎无法抵御这些苍白的怪物，他们又哪有机会呢？ 

一个幼儿无法保持冷静，她的触角腺体渗出液体。她的母亲紧紧抱住她，咔嗒着用勉强能被听见的咕噜声传递着安慰。 

“我能闻到你的恐惧。” 

他们上方的金属在亡魂的重量下吱吱作响。一名堕落者士兵开始逃窜，但他的膝盖被一支长矛钉在了地上。 

“不要哭泣，”那声音唱道，他如此接近，下颚刮擦过了堕落者士兵的呼吸机。“欢欣吧，今天你会变得完整。”当他们紧紧抱在一起时，不死者巨物垂涎欲滴。 

一根霓虹绳索缠住了畸形怪物的甲壳，仿佛有无形的手将它拉入空中。 

不死者的喉咙喷出腥气的液体时，母亲遮住了幼儿的眼睛。接连两发穿甲弹之后，他倒在雪地里，从短暂的束缚中解脱了。 

幼儿挣脱开来，看到一名如同古老史诗中走出的杀手公爵，穿过狂风而来。 

“妈妈！”她安心地咔嗒道。“是你故事里讲过的命运编织者！” 

大雪渐渐平息，揭示出矗立身影的外星躯体。“不，这是一个新的故事。”

96550318.name: Shadestalker Helm
96550318.subtitle: Ulan-Tan was right.
96550318.text:
[SALVATION ANNALS:: SERVITOR NIRIKS Perception Feed dump:] 

[[Filtering Highspeak]] 

ER: The call for aid is sent. This conversation is over.  

IX: You owe me answers. 

ER: You owe allegiance to your Kell. Prepare your nest for evacuation. 

IX: They will kill you. Or worse. 

ER: A cost I will gladly pay. Our people will not survive the Scorn on our own. 

IX: But in what state will we survive? 

ER: Anything is better than annihilation. 

IX: You may feel differently in a Human cage. 

ER: Leave. I have weapons to prepare. Where Scorn go, he often follows. 

IX: As ever, I walk my own path. If I don't see you again, I will know another piece of Old Riis is lost.  

[A snap-hiss. Metal groans and shakes.] 

IX: You can't lead from a cage. You can't inspire from the grave. 

ER: I do what I can. With what I have.
96550318.text_zh:
[救赎编年史:: 魔眼尼瑞克斯感知记录转储:] 

[[过滤高等语言]] 

ER：求助请求已发出。我们没什么可谈的了。  

IX：你欠我答案。 

ER：你应该效忠你的凯尔。让你的巢穴准备好撤离。 

IX：他们会杀死你的，或者做更糟的事情。 

ER：我愿意付出这个代价。我们的族人无法靠自己对抗嗤魅。 

IX：但我们会以何种状态生存下来呢？ 

ER：任何状态都比毁灭好。 

IX：你在人类的牢笼里可能就不会这么想了。 

ER：你走吧，我得准备武器了。嗤魅去哪里，他通常就会跟到哪里。 

IX：我会一如既往地走我自己的路。若再见不到你，我就会知道旧里斯又消亡了一部分。  

[一声呲嗤，金属嘎吱作响。] 

IX：你在笼子里做不了领导者，也没法从坟墓里激励任何人。 

ER：我会尽我所能，不遗余力。

43003873.name: Shadestalker Greaves
43003873.subtitle: The affordances of love do not reside in analogous exchange.
43003873.subtitle_zh: 爱的原则不是等价交换。
43003873.text:
Deep within the maze of the Bazaar, throngs of the City's residents wandered, enjoying all the market had to offer. An Iron War Beast sampled fresh fruits. Awoken haggled over the price of pastries. The smells of caramelized meat and rosemary wafted on the breeze, past every vendor and artisan.

The hum of activity was overpowering yet reassuring to Saint-14 as he stopped to watch an older Eliksni expertly weave fabric on a well-worn loom. The woven symbols were unique and unfamiliar to the Exo, but he watched in awe as an iridescent glow emerged within the vibrant cerulean cloth.

Fit for a Kell, Saint mused to himself—

Breath caught in his throat; hands shook—

Flashes of memory echoed in his mind. All he could feel in this moment… was shame.

He hurried past the weaver and through the crowd, landing squarely in front of a tea stand, a sample placed in his hand before he could open his mouth to refuse. He looked down. The opaque liquid steamed in his cup, pungent and medicinal.

Like distilled Darkness, Saint realized—

Breath caught in his throat; hands shook—

Flashes of memory filled his sight. All he could feel in this moment… was sadness.

He stumbled; apologies and hot liquid spilled all around him as the sounds of the Bazaar became a dull roar in his ears. He needed to escape. The noise, the tea, everything.

He closed his eyes and then rushed away at a fevered pace.

Daylight had waned against the City's walls when Saint found himself in a quiet area, where vibrant green vines stretched down from above, and below, the silhouette of his helmet stretched long and thin across the floor where Mithrax's weathered medical Servitor often waited. Saint breathed a sigh of relief.

He was alone.

Saint placed his favorite keepsake, a small stuffed bear, on the Kell's throne. Gently, he adjusted the lavender ribbon at its neck; the crisp satin sat in stark contrast to the bear's hazy black eyes, to its slightly worn ear and well-loved fur. A gift, once a comfort to a child of the City.

A gift, once a comfort to Saint in the face of loss, in the face of—

Breath caught in his throat; hands shook—

Flashes of memory swelled in his heart.

Osiris.

His strong laugh. His deep, soulful eyes. The warmth of his smile. Of his touch.

Memories of comfort, but all he could feel in this moment… was guilt. Intense and overwhelming, like daggers cutting through him, sharpness bleeding through sweetness. Saint breathed deeply and stared at the medical equipment around the empty throne before him.

"The cost of my joy," Saint whispered, and he wept.
43003873.text_zh:
迷宫般的集市深处，圣城居民川流不息，享受着市场的一切。一只钢铁战兽正品尝新鲜水果，觉醒者讨价还价购买糕点，肉食的焦香和迷迭香的气味随风飘散，经过每个商人和工匠的摊位。

此起彼伏的声势对圣人14号来说既具有压倒性又让人安心，他停下来观看一名年长的埃里克斯尼族熟练地在磨损的纺织机上编织。编出的符号对这个Exo来说独特而陌生，但当鲜艳的天蓝布上闪耀出彩虹般的炫彩时，他不禁瞠目结舌。

很适合凯尔，圣人心想——

呼吸一滞，他的双手颤抖——

记忆的片段在他脑海中回荡。这一刻他所能感受到的…只有羞愧。

他匆忙走过编织者，穿过人群，径直来到一个茶摊前。他还没来得及张口婉拒，手中就被塞了杯试喝。他低头看去，杯中的茶色液体冒着蒸汽，散发着浓烈的草药味。

像是提炼出的暗影，圣人意识到——

呼吸一滞，他的双手颤抖——

记忆的片段充斥他的视线。这一刻他所能感受到的…只有悲伤。

他踉跄了一下，耳边响起道歉声，滚烫的液体洒了一地，集市的喧嚣在他耳边成了低沉的轰鸣。他需要逃离喧嚣、茶，周遭的一切。

他闭上眼睛，然后急匆匆地离开。

圣人回过神，发现自己在一片安静的区域，圣城的墙壁外，白昼已在消退。鲜绿的藤蔓从上方垂下，他头盔的轮廓在地上拉得又长又细，那是米瑟拉克斯那饱经风霜的医疗魔眼常等候的地方。圣人松了一口气。

这里只有他。

圣人把他最喜欢的纪念品，一只毛绒小熊，放在凯尔的王座上。他轻轻地调整着熊脖子上的薰衣草色缎带；洁净的缎带与熊朦胧的黑眼睛、略微磨损的耳朵和饱受搓揉的毛形成了鲜明对比。这份礼物曾给圣城中的一个孩子带来过慰藉。

这份礼物曾在圣人面对失去时带来过慰藉，在——

呼吸一滞，他的双手颤抖——

记忆片段在他心中涌动。

奥斯里斯。

他爽朗的笑声，深邃的眼神，温暖的微笑，以及触碰。

是充满慰藉的记忆，但在这一刻，他所能感受到的…只有强烈而无法承受的内疚，如同匕首将他刺穿，甜美中透着锋芒。圣人深吸一口气，凝视着空荡王座前的医疗设备。

“为我的快乐而付出的代价，”圣人轻声说道，然后啜泣起来。

1188437342.name: Blastwave Striders
1188437342.subtitle: Take the hits. Give the hits.
1188437342.text:
With skies this clear, the Hawk practically flies itself, gliding smoothly across the firmament. Keris feels the comfortable silence take a turn toward the soporific, and pours herself some coffee.

"Hey," she says, "How much longer?"

Hayes doesn't even have to check. "Ten minutes out."

So much of this journey takes place over long stretches of nothing. Dead air on the sensors, not a power spike for miles. It's always a relief to see the Farm coming into view on the instruments.

The Farm's denizens are still piecing together plans with the Vanguard: working out whether they can convince a few Guardians to take a post out here for a while, discussing permanent fortifications.

Keris's part in all this is simple: she and Hayes get the supplies out to those who need them, and that's that. The politics are well beyond her.

"Look at that," Hayes murmurs.

Keris looks at the panels, and sees it: dotted constellations of energy signatures, worming through the neighboring hills and valleys. Stretching out for miles.

"Guess they got that solar cell network going," she says.

"Guess so."

She forgets about the coffee.
1188437342.text_zh:
在这样晴朗的天空下，鹰隼几乎可以自己在空中滑翔。克莉丝觉得这种安静很舒服，渐渐地困意袭来，于是给自己倒了杯咖啡。

“嘿，”她说，“还要多久？”

海斯看都没看一眼。“十分钟。”

这次旅程的大部分时间都在空虚中度过。传感器上一片死寂，方圆几里没有任何能量波动。每次看到农庄出现在仪器上时，总是让人如释重负。

农庄的居民们仍在与先锋制定计划，商量是否能说服几名守护者在这里驻扎一段时间，讨论建立永久性的防御设施。

克莉丝在其中的角色很简单：她和海斯将物资送到需要的人那里，仅此而已。政治对她来说太复杂了。

“快看，”海斯低声说。

克莉丝看向面板，那是点缀在周围山谷中的能量信号，延伸出了好几里。

“看来他们把太阳能电池网络启动了，”她说。

“看来是。”

她忘记了要喝咖啡。

3234613634.name: Spacewalk Gloves
3234613634.subtitle: Archival|Castor|231| —don't understand. We're all excited for successful code injection, but it's much too early for insertion into a chassis—
3234613634.subtitle_zh: 档案|卡斯托|231| ——不明白。代码注入成功我们都很兴奋，但现在就插入底架还为时过早——
3234613634.text:
Seventeen days since arrival. 

Karrho is busy all the time talking to the Vandals and Marauders too big to even look at Yaraskis. They're working together to build an Ether refinery, using old human blueprints from the station. He rarely has time for Yaraskis. 

Yaraskis would make a terrible engineer. In her cocoon she dreamed of being a Captain, not a priest. She fetches and carries and mops up the old stains nobody else wants to touch, making the station livable again. 

Day by day, their home fills up with comforting noise: the pleasant creak of cable ties stringing platforms together, the thump-click, thump-click of footwraps and claws on decking, of the arguments between the only two crewmembers who understand Servitor code. 

It's nothing like a good solid warren—but it's safe, and that's good enough. And once they have Ether flowing in, it'll be even better. 

Yaraskis tries to ignore the station-voice as she tosses a rag into the machine that is almost an incinerator. 

From behind, a hand yanks at her hood. She yells. Its owner dodges her return swipe. 

Karrho. "I need to talk to you. Something is wrong. I can't find Paskir." 

Paskir is another engineer, big for a Vandal. Big enough that his former Captain was eyeing him as a challenger, which is why he agreed to steal a Ketch with them in the first place. 

"Maybe he got lost. Or stuck in some goo." Whatever the Humans did on this station, it involved a lot of… liquids. Yaraskis disinfects her hands at least five times a day. 

"He was going to help me with the nuclear power supply and never showed up. And I heard something in the halls." At her look, Karrho adds, "Something big!" 

"Anything big would have starved long before we got here. Just wait, I bet he got stuck in one of the zero-gravity areas and he'll call for help soon." 

"You'll help me look?" 

She hooks an arm around Karrho and pulls him away from the almost-incinerator. 

"If he doesn't turn up with an embarrassing story in the morning, we'll all look for him." 

Karrho loves engineering. He should be a Servitor's priest or a Splicer. Yaraskis wants to be his Captain, assign him to the priesthood. She wants to get so tall that her head brushes the ceiling, and her arms are long enough to wrap around the whole crew. 

It's better to be here than with the Houses. 

It has to be better.
3234613634.text_zh:
抵达后十七天。 

卡霍一直在忙着和那些暴徒和狂暴劫匪交谈，他们体型大到甚至不屑于看雅拉斯基丝一眼。他们要利用来自空间站里旧人类的蓝图，合作建造一座乙太精炼厂。他很少有时间陪雅拉斯基丝。 

雅拉斯基丝成不了一名优秀的工程师。她在茧里就梦想着成为一名船长，而不是祭司。她负责跑腿、搬运、清理那些无人愿意触碰的陈年污渍，让空间站重新变得宜居。 

一天天过去，他们的家园充满了各种令人心安的声响：缆绳将各个平台绑在一起时发出的悦耳嘎吱声，裹足和爪子踩在甲板上发出的咚咚声，以及仅有的两名懂得魔眼代码的船员之间的争论声。 

这里一点也不像个坚固的杂院——但它很安全，这就足够了。而且一旦他们有了乙太，这里就会变得更好。 

雅拉斯基丝一边把抹布扔进那台差不多算是焚烧炉的机器，一边试图忽略站内系统音。 

突然，有只手从后面扯住了她的兜帽。她大叫一声。那只手的主人躲过了她的回击。 

是卡霍。“我需要和你谈谈。出事了。我找不到帕斯基尔。” 

帕斯基尔是另一位工程师，就暴徒来说体型挺大。大到足以让他的前任船长把他视为挑战者，这也是他当初同意跟他们合谋偷一艘双桅船的原因。 

“也许他迷路了。或者被什么粘液困住了。”不管人类之前在这个空间站上做什么，都跟很多的…液体有关。雅拉斯基丝每天至少要给她的手消毒五次。 

“他本来要帮我解决核电供应问题，但一直没出现。我还听到走廊里有动静。”看着她的表情，卡霍补充道，“是个大家伙！” 

“就算有大家伙，肯定也在我们来到这里之前就饿死了。等着瞧吧，我打赌他一定是困在某个零重力区里，他很快就会求救的。” 

“你会帮我一起找吗？” 

她挽起卡霍的胳膊，把他从那台近似焚烧炉的机器旁拉开。 

“如果他明天早上还没有带着尴尬的故事出现，我们就一起去找他。” 

卡霍热爱工程学。他应该成为一名魔眼祭司或熔岩军团。雅拉斯基丝想当他的船长，让他担任祭司的职务。她想变得高高的，头能碰到天花板，手臂长到能环绕整个船队。 

待在这里总比留在那些氏族里要好。 

必须得更好才行。

4190676582.name: Spacewalk Robes
4190676582.subtitle: Urgent|Tech|Helios|412| Someone call the boss. Call Central. We can't shelter in place here. Repeat, we can't—
4190676582.subtitle_zh: 紧急|技术|赫利俄斯|412| 快来个人联系老大。呼叫中枢。我们不能就地避难。重复，我们不能——
4190676582.text:
Twenty-three days since arrival. 

The Ether generator is taking shape, a big ringed shell set a safe distance from the hull, cradled in wiring. Their crew's three spinners are busy all the time making more cabling. 

Except somehow it's too quiet. The older crew are a little snooty about Drekhs, and that's fine—but Yaraskis can't even find one of them to be snooty at her. 

Paskir is still missing. She and Karrho hunted for him up and down the station for hours. 

Nobody suggests going back down to the surface. They'd be killed outright. Their big plan—a hidden warren where nobody will ever bother them again—has to work. 

Yaraskis sticks to the smaller, dimly lit corridors now, where only the Drekhs fit. She doesn't like the big, open ones with their flat, bright lights, reverberating acoustics, and the feeling that something is always watching her. 

Karrho stays at his work. Yaraskis, ignoring her own, explores the station instead, hunting for their missing crewmates. She makes a tally as she goes, checking every corner of the station, and keeping an ear out for the barely audible whine of a charged scattercape. 

A full third of the crew are… gone. 

She hears a muted shriek, something under the flickering buzz of a dying light. Then the scrape of metal on metal. She hunches her shoulders deeper into her cloak against the feeling of being followed. 

The scraping sound stalks her even through her shortcuts. She turns to look back. Still nothing. 

She can't find Paskir. She can't find anyone. There's nothing to do but give up.  

Yaraskis heads back to Karrho's workshop. 

It's empty. Silent as a dead warren.  

Karrho is gone.
4190676582.text_zh:
抵达后二十三天。 

乙太发生器已初具雏形，一个巨大的环形外壳，与船体保持着安全距离，用电线裹着。船员们的三台纺纱机在忙着制造更多的电缆。 

只是不知道为什么，这里太安静了。老船员们对堕落者士兵有点嗤之以鼻，这没什么，但雅拉斯基丝却连一个对她嗤之以鼻的人都找不到。 

帕斯基尔还是下落不明。她和卡霍在空间站里上上下下找了他好几个小时。 

没有人提议返回地表。他们会被立即处死。他们的大计划——这个没人会再打扰他们的隐蔽杂院——必须成功。 

雅拉斯基丝现在喜欢呆在光线昏暗的小走廊里，那些只有堕落者士兵才能容身的地方。她不喜欢那些宽敞开阔的走廊，那里有平直明亮的灯光、回荡不绝的传声混响，以及被什么东西盯着的感觉。 

卡霍继续他的工作。雅拉斯基丝则忽略了自己的差事，转而探索空间站，寻找失踪的船员。她边走边做记录，检查空间站的各个角落，留心听着充能散射披肩那几乎听不见的鸣响。 

整整三分之一的船员…消失了。 

她听到一声低沉的尖叫，它在一盏即将熄灭的灯光闪烁的嗡鸣声中似有若无。紧接着是金属与金属的摩擦声。她紧紧地裹紧披风，耸起肩膀，抵御那种被跟踪的不安感。 

即使她抄近路走，那刮擦声还是紧随其后。她回头看了看，还是什么都没有。 

她找不到帕斯基尔。她找不到任何人。她别无选择，只能放弃。  

雅拉斯基丝回到了卡霍的工作间。 

里面空无一人。跟杂院一样死寂。  

卡霍消失了。

213803727.name: Spacewalk Bond
213803727.subtitle: Tech|Notice|42| All—use of the sample decommission tool is restricted to accredited researchers. If you need to contain something, call security.
213803727.subtitle_zh: 技术|通知|42| 全体注意——所有样本处理工具仅限经认可的研究人员使用。如果你需要隔离处理某物，请联系安保人员。
213803727.text:
Time is suspended.  

All that remains is the appointed task. 

The spinners craft towropes, powerlines, and all-purpose cable, hour after hour without rest. 

The White Captain moves among them with her many limbs. She feels what they feel, knows what they know, as soon as they know it. She uses this information to align, and together, they build something new in this home they've found. 

Every Drekh yearns for more arms than their Captain allows. Every four-eyed Eliksni looks with envy upon the eight-eyed. Every Kell and Archon raises their horns as high as they dare. 

Now, together they are as no Eliksni before them. A miracle. A being of hundreds of limbs, lungs, eyes. 

The White Captain gently touches the limb previously named Yaraskis. Her appointed portion of the great diagram flowers to life in her head. 

Legs stumbling under her, she moves towards the station's prow. One limb may be unsteady, but their great shared body is strong. 

Faint noises make no sense. Words she doesn't understand. The un-Eliksni babbling of a foreign mind. 

The only mind that matters is the White Captain's. 

Hands connect circuits and power lines. The diagram is beautiful but difficult to grasp. She searches for the right shape, the right configuration that will let power flow through its appointed channels. 

The work goes on.  

Until the hands tie off the last cable.  

The eyes look up. The knees buckle in joy. The heart surges along the bright paths of the diagram. 

Somewhere in the joined crowd, a single hand throws a single lever. 

The mind rejoices. 

Orange light flares to life in the cold dark. 

It flares in hundreds of souls. Yaraskis is there. 

Somewhere.
213803727.text_zh:
时间停滞不前。  

现在只剩下那些指定好的任务。 

纺纱机不停地编织着拖曳缆、电源线和多用途电缆，几个小时不停地工作，从不休息。 

白色船长用她那众多的肢体，在它们之间穿梭。她能够即时感知到他们的感受，知晓他们所了解的一切。她利用这些信息进行协调，一起在这个他们找到的家园里建造新的事物。 

每个堕落者士兵都渴望拥有超过其船长允许数量的手臂。每个四眼埃里克斯尼族都羡慕地望着那些八眼的同类。每一位凯尔和执政官都尽可能地高举起他们的犄角。 

如今，他们合为一体，成为了前所未有的埃里克斯尼族。这是一个奇迹。一个拥有成百上千的肢体、肺和眼睛的存在。 

白色船长轻抚着之前被称为雅拉斯基丝的肢体。她脑海中，巨大图示中分配给她的那部分瞬间鲜活了起来。 

她带着身下颤抖的腿，向空间站的船头走去。其中一个肢体可能不稳，但他们共享的庞大身躯却十分强壮。 

无意义的微弱杂音。她听不懂的词语。外来思维的非埃里克斯尼族语唠叨。 

唯一重要的是白色船长的思维。 

手连接着电路和电源线。图示虽美，却难以捉摸。她寻找着合适的形状、正确的配置，让电力在指定的通道中流动。 

工作还在继续。  

直到手将最后一根电缆系紧。  

眼睛向上看去。膝盖因喜悦而发软。心脏沿着图示中明亮的路径而激涌。 

在聚群中的某个地方，一只手拉动了一根杠杆。 

思维欢欣鼓舞。 

在寒冷的黑暗中，橙色的光芒突然亮起。 

它在数百个灵魂中闪烁着。雅拉斯基丝就在那里。 

那里的某个地方。

1446639859.name: Spacewalk Cover
1446639859.subtitle: Tech|Direct|124| —ate through another container. What cleaning agents are safe to use? We can't afford another fume incident, István.
1446639859.subtitle_zh: 技术|指示|124| ——蚀穿了另一个容器。哪些清洁剂可以安全使用？我们承受不起另一次烟气事故了，伊什特万。
1446639859.text:
Six days since arrival. 

Metal groans. Power lines hum. Things skitter in the pipes. 

Yaraskis picks her way through rubble with a double armload of scrap. She's finally growing out of Drekh scale, lower arms regrown all the way down to her talons, but she's still slight enough to duck through the smallest shafts of their new home. 

An orbital station, ancient and damaged, but fixable, everyone thinks. The station hasn't been inhabited for a very long time, but Yaraskis catches herself looking over her shoulder repeatedly. 

Her spine prickles as an eerie mechanical voice speaks above her head; some old message for Humans, Karrho said. Nothing to worry about. But… unsettling all the same. 

It's a relief to get to the workshop. She kicks at the doorframe. "Scrap delivery." 

Karrho is smaller than Yaraskis, still true Drekh. Even so, people pay attention to him because he hatched with eight eyes. That means he's handsome, one-in-a-million lucky. And he's sharp. He was in on the plan from the beginning. Yaraskis only got tapped because she's his egg-cousin. 

Karrho gestures without looking up from his screens. "Put it anywhere." 

The workshop is one of the creepier rooms on the station, in Yaraskis's opinion. It's filled with metal tables bolted to the floor. They had had to clear out a whole pile of empty Vex bodies before the room was usable. Yaraskis tries not to touch anything as she sets down her bundle. 

"What are you working on?" 

"Analyzing some old mechanical blueprints. If we can splice into the systems, there's as much to use up here as down on the surface. And there aren't any Vex up here. No Hive. No Lightbearers." 

"No Kells," Yaraskis says firmly. 

"No Kells." Karrho adds, "Plenty of Ether if these blueprints hold true, though. There's this machine. It's in two parts—one collects energy, one uses it. We just need the collector for the Servitors, and we're set for life." 

He tilts one of the screens her way. 

Ether for life, up here in the cold dark. It makes everything worth it, the overwhelming feeling of fear as they escaped from Europa, the careful navigation around the hazards on the station as they work to make it livable. 

And yes, Yaraskis might get shooed out of engineering meetings she doesn't understand, but nobody will cut off her arms for insubordination. 

She flexes her lower hands and leans in to study their future.
1446639859.text_zh:
抵达后六天。 

金属嘎吱作响。电线发出嗡鸣。管道里传来窸窸窣窣的声音。 

雅拉斯基丝揽着双臂的废料在瓦砾中艰难前行。她终于摆脱了堕落者士兵的体型，下臂已重新长出，一直延伸到利爪处，但她仍然很瘦小，小到可以穿过他们新家中最小的通风井。 

他们的新家是一座古老而破损的轨道空间站，不过还是可以修复的，大家都这么觉得。这座空间站已很久没人居住了，但雅拉斯基丝却总是不由自主地频频回头张望。 

一个阴森诡异的机械声音在她头顶上方响起，引得她的脊背一阵刺痛；卡霍说那是给人类听的一些旧广播。没什么好担心的。但…还是让人感到不安。 

到了工作间，她才松了一口气。她踢了踢门框喊道。“废料快送。” 

卡霍比雅拉斯基丝体型瘦小，仍然是纯正的堕落者士兵。即便如此，人们还是会在意他，因为他出生时长着八只眼睛。这意味着他英俊潇洒，是万里挑一的幸运儿。他还很聪明。从一开始他就参与了这个计划。雅拉斯基丝之所以被选中，仅仅是因为她是他的表亲。 

卡霍的视线没有离开屏幕，只是摆了摆手。“随便找个地方放。” 

在雅拉斯基丝看来，工作间是空间站里最让人毛骨悚然的房间之一。里面摆满了用螺栓固定在地板上的金属桌子。他们不得不清理掉一大堆Vex空壳，然后才用上了这个房间。雅拉斯基丝放下包裹时尽量不去碰任何东西。 

“你在忙什么呢？” 

“分析一些旧的机械蓝图。如果我们能入侵系统，这里能用的资源就会跟地表上一样多。而且这上面没有Vex，没有邪魔族，没有负光者。” 

“没有凯尔，”雅拉斯基丝坚定地说。 

“没有凯尔。”卡霍补充道，“不过，如果这些蓝图是真的，那这里就有很多乙太。有这样一台机器。它分为两部分，一部分收集能量，一部分使用能量。我们只需拿到魔眼用的收集器，以后就不用愁了。” 

他把其中一块屏幕转向她。 

在这寒冷黑暗的地方，有一辈子用不完的乙太。它让一切都变得值得，包括他们逃离木卫二时令人窒息的恐惧感，还有他们为了让空间站变得宜居而小心绕过各种危险的艰难过程。 

当然，雅拉斯基丝可能会被赶出她听不懂的工程会议，但没有人会因为她违抗命令而砍掉她的手臂。 

她活动着下肢的手，俯身研究他们的未来。

1025368892.name: Spacewalk Boots
1025368892.subtitle: Research|Direct|132| Pull that log. If someone sends it up the chain we're all dead.
1025368892.subtitle_zh: 研究|指示|132| 把那段日志删掉。要是有人上报，我们就全完了。
1025368892.text:
Thirty-nine days since arrival. 

Ketches and warrens are creaky things. Cables groan, steps squeak, hammocks rustle. Ether-bright eyes should glow and blink in the comfortable dark. 

Yaraskis had expected they would fill up the station, all of them, with repaired machinery and stolen comforts and familiar sounds. 

All the station's sounds are lonely now. Even the station-voice would be a comfort, almost. 

She hasn't seen Karrho in days. The remaining engineers only talk to each other, and the Servitors groan and bob in the air together in one nervous bundle. 

And something is stalking the hallways. 

It has eyes like an Eliksni, but they don't flicker like they should. They burn steadily, lit not by Ether but by something else. Even the Marauders tell her about it in whispers, so scared they ignore hierarchy. 

Yaraskis feels its presence in her spiracles. She decides to head for Karrho's workshop. She can hide there. 

Then a Marauder swings into view. His eyes are strange and he doesn't look at Yaraskis. He just says, "Come here." 

She runs. Through the halls, leaping over platforms strung together, scoring her side badly on an unexpected twist of metal. 

The missing crew loom out of corners, calling out as she runs past. She doesn't stop. 

Till a voice calls her by name. 

It's Karrho. He's braced himself in a corner of the ceiling near a broken vent grate that Yaraskis knows leads to the station hull. It's too small for anyone bigger than a Drekh. 

She leaps. Hands claw at her ankles as Yaraskis kicks her way up the wall. 

"This way," Karrho urges. They scurry through twisting passages, through the vents and under floors that long-ago Humans never meant for anyone to walk in. They run over wreckage, in and out of the gravity generators' pull, towards the Ketch. Maybe they'll be safe there. Maybe they can cast off and run. 

"What's wrong with them?" Yaraskis asks, panting. Her heart kicks hard in her chest. 

"Nothing." 

Karrho stops on a dime at the vent's exit. Yaraskis's momentum takes her clear past him, into a wide room. 

She looks far up into the bright steady glare of mechanical eyes. Filled with an alien light. 

And Karrho pushes her forward into the waiting arms of the White Captain.
1025368892.text_zh:
抵达后三十九天。 

双桅船和杂院都已破旧不堪。电缆发出嘎吱声，台阶吱吱作响，吊床沙沙有声。乙太充足的明眸应闪烁着光芒，在舒适的黑暗中眨动。 

雅拉斯基丝原本以为他们大家会用修好的机器、偷来的舒适用品和熟悉的声响，把整个空间站填满。 

可现在，整个空间站的声音都显得孤独。即使是站内系统音，也几乎成了一种慰藉。 

她已经好几天没见到卡霍了。剩下的工程师们只会互相交谈，魔眼们则一齐呻吟着，紧张地聚在空中晃来晃去。 

走廊里有什么东西在潜行。 

它有类似埃里克斯尼族的眼，却不像正常的那样闪烁。它们持续燃烧，点燃它们的不是乙太，而是别的什么。就连狂暴劫匪们也小声地跟她提及此事，他们害怕得顾不上等级制度了。 

雅拉斯基丝在她的气孔中感觉到了它的存在。她决定前往卡霍的工作间。她可以躲在那里。 

这时，有一个狂暴劫匪出现在眼前。他的眼神很奇怪，没有去看雅拉斯基丝。他只是说道，“过来。” 

她转身就跑。穿过走廊，跃过一个个串连起来的平台，被一个突然出现的金属拐角严重划伤了侧身。 

失踪的船员从各个角落里冒了出来，在她跑过时大声呼喊。她没有停下。 

直到一个声音叫出了她的名字。 

是卡霍。他靠着天花板的一个角落，旁边有个破损的通风格栅，雅拉斯基丝知道这个通风口通往空间站船体。任何比堕落者士兵块头大的人都进不去。 

她纵身一跃。卡霍用手抓着她的脚踝，雅拉斯基丝奋力踢着墙壁向上攀爬。 

“这边走，”卡霍催促道。他们匆匆穿过曲折的通道，穿过通风口和地板下，昔日的人类住民从未打算让任何人进入的地方。他们越过残骸，在重力发生器的引力场里进出，朝着双桅船跑去。或许在那里他们能够安全一些。也许他们可以搭船逃离。 

“他们有什么毛病？”雅拉斯基丝气喘吁吁地问道。她的心怦怦直跳。 

“没毛病。” 

卡霍突然停在通风口的出口。雅拉斯基丝因惯性径直冲过他，进入了一个宽敞的房间。 

她抬头看向高处那些明亮而坚定的机械眼睛。里头充满了异样的光芒。 

卡霍把她推进了前方白色船长等候着的怀抱中。

1754155306.name: Shadestalker Gloves
1754155306.subtitle: Turn the shadows against themselves.
1754155306.text:
His knee had grown stiff under his desk. 

Zavala initially ignored it. Let the pain burn in the side of his knee, seize the top of his calves. His leg had grown stiff countless times before. But this time, this early in the morning, this soon after sitting down, was something else. 

He moved his chair back and considered his knee. What had he done to hurt it? He had not exercised yet, he had not gone on his usual patrol… he had done nothing. Why would a knee hurt from doing nothing? 

The riddle dissolved. He was starting to age. 

Zavala had anticipated this, part of mourning Targe was preparing himself to furiously resist the inevitable physical breakdown. He'd calculated how to negotiate with his own body, subdue it to stoicism, and make it follow his sturdy command. But what he had not anticipated was how he would feel. He ought to feel dread, terror at evidence of his mortality. But instead…  

He allows a hand to rest on his aching knee. To venerate it. He feels it solid under his palm. It is his, it is real, it is both portentous and precious. He is aging. He will age. An absurd and joyous thought warms in his chest: how fortunate, to have lived long enough to grow old. How invaluable, to make the space between himself and the horizon matter. How much time is left? And is it best spent with his knees under a desk? 

"Zavala?" 

Ikora stands in the doorway. Hundreds of years of knowing each other too well draws her to his seat. 

His expression softens, and he stretches out his knee. 

Ikora watches his readjustment, and smiles sadly, the same way she smiles when all their mortal friends grow old. 

The commander sighs, but with content assurance, not heavy resignation. He looks at his friend. "I think I'd like to go on leave for a week." 

Ikora nods, then half-smiles. "How about two?"
1754155306.text_zh:
桌下，他的膝盖僵住了。 

萨瓦拉最初选择了忽视，任由疼痛从膝盖侧面一路爬到小腿上半截。他的腿以前也这样僵过很多次，但像这样，一大清早，刚坐下不久就这样，非比寻常。 

他把椅子往后移，打量着膝盖。是做什么伤到了它吗？他还没锻炼，也没有进行日常巡逻…什么都还没做，为什么膝盖会疼？ 

答案很简单：他开始变老了。 

萨瓦拉对此早有预期。哀悼塔格的同时，他也在做准备要去奋勇对抗身体必然的衰颓。他计算过如何与自己的身体谈判，用坚忍去征服，去让它服从他坚决的命令。但他没有料到自己的感受，他本该觉得恐惧，对自己不再永生的证据感到恐慌，但正相反…  

他怀着崇敬的心，把一只手放在疼痛的膝盖上。它在他手掌下坚实又可靠，这是他的身体，真实存在，既珍贵又包含着不祥的预兆。他正在衰老，必会衰老。一个荒谬而愉悦的念头让他的胸口温热起来：能活到开始衰老是多么幸运，让自己和地平线之间的空间变得有意义，又是多么的宝贵。他还剩多少时间？真的应该用来在桌前感受膝盖的疼痛吗？ 

“萨瓦拉？” 

艾可拉站在门口，几百年来对彼此的了解引导她来到了他的座位旁。 

他的表情缓和下来，开始舒展膝盖。 

艾可拉观察着他的动作，露出带点苦涩的微笑，凡人朋友们开始衰老时她总是这样的表情。 

指挥官叹了口气，但这反应中透着安心和自信，而不是无奈地听天由命。他看向好友，“我想我会请一周的假。” 

艾可拉点点头，然后似笑非笑地说，“要不两周？”

2121930590.name: Shadestalker Robes
2121930590.subtitle: Unseen deliverance.
2121930590.text:
TYPE: REDJACK SURVEILLANCE FEED [21058] 

PARTIES: Five [5]. One [1], Guardian-type, Class Hunter [u.1]; One [1], Frame-type, Unit Combat [u.2]; Three [3], Scorn-[ERROR] Type.  

ASSOCIATIONS: Lev [Unit5003];  Scorn; Crucible; Frame; Lord Shaxx; Redjacks 

//AUDIO UNAVAILABLE// 

//TRANSCRIPT FOLLOWS…/ 

[u.1:01] Relax, I have you. 

[u.1:02] "Relax" means stop. You're in pieces, and you're making it worse. 

[u.2:01] Hostiles still pushing from the front. Scans incomplete. 

[u.1:03] Your fireteam is gone. Scans are irrelevant if I can't get you back to the Tower to link up. 

[u.2:02] Incoming. 

[A hissing snap washes the feed with high-yield paracausal discharge, followed by the loud crack of three hard rounds.] 

[u.1:04] Stop moving. You're making this worse. 

[u.2:03] Thank you, Guardian. Spectral analysis complete. 

[u.2:04] Hunter Vanguard suppositions were correct. 

[u.1:05] Crow is usually on point. What about? 

[u.2:05] Despite being Scorn of unknown type, the hostiles were alive. Also, Traveler radiation was detected emanating from the Dark Ether in their bodies. Thus their origins may be paracausal. 

[u.2:06] Confirmation through Redjack surveillance was necessary for verification. 

[u.1:06] Quiet down. And make sure they're not sneaking up on me. 

[u.2:07] Everywhere type-Fikrul goes, Eliksni of the City are in danger. 

[u.1:07] We know. We'll find him. 

[u.2:08] Guardians have discovered no tangible means of terminating that unit type. 

[u.1:08] You're not helping. 

[u.2:09] I am encouraging you to seek confirmation through combat. 

[u.1:09] Shaxx. I know you listen to every feed. Your friend is going to give me a panic attack.
2121930590.text_zh:
类型：红桃杰克监控记录[21058] 

相关方：五[5]。一[1]名守护者，职业：猎人[未知1]；一[1]名机械仆从，战斗单位[未知2]；三[3]名嗤魅-[错误]类型。  

关联：列弗[单位5003]；嗤魅；熔炉竞技场；机械仆从；领主沙克斯；红桃杰克 

//音频不可用// 

//转录如下…// 

[未知1: 01] 放轻松，有我在。 

[未知1: 02] “放轻松”的意思是停下。你支离破碎，只会让情况变得更糟。 

[未知2: 01] 前方仍有敌人推进，扫描未完成。 

[未知1: 03] 你的火力战队已经没了。如果我不能把你送回高塔建立连接，扫描也没有意义。

[伴随着强效超因果放电，监控被嘶嘶的杂音覆盖，紧接着是三发硬弹的爆裂声。] 

[未知1: 04] 别动。你只会让情况变得更糟。 

[未知2: 03] 谢谢你，守护者。光谱分析已完成。 

[未知2: 04] 猎人先锋的推测是正确的。 

[未知1: 05] 乌鸦通常都是对的。什么推测？ 

[未知2: 05] 尽管是未知类型的嗤魅，但这些敌人是活的。此外，他们体内的黑暗乙太中检测到了旅行者的辐射。因此其起源可能是超因果的。 

[未知2: 06] 需要通过红桃杰克监控进行验证。 

[未知1: 06] 安静点。确保他们不会暗中接近我。 

[未知2: 07] 在费克鲁类型出现的地方，圣城的埃里克斯尼族都有危险。 

[未知1: 07] 我们知道。我们会找到他的。 

[未知2: 08] 守护者尚未发现终结那个单位类型的有效方法。 

[未知1: 08] 说点有用的话。 

[未知2: 09] 我鼓励你通过战斗寻求确证。 

[未知1: 09] 沙克斯，我知道你会听每一条记录。你的朋友要把我给吓坏了。

1493134439.name: Shadestalker Bond
1493134439.subtitle: In history's long shadow.
1493134439.text:
Undead screeches bounce off the ruined walls of Riis Reborn, carried by blizzard winds that obscure any path to safety. The small band of Eliksni got separated from the rest at the jetty and fled down this abandoned ally. A Salvation Ketch could barely defend itself from these pale monstrosities; what chance did they have? 

A second molt is unable to hold her composure; her antennal glands leak as her mother holds her close. Her clicking purr is hushed, just enough to voice comfort. 

"I can smell your fear." 

Above them, metal creaks under the Revenant's weight. One Dreg begins to scurry away, but his knee is pinned to the ground by a spear. 

"Do not weep," it sings, so close his mandibles rake the Dreg's respirator. "Rejoice. Today you will be made whole." The undead hulk salivates as the small band huddles together. 

A neon cord catches the aberration's carapace, pulling it up into the air by an unseen hand. 

The mother shields her brood's eyes as bitter ichor erupts from the undead's throat. Two more piercing rounds, in quick succession, see him sinking into the snow, now loosed from the ephemeral thread. 

The second molt breaks away to see a Slayer Baron, as if from an ancient epic, stepping through the gale. 

"Mother!" She chitters in relief. "A fate weaver from your stories!" 

The snowdrift clears, revealing the upright figure's alien anatomy. "Not my stories. A new one."
1493134439.text_zh:
不死者的尖啸声在重生的里斯的废墟墙壁间回荡，暴风雪将它传得更远，也遮蔽了任何通向安全的路径。一小群埃里克斯尼族在栈桥和大部队走散，逃进了这条废弃的小巷。救赎双桅船都几乎无法抵御这些苍白的怪物，他们又哪有机会呢？ 

一个幼儿无法保持冷静，她的触角腺体渗出液体。她的母亲紧紧抱住她，咔嗒着用勉强能被听见的咕噜声传递着安慰。 

“我能闻到你的恐惧。” 

他们上方的金属在亡魂的重量下吱吱作响。一名堕落者士兵开始逃窜，但他的膝盖被一支长矛钉在了地上。 

“不要哭泣，”那声音唱道，他如此接近，下颚刮擦过了堕落者士兵的呼吸机。“欢欣吧，今天你会变得完整。”当他们紧紧抱在一起时，不死者巨物垂涎欲滴。 

一根霓虹绳索缠住了畸形怪物的甲壳，仿佛有无形的手将它拉入空中。 

不死者的喉咙喷出腥气的液体时，母亲遮住了幼儿的眼睛。接连两发穿甲弹之后，他倒在雪地里，从短暂的束缚中解脱了。 

幼儿挣脱开来，看到一名如同古老史诗中走出的杀手公爵，穿过狂风而来。 

“妈妈！”她安心地咔嗒道。“是你故事里讲过的命运编织者！” 

大雪渐渐平息，揭示出矗立身影的外星躯体。“不，这是一个新的故事。”

294976891.name: Shadestalker Hood
294976891.subtitle: Ulan-Tan was right.
294976891.text:
[SALVATION ANNALS:: SERVITOR NIRIKS Perception Feed dump:] 

[[Filtering Highspeak]] 

ER: The call for aid is sent. This conversation is over.  

IX: You owe me answers. 

ER: You owe allegiance to your Kell. Prepare your nest for evacuation. 

IX: They will kill you. Or worse. 

ER: A cost I will gladly pay. Our people will not survive the Scorn on our own. 

IX: But in what state will we survive? 

ER: Anything is better than annihilation. 

IX: You may feel differently in a Human cage. 

ER: Leave. I have weapons to prepare. Where Scorn go, he often follows. 

IX: As ever, I walk my own path. If I don't see you again, I will know another piece of Old Riis is lost.  

[A snap-hiss. Metal groans and shakes.] 

IX: You can't lead from a cage. You can't inspire from the grave. 

ER: I do what I can. With what I have.
294976891.text_zh:
[救赎编年史:: 魔眼尼瑞克斯感知记录转储:] 

[[过滤高等语言]] 

ER：求助请求已发出。我们没什么可谈的了。  

IX：你欠我答案。 

ER：你应该效忠你的凯尔。让你的巢穴准备好撤离。 

IX：他们会杀死你的，或者做更糟的事情。 

ER：我愿意付出这个代价。我们的族人无法靠自己对抗嗤魅。 

IX：但我们会以何种状态生存下来呢？ 

ER：任何状态都比毁灭好。 

IX：你在人类的牢笼里可能就不会这么想了。 

ER：你走吧，我得准备武器了。嗤魅去哪里，他通常就会跟到哪里。 

IX：我会一如既往地走我自己的路。若再见不到你，我就会知道旧里斯又消亡了一部分。  

[一声呲嗤，金属嘎吱作响。] 

IX：你在笼子里做不了领导者，也没法从坟墓里激励任何人。 

ER：我会尽我所能，不遗余力。

410486468.name: Shadestalker Boots
410486468.subtitle: The affordances of love do not reside in analogous exchange.
410486468.subtitle_zh: 爱的原则不是等价交换。
410486468.text:
Deep within the maze of the Bazaar, throngs of the City's residents wandered, enjoying all the market had to offer. An Iron War Beast sampled fresh fruits. Awoken haggled over the price of pastries. The smells of caramelized meat and rosemary wafted on the breeze, past every vendor and artisan.

The hum of activity was overpowering yet reassuring to Saint-14 as he stopped to watch an older Eliksni expertly weave fabric on a well-worn loom. The woven symbols were unique and unfamiliar to the Exo, but he watched in awe as an iridescent glow emerged within the vibrant cerulean cloth.

Fit for a Kell, Saint mused to himself—

Breath caught in his throat; hands shook—

Flashes of memory echoed in his mind. All he could feel in this moment… was shame.

He hurried past the weaver and through the crowd, landing squarely in front of a tea stand, a sample placed in his hand before he could open his mouth to refuse. He looked down. The opaque liquid steamed in his cup, pungent and medicinal.

Like distilled Darkness, Saint realized—

Breath caught in his throat; hands shook—

Flashes of memory filled his sight. All he could feel in this moment… was sadness.

He stumbled; apologies and hot liquid spilled all around him as the sounds of the Bazaar became a dull roar in his ears. He needed to escape. The noise, the tea, everything.

He closed his eyes and then rushed away at a fevered pace.

Daylight had waned against the City's walls when Saint found himself in a quiet area, where vibrant green vines stretched down from above, and below, the silhouette of his helmet stretched long and thin across the floor where Mithrax's weathered medical Servitor often waited. Saint breathed a sigh of relief.

He was alone.

Saint placed his favorite keepsake, a small stuffed bear, on the Kell's throne. Gently, he adjusted the lavender ribbon at its neck; the crisp satin sat in stark contrast to the bear's hazy black eyes, to its slightly worn ear and well-loved fur. A gift, once a comfort to a child of the City.

A gift, once a comfort to Saint in the face of loss, in the face of—

Breath caught in his throat; hands shook—

Flashes of memory swelled in his heart.

Osiris.

His strong laugh. His deep, soulful eyes. The warmth of his smile. Of his touch.

Memories of comfort, but all he could feel in this moment… was guilt. Intense and overwhelming, like daggers cutting through him, sharpness bleeding through sweetness. Saint breathed deeply and stared at the medical equipment around the empty throne before him.

"The cost of my joy," Saint whispered, and he wept.
410486468.text_zh:
迷宫般的集市深处，圣城居民川流不息，享受着市场的一切。一只钢铁战兽正品尝新鲜水果，觉醒者讨价还价购买糕点，肉食的焦香和迷迭香的气味随风飘散，经过每个商人和工匠的摊位。

此起彼伏的声势对圣人14号来说既具有压倒性又让人安心，他停下来观看一名年长的埃里克斯尼族熟练地在磨损的纺织机上编织。编出的符号对这个Exo来说独特而陌生，但当鲜艳的天蓝布上闪耀出彩虹般的炫彩时，他不禁瞠目结舌。

很适合凯尔，圣人心想——

呼吸一滞，他的双手颤抖——

记忆的片段在他脑海中回荡。这一刻他所能感受到的…只有羞愧。

他匆忙走过编织者，穿过人群，径直来到一个茶摊前。他还没来得及张口婉拒，手中就被塞了杯试喝。他低头看去，杯中的茶色液体冒着蒸汽，散发着浓烈的草药味。

像是提炼出的暗影，圣人意识到——

呼吸一滞，他的双手颤抖——

记忆的片段充斥他的视线。这一刻他所能感受到的…只有悲伤。

他踉跄了一下，耳边响起道歉声，滚烫的液体洒了一地，集市的喧嚣在他耳边成了低沉的轰鸣。他需要逃离喧嚣、茶，周遭的一切。

他闭上眼睛，然后急匆匆地离开。

圣人回过神，发现自己在一片安静的区域，圣城的墙壁外，白昼已在消退。鲜绿的藤蔓从上方垂下，他头盔的轮廓在地上拉得又长又细，那是米瑟拉克斯那饱经风霜的医疗魔眼常等候的地方。圣人松了一口气。

这里只有他。

圣人把他最喜欢的纪念品，一只毛绒小熊，放在凯尔的王座上。他轻轻地调整着熊脖子上的薰衣草色缎带；洁净的缎带与熊朦胧的黑眼睛、略微磨损的耳朵和饱受搓揉的毛形成了鲜明对比。这份礼物曾给圣城中的一个孩子带来过慰藉。

这份礼物曾在圣人面对失去时带来过慰藉，在——

呼吸一滞，他的双手颤抖——

记忆片段在他心中涌动。

奥斯里斯。

他爽朗的笑声，深邃的眼神，温暖的微笑，以及触碰。

是充满慰藉的记忆，但在这一刻，他所能感受到的…只有强烈而无法承受的内疚，如同匕首将他刺穿，甜美中透着锋芒。圣人深吸一口气，凝视着空荡王座前的医疗设备。

“为我的快乐而付出的代价，”圣人轻声说道，然后啜泣起来。

4060793397.name: Rime-coat Raiment
4060793397.subtitle: "The impossibility of any situation is flexible, if you know where to look." —Mara Sov
4060793397.subtitle_zh: “如果你知道该去哪里找，任何不可能的境况都会有出路。”——玛拉·索维
4060793397.text:
Not for the first time, Mara finds Crow sitting in the rafters of her court, watching the clockwork creatures through high windows. 

"You wish to speak with me." She does not wait for him to come down, but joins him in the aerie. 

"How can you bear to see them cursed… knowing there is nothing you can do?" 

Mara considers this. "The impossibility of any situation is flexible, if you know where to look." Her brother's defeated sigh mirrors her own frustrations. "You're not wrong. It's heartbreaking to see those in your charge suffer." 

Up close, Mara can see how Light and time have reshaped him. Crow fidgets with a strand of his new cloak. "Eido is no closer to a cure. Though she would never admit it. We have nothing but dead ends and ticking clocks." 

"Do you suspect she will do something reckless?" she asks. 

"I've seen love drive people to extremes, break any law, fight any battle, just for a glimpse of hope." 

"Sometimes, hope is enough." Mara watches the battle play out below them, as it has countless times before. "Sometimes hope is all a leader can offer. Actions may build a bridge, but it is hope that drives us to cross to the other side." 

The cycle continues around them, a still point in the center of a whirling, recurring dream. 

For a moment, their duties wait.
4060793397.text_zh:
玛拉并非第一次发现乌鸦坐在她宫殿的椽子上，透过高高的窗户观察那些像发条一样的生物。 

“你想和我谈话。”她没有等他下来，而是飞了上去。 

“你怎能忍受看着他们遭受诅咒…心知自己无能为力？” 

玛拉思忖着这个问题。“如果你知道该去哪里找，任何不可能的境况都会有出路。”她兄弟挫败的叹息与她自己的沮丧如出一辙。“你说得没错。看到自己手下的人受苦，确实叫人心痛。” 

近距离观察，玛拉可以看到光能与时间如何重塑了他。乌鸦摆弄着他新披风上的一缕丝线。“解药的事，艾多完全没有头绪。尽管她绝不会承认。我们只是在接连走进死胡同和浪费宝贵的时间。” 

“你担心她会做出鲁莽的事吗？”她问道。 

“我见过爱让人走向极端，不惜一切代价，哪怕犯法，哪怕上战场，只为了一线希望。” 

“有时候，有希望就够了。”玛拉看着他们脚下的战斗，就像以前无数次发生的那样。“有时，领袖能给予的只有希望。行动也许可以搭建桥梁，但希望才是我们到达彼岸的动力。” 

循环在他们周围继续着，他们就像在快速旋转、不断重复的梦境中央，一个静止的点。 

有那么一瞬间，他们放下了自己的职责。

3031600404.name: VS Tech Sledge
3031600404.subtitle: Urgent|Personal|Unsent| Tell me you haven't signed on yet. Stay on the surface. Better yet, go back to Earth and out of Bray's orbit—
3031600404.subtitle_zh: 紧急|私人|未发送|告诉我你还没有签约。留在地表。最好还是返回地球，远离布瑞的轨道——
3031600404.text:
Leaning over on his sledge, István smacks the airlock button. 

Through the airlock speaker, the station says, "Lock-out procedure initialized. Remember to double-check your personal oxygen supply!" 

István gives a little get-on-with-it motion with a hand, waiting for the cycle to complete and let him out. The station's solar catchers should be self-repairing, but something always breaks, and then it's always his problem to fix. 

Normally alerts would come through his earpiece, but István's tweaked his to only give alerts for problems within 100 meters of his location. Issues with the labs five sectors away aren't his issue. At least not until his shift leader messages him. 

"Airlock opening. Technicians are asked to return once system charge drops to 40%." 

Nobody follows that procedure. 40% charge is an absurdly huge margin for getting back inside safely. But their fussy station keeps reminding them, always in the same cadence. 

He kicks his sledge into gear. It's a relief to get away from the research complexes, from everything in them he doesn't understand. 

István gets to work. Powering down a grid of the solar catchers, cutting out the damaged material, cutting a new piece from the replacement roll. The only sounds are the squeaking of his suit joints and the hiss of his cutter. 

 Until the station says, the loudest he's ever heard it, "Charge at 93%. Threat level alpha!" 

István jerks up, cutter gouging a hole in his repair material. No detail. Another false alarm from their fussy station. 

Even louder, the station says, "Charge at 93%. Threat level alpha!" 

He looks around. Nothing. Except—a handful of fiery glints in the dark. 

István grabs his sledge. It drags him up the hull, his suit scraping across the catchers in a way that'll leave bruises. He doesn't stop until he finds an overhang. 

And then he watches fragments of meteor coming in hot from far out of orbit, impacting the solar catchers right where he was standing. His roll of repair material is torn apart in an instant. 

"Technicians are asked to return once system charge drops to 40%." 

His charge is sitting steady at 86%. 

Shakily, he says, "Heading in. Now."
3031600404.text_zh:
伊什特万靠在机车上，按下了气闸按钮。 

通过气闸的扬声器，空间站广播道，“锁定程序已启动。请检查个人氧气供应是否正常！” 

伊什特万用手比了一个催促的动作，等待循环完成，让他出去。空间站的太阳能捕捉器本应自动修复，但总有东西会坏掉，而他总是那个修理的人。 

通常他的耳机会收到警报，但伊什特万设置了耳机只接收100米范围内的警报。五个区外实验室的问题？至少在他的值班领导发消息之前与他无关。 

“气闸正在打开。技术人员请在系统充能降至40%时返回。” 

没有人遵守这个程序。40%的充能对于安全返回来说绰绰有余，但喜欢小题大做的空间站总是以夸张的语音提醒他们。 

他启动了机车。能远离研究综合楼，远离里面他无法理解的一切，让他松了一口气。 

伊什特万着手开始工作，他关闭了一组太阳能捕捉器的电源，切掉损坏的材料，裁剪并安装新的修复材料。他能听到的只有防护服关节的嘎吱声和切割器的嘶嘶声。 

 突然，空间站传来他听过的最高音量，“充能93%。威胁等级Alpha！” 

伊什特万猛地站起来，切割器戳穿了修复材料。广播没有再说什么。看来大惊小怪的空间站又发出了错误警报。 

空间站的声音更大了，“充能93%。威胁等级Alpha！” 

他环顾四周，什么都没有，除了黑暗中几缕炽热的闪光。 

伊什特万抓住机车，借力爬上船体。他的防护服在捕捉器上摩擦，肯定会留下淤青，但他没有停下，而是径直去往一个悬架。 

然后，他看到流星碎片从轨道外飞来，撞击到他之前站立的太阳能捕捉器上。一卷修复材料瞬间被撕碎。 

“技术人员请在系统充能降至40%时返回。” 

他的充能还有86%。 

颤抖着，他说，“让我进去。”

3039049959.name: Rustpiercer
3039049959.subtitle: more pierce bodies front
3039049959.text:
It welds a rusted steel sliver to the front of the vehicle. The light from the Hadium welder flash-burns its eyes, leaving a reddish film over its vision. It does not blink. The searing metal chars the flesh on its hand, creating a blackened crust. It does not flinch. 

A Chieftain passes behind. It picks up another long spike of scrap from the pile. It jabs the welder in the middle of its back. 

The welder makes a sound between a chitter and a gurgle. 

an noy  di srupt ion  wha t  w ant 

The Chieftan drops the metal skewer at the welder's side. 

mor e  pier ce b odie s fr ont 

It mimes a stabbing motion and gestures to the nose of the vehicle. 

The welder hisses in dismay. It points aggressively at the ground with all four sets of claws. It clicks its teeth. 

ba lanc e  fal l 

The Chieftain growls deep in its thorax. An almost subaudible rumble. It points to the empty section of the frame where the engine has yet to be mounted. 

o bey  wor k o rg o pit 

The welder stares blankly at the empty engine mounting, uncomprehending. It hisses, without conviction this time, and picks up the metal sliver. 

The Chieftain looks out across the bay, where a fleet of similar vehicles are being assembled. It pushes a dim sensation of satisfaction far from its mind.
3039049959.text_zh:
它将一段锈迹斑斑的钢银焊接到载具前部。哈迪姆焊机发出的光灼伤了它的眼睛，留下一层红色的薄膜，但它没有眨眼。炽热的金属烫伤了它的手，形成了一层黑色的硬壳，但它的手没有抖。 

一位族长从后面走过。它从料堆中取出一根长长的废金属尖刺，戳了下焊工的后背中部。 

焊工发出一种介于啾啾和咯咯之间的声音。 

讨 厌干 扰要 什么 

族长将金属杆放在焊工的一旁。 

更 多尖 刺 正 面穿 敌 

它模仿着突刺的动作，指向载具前端。 

焊工发出失望的嘶鸣。它用力地将四组爪子指着地面，咔嗒咔嗒地咬牙。 

失 去平 衡 

族长从胸腔深处发出低吼，几乎是低鸣般的隆隆声。它指向框架上尚未安装发动机的空荡位置。 

服 从工 作否 则进 搏斗 场 

焊工茫然地盯着发动机的安装位置。它发出不再坚定的嘶鸣，然后捡起了那根钢银。 

族长望向舱室，那里正在组装一系列类似的载具。它将一丝微弱的满足感推到脑海深处。

3489448910.name: Old Rancor
3489448910.subtitle: See the world with fresh eyes.
3489448910.text:
CORMORANT-LEVEL ENCRYPTED MESSAGE FOLLOWS.  

AUDIO SURVEILLANCE TRANSCRIPT AA726CBJ913JHS443 

UNRESOLVED EVALUATION: PENDING DIRECTIVE 

I greet you in the Light, Ixis. Thank you for speaking with me. I understand you have some questions about the House of Light? 

… 

Oh! Umm. No offense taken. Our Houses haven't always embraced with four arms.  

… 

I understand your reluctance. Your history is so much longer than mine. As Variks is constantly reminding me. You haven't had much reason to trust the Humans. 

… 

I can see why you believe that. But you must admit, much has changed since the Twilight Gap. This is a new period in history. Potentially, the greatest era of development we've known since the Drift. It's an opportunity to move beyond traditional rivalries to create new— 

… 

Eramiskel may have evolved more than you think. We've spoken at length about the hardships your generation faced. Many at the hands of the Humans. And many more self-inflicted. I know it's hard to change old ways. But the young Eliksni of House Light—those hatched after the Drift—we have no appetite for more death. We share no animosity with the Humans. They're our neighbors now. 

… 

Well, if cooperation is defeat, then we are defeated! All thanks to the bloody mess left to us by our venerated elders! 

… 

I apologize. That was… unkind. I know you've faced much, and persevered. But if a loss of pride is the cost of peace, then so be it. The House of Light will raise their hatchlings in safety, free from old bitterness, and be glad of it. I just hope you're able to see the City as I do. Someday.
3489448910.text_zh:
以下为鸬鹚级加密信息。  

音频监控记录AA726CBJ913JHS443 

尚未评估：等待指示 

我在光能之下问候你，伊克西斯。感谢你愿意与我交谈。我知道你对光能氏族有一些疑问对吗？ 

… 

哦！呃，我不介意。我们两氏族并不总是张开四臂相互拥抱的。  

… 

我理解你的不情愿，你们氏族的历史比我的悠久得多。瓦里克斯总是提醒我，你们没有多少理由信任人类。 

… 

我明白你为什么这么认为。但你得承认，暮光峡谷之后很多事都变了。这是个新的历史时期，可能是大漂流以来最伟大的发展时代。是个机会去化解前嫌，创造新的—— 

… 

也许伊拉莫斯凯尔的演变远超你的想象。我们详细讨论过你们这一代人遭受的苦难，不少是人类造成的，而更多是自身造成的。我知道要改变旧习很难，但光能氏族的年轻埃里克斯尼族——大漂流后孵化的那些——我们不希望看到更多的伤亡。我们对人类没有敌意，他们现在是我们的邻居了。 

… 

如果合作就是失败，那我们就是失败了！全都要感谢尊敬的先辈们留给我们的血腥烂摊子！ 

… 

对不起，这么说…太苛刻。我知道你们历尽艰辛坚持了下来，但如果和平的代价是失去骄傲，我们接受。光能氏族将在安全的环境中抚养幼雏，满怀喜悦地远离旧怨。我只希望你有朝一日能用我的视角看看这座圣城。

3158812152.name: The Xûrfboard
3158812152.subtitle: Who knows where the next wave will take you.
3158812152.subtitle_zh: 谁知道下一波会把你带向何方。
3158812152.text:
The ship's a spruced-up Galliot, glorious in its pearlescent blue paint and bizarre angles. Just looking at it makes Rahila want to take it on a joyride clear out of the Sol system. Walking up the gangway into the ship itself makes her want to cry.

The ship has the necessary long-range capabilities and just enough expanded capacity for a full fireteam's worth of supplies and survey equipment. Between the Vanguard's support, generous contributions from the Awoken, and several upgrades courtesy of a lapsed Dead Orbit adherent, the ship's a lot to be entrusted with. 

"These new sensors are something else," Isidro announces from the cockpit. "If so much as a mouse sneezes out there in the black, we'll pick it up."

Rahila squints at him. "A mouse?"

"Space-mice. Or, you know, a gravitational anomaly. Or mysterious, freaky signals." 

"Vanguard will be along in a few to see us off." Roche-5's composed baritone emerges from the hatch leading to the cargo hold. "You two ready?" 

 Rahila settles into the copilot's chair. "To go find out what's left of our solar system? 'Course we are." 

"Remember," Roche intones gravely, "This is pure recon. No big risks." 

Rahila and Isidro exchange grins. "Sure thing."
3158812152.text_zh:
这是一艘精心装饰的快船，形状独特，涂着珍珠蓝色的漆面。仅仅一瞥就让拉吉拉想驾驶它直接离开太阳系。登上舷梯进入飞船的那一刻，她几乎感动得要落泪。

这艘飞船具备必要的远程能力，而且刚好有足够的扩展空间可以容纳一整支火力战队的补给和调查设备。凭借先锋的支持、觉醒者的慷慨捐赠，以及一位死亡轨道的前拥护者提供的几项升级，这艘飞船承载着众多期望。 

“这些新传感器简直令人叹为观止，”伊西德罗在驾驶舱中说道。“就算只是黑暗中的一只小老鼠打个喷嚏，我们都能探测到。”

拉吉拉眯眼看着他，“小老鼠？”

“太空老鼠，或者引力异常，又或是神秘的怪信号之类的。” 

“先锋马上就会来送我们走。”罗切-5沉稳的男中音从通往货舱的舱口传来。“你俩准备好了吗？” 

 拉吉拉在副驾驶椅上坐定，“去看看太阳系还剩些什么吗？当然准备好了。” 

“记住，”罗切严肃地说，“这次只是去侦查，别铤而走险。” 

拉吉拉和伊西德罗相视而笑，“没问题。”

4123860739.name: Nightlight
4123860739.subtitle: "It's even worse in the dark. Those little things are fast!"
4123860739.subtitle_zh: “在黑暗中更糟糕。那些小东西太快了！”
4123860739.text:
"You ever seen a Screeb?" the Hunter asked and tilted his head toward the Eliksni before him. They perched on a stack of crates, spending their break well above the hustle and bustle of the Variisis Core.

"I've heard of them through Scribe Eido's retellings, but never seen one. Are they not simply small, bulbous creatures?" the Eliksni inquired and folded both sets of his arms.

"That explode."

"Yes, but… I don't understand the fear induced by them," the Eliksni said. "Surely something like an Ahamkara would warrant more terror?"

"He's just mad that every time we encounter them, he somehow always becomes their target," a Warlock said. "It's practically serendipitous." She hopped up onto the crate beside the Hunter, who rolled his eyes. 

The Eliksni chuckled.

"What about those Tormentors?" said a Corsair, placing a box down and joining the conversation. "Hearing your bones strain while within their clutches…"

The Eliksni tapped his mandible and nodded slowly.

"Agreed, worse than a Screeb," the Warlock declared.

"Okay, fine, what's the scariest thing YOU'VE seen out there?" the Hunter bit back.

The Warlock didn't even hesitate.

"Eris Morn."

There was a long pause. Someone dropped something further down the street, and the noise echoed in their silence.

"…Yeah," the Hunter said. The Corsair and Eliksni mumbled their agreement. "Fine, but Screeb juice on its own—"

A bout of groans and disgust swept through the group as they scattered. The Hunter followed quickly behind the Warlock to continue his rant. The Eliksni shook his head and followed the Corsair in the opposite direction, inquiring further about the Tormentors.
4123860739.text_zh:
“你见过变异体吗？”猎人问道，把头偏向了他面前的埃里克斯尼族。他们居于一堆板条箱上，远离瓦里希斯核心的喧嚣，享受着休息时间。

“我听文士艾多讲过，但从未亲眼得见。它们不就是些小球根状生物吗？”埃里克斯尼族问道，交叉着两对手臂。

“会爆炸的那种。”

“对，但…我不明白为什么它们会让人感到害怕，”埃里克斯尼族说道。“像阿罕卡拉那样的东西肯定会让人更加恐惧吧？”

“他只是生气每次我们遇到它们时，自己总是莫名其妙地成为它们的目标，”一名术士说道。“简直是命定般的巧合。”她跳上猎人身边的箱子，猎人翻了个白眼。 

埃里克斯尼族轻笑起来。

“那些折磨者呢？”一名海盗军放下一个箱子，加入了谈话。“听到它们抓住你时骨头嘎吱作响的声音…”

埃里克斯尼族敲了敲下巴，缓缓点了点头。

“同意，比变异体还糟糕，”术士说道。

“行，好吧，你在外面见过的最可怕的东西是什么？”猎人反问道。

术士完全没有犹豫。

“埃里斯·摩恩。”

一阵长久的沉默。街上更远处有人掉落了东西，声音在寂静中回响。

“…的确，”猎人说。海盗军和埃里克斯尼族低声表示同意。“好吧，但光是变异体汁——”

一阵呻吟和作呕声在人群中蔓延，他们一哄而散。猎人快步跟在术士身后，继续闲聊。埃里克斯尼族则摇摇头，跟着海盗军朝相反的方向走去，进一步打听折磨者的事情。

1681909867.name: 1. Judgment
1681909867.text:
This being the recollection of Irrha of the House of Slayers, apprentice to the Baron Kiiraskes.

[This is so exciting! I will translate as best I can. –Eido, Scribe of the House of Light] 

It was a beautiful day at the end of the wet season, and the waters had risen high in the canals such that the Palace of Judgment sat on a limned mirror.

My pilot rowed us steadily between the raised walkways. The banners of the great Houses flanked us on either side of the channel. Nearest to the landing, the banners of Kings and Judgment cast long shadows down upon us. It was through them that our unity was possible, and we were not to forget it. 

I had spent five days traveling to reach Riis-Ath-Lodrii [1], and just as long before that receiving instruction in the formalities and proper courtesies to be observed in the presence of the Scribes of Judgment. But I was greeted at the landing not by a formal assemblage, but by a lone thin figure dressed in the layered finery of Judgment's officers.

He reached down to help me up out of the watercraft before I had time to bow, sparing only a moment to dust Ether accretion from my cloak. 

"Velask, Apprentice Irrha," he said, in a tone that conveyed I had already erred in some way. "Please hurry." 





I was led to a side entrance into the Halls of Judgment, where my escort expertly navigated a maze of corridors that led into a small, unremarkable reception room. We stepped into the hushed silence of stifled argument.

There were two figures waiting for us in the room. The first was dressed in the mantle of the city Peacekeepers and the ornamented headdress of the House of Stone [2]. 

Members of the House of Stone were the foundation upon which the city's defenses were built, and I thought then—as I still do—that the virtues of that House showed in none more nobly than its Kell, Chelchis. She stood twice as tall as I, her limbs as thick as the support beams above us. I could have believed any number of stories about her. 

The second figure was clad in a void-black cloak and a pytha-hide [3] crest. The absence of a House symbol marked her as a Baron of the Order of Slayers. 

The Slayer Barons had tamed Riis back when it grew wild and disordered in the first century of the Great Machine's Ether Flood. First Riis, and then the moons beyond our sky, which were often hostile to us. Within the hatchling-schools, the minders showed us shadow-stories of cunning hunters, adepts of the Great Machine, working in tandem to bring down the biggest monsters of their age.

I did not think so highly of Baron Kiiraskes when I saw her—leaner than Chelchis, but twice as scarred—until she raised her head and I saw the gleam of her eyes beneath her cap. There was a feverish cunning in her scrutiny.

"You brought me a hatchling," she complained. 

I felt a hot, familiar resentment—and desperation. It was more important than anything that she not turn me away.

"I have been two solar cycles studying," I pleaded.

"I think Chelchis here has carried clutches for longer than that," said the Baron.

Chelchis' irritated tolling [4] would have withered me in my shell, were it directed at me. All the same, I felt a sick humiliation for having been slighted in front of her.

Nearby, the Judgment official bobbed his head in disapproval.

"You have been assigned what you require," he said. "When was the last time that you needed to be summoned out here, that our Peacekeepers could not handle matters? Apprentice Irrha will suffice."

Kiiraskes gave little indication she heard the official's words. 
"What is your House?" she asked me.

This moment was inevitable.

"I do not have one." It occurred to me at last that I might have been brought here as an insult.

Kiiraskes regarded me steadily. "We can't all be Kings."

The official rubbed his hands together in agitation. "It will be quick work, Baron. Travel to the farm of Haaksis and dispatch the animal that troubles him. If you require reinforcements, send for the support of a House."

Kiiraskes grunted and turned away. I began to bow and felt her claws latch onto my arm like a star-steel cuff, pulling me from the room.

"Be careful, Slayer Baron." The small chimes on Chelchis' headdress rang softly as she turned her head. 

I did not see the gesture Kiiraskes made in response, but I heard Chelchis' amused hiss.



[1: "Veins of Riis," or the Channels Through the Body of Riis. One city of many!] 
[2: The famed House of Stone!]
[3: A vicious predator native to Riis. Variks says that these were delicious.] 
[4: To click a warning at an Eliksni that they can feel in their shell. I bet Humans can feel the vibration in their sternums!]  
[I was going to translate everything very literally, but Variks told me I was "ripping the soul from every word." Please forgive me some poetic license! –Eido, Scribe of House Light]
1681909867.text_zh:
这是基拉斯克丝公爵的学徒，杀手氏族的伊尔哈的回忆。

[这太激动人心了！我会尽力翻译的。——光能氏族文士艾多] 

雨季末的这天风和日丽，运河里水位高涨，审判宫殿仿佛坐落在一片精细勾勒的明镜之上。

我的领航员稳稳地划动着桨，带我们穿梭在高出的走道之间。航道两岸，各大氏族的旗帜在我们的侧面迎风招展。在最接近登陆点的地方，王族氏族与审判氏族的旗帜投下的长影盖住了我们。正是因为他们的存在，我们方能团结一心，而我们绝不能忘记这一点。 

我历经五天的长途跋涉抵达里斯-阿斯-洛德里[1]，在此之前还耗掉了同样的时日研习在审判氏族文士面前应遵循的礼节与得体的仪态。但在登陆之时，迎接我的并非庄重的集会，而是一个身着审判官员层层华服的孤瘦身影。

我还没来得及鞠躬，他就伸手扶我从船上起来，又花了片刻工夫拍去我披风上积落的乙太尘埃。 

“维拉斯克，学徒伊尔哈，”他的话语中带着一丝我已经犯了错的意味。“请快点。” 





我被带到审判大厅的侧门，护送我的那位官员熟练地穿过一系列错综复杂的走廊，最终带我来到了一间不起眼的小接待室。我们走进时，里头原本嘈杂的争论顿时变得鸦雀无声。

房内有两个身影在等候我们。第一个人身穿城市和平守护者的斗篷，头上戴着顽石氏族[2]的华丽头饰。 

顽石氏族的成员是城市防御的基石。我当时就在想——现在也还是这么认为——顽石氏族的美德在其凯尔切尔奇斯的身上体现得最为淋漓尽致。她的个子比我高出一倍，肢体则跟我们头上的顶梁柱一般粗壮。关于她的种种传说，我都愿意相信。 

第二个人身穿一袭漆黑如夜的披风，头戴一顶由皮塔兽革[3]制成的头冠。其上没有氏族标志，这表明她是一位隶属于杀手教团的公爵。 

在那个大机器乙太洪流肆虐的初始世纪，里斯曾陷入狂野无序，那时便是由杀手公爵们将它驯服的。他们的征服之旅，始于里斯，随后延伸至我们苍穹之外那些常常对我们抱有敌意的卫星。在幼雏学校里，保育员带我们看了许多暗影戏，戏里那些狡黠的猎人，亦是深谙大机器之道的专家，携手击败了属于他们时代的最恶怪物。

初见基拉斯克丝公爵时，我对其评价不高——她比切尔奇斯更瘦削，身上的伤疤却多了一倍——直到她抬起头，我看到她冠帽下闪烁的眼眸。她的眼神中蕴藏着一种狂热的狡黠。

“你给我带来了一只幼雏，”她抱怨道。 

我感受到一股炽热而熟悉的愤恨——以及绝望。无论如何都不能让她把我赶走。

“我已经苦学了两个太阳周期，”我恳求道。

“我想这位切尔奇斯怀卵的时间都比那要长，”公爵说道。

如果切尔奇斯生气的鸣响[4]是冲我来的，恐怕我早就萎缩进自己的壳里了。尽管如此，我还是因为在她面前受到轻视而感到难忍的屈辱。

附近的审判官员不以为然地晃了晃头。

“你已被指派你要求的人力，”他说道。“上一次因为我们的和平守护者处理不了，而需要召你来此是什么时候？学徒伊尔哈就足够了。”

基拉斯克丝几乎没有表现出她听到了官员说的话。 
“你属于哪个氏族？”她问我。

这一刻是不可避免的。

“我没有氏族。”我终于意识到自己可能是为了侮辱她而被带到这里来的。

基拉斯克丝坚定地看着我。“不是王族氏族咯。”

官员不安地揉着手。“这是一项简单的工作，公爵。前往哈克西斯的农场，解决掉那头困扰他的野兽。要是你需要增援，就派人请求氏族的支援。”

基拉斯克丝咕哝了一声，转过身去。我刚开始鞠躬，却突然感到她的爪子如同星钢打造的镣铐一般扣住了我的手臂，把我拉出了房间。

“小心点，杀手公爵。”切尔奇斯转过头时，她头饰上的小铃铛轻轻地响了起来。 

我没有看到基拉斯克丝作出回应的手势，但听到了切尔奇斯被逗乐的嘶鸣。



[1: 里斯脉城，或称里斯的体脉。众城之城！] 
[2: 久负盛名的顽石氏族！]
[3: 一种原产于里斯的凶猛食肉动物。据瓦里克斯说它们很美味。] 
[4: 向埃里克斯尼族发出让其能透过壳感觉到的警告。人类肯定也能感觉到胸骨的震动！]  
[我本来打算逐字逐句地直译，但瓦里克斯告诉我，那样做是“剥夺了每个词的灵魂”。请原谅我加入了一些诗意的发挥！——光能氏族文士艾多]

1681909864.name: 2. Fields
1681909864.text:
Kiiraskes stank strongly of sea-grass and sunsoak root [1]. I took care to sit toward the front of the watercraft, but the odor wrestled powerfully against the wind.

I did my best to focus on the task I had been given, which was to mix the contents of three flasks into a fourth. I prided myself on the steadiness of my hands, and the work was not so difficult that I couldn't steal glimpses of our route.

We followed the river as it skirted the sprawling residential districts, then turned and cut toward the listing sun. I watched the crowds thin as canal-side markets gave way to orderly arrays of residential towers and aerial traffic, then to radiating lines of transport arterials, waterways, and roads, connecting each of Riis's great cities to one another in a shimmering network.

We passed lines of pilgrims making their way to the site where the Great Machine first came to Riis, the hill at the heart of Riis-Ath-Lodrii. I saw high priests of the House of Dancers, devoted clerics who gorge themselves past satiation on Ether until they tower above their peers, then amputate their lower arms in ritual supplication to the Great Machine.

It was strange to see those shambling giants. But there was something awe-inspiring in it. The shuffling march of hundreds, unified in purpose.

Kiiraskes followed my gaze, then spat audibly into the water. "Fanaticism is what landed us in the wars. Fanaticism, pride, and Ether-thirst."

I looked at her. "You were in the Edge Wars?"

Kiiraskes hissed. "I have no war stories for you, hatchling." She gestured toward the flasks. "If this is serious, you should be prepared."

"And if it truly is only an animal?"

"You should still learn how to mix a tonic on the go. Don't drop that."





The farms of the House of Rain were among the most splendid on all of Riis, and the quadrant assigned to Baron Haaksis was no exception. There were great swathes of forest, carefully hemmed and controlled, arranged neatly around crop fields.

It could not have been done without the machines.
 
Baron Haaksis had a fleet of them: small, autonomous drones that moved about planting, harvesting, and measuring Ether uptake. The sound of their toil was that of wind across grassland. A thousand small tasks undertaken without rest or complaint.

For all this, the farm was strangely absent of workers. There should have been at least a few machine-tenders, monitoring the proceedings and providing maintenance and direction. Nor did any guards come to meet us as I lashed the watercraft to the dock.

We stepped out onto sun-fed walkways braced by beautiful, leafy plants. Kiiraskes pointed to the bags of supplies, and in my eagerness to prove my strength, I gathered all of them. They were very heavy, and by the time I managed to follow Kiiraskes to Haaksis' doorstep, I felt as if I were pinned to the earth.





Considering the lush abundance that surrounded it, the round building where Haaksis kept his office was sparse and joyless. The sole decoration was two twin sets of blades he kept on one wall: a memento of the Edge Wars. I had seen dozens like them throughout my upbringing, only some of them genuine.

More interesting was the drone on his desk, which Haaksis seemed to be in the process of repairing. It was a hybrid reconnaissance-defense drone called a "Shank," the kind that became popular during the war. Not many Eliksni still possessed them in peacetime. But such an interest suited a noble like Haaksis. 

Haaksis was dressed in the rich hues of Rain. He was of a height with Kiiraskes, if slighter in build, and stiff in his bearing.

I bowed low and formally, feeling the weight of my House-less status. Kiiraskes reached out and lifted me bodily upright by the carapace with no more difficulty than she might have plucked a flowering plant.

"I sent for Slayers," Haaksis said. He looked at me, and I felt my shell itch.

Kiiraskes spread her hands, untroubled. "So we've come. The House of Judgment mentioned an animal."

"No. I told them… I told them many times. This is not an animal," Haaksis said. At his sides, his claws clenched into fists, one after the other. "It is an old evil."

I looked up at Kiiraskes but found no sign of her thoughts. Her mandibles clicked quietly. "You've seen it?"

Haaksis sagged then, as if already weary of conversation. "It attacked my people. I tried to recover the bodies, but… And then the House of Judgment took its time—"

"Do you know where it is now?"

"No. Nothing can hide on this farm without the sensors tracking it. The forest tracts are just as well-tended. But there is a Garden-Way [2], between… we were letting that grow, re-wild for a few cycles…"

"We'll track it down," Kiiraskes said. "Tell me where the bodies are."
 
I felt relieved to hear her speak of us as "we." But the feeling didn't last long. Even as he brought up the displays and maps to guide Kiiraskes, Haaksis kept staring in my direction, and I realized he did not expect me to survive.



[1. Sea-grass seems straightforward enough, but I found few other references to "sunsoak root." Does it absorb Light?]
[2. A space around farmland where the local flora and fauna are left to grow naturally. These were carefully maintained, so you couldn't really call them wild.]
1681909864.text_zh:
基拉斯克丝身上散发出浓烈的海草和日晒树根的气味[1]。我特意坐在船头，但那气味却顽强地逆着风势阵阵袭来。

我尽力集中精神完成交给我的任务，也就是将三个烧瓶里的东西混着倒进第四个烧瓶里。我手很稳，这一点我一直引以为豪，而且这活不算太难，我还能偷瞄一下我们的路线。

河流蜿蜒穿过了大片杂乱延伸的居民区，我们顺着河前行，然后转向朝着落日驶去。我看着人群逐渐稀疏，运河畔的市集渐渐隐退，被整齐的住宅塔和空中交通取代，最后只剩四通八达的交通干线、水道和道路，它们将里斯的各大城市紧密相连，编织成一张熠熠生辉的网络。

我们经过了朝圣者的队伍，他们正前往里斯-阿斯-洛德里中心的山丘，那里是大机器初临里斯的地方。我看到了舞者氏族的高阶祭司，那些虔诚的教士们贪婪无度地吸收着乙太，直至身形超越常人，然后在仪式中斩断自己的前臂，以此向大机器献上虔诚的祈求。

目睹那些步履蹒跚的巨人，感觉既奇特又令人敬畏。数百人虽步伐踉跄，却因抱有共同使命而整齐前进。

基拉斯克丝顺着我的目光看去，然后用力向水里吐了一口唾沫。“正是狂热主义让我们陷入了战争。狂热、傲慢，还有对乙太的饥渴。”

我看着她。“你参加过边缘战争？”

基拉斯克丝发出嘶鸣。“我没有战争故事讲给你听，幼雏。”她指了指那些烧瓶，“如果这差事不简单，那你就该做好准备。”

“如果真的只是一头野兽呢？”

“那你也该学会怎么快速配制药剂。别懈怠。”





骤雨氏族农场的壮观程度在整个里斯都是首屈一指的，分配给哈克西斯公爵的地块也不例外。这里有大片精心围护看管的森林，整齐地环绕在农田周围。

如果没有机器，这是不可能完成的。
 
哈克西斯公爵拥有一支这样的无人机队：它们小巧且自主运行，在田间往来穿梭，负责种植、收割和测量乙太摄取量，辛勤劳作的声音如同风吹过草原一般，不辞辛劳、毫无怨言地执行着上千个小任务。

尽管如此，农场里却出奇地缺少工人。本应至少有几名机器操作员来监督作业，提供维护和指导的。我把船系好停靠在码头时，也没有任何守卫前来迎接。

我们走到阳光充足的步道上，旁边是枝繁叶茂的美丽植物。基拉斯克丝指向补给袋，而我急于展示自己的力量，便把它们都收集了起来。这些东西非常重，等我勉强跟着基拉斯克丝走到哈克西斯的家门口时，我感觉自己好像被钉在了地上。





与周围葱郁的丰饶景象相比，哈克西斯设立办公室的圆形建筑显得简朴而无趣。唯一的装饰是他挂在一面墙上的两套双刃：边缘战争的纪念物。我在自己的成长过程中见过几十件这样的战刃，但其中只有少数是真品。

更有趣的是他桌上的无人机，哈克西斯似乎正在修理它。这种名为“侦察机”的混合型侦察防御无人机在战争时期非常流行。和平年代还保有这种无人机的埃里克斯尼族为数不多。但这样的爱好正适合像哈克西斯这样的贵族。 

哈克西斯身着骤雨氏族标志性的华丽色彩。他的身高与基拉斯克丝相仿，但体型稍显瘦削，举止也有些僵硬。

我恭敬地深深鞠躬，体会着自己无氏族的卑微。基拉斯克丝伸出手，抬着甲壳将我扶起，像摘下一株花草般的轻而易举。

“我请他们派来杀手，”哈克西斯说道。他的目光让我感到一阵外壳发痒。

基拉斯克丝摊开她的手，神色自若。“所以我们来了。审判氏族提到了一头野兽。”

“不。我告诉过他们…我告诉过他们很多次。不是什么野兽，”哈克西斯说道。他两侧的爪子一个接一个地紧握成拳。“是古老的邪恶。”

我抬头看向基拉斯克丝，但察觉不出她的想法。她的下颚轻柔地咔嗒着。“你见过它？”

哈克西斯垂头丧气，仿佛已厌倦了交谈。“它袭击了我的人。我试图找回尸体，可是…而审判氏族迟迟不肯行动——”

“你知道它现在在哪里吗？”

“不知道。在这个农场里，没有任何东西能躲过传感器的追踪。林地也一样管理得井井有条。但有一片‘花园之路'[2]…我们让它自然生长了几个周期，重新野化…”

“我们会找到它的，”基拉斯克丝说道。“告诉我尸体在哪里。”
 
听到她用“我们”来称呼她和我，让我感到了一丝宽慰。但这种感觉没有持续多久。哈克西斯拿出显示屏和地图来为基拉斯克丝指路时，仍会不断盯向我这边，而我意识到他认定我必死无疑。



[1: 海草似乎很直白明了，但我几乎没找到其他关于“日晒树根”的记载。它能吸收光能吗？]
[2: 农田周围让当地动植物能够自然生长的一片区域。这些地方受到精心养护，所以并不算是真正的野生区域。]

1681909865.name: 3. Light
1681909865.text:
At the time, it seemed natural to pursue the creature at the hour of night when it was most likely to be on the hunt. I was distracted from all thought of fear by Kiiraskes, who decided to question me briefly on the qualities of Tenar, Brossk, and Liisok [1]: which excelled as purgatives, and which burned through chitin and stone alike.

At last, she said, "You said you studied. From records?"

"Yes, Baron." There were no Slayer-apothecarists left to train under. And even if any survived, none who would visit the common quadrants of the small city where I was raised.

Kiiraskes paused in her trudging progress up the path. We had divided the supplies between ourselves this time, and now she passed me a vial. "Drink this."

I was quick to obey, noting the odor of sunsoak root that clung to the liquid. I hoped this first taste of a Slayer's tonic would fill me with strength, or make me grow as if I had molted five times over.

It tasted foul. I became very aware of how little I had eaten since arriving.
 
"Come," Kiiraskes said. "I think I smell one of Haaksis' guards."

I could not smell anything but Kiiraskes. I followed her as she stepped nimbly across one of the sluices and onto the rich, loamy soil that marked the wildest part of Haaksis' property.

It was around this time that I started to feel the tonic's effects. I saw Light—a tiny luminescence at the edge of my sight. I turned to watch it drifting slowly toward the ground, and by the time it landed, I could see more motes gathered over the undergrowth in clouds, like dust. Far above, I read the flow of Ether like a river through the sky. I set my bags down, looked at my hands, and saw a glow beneath my shell, as if the tonic had illuminated me from the inside out.

But it was not just me. I looked at Kiiraskes and saw Light. The push-pull of air through spiracles, the misting of expelled Ether, the fervent radiance of her eyes.

She had stilled to observe me, and now she spoke.

"The Light is in all things. We cannot control it, but we can entice it. Draw it close." She chuffed. "Like a greedy pellauk."

I was cradled in the grip of awe, and the interruption was like a clout to the face. "The Great Machine is not a herd-animal sniffing after Yka fruit!" In my offense, I forgot that I was her apprentice, and at her mercy.

Kiiraskes laughed. "Don't you like Yka fruit?"

Annoyed, I looked away, to the sky. On a clear night like this, it was possible to watch the Great Machine drift across Riis's upper atmosphere. Under the tonic's influence, I saw it trailing Light—Life, I thought dizzily—like a comet.

The Great Machine had terraformed Riis's moons in four blinks, then brought the Ether-flood to Riis. A time of plenty, when no hatchlings starved and foundered in their development. A time of too-much, as the House of Judgment would tell it. A time without hierarchies, without sense. Our people had to change, to adapt.

In this new age, they called me a "Drekh." Useless, House-less.

"And now, the body," Kiiraskes said. 





It was Eliksni—or had been. The mangled form at our feet had been twisted into a tangle of limbs. If not for the torn mantle attached to it, I am not sure I would have known the body to belong to one of Haaksis' guards.

Worse was the emptiness of it. Every living thing around the body shone with the Great Machine's influence. I had not known this stranger [2], but their death left a void in the world which the tonic now permitted me to see. I was glad then for my empty stomach.
 
Kiiraskes crouched down near the body and at once began touching it, shifting an arm here and there, inspecting it. I stood by, uncertain of whether I disapproved, too afraid to complain in any case. The plant life here was not yet so dense, and we were exposed, though—as Kiiraskes had pointed out—any creatures would be as well.

"Was it an animal?" I asked. There were predators out here, after all. Though nothing that would voluntarily attack Kiiraskes unless it was desperate.

She gestured for me to crouch beside her. "Look," she said. And then, once I had settled beside her: "What don't you see?" 

"Light," I said, suffused again with sudden grief.

She swatted me. "Look down."
 
I did. I saw a cluster of lights—small larvae that had gathered in the footprints I'd left around the body. I brushed one absently from my leg, then realized…

"They're avoiding the body," I said.

Kiiraskes grunted, pleased. "Touch here. Tell me what you feel."

I touched the guard's carapace and felt something wet under my claws. I had long enough to recognize that the beast had cracked his shell down the middle, and to fear that I could never stomach a meal again. And then, suddenly, it was as if I had dipped my hand into a cold pond. 

I felt anger. A sharp, foreign fury that had nothing to do with my own revulsion and fear. Beneath it, there was something like… remorse [3]. Could an animal feel remorse?

"You feel it? We cannot see this evil [4], but it's there," Kiiraskes said. "Come. Judgment was wrong. I'm taking you back to the boat—if we're quick, it won't have time to follow us."
 
But the monster did not stalk us across the forest.

It poured out of the air in a cloud of billowing shadow. 



[1: For reference, I believe Brossk is the purgative. Liisok translates as Rock-Destroyer, or maybe Stone-Eater.] 
[2: Technically, the archaic word used here means "Eliksni from outside one's House."]
[3: This word is not quite right, but I don't know a better one. Guilt for something that has not yet occurred? A voluntary acceptance of responsibility that was not yours. Variks has not been forthcoming.] 
[4: I believe we would now call this "Darkness."]
1681909865.text_zh:
当时，在夜深人静、怪物最有可能出没狩猎的时候追捕它似乎是理所当然的，而我所有的恐惧念头都被基拉斯克丝分散了，她决定让我简单介绍一下特纳尔、布罗斯克和利索克[1]的特性：哪种作为泻剂效果最佳，哪种又能毫不费力地穿透甲壳和石头。

最后，她问道，“你说你苦学过。是从记载里学的吗？”

“是的，公爵。”这世上已经没剩下能教我的杀手药剂师了。就算有人幸存，他们也不会到访我长大的小城的平民街区。

基拉斯克丝停下了在小径上艰难前行的脚步。这次我们各自分担了补给，而现在她递给我一个小瓶。“喝了它。”

我很快就照做了，并注意到液体中附着的日晒树根气味。我希望这第一口杀手药剂能让我充满力量，或者让我像蜕了五次皮一样成长。

它的味道难以下咽。我开始清楚意识到，自从到这里后，我几乎没有吃过什么东西。
 
“走吧，”基拉斯克丝说道。“我想我闻到了某个哈克西斯守卫。”

我除了基拉斯克丝的气味什么都闻不到。我跟在她后面。她灵活地跨过一个水闸，踏上肥沃的壤土，那里是哈克西斯的农场中最为野生的地方。

就在这时，我开始感受到药剂的效果。我看到了光能——在我视线边缘闪烁的一种微弱荧光。我转过身，看着它慢慢飘向地面，当它落地时，我看到更多萤光像尘埃一样聚集成云。在遥远的上空，我看到乙太的流动像一条河穿过天空。我放下背包，看了看自己的手，只见我的外壳下闪耀着光芒，仿佛是药剂从里到外照亮了我。

不仅我是如此。我望向基拉斯克丝，也看到了光能。通过她气孔一进一出的空气，被排出的乙太形成的雾气，以及她眼中狂热的光芒。

她一直在静静观察着我，现在她开口说话了。

“光能存在于万物之中。我们无法控制它，但我们可以吸引它。让它靠近。”她哼了一声。“就像一头贪婪的佩劳克。”

我正沉浸在敬畏之中，这突如其来的话语像是一记耳光打在我的脸上。“大机器可不是嗅探着亚卡果的畜牧动物！”我如此冒犯地说道，忘了自己是任她摆布的学徒。

基拉斯克丝笑了。“你不喜欢亚卡果吗？”

我恼怒地看向别处，仰望天空。在这样一个晴朗的夜晚，可以看到大机器在里斯的高层大气缓缓飘过。在药剂的作用下，我看到它像彗星般拖着光能——恍惚间觉得那即是生命。

大机器眨眼间就完成了对里斯卫星的地貌改造，然后把乙太洪流带到了里斯。那是一个富足的时代，没有幼雏会在成长过程中挨饿或夭折。如审判氏族所言，那也是一个物极必反的时代，一个缺乏秩序和理智的时代。我们的族人必须改变，必须适应。

在这个新时代，他们管我叫“堕落者士兵”。无用，无氏族。

“现在，来看尸体吧，”基拉斯克丝说道。 





这是埃里克斯尼族的尸体，或者说曾经是。我们脚下这具残缺不全的躯体已经肢体交缠，难以辨认。要不是连着它的那件残破斗篷，我可能都不会知道它曾属于哈克西斯的一名守卫。

更糟糕的是它的空虚。尸体周围的每个生物都闪耀着大机器的光芒。我不认识这个陌生人[2]，但其死亡在这世界上留下了一处空洞，而此刻在药剂的作用下，我能够看到这个空洞。我当时很庆幸自己的肚子空空如也。
 
基拉斯克丝在尸体附近蹲下，立刻开始触摸它，挪动手臂，仔细检查。我站在一旁，不知道自己该不该反对，但无论如何也不敢去抱怨。这里的植物还不是很茂密，我们暴露在外，不过——正如基拉斯克丝指出的那样——任何生物都是如此。

“是野兽干的吗？”我问道。毕竟这里确实有掠食动物出没。不过除非走投无路，任何野兽都不会主动攻击基拉斯克丝。

她示意我蹲在她身边。“看，”她说道。接着，等我在她侧面稳住后：“你没看到什么？” 

“光能，”我说道，突然的悲痛再次袭上心头。

她拍了我一下。“向下看。”
 
我照做了。我看到了一簇光——那是一群小幼虫，它们聚集于我在尸体周围留下的脚印里。我轻轻地拂去腿上的一只，然后意识到…

“它们在避开尸体，”我说道。

基拉斯克丝高兴地咕哝着。“摸摸这里。告诉我你感受到了什么。”

我摸了摸守卫的甲壳，感觉爪子下有湿湿的东西。我花了一段时间才意识到野兽从中间撕裂了其甲壳，并担心自己再也吃不下饭了。然后，突然间，我的手好像浸入了冰冷的池塘。 

我感受到愤怒。一种强烈、陌生的怒火，这与我自己的反感和恐惧无关。在愤怒之下，还有一种情绪，类似于…悔恨[3]。野兽会感到悔恨吗？

“你感受到了吗？我们看不到这种邪恶[4]，但它确实存在，”基拉斯克丝说道。“走吧。审判氏族是错的。我带你回船上去——要是我们动作快，它就不会有时间追上我们。”
 
但那头怪物并没有在森林里追踪我们。

它凭空倾泻而出，如同一团翻腾汹涌的阴影。 



[1: 这仅供参考，但我相信布罗斯克是泻剂。利索克可翻译为碎岩者，或是食石者。] 
[2: 严格来讲，这里所用古语的意思是“某个氏族之外的埃里克斯尼族”。]
[3: 这个词不太准确，但我也找不到更好的表达。它指的是对尚未发生的事情感到内疚？或者是自愿承担本不属于你的责任。瓦里克斯一直不太愿意解答。] 
[4: 我相信我们如今称之为“暗影”。]

1681909870.name: 4. War
1681909870.text:
I do not know if I would have seen anything at all had I not been given the tonic. What I did see, I did not understand at first: a dark shape clawing its way into being, caught on the edges of reality and tearing itself apart in order to make its existence possible.
It bellowed, and I felt the force of that sound rattle through my shell.

Something collided against my shoulder—Kiiraskes, pushing me away. 
"Irrha, the tonics!"

I stumbled toward the supplies. Behind me, I heard the whine and snap of Arc energy, and I turned to see Kiiraskes draw a short rod from the lining of her cloak. In her hands, it drew apart into a thin spear, crackling with power, and this she threw into the dark heart of the thing that hung suspended in the rift.

I heard the squelch of impact. The air filled with the strange, unpleasant stink of bad Ether and wet dirt. The creature rippled, clawed, and fell unhindered to the earth. The shape of it changed. I saw it rise upon six heavy limbs. Its misshapen head turned toward me.

In the next instant, a flask burst against it, and hissing steam roiled along its flank. I saw the beast's pointed maw part as it screamed.

"The Stone-Eater!" Kiiraskes cried. She pulled her sword from her belt and scraped something over the blade's surface. I saw Light bloom where she had touched it, and then she was moving toward the monster.

I opened the pack, but in my terror, I could not read the symbols on the bottles, nor think of what to do. I stared down at the rows of tonics I had so confidently described for Kiiraskes only an hour before, and I thought of how much of a hatchling I really was. I had studied the work of the Slayers as if it were only a story, and had expected only a story. All I had wanted was an escape.

Then I heard Kiiraskes yell. I thought of my time training, hoping I might become a healer in one of the great Houses. I looked in the pack, and there it was: the vial of Stone-Eater. I pulled it free and threw it as hard as I could toward the beast's head.

My will outpaced my aim. The flask struck the monster in the leg, and at once began to eat through its flesh. I saw it stumble briefly, only to shift its weight and turn. It made no sound of pain when struck, but now it sent another thundering bellow toward me, and with that rippling wave came a cold like nothing I've ever felt.

The air stung my throat and eyes. I threw my arms over my face and leapt away blindly toward the trees. When I looked back, I saw that the Light had been snuffed from a broad line of the undergrowth, leaving a sprawling emptiness into which I too might fall. I saw the monster rear up in preparation to charge.

A flash. Kiiraskes's blade, slicing deep into the monster's throat.

I saw that great maw descend upon her. I heard her scream.

The beast had her snared in its jaws, but she was levering them apart with two of her hands. The third held fast to her blade in the thing's neck, and in the fourth, I caught the shine of glass.

She thrust the flask deep into the creature's throat. For a long moment, nothing happened. Then the creature shuddered, and I saw the shell of it—the bones—lit from within by pale fire [1]. Its jaws crashed shut around Kiiraskes, once, then parted to scream. I saw the Baron haul at the blade—heard more terrible, wet screaming as the fire caught and spread.
 
The beast writhed and fell. Kiiraskes fell with it.



[1: I think this must be Tenar: 'wrath', and presumably the wrath of Light.]
1681909870.text_zh:
如果我没有服用药剂，不知道我当时是否能看到任何东西。而我所看到的，起初我并不理解：一个黑暗的形体挣扎着成形，被困在现实的边缘，自我撕裂方得以存在。
它吼叫着，我感到那声音的力量震得我的躯壳咯咯作响。

有什么东西撞到我的肩膀——是基拉斯克丝，把我推开了。 
“伊尔哈，药剂！”

我踉跄地朝补给跑去。我听到了身后电弧能量发出的嗡鸣和噼啪声响，于是我转过身去，看到基拉斯克丝从披风内衬中抽出一根短棒。在她的手中，短棒分离成一根细长的矛，噼啪作响，充满了能量，她将这根长矛投进了悬浮在裂缝中那东西的黑暗心脏。

我听到了撞击的嘎吱声。空气中弥漫着变质乙太和潮湿泥土的恶臭。那怪物翻滚着、抓挠着，径直倒在地上。它的形体发生了变化。我看到它用六条沉重的肢体站起来，将它那畸形的头转向了我。

下一瞬间，一个烧瓶在它身上爆裂开来，嘶嘶作响的蒸汽沿着它身体一侧搅动着。我看到那野兽尖叫着张开了巨嘴。

“食石者！”基拉斯克丝喊道。她从腰间拔出刀剑，在刃面上刮附了什么东西。我看到她触剑之处绽放出光能，然后她就朝着怪物过去了。

我打开背包，但由于惊恐，辨认不清瓶子上的符号，也无法思考该做什么。我低头凝视着数排一小时前我还自信满满地向基拉斯克丝描述过的药剂，真切地认识到自己是多稚嫩的一只幼雏。我一直把杀手的工作当作故事来研学，而期望着的也只不过是个故事。我所想要的只是逃离。

接着，我听到了基拉斯克丝的喊声。我想起了自己期盼着成为某个大氏族的治疗师而接受训练的日子。我在背包里搜寻着，总算找到了它：食石者的药瓶。我迅速把它拿出来，用尽全力扔向了那野兽的头部。

我的准头没能赶上我的决心。烧瓶击中了怪物的腿，并立刻开始侵蚀它的血肉。我看到它短暂地踉跄了一下，但随即挪动重心转过身来。被击中时，它没有发出任何痛苦的声音，但现在它再次朝我发出了雷鸣般的吼叫，伴随着那滚滚的声波，我感到了前所未有的寒冷。

空气刺痛了我的喉咙和眼睛。我手捂住脸，盲目地跳向树林。我回头望去，只见光能已经从一大片灌木丛中消失，只剩一片我也可能落入其中的无垠虚空。我看到怪物正蓄势待发，准备冲锋。

一道闪光划过。基拉斯克丝的利刃深深地刺进了怪物的喉咙。

我看到那张巨嘴向她扑去。我听到了她的尖叫声。

野兽用它的巨嘴咬住了她，但她用两只手将其撬开。第三只手紧紧抓住怪物脖子上的刀刃，而在第四只手中，我看到了玻璃的光泽。

她将烧瓶深深地插入怪物的喉咙里。很长一段时间，什么都没发生。然后那生物颤抖了起来，我看到它的外壳——骨头——被苍白的火焰从内部照亮[1]。它猛地合上巨嘴咬住基拉斯克丝，然后再张开尖叫。我看到了公爵用力去拉刀刃，随着火焰的燃烧和蔓延，听到了更可怕、夹杂着粘液的尖叫。
 
野兽扭动着身体扑地。基拉斯克丝也随之倒下。



[1: 我想这肯定是特纳尔，即怒火，应该是光能之怒吧。]

1681909871.name: 5. Monsters
1681909871.text:
I thought her dead.
 
Kiiraskes sat up, then fell over again. She spoke a very foul oath.
 
"You're hurt!" I cried stupidly.

"I'm not," she hissed. "Help me face the Great Machine."

She was too heavy to drag anywhere she did not want to go. I helped her sit up, and saw then the extent of the damage. She had lost a primary arm at the elbow, but that was the least of it. The wound in her middle yawned wide as she repositioned herself. In my certainty that I had failed her, I did not see her reach into the pack beside us.

She slathered a foul-smelling concoction onto her stomach, then activated her Arc-knife and held it close. I think I must have shouted. I heard the popping hiss of the salve igniting, and the air filled with the stink of roasting flesh.

Kiiraskes groaned and shuddered as the dying beast had.

"Now help me up," she said.

Together, we shuffled toward the burning ruin of Haaksis's creature.

It looked ordinary after the fire had worked through it. It seemed like it might have been a river-catcher, one of several common predators that fed along the waterways. But we had both seen it cloaked in boiling shadow, wielding a power that could douse the Light of the Great Machine. And no river-catcher ever grew so large.

Amid the pile of bones, I caught the shine of something metallic. A gleaming sphere. I reached for it, and Kiiraskes pulled me back.

"Don't touch it." With the stump of her arm, she gestured toward the pack I had abandoned nearby. "Bring that here."

I watched as she tipped a canister of powder over the sphere. The effects of the tonic were fading now, but I could still see the motes as they drew together. A cluster of Light, like a frenzied swarm of fish, gathering closer and closer together over the sphere until I had to cover my eyes.

When I looked again, the sphere was gone.

"What was it?" I could not help but regret that I had not had a chance to study it.
 
"Haaksis's old evil," Kiiraskes said. "Let's see what he can tell us about it."





Haaksis prepared hot, sweet drinks for us both. Later, I would wonder at his kindness. At the time, I was too tired and sore, and the drink soothed the ache in my throat.

Kiiraskes's wound still looked terrible: a livid stretch of cauterized flesh beneath a cracked carapace. But Kiiraskes refused both food and aid; she stood at the ready, listening.

"I wanted to pilot a Ketch," Haaksis told us. "When I was young. I stole a scout-ship to prove myself. I got lost."

"I didn't have much fuel. I set down on what I thought was one of the moons. But there was no air. No life. No Great Machine. I took my mask. My Ether-pack. I stepped outside."

I watched him clench his fists again, one after the other. Helplessly.

"I found a tower. A fortress-city of tombs like nothing you've ever seen. Something monumental. Something older than us."
 
I shivered.

"And at its heart, a ship. A ship like a blade." Haaksis's mandibles scraped together. "I found a sphere [1]. And when I held it…"

I heard Kiiraskes inhale, very softly.
 
"…showed me how to get home."

Kiiraskes said nothing. I sipped my drink, saying nothing. Understanding nothing.
