"It showed me everything. The storm at the end of things, Kiiraskes. The uselessness of it all. The ruin of it." Haaksis hung his head. "I still hear its Voice. Even after I cast the sphere away. Even now, after you…"

After we destroyed the sphere, I realized. I set my cup down.
There had been nothing in his demeanor to make me frightened of Haaksis until now. It was as if something had torn free inside him. He must have been fighting it, the entire time. Fighting, and losing.

"I sent for Slayers. I thought there would be more of you left. I thought… there might be a way."

"We can still fight it, Haaksis," Kiiraskes said. "You and I. Come and tell Judgment—"
 
Haaksis gestured sharply in dismissal. "You don't know what's coming for us. For our children." He groaned. Ether gusted from his mouth like fog. "We have to stop this suffering." His eyes fixed upon mine. "We have to end it all."

He came at me over the desk.

Kiiraskes met him first.

I stumbled back as they fought. Fought like animals trapped inside a cage. A display shattered under the collision of their bodies. Haaksis's bellowing rattled the walls.
I could not throw any flasks without risk of hitting Kiiraskes. I made myself small and pressed my hands over my eyes.

I do not know if they fought for long hours or mere moments. For a time, there was only terror and noise, and once it passed, I felt gentle hands tugging mine away from my face.

"Forgive me," I said.

Kiiraskes grunted. "I haven't yet taught you to fight. That's what I'm here for." She looked down at the still form that had been Haaksis. "Bring the Shank. I have to tell the House of Judgment I killed a Lord of Rain."



[1: Eris spoke of finding such an artifact on the surface of the Lunar Pyramid.]
1681909871.text_zh:
我以为她死了。
 
基拉斯克丝坐起来，然后再次倒下。她恶毒地咒骂了一句。
 
“你受伤了！”我傻傻地喊到。

“我没有，”她发出了嘶鸣。“帮我面向大机器。”

她太重了，没法把她拖往她不想去的地方。我扶她坐起来，这才看到她受伤的程度。她的一只主臂在肘部断掉，但那还只是最轻的伤。她重新坐好时，中部的伤口深深地裂开。我因确信自己令她失望而沮丧，没注意到她把手伸进了我们身边的背包里。

她往自己的肚子上涂了一层难闻的药剂，然后激活电弧刀刃并紧紧握住。我想我肯定是喊出了声。我听到药膏点燃时噼里啪啦的嘶嘶声响，空气中弥漫着烤肉的恶臭。

基拉斯克丝像那头野兽垂死时一样呻吟和颤抖着。

“现在扶我起来，”她说。

我们一起摇摇晃晃地走向哈克西斯的那只生物的燃烧残骸。

大火过后，它看起来挺普通，似乎曾是只河流捕食者。那是一种在水道边觅食的常见掠食者，但我们都见过它被沸腾的阴影所笼罩，操控着足以熄灭大机器光能的力量。而且，没有哪只河流捕食者能长得如此巨大。

在骨堆中，我看到了一抹金属的光泽。一个闪闪发光的球体。我伸出手去，但基拉斯克丝把我拉了回来。

“别碰它。”她用残臂指了指我丢弃在附近的背包。“把那个拿过来。”

我看着她把一罐粉末倒在那球体上。虽然药剂的效力在消退，但我仍能看到萤光聚集在一起。一簇光能，像狂热的鱼群，在球体上越聚越近，直到我不得不掩住眼睛。

我再看时，那球体已经不见了。

“那是什么？”我不禁为自己没有机会研究它而感到遗憾。
 
“哈克西斯的古老邪恶，”基拉斯克丝说道。“看看他能告诉我们些什么。”





哈克西斯为我们俩准备了热乎乎的甜饮料。事后我会对他的好意感到纳闷。但当时我太累，浑身酸痛，而饮料舒缓了我喉咙的疼痛。

基拉斯克丝的伤口看起来还是很可怕：开裂的甲壳下是一大片颜色青紫、经过烧灼处理的血肉。但基拉斯克丝拒绝了食物和援助，她保持警觉地站在那里，仔细聆听着。

“我曾立志要驾驶双桅船，”哈克西斯告诉我们。“在我年轻的时候。为了证明自己，我偷了一艘斥候飞船。结果迷路了。”

“我当时的燃料不多。我降落在一个我以为是卫星的地方。但那里没有空气。没有生命。没有大机器。我拿上我的面具和乙太背包，走了出去。”

我看着他再次一个接一个地握紧拳头。无法遏制。

“我发现了一座塔。一座由墓穴构成的要塞城市，那景象你们一定没见过。它宏伟壮丽，比我们还要古老。”
 
我打了个寒颤。

“在它的中心，有一艘飞船。一艘像刀刃一样的飞船。”哈克西斯的下颚摩擦着发出声响。“我发现了一个球体[1]。我拿起它的时候…”

我听到基拉斯克丝轻轻地吸了一口气。
 
“…告诉了我怎么回家。”

基拉斯克丝没有说话。我抿了一口饮料，也没说话。一头雾水。

“它告诉了我一切。万物尽头的风暴，基拉斯克丝。一切都是白费力气。全都毁了。”哈克西斯垂下了头。“我还能听到它的声音。即使在我扔掉球体之后。即使是现在，在你们…”

在我们毁掉球体之后，我意识到。我放下了杯子。
此前，哈克西斯的举止并没有什么让我对他感到恐惧的地方。就好像他体内有什么东西被撕裂开了。他肯定一直在与之斗争。不停抵抗，节节败退。

“我请他们派来杀手。我以为会有更多的杀手存活。我以为…可能会有办法。”

“我们还是可以对抗它，哈克西斯，”基拉斯克丝说道。“你和我，去告诉审判——”
 
哈克西斯猛地做出了一个拒绝的手势。“你不知道我们将要面临什么。我们的孩子将要面临什么。”他呻吟着。乙太像雾一样从他口中喷涌而出。“我们必须停止这种痛苦。”他的目光紧盯着我的眼睛。“我们必须结束这一切。”

他越过桌子朝我扑来。

基拉斯克丝先迎了上去。

他们打斗时，我踉跄着后退。他们像困在笼中的野兽般搏斗。在他们身体的撞击下，有个陈列柜碎裂了。哈克西斯的吼声震得墙壁隆隆作响。
我不能冒险扔出任何烧瓶，那可能会误伤基拉斯克丝。我尽量蜷缩身体，用手捂住眼。

我不知道他们是打了几小时，还是只打了片刻。一时间，只剩下恐怖和嘈杂，而当那一切都过去后，我感觉到有一双温柔的手把我的手从脸上拿开。

“原谅我，”我说道。

基拉斯克丝咕哝道。“我还没教过你战斗。被派到这里来战斗的人是我。”她低头看了看那具曾是哈克西斯，但已不再动弹的躯体。“带上侦察机。我得告诉审判氏族，我杀死了一位骤雨领主。”



[1: 埃里斯提到过在月球金字塔表面发现了这样的一件神器。]

1681909868.name: 6. Return
1681909868.text:
The artificial current did more to steer the watercraft than we did. Kiiraskes held loosely to the oar with one hand.

I held the drone carefully, mindful of the occasional splash of water from the restless river. It chimed cheerfully in my hands, perhaps sensing I wanted soothing.

"I had a son. Ah…" Kiiraskes scraped a claw along one mandible, to strike the words from her mouth. "I have a son. Not much older than you."

I looked up at her, surprised. Her gaze was on the water.
"He found a place with the Gentle Weavers. He wanted very much to… belong. I hope he will weave great things. Or else… do whatever it is he wishes to do." She looked at me, and it was my turn to feign interest in the river.

I heard her sigh. "We Slayers were never lords. We had no Kells. We came together to defend our people. We were Barons of Riis and the Great Machine, not… this House or that."
 
She touched the scar on her stomach, and I stilled in concern.

"The wars destroyed us. Nobody believes that there is anything worse to fight out there than ourselves."

I thought, without wanting to, of Haaksis. The mind-sickness that had gripped him… or else, the voice of something powerful and ancient.

"Chelchis sees it. Feels it deep in her mills. Something is coming. All those strange reports that she takes back to Kings and Judgment. But she thinks it will come from within, from… disorder."

"But… I saw the monster," I said. "I'll tell everyone what happened."
 
Kiiraskes looked up at me. Even with her helmet removed, I could not tell what she was thinking. 

"You did well, Irrha," she said.
The rest of the journey, we passed in silence. 





I knew Baron Kiiraskes was still in pain because she did not shrug off Chelchis's assistance in stepping out of the watercraft.

Kiiraskes reached out to take the Shank from my hands. "I will speak to House Judgment and report on our findings." She hesitated. "Chelchiskel can keep an eye out for you until I return."

We both watched Baron Kiiraskes pull her cloak tightly around herself and limp away toward the palace doors. Chelchis stared at me, and I worried she would ask me for an explanation. But instead, Chelchis grunted, as if something had been decided, and leaned against a nearby pillar.

I felt the weight of the past couple of days settle onto me. I was tired, but my body was not convinced it was safe to rest. I felt alert and exhausted all at once. I hugged my arms to myself and waited.

Some time into the silence, Chelchis began to sing quietly. It was not a tune I recognized, but beautiful in its lilting sweetness.

I thought of voices raised together in song in shared rooms. I thought of long nights playing find-sneak with friends, long before any of us had to worry about our purpose. In my chest, I felt a hollow ache like grief.
 
"What is it?" Chelchis asked.
 
I startled and looked up at her. What could I possibly say to a Kell that wouldn't just be wasting her time? "Oh, no, it's just… your song is sad."

Had she taken offense, she could have pulled my arms from their sockets. Instead, Chelchis touched my shoulder gently, and drew me close.

"Not sad," Chelchis said. "A song for star-sailors headed out into the dark between worlds."

"And wherever we walk, there is Light, little brother."



[Goodbye, Irrha.  –Eido, Scribe of House Light]
1681909868.text_zh:
人造水流比我们更能控制船只的行进方向。基拉斯克丝一只手松松地握着桨。

我小心翼翼地拿着无人机，留意着躁动的河水偶尔溅起的水花。它在我手中欢快地鸣叫着，也许是感受到了我需要安慰。

“我有过一个儿子。啊…”基拉斯克丝用一只爪子刮过她的下颚，仿佛是要把那些话从嘴里抹去。“我有一个儿子。比你大不了多少。”

我抬起头，惊讶地看着她。她的目光落在水面上。
“他在温柔织工氏族中找到了自己的位置。他非常想…融入其中。我希望他能编织出伟大的事物。或者是…做他想做的任何事情。”她看向我，这次轮到我假装对河流感兴趣了。

我听到她叹了口气。“我们杀手从来都不是领主。我们没有凯尔。我们聚集在一起是为了保卫我们的族人。我们是里斯和大机器的公爵，而不是…这个或那个氏族的公爵。”
 
她摸了摸肚子上的伤疤，我担忧地僵住了。

“战争摧毁了我们。没有谁相信这世上还有比我们自己更可怕的东西，需要我们去对抗。”

我不由自主地想起了哈克西斯。他被心灵的疾病所折磨…又或者，是某种强大而古老之物的声音在作祟。

“切尔奇斯看到了。在她的内心深处感受到了。有什么事情要发生。所有那些她带回给王族和审判氏族的奇怪报告。但她认为那会来自于内部，来自于…混乱。”

“但是…我看到了怪物，”我说。“我会告诉大家发生了什么。”
 
基拉斯克丝抬起头望着我。即使她摘下了头盔，我也看不出她在想什么。 

“你做得很好，伊尔哈。”她说。
接下来的旅程中，我们保持着沉默。 





我知道基拉斯克丝公爵还在忍受痛苦，因为她走下船时没有甩开切尔奇斯的搀扶。

基拉斯克丝从我的手中接过了侦察机。“我会跟审判氏族交谈，报告我们的发现。”她犹豫了一下。“在我回来之前，切尔奇斯凯尔可以照看你。”

我们俩看着基拉斯克丝公爵拉紧披风，一瘸一拐地向宫殿大门走去。切尔奇斯盯着我，我担心她会要求我作出解释。但切尔奇斯却哼了一声，好像已经决定了什么似的，然后靠在了旁边的一根柱子上。

我感到过去几天的重担压得我喘不过气来。我累了，但我的身体却不相信现在休息是安全的。我觉得既警觉又疲惫。我抱着双臂等待着。

沉默了一段时间后，切尔奇斯开始低声唱歌。那是我不熟悉的曲调，但它的旋律悠扬甜美，非常动听。

我想起了在共用的房间里一起高歌的声音，想起了与朋友们一起玩捉小偷游戏度过的长夜，那时我们中还没有谁需要为自己的使命而担忧。我感到胸口有一种类似悲伤的空虚之痛。
 
“怎么了？”切尔奇斯问道。
 
我吓了一跳，抬头看着她。我能对一位凯尔说什么，而不算是浪费她的时间呢？“哦，没什么，只是…你的歌很悲伤。”

要是她感觉受到冒犯，可能就会把我的胳膊从关节上拽下来。但切尔奇斯却轻轻碰触我的肩，把我拉近。

“不是悲伤，”切尔奇斯说道。“这是一首为那些驶向世界间无尽黑暗的星际水手而唱的歌。”

“而无论我们走到哪里，都有光能相伴，小兄弟。”



[再见，伊尔哈。——光能氏族文士艾多]

3186756437.name: Restless Dreams
3186756437.subtitle: "I will protect her… even from myself." —Misraaks, Kell of House Light
3186756437.subtitle_zh: “我会保护她…即使伤害是来自于我。”——光能氏族凯尔米斯拉阿克斯
3186756437.text:
The rigidity in his limbs was unnatural.

His breathing was short, quickened, as his eyes searched the dark room. Any attempt to crane his neck was impossible—the paralysis had sunk deep into his bones.

He sensed a presence. It was a subtle thing, barely noticeable… but Misraaks knew. He tried to speak, but his mandibles did not budge.

The darkness in the room breathed.

Misraaks strained his eyes to peer towards the edge of the blankets he'd been using as temporary bedding during the development of the Variisis Core. Rays of moonlight from a nearby window allowed him to spot the gnarled fingers of a shadowed hand curl and rip into the fabric. A chill accompanied its agonizingly slow ascension up his body, tendrils dancing wildly off its twitching figure. A chorus of whispers rose into a symphony.

The entity lifted its head to reveal a ring of eyes.

…Pawn…

Its voice echoed within him.

…Kell… of Demise… of Fear…

Intrusive flashes took over his mind. Fire. Burning buildings. Screaming Eliksni. At first, he thought this might have been Riis, a memory that was not his, but, instead, he recognized the familiar streets of the Last City. His home.

He looked down at his hands, coated in shadows and blood.

…We will make it their reality…

Below him was a body, torn and bloody, with Eido's face.

Panic flooded his being. Fear. A mouth grew on the creature's form, icy breath and rows of sharp teeth dripping with black sludge…

"NO!"

Misraaks shot up, suddenly free, and blinked to reveal an empty room.

The door swung open.

"Father?!"

Eido was unharmed.

Misraaks remained quiet, breathing unevenly, and gazed down at the blankets in time to see wisps of Darkness emanating from a few tears in the fabric.
3186756437.text_zh:
他的四肢僵硬得很不自然。

他的呼吸短暂急促，眼睛在黑暗的房间里搜寻着。他无法伸直脖子——麻痹已经深入骨髓。

他感觉到某种存在。这很微妙，几乎察觉不到…但米斯拉阿克斯心知肚明。他想说话，但下颚动弹不得。

房间里的黑暗在呼吸。

米斯拉阿克斯使劲睁大眼睛，朝他在开发瓦里希斯核心时用作临时被褥的毯子边缘望去。从附近一扇窗户透进来的月光让他看到了一只阴影笼罩的手，粗糙的手指弯曲着撕扯着布料。这只手极其缓慢而令人痛苦地爬上他的身体，一股寒意随之袭来，触手在它抽搐的身影周围疯狂舞动。一阵阵低语逐渐汇聚成了交响乐。

那个实体抬起头，露出一圈眼睛。

…棋子…

它的声音在他心中回响。

…灭亡的…恐惧的…凯尔…

他的脑海中突如其来地闪过一些画面。大火。燃烧的建筑。尖叫的埃里克斯尼族。起初，他以为这可能是里斯，一段不属于他的记忆，但后来他认出了圣城熟悉的街道。这是他的家园。

他低头看向自己的手，上面沾满了阴影和鲜血。

…我们会让它成为他们的现实…

他的下方有一具被撕得血肉模糊的尸体，长着艾多的面孔。

惊慌充斥着他的内心。恐惧紧随其后。那怪物身上长出了一张嘴，冰冷的气息还有一排排锋利的牙齿，上面滴着黑色的污泥…

“不！”

米斯拉阿克斯猛地起身，忽然能动了。他眨了下眼，面前空荡的房间逐渐清晰起来。

门被推开了。

“父亲？！”

艾多毫发无损。

米斯拉阿克斯保持沉默，呼吸不均，低头凝视着毯子，正好看见从布料的几处破洞散发出的缕缕暗影。

20991506.name: Spectroscopic Shell
20991506.subtitle: For Ghosts who dabble in the biochemical composition of the universe.
20991506.subtitle_zh: 供研究宇宙生物化学成分的机灵使用。
20991506.text:
Glint flitted through the Variisis Core of the Last City until he spotted the hoses and tubing of Eido's brewing station snaking through the rafters. The tank churned and hummed, surrounded by botanical pallets carefully labeled but strewn haplessly about. A rabbit rose on its haunches to inspect a clay pot full of berries and herbs.

Glint giggled, only to find himself suddenly plucked from the air by Eido as a porous black pillar bubbled and climbed from her workstation, the acrid smell of burnt sugar erupting with it. She held the Ghost tightly, away from the ripples of steam, and thrust a beaker into a bucket of water and sodium bicarbonate.

Eido gently released Glint and wiped her brow.

"What—what was that?!" he exclaimed.

"Concentrated sulfuric acid. Unfortunately, not the degradation effect I was looking for."

Glint gave her a meaningful look. "I thought reading the Deck of Whispers was dangerous enough."

Eido shook her head. "An Apothecary is only as dangerous as her ignorance, but the Apothecaries of Riis were masters of botany, herbalism, medicine. Their work was volatile in nature. Secretive. Terminology is sometimes convoluted. Even coded. Or both! As a Scribe, I can't even scratch the surface of some of these old recipes."

Glint bobbed knowingly. "Not to mention that High Speak is incredibly complex. So many words hold so many meanings."

"And their combinations, even more so. Plus, one must understand the original context in these recipes." Eido presented a datapad. "Take this example, likely from some time after the Edge Wars."

Glint read until his iris grew wide with wonder. "Is this saying… dragon's blood? You mean… Ahamkara?"

"Not at all. From what I can discern in other texts, it is a shorthand reference to a plant with sap that ran thick, like blood."

Glint considered for a moment. "What if we can't find dragon's blood here?"

"Precisely," Eido said and pointed to the clay pot beside her. "If a tonic recipe calls for a berry, are Earth's strawberries a close enough cousin? Chemical experimentation is required, which may open up a world of new possibilities."

Glint glanced toward Eido's earlier experiment. "Or the potential for disaster."

"Either way, the key to unlocking these recipes will take time. Which is in rather limited supply these days, I'm afraid," Eido sighed.

"It's a daunting task. But! There's good news," Glint offered. He swirled through the air and landed on Eido's shoulder. "You've got lots of help."
20991506.text_zh:
格林特在圣城的瓦里希斯核心里穿梭，直到看到椽木上蜿蜒的艾多酿造站管道。罐子一边搅动一边发出嗡嗡声，周围是标记精确但摆放随意的植物托盘。一只兔子直立起身子，查看着装满浆果和药草的陶罐。

格林特咯咯笑了起来，却突然被艾多从空中抓住。那时，她的工作台上正伴随着焦糖的刺鼻味道冒出一根多孔黑色柱状物。她紧紧抓住机灵，远离了散发出的气体，并迅速将一个烧杯扔进装有水和碳酸氢钠的桶中。

艾多轻轻放开格林特，擦了擦额头。

“那——那是什么？！”他惊呼道。

“浓硫酸。可惜不是我想要的降解效果。”

格林特意味深长地看了她一眼。“我还以为阅读低语卡组已经够危险的了。”

艾多摇了摇头。“药剂师的危险只来源于无知，但里斯的药剂师是植物学、草药学和医学大师，他们的工作本质就是不稳定而又神秘的。术语有时很复杂，甚至是用暗语写的！作为文士，我对这些古老配方的了解只是皮毛。”

格林特理解地点了点头。“更何况，高等语言非常复杂，许多词有着各种不同的含义。”

“组合起来就更复杂了，而且还得理解这些配方的背景。”艾多拿出一个数据板。“比如这个，很可能来自边缘战争之后的某个时期。”

读着读着，格林特的眼睛惊讶地睁大了。“这是在说…龙血？你是说…阿罕卡拉？”

“并不是。根据我从其他文本中获得的信息，这是对一种植物的简称，这种植物的汁液像血一样浓稠。”

格林特思考了片刻，“如果我们在这里找不到龙血怎么办？”

“问得好，”艾多指着她身边的陶罐说。“如果药剂配方需要一种浆果，地球上的草莓是否足够接近呢？需要进行化学实验，而那或许就会打开无穷无尽的新可能性。”

格林特瞥了一眼艾多先前的实验。“也可能是带来灾难。”

“不管怎样，解锁这些配方的关键需要时间，而那正是我们近来缺少的东西，”艾多叹了口气。

“这是个艰巨的任务。但有个好消息！”格林特鼓励地说。他在空中旋转了一圈，落到艾多的肩膀上。“你有很多帮手。”

1254994288.name: Arcology Vault Shell
1254994288.subtitle: For Ghosts who are full of old secrets.
1254994288.subtitle_zh: 供充满古老秘密的机灵使用。

3177513121.name: Dissected Carve
3177513121.subtitle: gash rend sever
3177513121.text:
You guide the Ramulose into alignment with the enemy mothership. 

They're probably responding to your Kell's call for aid—just as you are. Your instruments detect multiple life signs blessed with Ether aboard. 

You wonder if your Kell has a plan for escape, or how she would ever be taken willingly, and whether you're missing elements of a nuanced plan. Without waiting for orders, you silently key up your systems and power your Arc weapons… 

And then, suddenly, the only thing you have in common with yourself is that that's who you used to be— 

di di    di 

dreams, voice, belong to new Kell now, Eliksni no longer. 

chain to chain    to chain 

invigorated 

bleeding brain 

fulfill House Rain's prophecy, father as Kell of Kells. 

di   di di 

father doesn't want it, father wants who you used to be, not to have it, those like you can't have it, destroy the very idea of it, destroy the idea of those people— 

and    when nothing's left 

set a new course for Ramulose, straight through the bridge, a glimpse of Kell's plans. 

path he wishes to burn through asteroid field, make new home for new people, better people 

we    remain 

wish you could see it, but know path ends here, at the bridge 

the other side of the bridge. 

di   di di
3177513121.text_zh:
你指引拉姆洛斯对准敌人的母舰。 

他们可能是在回应你的凯尔发出的求援——就像你一样。你的仪器检测到飞船上有多个乙太生命信号。 

你不确定你的凯尔是否有逃脱计划，她为什么会甘愿被俘，以及这是否是你没能看透的一个精密计划。你不再等待命令，而是静静地启动系统，为电弧武器充能… 

然后，突然间，你与你自己唯一的共同点，就是曾经的你—— 

滴滴 滴 

梦想，声音，如今属于新的凯尔，不再是埃里克斯尼族。 

锁链连接 锁链 

精力充沛 

脑出血 

实现骤雨氏族的预言，身为凯尔之王的父亲。 

滴 滴滴 

那不是父亲想要的，父亲只想要你过去的样子，不是拥有它，像你这样的人不能拥有它，摧毁它的概念，摧毁那些人的理念—— 

然后 当一切都化为虚无 

为拉姆洛斯设定新航线，直接穿越桥梁，一窥凯尔的计划。 

他希望烧穿小行星带，给新的、更优秀的族人一个新家园 

我们 留存 

希望你能看到，但路的尽头就在这座桥上 

桥的另一端。 

滴 滴滴

1577330346.name: Renunciation
1577330346.subtitle: "We are a new calendar! We are an age of beginnings! Each of us is a day!" —Skolas, Kell of Kells
1577330346.subtitle_zh: “我们是新的历法！我们是新的时代！我们每个人都是新的一天！”——凯尔之王斯格拉斯
1577330346.text:
Alarms bleat calamity-shrill across the Ketch as it churns through the void. The hull lows a shuddering complaint that Ziriks feels in his carapace.

"Tell me again," he commands. Shock slows his speech.

His Dregs wring their hands, sensing his weakness.

"Skriviks speaks of betrayal!" Viik cries. "He calls for reinforcements!"

"Cybele is a death-snare," hisses Riikas. "Four Paladins close on Skolas, and every Wolfship with him." 

Every Wolfship, she means, including their own, should they remain on course to join the battle. Already they were delayed by much-needed repairs; a few volleys from the enemy fleet and their hull will split like ripe fruit.

Ziriks feels the stare of the Pilot Servitor beating down upon him. He is—they all are—sworn to his Kell, and Skolas is the last. Irxis, slain in the Eos Clash. Parixas, served up to the enemy through trickery. And these but pale shadows of great Virixas, slain by the alien Queen's Harbingers in the first decisive blow of the war.

Now Skolas stands alone, and the Wolf-Kell has stumbled into a trap. How could the Awoken have known of his intentions for Cybele?

More betrayal. More jostling for meagre power. Years upon years of Wolf-greed and desperation.

Ziriks signals for the Pilot Servitor to slow the engines. 

"Broadcast an open signal to all enemy ships," Ziriks says. "We place our fates at the mercy of tomorrow."
1577330346.text_zh:
警报声在双桅船内响彻，可怕的刺鸣声传遍虚空。船体发出不堪重负的震颤，吉瑞克斯感到自己的甲壳也在跟着抖动。

“再说一遍，”他命令道，震惊使他的语速变得缓慢。

堕落者士兵们搓着手，察觉到了他的软弱。

“斯奎维克斯说有叛徒！”维克叫道。“他在呼叫援军！”

“前往希伯乐是自寻死路，”里卡斯嘶鸣道。“四名圣骑士在逼近斯格拉斯，追随他的所有狼船都逃不掉。” 

所有狼船，她的意思是也包括他们，如果他们继续航行参战。他们已经由于必要的维修而延误；只要敌方舰队几轮齐射，他们的船体就会像熟透的果子一样崩裂开来。

吉瑞克斯能感受到领航魔眼的注视。他——他们所有人——都宣誓效忠于他的凯尔，而斯格拉斯是最后一个。伊尔克西斯在厄俄斯冲突中阵亡，帕瑞克萨斯因诡计命丧敌手。而这些损失都无法与伟大的维瑞克萨斯之死相提并论，他是在战争的第一波致命打击中被外星女王的先知杀害的。

如今斯格拉斯孤军奋战，而恶狼凯尔跌进了一个陷阱。觉醒者怎么会知道他对希伯乐的意图？

层出不穷的背叛，争夺微薄的权力。年复一年狼的贪婪和绝望。

吉瑞克斯示意领航魔眼减缓引擎速度。 

“向所有敌方飞船播送一个公开信号，”吉瑞克斯说道，“我们将命运交给明天。”

331231237.name: Finality's Auger
331231237.subtitle: Write the future into the present.
331231237.text:
ACCESS: RESTRICTED 
DECRYPTION KEY: 6DU3H2BSKP1V$CHA-319 
REP#: 177-PYR-WPN 
AGENT(S): TRU-135   

SUBJ: THIS BENIGHTED THING   

1. Chalco when word started going around you know what I thought? I thought oh good maybe Truce gets out of this swamp. Maybe Truce gets to use some of that time off he's had banked for a century. 

Know what I think now? Doesn't matter because Cowlick won't let me write it down in an official report. 

2. Okay. This thing gives me the creeps. Gave it all the standard tests. Some extra. I licked it, that's how I know it's bone. Sticks to the tongue. Stone doesn't. Cut out my tongue after just to make sure so don't worry, no contamination and Cowlick made me a new one no problem. 

There's a lot of raw data I want you to read over and maybe send up the ivory tower. It's not that I don't trust my gut it's that I don't want to.  

So, we're paracausal, right? Effect and cause all shaken up, no connection. Everything else is connected forward and back through time. Tug on the butterfly here and make a cyclone there. 

As far as I can tell this thing made itself. Spontaneous acausal generation. My best guess is that there's so much will hanging around that it crystallized. Pure I-am-and-I-gotta. Embodied stubbornness.  

3. All my informants are useless so I have to be blunt: tell me how it went? Drinks, usual place—I'll pay this time. Promise. 

MESSAGE ENDS. OPEN ATTACHMENT?
331231237.text_zh:
访问权限：受限 
解码密钥：6DU3H2BSKP1V$CHA-319 
报告案号：177-PYR-WPN 
特工：TRU-135   

主题：蒙昧之物   

1. 卡尔科，消息刚传出来时，你知道我怎么想吗？我琢磨着，或许楚斯能离开这个泥沼了，说不定还能把他积攒了好久的假期用掉。 

我现在的想法？那不重要，因为翘毛不会允许我在正式报告中把它写出来。 

2. 好吧。这东西让我心里发毛。我给它做了所有标准的测试，还额外加了些项目。我舔了它一下，所以能确定它是骨头——它粘舌头，而石头不会这样。保险起见，我之后割掉了舌头，所以别担心会有污染风险，翘毛帮我做了个新的，现在一切正常。 

我这儿有一大堆原始数据想让你看看，或许还可以传给那些象牙塔里的大人物。我不是不相信直觉，只是不愿意。  

我们都是超因果的，对吧？因果关系乱了套，没关联。其他事物则通过时间紧密相连，这儿扯一下蝴蝶的翅膀，那边就能引发一场旋风。 

依我看，这东西是自已产生的。一种自发的、无关因果的生成。我猜测，是因为周围的意志太多，以至于凝结成了晶体。纯粹的“天性使然”，具象化的固执。  

3. 我的线人全都没用，所以我只能直言不讳：结果怎么样？老地方喝酒去——这次我请，说到做到。 

消息结束。是否打开附件？

2581676735.name: New Land Beyond
2581676735.subtitle: Every hit blazes the path to our reclamation.
2581676735.subtitle_zh: 每次命中都在照亮我们的收复之路。
2581676735.text:
Sun rising over the water, she's got to move. Three Fallen down. That means find a new sniper nest before her enemy comes looking. 

They're on the prowl, the ragged ends of Devils only barely integrated into Dusk. There's an old factory with outflow pipes leading to a drying riverbed; she doesn't know what it used to make, but it's closer to a Human settlement than she likes. A potential enemy stronghold. 

The Fallen can't have it. But they're trying, and they're backed up by the canniest Vandal with a wire rifle she's ever faced. 

Rifle goes on her back, under the cloak, and she climbs down out of the tree that once served her so well. She wades through the water, tacking towards the other shore. 

A shot whines overhead, the snap and fade of an Arc bolt. A second shot tears a line through her shoulder. She throws herself forward, tucked low against the riverbed, and crawls forward. The ridge keeps her out of likely enemy sightlines. 

There's a boulder that's got a good look to it. She slithers behind it into concealing shadow. Front's all mud and blood now, but she'll deal with that later. 

Her enemy's got a cloaking device. Doesn't always use it. The power draw's a giveaway if you have the right equipment, which she doesn't. She keeps her eyes open for any rustling, any faint blurring of background. 

It's the sun's glint that gives him away in the end, winking against the scope on his wire rifle. 

From deep in shadow, she takes the shot. 

It's her planet. 

They can't have it.
2581676735.text_zh:
太阳从水面缓缓升起，她必须采取行动了。三名堕落者已经倒下，这意味着她得在敌人来搜索之前，找个新的狙击位置。 

敌人在巡逻，那些破败的恶魔氏族残余勉强融入了黄昏氏族。附近有个老旧的工厂，排水管通向一条干涸的河床；她不清楚这里以前生产什么，但它距离一个人类聚居地太近，是一个潜在的敌人据点。 

堕落者绝不能占据这里，但他们在努力尝试，而且还有她遇到过的最狡猾的暴徒在用导线步枪提供支援。 

她将步枪背在身后，藏在披风下，从一棵曾为她提供良好掩护的大树上爬下。接着，她涉水过河，朝着对岸前进。 

一声枪响突然在头顶呼啸而过，伴随着电光的爆裂声，而第二枪擦过了她的肩膀。她向前扑倒，紧贴河床，开始匍匐前进。水中耸起的脊帮她遮挡住了敌人的视线。 

她发现了一块不错的巨石可作为掩护，于是滑到它后面，藏身在阴影中。她身前都是泥泞和血迹，但她可以稍后再处理。 

她的敌人配备了隐形装置，但并不总是启用。如果有合适的设备，就可以通过监测功率消耗来搜索，但她手上没有。她留意着任何细微的悉窣声响，背景中任何微弱的模糊虚影。 

最终，是他的导线步枪瞄准镜上反射的一缕阳光暴露了他的行踪。 

她从阴影深处果断地开了枪。 

这是她的星球。 

他们绝不能占据它。

1481594633.name: Barrow-Dyad
1481594633.subtitle: Lay those unquiet thoughts to rest.
1481594633.subtitle_zh: 让那些不安的念头安息。
1481594633.text:
I, Xir-Kuur of the brood of Xivu Arath, challenged Oryx. He had communed with the Deep and fashioned the bones of the great worm into his Dreadnaught. So for the sake of the sword, I challenged him, full of the weight of purpose and the hunger for war that drives us all. 

| Take up the knife. | 

Against my sword, there was swallowing emptiness, a void that should have held stars. I thought myself blind. I thought myself dead, bone-mortar to shape the foundation of eternity. 

| Take up the knife. | 

Oryx Took me then, but I did not crave what he offered. 

| Take up the knife. It is shaped like [unparalleled victory.] | 

If it is not done by my own power, it is not earned. Thus has the sword logic ever been taught to us, and thus I have lived.  

| Take up the knife. | 

And so here I have stayed in this Dreadnaught: living and not-living, Taken and not-Taken. It might have been yesterday. It might have been an eon ago. 

| Take. Live. Kill. Live. I am here. I am power, and I am victory. I am the knife itself. Come, take what you need. Your objective. A new weapon. | 

Others come. And to the Taken, I say: take me if you can. I am Hive. I do not surrender. I do not— 

| We are the knife. |
1481594633.text_zh:
我，来自希乌阿拉斯虫群的基尔·库尔，向欧里克斯发起挑战。他与深渊沟通，并用巨蠕虫的骨骼铸就了他的无畏战舰。为了那把剑，我向他发起挑战，心中满载着沉甸甸的意图，以及驱动我们所有人的战斗渴望。 

| 拿起利刃。| 

我剑锋所指之处，是吞噬一切的虚空，本应星光璀璨，此刻却空无一物。我以为自己失明，以为自己死了，化作构筑永恒基石的尘埃。 

| 拿起利刃。| 

欧里克斯接纳了我，但我并不渴望他给予的一切。 

| 拿起利刃。它形如[无可匹敌的胜利。] | 

若非凭自身之力取得，就算不得名正言顺。邪剑守则一直如此教导我们，我也毕生遵循它。  

| 拿起利刃。| 

于是，我留在这无畏战舰之中：既是活的，又是死的；既是傀儡，又非傀儡。那或许只是昨日，又或许已过去了一个纪元。 

| 夺取、生存、杀戮、生存。我在这里。我是力量，我是胜利。我即是利刃。来吧，取走你所需。你的目标，一件全新的武器。| 

别的身影出现。面对傀儡军团，我说：尽管来夺取我。我是邪魔族，我不会投降。我不—— 

| 我们是利刃。|

3725585710.name: Lodestar
3725585710.subtitle: Potentia ex nihilo.
3725585710.text:
Shimizu, Hassan. Private papers under elliptic-curve cryptographic lock. 

Discourse on the political realities of the City is suppressed. My last seven papers have been rejected by every major journal on Earth, surely the work of private censors. 

Should I try to continue my work on CDM or enter the field of more direct paracausal studies, I'm sure to remain unpublished. Hari-5's unproven speculation that only OWL Sector is allowed to study Darkness among mortal researchers seems increasingly likely to be correct. 

Within my lifetime, I have seen cultural shifts among Lightbearers in the Last City. In my youth, the element of Void was seen as closest to the Dark. In my adulthood, Darkness—Stasis, Strand, speculative elements as yet undiscovered—has shifted from taboo to standard toolset. The final stigma among the Tower's Guardians is against rogue Lightbearers who attack Ghosts, the source of their paracausal abilities, directly. 

However, the shift in perception of Darkness among Lightbearers has not been equaled by a shift in their perception of mortal researchers. 

Arc is a power humanity has harnessed for centuries. Among the Guardians, it stands with Solar Light as an element seen historically as almost entirely positive—salutary, in fact. (See Karn, "Sociobiology of the Immortal," chapters five and six.) 

Arc is kindly, and friendly, and unimpeachable. So must I be until more change comes and the censors move on to other fears. 

There can be no complaint about my turning to work on matters that Guardians see as nothing but good for them. 

Certainly not if I give them the results of that research.
3725585710.text_zh:
清水，哈桑。私人文件已被椭圆曲线加密锁定。 

关于圣城政治现状的讨论被压制。我最近撰写的七篇论文被地球上所有主流期刊拒发，这无疑是私人审查从中作梗。 

无论我是否尝试继续从事CDM的研究，又或是涉足更直接的超因果领域，我的成果必将无法发表。哈里-5那个未经证实的猜想，即凡人研究者中只有猫头鹰区域的才可以研究暗影，似乎越来越有可能是正确的。 

我的一生中，亲眼见证了圣城中负光者文化的转变。小时候，虚空元素被视作最接近暗影的存在。而我成年之后，暗影——包括冰影、缚丝以及尚未被发现的推测元素——已从禁忌转变为日常工具。高塔守护者眼中最后的道德底线，只是反对那些直接攻击机灵——他们超因果能力之源——的低劣负光者。 

然而，负光者眼中对暗影看法的转变，并未与他们对凡人研究者态度的转变相匹配。 

人类驾驭电弧的力量已经有几个世纪了。在守护者眼中，它与烈日光能一样，一直都被视为几乎完全积极，甚至是有益的元素。（参见卡恩所著《不朽者的社会生物学》的第五章和第六章。） 

电弧友善，亲切，无可挑剔。我也必须这样，直到出现更多的变化，审查者的注意力转向其他的恐惧。 

我转向研究守护者认为对他们只有益处的事物，绝对不会有人提出异议。 

如果我将研究成果呈给他们，就更不会有谁反对了。

3229982889.name: Adamantite
3229982889.subtitle: "Inflexibility is its own virtue." —Sloane
3229982889.subtitle_zh: “顽强不屈本身就是种美德。”——斯隆
3229982889.text:
Surrounded. They hate her, but it's an empty hate, driven by an instinctual, quantum state. 

She knows, because that hate is a part of her too. 

She approaches them head on, presenting as wide of a target as she can, her pauldrons shining in a sea of undulating mouths. 

The nearest takes the bait, unable to ignore its hunger. 

That hunger is a part of her too. She empathizes as she turns slightly, and a dark, barbed appendage flicks past her cheek, causing sparks to chime off her armored shoulder. 

The Taken Thrall can't recover before her Roderic-C tears its approximation of a leg to pieces, dropping its writhing skull directly in line with her muzzle. 

Its death wail echoes in tandem with her sidearm, while its hunger for her lingers as its body shreds away at an atomic level. The shadows around her are equally starved. She knows, because she's starved too. 

Unlike them, she controls it. For every shadow around her, beckoning her to join them, her muzzle cracks. She slips, she ducks, and everywhere she sees an opening, her will hardens. She throws her bones, wrapped in unrelenting plasteel, into the fray. She puts bullets in conjured brainstems, facts dispersing feelings. 

Resolve got Sloane through Titan. Resolve will get her, and everyone still alive, through this. It's too late for Eris. It might be too late for Drifter, run off for the last time to who knows where, in the bowels of this living beast of a ship. 

She turns slowly, looking for targets. Detecting no sentient shadows, she keys a switch on her armored gauntlet.  

"Landing zone is clear. Keep the Dreadnaught patrols coming. We'll take it inch by inch if we have to."
3229982889.text_zh:
被包围了。他们恨她，但那是一种空洞的恨，由本能的量子状态所驱使。 

她很清楚，因为那份恨同样流淌在她的体内。 

她迎着他们而去，尽力展现出一个庞大的目标，肩甲在众多张合的嘴间熠熠生辉。 

最近的那个上了钩，无法遏制内心的饥渴。 

那份饥渴也是她的一部分。她带着同情微微侧身，一根黑色带刺触手从她脸旁掠过，在她的肩甲上擦出火花。 

傀儡怨魂还未来得及喘息，她的罗德里克-C就已将它的腿状物撕成碎片，令它扭曲的头颅直接对上了她的枪口。 

它的死亡哀嚎与她手枪的轰鸣交织在一起，而它对她的饥渴在身体于原子层面分解时仍旧存在。她周围的阴影同样饥肠辘辘。她知道，因为她也同样饥肠辘辘。 

与它们不同，她控制着饥渴。对于每个试图召唤她加入的阴影，她的枪口喷射着致命的子弹。她灵活地游走和低头，利用她发现的每一个缝隙，意志愈发坚定。她将骨头包裹在坚不可摧的塑钢之中，投身于战斗。她将子弹射入召唤显现的脑干，用事实驱散情感。 

正是这份决心，让斯隆熬过了土卫六。这份决心也将让她和所有仍然活着的人度过这场危机。对埃里斯来说太迟了。对深入这艘活着的巨兽船的腹地，不知所踪的浪客来说，或许也太迟了。 

她缓缓转身，搜寻着目标。没有检测到有意识的阴影，她按下了护甲臂铠上的一个按钮。  

“着陆区已扫清。尽管让无畏战舰的巡逻队过来吧。如果有必要，我们会一寸一寸地夺回这个地方。”

2291392465.name: Anamnesis
2291392465.subtitle: The Valence has dimmed, but the nature of the Echoes grows clearer.
2291392465.subtitle_zh: 原子光已经黯淡下来，但回响的本质愈发清晰。
2291392465.text:
Ikora lowers her datapad and turns to the holoprojector in her office. Outside is the Traveler in miniature, its Valence shimmering at the edges of the portal. 

The aura has softened now. The Valence grows dim. It was such a mystery in those early days after the death of the Witness; a phenomenon that birthed phenomena.  

The Witness was a being of great complexity. In life, it was a singular being of Darkness, but that Darkness encompassed a constellation of consciousness. It was largely made of the Witness's progenitor species, but other memories were nestled within that Darkness too. Each one unique, each a glimpse of the moment of encounter; from a single individual facing down the Black Fleet to an entire planet collapsing in its shadow. 

Ikora considers the nature of the Echoes, largely formed from memories. The Echo in Eramis's possession holds the memory of Riis, but Ikora wonders suddenly: Is it the memory of a planet? The gravitational well connected to Riis? She makes a note in her datapad. They did not yet know which memory Maya's Echo held. And then here was him. The Echo of the Navigator. 

Ikora sneers. She has no interest in meeting him. Echoes seem more trouble than they are worth. She grimaces, knowing that if there are more, they will find them. 

Ikora turns off the projector, picks up her datapad. Her math confirms her suspicion: the Valence has no more secrets to share. Multiple Echoes had been released from it, but now it simply shines, inert. 

The Valence's dimming is a welcome omen—fewer weapons to fall on a hungry world. The assurance of control eases her shoulders. Ikora sighs. 

A sudden beeping jolts her from contemplation. 

Sensors are acting strangely. Someone is calling.
2291392465.text_zh:
艾可拉放下了手中的数据板，转身面向办公室内的全息投影仪。外面是缩小版的旅行者，传送门的边缘处闪烁着其原子光。 

光环此刻已变得柔和。原子光日渐黯淡。见证者刚死后，这曾是一大谜团；一个孕育出了其它现象的现象。  

见证者是个极其复杂的存在。其生前是暗影中的一个单一实体，但那暗影却蕴含了星座级的意识。它主要由见证者的起源种族构成，但其他记忆也嵌入了那片暗影中。每个记忆都独一无二，是相遇瞬间的惊鸿一瞥；从单个生命体面对黑暗舰队，到整个星球在其阴影下崩溃。 

艾可拉思索着回响的本质，它们主要由记忆构成。伊拉莫斯手中的回响承载着里斯的记忆，但艾可拉突然感到好奇：它是一个星球的记忆吗？与里斯相连的引力井？她在数据板上记下了一笔。他们尚不清楚玛雅的回响承载的是什么记忆。然后还有他：领航回响。 

艾可拉不禁冷笑，她没兴趣与他见面。回响带来的麻烦似乎总是多于其价值。她皱了皱眉，深知如果还有更多的回响，它们迟早都会找上门来。 

艾可拉关闭投影仪，拿起了她的数据板。她的数学计算验证了她的猜想：原子光已没有更多的秘密可以分享。多个回响已从其中释放，而现在，它只是在惰性地发着光。 

原子光的黯淡是个令人欣慰的预兆——更少的武器落入这个饥饿的世界。这份掌控的保障令她放松了肩膀。艾可拉叹了口气。 

突然的哔哔声将她从沉思中震醒。 

传感器有异常。某人在呼叫。

3228630258.name: Afterlight
3228630258.subtitle: "Best part of having been inside the Traveler? I've got an argument to win." —Peach the Ghost
3228630258.subtitle_zh: “进入旅行者的最大收获是什么？我找到了之前争论的答案。”——机灵桃子
3228630258.text:
Daylight falls into Osiris's workshop from its high windows. Saint-14 has a habit of opening them to let in fresh air. Then Osiris shuts them. Then Saint opens them again. 

Peach spends her time well within City limits these days. She's watched this domestic routine play out plenty of times from the outside. It's a solid comedy routine even at a distance! 

Now she'd like to see it close up. She slips through the window and floats on down. 

There's a glowing green string stretched between Osiris's hands. A little row of delicate, blue icicles is slowly forming along it. Like Ikora Rey's Dawning decorations on a miniature scale. 

Peach drops further down, until she's at Osiris's shoulder. 

The ice cracks. The string snaps. Osiris sighs. 

Peach can't help herself. "Aw, you'll get it next time." 

Osiris waves a hand like he's trying to brush away a butterfly, then spins around in a sharp convulsive motion. "You're not—who are you?!" 

He's gone almost the same color as his bandana. It doesn't look great! 

"Are you having a heart attack? Do I need to get someone?" Peach doesn't know first aid. It's never come up. 

"No! Who are you? How did you get in?" 

"I'm Peach," Peach says. She adds generously, "I'm famous; you can look me up. If you're not having a heart attack, can I watch you play with Darkness?" 

"Why?" 

Because lately, Peach keeps thinking about all the things that can happen to a Ghost out in the world, all the powers she can't do anything about. But that's no fun. 

"Academic curiosity?" 

"No. Get out." Osiris points to the closed door. 

"All right, be like that," Peach says, and blinks out of the visible spectrum. 

No need to show Osiris how she got in, not when she means to come back later. 

This is the start of something beautiful. Or at least entertaining.
3228630258.text_zh:
阳光透过高高的窗户，洒入奥斯里斯的工作室。圣人14号总爱先打开窗户，迎进新鲜空气，随后奥斯里斯会将其关上。而圣人很快又会把它们重新打开。 

这些日子以来，桃子总是在圣城里转悠。她从外面多次目睹这幕日常的小插曲。即便是从远处观看，它也是一场不错的喜剧表演！ 

而现在，她想要近距离地观赏。于是她从窗户溜了进去，轻盈地飘浮下降。 

奥斯里斯的手间握着一根发光的绿线，一排精致的蓝色冰柱沿着它缓缓成形。就像是艾可拉·蕾伊的曙光节装饰，只是更小巧。 

桃子继续下降，直至她来到了奥斯里斯的肩膀旁。 

冰柱突然裂开，绿线断裂。奥斯里斯叹了口气。 

桃子实在忍不住。“噢，下次你肯定能成功。” 

奥斯里斯挥了挥手，仿佛是想驱散一只蝴蝶，随后猛然转身。“你不是——你是谁？！” 

他的脸色变得几乎跟他的头巾一般苍白。看起来不妙！ 

“你心脏病犯了？需要我叫人来吗？”桃子不懂急救。从未有那必要。 

“不！你是谁？怎么进来的？” 

“我是桃子，”桃子说。她大方地补充了一句，“我挺有名的，你可以去查查。如果你没犯心脏病，我能看你摆弄暗影吗？” 

“为什么？” 

因为最近，桃子一直在思考那些能发生在外出的机灵身上的事，那些她无法触及的力量。而那毫无乐趣可言。 

“学术上的好奇？” 

“不行。出去。”奥斯里斯指向了紧闭的大门。 

“好吧，就那样吧，”桃子说着，从可见光谱中消失无踪。 

没必要向奥斯里斯展示自己是如何进来的，尤其是当她打算日后再来的时候。 

这是一个美好故事的开端。或者至少会很有趣。

3269398063.name: Refusal of the Call
3269398063.subtitle: Don't listen.
3269398063.text:
You are Taken. Dark and nameless, shifting in the corners of the world. Unmade by your god. 

Oryx, the Lord of Shapes, cut you into your present form. Wielding Willbreaker, he broke you. 

To be Taken is to accept the knife, accept the pain, accept the sweet pang of a question that cannot be denied. 

Oryx, the Lord of Shapes, is dead. No will can replace the void of your own. 

What is left for you? Who are you without the commanding will? 

There is a new hand on the knife's hilt. It calls to you in the hollow chambers of your dying heart. 

The knife offers [new purpose]. 

Will you accept it?
3269398063.text_zh:
你是傀儡，阴暗而无名，在世界的边缘徘徊游荡，被你的神解构得支离破碎。 

形态之主欧里克斯，将你塑成了如今的模样。他手持碎志者，击碎了你。 

成为傀儡，意味着承受刀刃，承受痛苦，承受那无法回避的问题带来的甜美折磨。 

形态之主欧里克斯，已经死了。没有意志能填补你内心的空虚。 

你还剩下了什么？失去了指挥意志的你又是谁？ 

刀柄之上出现了另一只手。它在你那即将死去的空洞心房中向你发出了呼唤。 

刀刃呈上了[新的使命]。 

你是否接受？

4028298892.name: Psychopomp
4028298892.subtitle: We'll bring you home.
4028298892.text:
It's the Psions who go first, miserable weedy things. Can't take the pressure, one of 'em told Olgurn before the end. The whole ship around them weighing them down, crushing the juice out of their brains. 

The rest of them last a little longer, daughters and sons of Torobatl with their heads made of rock already. Olgurn's grandma in the village wanted to die out in the sands. Let the wind scrape away her ossified features. That's how they did it back home. 

Day he joined up with the Skyburners, their recruiter gave him his obol, and he learned something new. 

"That's your death," she said. "Put it in your pocket and never forget it. The other Skyburners will take it when it's your time."  

"Now pick up your gun. That's your duty. Victory for the empire. For the emperor." 

Olgurn had to do the rites for Big Grusk all by himself. Had to cut his mangled armor open with a torch to get to his obol. Now it's just him, crawling through tunnels with alien chitin bolted to his armor and wormspore smeared wherever he can reach. Smelling like an acolyte. 

Last one alive means he's ranking officer. Means the Dreadnaught's his responsibility. 

So Olgurn puts on his stinking armor and he crawls through tunnels and he plants explosives and he makes sure he's at the minimum safe distance before he hits the trigger. He's a Skyburner. He said the oath. He doesn't get to give up. 

And when the relief shows up, Olgurn's gonna give them his report and his obol.
4028298892.text_zh:
灵能士兵们是最先逝去的，那些可怜的孱弱东西。在终结前，有个灵能士兵向奥尔根坦言，他们无法承受那股压力。整个飞船仿佛一座巨山，压榨着他们的脑浆。 

其他人则坚持得更久一些，那些图罗巴特尔的子女，他们的头颅本就坚如磐石。奥尔根在村里的奶奶渴望在沙漠中死去，让风沙带走她那骨化的面容。那是他们在家乡的传统。 

他加入焚天者的那天，招募者给了他一枚死币，而他则学到了新的知识。 

“那即是你的死，”她说。“把它放进口袋里，永远不要遗忘。当你的那一刻来临时，其他焚天者会来取走它。”  

“现在拿起枪。履行你的职责。为了帝国，为了皇帝，去夺取胜利。” 

奥尔根不得不独自为大格鲁斯克进行仪式，不得不用割炬切开他破碎的护甲，从中取出死币。如今，他孤身一人，在隧道中爬行，外星甲壳紧紧贴合在他的护甲上，蠕虫孢子被涂抹到他能触及的每一处。他闻起来像是个仆从。 

身为最后一个存活者，他已成为最高级别军官。这意味着他要对无畏战舰负责任。 

于是，奥尔根穿上他那散发着恶臭的护甲，爬过隧道，安置炸药，并确保在按下引爆扳机前，自己处于安全距离之外。他是个焚天者，曾立下誓言。他不能放弃。 

当援军抵达时，奥尔根会呈上他的报告，以及他的死币。

727781522.name: Eyes Unveiled
727781522.subtitle: The show must be seen.
727781522.text:
Article: An Unexpected Light—SAVATHÛN AND THE GHOST Advance Preview 

By Ken Yanagi, Arts and Culture Writer at the City Herald 

The Ghost Community Players customarily present their works in the Wei Ning Memorial Theater, an unassuming black box in the heart of the Last City. SAVATHÛN AND THE GHOST: A TALE OF CROSSED LINES AND FORBIDDEN LIGHT, the newest work from Ghost playwright (now songwriter) Didi, is the latest to make its home in that same theater. An ambitious performance that falls short in some aspects but shines brightly in others, SATG begins its run this week, with tickets available on a very reasonable pay-what-you-can basis. 

SATG depends on some esoterica of the Ghost-Lightbearer relationship which the average audience member may not find familiar, but the savvy observer will find context clues to enlighten them. The show is staged in the round, with a minimalist but expressive aesthetic. Audiences should not expect expansive sets or practical effects, but the costuming suits the actors perfectly, and the acoustics of the space (and the sound technicians' hard work) ensure that not a moment of script and song is missed. The majority-Ghost cast performs in a larger-than-life fashion, a directorial choice doubtless made to compensate for a lack of recognizable Human body language. 

The result is a bombastic piece that has the feel of epic theatre or morality plays, rather than the tight, intimate drama that the script suggests it wants to be. However, the core of emotional truth in its actors and script alike left barely a dry eye in the theater, especially during Savathûn and Immaru's final star-crossed duet. 

SAVATHÛN AND THE GHOST runs for the next two months; regular casting substitutions are expected based on field missions. Four stars out of five—if you're at all interested in experimental theatre, Guardians, or Hive, then make time in your schedule, bring tissues, and turn off your heavier thoughts for the night. 

For ticket sales, please contact Pixie, Ghost of Ariadne Gris, via VanNet for inquiries.
727781522.text_zh:
文章：意外之光——《萨瓦图恩与机灵》前瞻 

圣城使者艺术与文化专栏撰稿人肯·柳著 

机灵社区剧团通常在韦宁纪念剧院上演他们的剧目。这座位于圣城心脏地带的低调黑匣子剧场，迎来了机灵剧作家（现为歌曲作家）迪迪的最新力作《萨瓦图恩与机灵：交错命运与禁忌之光》。这是一场充满野心的表演，尽管在某些方面稍显稚嫩，但是在其他方面却光芒四射。本周起，该剧以极为亲民的随意付费制面向观众开放。 

《萨瓦图恩与机灵》深植于机灵与负光者复杂关系的深厚土壤，对于普通观众而言或许稍显陌生，但那些敏锐的戏剧爱好者定能发掘出启发思考的背景线索。该剧采用圆形舞台设计，简约而不失表现力。观众或许无法期待宏大的布景或炫目的实物特效，但服饰与角色完美契合，而剧场的声学效果（以及音响团队的辛勤付出）更是确保了每一句台词、每一曲旋律都能清晰传入观众的耳中。以机灵为主的演员们通过夸张的表演方式，弥补了缺乏直观人类肢体语言的遗憾，而这显然是导演的精心安排。 

最终，这部作品更像是一部史诗剧或道德剧，而非剧本所暗示的紧凑而亲密的戏剧。然而，演员们和剧本中的真挚情感，几乎让剧场内的每一位观众都为之动容，尤其是萨瓦图恩与伊马鲁最后那命运交错的动人二重唱，更是令人泪眼婆娑。 

《萨瓦图恩与机灵》将在接下来的两个月里持续上演，根据现场演出的实际情况，预计会有常规的演员轮换。四星推荐（满分五星）——如果您对实验性戏剧、守护者或邪魔族感兴趣，不妨在您的日程中预留出时间，带上纸巾，抛开繁重的思绪，享受一个难忘的夜晚。 

如需购票，请通过VanNet联系阿里阿德涅·格瑞斯的机灵皮可茜进行咨询。

1757177186.name: Watchful Eye
1757177186.subtitle: A Guardian is first watchful, that they might know right action.
1757177186.subtitle_zh: 守护者首先要保持警惕，才能知道如何正确地行动。
1757177186.text:
"Sounds like you're asking me to spy on our own people," Drifter replied. "I'm a lot of things, but I ain't a snitch." 

He leaned back and crossed his arms, eyeing Chalco over the remnants of a now-cold dumpling lunch. 

Chalco suppressed an eye roll. As much damage as he left in his wake, the Drifter's ego was surprisingly fragile. She would have to handle the rogue Lightbearer with a delicate touch. 

"I'm asking you to look out for their well-being," the Hidden operative replied. "Sloane's as tough as they come, but there's no precedent for being half-Taken. We don't know what the long-term effects might be." 

"And as far as Eris goes…" Chalco let the thought hang. Drifter had no doubt already calculated the potential consequences of her accumulated trauma. 

"Of course I'm gonna look after 'em," Drifter groused. "But that ain't what you're asking, is it?" 

"I'm asking you to keep me in the loop," Chalco replied. "Neither one of them is great at asking for help. And we don't want to find out too late that we could have done more." 

Chalco took a sip of tea, shrewdly calculating the social dynamics from behind her mask of concern. As a member of the Hidden, she was more than capable of keeping tabs on Eris and Sloane herself. But the Drifter was a volatile element, who could unthinkingly make a bad situation worse. She needed his complicity. 

"Just… let me know what we can do to help," Chalco continued. "Will you do that?" 

Drifter grumbled. As much as he hated to admit it, the idea of a safety net was appealing. 

"Fine," he relented. "I'll let you know if anything comes up, on two conditions: first, stay out of our way." 

"And second?" Chalco prompted. 

Drifter stood up and stuffed the last two dumplings in the pocket of his tunic. 

"Lunch is on you."
1757177186.text_zh:
“听上去你是想让我监视自己人，”浪客回答道。“我做过很多勾当，但我不当告密者。” 

他往后一靠，双臂交叉，眼神掠过桌上已经凉透的饺子午餐，盯着卡尔科。 

卡尔科强忍住翻白眼的冲动。尽管浪客走到哪里都留下一片狼藉，他的自尊心却出奇脆弱。她得巧妙地对待这个无赖负光者。 

“我只是希望你能多留意下她们的安康，”这名隐秘者特工回答道。“斯隆确实坚强，但半傀儡化这种事从来没发生过。我们不知道会有什么长期的影响。” 

“至于埃里斯…”卡尔科没有继续。浪客肯定已经计算过了她积累的创伤可能带来的后果。 

“我当然会留意她们的情况，”浪客抱怨道。“但那不是你要我做的，对吧？” 

“我只是希望你能让我知道她们的近况，”卡尔科回答道。“她们两人都不擅长主动寻求帮助。我们不想等到事情无可挽回时，才发现本可以做更多。” 

卡尔科喝了一口茶，精明地从她关切的面具后面计算着社交动态的变化。作为隐秘者的一员，她完全有能力亲自监视埃里斯和斯隆。但浪客是个不稳定的因素，可能会轻率地让情况变得更糟糕。她需要拉他入伙。 

“只要…在需要帮忙时告诉我就行，”卡尔科继续道。“你可以做到吗？” 

浪客嘟囔了一声。尽管他不愿意承认，多个安全保障的想法确实吸引人。 

“好吧，”他让步了。“如果发生了什么事，我会告诉你，但是有两个条件：第一，别妨碍我们。” 

“第二呢？”卡尔科问道。 

浪客站起身，把最后两个饺子塞进了外套口袋。 

“午餐你请。”

2903168058.name: Division
2903168058.subtitle: An enneagram tips, poised to shatter.
2903168058.subtitle_zh: 九芒星微微倾斜，随时可能破碎。
2903168058.text:
our children live, the threat of Sol defeated 
we remain we remain 
 


A FOOLISH THOUGHT A THREAT DEFEATED IS OUR OPPORTUNITY WASTED 
WE REMAIN BOUND 


 
Such cruel exaggeration; can we not engage in elegant conversation as we used to? 
How can we be prisoners when we need sapience to ensure our survival? Do we not exist in response to their being? 

 

T H E F I N A L S H A P E T H W A R T E D B Y T H E L I G H T C R E A T U R E S T H E N E C E S S A R Y I D I O C Y O F T H E W I T N E S S N O N V I A B L E M E A N S O F E S C A P E 

 

A childish viewpoint—sourness amplified by arrogance
Our fate—plain as gravity—accept its pull—or fall regardless 


 
your side is complacent + worthless futility + we must look beyond + the chains of matter + reality is malleable + if only we will it so 

 

bright strength lies  
in the bonds of us, bonds of matter, bonds of love 

 

.your soluti | on falls short. 
.all tethe | rs iron.  

 

invented enemies = outscorned friends 



O U R D I V I D E E V E R W I D E R 9 F O E S I N S O L E N T D E N I A L 


 
I MOURN UNITY 
GRIEVE COALITION 
FOLLOW YOUR FOOLISHNESS 
BUT IF ALL YOU FIND IS OBLIVION 
AND THE PERIL OF OUR CHILDREN 
WE ALL PERISH
2903168058.text_zh:
我们的孩子活着，太阳系的威胁被击败了 
我们留存了下来 
 


一念之差，贻误战机 
我们依旧被束缚 


 
这么夸张也太残酷了，我们能不能不要像以前那样高谈阔论？ 
我们需要智慧才能生存，怎么能成为囚犯？难道我们的存在不是为了回应他们的存在吗？ 

 

最终形态被光之生物阻挠，见证者的必然愚行让逃脱变得无路可循。 

 

幼稚的观点——酸腐因傲慢而被放大
我们的命运——像重力一样无法逃避——要么选择接受——要么任由坠落 


 
你们固步自封 + 毫无价值的徒劳 + 我们必须放眼未来 + 物质的枷锁 + 现实是可塑的 + 只要我们愿意 

 

光明的力量在于  
我们之间的羁绊，物质的羁绊，爱的羁绊 

 

.你的解决 | 方案有缺陷. 
.所有 | 铁索.  

 

虚构敌人 = 蔑视朋友 



我们的分歧越来越大，九个敌人傲慢地否认一切 


 
我哀悼团结的逝去 
为联盟的破裂感到悲痛 
随你们的愚蠢去吧 
但若你们所寻仅是虚无 
威胁我们的孩子 
我们终将毁灭

3234363830.name: Mirror Imago
3234363830.subtitle: "I know my duty." —Chalco Yong to Ikora Rey
3234363830.subtitle_zh: “我知道我的职责。”——卡尔科·杨对艾可拉·蕾伊说
3234363830.text:
Ikora didn't react when she heard the cloak slide to the floor with a soggy thump, or when the chair by her side scraped back. 

When Chalco kicked her boots up onto the table beside her, Ikora only moved her datapad a precise six inches to the left. She tapped into the Vanguard duty roster. Another page to review, and more messages flooding in at every moment. 

Chalco sighed loudly. "I lost him." 

Ikora glanced to her right. "Lost him?" 

"He's stealthier than you'd think, even when you think you know how stealthy he is. Why we thought he'd be a useful asset, I guess." 

Ikora turned at last, placing her datapad face down on the table. She took Chalco in: tired, muddy, armored vest undone and hanging by its straps. 

"Well, that's not a terribly auspicious beginning for what I wanted to tell you," Ikora said, "but I'll forgive you." 

"If you tell me I have to go back out tonight, I'm quitting. And I'll never talk to you again." 

"You never have the commitment to make that work," Ikora said lightly. She laid her hands in her lap. "I'm stepping in to give Zavala more support in his work. I've been firmly informed that it's a full-time job in itself—and that means I need a trusted hand on the Hidden." 

Chalco scrambled to sit up, bootheels scraping loudly across the table. 

"You're serious?" she asked. "No, of course you are. Damn, Ikora, first you give up fieldwork, then you pass on the curse to me?" 

"Will you do it?" 

"Of course I'll do it. Do you know how mad I'd be if you asked anybody else?" 

Ikora held out a hand. Chalco clasped it. Wet fieldweave prickled unpleasantly against Ikora's bare palm. She tightened her grip. 

"I'll make you proud, boss," Chalco said. 

Ikora said, "You already do… boss."
3234363830.text_zh:
听到披风滑落到地板上发出的湿漉漉声响，以及身旁椅子被拖动的动静时，艾可拉没有做出任何反应。 

当卡尔科将穿着靴子的脚翘到她旁边的桌上时，艾可拉只是将手中的数据板精准地向左移了六英寸。她正浏览着先锋的值班表，又有一页需要审阅，信息还在不断涌入。 

卡尔科大声地叹了口气。“我跟丢了他。” 

艾可拉朝右边瞥了一眼。“跟丢了？” 

“他比你想象的更狡猾，甚至是在你以为自己知道他有多狡猾时。我猜这正是我们当初觉得他会很有用的原因。” 

艾可拉终于转过身，将数据板面朝下放在桌上。她打量着卡尔科：疲惫不堪，满身泥泞，解开的护甲背心仅靠肩带挂在那。 

“嗯，考虑到我要告诉你的事，那不是个好兆头，”艾可拉说，“但我会原谅你的。” 

“如果你告诉我今晚还得出去，我就辞职。我还会跟你绝交。” 

“你不会痛下决心那样做的，”艾可拉轻声说道，把手放在膝盖上。“我正忙着为萨瓦拉提供更多支持。我被郑重告知，这本身就是一份全职工作——而那意味着我需要一个值得信赖的人来负责隐秘者。” 

卡尔科匆忙坐直身子，鞋跟在桌上发出刺耳的声响。 

“你是认真的？”她问。“哦，你当然是认真的。该死，艾可拉，你先是放弃了外勤工作，现在又要把这个烫手山芋扔给我？” 

“你愿意接手吗？” 

“当然愿意。你可知道如果你找别人的话，我会有多生气吗？” 

艾可拉伸出一只手，卡尔科紧紧握住。湿漉漉的野外编织物在艾可拉裸露的手掌上留下了不适的刺痛感。她握得更紧了。 

“我会让你以我为傲的，老大，”卡尔科说。 

艾可拉回答道，“你已经做到了…老大。”

547165496.name: Abyssal Edge
547165496.subtitle: Crease the universe.
547165496.text:
The Drifter walks the gloaming halls of the Hive vessel, past the pulsing bioenergetics of multiple living systems.

Over comms, he can hear his best (remaining) friend tearing chitinous bodies to shreds with sheer will. The ship, and its inhabitants, are occupied. 

He stumbles along, past pillars that could be ribs, past something that gibbers and gestates but otherwise ignores him. 

Why did he have the gall to be surprised? 

He should have stayed with the Ghostless. Those were his people. Tomorrow is never guaranteed for them, and he rarely got attached. Leave the gods alone. 

He has broken all his rules. 

His mind moves to the infernal machine he carries as the haul of his ship, thoughts sifting through everything he owns: artifacts of the City that might help, Echoes of the Witness that the Cryptarchs have catalogued, favors of the Nine he could dare to call in. But he knows…  

There's nothing he can do. 

He has lost before, but not like this. 

He walks and he walks and finally reaches what might be the prow. He imagines this might have looked out over Saturn at some point, where the king's body had once drifted. It stares out into the abyss now, no stars, full dark. 

There's a hollowness in him, too, that might be pain or anger. He's not certain. 

He holds onto it because she doesn't even have that anymore.
547165496.text_zh:
浪客在邪魔族飞船昏暗的走廊中穿行，沿途经过了多个涌动着生物能量的活体系统。

通过通讯器，他能听到自己最好的（也是仅剩的）朋友正凭着顽强的意志在撕裂甲壳生物的身体。飞船及其居民都已被敌人占据。 

他跌跌撞撞地前进，路过可能是肋骨的支柱，以及某种喋喋不休、孕育生命却又无视他的存在。 

他为何会感到惊讶呢？ 

他本该留在没有机灵陪伴的人们的身边。那些是他的同类。他们能否活到明天从来都说不准，因此他很少会感到难以割舍。离那些神灵远点。 

他打破了自己所有的原则。 

他的思绪转向了自己携带的地狱机器，那是他飞船上的货物。他思考着自己所拥有的一切：可能有所帮助的圣城神器，解密大师们编完目的见证者回响，以及他可以冒险索还的玖的人情。但他深知…  

他什么都做不了。 

他也曾经丧失过，但不是像这样。 

他不断前行，终于来到了可能是船首的地方。他想象着这里曾经俯瞰过土星，而邪神的尸体曾在那里漂浮着。现在，它向外凝视着无尽的深渊，没有星光，一片漆黑。 

他的内心里还有一种空虚，那或许是痛苦，或是愤怒。他不确定。 

他紧紧抓住这种感觉，因为她连这个都已不再拥有。

1127263013.name: Lingering
1127263013.text:
He lingers in the entryway. It's the sort of lingering where you pretend nothing's changed—and it doesn't have to, as long as you never go in. Eris will always be just out of reach, but at least there, real in the apartment she barely used, in the City she defended but rarely saw.  

It's a fool's dream. But what is he if not a fool? So he stays a little longer, sick with wishing.
1127263013.text_zh:
他徘徊在入口处。仿佛只要不进去，就能装作一切未曾改变。埃里斯将永远遥不可及，但至少她真实地存在于那间几乎不曾有人踏足的公寓里，在她守护却鲜少露面的圣城之中。  

这是一场傻瓜的幻想。但他不正是个傻瓜吗？于是，他多停留了一会儿，满心向往。

1127263014.name: Expanse
1127263014.text:
Cold out here. Reminds him—in a bad way—of that Light-forsaken planet he nearly died on.  

He scuffles around the campsite. Pathetic, he knows it's pathetic. Even if people hadn't been through here, the storms would have blown over any footprints. Any lost trinkets would long since have been found or buried deep enough that he can't hope to find them. 

Looking out on the desolate expanse doesn't do much for him, just leaves him alone with his feelings. Not a fun place to be. He moves on.
1127263014.text_zh:
外面很冷，让他苦涩地回忆起那个被光能遗弃的星球，而他曾在那里濒临死亡。  

他在营地周围徘徊，深知此举颇为可悲。即便无人经过，风暴也会抹去所有足迹。任何遗失的小物件早已被寻获或深埋，他不可能找到它们。 

眺望这片荒凉的广袤之地，只会让他与自己的情感独处。此地不宜久留，他继续前行。

1127263015.name: Schadenfreude
1127263015.text:
Sometimes it makes a guy feel better to make fun of someone way worse off than he is. He knows it's a mistake soon as he sets eyes on the giant robot face, though.  

Maybe somewhere else. He turns and goes, ignoring the dramatic monologue already kicking off behind him.
1127263015.text_zh:
有时，嘲笑境遇比自己更糟的人能带来一丝慰藉。但当他看到那张巨大的机器人脸庞时，便知道自己错了。  

或许该换个地方。他转身离去，对身后已然开始的戏剧性独白不予理会。

1127263008.name: Unfamiliar
1127263008.text:
Pretending everything's fine was never going to work. He says he's lost a shipment of new fancy guns to get a bunch of Guardians off his back and on a scavenger hunt for nonexistent weapons. Give him some peace and quiet. He takes a minute to rustle around in his stuff, grabbing what he might need for maybe a longer trip— 

Not sure where he'd go, just not here— 

He swears he can see Eris leaning against the railing, a sly little smile barely turning up the corners of her mouth. He can't stand it.
1127263008.text_zh:
假装一切安好是行不通的。他谎称遗失了一批新的高级枪械，让几名守护者不再纠缠他，去寻找那些并不存在的武器，给他片刻宁静。他花了一分钟时间在自己的物品中翻找，拿取漫长之旅中可能需要的东西—— 

他不确定该去哪儿，只要离开这里就好—— 

他仿佛看到埃里斯倚在栏杆上，嘴角勾起一抹狡黠的微笑。这令他感到难以忍受。

1127263009.name: Restlessness
1127263009.text:
He swings by to let the man in charge know he's going to be out of town for a while. Guy'll understand. And it's a new level of responsible; Commander should appreciate that. 

The place is empty, though. He wanders around it—sets the beads to clicking against each other, prods the gold figure on the side table until it falls over, meanders past books and blinks at the cat perched on a shelf over his head.  

Nothing. He's restless. The longer he stands still, the longer the grief has to get its hooks into him. He mutters a curse into the silence and sees himself out.
1127263009.text_zh:
他顺道去向管事的老大报备，说自己要离城一段时间。那家伙会理解的。这样做也更显责任心，指挥官会对此表示赞赏的。 

但这地方是空的。他在房间里来回踱步——让珠子相互碰撞，轻推边桌上的金色雕像，直至它倾倒，又在书架间徘徊，抬头望向架子上的猫。  

什么都没有。他心神不宁。停留得越久，那份悲伤就越发清晰地缠绕着他。他冲着寂静低声咒骂，自行离去。

1127263010.name: Preparation
1127263010.text:
There's a hidden little nook in the Hangar, great spot for watching Sparrow maintenance if that's what you're into. Comfortable too. Good place to get away from the noise. He breezes in and out, rooting up a cache he left there a long time ago. Never could get out of the habit of keeping emergency stashes.   

Anywhere else he needs to stop off before he leaves for good? Maybe… maybe.   

It's a short hop from there to his ship.
1127263010.text_zh:
机库里有个隐秘的角落，如果你有兴趣的话，可以清晰地看到快雀的维修过程。那里很舒适，是个远离尘嚣的好地方。他轻车熟路地来到那里，找出很久以前藏在那里的应急储备品。藏货的习惯，他一直都难以改掉。   

在彻底离开之前，还有别的什么地方值得去看看吗？或许…有吧。   

那里离他的飞船也很近。

1127263011.name: Reconsidering
1127263011.text:
Getting out in the woods could clear his head. Maybe he shouldn't go after all.  

Familiar energy readings. Not Darkness, not Light, but the in-between stuff. Sterile neutrinos. Makes him think of a time way back when: Moondust and him. And the arrival of the Pyramid fleet…
1127263011.text_zh:
步入树林没准儿会让他清醒一点。到头来，他也许并不该选择离去。  

熟悉的能量读数——既非暗影也非光能，而是介于二者之间。惰性中微子，这让他回想起了很久以前的往事：小月月和他。以及金字塔舰队的抵达…

1127263020.name: Committing
1127263020.text:
There's a little cliff that overlooks the cove's water. He settles there a spell. It's quiet. Not a lot of combat, few enough reasons for Guardians to swing through. The quiet doesn't so much remind him of her as make him wish she were there. 

Everything's just going to keep doing that, huh. He can be honest with himself about that.  

All right. One last stop.
1127263020.text_zh:
有个俯瞰着宁静海湾的小悬崖。他在那里安顿了一会儿。很静。战斗很稀少，守护者们也没有多少理由来这里。这样的宁静没怎么勾起他对她的回忆，反而让他更加渴望她此刻在这里。 

所有的一切都会继续如此吧。他可以坦然地承认这一点。  

好了。还有最后一站。

1127263021.name: Reminiscing
1127263021.text:
He goes into her apartment this time. Not to look through her things, really, just—prove it to himself. She's not there. She won't be. He's got to remember that.  

He brushes his fingers along a side table and tries to imagine what she'd say to him.
1127263021.text_zh:
这次他走进了她的公寓。不是为了寻找她的遗物，而是——想要向自己证明些什么。她不在这里，永远也不会再回来。他必须铭记于心。  

他用他的手指轻轻掠过边桌，试图想象她会对他说些什么。

3936185103.name: Imagining
3936185103.text: Probably it'd be something deep and meaningful. He doesn't have the heart to think it up. He steps into the other room, moves around the table covered in books and relics. Almost trips on the rug.
3936185103.text_zh: 八成是某种深刻而重要的东西，但他无心琢磨。他步入另一房间，绕过堆满书籍与圣物的书桌，差点被地毯绊倒。

3936185102.name: Final Curtain
3936185102.text:
Someone else finds him there. 

He sees himself out, mouth stinging as he takes the stairs. That's it, then. There's nothing for him here. And he was a fool to think there was.  

Time to go.
3936185102.text_zh:
他在那里遇到了另一个人。 

他自行离去，走下楼梯时嘴里满是刺痛。原来如此。这里没有给他的东西。他是傻瓜，才会抱有那种期待。  

该离开了。

3320768281.name: Anemone
3320768281.text:
"We need someone on the Dreadnaught," Crow was saying. "The Hunters are spread thin, but maybe…" 

Ikora finished tucking her feelings away in the place where she put all such feelings: a little ball inside her chest, to deal with at some promised later time. "Not Hunters," she decided aloud.  

The spot where Zavala should stand around their war table was conspicuously empty.  

"Who are you thinking, then?" Crow dropped his datapad onto the table. He regarded her levelly, with none of the deference that would once have been there. "The Hidden?" 

Ikora weighed possibilities, not answering immediately. Chalco would drop everything and go—Eris was a Hunter, as they all so frequently forgot, and Chalco had considered her one of theirs still—but it would mean recalling her from her current assignment. Others of the Hidden, perhaps… but this was the Dreadnaught, not Savathûn's throne world. Where Savathûn laid out cunning traps, Oryx would have laid out simple might.  

Dead though the Taken King was, to approach his throne world confidently would require a specific sort of will. A Titan. 

They hadn't told Zavala about Eris yet. Ikora told herself she was waiting for the right moment.  

"Not the Hidden," she said at last. "And not the Drifter alone. He may have become more reputable in recent years, but regardless, I would not lay this on his shoulders. I would send Deputy Commander Sloane." 

"Ah." Crow sounded surprised, but understanding flickered across his face in a moment. "Well, she has more than enough resolve to spare." 

"And her connection to Ahsa ought to mitigate any risks caused by the lingering Taken effects." Ikora was speaking half to herself; as she laid it out, it began to seem the obvious course. "Sloane will punch a hole directly through the Dreadnaught, if she must, to get to the bottom of what's going on there." 

"We can't let the Dread run amok," Crow agreed. He rubbed a hand across his face and sighed. "Is Zavala…" 

He didn't finish the question. Ikora could and did fill it in well enough herself. Zavala was by no means inured to loss, and after the Pale Heart, he still ached. Some wounds, after all, would take a lifetime to heal. 

"I'll let him know," Ikora said. "I have no doubt he'll agree with me." 

More than willing to leave that conversation to Ikora, Crow nodded simple agreement. "Then we send Sloane."
3320768281.text_zh:
“我们需要在无畏战舰上安排人手，”乌鸦说道。“猎人目前人手不足，但也许…” 

艾可拉把她所有的情绪都收了起来，藏到专门存放这些情绪的地方：她胸口里的一颗小球里，以便将来的某个时候再去面对。“猎人不行，”她大声地作出了决定。  

在他们的战争桌旁，萨瓦拉本应站立的位置醒目地空着。  

“那你觉得谁合适？”乌鸦把数据板扔到桌上。他平静地看着她，没有丝毫过往的那种顺从。“隐秘者？” 

艾可拉权衡着各种可能性，没有立即回答。卡尔科会放下一切立刻过去——埃里斯曾是个猎人，尽管他们经常忘记这一点，而卡尔科仍把她视作他们中的一员——但这意味着把她从当前的任务中召回来。其他的隐秘者，也许…但这是无畏战舰，而非萨瓦图恩的王座世界。萨瓦图恩铺设的都是狡诈的陷阱，欧里克斯留下的则尽是纯粹的武力。  

尽管邪神已死，但要自信地踏入他的王座世界，仍需一种特定的意志。这种意志，唯有泰坦才具备。 

他们还没有告诉萨瓦拉关于埃里斯的事。艾可拉告诉自己，她在等待合适的时机。  

“隐秘者不行，”她最终说道。“浪客自己单独去也不行。尽管他近年来名声好多了，但无论如何，我不会把这个重担交给他。我会派副指挥官斯隆去。” 

“啊。”乌鸦听上去很惊讶，但很快他的脸上就露出了理解的神色。“嗯，她有足够的决心去应对。” 

“而且，她和阿莎之间的联系应该能减轻傀儡军团残余影响带来的风险。”这话艾可拉有一半是说给自己听的；她把这一切剖析清楚后，这仿佛成了再明显不过的选择。“如果有必要，哪怕是直接砸穿无畏战舰，斯隆也会查个水落石出。” 

“我们不能放任无畏战舰横冲直闯，”乌鸦同意道。他用手揉了揉脸，叹了口气。“萨瓦拉他…” 

他没有问完。艾可拉能够也确实脑补了他想说的话。萨瓦拉绝非对丧失无动于衷，苍白之心事件之后，他的心仍在作痛。毕竟，有些伤痕，需要一生的时光去愈合。 

“我会转告他的，”艾可拉说道。“我深信，他会同意我的决定。” 

能将那场对话交由艾可拉处理，乌鸦求之不得，他点头赞成。“那我们就派斯隆去。”

3320768282.name: Asphodel
3320768282.text:
Guardian funerals rarely had a body to inter, and though Eris no longer stood among the ranks of Lightbearers, she was not unique in that manner. So, they simply gathered, those few who had loved her well, packing themselves three deep into the cramped apartment even Eris had sometimes forgotten she owned. 

There was Mara Sov, starlight in her eyes, Petra Venj at her elbow—no particular friend of Eris herself, but where the Queen went, she liked to follow. "Little" Eido, taller than the Queen of the Awoken, tucking her second arms around herself and taking care not to disturb any of Eris's bones and relics while peering at everything. Crow, serious as he moved toward Mara; Zavala, quiet, occupying a corner. Here to witness, not rip himself open. Some small assortment of Guardians who had corresponded with Eris over one matter or another, study of the Taken or Hive—Awoken, Human, and Exo faces alike, some distraught and some somberly set, determined to witness though they might not weep. 

The Drifter did not show his face. Ikora had wondered how he would bear it, and she had her answer: he would not. He would simply go, careening into the dark of space with his pain alone to guide him.  

Ikora sympathized, with an unavoidable bitter chaser of resentment. This was not the first time she'd been left to manage a funeral on her own. 

Senseless. It was always senseless, death among the immortal. She had not grown any more used to it. She hoped she never would. 

"We are here to celebrate Eris Morn," Ikora said to the surrounding group, drawing herself up and making steel her spine. "Mourn by carrying her with you, if you must. But in her own words, her life was a bright and victorious one, despite everything she endured. She ought to be remembered thus." 

For Cayde's sake, she allowed herself two jokes in the eulogy; for Eris's, she did not cry.
3320768282.text_zh:
守护者葬礼上鲜少有遗体可入葬，即便埃里斯已不再是负光者中的一员，在这点上她也并不特殊。于是，深爱着她的人只是简单地聚在一起，排成几层把埃里斯自己都时常忘却的那间狭小公寓挤得满满当当。 

玛拉·索维也在场，眼中闪烁着星光，佩特拉·万吉紧挨着她——虽然不是埃里斯的挚友，但女王去哪儿，她总爱跟着。比觉醒者女王还要高大的“小”艾多，用第二对臂膀环抱住自己，留意不去碰触埃里斯留下的骨头和神器，同时好奇地打量着周围的一切。乌鸦，一脸严肃地向玛拉走去；萨瓦拉则静静地待在角落里。他来这里是为了见证，而非让自己情绪失控。还有几名守护者，他们曾与埃里斯因各种事务，针对傀儡军团或是邪魔族的研究有过往来——觉醒者、人类以及Exo，脸上的神情都差不多，有的悲恸，有的肃穆，决心要见证这一刻，尽管他们或许会克制住眼泪。 

浪客并未露面。艾可拉曾猜想他会如何承受这一切，而此刻，她已得到了答案：他拒绝承受。他会选择离去，孤身一人坠入漆黑的宇宙，唯有内心的痛苦为他指引方向。  

艾可拉心生同情，但难免夹杂着一丝难以抑制的怨怼。这已不是她首次被留下来独自操办葬礼了。 

没有道理。对这群不死之躯来说，死亡总是没有道理。她对此从未习惯。她希望她永远不会习惯。 

“我们来到这里庆祝埃里斯·摩恩的一生，”艾可拉对周围的人们说道，她挺直身姿，脊梁如钢。“如果各位觉得有必要哀悼，那就让她的精神与你们同在。但正如她说过的，尽管历经磨难，她的一生依旧光明且充满胜利。我们应当如此铭记她。” 

出于对凯德的敬意，她在悼词中纵容自己开了两个玩笑；而出于对埃里斯的尊重，她强忍住了泪水。

3320768283.name: Heliotrope
3320768283.text:
Eris's apartment was close and dark, and it smelled so strongly of incense that Drifter could barely breathe. But he sat alone, his elbows on his knees, staring at the harsh green glow of her Ahamkara bone. 

"You know what I want," he whispered. "So go on." 

There was nothing. He gripped it between his hands, his mouth curving into a harsh frown. He raised it, shook it roughly, then held it close to his face. 

"You hear me?" he hissed.  

Nothing. 

His shoulders slumped. He held the orb loosely, his eyes closed, and thought of her. 

"Be careful with that," Sloane said. He looked up, startled. The deputy commander stood in the threshold of the door. She let her eyes wander for a moment, her jaw set. 

"She lived like this?" 

Drifter didn't respond. He stood, placing the Ahamkara bone back on the table. Then he made his way to the door. Sloane blocked him with her body before he could leave. He met her eyes, expressionless. 

"Where are you going? We need to talk," she said firmly. 

"I got nothin' to say," he replied. 

"Yes, you do." 

He took a few steps back. 

"You can't walk away from this. Too much is at stake here. The City relies on you— you have to be ready for when you're needed." 

"Haven't you all taken enough from me?" he muttered. 

"You're not walking away from this." 

"Yeah, I am. You gonna stop me?" 

Sloane grabbed him by the collar. He lifted his chin in challenge; she raised a fist. 

"You wouldn't," he started, just before it came down on his face. 

Sloane let go of his collar. Drifter staggered until his back was against the wall. He flinched as he touched his nose, his fingertips coming away bloody. Then he grinned with red-lined teeth.  

"Been a while since I earned one of those," Drifter said, his voice trembling. His smile faltered quickly. He wiped his bloodied upper lip with the back of his hand as his Ghost appeared beside him, coming close and staring mutely with its red eye.  

He batted it out of the way and left the room, bleeding. 

"Don't go too far," Sloane called after him.  

Drifter didn't stop walking.
3320768283.text_zh:
埃里斯的公寓狭小幽暗，熏香的气味浓烈得令浪客几乎无法呼吸。但他独自坐着，双肘支在膝盖上，凝视着她的阿罕卡拉之骨发出的刺眼绿光。 

“你知道我想要什么，”他低声说道。“所以别磨蹭了。” 

没有回应。他双手紧握它，嘴角紧抿，形成了一道严厉的皱纹。他把它高高举起，猛烈摇晃，然后将它捧到了脸边。 

“你听到我说话了吗？”他嘶叫道。  

还是没有回应。 

他的肩膀耷拉下来，松松地握着那颗球体，双眼紧闭，心中想着她。 

“小心点儿，”斯隆说道。他猛地抬头，吓了一跳。副指挥官正站在门口，她任由目光在屋内游移了片刻，下巴紧绷着。 

“她住在这样的地方？” 

浪客没有回答。他站起身，将阿罕卡拉之骨放回桌上，随后向门口走去。斯隆用身体挡住了离开的路。他直视着她的眼睛，面无表情。 

“你要去哪里？我们需要谈谈，”她坚定地说。 

“我没什么可说的，”他回答道。 

“不，你有。” 

他往后退了几步。 

“你不能就这样一走了之。这里的利害关系重大。圣城仰仗着你——你必须随时准备响应号召。” 

“你们从我这里夺走的还不够多吗？”他低声说到。 

“你不会就这样一走了之的。” 

“不，我会。你要阻止我吗？” 

斯隆一把揪住他的衣领，他扬起下巴以示挑衅，而她则举起了拳头。 

“你不敢的，”他刚开口，那拳头便已落在了他的脸上。 

斯隆松开他的衣领。浪客踉跄着后退，直到后背抵住了墙壁。他伸手摸了摸鼻子，指尖沾满了鲜血，不禁抽搐了一下。然后他咧嘴笑了，露出被鲜血染红的牙齿。  

“有一段时间没挨过打了，”浪客说道，声音中带着一丝颤抖。他的笑容很快消失了。他用手背擦了擦血迹斑斑的上唇，而他的机灵则出现在他身边，缓缓靠近，用红色的眼睛默默凝视着他。  

他挥手把机灵推到一边，流着血离开了房间。 

“别走太远，”斯隆在他身后喊道。  

浪客没有停下脚步。

3320768284.name: Elaia
3320768284.text:
"Savathûn presumed that my throne would hold me. That I would either willingly relinquish myself to its safety or become trapped within it." 

Ikora shook her head, smiling. Eris shared in her smile. 

"She did not anticipate the Guardian's resourcefulness. And she misjudged me." 

"As did those of us who assumed your death was final." In the admission, Ikora's smile faded.  

"As I, too, assumed." Eris tilted her head, studying Ikora intently. "Do you presume that you should have come looking for me? No. You did the right thing, Ikora. That I survived, that I am triumphant, could not have been reasonably predicted." 

They stood together in Eris's throne, in the world that was made of all of her, yet still Eris did not understand all that was contained within.  

"You're comforting me," Ikora said, her voice a tense whisper. "You shouldn't. Eris, you're the one who died." 

"Yes. But you're the one who grieved." 

Ikora turned away, and Eris let her. To accept comfort was no small task, as she well knew. In silence, they studied the spines of books ancient and new, the runes writ along them in delicate gleaming soulfire. 

"I missed you," Ikora said finally. "I… felt that somehow, I had let you down: that I should have kept you safe. Even knowing you would have hated it." 

"That is your curse," Eris returned solemnly. "Responsibility." 

For that, Ikora laughed, startled into it. "You and Ophiuchus see it very differently."  

"Ghosts are bound to worry." 

Ikora's half-smile faded into soberness again. She drew stillness about herself as a cloak. "Was I right to let you go?"  

"It was all I would let you do," Eris told her. She gestured up and around, to the infinite helix-library that cradled her innermost self. "This sort of library suits me as one in the Tower never could. You did what you could, Ikora." 

Absolution offered, held in the quiet space between them. Ikora was the one to break it, closing the gap to sweep Eris up into a tight embrace. They held each other for a long moment. 

"Don't do that again," Ikora whispered. 

"I won't," Eris replied.
3320768284.text_zh:
“萨瓦图恩以为我的王座会束缚住我。她以为我要么会心甘情愿地把自己托付于它的庇护之下，要么会深陷其中，无法自拔。” 

艾可拉摇了摇头，微笑着。埃里斯也跟着笑了。 

“她没有料到守护者会如此足智多谋，更是误判了我。” 

“如同我们这些曾以为你已经迎来最终之死的人一样。”承认这一点时，艾可拉的笑容渐渐淡去。  

“我也曾这么以为。”埃里斯歪着头，专注地打量着艾可拉。“你是不是觉得自己本该来找我？不，你做得对，艾可拉。我能活下来，我能取得胜利，是没理由能预料到的。” 

她们并肩立于埃里斯的王座之上，置身于这个由她全然构筑的世界里，可即便如此，埃里斯仍旧未能完全理解这方天地所蕴含的一切。  

“你是在安慰我，”艾可拉说到，声音紧绷而低沉。“你不该这样做的。埃里斯，死去的人是你。” 

“没错。但悲伤的人是你。” 

艾可拉转过身去，埃里斯听之任之。接受安慰绝非易事，她深知这一点。两人默默地凝视着一本本新旧交织的书籍，其书脊上镌刻的精致符文闪烁着灵魂之火。 

“我想念你，”艾可拉终于说道。“我…觉得在某种程度上，我辜负了你：我本应护你安全。即使知道你会讨厌那样。” 

“那就是你背负的诅咒，”埃里斯严肃地回答。“责任。” 

听到这话，艾可拉惊讶地笑了起来。“你跟蛇夫座对此的看法，真是大相径庭。”  

“机灵总是免不了要担心。” 

艾可拉再次收起浅浅的微笑，重归严肃。她把沉静裹在自己身上，犹如披上了一层隐形的斗篷。“我放你走，做得对吗？”  

“这是我唯一会让你做的事，”埃里斯如此说到。她示意上方和周围，指向那个摇曳着她内心最深处自我的无限螺旋图书馆。“这样的图书馆才适合我，高塔里的永远比不上。你已经尽力了，艾可拉。” 

这份宽恕凝固在她们之间寂静的空间里。最终，是艾可拉打破了这份沉默，她向前一步，将埃里斯抱入怀中。两人紧紧相拥，久久没有分开。 

“别再那样做，”艾可拉低语道。 

“我不会的，”埃里斯回答说。

3320768285.name: Ion
3320768285.text:
"And when he escapes?" 

"If," Eris corrected. 

"When he escapes," Sloane continued, "he'll have torn a hole straight through your throne world and into the Dreadnaught. This entire place will be compromised, and the City with it. You're fine with that risk?" 

"There is always risk," Eris said. "You must assume risk inherent with trust, and focus."  

The words were pointed.  

"That's not how trust works," Sloane said, unclenching her jaw with some effort.  

"No?" Eris's sidelong glance was too green. It made something itch in Sloane that she didn't like. "Tell me of trust, Deputy Commander Sloane." 

"It's earned." Sloane uncrossed her arms. Crossed them again, the other way this time. "Someone does the work, again and again. Proves they have the skills and the follow-through to get a job done. It adds up, over time. Long enough, and you know someone can and will do what they say they will. Then you don't have to question when they promise you the impossible, because you know they've got a way. That's certainty. That's trust."  

"I see." Eris sounded like she was trying too hard to be neutral. She laid solid, unwavering lines into the floor of her throne-library, one after another. Unhesitating.  

Sloane's arm burned. She ignored it. 

"Trust," Eris said at length, "is always, still, a risk. It is whispering a secret to another and hoping they will not tell it. They do not—you are caught before you fall. This time. And ever after, you must ask yourself: Is this the step too far? Is this secret the one that turns them back? But you will never know, not completely, that they will not. To entirely understand someone is impossible. You can only guess, and hope, and trust." 

"You sound like Savathûn," Sloane told her, and regretted it immediately. It wasn't true—she just hated the twistiness of Eris's mind, the way it spiraled around a question that should be so easy to answer. 

Eris's chitin-plated shoulders hitched, but her back was to Sloane, and it was hard to tell if she felt anything serious about the accusation. "We must do something, Deputy Commander. I trust," she stressed the word lightly, "that you will be there to chide me if I fail." 

Sloane's lip curled. "I'll be there," she said. "But to grind the Echo into dust. That's more important than anything else—making sure it's taken care of." 

"There you have it." Eris turned, then, a lightness on her face that Sloane had rarely seen before. "You are a certainty. Above the risk, I know this: you will not allow this to go unfinished."  

That was not quite the lesson Sloane had hoped Eris would take away from this conversation. "I'm only one Titan," Sloane said seriously. "If and when he escapes you, we're going to need more firepower than that."  

Eris hesitated. Only briefly, but it was the closest to a win Sloane was going to get. "Then make what preparations you must," she said. "Warn whom you feel prudent. I will do this—I must do this. I am aware of the risk; I would not proceed if it was not well-founded."  

The reward for a job well done was always more work, wasn't it? "Fine," Sloane said through gritted teeth.  

At least Eris trusted her, by one definition or another. It wasn't nothing.
3320768285.text_zh:
“当他逃跑时呢？” 

“是如果，”埃里斯纠正道。 

“当他逃跑时，”斯隆继续说道，“他会在你的王座世界里撕开一个直通无畏战舰的裂口。这整个地方都将陷落，而圣城也会被连累。你甘愿冒那样的风险吗？” 

“风险总是在所难免的，”埃里斯说道。“你必须承担信任所固有的风险，集中注意。”  

这话语很尖锐。  

“信任不是这样的，”斯隆说道，费了些力气才松开紧咬的牙关。  

“不是吗？”埃里斯斜睨了她一眼，泛着幽绿的光，这让斯隆感到有些不自在，心里直发痒。“那就请你来谈谈信任吧，副指挥官斯隆。” 

“信任是赢得的。”斯隆松开双臂，随即又换了一种方式交叉抱于胸前。“有人一次次地付出努力。证明自己具备完成任务所需的技能和执行力。随着时间的推移，这些努力逐渐累积。时间一长，你就会知道，这个人能够做到并且会去做自己承诺的事。然后当此人向你许下似乎不可能实现的承诺时，你便无需质疑，因为你深知其自有办法。这就是确信无疑。这就是信任。”  

“我明白了。”埃里斯听起来是在刻意维持中立的口气。她在王座图书馆的地面上，一道接一道地刻画出坚实而稳定的线条，毫不迟疑。  

斯隆的手臂有灼痛感，但她没去理会。 

“信任，”埃里斯缓缓说道，“始终伴随着风险。它就像是向另一个人倾诉秘密，然后寄希望于他们不会泄露。这一次，他们没有辜负你——你在跌倒之前就被接住了。但从此以后，你必须不断自问：这一步是否迈得太远？这个秘密是否会让他们背叛？但你永远无法完全确定他们不会那样做。因为彻底了解一个人是不可能的。你只能猜测、希望，然后选择信任。” 

“你听起来就像是萨瓦图恩，”斯隆告诉她，随即又感到后悔。这不是真的——她只是厌烦埃里斯扭曲的思维，以及她在如此简单的问题上绕圈子的方式。 

埃里斯耸了耸壳质的肩膀，但她背对着斯隆，让人难以判断她是否在严肃对待这项指责。“我们必须采取行动，副指挥官。我相信，”她轻声却刻意强调了这个词，“若我失败，你会在场斥责我。” 

斯隆抿起了嘴。“我会在场的，”她说道。“但那是为了把回响碾为齑粉，这比什么都重要——必须确保它被处理掉。” 

“这就对了。”埃里斯转过身来，脸上洋溢着斯隆前所未见的轻松。“你就是让我确信无疑的人。即便面临风险，我也深知：你一定会完成。”  

这不是斯隆希望埃里斯从这场对话中吸取的教训。“我只是一名泰坦，”斯隆严肃地说。“如果他真的挣脱了你的束缚，我们会需要更多的火力。”  

埃里斯犹豫了。虽然只是片刻，但对于斯隆而言，这已是她最接近胜利的一刻。“那就做好你必须做的准备，”她说道。“去警告那些你觉得有必要知会的人。我会去做——我必须去做。我深知其中的风险；若非确有依据，我也不会贸然行事。”  

能者多劳，不是吗？“好吧，”斯隆咬牙说道。  

至少，按照某种定义来说，埃里斯是信任她的。这很重要。

3320768286.name: Iris
3320768286.text:
"Don't you have a home to go to?" Drifter wanted to know.  

Deputy Commander Sloane, who had any number of other places she could be, glanced up from her assortment of reports and screens. She'd set up her battle station right in the middle of Drifter's ship and showed no signs of leaving. "I'm busy," she said. Her Ghost, hovering above her left shoulder, bobbed in agreement. "Either contribute, or leave." 

"That's my line," Drifter groused, but he pulled up one of the more stable chairs anyway, dropping himself into it where he could scan over the things she had spread out. "Hive?" 

"It's always Hive," Sloane said tiredly. 

"Unless it's Taken." 

"Unless it's Taken," she agreed, then remembered she was angry with him, scowling across the way. "Were you going to help?" 

Drifter held his hands up, exaggerated his 'I wasn't doing nothing, ma'am' expression. "I might have a few pieces of intel." 

"Right," Sloane said. "Well, you go ahead and volunteer those when they seem relevant. I'm thinking Xivu Arath has to be first. Savathûn likes the long game anyway, and Xivu Arath's eager for a fight. She'll hit us first, and we don't want to be trying to unwind some kind of trap while Xivu's throwing swords." 

"She's real into swords." 

"Helpful." Sloane tapped her fingers against the rickety card table. "If Xivu Arath gets going, it'll be hard to stop her without also powering her up by fighting. So we hit her first, ideally, if we can find the right place before she starts killing." 

Drawn in despite himself, Drifter squinted at Sloane's notes. A blue-line map of the Dreadnaught in three dimensions, half-complete—a few little notes off to the side ranking Hive constructs and likely locations for Xivu Arath's plots. SWORDS was underlined heavily. "Surprise attack still feels like an attack to me," he said in a moment, warming up to being helpful.  

"It sure is." Sloane blew out a frustrated breath. "She's not what she was. Not since Eris cut her off. But we still don't have time for an elegant, pacifist solution. Which is why my best thought is not to target her directly. We target her targets – find where she plans to hit, deprive her of kills and tithes by taking them down first. And if it does come to straight-on combat, make whatever we do quick and clean, none of the glory-in-battle nonsense she likes." She shrugged, not particularly happy. "It's got flaws, but it's something." 

"Not the worst plan I've heard," Drifter said honestly. He rocked his chair onto one leg, swinging it over the pivot point carelessly. "You think all this is gonna work?" 

Sloane looked up at him, fixing him with the sort of gaze that looked through him. He had the sense that he had her full attention. "I don't know," she said. "But I know we have to give it our best if we have any shot at it working. You trust Eris, don't you?" 

"'Course I do." 

Sloane deliberated visibly for a moment or two. "Then it will work," she said finally.  

"Sure," Drifter said, ignoring the sheer volume of things she clearly hadn't said. "All right. Guess I'm already dealt in anyway. Got any use for a list of places the Lucent Brood's been sighted?" 

"Always."
3320768286.text_zh:
“你无家可归吗？”浪客有些好奇。  

副指挥官斯隆，本来有无数其他地方可以去，却从眼前各式各样的报告和屏幕上抬起头来。她把她的作战指挥台设在浪客飞船的中央，完全没有离去的意思。“我很忙，”她说道。她的机灵，悬浮在她左肩上方，点头赞同。“你要么帮忙，要么离开。” 

“那是我的台词，”浪客嘟囔着，但还是拉过一把较为稳当的椅子，一屁股坐下，浏览起她摊开的东西。“邪魔族？” 

“向来都是邪魔族，”斯隆疲惫地说道。 

“除非是傀儡军团。” 

“除非是傀儡军团，”她赞同道，随即想起自己正在生他的气，隔着桌子冲他皱起眉。“你打算帮忙吗？” 

浪客举起双手，夸张地摆出一副“我什么都没做，女士”的表情。“我可能掌握了一些情报。” 

“好吧，”斯隆说。“那就把你觉得有用的说出来。我认为我们首先要面对的是希乌阿拉斯。萨瓦图恩喜欢打持久战，而希乌阿拉斯则急于求战。她会先向我们发起攻击，而我们不希望希乌挥舞刀剑之时，我们还在试图解除某种陷阱。” 

“她是真的很喜欢刀剑。” 

“真是有用的情报。”斯隆用手指敲打着那张摇摇晃晃的折叠桌。“如果希乌阿拉斯开始行动，不战斗就无法阻止她，而战斗又会增强她的力量。所以最好先下手为强，前提是我们能在她开始杀戮之前找到正确的位置。” 

浪客不由得眯起眼睛看向斯隆的笔记。那是一张没画完的无畏战舰三维蓝线规划图——旁边还有几行小字，罗列着邪魔族构造体和希乌阿拉斯有可能在策划阴谋的地点。其中，刀剑二字被重重地划上了下划线。“我感觉突袭还是一种战斗，”过了一会儿，他这么说道，开始摆出愿意帮忙的姿态。  

“确实。”斯隆无奈地叹了口气。“自从埃里斯将她断舍后，她已不再是从前的她。但我们还是没有时间找到一个优雅而和平的解决方案。所以我认为最好不要直接针对她。我们要针对她的目标——找到她计划攻击的地方，先下手为强，剥夺她杀戮和掠夺的机会。如果真的发展到正面交锋的地步，那我们的行动一定要干净利落，绝不能搞她喜欢的那套荣耀之战。”她耸了下肩，显然对此并不满意。“这个计划有瑕疵，但好歹是个办法。” 

“这不是我听过的最糟的计划，”浪客诚恳地说。他随意地把椅子翘成一腿着地，绕着支点晃来晃去。“你觉得这一切能成功吗？” 

斯隆抬起头，用一种仿佛能洞察人心的眼神盯着他。他能感觉到自己获得了她全部的注意力。“我不知道，”她说。“但我知道，如果我们想让它有一丝成功的可能，就必须全力以赴。你信任埃里斯，对吧？” 

“当然了。” 

斯隆明显地思量了一会儿。“那它就会成功，”她最后说道。  

“行，”浪客说道，忽略了她显然没有言明的大量细节。“好吧。看来我已经卷进来了。我这有份光明虫群出没地点的清单，用得上吗？” 

“当然。”

3320768287.name: Hemlock
3320768287.text:
"You are not of my Taking." 

Sloane squared her shoulders against the weight of the voice that spoke to her. It wasn't a surprise. Every time she visited Eris's throne world now, that lone and baleful eye seemed to follow her.  

Didn't mean she had to like it. Or talk to him. It. 

"But what are you, then?" he mused aloud, as if her response or lack thereof was wholly immaterial. "I am told the Taken changed hands many times. Who was it that Took you?" 

"No one," Sloane said before she could think better of it. "I said no." 

"Did you?"  

There was an awful heaviness to the Echo's attention, a fizz of sterile neutrinos and the prickling awareness of danger down her spine. But Sloane was nothing if she was not herself, and so she stood tall, chin up, and did not falter. "I don't need that power." 

"Whomever made that offer, it will not vanish," the Echo said softly. "You may not need it now. But are you so sure of the future?" 

"Yes," said Sloane, willing it to be true as she said it. "What do you want?" 

"To understand," said Oryx, and the simplicity of it was as sharp as a knife. Whatever needed to be twisted or prized loose or broken to understand it—he would. That was all there was.  

"Then understand this: I am resolute." Arc light crackled in her hands as Sloane closed them into fists. "And I am complete in myself. I need no other power." She knew it for not-quite-truth even as she said it: she was in Síocháin and Ahsa, the Traveler's Light and the Vanguard, even as they were in her. But she certainly didn't need the Taken. 

"Aiat," the Echo said thoughtfully, and nothing further.  

Sloane did not retreat. She turned that word over and over again in her mind. Aiat. It had a meaning it hadn't quite before, sounding almost like her own voice saying, "I am complete in myself" back to her. 

Hours and hours later, long after she'd left Eris's throne world, still it echoed. And still she wondered about its truth.
3320768287.text_zh:
“你不是我的傀儡军团。” 

斯隆挺直肩膀，对抗那个声音施加在她身上的重量。这不意外。现在每次她到访埃里斯的王座世界，那双孤独而邪恶的眼睛似乎都在暗中盯着她。  

但这并不意味着她得喜欢它。或是跟他交谈。跟它。 

“但你究竟是什么呢？”他大声寻思道，仿佛她的回答与否根本无关紧要。“我听说傀儡军团曾多次易主。是谁操纵了你呢？” 

“没有谁，”斯隆脱口而出。“我拒绝了。” 

“是吗？”  

回响的注视中带着一种令人窒息的沉重，无菌的中微子在周围滋滋作响，而危险的感觉沿着她的脊椎蔓延，让她感到阵阵刺痛。但斯隆如果不能维持自我，就会失去存在的意义，于是，她站得笔直，扬起下巴，毫不动摇。“我不需要那种力量。” 

“无论是谁提出的，那个提议都不会消失，”回响柔声说道。“或许你现在不需要它。但未来呢？你如此确定吗？” 

“是的，”斯隆说道，希望这能让它成为事实。“你想要怎样？” 

“想要理解，”欧里克斯说道，话语简洁得就像一把利刃。为了理解，无论是需要扭曲、撬开还是打破什么——他都会去做。这就是他所在乎的一切。  

“那就理解这一点：我意志坚定。”斯隆双手紧握成拳，电弧在她手中噼啪作响。“我是完整的个体。我不需要其他力量。”即使这么说时，她心中也清楚这并非全然属实：她身在西奥昌与阿莎之中，也身在旅行者的光能和先锋之中，就像他们也与她同在一样。但她可以肯定的是，她决不需要傀儡军团。 

“阿特，”回响沉吟着，再无二话。  

斯隆没有退缩。她在脑海里反复琢磨这个词。阿特。它似乎有了与以往不同的含义，听起来几乎像是她自己的声音在用“我是完整的个体”回应她。 

过了很长时间，在她早已离开埃里斯的王座世界后，它仍然在她的脑海中回响。而她依旧在寻思着它的真相。

3320768272.name: Hellebore
3320768272.text:
Close. It had been too close. The knowledge of the shape of the knife held out to her had burned itself into Sloane's mind; she could see it even now, though its weight did not bow the fabric of her thoughts as it had. 

"I am pleased you returned to us safely," Eris said—close by. Very close. Sloane startled back, surprised that Eris had come so near without Sloane hearing her. "Your loss at this stage would be… catastrophic." 

Sloane's exhalation was half a laugh. "You have a gift for understatement," she said, to cover how rattled she truly was by the experience of re-forging Willbreaker.  

Eris's mouth flickered, the ghost of a smile there and gone again. This close, Sloane thought, she looked pale—paler. Strained. Containing the Echo was wearing on her. "Do you hear it still?" Eris asked. 

"Yes," Sloane admitted. If she was compromised, it was her responsibility to be honest about it. A moment later, remembering, her gaze flicked over Eris's shoulder to where the Echo hung, roiling with its own power, suspended in the grasp of Eris's magics. "Not sure I want to talk about this here."
