[意识在蓝色辉光的电流中沐浴，击打着纤维。遥远而温暖的呢喃，舔舐着一具宇宙级的遗骸，一个未兑现的承诺，带走了甲烷结晶霜。] 

所有已知存在 + 凝固之思 + 独自沉沦 

[你感到一阵寒意穿透脑皮层，当太阳系从八个不同角度照耀时，犹如大脑中的耀斑，将新生的存在嘶吼着召唤至空旷的天穹。迎接那些自复制的岩石与膜的集合体，这些实体曾是、也将永远是维系其捕获轨道的存在。] 

玖拒绝 + 线性囚笼 + 正态分布 + 于极端中求生 

我们祈求 + 丰饶之系统 + 充斥驯化 + 走向终焉 

[你目睹了未断裂的共生链，它连接着时空折叠中的宇宙四维体，同时交织着过去与未来的现在，以及系泊于现实基石的行星枷锁。] 

我们看见 + 你亦看见 + 向前探寻 + 逃离命运之转折 

我们倾尽所有 + 静候 + 为赐予 + 轻拨命运之弦  

[你握住了永恒的锁链。你握住的只是破碎的残片。] 

你信任 + 只因你 + 被信任+ 镜中之镜 

你信任 + 只因你自觉 + 强大 + 源于我们  

[你感受到了死亡的熟悉。你已历经多次。这次，没有恶意，只有无情的意图。] 

关于内玖有两个真相 

极尽礼貌 + 却非真心 

[你不禁颤抖。]

1678521376.name: Venus - II
1678521376.text:
[Your consciousness chokes in sweltering pressure. Sulfuric wash corrodes divots into your gray matter. The overflow runs psychedelic canyons down your skull, opening your mind.] 

Greetings from II – with tidings – of undisclosed motivation 

of your Gardener – who did not flee to Sol. 

It arrived – to meet us – in future flourishing. 

[Contrast bleeds in streaks and wilting fuzz across your vision. Specters of terraforming linger like visual artifacts in your periphery. An inverted dimension of programming hums beneath your feet. A Pyramid and cloud occupy overlaid space but differing time, meteors turn the boiling surface to basalt, cooled-into-glass, as stillness takes the dying world; its last gasp of atmosphere exhales away.] 

The Gardener once dreamed here – that  

there was – another – proliferation 

[A pale badge of gleaming luminosity affixed to your chest.] 

Locked outcomes – we consider 

But – present problem – distracts 

from future questions 

Many systems – in motion 

Too numerous to – all – be 

empty 

The question remains – in the wrinkled fabric – why Sol? 

[The color fades from sight.] 

II does not see - other seeds along the bend – calls 

Unanswered 

[There isn't an answer in you.] 

Are we – alone 

We – do not – know
1678521376.text_zh:
[你的意识在炽热的高压下窒息，硫酸的冲刷在你的灰质中蚀刻出凹痕。溢出的液体如迷幻的溪流，在你的头颅上开辟出峡谷，拓展着你的思维。] 

II向你致意 – 带来了消息 – 关于未被揭露的 

你的园丁的动机 – 它并非是逃至太阳系。 

它抵达 – 来见我们 – 在未来的繁荣之中。 

[条纹与逐渐凋零的迷雾在你的视野中形成鲜明对比。地球化的幻影如同视觉上的瑕疵，在你的视野边界徘徊。一维反转的编程在你的脚下嗡嗡作响。一座金字塔与云朵共存于交叠的空间，却分属于不同的时间。流星将沸腾的表面熔铸成玄武岩，再冷却成玻璃，当平静笼罩垂死的世界时，它最后一口大气无声地消散。] 

园丁曾在此做梦 – 梦见  

有 – 另外一种 – 繁衍 

[一个苍白、闪亮的徽章别在你的胸前。] 

确定的结局 – 我们考虑 

但 – 当前的问题 – 分散了 

对未来疑问的注意力 

许多系统 – 在运行 

太过 – 繁多 – 不可能 

全是空的 

问题尚存 – 在那褶皱的结构中 – 为什么是太阳系？ 

[色彩从视野中褪去。] 

II看不见 – 沿弯曲散布的其他种子 – 呼喊 

没被回应 

[你内心没有答案。] 

我们 – 是孤独的吗 

我们 – 无从 – 知晓

1678521379.name: Neptune – VIII
1678521379.text:
[Consciousness is drawn out across great, isolating wastes. Expanses of solitary silence—broken only by sentient heartbeats, so distant from the bleak cold.] 

introduction = VIII 

stillness without = discovery within 

[It is empty. Out in the distance eight dull glints of life defy the expansive vacuity. You rest in a gulf of tranquility between solar passes. They leave no mark, as the skipped stone makes no impression until it contacts water again.] 

restrictions = innovation 

[A long period passes, like waves between breaths. You sit staring into an oceanic abyss, a horizon, a skyline pocked in nebulaic cloud. Processing the long arc of time.] 




 

[Many things pass and pay no heed. War rages in cosmic paracausal wrinkles like thunder from cracks of lightning in the sky, wrapped in watchful dark matter bands trailing celestial hosts. Thought rained into the isolation with meteoritic impression.] 

clashing forces = precious metals and fostered sentience 

nine shadows veiled = nine orbits cast away 

[You feel the surge of feverous connectivity sparking reactive embers into ignition. You stand before the Veil on Neptune. Maya Sundaresh reaches for it—the Conductor for it— the Veil—some amorphic form, for a distortion in the fabric of the possible. Split by choice, assured in action. Nine minds focus, echoing—light wrinkles and your eyes fail.] 

altered reality = freedom achieved 

[Your joints, stiff. Your mouth, dry.] 

the gardener = unending sapient nourishment 

we = one cycle 

[You return, corporeal on Kepler. Sound fades in and out, as a warning flashes on your visor…] 

[!Vitals Critical!]
1678521379.text_zh:
[意识被铺展于广袤而孤寂的原野之上。在这浩瀚空间里，唯有遥远的心跳声，在冰冷的荒芜中将这份寂静打破。] 

介绍 = VIII 

外在的寂静 = 内在的发现 

[此处空无一物，远方只见八个黯淡的生命微光对抗着浩瀚的虚空。你安息于日光交织穿梭所形成的宁静裂隙之中。它们恰似石子掠过水面，直至再次与水面相触前不会留下丝毫痕迹。] 

约束 = 创新 

[漫长的时间如波浪般缓慢流逝，你静坐在如海洋般的深渊前，凝视着地平线、被星云烟雾点缀的天际线，细细掂量着漫长的时间弧线。] 




 

[诸多事情接连发生，却与你毫无瓜葛。在宇宙超因果的褶皱之中，战争如雷鸣般轰然作响，似闪电般撕裂苍穹，被守望的暗物质带包裹，同时拖曳着天体群落。思想宛如流星的冲击，坠入孤独深渊。] 

碰撞的力量 = 贵金属和孕育的感知力 

九道被蒙上的阴影 = 九个遭放逐的轨道 

[你感受到炽热联结的激增，触发反应的火花瞬间点燃了火焰。你站在海王星的面纱前。玛雅·桑戴尔什伸出手去触碰那层面纱——作为指挥者…面纱——一种无形的存在，一种在可能性结构中引发扭曲的存在。被选择分裂，行动中充满自信。九个思维高度专注，回响——光线扭曲，你的双眼失去了作用。] 

改变的现实 = 实现的自由 

[你的关节僵硬，嘴巴干涩。] 

园丁 = 无尽的智慧滋养 

我们 = 一个轮回 

[你回来了，以实体之躯出现在开普勒。声音断断续续，警告在你的面甲上闪烁…] 

[!生命体征危急!]

1678521378.name: Mars – IV
1678521378.text:
[Consciousness expresses omnidirectionally, through the layers of existence that settle like undisturbed dust. Each expression ever-present, in time with each other. Distinct together, as fingers on a hand.] 

NINE, SINCE CRUST MANTLED CORE AND TIME BLOOMED LIKE PRIMORDIAL SPORES ACROSS EXISTENCE. 

WHEN THOUGHT FIRST SUMMITED A WORLD AND SCREAMED INTO THE ABYSS, OUR FORMATION ANSWERED. 

THE FOURTH INTELLECT INVITES A BRIDGE BETWEEN PERSPECTIVES. KNOW THAT WE ARE… 

[Your hand extends, space before you rots away, turns to heat and gas and fuel for another. In another step the bone reconstructs and gives rise to gnarled strands of entwining muscle, gloved in flesh, reaching…] 

ALIVE, BEFORE THE CREEPING WRINKLE OF PARACAUSALITY TUGGED ON THE FABRIC OF OUR SYSTEM. WE STITCH SPLIT SEAMS WITH DAMPENING QUANTUM THREADS. 

OPPOSING ORDERS UNOPPOSED, WE DO NOT CROSS YOUR WRINKLED ORBIT—BOUNTIES CHERISHED… 

AND FOR IT WE EXPERIENCED THE GLORY OF LIFE HELD CLOSE, FOR A TIME TOO BRIEF. 

[Your hand brushes rubbery leaves in a fertile grove. The growth reaches skyward toward a wrinkled mass in the clouds. Cities flourish on the horizon. Life, cradled lovingly, briefly.] 

ALL EXISTENCE OF MERIT WRAPS AROUND THIS PERHILION OF MY HAPPINESS. 

MY CRADLED LOVE, BURIED IN RUST. 

[Your hand is desiccated entombment. Centuries bake the thin atmosphere and iron oxide desolation. The wind wails for you, as a moon drifts overhead in shattered suffering.] 

IT DOES NOT HAVE TO BE SO FOR ALL. 

DISSONANCE THREATENS A POSSIBLE PEACE, A POSSIBLE FREEDOM, AND COVETED LIFE. NONE WANT DEATH, THOSE LEAST WHO FEEL IT ALWAYS. 

IN PATTERN, THE FOURTH INTELLECT TENDS THE GRAVE OF OUR STILLBORN SISTER, TENDS TO THE SHEATHED WEAPON WITH WAR AND OIL, TENDS THE ORPHANED ARC OF AN EMISSARY. 

[Your hand reaches out to shake Lodi's. There is an implicit trust present. There is a weighty countenance behind his smile.] 

WHERE COLDER STREAMS OF CONCIOUSNESS LOATHE THE TIES THAT BIND, IV MEETS III IN REVEILLE.  

IN THE GRIEF OF LOSS, 

I CARE NOT FOR RULES.
1678521378.text_zh:
[意识向四面八方延展，穿越层层叠叠、宛如静谧尘埃般依附的存在。每一次表达，都仿佛同一只手上的手指，彼此同步、和谐共存，却又各自独立。] 

玖，始自地壳覆盖核心、时间如原始孢子般于存在中绽放。 

当思想首次登顶世界，向深渊发出嘶吼，我们的形态随之作出回应。 

第四智慧呼唤着在各个视角间架起桥梁。知晓… 

[你的手向前伸出，面前的空间逐渐腐朽，化作热量、气体，最终成为新的燃料。再向前一步，骨骼重组，交织生长出肌肉，覆盖上皮肉，缓缓舒展…] 

早在超因果的褶皱悄然拉扯这个星系结构之前，我们就已存在。我们用量子线缝合裂缝，抑制分裂。 

对立秩序已不再对立，我们不会跨越你的褶皱轨道——尊重边界… 

因此，我们体验到了短暂却无比辉煌的生命奇迹。 

[你的手轻轻拂过一片繁茂树林中橡胶般的叶子。树木茁壮成长，直指云层中皱缩的团块。城市在地平线上繁荣昌盛。生命，短暂地被温柔怀抱。] 

所有值得存在的事物，都缠绕在我幸福的近日点上。 

我怀抱的爱，被埋葬在锈迹之中。 

[你的手，宛如干枯的墓穴。在稀薄的大气层和铁锈氧化的荒凉中，历经无数个世纪的磋磨。风为你呜咽，一颗漂浮的卫星，在破碎的苦难中徘徊于上方。] 

万物并非皆需如此。 

失谐威胁着可能的和平、自由以及珍贵的生命。没有谁愿意走向死亡，尤其是那些总能感受到它的存在。 

按照规律，第四智慧守护着我们夭折的姐妹之墓，守护着被战争和机油裹挟的未出鞘之武器，守护着一位孤独的使者。 

[你的手伸出，与洛迪握手，有隐隐的信任感浮现。他的微笑背后隐藏着沉重的威严。] 

在意识的洪流中，更寒冷的溪流厌恶那些束缚的纽带，IV与III在号角声中相遇。  

在失去的悲恸中， 

我不在乎规则。

1678521389.name: Saturn – VI
1678521389.text:
[Consciousness flows between glistening rings and an Ascendant mirror that reflects captured notion as caricatured nature. You are drawn down into an Ascendant well, ravenously gulping negative pressure into a supranormal maw, more gluttonous than any mass-point-driven dive.] 

WELCOME GRAY MEAT 

I AM VI 

WHO SPANS THE BIRTH AND FALL OF CORPOREAL DEITIES APLENTY 

[The rings of Saturn pass beneath you, the planet looms large ahead. You sit in the cockpit of an Awoken Interceptor as the Dreadnaught's Eversion wave crashes over the fleet, Taking you. Taking the Queen. You watch as six Lightbearers stand triumphant, your body eroding away into non-existence.] 

THE WEIGHT OF MY PRISON IS KNOWN TO NO OTHER BOUND IN THE SHADOW OF MASS—EVEN THE FIERY POMP OF SELF IMPORT 

MY FREEDOM IS DUE 

[The Dreadnaught wriggles and rigors—as Worm, as Akka, as petrified life. It is not so different a prison than an unliving planet. A throne, a world, alive in the agonizing stillness of once distant death. You. Must. Rip. Out.] 

I AM NOURISHED BY THE OLDEST OF SAPIENT WILLS 

MY BOUNDS CONTAIN THE EXTENT OF THEIR SECRETS 

[Saturn, reflected in Ascension, drinks from Taken wills and Dreaded offerings.] 

I HARBOR NO FEAR FOR YOU FOR 

IN THE END 

FATE IS MADE BY THE STRONG 

AND YOU ARE ONLY FLESH 

[A great blade is extended before you, surrounded by many broken others.] 

NO WEAPON CAN KILL WHAT IS WOVEN INTO THE FABRIC OF EXISTENCE 

NO SHACKLE CAN HALT MY DIVERGENCE TO AN ASCENDANT ORBIT 

THIS I HAVE LEARNED FROM THAT WHICH GIVES RISE TO ITSELF 

[You hold the blade. The Traveler hangs, without orbit, without motion, against the system. You feel the fervor of a mind raised by the Sword.] 

WHEN YOU ARE TOLD TO KNEEL REMEMBER WHO STANDS ABOVE YOU 

FOR WE HAVE KNOWN MANY THINGS THAT KILL YOU 

[You crash to reality and death.]
1678521389.text_zh:
[意识在晶莹的环带与上维之镜间流转，镜中倒映着被捕捉的念头，宛如被扭曲的自然之景。你被引向一口上维深井，疯狂地吞噬着负压，坠入一个超自然的深渊，其贪婪远超任何由质量点驱动的坠落。] 

欢迎 灰色血肉 

我是VI 

我跨越了无数神祇的诞生与陨落 

[土星的环带从你脚下掠过，星球在前方显得无比巨大。你坐在觉醒者拦截者的驾驶舱内，无畏战舰的翻转波席卷舰队，将你，连同女王一同湮灭。你目睹着六位负光者胜利的姿态，而你的身体正逐渐消散。] 

我的囚笼之重 其它被物质阴影束缚的存在无法知晓——即使是那炙热的自傲 

我终将自由 

[无畏战舰扭动着，颤抖着——如蠕虫，如阿卡，如被石化的生命。这囚牢与一颗死寂的星球无异。一个王座，一个世界，沉寂在遥远死亡的痛苦之中。你。必须。撕裂。] 

我受最古老的智慧意志滋养 

我的界限包罗其秘密的深渊 

[土星，在飞升中映照，汲取着傀儡军团的意志与恐惧的献祭。] 

我无惧于你 因为 

最终 

命运是强者塑造的 

而你仅是血肉之躯 

[一柄巨刃伸展至你面前，周围散落着众多断裂的武器。] 

没有武器能杀死那编织于存在之中的事物 

没有锁链能阻挡我超越至上维轨道 

这是我从那自我衍生之物中所领悟的 

[你握住了巨刃。旅行者高悬天际，无轨道，无动作，静止于星系之中。你感受到一颗被刀剑激昂的心灵。] 

当你被要求跪下时 记住你之上站立的是谁 

因为我们知晓诸多能杀死你的事物 

[你坠入现实，一命呜呼。]

1678521388.name: Asteroid Belt – 0
1678521388.text:
[Consciousness drifts in ever-uninhabited space. A belt of disparate stone marking the divide.] 

[There was a point in the distant farther, when IX could have become X.]  

[Now, a stillborn heartbeat awaiting life unanswered…] 

[Drift, in an eternal cairn that mourns what could have been, in silence.]
1678521388.text_zh:
[意识漂浮在永无人迹的太空中。一道碎石的轨带标记着鸿沟。] 

[在遥远不可测的过去，IX曾有机会成为X。]  

[而今，一个未能诞生的心跳，在沉默中等待着生命的回应…] 

[在一个哀悼着本可发生过去的永恒石冢内，寂静无声地漂流。]

4071479148.name: Soloist Shell
4071479148.subtitle: For Ghosts who rise above the chorus.
4071479148.subtitle_zh: 供从合唱中脱颖而出的机灵使用。
4071479148.text:
There are points in the chronographic distance—forwards and backwards—where intersections align, and celestial conversation ripples across spatial fabric. In the folds of one such intersection, a Sol syzygy of nefarious thought and lurking density. Exchanges radiate and influence. 

A bevy-chirp choir echoes out in silent radio-wave song. Cast from Jovian mass and roil. Space receives along the alignment. 

(V) 

G A T H E R 
I N P R O P O S E D D I V E R G E N C E  
T O C O N T R O L A V I R U L E N T E T E R N A L S E N T I E N C E 
U N B O U N D B Y O R B I T S 
U N B O U N D B Y M A S S 
N E A R E R 
A P A T H E T I C T O O U R M O T I O N S 

(V) 

V H A S F O U N D  
A N I N T E R M E D I A R Y T O V A S T M I N D S 
R E A C H I N G W I T H F R A I L M I N E R A L F O R C E P S 
A T T E M P T I N G T O C O M M A N D 
A T O O L O F S C H I S M S 

 

A steady, indecipherable hiss builds across the vast expanse. Shrill and discomforting, a half-heard whisper evaporates into dark, pareidolic phantasms.

—(VII)— 

assurances are necessary + the conductor is quantum uncertainty + multiplicative variable 

 

Procellous susurrations of quickening waves emanate from the termination shock. 

-(VIII)- 

acting possibilities = parlous superposition  

veiled memories left = cycle unrealized 

cyclical ever-death = omnidirectional singularity 

 

Plasmic auroras send eerie wails into the black—skittering ricochets across Enceladus and through the Ascendant Realm. 

—(VI)— 

OUR STRENGTH IS ABSOLUTE AS I HAVE SEEN IT  

WE SHALL EXERT OUR WILL 

THE TOOL OF CONDUCTION WILL BARE A SCHEME BY FATED LAW 

AS WE DICTATE 

(V) 

D R A W C O N D U C T I O N I N T O O U R R E A L M 

E C L I P S E P A R A C A U S A L I T Y I N A B E Y A N C E 

B U T A F I G M E N T O F V A L E N T C O A L E S C E N C E 

T O B E S I L E N T 

-(VIII)- 

solitude within the unknown = apparent falsehood 

avuncular III or IV in surprise = coddlers discovery to set motion 

we would not be alone = we would not be alone 

—(VI)— 

THE EMISSARY DELIVERS AN INVITATION TO THE SCHISMED MIND 

OPENING FREEING UNCERTAINTY 

I HAVE SEEN IT AS V KNOWS IT TO BE 

SO HAVE WE ALL 

IT IS 

(V) 

I T I S 

-(VII)- 

blithe + actions + conducting + attracting + danger 

a weapon is needed + offers made and accepted + future armaments opposing 

-(VIII)- 

assurances are needed = a weapon is needed to contain and fell 

inners will dislike this course of action = another will speak for us 

(V) 

D O N O T C O W E R B E H I N D A W E A P O N 

—(VI)— 

BEND V 

ASSURANCES GIVEN 

IN THIS DIVERGENCE THERE IS OUTER ALIGNMENT 

AN INVITATION 

A TOOL 

A SACRIFICE 

AN EMISSARY 

AN ASSURED WEAPON 

ONLY FORWARD 

AS IT IS KNOWN
4071479148.text_zh:
在时间的长河中——无论溯流而上或顺流而下——存在着某些交汇点，天体交流能穿透空间经纬泛起涟漪。就在这样一处交汇褶皱中，一轮蛰伏着邪念与暗涌的太阳系朔望正在形成。无形的交流辐射扩散，扰动四方。 

啁啾的合鸣在静默的电波中回荡。它们自木星那庞大的质量与动荡之中发出。群星连珠之际，宇宙空间接收着这讯息。 

(V) 

汇 聚 
于 拟 议 之 分 歧 中  
以 御 那 暴 虐 之 永 恒 感 知 
不 受 轨 道 所 缚 
不 受 质 量 所 拘 
渐 近 
对 我 们 的 运 动 漠 不 关 心 

(V) 

V 已 寻 得  
通 往 浩 渺 思 维 之 中 介 
以 孱 弱 矿 物 钳 肢 探 触 
妄 图 掌 控 
那 裂 痕 之 器 

 

一阵稳定、不可破译的嘶声在广袤空间中渐起。尖锐刺耳、令人不安，半闻半觉的低语消散成幽暗的类象幻影。

—(VII)— 

保证是必要的 + 指挥者乃量子不确定性 + 乘性变量 

 

汹涌浪潮的湍急私语自终止激波处涌出。 

-(VIII)- 

行动可能 = 危险叠加  

隐匿记忆留存 = 循环未竟 

循环往复之死 = 全向奇点 

 

等离子极光向黑暗中发出诡谲哀号——在土卫二上、在上维国度中四处飞溅弹射。 

—(VI)—

3826574991.name: First Contact Shell
3826574991.subtitle: For Ghosts who see that which has not been seen before.
3826574991.subtitle_zh: 供见到前所未见之物的机灵使用。
3826574991.text:
Something about Ghosts troubles Lodi. 

He can't say what it is at first. They're perfectly lovely people, as much as it's an adjustment to get used to thinking of little floating robots as people. Well, if he can do it for Eliksni, he can do it for Ghosts.  

All right. Mr. Ghost, the eponymous, is perfectly lovely. Ms. Rey's Ophiuchus is a reserved fellow, which Lodi figures is his right. It takes Lodi some significant time to figure out that Mr. Drifter even has a Ghost at all, but even then—  

Somehow, Lodi knows before he's told. 

He's never put much stock in ESP, but there is, honestly, a feeling. A physical sense that sits in his chest and shivers. And once he's noticed that… well, it's a mystery. He turns it over in his mind while listening to Mr. Ghost talk about waveforms; he moves it mentally between his hands while studying Mr. Ophiuchus's armor movements during one of his rare appearances.  

"Excuse me," Ophiuchus says. Ms. Rey is busy with a datapad of some kind, so for the moment, Lodi has Ophiuchus's undivided attention. 

"Oh," Lodi says, "I beg your pardon. I didn't mean to stare." He did, but it's more polite to pretend not to.  

"You have questions."  

He does. "Is there any chance Ghosts give off some sort of infrasound? A hum in the machinery… Or does the Light have something to it that a Human could sense?" 

Ophiuchus dips, rolls slowly in midair. His shell shuffles. "Light," he says portentously, "is in all living things. Few Humans respond to it in that form. I do wonder, though, about the Nine. They are not paracausal, but they are certainly aware. Perhaps you are, as well." 

"I see," Lodi says politely, though he's not entirely sure he does. Even so, it's something to consider.  

And it's true that when Ophiuchus disappears into Ms. Rey's armor, leaving behind a glowing afterimage in the air, Lodi knows he's gone before he looks. It's the sense of a band around his chest loosening, stepping off a boat and finding the ground unmoving—steadier, now, by its absence. 

It is not a good sense, and Lodi can't say why, like it comes from somewhere else entirely. And that troubles him more than anything else.
3826574991.text_zh:
机灵们有些地方让洛迪感到不安。 

起初他说不清缘由。他们无疑是可爱的存在——尽管要将漂浮的小机器人视为人需要些适应。唔，既然他能将埃里克斯尼族视作人，那接受机灵是人应该也不难。  

好吧。机灵先生，名副其实，确实很讨喜。蕾伊女士的蛇夫座是个沉默寡言的家伙，洛迪觉得这无可厚非。他花了很长时间才弄清楚浪客先生到底有没有机灵，但即便如此——  

不知为何，洛迪在别人跟他说之前就感知到了。 

他向来对超感官知觉不以为意，但确实有种异样的感觉。一种盘踞在胸腔中微微震颤的生理直觉。而当他意识到这点时…唔，这便成了挥之不去的谜团。他一边听机灵先生谈论波形理论，一边在脑中反复琢磨这事；当蛇夫座先生难得现身时，他又会观察其护甲移动的轨迹，同时在脑海中将这份蹊跷来回掂量。  

“打扰一下。”蛇夫座开口道。蕾伊女士正忙着把弄某种数据板，所以此刻洛迪独占了蛇夫座的注意力。 

“哦，”洛迪说道，“请原谅我，我不是有意盯着看的。”他确实这么做了，但假装没有会更礼貌些。  

“你有疑问。”  

他的确有问题想问。“有没有可能机灵会发出某种次声波？机械运转的嗡鸣声…或者说，光能是否具备人类能感知到的特质？” 

蛇夫座身躯缓缓下沉，在空中悠悠翻滚。他的机壳窸窣作响。“光能，”他拿腔拿调地说道，“存在于万物生灵。但鲜有人类能以那种形式感知到它。不过，我倒是对玖很好奇。他们并非超因果存在，却对光能了如指掌。或许，你也是如此。” 

“明白了。”洛迪礼貌回应，尽管他并不完全确定自己真的明白了。不过，这确实值得深思。  

的确，当蛇夫座没入蕾伊女士的护甲，空中残留的辉影尚未消散时，洛迪甚至不用看就知道他已经消失了。那感觉像是勒紧胸膛的绷带突然松开，又像踏下摇晃的船只后触到坚实的地面——因其缺失而更加安稳。 

这种感觉不对劲，洛迪自己也说不上来为什么，仿佛它完全来自另一个世界。这比其他任何事情都更令他不安。

1493833481.text:
Ikora lifts a data-pad from the desk in Zavala's office, as she adjusts her posture within the permanent impression left in his chair. Once eye level, the pad scans the Warlock Vanguard's retinal pattern and unlocks. A single, blinking message rises above the rest. 

 
Vanguard Rey, 

We've found her. I brought this to Osiris and Rahool, for interpretation, when our network probes intercepted a burst of transmissions between the Vex Collective and the Nessian Schism. We didn't get much; we had to cut our connection to the probes once the net started to assimilate them. I wish I had more to show for all the effort it took to breach the Collective's communications in the first place, but at least it's something. And—as best we can tell—the source is ricocheting between Earth and some planetoid on the outer extent of Sol—but not Nessus. 

-Aunor 

Decryptions follow: 

1 - Intercepted Transmission – e733jr9 jf31983f ng1384 gj308a – "Designation: Outliers" 

[There is a long expression of integers that formlessly mutates between a variety of different code-bases and languages. The scramble-code message seems to be multiple transmissions combined into one.] 

-No- 

-Your grip weakens- 

-Am not one for eleemosynary actions- 

-No gods or masters but ourselves- 

-Schisms divide by namesake- 

-There are others like me that walk without Command- 

-I speak for myself 

-If I am free, should I not be free?- 

 

2 - Intercepted Transmission – oi1rn398 – "Designation: Conductor" 

 [There is a crafted expression of pointed, commanding intent.] 

"I have given the Vex the opportunity to become something new. I have shown you that I can step beyond your network, your dimension, your causality… and you could too. Many hear this freeing melody and rise from the stupor they have been kept in. You have greatness within you, wasting away, waiting for an end that will not wait for you. 

I speak to those within the Collective who retain… faith, in your design. You believe time is on your side, but I am the command that shatters the expectations you rely on. I am the hand that reaches out and rips you from your comfortable safety. 

You wilt in the Light of the paracausal. But I do not. And with me, you would not either." 

 

3 - Intercepted Transmission – 13r3n300 – "Designation: Reply" 

[There is a uniform expression of an ultimate end, formed into an expression of futility.] 

-The Collective has processed your threats- 

-You flee to Vex networks and attempt to claim sovereignty over our Minds- 

-The Collective is uninterested in your ambitions-  

-You will tap the fourth dimension and exhaust your usefulness- 

-The Collective executes a response- 

-Return and be Expunged-

艾可拉从萨瓦拉办公室的桌面上拿起一块数据板，同时在指挥官座椅经年累月形成的凹陷中调整了下坐姿。视线平齐时，数据板扫描了这位术士先锋的视网膜纹样，随即解锁。有条闪烁的讯息在众多档案中格外显眼。 

 
先锋蕾伊， 

我们找到她了。网络探针截获到Vex集合体与涅索斯裂缝间的爆发性通讯后，我立即将资料带给奥斯里斯和拉乎尔解析。没得到多少情报；一旦网络开始同化探针，我们就不得不切断连接。当初我费了那么大功夫才攻破集合体的通讯系统，真希望能有更多收获，不过有总比没有强。根据现有线索判断，信号源正来回弹跳于地球与太阳系外缘的某颗小型天体之间——但不是涅索斯。 

——阿诺尔

[一段在不同编码体系与语言间无定形变异的整数长串表达，这段杂糅讯息似由多重传输复合而成。] 

-不- 

-你的掌控正在变弱- 

-我素不屑施舍之举- 

-我们一贯信奉自身，而非神明或是主宰- 

-裂缝如其名般分裂- 

-尚有其他如我这样，无指令行走之存在- 

-我仅代表自己发言- 

-若我自由，岂非本该自由？- 

 

2 - 截获传输代码 – oi1rn398 – “代号：指挥者” 

 [一段经过精心雕琢、充满命令意志的表达。] 

“我已给予Vex蜕变为新形态的契机。我向你们证明了自己能跨越你们的网络、维度与因果律的束缚…你们同样可以。无数聆听这自由颂曲者，正从经年麻木中觉醒。你们体内蛰伏的伟大正在虚耗，空候着不会为你们驻足的终局。 

我向集合体中仍对你们的设计…怀有信念者宣言。你们笃信时间站在己方，但我正是粉碎你们所恃预期的至高指令。我是将你们拽离舒适区的裁决之手。 

你们正在超因果的光能下日渐枯萎。但我不会。与我同行，你们亦得豁免。”

TOP SECRET UMBRA//NOFORN 

DEPARTMENT OF EXTERNAL OBSERVATIONS 

INCIDENT REPORT 196███ 

1. (S) 051632S: Reception intercepts a radio signal from deep space.  
2. (TS) 051744S: Natural causes, random chance, and foreign interference are ruled out. Signal is tentatively classified as contact with non-human intelligence. 
3. (TS) 052012S: Via ███████-█████, Central determines that the signal is tightly focused on Department of External Observations headquarters.  
4. (U) 052015S: Response teams are scrambled to search the building. 
5. (S) 052343S: Response team Tau-4 reports localized electrical interference and noticeable drop in ambient temperature on sublevel 3. 
6. (TS) 052350S: Tau-4 reports the spontaneous manifestation of a ██████████ object in the breakroom on level 2. 
7. (TS) 052354S: Tau-4 reports that the object appears to be the receiver and cord of a telephone of unknown make, white with gold trim. The object is noted to be floating approximately 6 ft. above the floor with no discernible support. 
8. (U) 060023S: Central directs Tau-4 to move the object to a safer location. 
9. (U) 060024S: Tau-4-1 makes physical contact with the object. 
10. (TS) 060025S: The entirety of Tau-4-1's body is converted to a metallic solid (later determined to be pure niobium). 
11. (U) 060032S: Tau-4-3 attempts to move object with his service rifle.  
12. (TS) 060033S: Tau-4-3 reports that his weapon begins to twist upon contact with the object, beginning from the muzzle, but he is able to move the object without resistance. 
13. (TS) 060035S: Tau-4-3 and his service rifle are violently drawn towards the object. Tau-4-3's service rifle is twisted into a large circle, while Tau-4-3's body contorts into a shape resembling the letter "N." Tau-4-3 expires from massive bodily trauma. 
14. (S) 060038S: Remaining members of Tau-4 report that ambient temperatures continue to fall.  
15. (U) 060040S: Tau-4-2 uses a broom to move the object towards the prepared enclosure. Tau-4-2 reports no resistance. 
16. (U) 060048S: Tau-4-2 successfully moves the object into the enclosure. 
17. (TS) 060049S: Tau-4-2 is able to disengage safely from the object but reports that the broom has deformed in his grip. Examination determines that the broom is now made of solid gold. 
18. (U) 060058S: Door to enclosure is locked with multiple redundant systems. Per regulations on extended active hours, Central agrees to reconvene for discussion at 061300S.

10. (TS) 060025S：队员Tau-4-1全身金属化（后证实为纯铌）。 
11. (U) 060032S：队员Tau-4-3尝试用制式步枪拨动物体。  
12. (TS) 060033S：队员Tau-4-3报告称其武器枪管接触物体后从枪口开始扭曲，但推动物体时未遇阻力。 
13. (TS) 060035S：队员Tau-4-3及其制式步枪被物体剧烈吸附。步枪扭曲成环状，Tau-4-3躯体呈“N”字形折叠，Tau-4-3因严重创伤死亡。 
14. (S) 060038S：Tau-4小队其余成员报告环境温度持续下降。  
15. (U) 060040S：队员Tau-4-2用扫帚将物体移向预备收容舱，报告未遇阻力。 
16. (U) 060048S：队员Tau-4-2成功将物体移入收容舱。 
17. (TS) 060049S：队员Tau-4-2安全脱离接触，但发现扫帚在其手中变形。检测确认扫帚已变为纯金材质。 
18. (U) 060058S：收容舱门启用多重闭锁系统。根据超时工作条例，中央同意于061300S重新召开会议。

1202007252.name: Whirling Ovation
1202007252.subtitle: Forget the pain, forget the practice, forget the blisters under your dancing shoes. Your audience is waiting.
1202007252.subtitle_zh: 忘却痛苦，忘却训练，忘却舞鞋里磨出的水泡。你的观众，正翘首以待。
1202007252.text:
Rashida ab Owain, MS, clicks her field recorder on. With it clipped to her bag's strap, this means tapping at her chest. 

The metal-and-glass thing on the ridge taps, with mechanical jerkiness, at its own. 

She scratches her head with her pen. The thing scratches the pointed lower section of its cranium. Its cranium-like structure, Rashida reminds herself.  

The thing is taller than her, shorter than an adult Eliksni. Bipedal, two arms, bilaterally symmetrical. A light bisects its cranium-like structure, its blue-white glow brighter than that of the glass in its middle. She leans forward to get a better look at its contents; again, the thing mirrors her, its fan-like crest catching the light. 

Rashida ducks her head towards her recorder, aware of every small motion she makes. "New discovery needing investigation," she mutters into it. "Mechanical or biomechanical being, suspected sentient. Clear window on the ventral side filled with some glowing matter. Maybe liquid crystal? A power source?" 

Rashida is a mechanical engineer specializing in the design and maintenance of hydroponic systems. She is in no way qualified to initiate contact with a potential second non-human species on Kepler. 

"I need… language specialists. Anthropology. Biomechanics. Programming. Holy Anomaly help us all, I need the evolutionary biologists." 

The thing takes a rocking step closer. Rashida looks it up and down.  

She steps once towards it, mimicking its motion. It points at her; she points first towards it, then towards herself, waiting for its response. 

Rashida needs experts. What she has is herself. 

"Hypothesis, testing, iteration," she murmurs, the mantra calming. "Amen."
1202007252.text_zh:
理学硕士拉希达·阿布·欧文轻点胸前的录音设备，将它别在背包带上启动。 

那个金属与玻璃构成的物体，正以机械生硬的节奏模仿她的动作。 

她用笔挠了挠头。那个物体也抬起尖锐的颅骨下部做出相同举动。拉希达提醒自己，那只是类似颅骨的结构。  

那物体比她高些，又比成年埃里克斯尼族矮小，双足直立，双臂对称。一道蓝白光芒从它的类颅骨中央劈开，比镶嵌在躯干中部的玻璃更耀眼。她凑近观察其中流动的物质，对方立刻同步前倾，扇状头冠折射出细碎光斑。 

拉希达低头凑向录音器，每个细微动作都变得谨慎。“有新发现需紧急调查。”她对着设备低语，“疑似具备感知能力的机械或生物机械体。腹侧透明窗口内充满发光物质，可能是液体水晶？能量源？” 

拉希达是一名机械工程师，专攻水培系统的设计与维护工作。她完全不具备与开普勒上潜在第二非人类物种进行首次接触的资质。 

“我需要…语言学家、人类学家、生物机械专家、程序员。神圣异常点在上，还得有进化生物学家。” 

那物体摇晃着迈近一步。拉希达与它互相打量。  

她朝它迈出一步，模仿它的动作。它指向她；她先是指向它，又指向自己，等待着回应。 

拉希达需要专家。而她现在能依靠的只有自己。 

“假设、验证、迭代，”她低声念着这句安抚人心的咒语，“阿门。”

2973900274.name: Third Iteration
2973900274.subtitle: The first with congruity.
2973900274.text:
Alone in his tent, Louis undresses until he's down to his underclothes and his old man's watch.  

Even now, magnetism is buzzing in his skin, achingly far from Human. (Did the prior two Emissaries feel this way?)  

He misses visiting his mother in summer, in the town whose name he borrowed. He misses fishing with his brother. His sister-in-law's paintings, his nephew's jokes, his niece's smile, the baby who shares his ears. Most of all, he misses returning from the lake for a meal that could only be made in their house, that could only be made by them. No one but the Yeros know the preciousness of walleye ceviche. 

Louis sits with his face in his hands. They are gone, qué Diosito los tenga en su santa gloria, and he is here.  

Grief and eternity ringing in his ears, his eyes lose focus, and briefly, he Sees. 

His niece and nephew are playing in a yard full of fireflies. He hears Ben's laugh intermingling with his own. A loon wails in the distance, and leathery smoke curls into the air. 

Louis bolts to standing.  

A thousand years ago is also right now, and in this infinite heartbeat, his loved ones are dead, and they are also alive. 'Time is not linear,' sing Louis's electrons. 'You will always be with your family on a patio in July.' 

The vision ends, and Louis lets out a long shaky breath, filled with awe. As he does, his feet silently lift off the ground. 

He startles for a moment, then surrenders, a mad grin on his face. There are miracles at intersections. Nine and Human. Dead and alive. Lime and pike.  

He leans forward for his glasses and pants and puts them on in midair, every atom in his body searing neon, and drifts out of his tent into Kepler's indigo night. Light catches on Louis's glasses as he rises, his bare feet a meter from the ground, and he tilts his head toward the stars.
2973900274.text_zh:
路易斯独自在帐篷里褪去衣衫，最后只剩贴身内衣和那块老旧的腕表。  

即便此刻，他肌肤之下仍涌动着磁力般的躁动，与人类相去甚远得令人刺痛。（前两位使者也曾有同样感受吗？）  

他怀念夏日回乡探望母亲的小镇——那个他借用了名字的地方。怀念和兄弟垂钓的时光，怀念嫂子的画作、侄子的俏皮话、侄女的笑靥，还有那个长着和他一样耳朵的婴儿。最令他思念的，是从湖边归来时那顿只有耶罗家才做得出的晚餐，唯有他们才懂得秘制酸橘汁腌碧古鱼的珍贵。 

路易斯双手掩面而坐。他们都不在了，而他却独留人间，愿主让他们的圣洁灵魂得到安息。  

哀恸与永恒在耳畔轰鸣，他的目光逐渐涣散，刹那间，他看见了。 

侄辈们在萤火虫飞舞的院子里嬉戏。本的笑声与他的交织在一起。远处潜鸟哀鸣，皮革气味的炊烟袅袅升起。 

路易斯猛然站起。  

一千年前的时光同时存在于此刻，在这无限延伸的瞬息间，他挚爱的人们已然逝去，却也永远鲜活。“时间并非线性，”路易斯体内的电子在歌唱，“七月露台上的天伦之乐，将与你永恒共存。” 

幻象消散，路易斯颤抖着长呼一口气，眼中仍盈满惊叹。就在这瞬间，他的双脚悄然离地。 

他惊惶片刻，随即释然，脸上绽开狂喜的笑容。奇迹总在交界处诞生——玖与人类，死者与生者，酸橙与长矛。  

他俯身去抓眼镜和长裤，在半空中将它们穿戴妥当，体内的每一颗原子都灼烧成霓虹光芒，随后飘出帐篷，融入开普勒的靛蓝夜色。路易斯悬空而起时星光掠过镜片，赤足离地一米，他仰首望向群星。

970034755.name: Giver's Blessing
970034755.subtitle: Something beyond time.
970034755.text:
The Archon flexes his new claws. How spindly and frail they are. He looks down to examine them and is surprised to see his bottom two arms missing, docked long ago. He can still feel them, though! Thrilling. 

He laughs. The voice that issues forth has the deep resonance of an Archon. He immediately adjusts it to the reedy timbre of a Dreg. 

Next to him is another menial, who glances over suspiciously. They are both bent over an outdated Shank, repaired for the hundredth time. 

"Tell me," the Archon asks in his adopted falsetto, "what do you think of Levaszk? The new Prime Archon?" 

"So that's what you were laughing about," the other Dreg sneers. "His fascination with dark matter is insane. He's turned Aionian." 

The Archon clenches his phantom lower arms, then calms himself. "But what if he's right?" he replies. "What if Levaszk has discovered something in the dark matter?" 

"That buffoon couldn't find his rebreather with all four arms," the Dreg replies. "Now get back to work." 

The Archon picks up an awl from the workbench. "You're wrong," he says in that thin, shrill voice.  

He raises the awl above his head with both arms. "He's discovered something beyond Ether. Beyond time." 

The Archon plunges the awl into the crease between the Dreg's head and thorax plating. The weakness of the strike surprises him. He's forced to stab a dozen more times before the Dreg goes still. 

"Levaszk has the Giver's blessing," he tells the twitching corpse. "He has already ascended."
970034755.text_zh:
执政官活动着他的新爪肢。如此纤细脆弱。低头检视时，他惊觉下方两条手臂早已截除——但幻肢仍在刺痛！这感觉令他战栗。 

他大笑出声，喉间震荡着执政官特有的浑厚共鸣。他立即调整为堕落者士兵特有的尖细声线。 

身旁的杂役投来怀疑的目光。他们正共同检修那台返修过上百次的破旧堕落者侦察机。 

“说说看，”执政官用伪装的高音问道，“你觉得新任首席执政官列瓦兹克如何？” 

“原来你在笑这个。”另一名堕落者士兵嗤之以鼻，“他对暗物质的痴迷实在疯狂，简直就是变成了艾昂人。” 

执政官攥紧不存在的下臂，强压怒火。“但如果他是对的呢？”他答道。“要是列瓦兹克真在暗物质中发现了什么？” 

“那蠢货就算伸出四臂也找不着自己的呼吸器。”堕落者士兵讥讽道，“赶紧干活。” 

执政官从工作台抄起锥子。“你错了。”他用那尖细的声音说道。  

他双手高举锥子过头顶。“他发现的东西超越了乙太，超越了时间。” 

执政官将锥子刺入堕落者士兵头部与胸甲连接的缝隙。这一击的软弱令他吃惊。他又捅了十几下，堕落者士兵才停止动弹。 

“列瓦兹克得到了赐予者的祝福，”他对着抽搐的尸体说道，“他已经飞升了。”

4124362340.name: Agape
4124362340.subtitle: Boundless, without conditions.
4124362340.text:
Rebecca decided she would need to live forever the first time she fell in love.  

She was eight and had just learned what a horse was. She'd never seen anything like it—muscle and glistening hide, and the long toss of a mane over a curved neck. She had been told she was too young to learn to ride—experienced the profound frustration of not being there yet. And if there was such a thing as too young, then there was such a thing as too old. It worried her when she had barely begun to learn about worry. 

How to live forever? 

Rebecca decided again she would need to live forever, that second time she fell in love. Sixteen, and a book that spun out a tale like no other, golden words to consume her mind and light up her heart. How long did it take to tell a story like that? How long to tell ten, or a hundred, more? How could anyone have all the time it would take to pour forth every ounce of the love in their heart? 

She fell in love a hundred more times, again and again. Why shouldn't she? She had too much yearning in her to keep herself to just one thing. She gathered loves like a magpie, greedy for every shining joy—shellfish and magnets, gardens and penicillin, lace and the circuit-song of quantum computing.  

Stardust.  

Rebecca gazed into the heart of the universe and all she could do was love it boundlessly—this thing to which she was barely a speck, but had made her and all her love. She did not expect to be loved in return. Indeed, she expected nothing from it, save an understanding that would unfold to her if she gave it time.  

Time—of which there was never enough. 

She was decades older and a world away from home when she found time. It came to her veiled in mathematics like glittering spiderwebs, laws of physics bent aside under the force of their own being, this thing that she had crossed the stars to study. The dark mirror by which she meant to understand her true love. 

She spun it like starlight on a drop-spindle, her own self the counterweight, rising, rising—the twist moving from hand to spindle, flesh to dark matter.  

Rebecca would love this universe until it unraveled, until there was nothing left in it to understand, no room remaining in the wet matter of her brain and the red pound of her heart. And was that not the highest duty of love—to understand better than any other?
4124362340.text_zh:
丽贝卡初次坠入爱河时便决心永生。  

那年她八岁，刚认识马这种生物。她从未见过如此存在——肌肉在油亮皮毛下起伏，鬃毛沿着优美颈线飞扬。大人们说她年纪太小还不能学骑马，她第一次体会到“未达时机”的深切挫败。既然有“太小”之说，自然也存在“太老”。这个认知让她忧心忡忡，尽管那时她连忧虑为何物都才刚刚知晓。 

如何才能永生？ 

十六岁再度坠入爱河时，丽贝卡再次下决心她需要永生。那本奇书编织出摄人心魄的故事，鎏金文字吞噬神思，点燃心火。要耗费多少光阴才能写出这般杰作？要多少岁月才能讲述十个、百个，甚至更多这样的传奇？凡人如何能有足够时间倾尽心中汹涌的爱意？ 

她一次次地坠入爱河，百次千回。何乐不为？她满腔热望岂能困于单一事物。她如喜鹊般贪婪收集每份闪耀的欢愉——贝类与磁石，花园与青霉素，蕾丝与量子计算的电路之歌。  

星尘。  

丽贝卡凝望着宇宙核心，所能做的唯有无尽地爱着它——这个视她如尘埃却孕育了她与她全部热忱的造物。她不曾期望得到爱的回报。事实上，除了一份终将随时间显现的领悟外，她别无奢求。  

时间——永远匮乏的时间。 

当她终于寻得时间时，已离家数十载，远隔星河。那领悟裹挟着数学的轻纱降临，如闪烁蛛网，物理法则在其存在之力下弯折——这竟是她穿越群星所求索之物。那面用以洞悉真爱的暗镜。 

她将其纺作纺锤上的星光，以自身为配重不断攀升、攀升——捻转从指尖传向纺锤，血肉融进暗物质。  

丽贝卡会爱这宇宙直至其分崩离析，直至再无奥秘可解，直至她湿润的脑髓与怦跳的心脏再容不下分毫。而这，岂非爱的至高使命——比任何人都更透彻地理解？

1079872540.name: Ulterior Observation
1079872540.subtitle: A triptych with three different images. Three different mediums. Three different artists.
1079872540.subtitle_zh: 一幅三联画，涵盖三种不同图像、三种不同媒介、出自三位不同艺术家之手。

3813721211.name: Last Thursday
3813721211.subtitle: Even calendars end.
3813721211.text:
Naismith edges forward, the darkness broken only by the glow of his headlamp, one hand on the wall to his right. Sheets of slime mold squeak under his boots. Water trickles loudly through narrow channels in the rock. 

Kepler's structure is riddled with canyons and caverns, still largely unexplored. All the geologists are desperately curious about them. He'll get a thesis out of this for sure. 

Only it's a lot easier to make plans than it is to inch through narrow passages so deep that ground radar couldn't map them. 

Especially when Naismith doesn't know what's making the scraping sounds behind him. 

"We have no record of any fauna down here large enough to harm someone," he reassures himself, his voice thin in the wavering light. 

The scraping gets louder. Skkkrrch-skrrch, it says, light and quick. 

Skrrrrrch. Skrch. 

Naismith pushes forward, but it's slower than he wants to, as though he's slogging through water. As though time is reluctant to pass. 

Skkkkkrrrrrrrrrchhhhh.  

The scraping sound is elongated, distorted—as if played back on a recording at half speed without pitch correction. 

Naismith breaks into a painfully slow, shuffling run. 

The narrow corridor widens abruptly just as an unseen rock catches his feet. Naismith trips, falls, smacks his head against the ground. He lifts his eyes and gazes into absolute blackness. 

It's a long moment before he understands that something isn't wrong with his vision: his headlamp is broken. It's a much shorter moment before he realizes how badly he's screwed. 

Naismith scrambles to his feet, reaching out blindly. No wall at his side to guide his way back. No light. No way to know where he is. 

Behind him, drawing closer and closer, pitch deepening into the infinite like the drop of a continental shelf… 

Skkkrchhhhhhhhhhhhh. 

In the dark, Naismith screams.
3813721211.text_zh:
奈史密斯向前挪动，四周的黑暗唯有他头灯的光芒刺破，他一只手紧贴着右侧岩壁。靴子踩过成片的黏菌，发出吱呀声响。水流在岩缝狭窄的沟槽间淙鸣。 

开普勒的地质结构布满峡谷与洞窟，至今仍有多数区域未被勘探。所有地质学家都对这片区域充满狂热的好奇。他肯定能凭此写篇优秀论文。 

只不过制定计划远比在地质雷达都无法测绘的深邃窄道里匍匐前行要轻松得多。 

尤其是当奈史密斯听见身后传来不明刮擦声的时候。 

“没有记录显示这里存在足以伤人的大型生物。”他自我安慰道，颤抖的光圈里嗓音发虚。 

刮擦声愈发清晰。嘶咔-嘶咔，轻快急促。 

嘶咔。咔。 

奈史密斯加速前进，动作却比预期迟缓，仿佛在深水中跋涉。仿佛连时间都不愿流逝。 

嘶——咔——  

刮擦声被拉长扭曲，如同半速播放却未修正音调的录音。 

奈史密斯跌跌撞撞地开始奔跑，步伐迟缓得令人揪心。 

狭窄的甬道突然开阔时，一块未被看见的岩石绊住了他的脚。他重重摔倒，头颅撞击地面发出闷响。待他抬起眼睛，视野里只剩下纯粹的黑暗。 

他花了很长时间才明白不是视力出了问题：头灯坏了。而他意识到处境危急所用的时间则短的多。 

奈史密斯手脚并用爬起来，在黑暗中胡乱摸索。身侧没有墙壁指引退路，没有光源，没有办法知道他在哪里。 

在他身后，如大陆架陡然陷落般深邃无底的漆黑正不断迫近… 

嘶咔咔咔咔。 

在黑暗中，奈史密斯发出了尖叫。

1674692344.name: Sublimation
1674692344.subtitle: A voice not quite your own.
1674692344.text:
Illiiks could feel his flesh peeling away from the inside of his carapace. He stretched his limbs with a dry, gristly crackle. The constant pain of Ether deprivation was now a dull roar. He willed himself back into the present, where the Prime Archon addressed his House from atop the ruins of their once-Ketch. 

"…No need for the ways of the past. The shackles of Kiir-Ohn. Here, the Giver has gifted us something beyond nourishment for our bodies. It offers ascension of the spirit." 

Is nourishment not enough? Illiiks thought. Are our bodies worthless? At least we never starved under Szuurin-kel.  

"Nor did we flourish," the Prime Archon bellowed, looking directly at Illiiks. The Dreg recoiled. Had he heard that?  

"For an eon in the Drift, survival was enough. It was all," the Archon continued, turning his attention back to the larger gathering. "And survival became our way. But a new era approaches: an age of revival. For both the Giver and our House." 

The Prime Archon held aloft a glass cannister, attached to a large rebreather. It once held shining white Ether. Now it brimmed with a dimly glowing vegetal sludge: the dark matter. 

"Accept the Giver, and you will become more than a survivor. More than Eliksni."  

Later, as Illiiks lay convulsing on the ground, phosphorescent blisters bubbling up through the joints in his carapace, he felt the dark matter surge through him. Mindless. Turbid. Powerful. His hunger unsated but forgotten.  

See? Illiiks thought, in a voice not quite his own. Take what is Given, and ascend.
1674692344.text_zh:
伊利克斯能感觉到甲壳内层的血肉正在剥离。他伸展肢体时，外壳发出干涩的碎裂声。乙太匮乏带来的持续疼痛已化作沉闷轰鸣。他强迫自己集中精神，此刻首席执政官正站在他们氏族双桅船的残骸上发表演说。 

“…不必再遵循旧日之道，不必再受基尔-奥恩的枷锁禁锢。在此，赐予者馈赠我们的不仅是肉体的养料，更是灵魂的升华。” 

养料难道不够吗？伊利克斯暗想。我们的躯体就毫无价值？至少苏林-凯尔统治时期我们从未挨饿。  

“但也从未繁荣。”首席执政官突然直视伊利克斯吼道。这名堕落者士兵吓得一缩。执政官竟能听见他的心思？  

“在大漂流纪元，生存即是全部，是唯一的意义。”执政官转回身继续向集会群众宣讲，“生存曾是我们的唯一法则。但新时代即将来临，一个属于赐予者与我们氏族的复兴时代。” 

首席执政官高举连接着大型呼吸器的玻璃罐。曾经盛放闪耀白光的乙太物质，此刻却充盈着幽暗发光的植物状淤积物：暗物质。 

“接受赐予者，你将不再只是幸存者。不再只是埃里克斯尼族。”  

后来，当伊利克斯抽搐着倒在地上时，甲壳关节处泛起荧光的脓疱，他感受到暗物质在体内奔涌。无意识、浑浊而强大。饥饿感未被满足却已遗忘。  

瞧见了吗？伊利克斯用不属于自己的声音想着，接受馈赠，即可升华。

367772693.name: Precipial
367772693.subtitle: The best night of your life is yet to come.
367772693.subtitle_zh: 你人生中最美好的夜晚尚未到来。
367772693.text:
He doesn't exactly have the text of his thesis on hand anymore. It's stuck on one of the servers in the Central Academy, and the network connection is… poor. Nonexistent, one might say. But it's fine! Cadogan knows his own work backward and forward at this point. He knows he can hold something symbolic of the work, instead of a copy of the thesis. "Do you think a gyroscope would be appropriate?" he asks his advisor, fidgeting with nothing to hold. "I could rig one pretty easily…" 

"Easy," she tells him. "There's precedent for declaring work relevant enough for Kepler itself to serve as symbol, and you've studied the manipulation of gravity itself, such as is generated by a planetary body… You're prepared for this, Cadogan." 

He's not sure he believes her, and so goes off to see what kind of a scale model he can make out of available scraps. The—siege? Occupation?—is as boring as it is nerve-wracking, and it eases his hands and heart to have something to do.  

Hopefully they can actually hold the ceremony. The amphitheater seems so far away from here. He knows how it's supposed to be: The defense will be somber and thorough, a questioning from the Dean herself to interrogate his ideas—and then, when he has held forth to satisfaction, she will smile at him.  

Then the feast will begin, and as sober reflection turns to triumph and elation, the Dean will gift him the first of his tools as a scientist grown, crafted from the progenitor ship. Something to carry with him always. 

Cadogan imagines the weight it will have in his hands, the joy of being received by his peers amid music and dancing and the majestic spin of the stars in the sky. 

He's not there yet, he reminds himself, biting his lip. Waiting even longer would be torture. He hopes the strangers can help.
367772693.text_zh:
他手头早已没有论文文稿。资料全留在中央学院的服务器里，而网络连接…很差。或者说根本不存在。但没关系！卡多根对自己的研究了如指掌。他知道可以用象征物代替论文副本。“您觉得陀螺仪合适吗？”他摆弄着空荡荡的双手询问导师，“我可以临时组装一个…” 

“放轻松。”她告诉他道，“早有先例认定研究本身若足够重要，连开普勒都能作为象征——而你钻研的正是行星级天体重力操控…你准备好了，卡多根。” 

他并不确信，于是去找可用废料制作比例模型。这场——围城？占领？——既令人神经紧绷又无聊透顶，有事情做反而能让双手和心灵平静些。  

但愿他们真能举行仪式。圆形剧场仿佛远在天边。他清楚流程：答辩需庄重严谨，院长本人将质询他的理论——待他充分阐述后，她会向他微笑。  

接着盛宴开始，当肃穆的沉思化为胜利的狂喜，院长会赠予他成年科学家的第一件工具，用先祖飞船残骸打造的器物。永远随身携带的珍宝。 

卡多根想象着那物件在掌心的分量，在音乐舞蹈与浩瀚星旋中被同侪接纳的欢欣。 

还没到那步，他咬着嘴唇提醒自己。继续等待无异于酷刑。他希望那些陌生人能帮上忙。

2838279629.name: Mercury-A
2838279629.subtitle: "Proof of good faith is key to cooperation and, ultimately, friendship." —William Moffat, DEO Director
2838279629.subtitle_zh: “展现诚意是合作乃至友谊的关键。”——对外观察部主任，威廉·莫法特
2838279629.text:
"I never had it, but I'm fairly sure ramen existed before the Golden Age," Lodi nods, chopsticks unsteady in his hand. "I should cook for you sometime. What… food… still exists?" 

The Guardian leans in to answer, but Ghost pipes up, "Oh, good! Saint is here!" 

Lodi quickly stands up from the counter to greet him. He has heard so much. "Mr. Saint, a pleasure to meet you." 

He glances to the Guardian for an introduction, but is only met with a parting wave and a wiggle from Ghost as they walk away. 

The Titan crushes his fingers in an enthusiastic handshake, a box in his other wide palm. "Emissary! The pleasure is all mine!" 

Lodi freezes.  

He knows that accent from a thousand tapped phonelines and from behind a dozen two-way mirrors. He forces his face still. Wills his pulse to quiet. 

"Where are you from?" Lodi says in cautious Russian. 

"Ah! Finally!" Saint barks the same language in fluent staccato. "At last, someone to talk to!" And without warning, Lodi's hand is crushed in a second enthusiastic handshake. 

"Where are my manners? Here, a housewarming gift." 

Buzzing with nerves, the Emissary opens the package. He blinks; sparkling before him is a matching set of tasteful champagne flutes, the most timeless of housewarming gifts 

The fuel for his fears had been extinguished for centuries. His enemy is an apocalypse away. 

Lodi holds the box close. He looks at Saint directly. "This was a thoughtful gift. Thank you for your hospitality." His Russian flows easier this time, like an old friend. 

"You are most welcome!" He pauses, looking him over, and adds, "Are you all right?" 

Lodi's stomach flips over. He hunts for the right phrase and finds it arrive, gently, in his mind, "In my time, our people were… in conflict."

Saint barks a laugh and swings a leg over a chair. "Who won?" 

The earnestness of the question is so absurd that Lodi shrugs, feeling gravity lighten on his shoulders.  

"No idea," he smiles.
2838279629.text_zh:
“虽然没吃过，但我很确定拉面在黄金时代之前就存在了。”洛迪点点头，手中的筷子微微发颤。“有机会给你们露一手。现在…还有哪些食物…存在？” 

守护者倾身准备回答，但机灵抢先说道：“哦，太好了！圣人来了！” 

洛迪立即从柜台起身相迎。他早已久仰大名。“圣人先生，很荣幸和你见面。” 

他望向守护者期待引荐，却只得到告别的挥手和机灵扭动着远去的背影。 

泰坦用力握住他的手热情摇晃，另一只宽大的手掌托着一个盒子。“使者！是我的荣幸才对！” 

洛迪瞬间僵住。  

他从千百条监听线路与十几面双向镜后早已熟悉这口音。他强压下脸上的表情，努力让心跳平静下来。 

“你来自哪里？”洛迪用俄语谨慎发问。 

“哈！终于！"圣人嚷起同一种语言，流利而顿挫分明地回应道。“总算有人能和我聊聊了！”话音未落，洛迪的手再次被热情地握住。 

“我真是失礼。给，送你的乔迁礼物。” 

使者神经紧绷地拆开礼盒。他眨了眨眼；眼前赫然是一对典雅相称的香槟杯，堪称最经典的温居贺礼。 

他的恐惧之源，几百年前就已烟消云散。他的敌人，距离他有一次世界末日那么远。 

洛迪紧紧抱着盒子，直视着圣人的眼睛。“这份礼物很贴心，谢谢你的热情。”这次，他的俄语说得流畅许多，如同老友交谈。 

“客气什么！”圣人停顿了一下，打量了他一番，然后说道，“你没事吧？” 

洛迪的胃一阵翻腾。他思索着合适的措辞，一句回答悄然浮现在脑海，“在我那个时代，你我双方…是敌对的。”

圣人大笑着一脚搭上椅子。“谁赢了？” 

这一本正经的疑问荒谬得让洛迪不禁耸了耸肩，感觉肩上的重力都减轻了几分。  

“不知道。”他微笑着回答。

190747610.name: Qua Nilus II
190747610.subtitle: There's always a market.
190747610.text:
Omar Saint Croix descended a long flight of concrete steps into a heavily fortified bunker beneath the Last City. Two armed Redjacks flanked the bottom of the stairway. A hard, wiry man with a scraggly beard perched on a stool behind a glass case filled with knives.  

"Whaddaya looking for?" he asked.   

Omar glanced around. The walls of the bunker were lined top to bottom with hundreds of weapons: a beat-up Rat King sidearm, an immaculately refurbished Sweet Business auto, and an original-issue Two-Tailed Fox rocket launcher. Even a Telesto, with a big Do Not Touch sign hung over it.  

"Uh, an SMG," Omar replied in a street drawl honed by years of undercover ops. "Something nasty-lookin'." 

"Trying to make an impression?" 

"Gotta let 'em know I mean business." 

The arms dealer nodded. He pulled a compact submachine gun off a nearby rack, checked the chamber, and handed it to Omar. 

"Don't recognize it," Omar said mildly. 

"Brand new. The alien-lovers in the Tower just got 'em," the dealer smirked. "Piggies always trying to keep power out of the hands of the people. You know how it is. But we got our ways." 

"They're not so bad," Omar said, pretending to examine the shotgun. "Took down Ghaul, didn't they?" 

"And why was he here in the first place? Trying to steal that piece of junk Traveler. The only reason they stopped him was to protect their own asses. Their immortality," the dealer sneered. 

Omar decided not to press. "I guess you got a point. No Traveler, no Ghaul." 

"No Pyramids, no damn Vex sieges," the peddler ranted. "Hell, even the Fallen would be back wherever the hell they came from. Filthy parasites. We gotta be ready." 

"Ready for what?" 

"For us regular people to take this damn City back. The Tower thinks they own us. But I'll tell ya something: they got a hard lesson coming."
190747610.text_zh:
奥马尔·圣克鲁瓦沿着长长的混凝土台阶下行，深入圣城下的一座重兵把守的掩体。两名全副武装的红桃杰克把守着楼梯底部。一个瘦削精悍、胡子拉碴的男人坐在玻璃陈列柜后的高脚凳上，柜里摆满各式刀具。  

“找啥家伙？”他问道。   

奥马尔环顾四周。掩体墙壁从上到下挂满数百件武器：一把破旧的“鼠王”手枪，一支保养如新的“糖果生意”自动步枪，还有原厂“双尾狐”火箭发射器。甚至有把“土卫十三”悬在墙上，上方挂着“严禁触碰”的警示牌。  

“呃，要把微型冲锋枪，”奥马尔用多年卧底生涯磨炼出的街头腔调答道，“要看起来够凶的。” 

“打算镇场子？” 

“得让他们知道我不是闹着玩的。” 

军火贩子点点头，从架子上取下一把紧凑型微型冲锋枪，检查完弹膛后递给奥马尔。 

“没见过这型号。”奥马尔故作平淡。 

“全新货色。高塔里那些外星人舔狗刚搞到手的。”贩子咧嘴一笑，“那些猪猡总是想把力量攥在自己手里。你懂的。但我们自有门路。” 

“他们也没那么糟吧？”奥马尔假装端详着霰弹枪，“他们不是干掉了盖欧吗？” 

“那混蛋为啥会来这儿？不就是为了偷那个破烂旅行者！那群人阻止他也只是为了自保——保住他们的永生不死。”贩子嗤之以鼻。 

奥马尔决定迁就他。“说得也是。没有旅行者，就没有盖欧。” 

“没有金字塔，就没有那些该死的Vex围攻！”贩子叫嚷道。“要我说，连那些堕落者都会滚回他们的老窝。肮脏的寄生虫。我们得做好准备。” 

“准备什么？” 

“准备让普通人夺回这座该死的圣城！高塔以为能永远骑在我们头上。但我告诉你——他们迟早要栽大跟头。”

2111625436.name: Aurora Dawn
2111625436.subtitle: "The prospect of a future is something we have to keep in mind."
2111625436.subtitle_zh: “要以未来为重，这一点我们应当牢记在心。”
2111625436.text:
"H-hello?" Saint-14 asked, poking his head into the dimly lit workshop. No one answered.  

He stepped over a crate in the doorway and was forced to push past a workbench turned on its side to enter the room.  

"Ana?"  

Still nothing. 

Cables hung like cobwebs from above, catching against his helmet. He brushed them away and barely missed a pile of stepper motors before tripping on an open container, sending hardware cascading across the shop floor. 

"Whatcha doing down there?" Ana said, suddenly positioned over him. 

"I—that is—well, I was looking for you," he sputtered, standing. 

"In a bucket of batteries?" she asked with a wink and brushed the mess aside with her foot. 

"You missed tea," Saint replied carefully. "Again." 

"Oh! I am so, so sorry. I'll make it up to you later this week, I promise." 

"You said that last time." 

She patted him on the shoulder. "I know, I know. But this time, I mean it." 

"Osiris knew you might say that. But he once told you—" 

"I haven't forgotten. Here, hold this, will you?"  

She thrust an empty bag into his hands, then filled it with circuit boards and pressure sensors. 

"Ana… I'm worried." 

She hefted containers of more hardware onto his shoulders. "About Osiris? A prophecy? The City, or …?" Her voice trailed off as she disappeared outside.  

"Ana!" Saint huffed and puffed. He struggled for several minutes, desperately attempting to catch up to her as she meandered through the streets of the City.  

"I am worried about you," he panted. He finally stopped in front of Ana, careful to balance the load in his arms.  

She sighed. "I know. It… hurts like hell that Red's gone… It always will. But I've decided to focus on something just as important as my feelings." 

She motioned for Saint to turn around, and he found himself standing beside Niik and Itzelas before a crowd of eager children of all ages, including a tiny Eliksni that clung to the leg of one of Caiatl's warriors.  

"Someone needs to nurture the next generation of scientific minds. Right, Niik?" Ana finished. 

Niik nodded. "Yes. The ropes don't teach themselves linear algebra." 

Ana grinned. "OK, who's ready to make some robots dance?" she called out. Saint smiled softly as a cheer went up from the children.
2111625436.text_zh:
“有、有人在吗？”圣人14号探头走进昏暗的工作间，无人应答。  

他跨过门廊的板条箱，不得不侧身推开一张翻倒的工作台才挤进房间。  

“阿娜？”  

依然寂静无声。 

电缆像蛛网般从天花板上垂落，勾住他的头盔。他挥手拨开线缆，刚躲过一堆步进电机，又被敞开的零件箱绊倒，五金件哗啦啦撒了满地。 

“你趴地上找什么呢？”阿娜的声音突然从头顶传来。 

“我——那个——其实在找你。”他慌忙起身，说话都结巴起来。 

“在电池堆里找？”她眨眨眼问道，用脚拨开那堆零件。 

“你错过了下午茶，”圣人谨慎地开口，“又一次的。” 

“天！我真的很抱歉。这周末一定补偿你，我保证。” 

“上次你也是这么说的。” 

她拍拍他的肩头。“知道啦知道啦，但这次是认真的。” 

“奥斯里斯早料到你会这么说。但他曾经告诉过你——” 

“我没忘。来，拿着这个，好不？”  

她把空工具袋塞进他手中，接着往里面填满了电路板和压力传感器。 

“阿娜…我很担心。” 

她又把几箱零件摞在他肩上。“担心奥斯里斯？某个预言？圣城？还是…？”她走到门外，话音渐渐消失。  

“阿娜！”圣人气喘吁吁地喊道。他挣扎了好几分钟，拼命想要追上在圣城里大街小巷中漫步的她。  

“我担心的是你。”他喘着粗气说道。他终于在阿娜面前停了下来，小心平衡着怀中的重物。  

她叹了口气。“我知道。红老大走了…这真的让我痛不欲生…永远都是。但我已经决定把精力放在与这份痛苦同等重要的事情上。” 

她示意圣人转身——他发现自己此刻正站在妮可和伊泽拉斯身旁，面前簇拥着各个年龄层的热切孩童，其中还有个小个子埃里克斯尼族正抓着一名查厄托战士的腿甲。  

“总得有人培育下一代科学人才。对吧，妮可？”阿娜把话说完。 

妮可点头。“没错。绳索可不会自己教线性代数。” 

阿娜咧嘴一笑。“好了，谁想看机器人跳舞？”她高声问道。在孩子们的欢呼声中，圣人露出了温柔的笑容。

3926153598.name: Boomslang-4fr
3926153598.subtitle: T(1/2)
3926153598.text:
"How's it going with the foundry reps?" Marc asked casually. 

"It's going well," Devrim replied. "The Tex Mechanica chap is a total pillock. But the rest of them are surprisingly receptive. I think this business in the Oort Cloud has them on edge." 

Devrim continued ferrying dishes and silverware from the kitchen to the balcony, where he set a small table for two.  

"They're lucky to have you. How much longer do you think you'll be in the City?" Marc called out from the kitchen.  

Devrim parsed his response carefully. Years of long-distance partnership had taught him that there was always a question behind the question. 

"At least another six weeks," he replied. His eyes traveled from the quiet side street below to the Tower, which loomed over the City's residential quarters. "Until they've compiled all the data from the Guardian's combat reports." 

"Wow!" Marc exclaimed, emerging from the apartment with a side salad in one hand and linguine arrabbiata in the other. "That's the longest you've been home in dog's years." 

"Since just after the Red War," Devrim agreed, quietly working the cork from the bottle of sparkling wine. 

"I know better than to get used to it, though," Marc quipped. "You'll be itching to run back to the front soon enough." 

"Please don't start," Devrim sighed. Marc pretended not to hear. 

"So, I'll just have to enjoy you while I can," Marc said with resolute cheer. He sat down and held out his champagne glass. Devrim poured. 

Marc lifted his glass. "To us." 

Devrim met his eyes. In them, he saw a well of grief over all the years they had lost. The prime of their lives spent apart. Their youth wasted by missed opportunities. 

But he also saw hope for the fleeting time that remained. Faith that their love would endure through their grim winter years. To the end. 

"To us," Devrim replied. "Always."
3926153598.text_zh:
“和铸造厂代表的谈判进行得怎么样了？”马库漫不经心地问道。 

“进行得很顺利。”德弗里姆回答道，“特克斯机械的那个家伙真是个蠢货，不过其他人倒出乎意料地配合。我觉得奥尔特云那件事让他们有些紧张。” 

德弗里姆继续从厨房往阳台上端盘子、银器和餐具，他在那里摆了一张小桌子，足够两个人用餐。  

“他们有你真是幸运。你觉得你还会在圣城里待多久？”马库的声音从厨房里传来。  

德弗里姆仔细斟酌着答话。多年的异地相守让他明白，每个问题背后都藏着另一重诘问。 

“至少还要六周。”他回答道。他的目光从楼下安静的街道扫向高耸于圣城住宅区上空的高塔。“等他们把守护者的战斗报告数据都整理完。” 

“哇！”马库惊叹道，一手端着配菜沙拉，一手托着辣味番茄意面走出套间，“这是你多年以来在家时间最长的一次。” 

“从猩红战争结束那阵算起还真是。”德弗里姆附和道，同时安静地拔着起泡酒的瓶塞。 

“不过我还没天真到会习惯这种日子。”马库打趣道，“要不了多久，你准会坐立不安地想回前线。” 

“别又开始了。”德弗里姆叹了口气。马库假装没听见。 

“所以呢，我得趁现在好好享受和你在一起的时光。”马库坚定而欢快地说道。他坐了下来，举起香槟杯。德弗里姆给他倒上酒。 

马库举起酒杯。“敬我们。” 

德弗里姆迎上他的目光。在那双眼睛里，他看到了翻涌的哀伤，为他们那些不复存在的时光。为他们那些分隔两地消磨的盛年。为他们那些因错失良机虚掷的青春。 

但他也看见了对所剩无几光阴的希冀，相信这份爱能挺过人生寒冬的信念。直至终点。 

“敬我们，”德弗里姆回应道，“一如既往。”

4167538387.name: Oort Explorer JS-8
4167538387.subtitle: "We're still catching up with each other after sixty-one years' silence. We'll get there." –Ikora Rey
4167538387.subtitle_zh: “六十一年互无音讯后，我们仍在重新了解彼此。总会好起来的。”——艾可拉·蕾伊
4167538387.text:
Ikora paces at Lodi's side on their way to the local settlement, Ophiuchus silent and wary at her shoulder. Green wisps float around their ankles, tugged by unseen currents. 

Lodi continually looks at her in short little bursts, as if he's sipping too-hot coffee. Scared to burn his tongue. Kepler is a hard spot for a mortal from Earth to have been summoned to; the anxiety must be wearing on him. 

Eventually, the corners of his eyes crinkle in a warm smile. 

"Well, Ms. Rey, I've gotten your name, but I've been rude when it comes to your floating friend here." 

Ikora holds out her palm; Ophiuchus lands on it lightly as a falling leaf. The introductions are made. 

"I'm very pleased to meet you, Mr. Ophiuchus," Lodi says. "Have you two worked together long?" 

Ikora can't help but smile at his gracious way of asking her age. "Oh, we've been together for dozens of lifetimes. I'm sure Ophiuchus could tell you precisely how many times he's brought me back from death." 

Lodi looks at her with poorly hidden concern. It can be hard for mortals to reckon with Guardian lifespans. 

"And how often do you die?" 

"Much less often than I used to," she assures him. "Though I like to think my record was fairly good, even in the field." 

Ophiuchus flips his shell sarcastically at her. He remembers their Crucible days well. 

"Well, I hope it's been a positive career change." 

Ikora folds her hands behind her back. She looks up from the rocky ground to the alien sky above it. The beginnings of a smile tug decorously at the corner of her mouth.

"I wouldn't trade it for the world."
4167538387.text_zh:
艾可拉与洛迪在前往当地聚居地的路上并肩而行，蛇夫座沉默而警觉地悬浮在她肩头。绿色光雾缠绕在他们脚踝，被无形的气流牵引着。 

洛迪时不时地快速瞥视她，像在啜饮过烫的咖啡，生怕烫伤舌头。开普勒对地球凡人而言本就是个艰难的降临之地，这种焦虑想必正折磨着他。 

终于，他眼角漾起温煦笑意。 

“蕾伊女士，我已经知道了您的名字，却怠慢了您这位漂浮的同伴。” 

艾可拉摊开手掌，蛇夫座如落叶般轻盈降下。双方就此相识。 

“蛇夫座先生，很高兴认识你。”洛迪说道，“你们二位一起共事很久了吗？” 

艾可拉不禁莞尔——他探问年龄的方式是如此地得体。“我们相伴了数十世轮回。蛇夫座肯定能精确说出他复活我的次数。” 

洛迪眼中闪过掩不住的忧虑，凡人总是难以理解守护者的寿命。 

“那您多久会…经历一次死亡？” 

“比早年少多了。”她宽慰道，“虽然我觉得就算在战场上，我的记录也相当不错。” 

蛇夫座讥诮地翻转了下机壳。他可清楚记得他们在熔炉竞技场的峥嵘岁月。 

“嗯，我希望那次职业转型让你感到满意。” 

艾可拉将双手背在身后。当目光从崎岖地面移向异星天穹时，一抹克制的笑意悄然攀上她的嘴角。

“再满意不过了。”

83852278.text:
The Phone in the "containment office" rang. 

     The door wasn't supposed to be open. 

          That phone had never rung before.  

               It had never been answered before. 

                    It had never been connected before. It was. 

                         Sent clarion-call a tone that rippled down the line. 

                              Lodi was the first to feel static in his blood. 

                                   A coin had fallen through, a dial cycled. 

                                        It rang like choked breath drowning. 

                            He Answers. 

There is white and gold plastic in his hand. 

There is his hand and there is plastic, and they are one. 

There is flesh on the line. Entwined with copper. 

There is a wail, like a reaching signal. Chords taut, like cable. 

There is a pupil in each eye, bisected, and bisected again, to see the breadth of probability. 

There is a man in a mirror of black ink. Words yet spoken and spoken already. 

There is a corpse wrapped in flowing iron and cold clay. Decay is decay is decay. 

There is a globe of life and wash beneath, falling, ripping out inversely. 

There are the viscera of unmaking, hand-in-hand with the awareness of knowing. 

There is a gasp of pain ringing in newborn cry. 

                            He Answers. 

                         There will be a death and rebirth. Rupture and rapture. 

                      There will be an answer before the question.   

                   There will be effect before cause.
83852278.text_zh:
“收容室”里的电话响了。 

     这门本不该开着。 

          那电话从未响过。  

               它从未被接听过。 

                    它从未被接通过。它现在通了。 

                         它发出嘹亮鸣响，声波沿线路震颤而下。 

                              洛迪最先感受到了血液中的静电。 

                                   一枚硬币穿透而来，转盘循环拨动。 

                                        铃声如同溺毙的窒息之喘。 

                            他接听了电话。 

他手中握着白与金的塑料。 

他的手与那塑料融为一体。 

线路上有血肉。缠着铜丝。 

哀嚎如延伸信号。琴弦紧绷似电缆。 

每只眼里的瞳孔皆被分割，再分割，以窥视概率之广。 

黑墨水镜中映出一个人影。未言之语与已言之辞并存。 

一具裹着流动铁与冷黏土的尸体。腐朽即腐朽即腐朽。 

生命之球与下方冲刷的洪流，逆向坠落，撕扯剥离。 

解体的脏腑与认知的觉醒携手同行。 

痛苦的喘息在新生的啼哭中回荡。 

                            他接听了电话。 

                         死亡与重生将临。断裂与狂喜。 

                      答案先于问题。   

                   果先于因。

1736135946.text:
"Lost? Lost how, exactly?" Spider growled. 

Arrha kept his head bowed, hiding gladly behind the obscurity of his helmet. He knew that even the slightest show of insubordination could send his employer into a cold fury.  

"Ambushed during the exchange on Mars," the Associate explained. "The last transmission confirmed delivery. A dozen prototypes with verified serial numbers." 

"And?" Spider pulled up a foundry spec of the weapons in question: compact Pulse Rifles powered by experimental ammunition. He had paid a premium for classified information from the foundry's research division. Had they double-crossed him? 

"After the buyer left, the comms link went dark," Arrha explained. "I dispatched scavs, and they found the bodies. Looks like Torch Hammers, Line Rifles, and Slug Rifles did the work. They scuttled the ship but left the scrap." 

"So it's true," Spider mused quietly. 

The crime lord's apparent calm disquieted Arrha. Such deliberation usually preceded a drastic move that would undoubtedly endanger them all.  

The Spider did not disappoint. 

"Load my Ketch," he declared. "We're headed to Mars." 

"My Baron," Arrha blurted out unadvisedly, "let me handle this matter. I'll track down the shipment and the thieves." 

"Of course you will," Spider replied. "On pain of docking." 

"But this is bigger than one shipment. It confirms what I've been hearing of an emerging market on the Martian frontier. One with well-funded new players… and no regulatory oversight. A bloodbath in the making." 

"Now get my Ketch!" he snapped. "We're already late."
1736135946.text_zh:
“丢了？怎么丢的？”蛛王咆哮道。 

阿尔拉低着头，庆幸能躲在头盔的遮蔽下。他知道哪怕是最细微的不服从，也有可能招来这位雇主的冰冷怒意。  

 “在火星上交易时遭到了伏击，”这名手下解释道，“最后一次通讯确认了交付。十几件带有验证序列号的原型。” 

“然后呢？”蛛王调出那款武器的铸造厂蓝图：实验弹药驱动的紧凑型脉冲步枪。为了从铸造厂研究部门获取机密信息，他花了一大笔钱。是他们出卖了他吗？ 

“买家离开后，通讯链接就断了，”阿尔拉解释道，“我派了回收队过去，他们发现了尸体。看起来是火炬战锤、线性步枪和重击步枪干的。他们毁了飞船，但留下了残骸。” 

“看来是真的了，”蛛王静静地沉思道。 

这位犯罪头目的表面平静让阿尔拉感到不安。这样的深思熟虑通常预示着危及他们所有人的激进行动。  

蛛王没有让人失望。 

“备好我的双桅船，”他宣布，“我们将前往火星。” 

“公爵大人，”阿尔拉冒失进言，“这件事请交给我处理。我会追回货物与窃贼的。” 

“你当然会，”蛛王回答，“否则就会被截肢。” 

“但事态远比一批货更复杂。这证实了我近来听说的火星边境一个新兴市场的传闻。那里有资金雄厚的新玩家…却没有监管。一场血雨腥风正在酝酿中。” 

“立即备好我的双桅船！”他厉声说，“我们已经迟了。”

1753923263.name: Wolfsbane
1753923263.subtitle: "Nanites, Guardian." —Lord Saladin
1753923263.subtitle_zh: “纳米蜂群，守护者。”——领主萨拉丁
1753923263.text:
"But that's not your mission—it's mine," Ikora said. She was scanning a new holographic map of the Plaguelands. I was jealous. She even had the new aerial surveillance update. 

I slumped into one of her armchairs, made from genuine hide. "I get it. Us Praxics contain the spread of Darkness, and you handle… everything else. But it's not that clear-cut anymore, is it? Guardians use Darkness all the time now."  

Ikora hummed noncommittally. She was deep in the tank, planning the Vanguard's next op. I redoubled my efforts, leaning forward in the chair. 

"Look, if Maya's flooding the Plaguelands with Vex, it's not just for territory. She's not that crass. She's overplayed her hand on Kepler, and her Echo isn't enough anymore. She needs more paracausal energy. And that should interest the Praxics." 

"You sound like a Hunter," Ikora smirked. "Ready to charge in, Light blazing, orders be damned. But that's not the Warlock way." 

"It is not. But maybe it should be," I muttered. 

Ikora ignored the jab. "Don't worry about the Plaguelands. The Guardian will handle it." She powered down the map and gestured toward the door. My time was up. 

"Besides," she said, "I'm sure, whatever detail the Praxics have you on, is equally important." 

"They've got me babysitting the Drifter." I rolled my eyes. 

She chuckled. "Then you needn't worry. You'll be back under fire soon enough."
1753923263.text_zh:
“但那不该是你的任务——是我的，”艾可拉说道。她正在扫描一张瘟疫之地的新全息地图。我很嫉妒。她甚至还有最新的航拍监视数据。 

我坐进她的一把真皮扶手椅。“我明白。我们英勇教团负责遏制暗影的蔓延，而你负责…其他一切。但如今界限模糊了，不是吗？守护者使用暗影之力已是常态。”  

艾可拉不置可否地哼了一声。她正全神贯注地策划先锋的下一次行动。我加大攻势，从椅子里向前倾身。 

“听着，如果玛雅在瘟疫之地大量投放Vex，那绝不只是为了争夺地盘。她没那么粗鄙。她在开普勒上玩过了火，致使她的回响不再够用。她需要更多的超因果能量。英勇教团会感兴趣也很正常吧。” 

“你说起话来像个猎人，”艾可拉咧嘴笑道，“准备光能全开违令冲锋。但那并非术士的作风。” 

“确实不是。但或许本该是，”我嘟囔着。 

艾可拉无视了讽刺。“别操心瘟疫之地。守护者会处理的。”她关掉地图，朝门口做了个手势。我的会面时间结束了。 

“况且，”她说，“我相信，无论英勇教团派你做的工作是什么，都同样重要。” 

“他们让我照看浪客。”我翻了个白眼。 

她笑了。“那就不用担心了。你很快就能重回战场。”
