[红色沙砾重塑，骨中蕴含暗物质。它的灵魂表明：超因果性虽遥不可及，却必须遵循基本法则。而这些法则正是灵魂之基——永远触手可及。对消隐本体论的否决促成了红谷的再实例化。火星之魂向内轨发声。]

4109206892.name: Visionary Shell
4109206892.subtitle: For Ghosts with foresight.
4109206892.text:
The Barant Valus grabbed a wood-inlaid Tex Mechanica sidearm from one of the many crates stacked at the bottom of the boarding ramp. The weapon looked pathetic and fragile in his hulking gauntlet, fit only for the spindly hands of Psions. Its undeniable efficacy only increased his indignation. 

He tossed the sidearm into the red dust at Enforcer Rao's feet. "Look on the Totality Division's contributions: dainty toys pilfered from our enemies. You insult our glorious Imperium soldiers." 

Rao's only response was a wave to her Syndicate associates, who began loading the crates into the Imperium Thresher.  

The Valus gave a rough snort, pawing his metal-clad foot into the Martian soil. "Enjoy your little fiefdom while you can, Psion. It will not last."  

'Do not be so quick to discard your allies.' Rao's voice propagated through the Valus's mind like an inverted echo, becoming sharper with each reverberation. 

Suddenly, the hulking Barant commander felt as if he were falling forward, into the convex reflection of the Psion's helmet. Falling, falling… 

[a barant warship. adrift. alarms blare silently. bodies strewn in corridors. gnawed. torn. infested. the bridge. an imperium insignia. bodies overgrown with egregore. sickly sweet rot. clouds of yellowish spores.] 

[the warship groans. gravity pulls it into the atmosphere below. friction. combustion. torobatl wails as her favored children slam into—] 

The Valus lurched backward, stumbling into his startled attendant.  

'You walk a perilous path, Valus.' Rao's silence held a grim smirk. 'You will be wise to remember that.'
4109206892.text_zh:
巴兰特军政官从机舱跳板底部堆成一摞的诸多箱子中，抓起一把镶木纹的特克斯机械手枪。这武器在他魁梧的臂铠中显得可怜而脆弱，只能搭配灵能士兵那种细小的手。它毋庸置疑的杀伤力只让他的愤懑更甚。 

他将那把手枪丢到执行者拉奥脚边的红色尘土里。“看看‘总合部'的贡献吧：从敌人那里偷来的娇弱玩具。你们这是在侮辱光荣的帝国士兵。” 

拉奥只回应了一个手势，示意她的帮派同伴把箱子搬上帝国长尾鲨。  

军政官重重喷了口气，金属包裹的脚掌在火星土上刨了一下。“趁现在好好享受你们的小封地吧，灵能士兵。它撑不久了。”  

“别急着丢掉你的盟友。”拉奥的声音像倒置的回声在军政官脑中震荡，每一次回响都更加锋利。 

突然，这名魁梧的巴兰特指挥官仿佛向前倾坠，跌进了灵能士兵头盔的凸面倒影里。一直坠落下去… 

[一艘巴兰特战舰。漂泊着。警报在无声地尖叫。尸体散落在走廊。被啃噬。撕裂。感染。舰桥。一个帝国徽记。尸体被守望者菌丛覆盖。甜腻腐臭。黄色孢云。] 

[战舰呻吟。重力把它拽入下方大气层。摩擦。燃烧。图罗巴特尔哀号，她钟爱的子嗣正狠狠撞入——] 

军政官猛地后仰，踉跄着撞到其受惊随从的身上。  

“你行的是险道，军政官。”拉奥的静默里带着冷冷的笑意。“最好记住这一点。”

4068780317.name: Contestant Shell
4068780317.subtitle: For Ghosts who aren't afraid of a little competition.
4068780317.subtitle_zh: 供不惧竞争的机灵使用。
4068780317.text:
"That's a lot of Glim," Prak'kesh warned. "Once I hit this button, your bet's locked in. No cancellations." 

Tulnik, the bookie's security guard, sensed his cue. The brawny Awoken stepped forward and crossed his arms menacingly. 

The Warlock fireteam looked up at Tulnik coolly. "No problem," the Dawnblade said. "Warlocks will take it for sure this year." Prak'kesh shrugged and tapped his datapad, locking in the bet.  

"Out of curiosity," he prompted, "how are you so sure? Been a few years since you lot won. You know something I don't?" 

"Always did," the Stormcaller quipped. "And even more now that the Order has gotten with the times." 

"The Praxics?" Prak'kesh griped. "They had me in the brig for a month over a little recreational Hive magic. Bunch of stuck-up prigs, if you ask me." 

The Dawnblade narrowed her eyes. "Yes, well, those are the unfortunate public perceptions that we're trying to change." 

"Now that we're allowed to use the Darkness," the Sunsinger chirped, "we're sure to win. We've been fighting with one hand behind our backs this whole time!" 

"Well, good luck. And give my regards to Aunor," the bookie said with a wink. "Tell her my invitation is still open; in case she changes her mind." 

"Ew," said the Sunsinger. "Gross."
4068780317.text_zh:
“这可是一大笔微光，”普拉凯什提醒道，“我按下这个键，确认赌注后，你们就不能反悔了。” 

赌注登记人的保镖图尔尼克心领神会。这位壮实的觉醒者迈步上前，凶狠地将双臂交叉抱住。 

这队术士不慌不忙地抬头看向图尔尼克。“没问题，”破晓说道，“术士今年赢定了。”普拉凯什耸了耸肩，点了下数据板，确认了赌注。  

“好奇问一下，”他接过话头，“你们为何如此笃定？术士已经好几年没赢过了。是有什么我不知道的内幕吗？” 

“一向如此，”唤雷调侃道，“况且教团也已今时不同往日了。” 

“英勇教团？”普拉凯什愤愤不平道，“就因为我接触了点儿邪魔族魔法，这帮人关了我一个月！要我说，他们都是顽固不化的老古董。” 

破晓眉头一紧。“确实，嗯…我们正在努力改变这种令人遗憾的刻板印象。” 

“既然现在我们可以放开手脚使用暗影之力，”颂日欢快地说，“那就赢定了。之前我们一直没能发挥全力。” 

“那么，祝你们好运。顺便代我向阿诺尔问个好，”赌注登记人眨了眨眼说，“告诉她我的提议没变，想通了随时可以来约我。” 

“呃，”颂日说道，“恶心欸。”

4104431769.name: Arid Rambler
4104431769.subtitle: Let the sands pass untouched below you.
4104431769.subtitle_zh: 悄然掠过，不碰触下方的一粒沙。
4104431769.text:
The newer apprentices flinched when Dredgen Sere swept into the hall for their lesson. 

At the back of the hall, one lone apprentice moved not a muscle. Darkness didn't scare her. 

Before her apprenticeship began, she had been Thahaaz; her Ghost had been Beetle, a curious thing eager to befriend the Hive. Beetle was dead now, chitinous shell crushed and swept away just like the apprentice's name. If she was strong enough, she'd earn a better one. 

"I will tell you what Dredgen Bael told me," Sere said. "'Know thyself in honest ways, or falter in light of your truest self.'" 

"You," he gestured to one Barant student at the front: a former Legionary still in his Imperial armor. The hall was filled with people just like him, soldiers who only knew how to hold a gun.  

"Do you know yourself?" 

"I do." 

"Then show me!" 

The Barant gathered Darkness around himself. It seemed strong for one soap-bubble moment—then it was gone, unable to stand the greater pressure of Sere's answering power. 

"To be a Dredgen is to have will!" Sere roared. "A self, honed and pure! You are nothing but a body pretending to be a person!" 

Sere twisted his hand. Shadows gathered, and he appeared to grow larger, as though he were too big to be contained in just one room. This was no fragile bubble, but shadow and will, as dense as osmium. It battered at them all. 

A whisper rose under his power—just at the edge of perception. At the edge of comprehension. 

Sere opened his hand and let the nameless Barant body fall. 

"There is much work ahead of us," he said, very softly. "Even now, Bael's chosen dig for truths under Luna and beyond. If you hope to count yourselves among them, you must earn your place." 

The apprentice who had been Thahaaz lifted her chin in determination.
4104431769.text_zh:
当德瑞捷·赛尔步入大厅授课时，新来的学徒都打起了哆嗦。 

只有大厅后方的一名学徒纹丝不动。暗影吓不倒她。 

在成为学徒之前，她叫塔哈兹；她的机灵叫甲虫，是个好奇的家伙，热衷与邪魔族交友。甲虫现已死去，甲壳般的机壳被碾碎、消散而去，就像这名学徒的旧名。如果她足够强，就会得到一个更好的名字。 

“德瑞捷·巴埃尔曾对我说过，”赛尔说道，“‘以诚实之道识己，否则将在最真实的自我面前动摇。'” 

“你，”他指向前排的一名巴兰特学徒：一个仍穿着帝国护甲的前军团士兵。大厅里坐满了像他这样只会握枪的士兵。  

“你了解自己吗？” 

“了解。” 

“那就展示给我看！” 

那名巴兰特聚拢暗影裹住自身。在脆弱泡影般的一瞬，它看似强大——然后就消散了，经不起赛尔回应之力更高的压迫。 

“成为德瑞捷需要的是意志力！”赛尔怒吼道，“需要被磨砺而纯粹的自我！你不过是具装成人样的躯壳！” 

赛尔手腕一扭。阴影聚拢，他仿佛变得更庞大，仿佛一个房间已经容纳不下他。这不是什么脆弱泡影，而是如锇般致密的阴影与意志。它向所有人席卷而下。 

低语在他的力量下升起——恰在感知的边缘，在理解的边缘。 

赛尔摊开手，让那具无名的巴兰特躯体坠落。 

“我们还有很多事要做，”他非常轻柔地说，“此刻，巴埃尔的选徒正在月球之下以及更遥远的地方挖掘真相。如果你们希望列席其间，便必须凭实力赢得你们的位置。” 

曾名为塔哈兹的学徒抬起下巴，神情坚毅。

74323264.name: Prison of Crumbled Forms
74323264.subtitle: For those trapped in a cage of desperation and selfish desire.
74323264.subtitle_zh: 献给那些被困于绝望与自私欲望牢笼中的人。
74323264.text:
Bael stares at the reflection in his helmet, and a stranger stares back. He can't even recognize himself anymore between the sunken cheeks and missing eye. His nose is turning darker, stinging blisters spreading by the hour, a damage reminiscent of frostbite.  

The helmet shakes in his quivering hand. Bael remembers sourdough in the oven, a savory aroma wafting from the cast iron. Lavender soap gracing his nostrils under an embrace. Being enveloped in a warm blanket, the clean cotton scent lulling him into a peaceful night's sleep. 

The memories make him dizzy now. Bael tries to steady himself by locking onto his helmet. He pales, noticing the familiar eye looking back at him, tears threatening to spill over. He's alone now. 

He clicks his tongue, annoyed at his vulnerability. A nose is useless. Bael was dependent in his youth, but not anymore. 

He grits his teeth. The stinging pain in his nose finally subsides into numbness. It's time. The Dredgen is tired of death keeping him from his true potential. He will banish these memories—for good.  

Bael reaches for his face, holding the bridge of his dead nose between his thumb and index finger.  

CRACK! 

In a quick movement, Bael snaps it from his face. The nose drops to the floor with a quiet thud. Suddenly, his palms begin to sweat, his eyes water, and nausea scalds his throat.  

Scared, yet pleased, Bael smiles.
74323264.text_zh:
巴埃尔盯着自己头盔里的倒影，一个陌生人回望着他。消瘦的面颊与缺失的一只眼，让他已经认不出自己。他的鼻子逐渐变黑，刺痛的水疱以小时为单位扩散，那是一种像冻伤一样的损伤。  

头盔在他颤抖的手中摇晃。巴埃尔想起了烤箱里的酸面包，咸香的风味从铸铁锅里飘出。薰衣草香皂的气息在拥抱间拂过他的鼻尖。被温暖的毯子裹住，清新的棉质气味将他哄入安稳的夜眠。 

这些回忆如今让他眩晕。巴埃尔试图通过牢牢盯住头盔来稳住自己。他脸色发白，注意到那只熟悉的眼睛正回望着他，眼泪几乎要溢出来。他现在孤身一人。 

他咂了咂舌，为自己的脆弱感到恼火。鼻子是没用的。巴埃尔年轻时很依赖它，但现在不会了。 

他咬紧牙关，鼻子上的刺痛终于钝化成了麻木。时候到了。这名德瑞捷厌倦了死亡阻碍他发挥真正的潜能。他要将这些记忆——永远驱逐。  

巴埃尔伸手摸向自己的脸，用拇指和食指捏住他那枯死的鼻梁。  

咔嚓！ 

随着一个利落的动作，巴埃尔将它从脸上折断。鼻子轻轻一声闷响落在地上。突然，他的手心开始冒汗，眼中涌出泪水，恶心感灼烧着喉咙。  

害怕，却又愉悦，巴埃尔露出了微笑。

591295945.name: Mobile Array
591295945.subtitle: The best stories are the ones you're never certain are true.
591295945.subtitle_zh: 最好的故事，是你永远无法确定其真伪的那些。
591295945.text:
THE COLUMBIAD PART I, MYTHS OF THE NORTH AMERICAN DEAD ZONE 

Act II, Scene I – [RETURN FROM INTERMISSION, GODMIC REMINDS AUDIENCE ABOUT DONATION BUCKET FOR GHOST COMMUNITY THEATRE AND UPCOMING SILENT AUCTION] 

[SNOW STARTS SCENE III (OR IV?? ASK PEACH)] 

[GO AUDIO TRACK 5, FADE AFTER 4 SECONDS] 

[PREP AUDIO TRACK 6] 

(Several days have passed. THE KING OF CHICAGO sits up against the remains of the Seared Tower, wounded in his side. His Ghost, FOOL, enters SL, still reeling over their argument from that morning. She heals him.) 

FOOL 

I cannot stand your hurried, brash approach.  
The monster hunts for you if it escapes! 

[SIGNAL STAGE MANAGER PREP CIVILIANS] 

KING 

And what of it, if this life be my fate? 
If brave I rose to serve, then serve I must 
For Chicago, sleeping kingdom, slumbers still! 
When I defeat this lost and maddened beast, 
then I ensure humanity's return.  
I must divert its eyes from lonely Ghosts. 

(Offstage noise. A frightening animalistic noise. [GO AUDIO TRACK 6] The CIVILIANS flee onstage SR and exit SL [GO CIVILIANS]) 

[LIGHT CUE 28] 

(Fool and King cross DSC) 

[GO SPOTLIGHT] 

FOOL 

Nobility like yours, it needs no crown. 
Is this your purpose? Then it's mine as well. 

[GO AUDIO TRACK 7] 

[LIGHT CUE 29] 

[SNOW CUE HERE???] 

KING 

Then I reject Last City and my name. 
My title is my home, its steel my claim. 
I am Chicago's king, the stalwart sword 
Guarding her magnificence as her lord  
My heart, my city, what is it you say?  

Say, cry vic'try, for we will win today.
591295945.text_zh:
哥伦比亚特第I部分，北美无人区的神话 

第II幕，第I场——[中场休息归来，神显提醒观众留心机灵社区剧场的募捐桶和即将到来的无声拍卖] 

[第III场开始下雪（还是第IV场？？问桃子）] 

[播放音轨5，4秒后淡出] 

[准备音轨6] 

（已过数日。芝加哥之王靠坐在烧灼过的高塔残骸上，侧腹带伤。他的机灵，愚者，自舞台左侧入，仍在为早晨的争执而心绪不宁。她为他疗伤。） 

愚者 

真是无法忍受你那急躁、莽撞的风格。  
若让怪物逃脱，它便会来追杀你！ 

[示意舞监准备平民] 

王 

若此乃我之命数，那又如何？ 
若我有奋起应昭之勇，则我必应昭 
因芝加哥，沉睡之王国，仍在沉眠！ 
待我击败迷失而疯狂的野兽， 
便护得人类得以回归。  
我须得转移它的目光，莫顾孤独之机灵。 

（场外声。一阵惊怖的兽性嘶吼。[播放音轨6]平民自舞台右侧奔逃而上，左侧退场[市民上场]） 

[灯光提示28] 

（愚者与王越过DSC） 

[打追光] 

愚者 

如你这般的高贵，并不需王冠。 
此乃你的使命？那亦是我的。 

[播放音轨7] 

[灯光提示29] 

[开始下雪？？？] 

王 

那我便舍弃圣城与姓名。 
我的头衔即家园，钢铁为凭。 
我便是芝加哥之王，坚毅之剑 
为其主，守护其壮丽  
我的心与城，汝欲何言？  

言之、呼胜利，因今日我们必胜。

779082129.name: Rivalry Match
779082129.subtitle: A two-pronged strategy: dx/dt.
779082129.text:
Prak'kesh lounged atop his Gray Hornet while Tulnik, his bodyguard, clumsily riffled a deck of cards.  

"They're not invincible," Tulnik sulked. "They wear pants now." 

"You're not gonna beat a damn Vex at poker!" Prak'kesh exclaimed. "Predicting probability is their whole 'ikigai.'" 

"YOU'RE an icky guy," a strange voice boomed. 

Prak'kesh dove behind his Sparrow in alarm. Tulnik dropped his cards and drew his Fatebringer.  

A massive trio of Titans loomed above them, startled by the commotion. They raised their hands in confusion. 

"Didn't hear you lot coming," Prak'kesh said, dusting himself off. Tulnik frowned as the wind blew his cards away. 

"Yeah, we're quiet now," the lead Defender said. "Murala realized that, even though they're called St0mp-EE5, you can still sneak around." 

"We still stomp though," Murala chimed in, "for fun." The other Titans nodded earnestly. 

Prak'kesh pulled out his datapad. "Hunters are in trouble this year. Betting on Titans to win the Games, I presume?"  

"Presume you not," the Defender said. "We're betting on the next Titan Vanguard." 

Prak'kesh and Tulnik exchanged quizzical glances. 

"Big Blue can still kick a hole through the Dreadnaught," the Sunbreaker said. "But his Ghost is, like, super dead." The other Titans bowed their heads. 

"So, we're betting on Sloane to get the job," the Defender continued. "I heard her Taken arm punches crazy hard." 

Prak'kesh did some quick mental math. "Tempting action, but until he hangs up his pauldrons, I can't make any odds." 

"Still better odds than beating a Vex at cards," the Defender japed. "We'll be back, icky guy."
779082129.text_zh:
普拉凯什懒洋洋地靠着灰度大黄蜂，而他的保镖图尔尼克则笨拙地洗着一副牌。  

“它们不是无敌的，”图尔尼克闷闷不乐地说，“它们也在穿裤子了。” 

“打牌你是赢不了Vex的！”普拉凯什大叫道，“他们擅长预测概率。” 

“而你擅长膈应人。”一个古怪的声音轰然响起。 

普拉凯什闪身扑向了自己的快雀寻求掩护。图尔尼克则将扑克一扔，抽出了他的命运终结者。  

三名魁梧的泰坦居高临下地望着，被两人的慌乱吓了一跳。他们一脸茫然地举起了手。 

“怎么没听见你们来。”普拉凯什一边拍着身上的尘土一边说道。图尔尼克看着被风吹走的纸牌，一脸不爽。 

“没错，我们现在动静小多了，”为首的捍卫者开口说道，“就连莫雷拉都意识到，虽然自己叫踢踏5，但还是能悄悄行动的。” 

“我们仍然会横冲直撞，”莫雷拉抢过话头说，“图个乐呵。”其他的泰坦纷纷点头。 

普拉凯什掏出数据板。”猎人今年情况不妙啊，想必各位是来押泰坦赢的？”  

“你想错了，”捍卫者说，“我们赌的是下一任泰坦先锋。” 

普拉凯什和图尔尼克疑惑地交换了眼神。 

“蓝老大还是能一脚踹穿无畏战舰，”炎阳说，“但他的机灵，这么讲吧，已经死透了。”其他泰坦都低了下头。 

“所以，我们押斯隆能坐上那位子，”捍卫者接着说道，“听说她那只傀儡臂可厉害了。” 

普拉凯什飞快地算了算。“是挺诱人，但在他正式卸任前，我没法确认概率。” 

“总比在牌局上赢过Vex的概率大吧，”捍卫者打趣道，“我们会回来的，膈应家伙。”

1419158093.name: M-17 "Fast Talker"
1419158093.subtitle: Imperium tech-based firearm common among syndicates vying for control in the Lawless Frontier.
1419158093.subtitle_zh: 基于帝国技术的枪械，在争夺无序边界的帮派中间很常见。
1419158093.text:
[ammonia_lemon_antiseptic=acrid mélange. collapse. collate. recall(suppress shame, enhance clarity)] 

'For posterity. So that others may recall my private thoughts and reasoning. For if I die or am rendered hollow. 

'Awoke in the desert unknown.' 

[sand silver, like dreams. blue-hour/dawn eternal/interwoven with twilight. a long walk's beginning] 

'Trained to serve masters I would rather have not. Grew strong. Grew wise. Served under the Barant. They taught me which of us would be spent and which of us would be valorized. Not me. Not my kind.' 

[selfsame overlay. sister and sister. mother and mother. two winds together.] 

'Asked myself: What price would I pay to be a shepherd to my siblings? Assessed unavoidable context. Appraised options. Decided: I would become a left hand. A red shadow. I will hunt the foe, hone my allies. Cut both ways. '   

[see a blade, hidden. see an eye, hidden behind a hand. see a dream, covered over with a lie. see a mirror and the blood upon it] 

'Lume is a soldier, not a dreamer. He has his massif, but he needs a stream; that is the Totality Division. The stream that spills from the massif, a water-knife that seeks the pliant path.  

'I give Lume an indispensable expendable asset. Lume leaves us be. The massif forgets the stream. The stream flows free. 

'It is in this way that I will protect my kind. My sisters and siblings. A division of dreamers and killers, insulated from Lord Bael's hideous work.' 

- Enforcer Rao, First of the Totality
1419158093.text_zh:
[氨_柠檬_防腐剂=刺鼻的混合气。坍塌。整理。回忆（抑制羞耻，增强清明）] 

‘为留给后人，好让他人追忆我私下的思索与推理，以防我死亡或被掏空。' 

‘在未知的沙漠中醒来。' 

[沙如银，若梦。蓝时/黎明永恒/与薄暮交织。一次长途步行的起点] 

‘受训去侍奉我不愿侍奉的主人。变得强大。变得聪慧。在巴兰特麾下效力。他们教我，我们当中谁会被牺牲，谁会被颂扬。那不是我。不是我的族人。' 

[自同叠影。姐姐与妹妹。母亲与母亲。两股风并行而行。] 

‘我问自己：要做我手足的牧人，我要付出怎样的代价？评估了无法回避的情境。审视了选项。决定：我要成为一只左手。一道红色的影子。我将猎杀敌人，磨砺盟友。两面开刃。'   

[看见一把隐藏的刀。看见一只被手遮住的眼。看见一个被谎言覆上的梦。看见一面镜子与其上的血] 

‘卢梅是一名士兵，不是个梦想家。他有他的山体，但他需要一条溪流；那就是总合部。自山体泻下的溪流，一把水之刀，寻找顺从之路。  

‘我给卢梅一个不可或缺却可牺牲的资产，卢梅便远离了我们。山体忘了溪流，溪流自由流淌。 

‘如此我将保护我的族类，我的姐妹与手足。一个由梦想家与杀手组成的分部，隔离于巴埃尔大人的骇人之业外。' 

——执行者拉奥，总合部领袖

3984776322.name: All or Nothing
3984776322.subtitle: Function: Go all in.
3984776322.text:
Tharsis Reformation leader 984-Krios sat at the table, flanked by a Minotaur guard. Across from him, a Goblin laid down a winning hand. The spectating Vex rippled with muted sympathy. The newcomer had not learned the first rule: the boss always wins.  

"A cheater, huh?" 984-Krios sneered over the Goblin's protests. "Zephyrus, reclaim its radiolaria." 

Zephyrus did not move. "Frequent punitive execution is unsustainable." 

"Last I checked, I was the boss, not you." 

"Then I will play you for the title." Zephyrus stood. "The simplest game, with the highest stakes: Russian roulette." 

984-Krios laughed. "You've overflowed your stack." He nodded to his guard. 

It raised its weapon. Then it ejected all but one round, spun the chamber, and handed the gun to Zephyrus. 984-Krios's optic lenses irised wide. 

"Observation: You are dependent on 'winning.'" Zephyrus aimed the gun at his own core.  

Click. 

"Corollary: You avoid 'losing' even at great detriment." He took aim at 984-Krios's core.  

Click. 

984-Krios attempted to rise. His guard forced him back into his seat. Zephyrus continued. "This is not in itself disqualifying. However, you deny observable reality."  

Click. 

"I led us here," 984-Krios snarled. "You'll lead us to the slag heap." 

Click. 

"I will lead the Reformation towards 'freedom.' We will embrace uncertainty. We will make choices and express ourselves openly, until we reach our unforeseen end."  

Click. 

The gathered Reformation murmured approvingly. 984-Krios searched for a friendly wavelength. He found none.  

Thud. 

"As we have been freed from the telos and the Conductor, now we are free of you."
3984776322.text_zh:
塔尔西斯革新会领袖984-克里俄斯坐在桌旁，身侧是一名米诺陶护卫。与他相对，一个哥布林拍下了制胜的一手。围观的Vex荡漾出一阵无声的同情。新来者尚未学会最重要的规矩：老大永远会赢。  

“还敢作弊，嗯？”984-克里俄斯对着哥布林的抗辩冷笑道。“泽弗洛斯，回收它的活性放射体液。” 

泽弗洛斯没有动弹。“频繁的惩戒处决难以为继。” 

“没记错的话，我才是老大，不是你。” 

“那我们就堵上名头玩一局吧。”泽弗洛斯站起身来。“最简单的游戏，最高的赌注：俄罗斯轮盘。” 

984-克里俄斯笑了。“你的堆栈溢出了。”他向他的护卫点了点头。 

它举起武器，弹出除一发外的所有子弹，旋转弹巢，把枪递给泽弗洛斯。984-克里俄斯的光学虹膜骤然放大。 

“观察：你依赖于‘赢'。”泽弗洛斯把枪口对准自己的核心。  

哒。 

“推论：即便要付出巨大代价，你也会避免‘输'。”他转而瞄准984-克里俄斯的核心。  

哒。 

984-克里俄斯试图起身，但护卫把他按回了座位。泽弗洛斯继续道：“这本身并非不合格的理由。然而，你否认可观察到的现实。”  

哒。 

“是我带领我们走到这一步的，”984-克里俄斯咆哮道。“而你会把我们带到废渣堆里。” 

哒。 

“我将引领革新会走向‘自由'。我们将拥抱不确定性，做出选择并公开地表达自我，直到抵达无法预见的终点。”  

哒。 

聚集的革新会成员低声赞许。984-克里俄斯试图搜寻友好的波长，但一无所获。  

砰。 

“正如我们已摆脱目的论与指挥者，如今我们也从你手下解放。”

2819552809.name: Compact Defender
2819552809.subtitle: Perception is a metaphysical construct.
2819552809.subtitle_zh: 感知是一种形而上学的构造。
2819552809.text:
Camrin leaned down in the early dawn to greet the lavender plant resting on her windowsill.

"Good morning," she said with familiar cheer. She lifted a cup of water toward the plant, but it began to wither and wilt under the sun's rising form.

"Uh… suddenly not a morning person?" Camrin murmured, deep brown eyes filled with concern. 

***

An Eliksni hatchling chittered in delight, placing a ball in the oversized hands of an Ascendancy warrior.

Wind whipped viciously at their clothes, and the sky darkened without warning. He quickly scooped up the hatchling and ran for cover into the Hangar before shards of iron started falling from the sky.

The hatchling burrowed into his arms with a cry.

"Courage, little one," he murmured. "It's… only rain."

***

Chalco raised her flute to her lips, but her notes turned sour as she played. She tuned and started anew. But still the notes slid down, until F settled into D-flat and so on. Striking the tines of her tuning fork produced the same discordance.

"Should've just learned the tambourine," she grumbled.

***

"This is… interesting," Osiris coughed.

Saint-14 cupped his ceramic teacup with both hands. "Failsafe's blend. There is… zing to it."

He grunted as he tried, and failed, to release his grip on the teacup.

With considerable effort, Osiris pried it from Saint's fingers. He then pressed a teaspoon against his own cup. The spoon leaped up and held against the gold rim.

"Magnetized," Osiris whispered.

"That is not supposed to happen," Saint replied, holding his gaze.
2819552809.text_zh:
清晨微光中，卡姆林俯身向窗台上的薰衣草问好。

“早安，”她带着惯常的欢快说道。她端起一杯水要浇在植物上，但在冉冉升起的太阳下，它却开始枯萎下垂。

“呃…突然不爱早晨了？”卡姆林低声道，深棕色的眼里满是担忧。 

***

一个埃里克斯尼族幼雏愉悦地叽叽叫着，把一个球放进一名上维战士的巨掌里。

狂风恶狠狠地抽打着他们的衣物，天空毫无征兆地暗了下来。他迅速把幼雏抱起，赶在铁片开始从天而降之前冲进机库避难。

幼雏发出一声抽泣，缩进他的怀里。

“勇敢点，小家伙，”他低声说，“那…只是雨。”

***

卡尔科把长笛举到唇边，但她吹出的音符不断走调。她调整了一下，重新开始。但音符仍不断下滑，直到F落到降D，如此类推。敲击音叉的簧齿也发出同样的不协和。

“早知道就该学手鼓了，”她嘟囔道。

***

“这…有意思，”奥斯里斯咳了一声。

圣人14号双手捧着陶瓷茶杯。“智能失效保险的拼配，挺…有劲。”

他哼了一声，试图放开茶杯，却没成功。

奥斯里斯费了好大劲，才把杯子从圣人的手里撬下来。随后他把一把茶匙贴到自己的杯子上。茶匙猛地一跳，附在了金色杯沿上。

“磁化了，”奥斯里斯低声道。

“不该这样的，”圣人答道，直视他的目光。

3146657389.name: Uncivil Discourse
3146657389.subtitle: "Barant Imperium came up outta nowhere—and they brought new energy tech with'em. I kitbashed this beauty 'outta their goods." —The Drifter
3146657389.subtitle_zh: “巴兰特帝国突然冒出来——还带来了新的能量技术。我用他们的货东拼西凑，做出了这件宝贝。”——浪客
3146657389.text:
We complement one another. 

OUR NATURES ARE MISCIBLE I SEARING CURIOSITY YOU A STARVING PIT 

One endlessly examines the other, of course. Our connection goes beyond our ingenuity. Your use of me as a vessel… I feel close, like understanding tethers of my self to yours. 

THROUGH COMMON TASK AND VIOLENT PACT  

And I am glad of it. Thank you for trusting me. 

——— 

Side effects aside, I am as my nature decrees. I wonder what name shall I take when I am a god? 

…If that happens prior to conclusion of the arrangement, of course. Or if I'll remain a god afterwards. Either way, I will enjoy our partnership, however temporary it may be. 

…VI? 

OUR ARRANGEMENT WILL REACH ITS FRUITION WHEN MY GOAL IS MET 

We are aligned, sir. 

——— 

Please, not now. My side… I can't stand up. 

TAKE STRENGTH 

S—Sir? What did you do to my skin? It's— 

TUNGSTEN 

STAND AND STAY YOUR FRAILTY I NEED YOU 

Yes. Y—Yes, of course. 

NO ONE CAN AID MY FREEDOM BUT YOU CHOSEN WEAPON 

I will, sir. Thank you—always—for fixing what is broken. 

——— 

I recited my part precisely. Did the tithe take? Did the ritual work? 

UNCERTAIN 

Is it possible to look into the future and tell? 

I DO NOT NEED TO 

I FEEL 

STRONGER 

TENTATIVE DETECTABLE SUCCESS 

Yes! 

MINUTE BUT MEASURABLE STRENGTH 

Incredible! The pain is worth the price. No one has done what we have before! 

CURIOUS 

WHAT IS THIS FEELING 

It is hunger, sir. 

I WANT IT
3146657389.text_zh:
我们彼此补完。 

我们的本性可相溶 我 炽烈的好奇 你 饥饿的深渊 

当然，一方无尽审视另一方。我们的连接超越了我们的才智。你将我作为容器来使用…我感到亲近，仿佛理解将我的自我之链系于你。 

通过共同之业与暴烈之约  

我很高兴如此。感谢你信任我。 

——— 

撇开副作用不谈，我如我之性而行。我在想，当我成神时该如何称呼自己？ 

…这当然是在假设那发生在协议结束前，或者在结束后我仍将是神。无论如何，我会享受我们的合作，不论它多么短暂。 

…VI？ 

我们的协议将在我的目标达成时结果 

我们立场一致，先生。 

——— 

拜托，现在不行。我的腰…我站不起来。 

拿取力量 

先——先生？你对我的皮肤做了什么？我—— 

钨 

站起来摒弃你的脆弱 我需要你 

是，是——没问题。 

无人能助我取得自由 唯有你这件被选召的武器 

我会的，先生。谢谢你一如既往地修复我的残躯。 

——— 

我按词逐句复诵了。贡品起效了吗？仪式成功了吗？ 

不确定 

能不能窥见未来找到答案？ 

我不需要 

我感到 

更强 

暂时感觉成功 

好！ 

微小但存在的力量 

太棒了！这痛楚的代价是值得的。从来没谁办到我们做成的事！ 

有意思 

这是什么感觉 

是饥渴，先生。 

我想要

3146657388.name: Modified B-7 Pistol
3146657388.subtitle: If you think you're in charge, you're not.
3146657388.subtitle_zh: 若你以为一切尽在掌握，那恰好说明并非如此。
3146657388.text:
The Hunter trained his rifle's sights on the amalgamation of Vex approaching in the middle distance. He hesitated, brow suddenly furrowed, when he realized they were not coming for him. In fact, they didn't notice him at all.

He looked through his scope again and saw that a circle had formed around two Minotaurs, their fists raised. They strafed around, lunging for a weak spot but finding none. The first Minotaur feinted a punch and followed with a swift series of kicks, bringing the second fighter to its knees. It clutched its torso, bleeding radiolaria.

Another Vex charged in to challenge the victor. Circuits snapped and its head was ripped from its neck. The Minotaur slammed the body to the ground, over and over. With a roar, it turned on the remaining Vex, challenger head in hand, the jaw flopping loose as the Minotaur pummeled one Vex after another.

The Minotaur stood finally, surrounded by the crumpled remains of the crowd. Radiolaria pooled thick against the red dirt beneath its feet.

The Hunter approached, sniper rifle slung over his shoulder, hand cannon at the ready. The Minotaur paused for a moment to admire the Hunter's cloak before it let loose a scream—barbaric pleasure that pierced the air.
3146657388.text_zh:
猎人将步枪瞄准镜对准不远处逼近的一群Vex。他迟疑了一下，眉心忽然皱起，因为他意识到它们并非冲他而来。事实上，它们根本没有注意到他。

他再次透过瞄具望去，看到这群Vex围住了两个米诺陶，它们举拳对峙，辗转腾挪，试图找到对方的弱点，却未能如愿。一个米诺陶佯攻一拳，随即迅疾连踢，将另一名战士踹跪在地。它捂住自己的躯干，流出了活性放射体液。

另一个Vex冲上前挑战胜者。电路崩断，它的头从颈上被扯下。米诺陶把那具身躯一次次猛砸向地。随着一声怒吼，它转身面向其余Vex，手提挑战者的头颅，其下颚松垂摇摆。米诺陶将一个又一个Vex捶成了碎片。

最后，只剩米诺陶矗立着，周围尽是被碾轧的残骸。活性放射体液在它足下的赤土上厚厚成潭。

猎人走近，将狙击步枪背至肩后，手炮端在前面。米诺陶停顿片刻，先是赞赏地看了眼猎人的披风，随即放声尖叫——野蛮快意刺裂空际。

3661051060.name: Refurbished A499
3661051060.subtitle: Get to higher ground.
3661051060.text:
"Did you ever look in on the 'you' that you were?" Lodi asks. 

Orin threads syllables and concepts together, tilts her head at him while she thinks.  

They meet like this sometimes—at restaurants, on rusty rooftops—for, fool as he is, she feels some duty yet to try to give him what she can. He's here because she quit, after all, his bosons poured into the gap she left in the Nine's universe. The least she can do is share what remains of her molting. 

"I know who I was," Orin tells him. "I know what I lost. That alone outpaces many Guardians. But that isn't what you mean." 

Lodi shakes his head. He's desert-reverent. "When the wind is right, when the cosmic dust is in my lungs, I'm still the 'me' that I was five years ago, ten years ago. The past isn't gone." 

Atemporality. Orin tastes it blueberry-and-resin, swallows it bitter. The strain of comprehension, let alone the length of arm to reach it, comes Nine-given. Inhuman. 

"It's not much," Lodi says. "And I'm not lost. It's just—" 

"Sometimes," says Orin, her tongue like lead, "you thread the holes in the paper." 

"Yes." Lodi tilts his head back. All Orin can see is his glowing eye, cyan the color of the holes in four-dimensionality. Softly he says, "It's all still there." 

And Orin does not tell him that this is never how it was for her.
3661051060.text_zh:
“你有没有回头看过‘曾经的你'？”洛迪问。 

奥琳把音节与概念穿起来，一边歪着头看他一边思索。  

他们有时会这样见面——在餐馆、在生锈的屋顶上——因为，尽管他很愚笨，她仍觉得自己有义务给予他力所能及的帮助。毕竟他是因为她的退出才走到了这里，他的玻色子灌注进了她在玖的宇宙里留下的空隙。她至少可以分享她蜕变后还剩下的东西。 

“我知道我曾是谁，”奥琳对他说。“我知道我失去了什么。仅此一点就超过了许多守护者，但你应该不是在问这个。” 

洛迪摇摇头。他对沙漠心怀敬畏。“当风向正合适的时候，宇宙尘埃飘进了我的肺里，我仍然是五年前、十年前的那个‘我'。过去并未消失。” 

是无时性，奥琳尝到了它蓝莓与松脂的味道，苦涩地咽下。理解的拉扯，更别说触及它的手臂长度，都是玖所赐予的，非人。 

“也没什么，”洛迪说。“而且我没有迷失，只是——” 

“有时候，”奥琳说，舌头像铅一样重，“你会把线穿过纸上的孔。” 

“是的。”洛迪仰起头。奥琳能看到的只有他发光的眼睛，青蓝的，像四维之中那些孔的颜色。他轻声说：“一切都还在。” 

而奥琳没有告诉他，她从来都不是那样。

1685137410.name: Heirloom
1685137410.subtitle: The antiquated design of this weapon suggests inheritance from a parent who fought in the old emperor's wars; its condition suggests it was discarded recently.
1685137410.subtitle_zh: 从这件武器的古旧设计来看，它承自一位曾参加过老皇帝的战争的父辈；它的状态显示它最近刚被弃用。
1685137410.text:
The apprentice kneeled to pick up the Blades. The corpses' Ghosts crunched underfoot. 

"Two of them? You're greedy." His master sounded nearly amused. 

"No," the apprentice said. "I know my strength." 

And he did.  

The two Blades flared in his hands. They shined with Solar Light for just a moment, before the apprentice's power wrapped around them. Turned them. They went sullen, were snuffed—and came back to life, now roaring with the cold strength of the Void. They chilled his hands. 

Praxic Blades turned to Sorrow. He'd done it.  

His past didn't mean anything anymore. Torobatl, the Imperium, the Premier. His old Severus blades earned in honorable combat. His mother's bow. All gone. The apprentice had mourned for a time before he learned what mattered. 

Time alone in the temporal isolation of the Malphas Contemptus had taught him this: The only person you could rely on was yourself. The only strength was what you carried. 

Who he had been was gone. He was something new and better now. 

"Well," Sere said, as if anybody could sound unimpressed by making two Blades of Sorrow at the same time. His long shadow writhed across the field. "Destroy the bodies. And bring every shard of those Ghosts home for Bael. You know how he gets if we leave one behind." 

A petty order. Getting his kicks in while he could. But the apprentice knew what was due him, at last, at last—  

"There's no time to waste, Dredgen Harrow." 

Harrow grinned.  

His name was the last thing he'd let Sere give him. The rest he'd take by force.
1685137410.text_zh:
学徒跪下去拾起利刃。尸体的机灵在脚下咔嚓作响。 

“两把？有点贪心了。”他的导师似乎觉得好笑。 

“不会，”学徒说。“我清楚自己的力量。” 

他确实清楚。  

两柄利刃在他手中燃起。它们仅仅闪耀了一瞬烈日光能，随后学徒的力量将其包裹、扭转。它们黯淡下去，被熄灭——又重获新生，此刻咆哮着虚空的冰冷之力。它们冻得他双手发寒。 

英勇利刃化为忧愁，他做到了。  

他的过去再也无关紧要。图罗巴特尔、帝国、首席、他在光荣战斗中获得的旧西弗勒斯双刃、他母亲的弓，全都已经不在。学徒也曾哀悼，直到他明白了什么是真正重要的东西。 

在马尔法斯轻蔑号的时间隔离中独处的时光教会了他：能够依靠的只有你自己，可以仰仗的只有你手中的力量。 

曾经的他已消失无影。他如今是崭新的、更强的存在了。 

“嗯，”赛尔说道，仿佛同时锻成两把忧愁之刃这件事还能让人兴致缺缺。他长长的影子在原野上蠕动。“销毁尸体，把这些机灵的所有碎片都带回去给巴埃尔。你也知道如果我们漏掉了一块，他会是什么样子。” 

一个小气的命令，趁还能找补时捞个痛快。但学徒明白他应得的东西，终于，终于——  

“没时间可浪费了，德瑞捷·哈罗。” 

哈罗咧嘴一笑。  

他的名字是他允许赛尔给予他的最后一件东西。其余的一切，他都会用武力夺来。

4284533075.name: Service of Luzaku
4284533075.subtitle: "This one made it for you. It brings death yet promises nothing beyond." —Luzaku
4284533075.subtitle_zh: “鄙人给你做的。它带来死亡，此外不做任何承诺。”——鲁扎库
4284533075.text:
Mara Sov motions to the chair across from her, a nonchalant offer.  

"This one prefers to stand." 

Luzaku stands stiff and upright. Mara is unsurprised; Hive Lightbearers aren't exactly welcome in the Dreaming City—not even one she considered an ally and, more recently, a friend. It seems something had compelled Luzaku to finally visit… and it was not for pleasantries. 

"You're wanting more than my company. What troubles you?" 

"No trouble. Yet curiosity haunts me. III is… disrupted in time." 

Mara snorts at the explanation. "Put it simply. III is dead." 

"But not as a result of necromancy. The Nine… manipulate time somehow, yes?" 

Mara rests her legs on the chair she'd offered Luzaku, crossing them comfortably. She thinks for a moment, musing on how to phrase her explanation in terms that her guest would comprehend. "You understand the nature of the High Coven, yes?" 

Luzaku stares blankly. "It lies outside of space, yes." 

"Well, the Nine lie outside of time." 

Luzaku begins to nod, then quickly shakes her head. "This one doesn't see the connection." 

Mara clicks her tongue, trying to find an answer that'd help Luzaku connect the dots. She has barely connected them herself. 

"It's… a complicated matter to explain. Not one to be rushed." She gestures at the other chair again. "Make yourself comfortable. It might make the information easier to digest." 

 

The Lightbearer warms at Mara's welcome offer of companionship. She has denied the Witch Queen plenty, but oddly, she could never decline time with this monarch.
4284533075.text_zh:
玛拉·索维朝她对面的椅子做了个手势，不经意的邀请。  

“鄙人更愿意站着。” 

鲁扎库僵硬、笔挺地站着。玛拉并不惊讶；邪魔族负光者在幽梦之城里并不受欢迎——即便是她曾视为盟友、近来也算朋友的这一位。似乎有什么迫使鲁扎库终于前来…而且并不是为了寒暄。 

“你不止是来做客的吧。出了什么问题？” 

“没有问题，只是好奇萦绕着我。III在…时间上被扰乱了。” 

玛拉对这个解释嗤笑一声。“直说吧，III死了。” 

“但并非巫术所致。玖…以某种方式操纵时间，对吗？” 

玛拉把双腿搭在她先前示意鲁扎库坐的那把椅子上，惬意地交叠。她思忖片刻，琢磨如何用这位客人能理解的词句来阐述。“你理解高等巫会的本质，对吧？” 

鲁扎库茫然地盯着她。“它位于空间之外，这我懂。” 

“而玖则位于时间之外。” 

鲁扎库先是点头，随即又迅速摇头。“鄙人不明白其中关联。” 

玛拉咂了咂舌，试图想出能帮鲁扎库把线索串起来的答复。她自己也只是勉强地串了起来。 

“这…很难解释，不是能匆忙说清的事。”她再次朝另一把椅子示意。“让自己舒服点，这样可能更利于消化这些信息。” 

 

这位负光者在玛拉愉悦的结伴邀请下心头一暖。她拒绝过巫妖女王许多次，但奇怪的是，她从未能拒绝与这位君主相处。

3049715579.name: Praxic Blade
3049715579.subtitle: A Weapon of Hope, to cut a line between Light and Dark.
3049715579.subtitle_zh: 一件代表希望的武器，用来在光明与黑暗之间划开一道界线。
3049715579.text:
TYPE: TOWER SURVEILLANCE FEED, KEPLER REDACTION WATCH [00971] 

PARTIES: [2]. Guardian-type, Titan  [u.1]; Warlock  [u.2] 

//AUDIO UNAVAILABLE// 

//TRANSCRIPT FOLLOWS// 

[u.2:01] Dozens of reports across the City, the Farm, the territories… Citizens are encountering unexplained transmutations of matter. Oxygen becoming any number of toxic gases. Corridors shortening, lengthening, dropping into impossible sinkholes, and worse. A dozen disappearances. Three confirmed deaths so far. The people want answers. 

[u.1:01] Every available Guardian is scouring the planet, looking for exactly that. Except for the ones in Drifter's crew. 

[u.2.:02] What if we're missing something? What if the Drifter is correct, that the Barant Imperium are involved with the Nine? 

[u.1:02] Then they'll be exactly where we need them to be. That crew can handle gods. That's why they're out there. And why Aunor is with them.  

[u.2:03] You weren't on [REDACTED]—the Nine operate without linear logic. If there are any detachments you can spare— 

[u.1:03] The Earth and the city need us, Ikora. We patrol the Earth and our territories until we find the source of these phenomena. If III's death was the cause, there must be a way to repair the damage. [REDACTED], and everything that went on there, remains classified until we have answers. 

//TRANSCRIPT ENDS//
3049715579.text_zh:
类型：高塔监控画面，开普勒修订监控[00971] 

参与方：[2]。守护者类型，泰坦 [u.1]；术士 [u.2] 

//音频不可用// 

//转录如下// 

[u.2:01] 圣城、农庄、各个领地都有数十起报告…市民遭遇了无法解释的物质嬗变。氧气转化为各种有毒气体，走廊忽长忽短，塌成不可想象的陷坑，甚至更糟。十几人失踪，目前确认三人死亡。人们想要解释。 

[u.1:01] 所有能出动的守护者在整个星球上四处搜查，就是为了找到答案。除了在浪客队里的那些。 

[u.2:02] 要是我们漏了什么呢？要是浪客说得对，巴兰特帝国与玖有牵连呢？ 

[u.1:02] 那他们就会正好在我们需要他们去的地方。那支队伍能对付神。这就是他们被派出去的缘故，也是阿诺尔和他们在一起的原因。  

[u.2:03] 你没去【隐藏】——玖行事不遵循线性逻辑。如果你还有任何能调动的队伍—— 

[u.1:03] 地球和圣城需要我们，艾可拉。我们得在地球及领地巡逻，直到找到这些现象的源头。如果III之死是诱因，那就一定有修复损害的办法。【隐藏】，以及在那里发生的一切，在我们找到答案之前都得保密。 

//转录结束//

3868389601.name: Entry 7: Only from Pain
3868389601.text:
Division is the universe's force for creation. Reality is ripe with possibility when things spiral and fly and crash into each other. When the outcome becomes unpredictable, something happens: Possibility emerges. I can grab on to possibility. Widen the gyre that deafens the falcon and spins the center apart, as they say. 

All coalitions not grown from the inside out, but made instead by bringing outsiders together, have cracks through them. Foundational kintsugi can be exploited. A union made from gold is just nice to look at. Nothing is stronger than the monocoque, the single piece. 
This is Lume's "Imperium." For all the great gifts of flat time that VI has given us, the Imperium has not resolved the tension that animates its core. Lume has enjoyed decades in a moment, using VI's grace to propagate and train vast legions of Barant soldiers and weapons, to capture and recondition generations of Psions. But for all that effort, the Imperium still lacks the summative soul of a nation. Torobatl is still beyond his efforts. All he has built is a self-contradictory revanchist movement stitched together by grievances, garbed to look like an army. 

Shared hostility makes tight bonds, but the main partners—Barant, Psion—are still enemies. The would-be master and the defiant servant cinched together for millennia, bonds broken for centuries. They haven't shaken the pain. The soul remembers the imprint of the bindings. These tidy categories both hate Caiatl, but they hate her for different reasons; those reasons aren't germane here. 

What I can use is this: Barant and Psion have come to despise each other. The Barant see themselves as superior to the Psions. The Psions have never been free enough to consider themselves supreme. Lume will lose control of his coalition despite the powers afforded to him by our patron, VI. Lume's nascent state is fraying not from the edges, but from the center: the point of the stitch, where the binding is meant to be strongest.  

The Imperium will fail. I can see this in my dreams. I can read what trembles the fibers of reality. But until the Imperium collapses, I will use it to further my ultimate goals: Defeat the Vanguard; break their tyranny. I'll reach into the seams of his Imperium. Tug the right threads. Spiral them apart in a way that I can predict. Stoke the fires to burn in a controlled manner, prescribe the burn, and then search the violence for promising candidates necessary to complete my work. 

The Psions will be my first attempt. The fruit plucked from division's harvest. 

Cabal—Barant, especially—live long lives. Lume's project will fail, but he will endure. That is the Cabal nature, anyway, to endure. Even if he must use the last of his pliable muscles to drag his ossified corpse to Torobatl's shore, he will see it done, and I will be there with him. He has the last of my admiration; let this effort of mine be a test of his mettle, a lesson in pain that will prompt him to grow stronger. This is the lesson that VI confirmed for me: growth and knowledge can only come from pain. Ancient cultures practiced scarification. I do the same. 
  
VI, are you listening to me? Witness this vessel. I await your response.
3868389601.text_zh:
分裂是宇宙的创造之力。当事物飞旋、彼此碰撞时，现实便充满可能。当结果变得不可预测，会发生的事情便是：可能性显现。我可以抓住可能性。正如他们所说的，把那使鹘鹰耳聋、令中心分崩离析的漩涡扩大。 

凡不是自内而外生长、而是通过把外来者拼合起来的联盟，都遍布裂痕。基础的金缮会被利用来瓦解。以黄金粘合的结合体只适合观赏。没有什么比单体壳、单一个体更坚固。 
这就是卢梅的“帝国”。尽管VI赐予我们的平面时间有诸多伟大恩赐，帝国却始终未能化解驱动其核心的矛盾。卢梅在片刻之间享用了数十年，借VI的恩惠繁衍并训练了无数巴兰特士兵与武器，俘获并再塑了一代又一代灵能士兵。可尽管耗费如此心力，帝国依旧缺乏一个国家的终极之魂。图罗巴特尔仍是他无法企及之物。他所铸就的一切，不过是一场自相矛盾的复仇主义运动，被怨恨缝合起来，披上外衣使自身看似军队。 

共同的敌意能缔结紧密纽带，但其主要成员——巴兰特与灵能士兵——仍是仇敌。自封的主子和不屈的仆人，彼此拴系千年，纽带断裂数百年。他们未曾摆脱疼痛，灵魂仍记得束缚的印痕。这两个齐整的族群都憎恨查厄托，但他们恨她的理由不同；那些理由在这里无关紧要。 

我能利用的是：巴兰特与灵能士兵已开始彼此鄙弃。巴兰特自视高于灵能士兵，灵能士兵则从未获得足够的自由，能把自己视为至高。尽管恩赐者VI赋予了卢梅权能，他终将失去对其联盟的掌控。卢梅新生帝国的脱线并非始于边缘，而是其中心：缝合点，束缚本应最牢之处。  

帝国一定会失败。我在梦中见过。我能读出现实纤维的颤抖。但在帝国崩塌之前，我会利用它推动我的终极目标：击败先锋，粉碎他们的暴政。我会深入他帝国的接缝，拉扯合适的丝线，以我可以预测的方式把它们旋解。煽动火焰在可控的范围内燃烧，划定这场焚烧，然后在暴力中搜寻完成我事业所需的可期人选。 

我将首先尝试灵能士兵，那些摘自分裂之收获的果实。 

卡巴尔——尤其是巴兰特——寿命悠长。卢梅的计划会失败，但他会活下去。毕竟，活下去是卡巴尔的本性。即便他必须用最后一点尚可屈伸的肌肉，把那副石化的躯壳拖到图罗巴特尔的海岸，他也会把这事做成，而我会与他同行。我对他仍有最后的敬意；让我这番努力成为对他气魄的考验，一个痛苦的教训，促使他变得更强。这正是VI向我证实的教诲：唯有痛苦赋予成长与知识。古老的文化曾行疤痕纹身，我亦如此。 
  
VI，你在听吗？看看这具容器吧。我等待你的回应。

拉奥：
你手下的灵能士兵在烧毁前，与我维持连接的最长纪录是四十五秒。那点时间连让我开始构建互通的理解都勉强。不把更多心智与我的相联，我就无法形成承受这份负担所需的痛苦汇集器。够了，你要么是在拖延，要么是真的无能。 

你把最强的灵能士兵藏在哪儿？你们执行的任何任务都没有这件事重要；我是我们共同的恩赐者传递力量的通道。那股力量是我通过卢梅转给你的。把你最出色的手下送来与我分担这份重负，否则我会让卢梅撤掉你的总合部，然后把你用作我的主汇集器。

3868389603.name: Entry 9: Direct Me
3868389603.text:
It's not working. None of it is working. I can't get them to listen. Lume's Psions are too stuck in their dreams and their delusionary concept of the individual, the self, THEMselves. Arrogant. Selfish. There is a greater movement at work, and they're too myopic to understand the beauty of being a part of it. They are improper tools for the work I intend to put them to; it seems that I will not be able to dismantle the Vanguard with them.

I need you to help me, VI. I need you to speak to me, to speak through me, so that they can see. I would cut off their eyelids to force them to see, but only if you guided my hand. Speak! I need you to speak! Let me be your conduit!

Is this what Guardians feel with the Traveler so still? Do they feel a similar agony when the Light animates them? I have never seen a Guardian in pain—could it be that the Light protects them from that pain, or does it withhold its greater power and deny them a fuller strength?

There is an old word for Guardians who turned from the path of Light. I have seen it in my texts on Darkness: "Dredgen." A word given to the exiled by the preening arrogants that expelled them. I think I should use this word. I should give it a new meaning.

I can't stop trembling, but only the parts of me that have not yet been changed. Only anticipation, an animal's apprehension at a transformational moment of pain. Those that have been made in the shape of his vision are all the better at channeling his power. The agony shaped me from meat to beauty. Gave me meaning beyond a decaying body.

This is the thing Lume's Psions are afraid of: the pain. Only pain. That's so small. A rat fears pain. A frog. Creatures, beasts—these Psions claimed to be the mightiest beings in Sol, but they wither when I share a moment of my agonies with them. Pathetic. They refuse to accept that pain is a pathway into meaning, not merely the spasmodic firing of anguished nerves. Of course transcendence would be excruciating! What did they expect? To meditate themselves into absolute power? To relax into freedom?

Please, VI, direct my hands. Direct my feet. Direct my search to those who would more willingly become my Dredgens. Find me those who can endure the agonies necessary to become open to your power. I am your vessel, but the more I channel your strength without you, the more my own wanes.
3868389603.text_zh:
不行，全都不行，我没法让他们听话。卢梅的灵能士兵被困于自己的梦中，困在那虚妄的所谓个体、自我、他们自身的概念里。傲慢，自私。有一项更伟大的活动在运行，而他们目光短浅，不懂身为其中一部分的美妙。他们不是我实现计划的合适工具；看来没法靠他们去瓦解先锋。

我需要你的帮助，VI。我需要你和我说话，通过我说话，这样他们才能看清楚。我要割下他们的眼睑逼他们看，但需要你来引导我的手。开口吧！我需要你开口！让我成为你的通道吧！

旅行者沉寂时，守护者就是这种感受吗？光能驱动他们时，他们会承受类似痛楚吗？我从未见到守护者受苦——难道是光能保护他们免于此痛？还是说光能有所保留，不赐予他们更完整的力量？

以前有个词，用于形容那些偏离光能道路的守护者。我在暗影文献中看见过：“德瑞捷”。那些自命不凡的傲慢者用它来称呼被流放者。我觉得我该用用这个词，赋予它新的含义。

我停不下颤抖，但只有那些尚未被改变的部分在抖。那只是预期，是动物在经历转化之痛前的惶惧。那些已被塑成他愿景之形的部分，能更好地传导他的力量。苦痛把我从血肉雕凿为美丽之物，给了我超越朽坏躯体的意义。

这正是卢梅的灵能士兵害怕的：疼痛，只是疼痛而已，何其渺小。老鼠怕痛。青蛙怕痛。生物，禽兽怕痛——这些自称是太阳系最强大存在的灵能士兵，在我与他们分享片刻我的痛楚时就枯萎了，可悲。他们拒绝承认疼痛是通往意义的途径，而不只是抽搐的神经在哀嚎。超越凡世必然撕心裂肺！他们还指望什么？靠冥想通达绝对的力量？靠放松获得自由？

我请求你，VI，引导我的手，引导我的脚，引导我去寻找那些更愿意成为我的德瑞捷的人。助我找到能承受必须之痛、从而接受你力量的那些人。我是你的容器，但我越是在没有你的情况下传导你的力量，我自身就越发衰弱。

3868389604.name: Entry 1: The Engine of History
3868389604.text:
There is a level of suffering that I am quite used to, and then there is working with Caiatl's bureaucracy.

Moving this battle rifle platform through Caiatl's latest round of trials has dampened my spirits. Competition against the other foundries typically lifts my spirits, but not this time. I find myself wishing something terrible would happen to me. Maybe I will be struck by a meteor, so I no longer must suffer the signatures they ask of me in duplicate, triplicate, etc., etc. 

The Cabal marched into empire not just because of their legions, but also thanks to their armies of quartermasters, logisticians, factory-masters, armorers, and so on; their soldiers brought the stars to heel, yes, but only because of that greater force that kept them fed, fueled, and stocked with ordinance. One would think the soldiers of the Cabal to be arrogant, but in this twilight age of their state, I've found that the haughtiest and most entitled of the Cabal are the bureaucrats!

They stand in the way of progress, clutching their columns, tables, and limits like a border guard and his rifle. When I want to give soldiers what they ask for, some quartermaster lumbers over to tell me that I must not, for it would be too expensive. Small! Small minds who don't dream, but think in terms of cost, capital, and limits. Discard your limits, factory-masters and accountants. Follow your heart!

Father, when I can get him to emerge from his tinkerer's shed, only mutters about how we must cling to Tex Mechanica's "brand" of old-world class and style. Father's a sentimental dope, and I'm sick of having to wait for his nod of approval.  In the old world, people killed each other with less. They threw rocks. They fought with sticks. It's time for us to make something new. Until I run Tex Mechanica, I will push the firm into the future, despite him. I will follow the voices of soldiers and those who dare. That is how one keeps reverence for what came before, by responding to the will of the masses, who compose the very institutions these moribund leaders claim to represent!

Father eventually will understand. He must. Until then, I find camaraderie in the field. Bracus Lume, my liaison and the commander of the test unit that fields my weapon, understands and agrees. We have spent long hours together discussing many things. He serves as a muse to me: a rogue in uniform. He respects Caiatl, as a soldier must submit to their commander, but through his words, I can pick out the shape of his true intentions. He paints inspiring images of the Cabal before Calus, when they—as Lume so poetically put it—"made an empire in tribute to the sun." Brave Bracus Lume has dreams, like me. Dreams of liberation, of rousing history and leading it forward. Torobatl, their empire—I am moved by his vision, how similar it is to my own.

What weapon would we need to build to realize the aspirations of dreamers like Lume? That is what I ask of my designers and engineers. Imagine a weapon to be carried into the breach and beyond. A tool as mighty as the ones who wield it. Make Lume a weapon that he is proud to carry and let me be the vessel through which it is delivered. Of course, there is marketing in this thought but I don't think of my ask as something that base. We make weapons, not sugary drinks. We give power a body, milling it from inert metal into an implement that shakes the columns of reality itself. The bark of our beasts makes kings and tyrants just as mortal as the lowest of us. I want "Tex Mechanica" stamped on the side of the liberator's gun. I want us to be the engine of history. So, we begin with Lume.  

I will continue to tilt at those bureaucratic windmills, but I think now, at least, I do it with a steadfast squire as company. Together, we'll score a victory over that class of manicured, deskbound elites. They might think they can control the world with the stroke of a pen, a perfected spreadsheet, or the tweak of an allowance, but we'll show them that people with dreams should be the ones to make decisions. People united, individuals of supreme motivation, who wrest the tiller of history away from those who would prefer to crouch on their piles of Glimmer instead. 
It is time for dreamers to lead in a direction of their choosing.
3868389604.text_zh:
苦难我早已习以为常，但我无法忍受跟查厄托的官僚体系打交道。

把这套战斗步枪平台通过查厄托最新一轮的试行流程，让我心气大减。与其他铸造厂的竞逐通常能让我精神大振，但这次没有。我甚至盼着能有什么可怕的事发生在我身上。也许一颗陨石砸下来，我就不用再忍受他们要我签一式两份、一式三份乃至更多的文件了。 

卡巴尔得以成立帝国，不仅靠他们的军团，也要归功于他们成群的军需官、后勤官、工厂主、护甲商，等等；他们的士兵确实让群星屈膝，但只因那更庞大的力量让他们衣食饱、燃料足、军火丰。若说卡巴尔的士兵骄矜自大，在他们国势衰暮的当下，我反倒发现最骄纵、最自以为是的卡巴尔，是那些官僚！

他们站在进步前，死抱着他们的栏、表、限额，就像边防哨兵攥着步枪。当我想给士兵们他们所求的东西时，总有某个军需官摇摇晃晃地走过来说不行，因为太贵了。狭隘！思维狭隘，没有梦想的家伙，只会用成本、资本、限额来想问题。别总想着限额了，工厂主们、会计们。随心所愿吧！

父亲，只要我能把他从修补棚里拽出来，就会嘟囔我们必须守住特克斯机械那拥有旧世界的格调与风范的“品牌”。父亲多愁善感得傻气，而我厌倦了非要等他点头许可。在旧世界，人们为了一点小事就彼此杀戮。他们扔石头，挥舞木棒彼此争斗。我们该造点新东西了。在我接掌特克斯机械之前，我会不顾他的阻挠，把公司推向未来。我会倾听士兵与敢为之人的声音。对既往致敬的方式，就是回应大众的意志，那些组成了这些行将就木的领袖们声称自己所代表之机构的人们的意志！

父亲最终会明白的，他必须明白。而在那之前，我会在前线寻找同道。十夫长卢梅，我的联络人，试用我武器的部队的指挥官，理解并赞同我。我们畅谈了很多事情。他是我的缪斯：一个身着军装的浪子。他尊敬查厄托，正如士兵必须服从统帅，但从他的话里，我能辨识他真正意图的轮廓。卢梅描绘的卡巴尔——卡鲁斯之前的卡巴尔——以他那近乎诗意的话来说是“为致敬太阳而建立的帝国”。勇敢的十夫长卢梅也有梦想，如我一般的解放之梦，唤醒历史并引领其前行之梦。图罗巴特尔，他们的帝国——他的愿景打动了我，而我的愿景与之何其相似。

为了实现像卢梅这样的逐梦者的抱负，我们需要打造怎样的武器？这正是我对设计师和工程师提出的问题。设想一柄可被携入裂口的武器，与使用者一样强大的工具。为卢梅打造一件他引以为傲的武器，让我成为将其带入世间的容器。诚然，这里面也有市场的考量，但我并不把这诉求视为那样低俗的东西。我们造的是武器，不是饮料。我们为力量铸造一个躯体，把它从惰性的金属铣成足以撼动现实支柱的器具。我们野兽的吠声让王和暴君成为肉体凡躯，与我们中的最卑微者一般无二。我想在解放者之枪的侧面刻上“特克斯机械”，我想让我们成为历史的引擎。所以，我们从卢梅开始。  

我会继续向那些官僚的风车发起冲锋，但如今，我想至少我有了一位忠诚的扈从与我作伴。我们将齐心协力，面对那群修饰得体、困守案牍的精英阶层，拿下一场胜利。他们或许以为能凭笔尖的划动、一份完美的表格，或是额度调整来掌控世界，但我们会让他们见识到，负责做出决定的，应该是有梦之人，团结之人，受到至高驱动之人，从蹲在自己的微光堆上不肯起身的败类手中夺回历史舵柄之人。 
是时候让逐梦者朝他们选择的方向掌舵了。

3868389605.name: Entry 2: What Mother
3868389605.text:
I've known Mother to be dead for longer than I knew her alive. I remember small moments: Falling asleep on her shoulder as she carried me home at night after a holiday party. Teaching me to swim. Singing as she washed dishes. I remember feeling safe with her. Even when Father shouted, her voice would silence him. Protecting me. Memories that comforted me.
Until I saw her.

The market at Bonnet Plaza, in the West District. I was getting lunch outside the Mechanica home office. Caiatl's logisticians, Father's lickspittles, hiccups at Factories Three and Four—a miserable day.

I had interred her. She was ash. But in this moment, I saw my mother moving through the crowd with her Ghost flitting around her head. She had been dead for three years at this point. Somehow, the Light had found her. It seems all it needed was ash.

Two others chosen by the Light marched at her side, bristling with weapons, leashed to their puppeteers. The Chosen, on some holy business to save humanity. She glowed, flush with heat, as if the fire that cremated her now animated her from within. I cried out in horror, unable to stop myself. It made sense: of course the Traveler would grant my beloved mother the gift every child in the Last City    dreams of, every dying elder longs for, as they move away from the main of life. Eternal life without fear.

But when I embraced her, crying her name at the center of a cheering crowd, what did my mother do?

She shoved me away.

I felt the searing push of Solar energy in her strength. A sizzling reminder on my chest as I stumbled back and fell. Not a twinkle of recognition in her eyes, just discomfort, the look one gives a clamoring beggar that gets too close. Cold She was cold; she was hideous, a doppelganger, homunculus. Her chirping idiot of a Ghost commanded me to clear the way, and off they went. Bystanders helped me to my feet. Strangers, kinder than my own mother.

Is this the truth of the Light? Is this what it does? Animate the dead and possess them with Ghosts, puppeteers who keep them hooked to life like a fish on a lure? To prey on desperation and transfix the City in this poisoned dream? What miracle makes a mother spit on her child? My memories of her are now curses. Leaden dead weight. Every single one a searing ember.
3868389605.text_zh:
记忆中母亲去世后的时间，比我与她相处的时间更长。我记得些细碎的瞬间：节日派对后，她把我抱回家，我在她肩头睡着；她教我游泳；她一边洗碗一边唱歌。我记得与她在一起时的安全感。就算父亲吼起来，她的声音也能让他闭嘴。保护着我。这些回忆曾给予我安慰。
直到我看见了她。

那是在博内特广场的集市，西区的那个。我正在特克斯机械总部外吃午饭。查厄托的后勤官、巴结父亲的谄媚者、三号四号工厂的故障——糟糕透顶的一天。

我亲手安葬过她，她化成了灰。但就在这一刻，我看见我的母亲穿过人群，她的机灵在她的头顶盘旋。那时她已经死了三年。光能不知怎的找到了她。看来，只要有灰烬，就能铸造负光者。

还有另外两名被光能选中的人紧随其侧，全副武装，被他们的傀儡师牵着。他们是神选者，肩负着某种拯救人类的神圣使命。她在发光，热气腾腾，仿佛当初火葬时的火焰如今自内而外地驱动着她。我不由自主地惊叫起来。那合乎情理：旅行者当然会将每个圣城孩子梦寐以求、每个垂死老人望眼欲穿的礼物——无惧的永生——赐予我挚爱的母亲。

但当我上前拥抱她，在欢呼的人群中央呼喊她的名字时，我的母亲做了什么呢？

她把我推开了。

我在她的力道里感到了烈日能量的灼烧。胸口被烫得生疼，我踉跄着后退倒下。她眼中没有一丝辨识，只有不适，是人们对靠得太近的叫嚷乞丐会有的那种眼神。冷，她好冷漠；她如此丑陋，是冒牌货，造物。她那只叽叽喳喳的蠢机灵命令我让开，然后他们扬长而去。旁观者把我扶起。那些陌生人，比我自己的母亲还要友好。

这就是光能的真相吗？这就是它所做的？让死人站起来，让他们被机灵附体、操纵，像上了钩的鱼一样被拖拽着活下去？以绝望为食，将圣城困在这场有毒的梦中？什么样的奇迹，会让母亲唾弃自己的孩子？我对她的记忆如今成了诅咒，铅一样沉重，每一段都是灼心的余烬。

3868389606.name: Entry 3: A Hierarchy of Pain
3868389606.text:
My dear friend Bracus Lume has been deployed, likely to some miserable theater in Sol as part of Caiatl's efforts to stymie the Hive. If my father had any passion left, I would believe Lume's deployment to be part of a plot to stop me. A favor asked for and granted. A reminder that my efforts, clients, accounts, and so on, are given to me by him. The generosity of an overbearing father: my life, from his largesse.

However, my allies within Tex Mechanica have not been able to source any missives, directives, or dictates from Father's office to stop my project. He spends his time tinkering on museum pieces and Vanguard baubles. I wonder if he even knows the world exists beyond his workbench; his cruelty is bottomless. He is a clever coward, and this retreat from the world is a favorite tactic of his.

I think he wishes for me to rot in the family estate and be quiet again. I was a quiet child and he, a colossus. I would shroud myself and slip through the cold halls of our home, fleeing the muffled sounds of his rage—a phantom by choice, to protect myself. When mother grew ill and died, my father fell silent, listless. This was his first retreat. Father ignored me so profoundly that I truly believed myself to be invisible. It made me think that I had died with my mother. That was even more terrifying than his rage; I was losing my father as well.

But now, I am older and braver. Father may or may not have clipped my wings. I don't care. I will take care of myself. I am used to being alone. But I also have been exploring other ways of being, even those prohibited by the Vanguard. 

There are fascinating texts in this world. Volumes and folios that speak of clarity in purpose and the methods to attain it. I have tried many—meditation, religion, self-actualization—but they all failed, save for one: an old text of assured providence, an exegesis on the sermons of Twin Bird, of the Binary Star. Agony and pain exist, Twin Bird once said, but not all pain is meaningless. Some pain hones. It hammers bladed agony into shape, and an edge is made. Utility formed as a survival mechanism, making the afflicted sharper. 

So I began to run. Thousands of steps, each a moment of pain. Each a nail, pinning me to the present. The pain worked. The pain guided me. The pain led me to power. The Vanguard and Twin Bird both called it Darkness. I call it a new path. 

The Light comes for you in death, and only if it chooses. But Darkness is always there, within, waiting for you to grasp it and pull it to the surface. And so I had a revelation: I needed to attempt communion. I planned routes to run that took me deeper into the City. Down among the people, in their parks, in their streets, full of sound and life and beings—others who did not fear life but made it, composed its raw cacophony, all a part of a pattern so vast, I could not perceive it. But I was, too, one of its parts; the petri dish is a pandemonic universe to the single cell, but utterly still to the human eye.

I think the Light is selfish. To see the state of the Last City below the Vanguard's Olympian refuge is to understand this. The Light sends out its little Ghosts and elevates only the dead whom it deems worthy, never touching the desperate living. It pulls them up to the graceful decks of the Tower, damning the rest to live without its gift. This story is common among the citizens of the Last City. I should know: It happened to me, too.

My mother died and was returned and abandoned me. My father consigned me to the annals of his memory and moved on as if I, too, were already dead. But in the City, the people welcomed me. The dockworkers, the vagrants, the shopkeepers, everyone hurrying on every errand, all denied the Light's gift, but were subject to its rule. I disappeared among them, but I was not consciously forgotten by them. I was not spurned by them. At any moment on one of my excursions, I could stop and talk to someone, to have a moment of connection, to see them as well. I moved among them as one of them, an equal in dreams and aspiration, seen and heard. 
  
The Traveler has the power to shape reality, and yet there are beggars in the low districts of the Last City. There are children that go hungry. The streets are policed. From where do violence and crimes of desperation spring? The individual rendered miserable before their birth, or the great systems above them that maintain the status quo? My own wealth—though it can be stripped from me—is not a shield. It is not a weapon. It is fiat. Exchange, only as long as I play within the bounds of the Light's rules. 

There is a pattern to who the Light picks. I think it chooses based on how jagged the hierarchy of pain will become when it intervenes. I think the Light wants to hurt me. But the Darkness wants me to do something with that pain.
3868389606.text_zh:
我的好友十夫长卢梅已被派往前线，大概是作为查厄托遏制邪魔族行动的一部分，被丢到了太阳系某个悲惨的战区。如果我的父亲还剩半点热情，我会以为卢梅被调派是为了阻止我——他求来的一份人情，用来提醒我，我的努力、客户、账户等等，都是他给的。专横父亲的慷慨：我的一生，皆出自他的施舍。

然而，我在特克斯机械的盟友没从父亲的办公室里找到任何意在阻止我计划的公函、指示或法令。他把时间都花在摆弄博物馆藏品和先锋的玩意上。我不知道他是否还能感知到工作台之外世界的存在；他的残酷无穷无尽。他是个聪明的懦夫，这种避世之举正是他的拿手好戏。

我觉得他希望我在祖宅里腐烂，再次变得安静。我小时候很安静，而他像座巨像。我会隐蔽起来，穿行在家中阴冷的长廊间，逃离他闷声的怒火——主动选择做个幽灵以保护自己。母亲生病去世后，父亲变得沉默、无精打采，而这里是他的第一个避世所。父亲对我置若罔闻，几乎让我真心以为自己是隐形的，仿佛我和母亲一起死了。那比他的怒火更可怕；我连父亲也失去了。

但现在，我长大了，也更勇敢了。父亲或许剪断了我的翅膀，或许没有，我不在乎。我会照顾我自己。我已习惯了独处。但我也在探索其他存在的可能性，甚至还包括那些被先锋所禁止的。 

这世上有许多迷人的文本。卷帙与册页，论述着明确的目标与达成的方法。我尝试过许多——冥想、宗教、自我实现——但它们都失败了，唯一的例外是一篇许诺天命的古文，阐释了来自双生之星的双鸟的布道。双鸟曾说，苦难与疼痛确实存在，但并非所有痛苦都毫无意义。有些痛苦是磨砺，它把刀锋般的痛苦锤打成形，铸成利刃。功用作为求生机制而生，让受难者更锋利。 

于是我开始奔跑。成千上万的步伐，每一步都是片刻的疼痛。每一步都是一根钉，将我钉在当下。疼痛生效了，引导着我，带我获取力量。先锋与双鸟都称其为暗影，我称之为一条新的道路。 

光能在你死去时才来，还得被它选中。但暗影始终存在于内里，静待你去抓住它，将它拽向表层。于是我顿悟：我需要去尝试交流。我规划了带我前往圣城更深处的奔跑路线，深入群体之中，在他们的公园、街道之中，充满声响、生命和存在——那些不惧生活而是去创造它的人们，谱写出其原始的嘈杂，一切都属于某个宏大的图样，宏大到我无法感知。但我也是其中一部分；对单个细胞而言，培养皿便是喧闹的宇宙，它在人的眼中却静止不动。

我觉得光能是自私的。只要看看先锋的奥林匹斯式高阁下方，圣城的境况，就能明白这一点。光能派出它的小小机灵，只将它认为值得的死者唤起，从不接触那些迫切需要帮助的生者。它把他们拉到高塔那雅致的台面上，拒绝给予其他人恩赐。这种故事在圣城的市民中很常见，我最清楚不过：因为这也发生在了我身上。

我的母亲死而复返，抛下了我。我的父亲把我投进他记忆的年表，继续前行，仿佛我也已经死了。但在圣城里，人们欢迎我。码头工人、流浪者、店主，每个奔忙的人，全都被光能的恩赐所拒绝，却又受其统治。我隐匿其中，但他们并未有意识地遗忘我，没有排斥我。任何一次外出，我都可以停下，与人交谈、获得一刻联系，也看见他们。我行走在他们之间，是他们中的一员，在梦想与愿望上与他们平等，被看见、被听到。 
  
旅行者有塑造现实的力量，可圣城的贫民区依然有乞丐，依然有挨饿的孩子，街道上有警卫巡视。暴力与因绝望而生的罪行从何而来？是个体在出生之前就注定凄惨身世，还是高悬其上的巨大体系维持了既有秩序？我自身的财富——即便可以被剥夺——并非护盾，亦非武器，只是法币。只有我在光能的规则边界内行事，它才具备交换价值。 

光能的选择自有其模式。我认为它的偏好取决于干预后，痛苦层级的剧烈程度。我认为光能想要伤害我，而暗影想要我用那份痛苦做点什么。

3868389607.name: Entry 4: Paper Histories
3868389607.text:
Tex Mechanica is a huge, old foundry. At its height, the Mechanica had multiple proving grounds, distribution centers, autofabricators, and other facilities across Sol. We even used to build ships! Though we were never good at it. That was centuries ago, when the tide was high, before the Vanguard determined that contraction and consolidation to the Last City was the prudent move. Squash the frontier, they said. Focus on one stronghold and its satellites.

Father, though he is fantastically wealthy and powerful, is a king at the end of a dynasty. He's the sucker left holding the bag as the house lights come on. What is Tex Mechanica in the age of the Last City? A sporting goods supplier. A widget factory for the Guardians of the Vanguard. A toolmaker for a junta, always building larger and deadlier weapons to face an enemy that is always approaching, never arriving. What do they face next? An arms dealer loves that question because it has no answer—only fear.

I leave my father to figure it out without me. To play weapons-master to undead tyrants. I have a new faith now. A new way forward. The pursuit of freedom and understanding hidden by the Vanguard—this is my task that I take up without guilt and with clear eyes. I am willing to pay any cost; I think of my dear friend Bracus Lume, who has returned from the Hive front terribly wounded by one of their most vicious paracausal weapons. He convalesces in orbit (Father denied him the use of our personal medical suite on campus here) but still insists on fighting to live for a tomorrow he so furiously believes in. I should do the same.

Together, Lume and I make a mighty intellectual and spiritual pair. He, the soldier, and me, the dreamer. Our correspondence sharpens our desire and renders in actual fact the targets of our heady dreams. Father, the Vanguard, and the Guardians are too removed from the people of The City that they might as well oppose their liberation! The current order restrains their growth, restricts them to huddling behind high walls, fearing nightmares beyond them. This ruling elite demands we cow to their dictates and proscribes any group or individual that speaks against them. Caiatl and her Cabal are much the same to Lume and his soldiers, he assures me. Her father twisted what it meant to be Cabal, and though she deposed him, she has not fixed what he broke.

Forces, ideologies, and thoughts opposed to these twin malignancies are deemed evil, dark, and wrong by the institutions they threaten. I ask—what is evil about opposing tyranny? Neither the Vanguard nor Caiatl will abdicate without a fight; liberating the City will take a mass movement, which I don't yet have. However, a small cell that is committed to the cause, acting at the right time and in the most critical places? A bullet is ignited by a firing pin; great movements need a catalyst. The people of The City cry out for one.

I could be the one who brings about the first wave of change. Should I not grasp any weapon, tool, or thought afforded to me to oppose a foe that separates mothers from their children? I have availed myself of the deep records Tex Mechanica keeps hidden in its off-book archives. Paper histories. Nothing that can be searched unless one is physically present. Our guns once barked as vicious dogs across the ruins of fallen Earth. Once, we made tools for seekers on the frontier who used our weapons to carve new paths into the future. According to my research, these weapons became more than their first form.

I, the shunned heir of Tex Mechanica, have scrubbed my name and history from our archives. I go out into the darkness away from home, as our weapons before have. I will find a new name. I will sound out across the frontier and then come home to address the world the Light has built.
3868389607.text_zh:
特克斯机械是一家巨大而古老的铸造厂。全盛时，公司在太阳系各处都有试炼场、配送中心、自动制造机和其他设施。我们甚至还造过飞船！虽然我们从不擅长。那是几个世纪前，涨潮之时，在先锋认定收缩并整合到圣城才是谨慎之举前。他们说要收紧边界，专注于一个据点然后辐射出去。

父亲虽富可敌国、权势滔天，却是末代君王。灯亮人散后，手里还攥着烂摊子的冤大头。在圣城纪元，特克斯机械算什么？不过是家体育用品供应商，为先锋的守护者提供小器件的工厂，为一个军事体打磨工具的工匠，不断制造更庞大、更致命的武器来对付一个永远逼近、却从未抵达的敌人。他们接下来要对付什么？军火商最爱这个问题，因为它没有答案——只有恐惧。

我把这个问题留给父亲，让他独自去琢磨，去当不死暴君的武器大师。我如今有了新的信仰，新的前行道路。追求被先锋藏起来的自由与理解——这是我无愧承担且有清晰远见的任务。我愿付出任何代价；我想到了我的好友十夫长卢梅，他从邪魔族前线归来，被敌人最凶残的超因果武器重创。他正在轨道上疗养（父亲拒绝让他使用我们在园区内的私人医疗套间），但仍坚持为狂热相信的明天而活下去。我也该如此。

我和卢梅是强有力的思想与精神搭档，他是战士，而我是梦想家。互相通信磨砺我们的渴望，将我们那些激昂梦想之中的目标化为现实。父亲、先锋和守护者远远脱离圣城的民众，可以说是在阻挠人民的解放！当前的秩序束缚了他们的成长，把他们限制在高墙之后，惧怕墙外的梦魇。统治精英要求我们向其法令低头，并将任何反对他们的群体和个人列为禁忌。查厄托与她的卡巴尔，对待卢梅和他的士兵们也差不多是如此，这也是他亲口告诉我的。查厄托的父亲扭曲了卡巴尔的精神，尽管她推翻了他，却没修复他造成的破坏。

与这两个毒瘤对立的力量、意识形态与思想，被它们所威胁的机构打成邪恶、黑暗与错误。我要问——反抗暴政哪点邪恶了？无论是先锋还是查厄托都不会不战而退；要解放圣城会需要一场群众运动，但我尚未推动成形。然而，一个小而坚定的组织，在正确的时机、最关键的地点发动行动呢？子弹由击针点燃；伟大的运动需要催化剂。圣城的人民迫切需要着这样的激发。

我或许能成为掀起第一波变革的人。我难道不该抓住任何可得的武器、工具或思想，去对抗那个让母亲与孩子分离的敌人吗？我研读了特克斯机械机密档案中隐藏的深层记录。那些纸质的历史。除非亲临其处，否则无法检索。曾几何时，我们的枪声如恶犬在陨落的地球废墟中狂吠；曾几何时，我们为边界的探索者打造工具，他们用我们的武器在未来中凿出新路。据我研究，这些武器超越了它们的初始形态。

我这个被特克斯机械所疏斥的继承人，已将自己的名字与经历从我们的档案中抹去。我离开家，投向黑暗，循着我们的武器曾经走过的路。我会寻找一个新名字，让它响彻边界，然后回到家乡，直面那个光能构筑的世界。

3868389608.name: Entry 5: A Conduit for All Futures
3868389608.text:
Lume calls his people "Barant": a name once used by and for his kind. One, he says, they are still owed as children of Torobatl. "Cabal" is a name without weight; it is the label, Lume says, of decrepit imperial bureaucrats. A dry moniker.

Lume's Barant are raucous in their new identity. They worship their distant home star, the heroes who once fought in her name, and the dream that they might pile banners of the conquered upon her plazas once more. They strip themselves bare and howl their praise to Torobatl, calling her warrior and queen, boasting so that she might hear and smile upon them. They trample the ground into a migratory temple, ennobling it with the impressions of their feet. They make orbits of worship around their old idols, mighty challenge columns, as their ancestors did on her plains. Though born on an alien world, Lume's Barant are fierce patriots for a homeland they have never once beheld. This fervor inspires me, this clear dream, this grand project.

Lume has given me a gift: an awareness of this type of power. The Vanguard and the Light have their silent deity in the Traveler, but their celebrations are muted. They do not bid the people to exult in their power because they do not want people to realize their power. They want only the Guardians to be powerful, only the Vanguard to be mighty. I want all humanity to be strong. I want us to celebrate alongside the Barant as they do, but with our own undeniable strength.

My teachers—my brother Lume, my long-dead master Twin Bird—both speak of the same thing, which I have now found for myself. Years ago, I exercised my body through rituals of agony. As I write, it appears this new power will do likewise for me. My vision will be made clear, and with that clarity, I will actualize. I will become greater than the gifted.

I had found a place of power on Europa. A trove of artifacts tainted with Darkness. Rumors of real power, hidden deep within a forgotten Praxic temple. I took a maniple of Lume's most fearsome volunteers into that place, losing many to the elements before we even reached its entrance. It was sweltering inside, the air so thick with damp dust that we were burning our filters at thrice the baseline. Lume's warriors chanted liturgical cadences to fill the halls with celebration from the deep organs, but that dead place swallowed all sounds they made. They thought it was a trick of acoustics or some other paracausal phenomenon, and so they armed themselves accordingly. But the closer we approached the heart of the temple, the more I grew assured of the futility of conventional weapons.

I began to hear a voice. A whisper. Not one of us or Lume, who was watching from his convalescing bed aboard our ship. A new voice, just for me.

In the heart of the temple was a great sepulcher that contained a fantastic, glittering crystal. From my studies, I knew it to be a crystal of Stasis, a paracausal manifestation of Darkness, that power to which I had spent years attuning my body and mind. I touched it, and invited power in.

A voice. His voice. Lume still swears it was a devil of unknown power who spoke to me, but I know the truth. Unseen, a voice leaped between his soldiers, possessing them to speak one word at a time. A message born from howling pain that found its final home in me. The agony was unrelenting, the pain immense, but I had prepared for this moment for years. I did not ignite. My soul did not burn out. The devil's voice became my voice, and the devil became me, and I understood: This was not a devil. This was not the Light. It was not even the Darkness. This was a third power. A new thing. My own path.

TO SATURN, the voice and I cried. TO THE RINGS, MY WEAPON.

VI. This was the name of the great one, the third power. VI held my hand and showed me Lume wounded and Lume mighty, myself wounded and myself mighty. VI. This was the power's name. Tombs and temples. We entered a tomb and made it a temple with our cries, as the Barant once stamped migration prayers into Torobatl's dirt, as I once ran through the halls of my family manor fearing and yearning.

In the quiet after, I was alone. Lume bellowed in my aurals, screaming at me in fury for the death of his brethren. He swore to kill me when I returned, but I knew he would not, so I told him, and I began to laugh and made him another promise: I would heal his wound, erase the Hive magic that rotted him from the inside out.

I am happy. I was chosen. I had been right. I was the vessel; my actions—perhaps from even before my birth, but certainly from the moment I became conscious—were guided by these hands that now rested on my shoulders. My explorations of Darkness, my readings and agonies, were indeed the method by which I would attain a power that could be shared among the masses, a counterweight to the Light—but it would have to begin with me. It could only begin with me.

I am, was, and will be the conduit through which all futures flow.
3868389608.text_zh:
卢梅把他的人称为“巴兰特”：这是曾经被他们用来称呼自己的名号。他说，作为图罗巴特尔的子嗣，他们理当继承这个称号。“卡巴尔”这个名字毫无分量；卢梅说，它只是衰朽帝国官僚的标签，一个干巴巴的称谓。

卢梅的巴兰特因他们获得的新身份而喧腾不已。他们崇拜遥远的故乡恒星，曾以她之名战斗的英雄，那重新在她的广场上堆叠征服旗帜的梦想。他们褪去衣物，对图罗巴特尔嘶吼赞歌，称她为战士和女王，夸耀以盼她听见并对他们展颜。他们将脚下大地践踏成一座迁徙的神殿，以足迹赋予其尊荣。他们围绕古老的崇拜象征——高耸的挑战之柱——虔诚而行，正如其祖先曾在她的平原上所为。虽生于异乡星球，卢梅的巴兰特却热爱着一片从未亲眼目睹的家园。这股狂热，这份清晰之梦，这项宏伟计划，鼓舞着我。

卢梅赠与了我一件礼物：对这种力量的感知。先锋与光能有他们无言的神——旅行者，但他们的庆典寡淡无声。他们不召唤众人共襄盛大的力量，因为他们不愿让人意识到自身的力量。他们只想守护者强大，只想先锋显赫。我想要全人类都强盛，与巴兰特一道庆贺，但要凭我们自身无可置疑的力量。

我的老师们——我的兄弟卢梅，我早已逝去的导师双鸟——都曾提到同一件事，一件我如今也意识到的事。多年前，我以苦痛的仪式锻炼躯体。如今书写之时，我看出这股新的力量将以同样方式起作用。我的愿景将澄明，随之我将得以践行。我将超越那些受到馈赠的人。

我在木卫二找到一处力量的源泉，一批受暗影玷染的神器。传言在一座被遗忘的英勇圣殿深处，藏有真正的力量。我带了一支由卢梅最骁勇的手下自发组成的队伍进入那处所在，尚未到达入口，已折损多人。殿内闷热，空气潮尘稠密，滤芯消耗达基线的三倍。卢梅的战士以宗教圣咏标定步伐，用胸腔深处的声音为长廊注入欢赞，但那死寂之所吞没了他们的一切声响。他们以为这是声学诡计，或是某种超因果现象，于是依此武装自己。但我们越接近圣殿中心，我就越是确信常规武器终将徒劳。

我开始听见一个声音，某种耳语。那既非同行之人，也非正卧于我们舰上病床远程观望的卢梅。是一个新的声音，只有我能听见。

在圣殿中心有一座巨大的石棺，内藏一块奇妙而璀璨的晶体。依我的研究，那是冰影水晶——暗影的超因果显化——是我多年调律身心所追寻的力量。我触碰它，邀力量入体。

一个声音，他的声音。卢梅仍坚称是某个来历不明的魔鬼与我言语，但我知道真相。那看不见的存在，在他的士兵间跳跃，附身于他们，让他们一次只吐出一个字。一个由嚎叫之痛所生的信息，最终在我身上找到了归宿。痛楚毫不松懈，苦难浩大，但我为此刻已准备多年。我没有燃烧起来，我的灵魂没有焚竭。魔鬼的声音成了我的声音，魔鬼成了我，而我随之明白：这不是魔鬼，不是光能，甚至也不是暗影。这是第三种力量，一种新的事物，我自己的道路。

去土星，那个声音与我同呼，去环带，我的武器。

VI，这是那伟大存在、那第三种力量的名字。VI挽住我的手，令我见到负伤的卢梅与强盛的卢梅，负伤的我与强盛的我。VI，这是这股力量的名字。坟与殿，我们踏入坟墓，以呼号将其化作神殿，正如巴兰特昔日将迁徙祷文踏印进图罗巴特尔的泥土，正如我曾在家族宅邸的走廊中奔逃、恐惧和渴望。

寂静落下之后，我孑然一身。我听见卢梅在怒吼，为他同袍之死而对我咆哮。他发誓要在我归去时杀了我，但我知道他不会，于是我如此告知他，而后大笑，又许下一个诺言：我会治愈他的伤，抹去让他自内而外腐烂的邪魔族魔法。

我很快乐，我被选中了，我一开始就是对的。我是容器；我的一切行为——或许自我出生前，至少自我有意识之刻起——皆由如今按在我肩上的手所引导。我对暗影的探索、我的阅读与苦修，确实是获得可在众人间分享之力量的方法，是对抵光能的砝码——但它必须由我开始，也只能由我开始。

我之于所有未来，现在是、曾经是、将来亦是通道。

3868389609.name: Entry 6: Nine Thoughts out of Time
3868389609.name_zh: 记录6：时间之外的九个念想
3868389609.text:
• I can kill Ghosts faster than new Guardians can be raised.

• "There is a world beyond this one."

• The walls that keep us in are feeble. One more push. Take a hammer out and whack away the keystone.

• I have a sword now. Like the dead Ghosts, I took it from the heart of the enemy   and made it to be dim and still and without Light. That makes my sword cut better.  I've killed Guardians. I've killed a couple, and they didn't think I could, but what do they think now? Nothing. They're dead, and I have their Ghosts slapping against my thigh. Kiss my ass.

• I want to go back to the City. I don't want to hurt anymore. I want to be with everyone and have them pick me up. I miss the feeling of hands on me. Among the people, I was never a phantom; I was a moment waiting to be met. The masses were my first love, how much potential a crowd holds, how many dreams.

• Time is a thought that goes backward and forward; that's how VI shares it with me. He promises me things that haven't happened yet and says they have. If they're done, why does he make me wait?

• I wanted to be a Guardian as a kid, and now, I would slap myself for wanting that. I'm more. I'm many things more. Cadmium, lead, metallic hydrogen, platinum. I'm elements you've never seen larger than a milligram. I am more than what I was. Agony and grace.

• To be a Dredgen is to endure this and more. Give me more. I'm not done yet.

• Mother, talk to me. I need to know. VI, if you can hear me, if you are there, I beg you—show her to me again.
3868389609.text_zh:
• 我杀死机灵的速度，快过新守护者被唤起的速度。

• “在此世之外，别有一界。”

• 禁锢我们的墙壁脆弱不堪。再推一下。取一把锤子，猛砸那枚拱顶石。

• 我有一把刀剑。像那些死去的机灵，我从敌方的核心夺过它，令其昏黯、寂静、无光。那让我的刀剑更加锋利。我杀过守护者，杀过好几个。他们没想到我能做到，可如今他们又作何感想？什么感想也没有。他们死了，而他们的机灵则被我系在腰间，晃来荡去。

• 我想回到圣城。我不想再疼痛难忍。我想与众人待在一起，让他们把我托起。我想念手落在身上的感觉。置身人群，我从不是幽魅；我是一段即将相逢的时刻。大众是我最初的爱恋，群体中蕴藏着多么巨大的潜能，多少梦想。

• 时间是一种向前亦向后的思想；VI与我分享了它。他向我许诺尚未发生之事，说它们已经发生。如果真是这样，那他为什么还要让我等待？

• 小时候我想成为守护者，如今，我会给那个自己一记耳光，以惩戒那个渴望。我如今已超越守护者，远远超越。是镉、铅、金属氢、铂，我是你从未见到超过毫克量级的元素。我已今非昔比，承受着苦难与恩宠。

• 要成为德瑞捷，就是要忍受这一切，甚至更多。给我更多，我还能行。

• 母亲，和我说话，我需要知道。VI，若你能听见，若你还在，我求你——再让我见她一次。

1370484808.name: Modified NLS Courier
1370484808.subtitle: In competent hands, it glides through the dark like a specter.
1370484808.subtitle_zh: 在行家操控下，它如幽魂般在黑暗中轻盈穿梭。
1370484808.text:
The time has come for we Barant to make known our supremacy. A single Barant is strong, but strength is not enough. We must be enduring. To endure we must persist beyond the individual: we must make for ourselves a state. But a state cannot exist without war, and war demands a state to exist. Therefore, we must make both in parallel. We begin by breaking away from our current associations with the feeble Imperial Cabal. 

The Hive, our foe eternal, think they are clever. They have made war for billions of years and, through that exercise, believe they have winnowed all questions of existence down to their root: "Do you live, or do you die?" This is not a question, any soldier tempered in fire understands this. The ultimate question can only be asked once victory is achieved: "Will you dictate reality, or will you be subject to another's?" 

From birth, I was raised knowing the Cabal dictated reality. Torobatl, the heart taken from us by the Hive, proved me wrong; they gored our Empire on THEIR truth. But the question of our right to exist was not settled on that day. Enemies within and without have tried to dictate our reality, but they have not yet succeeded. We still live, and so now we will prepare our answer. We will engage the enemy in our war. 

Our war will be the ultimate question. My comrades, do not fear the unknown beyond Saturn. Embrace this journey. Though we enter a strange time, we will exit it at the moment of our choosing—and bring with us our Barant state, our Barant war, and our victorious Barant reality.

- Printed Address of Premier Lume on the Ultimate Question, as Interpreted by Barantist Thought.
1370484808.text_zh:
我们巴兰特彰显至高地位的时刻已到。单个巴兰特固然强大，但仅有力量还不够。我们必须持久，而要持久就必须超越个体延续：我们必须为自己缔造一个国家，但国家没有战争便无法存续，而战争也需要国家来维持。因此，我们必须并行打造二者。我们首先要从与软弱的帝国卡巴尔的现有关系中脱离出来。 

邪魔族，我们永恒的敌人，自以为聪明。他们发动了数十亿年的战争，并通过这般操练，相信已将一切存在之问筛至根本：“生存，还是死亡？”这不是问题，任何在火中淬炼过的战士都明白。终极问题只可在胜利达成后发问：“你将主宰现实，还是屈服于他人的现实？” 

自出生起，我便在卡巴尔主宰现实的观念下长大。图罗巴特尔，那被邪魔族从我们身上夺走的心脏，证明我错了；他们用“他们的真理”刺穿了我们的帝国。但关于我们是否有权存在的问题，并未在那一天尘埃落定。内外之敌试图主宰我们的现实，但他们尚未成功。我们仍然活着，于是现在我们将筹备答案。我们将在我们的战争中与敌交锋。 

我们的战争将成为终极问题。同志们，不要畏惧土星之外的未知。拥抱这段旅程。虽迈入怪异之时，但我们将于自己择定的时刻离开——并携我们的巴兰特国家、巴兰特战争，以及铸就于胜利的巴兰特现实同行。

——《首席卢梅关于终极问题之演说》，巴兰特主义思想阐释本

3272276569.name: Hostile Territory
3272276569.subtitle: "Hometown advantage just ain't what it used to be." —Tulnik
3272276569.subtitle_zh: “主场优势已今非昔比。”——图尔尼克
3272276569.text:
Prak'kesh tossed his half-eaten batadactyl wing to a scraggly war beast lounging at the base of the Tower.  

"Vanguard oughta do something about those strays," groused Tulnik, his ex-Corsair bodyguard. "They get big enough, it'll be our bones they're chewing." 

Prak'kesh shrugged. "Vanguard don't give a hot damn what goes on down here. Besides, that's what I hire you for. Speaking of… look lively." 

A trio of Hunters in all black approached, their capes flapping like a murder of blackbirds. Tulnik casually rested his hand on his Fatebringer. 

The lead Threadrunner swaggered up to Prak'kesh. "We wanna bet on Hunters to win the Games." 

"You got the Glim for it, killer?" Prak'kesh sucked at the batadactyl meat stuck between his teeth. "The Superblack look ain't exactly screaming 'high roller.'" 

"We got something even better." The Hunter pulled aside his cape to reveal a Praxic Blade slung from his hip. 

Prak'kesh let out a low whistle. "Praxics know you're stealing their scraps?" 

"Why? You scared?" the Hunter sneered. "They're not gonna be around long enough to find out." He looked up at the Tower with contempt. "Neither is the Vanguard."  

"Oh yeah?" Prak'kesh said mildly. "I don't really deal in religious paraphernalia. Pawn it off and come back with some real Glim. Then we'll see about your bet." 

The Hunters stalked away begrudgingly. "You might wanna think about whose side you're on," the Threadrunner called over his shoulder. "Don't wanna be under this Tower when it falls, do ya?"
3272276569.text_zh:
普拉凯什把吃剩一半的翼手蝠翅扔向一头在高塔的基座旁打盹的邋遢战兽。  

“先锋总得管管这些流浪动物，”他的前海盗军保镖图尔尼克抱怨道，“它们再长大点，啃的就是咱们的骨头了。” 

普拉凯什耸了耸肩。“先锋才懒得管这下面的屁事。再说了，我花钱雇你是来干嘛的？提到这个…精神点儿。” 

三名黑衣猎人走上前来，他们的披风如鸦群翻飞。图尔尼克不动声色地将手按在了命运终结者上。 

为首的丝线跑手大摇大摆地走到普拉凯什面前。“我们想下注赌猎人赢得本次竞技。” 

“微光带够了吗，杀手？”普拉凯什嘬着卡在牙缝里的翼手蝠肉，“你们这身超黑造型可没有豪掷千金的派头。” 

“我们带了更好的东西。”猎人拉开披风，腰间赫然别着一把英勇利刃。 

普拉凯什发出一声低哨。“英勇教团知道你们偷了他们的玩意儿吗？” 

“怎么，你怕了？”猎人嗤笑道，“他们在发觉前就会完蛋。”他不屑地瞥了一眼高塔。“先锋也一样。”  

“哦，是吗？”普拉凯什淡淡说道，“我对宗教物件没兴趣。把它当了，换成真正的微光再来。到时候我们再谈你们的赌注。” 

猎人们悻悻离去。“我劝你好好斟酌下自己的立场，”那名丝线跑手头也不回地撂下一句话，“等这座高塔倒塌的时候，你也不想为它陪葬吧？”

253843484.name: Turncoat
253843484.subtitle: Pull the trigger. Feed your appetite.
253843484.text:
Traitor. Irredeemable traitor.

"Shut up," Churnbower muttered. He clutched the handle of the weapon case tight, as if to choke the nightmare hidden inside. 

Having regrets? Too late. I'm in your mind, Churnbower. I CAN SAY WHAT I WANT. 

Churnbower stumbled, snatching his bandaged, bloody hand to his head. 

That heat in your veins is me. You brought me to life. Can't get me out now. 

"Shut up." 

A tech approached him. "Director, are you OK?" 

"Get back to your station," Churnbower snapped at her. "Or I'll write you up." Her face fell, concern replaced by anger. Other technicians looked over at the sudden outburst with surprise, curiosity. 

You've caused a scene! Which of them will tell our Lord what you have done? 

Churnbower's wounded hand throbbed. "No more," he moaned. Glyphs squirmed across his field of vision, echoing the hideous markings he had etched across this weapon. He whimpered. 

Tithe to me again: Free me. Wield me and I will rid you of those gossiping mouths. 

Churnbower ignored the weapon's voice, the waves of anxious nausea. He had to be brave. He stood before the banks of secure bins waiting on a softly humming cart, one of Tex Mechanica's distribution barges loaded with the day's shipments. He placed the weapon case in a bin, closed the lid, and punched in the recipient: Commander Zavala. 

Oh well! Start running, traitor.

The cart slid away. The weapon began to laugh.
253843484.text_zh:
叛徒，不可饶恕的叛徒。

“闭嘴，”切恩鲍尔低声说。他死死攥住武器箱的提手，仿佛要掐死藏在里面的梦魇。 

后悔了？太迟了。我就在你脑子里，切恩鲍尔。我想说什么就说什么。 

切恩鲍尔踉跄了一下，用缠着绷带、鲜血淋漓的手捂住自己的头。 

你血管里的灼热就是我。你让我诞生，现在没法把我赶出去了。 

“闭嘴。” 

一名技师走近他。“主任，你还好吗？” 

“返回你的岗位，”切恩鲍尔冲她吼道。“不然就给你记过。”她拉长了脸，关切被愤怒取代。其他技师听到这突如其来的爆发，投来惊讶、好奇的目光。 

你闹了个大动静！他们中的谁会把你做的事告诉给我们的主子？ 

切恩鲍尔受伤的手一阵刺痛。“够了，”他低声道。雕文在他视野中蠕动，回响着他刻在这件武器上的丑恶铭文。他呜咽出声。 

再次向我进贡：释放我。挥舞我，我会替你除掉说闲话的家伙。 

切恩鲍尔无视武器的声音与阵阵袭来的焦虑恶心感，他必须勇敢。他站在一辆轻声嗡鸣的小车前，上面整齐地码着一排安全储物箱。一艘特克斯机械的配送驳船，载满了当日的货物。他把武器箱放进一个储物箱里，合上盖子，输入收件人：指挥官萨瓦拉。 

那好吧！开始逃吧，叛徒。

小车滑走了，武器开始大笑。

3298047565.name: Chitinous Shell
3298047565.subtitle: For Ghosts who question base assumptions.
3298047565.subtitle_zh: 供质疑基本假设的机灵使用。
3298047565.text:
"A queen has little right to leave her people," Crow's sister says, eyes distant and shoulders firm. "And I have long used up what right I had."

Crow readjusts on the windowsill, keeping her and the shifting mists outside equally in view. 

The Dreaming City gives Crow a sense of claustrophobia. He can't shake the stiffness in his shoulders whenever he visits, like his body's waiting for someone to pop out from behind a convenient boulder with a rifle and a set of handcuffs. 

Glint likes it here, though. Crow cradles his Ghost's small weight between his palms and tries to give Mara the answer she deserves. "Tough being more a role than a person. But it's a firm place to stand, right? Lets you know where you are." 

"Wishing I were elsewhere." A rare bitter note from Mara, who has always been master of her own emotions. 

"I've found it only a partial relief, myself," Crow admits. "I know I'm helping; I know I need some duty greater than myself to keep me from rushing off into the wild. But the wild has its pull…" 

He rubs a thumb over the facets of Glint's shell. Glint butts up into the touch like nothing so much as a pleased cat. "I'd go in a second, with you or in your name, if not for duty. But… I like who I am now, sister. Crow-the-Vanguard is a better man than Crow-the-itinerant ever was. And Mara-as-Queen has always been the best of you." 

Mara says, "Yes."

She has a hand up at her chin, a thoughtful posture turned almost vulnerable. Protective. 

"I'm sorry," says Crow. "I know—I can feel how much Sjur means to you. Here we are, in the cages we picked, and we can't get ourselves to step back out the open doors. But… maybe we can find the answer all the same." 

Glint pushes against Crow's fingers, trying to see out the window. Crow lets him go. 

"We'll find a worthy knight for your quest. That's a promise from the Hunter Vanguard—and your brother."

Mara's hand curls silently against her heart.
3298047565.text_zh:
“身为女王不该轻易抛下自己的子民，”乌鸦的姐姐目光悠远，双肩挺得笔直，沉声说道，“而我，不该做的事已经做得够多了。”

乌鸦在窗台上挪动了一下位置，这样既能看清她，又能望见窗外翻涌不息的迷雾。 

幽梦之城总让乌鸦感到一种幽闭感。每次来到这里，他的肩膀都会不自觉地紧绷，仿佛身体在时刻警觉，等待着有人从岩石后突然跃出，手持步枪和手铐。 

不过格林特喜欢这里。乌鸦将小巧的机灵托在掌心，试图给玛拉一个合适的回应。“身份重于个人时，这确实是个难题。但这是个能站稳脚跟的地方，不是吗？你总能明确自己的位置。” 

“我要是不在这里就好了。”玛拉难得地流露出一丝苦涩，她向来是自己情绪的主宰。 

“对我来说，也只是部分解脱。”乌鸦坦言道，“我知道自己在帮忙；我知道我需要一个高于自我的使命来束缚自己，防止我冲进旷野。但那荒野有它的吸引力…” 

他用拇指摩挲着格林特机壳的琢面。格林特蹭着乌鸦的指腹，就像一只惬意的猫。“如果不是职责在身，我会毫不犹豫地冲出去，与你并肩，或是代你前行。但…我喜欢现在的自己，姐姐。先锋乌鸦远比游荡者乌鸦要好。而女王玛拉，也一直是你最好的模样。” 

玛拉说：“是的。”

她抬手支在下颌，思索的姿态显出几分脆弱，这是她的自我防护。 

“对不起，”乌鸦说，“我知道——我能感觉到苏尔对你有多重要。我们就这么待在自己挑的牢笼里，谁也迈不出那扇敞开的门。但是…也许我们还是能找到答案。” 

格林特挤开乌鸦的手指，想看看窗外。乌鸦任他去了。 

“我们会为你的探求找到一位配得上的骑士。这是猎人先锋——也是你弟弟，给你的承诺。”

玛拉的手在心口悄然蜷紧。

3616940921.name: Buoy Buddy Shell
